idea.title: CPU probe suite: where B2 loses its wrong answers
idea.summary: One read-only script run on the saved B2 checkpoints says whether B2's misses sit in the thinker state, the mode and pointer choice, or the register-by-register writer. It fits a free readout on the 9 final registers, checks which output path (NUM, WORD, GEN) could have produced the gold answer, swaps registers versus pointers between rows, sorts wrong GEN answers by error shape, and logs per-register EOS and per-round readability. Every writer idea below takes its go or no-go from this.
idea.change: S0: fix custom_io/diag_ledger.py:21, which decodes GEN with model.readout(R) (tied table, no copy gate) while talk() uses gen_copy when copy=True (ledger.py:384-389); any earlier GEN column from diag_ledger is the nocopy path. S1: new diag_talker.py (read-only on checkpoints) using a hooked copy of run() that also returns zf=ln_z(Z[:,1]), R, per-register p_r from gen_copy, and run(rounds=True) snapshots. M1: free 256x108+bias logistic fit on frozen final registers of 2,000 TRAIN rows (units-first target + EOS, ledger.py:447 convention), scored on dev rows B2 misses in GEN mode; sanity: the same fit must reach >=90% exact on GEN rows B2 gets right. Repeat on the six round snapshots (per-round readability). Tied-vs-free cost = M1 free head minus B2's tied head on the same features (gate for the untie idea). M2: per dev row, reach_NUM / reach_WORD (first 64 word tokens) / reach_GEN, as a confusion table of chosen path by reachable paths per family. M3: same-family donor swaps: register-only swap vs pointer/mode-only swap vs full donor (includes WORD pointer-transfer). Probe 2: classify wrong GEN rows (1 reversed; 2 copy-source: out and gold both substrings of the prompt; 3 one-edit or one-register length error; 4 off-prompt with edit distance >=2; 5 other), digit place for numeric answers, per-register P(EOS at gold length) and gold-character rank, per-round first-readable round. Zero-training write test: 200 random 1-9 digit and 200 random 9-14 character strings as answers. DECISION TABLE fixed now: M1>=60% on missed GEN rows = registers hold the answer (go to ideas 4, 12-14 per Probe 2 class); M1<=20% = thinker problem, no writer screen (levers W2/H1 in redesign-ideas); 20-60% = not shown, refit on 2,000 more train rows; reach_other>=30% on missed rows where that path was not chosen = chooser fault, not writer fault; M3: register swap moves >=50% of outputs to the donor answer and >=2x the pointer swap = registers carry identity, reverse = pointers carry it, else mixed.
idea.why: Each GEN register takes its own argmax over the tied table plus copy gate (ledger.py:387-390), so a register that holds the answer but cannot express it through the tied table looks the same in the output as one that never held it. B2 misses about 129 of 1,360 in_dist rows per seed and five families hold 72% of misses; two of the biggest (table_lookup, fewshot_number_rule) are GEN-heavy with copy share only 0.04-0.09, so their output is almost all the tied vocabulary readout. Saved JSON holds no per-row predictions (only chain-5 hits), so the error shape is unknown today. Without this split, talker ideas cannot be ranked against thinker ideas (Levelt split in notes/brain-talking.md).

test.where: Ben's PC CPU (needs the sk200k data root and the train split for the M1 fit); checkpoints from scratchpad code/b2ckpt B2_s200..205; seeds 200 and 201 first, then all six
test.arms: No arm comparison: M1 free fit vs B2's own tied GEN output (with sanity on right rows); M1 on six round snapshots; M2 path reach; M3 register vs pointer vs full donor swaps; Probe 2 error classes and register census.
test.pass_mark: Harness first: the probe's tied-readout path reproduces B2's own GEN-row exact within 0.5 points on both seeds, the five error classes sum to all wrong GEN rows, M1 sanity >=90% on right rows. Then the decision table in the change field applies; Probe 2 routing: reversed>=10% or copy-source>=40% goes to the copy-chain idea; one-edit-or-length>=25% (wrong-length alone) or order class>=30% goes to the feedback ladder; off-prompt>=50% with M1<=20% closes the writer line as 'not the writer'.
test.proved_wrong: Writer hypothesis is wrong if M1<=20% and reach_GEN<=10% on missed GEN rows (answer is in neither registers nor the vocabulary path). Chooser hypothesis is wrong if reach_other<=10%. Probe void if the sanity or reproduction check fails.

idea.rules_check: R1/R10: diagnostic, nothing added to the deployed model. R2: no teacher. R3: no parameters. R4: makes no claim; six seeds possible since checkpoints exist; marks fixed now. problems: [shown] No hard rule is broken as written: the probe is read-only, CPU-only, adds no parameters, uses B2 only, and scores dev rows with train rows for the fit. Rule 1 is not touched because nothing new runs at answer time. Rule 7 is at risk only through wording (see the gold() item below).

[shown] Already done: the zero-training write test. architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md line 13 (write_copy operand 29.3/30.9, answer 42.1/42.4 on seeds 200/201, S3 FAIL) and lines 18-27 (exact copy by digit length: operand 14% at 4 digits and 1% at 5; answer 59% at 4 and 1% at 5). The idea's write test repeats this on B2. The brief's 'T1 sealed, not run' is stale: T1 ran (T1-SCREEN-RESULT line 4), and checkpoints exist at /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/40b-t1-s200/T1_s200/checkpoint.pt and the s201 twin.

[shown] The B2 write test has no defined path and one arm that fails by construction. B2's GEN path caps at 8 characters plus EOS (ledger.py:62-63; data.py:11), so the 200 random 9-14 character strings score 0% before any run. PASS-MARKS.md line 408 says a B2 digit-copy test 'would need training' because B2 has no learned digit writer. The idea must say whether a zero-training write means prompt copy through the copy gate or register writing, and drop the 9-14 arm.

[shown] The full donor arm is already run. results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json lesions.donor.in_dist: exact 3.24, donor_match 58.2, n 1360, skipped 0. custom-io/gpt-b2-leak-and-credit-2026-10-05.md line 86 gives donor 3.8 on the two-seed screen. Only the register-only and pointer-only arms are new. diag_register.py lines 145-151 already implement a register swap (for RegisterLoop, not Ledger), and tests/test_register_loop.py line 191 has a register-only test. Port them instead of re-deriving.

[shown] The per-family talker-path diagnosis already exists. results/RESULTS-SCREEN.md lines 63-67 and design/design-B2.md lines 5-14 say diag_ledger.py was run on design B's checkpoint B_s101 (copy=False, so readout is the real talk path). The idea's 'written, never run here' is true only for this container. Its claim that 'any earlier GEN column is the nocopy path' is wrong for design B; the line-21 bug matters only for copy=True models (B2). The prior finding to beat is 'GEN registers cannot emit what they never emitted in training' (letter_ops answer split 0/40). B2's copy path was built to fix that, so the probe must test whether that bottleneck is still there.

[shown] The M1 sanity check conflicts with the copy path. The sanity check needs at least 90% on 'GEN rows B2 gets right', but those rows are copy-heavy. From RESULT.json for seed 200: cipher_map 40/40 right at copy share 1.00; story_chain3 40/40 at 0.75; syllogism 40/40 at 0.67; letter_ops 39/40 at 0.67; digits_parity 37/40 at 0.41 (extra.copy_gate.by_family). A free head on registers cannot be expected to recover letters that the copy attention supplies, and the idea admits low M1 is expected on cipher_map. Under its own rule, 'probe void if the sanity check fails', the probe is likely void. Fix: restrict M1 and its sanity to rows whose registers are mostly vocabulary (mean gate >= 0.5; table_lookup copy share 0.063 and fewshot 0.046), and report copy rows separately.

[suggested] M1 has no null control. A 256x108 free head fitted on 2,000 train rows can learn the answer prior of each family. Needed: the same head fitted on registers from donor rows (another row's state) and scored against the current gold, which should be near chance; plus a label-shuffled fit. Without these, M1 of 60% or more cannot be read as 'the registers hold the answer'.

[shown] Per-round readability cannot cover every round. ledger.py:340 is `if rounds and t <= n - 2`, so snapshots exist only for t = 1..6. The 7th program write (t = 7) and round 8 are never snapshotted. tool.py:124 asserts `not rounds`, so per-round snapshots cannot run on T1 without new code. Answer-level settle rounds are already measured: design/LOOPS-probe.md lines 17 and 49-56 and results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json (M2). Test LR, a per-round readout training run, failed on stability and leak (PASS-MARKS.md lines 188-204). The new part is only the no-training linear readout.

[shown] Probe 2's five error classes overlap and have no priority order. A reversed output can also be a substring of the prompt, and an off-prompt answer can be one edit from gold. 'Classes sum to all wrong GEN rows' cannot be checked without a first-match order. 'One-edit or one-register length error' and 'wrong-length alone' are not defined (edit-distance cut, which register, and what counts as the length).

[suggested] Several terms have no formula. reach_NUM, reach_WORD and reach_GEN are named but not defined; for example, does reach_GEN mean the gold string is the argmax of gen_copy over the 9 registers, or some top-k? M3's '>= 50% of outputs move to the donor answer' has no denominator (all rows, or rows where the donor answer differs from gold). M3 also needs stratifying by copy gate: on copy-target families a register swap moves the copy pointer, not the answer identity.

[shown] The harness and the S0 fix name different paths. S0 makes diag_ledger use gen_copy (the copy path, ledger.py:387). The harness then requires 'the probe's tied-readout path' to match B2's GEN exact within 0.5 points, and the tied-versus-free cost uses 'B2's tied head' (readout(R), ledger.py:365-366). These are different paths: the nocopy lesion is 78.97 in_dist on seed 200 (RESULT.json), against 90.51 with copy. Use one name per path. The reproduction check should compare the probe's output to talk() on the same rows, with exact match expected.
[shown] Name collision. probe_loops.py lines 3 and 35 and results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json use 'M1' for in_dist exact by loop count K. The idea's M1 is a free-head fit. Rename one of them.

[shown] Rule 7 wording risk. The idea says both 'units-first target + EOS, ledger.py:447 convention' and 'skip rows with answers over 8 characters'. gold() (ledger.py:446-447) cuts with r['answer'][:GEN_MAX], which is silent truncation. Any fit or probe target must use raw answers and skip long rows, never gold(). The fact-check says no pooled-5 or train answer exceeds 8 characters, but the data root is absent here, so that is untested.

[shown] The wave IDs cited for overlap (w1a-4, w1e-1 to w1e-5, w1f-1, w1b-4, w1e-3) do not appear in any .md, .json or .txt file under /mnt/project-files (grep found no hits). The overlap claims therefore cannot be checked; either define these probes in the idea or drop the claims.

NUM rows are 42% of dev rows for B2, so M2's reach_NUM and the digit-place parts measure a path T1 deletes. Running on T1_s200 and T1_s201 needs an adapter for tool.py talk(), which concatenates X, Xt and call text into gen_copy (tool.py:206-211), and no rounds hook (tool.py:124).

problems: Autonomy scope passes (shown): every D1 step is research-only (read-only hook, gold-label fit on 2,000 train rows, gold-based routing classes, researcher-picked strings and thresholds) and changes nothing in the deployed model. PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md line 8 and creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md section 7c (around lines 925-935) exempt tests, scoring, controls and marks. Ben's quote says 'everything that you do', so ask Ben to confirm the exemption. Read literally, D1 would need a deploy-time analogue, and it has none.

The autonomy risk sits downstream (suggested): the decision thresholds (60/20/30/50/10/25 percent) and the gold-based Probe 2 classes must not become runtime gates or routing rules in ideas 4, 5 and 12-14. That use would be a dev-tuned runtime value, which rule 10 forbids. Idea 4 (feedback ladder) needs an answer-free check that the model runs on its own tries, and D1 supplies none. An autonomous version would be a learned self-check head trained before shipping on the model's own tries, or an outside tool the model chooses to call.

Snapshot gap (shown, ledger.py:303-341): the loop runs t = 0..7 with n = 8 and writes program steps at t = 1..N_RES = 7 (ledger.py:317-319; progparse.py:8). It snapshots only when `rounds and t <= n - 2` (ledger.py:340), which gives t = 1..6. The step-7 write and the post-loop state are never captured. D1's 'six round snapshots' and 'first-readable round' cannot see rounds 7-8, so an answer that becomes readable only at the last write reads as never readable. Fix this in the probe's own hooked copy of run(), not in ledger.py.

Pass mark compares the wrong path (shown): after the S0 fix, GEN uses gen_copy, so the 'probe's tied-readout path' is the nocopy lesion. Seed 200 nocopy in_dist exact is 78.97 against 90.51 intact (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json, lesions.nocopy and final_eval.in_dist.exact). The 'within 0.5 points' reproduction check fails by construction, which under the idea's own rule voids the probe. Fix: reproduce B2's copy-path GEN output and report the tied path only as a nocopy control expected near 78.97.

reach_GEN, reach_NUM and reach_WORD have no formula (shown: M2 names them without a definition). Two natural readings break the proved-wrong clause. Oracle reading (gold characters reachable by some register choice): reach_GEN is near 100% on gold answers of 8 characters or fewer, so 'reach_GEN <= 10%' never holds and the writer hypothesis cannot be proved wrong. Argmax reading (GEN output equals gold): reach_GEN is 0% on missed GEN rows by construction, so the clause fires whenever M1 <= 20%. The 'reach_other >= 30%' chooser rule has the same flaw. Define it before the run.

The write test is partly fixed by architecture (shown: N_REG = 9 and GEN_MAX = 8, ledger.py:61-63). B2 cannot emit 9-14 character strings, and it cannot emit 9-digit strings either, since 9 characters exceed the 8-character cap. That half cannot pass, and the idea attaches no pass mark to the write test. The 1-9 digit range matches T1's CELLS = 11 (tool.py:37-38: 9 digits, sign, EOS). That looks like a calculator design constant (suggested), not a measured need. A write result should not set a fixed writer length without saying where the length came from.

Rule 7 wording (shown): the M1 target follows the 'ledger.py:447 convention', but that line silently cuts answers to GEN_MAX = 8 characters (r['answer'][:GEN_MAX]). The idea's R7 line says to skip over-8 rows and report them. The fit, the scoring and the round-readability target must drop those rows explicitly and report the count. They must not reuse gold() as written.

One weak probe is asked for a thinker verdict (suggested). M1 is one linear 256 x 108 head per register (27,756 weights each), fit on 2,000 train rows. A low M1 can reflect a weak probe, not missing information, yet 'M1 <= 20% = thinker problem' is written as a conclusion. The sanity check (>= 90% on dev rows B2 gets right) shows transfer only on easy rows. Require a second probe class (for example a small MLP on the same registers, or more rows) to agree before any thinker verdict. Otherwise log 'not shown'.

Name clash (shown): results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json uses M1 for in_dist accuracy by loop count (keys all, by_len, by_family) and M2 for settle statistics (probe_loops.py:35 and :52). The idea's evidence cites 'PROBE.json M1.by_family and M2.all' for round-8 family numbers. That path resolves, but those are loop-count results, not register or path probes. Rename D1's probes to avoid mixing them.

Dependency on Ben's PC (shown): data.py:7-9 points at an sk200k root under another session path, and it is absent here (checked). The M1 fit and every B2 probe need CUSTOM_IO_DATA set on the PC. This is a research-run step, not a deploy issue, but none of the probe numbers can be checked from this container.

A low M1 on those rows is not a thinker or writer verdict. The 60% and 20% thresholds should apply to gate-stratified subsets.

reach_GEN is undefined. If it means the gold answer is at most 8 printable ASCII characters, it is a length test, not reachability (GEN_MAX = 8 and N_REG = 9 at models/ledger.py:62-63 and 447; the data.py Dataset docstring says family-split answers run to 12 characters, shown). The kill rule 'reach_GEN <= 10%' would then fire only on long answers and would confuse the 8-character cap with the writer.

The pass marks use labels that are not in the class list. Classes are 1 reversed, 2 copy-source, 3 one-edit or one-register length error, 4 off-prompt, 5 other. The routing rules cite an 'order class' and 'wrong-length alone', which are undefined. Pre-registered thresholds need fixed definitions.

The zero-training write test cannot pass for 9-14 character strings, and 9-digit strings also fail, because GEN emits at most 8 characters plus EOS from 9 registers (ledger.py:62-63). The test would measure the cap, not the writer. It also duplicates the sealed T1 write_copy check (PASS-MARKS addendum 17, per the brief). What input is fed in the 'zero-training' version is not stated.

The harness reproduction target is not in any saved file. RESULT.json has no per-row or per-mode GEN results (shown: only the chain-5 hit map is saved; PREDS.json is written only with --save-preds, train.py:72-77). 'Reproduces B2's own GEN-row exact within 0.5 points' can only mean a comparison with talk() run in the same probe. The idea should say so.

Two different dev sets are mixed. Final-eval in_dist is 1,360 rows, 40 per family (RESULT.json final_eval; shown). The copy-gate and coverage numbers come from the big-root dev/in_dist.jsonl, 6,800 rows, 200 per family (ledger.py:555-556 in extra_evals; copy_gate n_rows = 2,038; shown). The '129 of 1,360' miss count and the copy shares come from different sets. The probe must name its row set and its power.

Feature mismatch in M1. run() returns raw registers Z[:, N_CTRL:] (ledger.py run(), shown), and the tied readout applies ln_t before the projection (readout(), ledger.py around line 365). The idea says to apply ln_z, which is for the control token only. Register features need ln_t, or the free-versus-tied cost compares unlike features.

The donor data already pre-judges much of the probe, and the idea does not mention it. Donor-carry ratio (donor_match divided by intact accuracy, by family, six seeds): word_filter about 100 (GEN 95% of gold rows), fewshot_number_rule about 81 (GEN 96%), seq_next about 73 (GEN 100%) (computed from RESULT.json lesions.donor.in_dist.by_family and final_eval; shown; the normalisation is ad hoc and list_stats gives 106). Suggested reading: on pure-GEN families the writer reproduces the donor's state faithfully, so writer loss is unlikely to be the main cause of the largest miss family. The probe should state this prior and what M1 range would contradict it.

table_lookup donor carry (about 13) is mixed-mode. Gold table_lookup rows are 31% WORD and 67.5% GEN (coverage.by_family, shown). WORD rows copy from the current prompt, so their low donor match is a pointer effect, not a register effect. The saved donor numbers cannot separate the two. The M3 split must be by mode and must be run.

Power and rule 4. Missed GEN rows per seed are not in the files; probably tens. Under a binomial model a 95% interval at n of about 70 is roughly plus or minus 11 points (suggested), which is wide against the 20% and 60% thresholds. Routing decisions act as claims, so all six seeds should be run first (checkpoints present, sha256 verified OK for all six, shown). Seeds 200 and 201 only give a screen.

No selectivity control. Linear-probe accuracy alone does not show that information is encoded, and low accuracy does not show absence. Hewitt and Liang (2019), EMNLP, D19-1275, which I confirmed exists by search, proposes random-label control tasks for this. The 20% 'thinker problem' rule needs a control task fitted on the same registers.

The S0 fix is feasible and the mechanism claim checks out (shown). diag_ledger.py:21 uses model.readout(R) with no copy gate, and run() returns X and xm when copy=True, so gen_copy can be called. The prediction should be exact equality, not 'near': with gate = 1, the argmax of the mixture equals the argmax of the vocabulary softmax, so the diag GEN column should equal the nocopy lesion (stored 78.97 on seed 200, against 90.51 intact). This prediction is untested but mechanically determined.

M3 and the per-round snapshots need new code. diag_register.py cannot run on Ledger, because models/ledger.py has no rounds() method and no n_reg attribute (shown). The probe therefore needs a hooked copy of run(), and the idea does not cost it. The round-8 family-group means (82.1/85.2, 96.5/98.0, 94.4/95.3) cannot be checked because PROBE.json does not save group membership. The M2 settle-bucket shares (59.9% and 49.9% at len+1) do check out (results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json, seeds 100 and 101, shown).

problems: M1 cannot run as written: the '2,000 TRAIN rows' are not defined as gold-GEN rows. shown: gold() writes register targets only for gold mode 2 (ledger.py:446-448); other registers stay -100 (unlabelled). A random train sample is about 30% GEN (suggested, from the dev GEN share 29.97 in RESULT.json extra.coverage.all), so most rows would carry no label. The fit must say 2,000 gold-GEN train rows, or all available.

The M1 fit has no fixed recipe and is underdetermined: 27,756 parameters (256x108+108) against roughly 8,000 labelled register targets (suggested: 2,000 rows x answer length plus EOS, at most 18,000). Optimizer, epochs, L2 and stopping are unstated, and the sanity gate (at least 90% on right rows) can be met by tuning. Fix the recipe before any run.

The tied-vs-free comparison is biased toward the tied head. shown: B2's tied readout was trained on the full train set for 24,000 updates at batch 256 (RESULT.json config). The free head sees 2,000 rows. The 'tied-vs-free cost' gate has no number. Both heads need the same rows, and the gate needs a stated threshold.

The harness reference does not exist in any saved file. The pass mark 'reproduces B2's own GEN-row exact within 0.5 points' has no source: RESULT.json has per-family totals only, with no mode split (shown). The saved run was CUDA with bf16 (33-pc-confirm-b2.txt header; config bf16 true), so a CPU fp32 rerun can differ by a few rows. Require bit-exact agreement between the probe's path output and model.talk() on every dev row instead.

M1 has no null or floor, so the 20% and 60% marks have no reference. Two cheap floors exist. First, loops:0: shown, seed 200 in_dist is 0.0 (RESULT.json lesions.loops:0). At loops=0 the registers are the place rows only and identical across rows (ledger.py:303-307), so a probe on them is prior-only. Second, a per-family train-majority answer, since low-entropy answers (yes/no, small numbers) can score by prior alone.

reach_GEN is tautological on the missed GEN rows if it means B2's own GEN output (suggested: those rows are wrong by definition). The writer kill clause (M1 at most 20% and reach_GEN at most 10%) then reduces to M1 at most 20%. Define reach_GEN by the gold character's rank under the gen_copy distribution (ledger.py:387-390), or drop the clause.

reach_NUM and reach_WORD have no chance null. Short word answers (yes/no, single letters) and small numbers match prompt words or slot values by coincidence (suggested), so the chooser threshold (reach_other at least 30%) can pass by chance. Use a null built from the gold answer of a different same-family row.

The decision band is an open loop, and two labels overreach. '20-60%: refit on 2,000 more train rows' is not a decision; it should be a recorded 'not shown' with a fixed next step. 'M1 at most 20% = thinker problem' only shows the registers do not linearly carry the answer; the reader is also upstream (suggested). Only the M1 at least 60% branch falsifies the thinker branch. What ideas 4, 12-14 are, and what the untie gate's threshold is, cannot be checked in the files read.

The GEN sample is small and the seeds are not independent. shown: no per-row predictions are saved (RESULT.json has none), so missed GEN rows must be estimated. From the coverage shares (approximate, all-split proxy) that is about 62-78 per seed, and about 65% come from fewshot_number_rule and table_lookup. The six seeds reuse one dev set, so the union of unique rows is the real n. The report must state it.

The copy confound is smaller than the orchestrator note implies. shown: cipher_map has 0-1 in_dist misses per seed (RESULT.json). The copy-mixed families (order_chain, kin_chain, digits_parity, verify_claim, letter_ops; copy share 0.40-0.67) hold about 13 of the roughly 65 estimated missed GEN rows (suggested). Report them as a separate stratum, not inside one pooled M1 number.

M3 has no denominator and an unstated baseline. A register-only swap changes only rows whose chosen mode is GEN (NUM and WORD outputs read vals and pointers, not the registers), so the '50% of outputs' bar must be over GEN-mode rows. Copy-type families cannot carry a donor answer by construction. shown: a full-state donor lesion already exists (evalx.py:93-115 swaps model.state(); RESULT.json lesions.donor), with table_lookup donor_match 3.8% (six-seed mean) against 28.8% intact accuracy. The new content of M3 is only the split arms.

The zero-training write arm cannot test what it names. shown: GEN targets stop at 8 characters plus EOS (ledger.py:63 and 446-448; data.py:11), so the 9th register is never trained to emit a character. The 9-digit and 9-14 character arms therefore measure the cap, not the writer. The arm has no pass mark and no prompt format for injecting the strings, and it duplicates T1's write_copy (brief: scored at T1, at least 99.0). Drop it or move it to T1.

Probe 2 classes overlap and their routing is unreconciled. Reversed, copy-source and off-prompt can each match the same row, so 'the five classes sum to all wrong GEN rows' needs a stated precedence. Its thresholds (reversed at least 10%, copy-source at least 40%, edit-or-length at least 25%, order at least 30%, off-prompt at least 50%) sit beside the M1 table with no rule for when both fire.

Cost and location. The probe has no training. shown: B2 training took 13,160 s for seed 200 (1.82 steps/s with three jobs on one card; RESULT.json train_s and the --par 3 header), not the 'about 1 hour' in the brief. A CPU run of 1.5 h for six seeds is plausible but untested. A GPU run would take minutes per seed, and memory is far under 16 GB for a 3.3M-parameter forward at batch 128 (suggested). The probe cannot run in this container: the sk200k root in data.py:7-9 is absent, and no dev or train jsonl is in the code or project folders. It must run on the PC with CUSTOM_IO_DATA set.

Build scope is larger than the first cut needs. The hooked copy of run() is only needed for zf, which the register test does not use. run() already returns R, X and xm (ledger.py:344), and rounds=True gives the snapshots (ledger.py:341). Per-round readability is partly on file: shown, results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json results[].M1.all gives talker-level in_dist exact by loop count K=1..16 on seeds 100/101 (K=1 30.6, K=3 69.1, K=8 89.4). chair.reasons:
Verdict: plan, as a cheaper and tighter read-only probe. It is CPU-only, adds no parameters, trains nothing in the model, uses B2 only and touches no protected panel, so rules 1-9 hold. Rule 10 (autonomy) is not touched because the probe does nothing at deploy time (suggested: research tests and scoring are exempt under PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md line 8; ask Ben to confirm his 'everything that you do' covers research probes). Rule 10 does bite downstream: the 60/20/30/50/10/25 percent thresholds and the gold-based error classes are research-only. They must never become runtime gates or routing rules in ideas 4, 5 and 12-14. Those ideas each need a deploy-time check that uses no answer key, such as a self-check head learned before shipping or a tool the model chooses to call.

Facts I checked in the code and files (shown):
- diag_ledger.py:21 decodes GEN with model.readout(R) and skips gen_copy. talk() at ledger.py:384-389 uses gen_copy when copy=True. With the gate forced to 1 the mixture argmax equals the vocabulary argmax, so the fixed diag column should equal the nocopy lesion exactly (78.97 vs 90.51 in_dist, seed 200, RESULT.json).
- ledger.py:340 snapshots only when `rounds and t <= n-2`, so t=1..6. The step-7 write and the post-loop state are never captured.
- ledger.py:446-447 gold() cuts answers with r['answer'][:GEN_MAX]. The probe must use raw answers, skip rows over 8 characters and report the count (rule 7).
- The brief is stale on T1. architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md shows T1 ran on two rented RTX 5090s. Verdict: NOT SHOWN. S3 write_copy is 29.3/30.9 operand and 42.1/42.4 answer, a FAIL. Copy works at 1-3 digits (86-98%) and fails at 4 digits and above (operand 14% at 4, 1% at 5, 0% at 6-9; answer 59% at 4, 1% at 5), which matches the training lengths. So the idea's zero-training write test is already answered. Its 9-14 character arm cannot pass anyway because B2's answer cap is 8 characters plus EOS (ledger.py:62-63). Drop the whole write arm.
- The full-donor arm already exists in RESULT.json lesions.donor (seed 200 exact 3.24, donor_match 58.2). Only the register-only and pointer-only splits are new.

Critic problems I upheld, because they would void or mislead the probe as written:
(a) The M1 sanity gate of at least 90% on right GEN rows fails by construction on copy-heavy rows. cipher_map is 40/40 right at copy share 1.00, and letter_ops and syllogism are at 0.67. A free head on registers cannot emit letters that the copy attention supplies (suggested).
(b) reach_NUM, reach_WORD and reach_GEN have no formulas. As written, reach_GEN is either tautologically false on missed rows or a length test.
(c) The harness compares the wrong path. The 'tied-readout' path is the nocopy path, about 78.97, not the copy-path output.
(d) The five error classes overlap with no precedence.
(e) M1 has no null control or floor. A 27,756-weight head on about 8,000 labelled register targets can learn the per-family answer prior.
(f) '2,000 TRAIN rows' must mean gold-GEN rows. gold() only labels registers for mode 2 (ledger.py:446-448), and GEN is about 30% of dev rows (RESULT.json extra.coverage.all).
(g) Register features need ln_t, which readout() applies. ln_z is for the control token only.
(h) M3 needs a denominator and a split by copy gate and by answer mode.
(i) The names M1 and M2 collide with results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json, where they mean in_dist exact by loop count and settle statistics.
(j) The 20-60% band is an open loop, and 'M1 at most 20% means thinker problem' overreaches. A weak linear probe, or a reader-side fault, gives the same reading.

Two critic claims I did not rely on, because I could not check them in the files: the exact per-seed counts of missed GEN rows (estimated 62-78 per seed from coverage shares, with about 65% in table_lookup and fewshot_number_rule), and any wave-ID overlap (w1a-4, w1e-1 and the rest appear in no file).

Value (suggested): this is the cheapest evidence anywhere for ranking writer ideas against thinker ideas, since no per-row predictions are saved. Prior from existing data: table_lookup full-state donor match is only 3.8%, so its registers may not carry a transferable answer, and the probe may land in the 'state problem' branch for the biggest family. That is a useful no-go. Limit (shown): B2's 8-character cap and independent per-register argmax mean the probe says little about a sentence-length English talker. It only decides whether the register-to-vocabulary writer is B2's bottleneck. Do not present it as English-talker evidence (rule 9: B2 only).
chair.revised_idea:
talker-D1 (revised): a read-only CPU probe suite on the six saved B2 checkpoints (seeds 200-205, sha256 checked). Nothing is trained in the model and nothing changes at deploy time. Run on Ben's PC with CUSTOM_IO_DATA set (the sk200k root is absent in this container). All six seeds run before any routing decision, and all stats are pooled over seeds and over unique dev rows. Name the dev set in the sealed spec: the 1,360-row final-eval in_dist (40 per family) as the primary set, with the 6,800-row big-root in_dist (200 per family) used for the family-level power check.

Naming: 'vocab' = readout(R) with ln_t (the nocopy path); 'copy' = gen_copy (the real path). The free-head fit is called REGFIT, not M1 or M2, to avoid the probe_loops names.

Stage 0 (harness, void on failure). Fix diag_ledger.py:21 to call gen_copy(o['R'], o['X'], o['xm'], batch['prompt_ids']). Write diag_talker.py as a hooked copy of run() that returns R, X, xm and ln_z(Z[:,1]), with snapshots at t=1..7 plus the post-loop state (the repo's t<=n-2 rule gives only t=1..6; do not edit ledger.py). Check that every dev row's copy-path output equals model.talk() on the same device, bit-exact, on all six seeds. Then run the gate-forced-to-1 vocab path, which should equal talk(lesion='nocopy'); the stored seed-200 nocopy 78.97 is a reference expected within about 0.5 (CPU fp32 vs the original bf16 CUDA run), not an exact match. Report the count of dev and train rows with answers over 8 characters and skip them. Never call gold() for targets; use raw r['answer'] reversed plus EOS (rule 7).

Stage 1 (no fit). For each missed gold-GEN row and each register, record the rank of the gold character (units-first, EOS included) under the copy mixture and under the vocab path alone. Define: reach_GEN = gold is at most 8 printable ASCII characters and every gold register character, plus EOS, is in the top 5 of the copy mixture; reach_NUM = gold equals str(vals[k]) for some valid slot k; reach_WORD = gold equals one of the first 64 word spans. Each reach_* is scored against a chance null built from the gold answer of a different row of the same family. Run the same on loops:0 as the prior-only floor. Report per family, with table_lookup and fewshot_number_rule as their own rows, and split by gate: vocabulary-path rows (mean gate at least 0.5) versus copy-path rows. Classify wrong GEN rows with first-match precedence: (1) reversed, (2) copy-source (output and gold both substrings of the prompt), (3) length-only (edit distance equals the absolute length difference), (4) one-edit, (5) off-prompt (edit distance at least 2 and output not a prompt substring), (6) other. The classes then sum exactly to the wrong GEN rows. Add per-register P(EOS at gold length).

Stage 2 (REGFIT, only on vocabulary-path rows). Fit one free 256x108+bias head per register on frozen ln_t(R), on gold-GEN TRAIN rows only (at least 2,000; state the exact count). The recipe is fixed in the spec before the run: fixed L2, fixed epochs, no tuning. Sanity is at least 90% exact on held-out TRAIN vocabulary-path GEN rows and on dev rows B2 gets right with mean gate under 0.2; copy-heavy rows are reported separately and never void the probe. Controls: (i) the same head fit on registers taken from donor rows (another row's state) and scored against the current gold; (ii) a label-shuffled fit; (iii) the loops:0 registers. Tied-versus-free cost is the free head's minus B2's vocab head's exact on the same rows with the same row counts. Pre-register that a free-minus-tied gap of at least 10 points on missed vocabulary-path rows opens the untie idea. Before any 'thinker problem' verdict, a second probe class (a small MLP on the same registers) must agree; otherwise record 'not shown'.

Stage 3 (swaps). Same-family donor pairs. Register-only swap (R from the donor, everything else from the current row) versus pointer/mode-only swap, ported from diag_register.py lines 145-151. The full-donor arm is not re-run; cite RESULT.json lesions.donor. Denominator: GEN-mode rows where the donor's gold answer differs from the current gold. Report the fraction of outputs equal to the donor's gold. Stratify by copy gate and by answer mode (table_lookup is about 31% WORD and 67.5% GEN, so WORD rows move with the pointer).

Stage 4 (per-round readability), conditional: run it only if stage 2 or 3 shows a register signal. Apply ln_t to the register snapshots at t=1..7 plus the post-loop state, and cite results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json for the answer-level settle rounds already measured on seeds 100/101.

Dropped: the zero-training write test (T1-SCREEN-RESULT already shows it), the 9-14 character arm, and the full-donor arm. Optional follow-on, not in this plan: a T1_s200/201 adapter for tool.py talk(), which has no rounds hook (tool.py:124).
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must keep this a read-only research probe: no checkpoint changes, no GPU, no deploy-time change. Fix all marks in the sealed spec before any run, and ask Ben to confirm that research probes are exempt under rule 10.

1. Harness gate (void on failure). Use the copy-path output and compare it bit-exact to model.talk() on every dev row, on the same device, for all six seeds. Treat the gate-forced-to-1 vocab path as a nocopy control that should equal talk(lesion='nocopy'). The stored seed-200 nocopy (78.97 in_dist vs 90.51 intact) is only a reference expected within about 0.5, because CPU fp32 differs from the bf16 CUDA original. Apply the diag_ledger.py:21 fix (gen_copy) and the t=1..7 plus post-loop hook inside diag_talker.py. Do not edit ledger.py.

2. Run order: stage 0 harness, then stage 1 (no fit, ranks, reach_*, error classes), then stage 2 (REGFIT, only on vocabulary-path rows), then stage 3 (register-only versus pointer/mode-only swaps), then stage 4 per-round only if a register signal appears. Stage 1 alone may settle the question.

3. Decision table (suggested, pre-registered; changed from the idea). Primary number: REGFIT exact on missed vocabulary-path GEN rows (mean gate at least 0.5), pooled over six seeds, with null controls (donor-state registers, label-shuffled) and the loops:0 floor reported beside it.
- At least 60%, above the null by at least 20 points: the registers hold the answer, so go to the writer ideas, routed by error class.
- At most 20% and a second probe class (an MLP) agrees: the registers do not linearly carry the answer. This is a state problem (thinker or reader), so no writer screen. It does not say whether the thinker or the reader is at fault.
- Anything between, or probe classes that disagree: record 'not shown'. Fixed next step: one refit with 2,000 more gold-GEN train rows and the same recipe, with no tuning.
- Chooser fault: reach_NUM or reach_WORD (against the different-row null) is at least 30% on missed rows where that path was not chosen.
- Writer hypothesis proved wrong: REGFIT at most 20% and top-5 reach_GEN at most 10% on missed vocabulary-path rows.
- Chooser hypothesis proved wrong: reach_other at most 10%.
- Probe void: harness fails, or the controls do not sit near chance.
- M3: a register swap moves at least 50% of outputs to the donor answer and at least 2x the pointer swap means registers carry identity; the reverse means pointers carry it; otherwise mixed. All three are over GEN-mode rows with donor gold different from current gold, stratified by gate.
- Error-class routing, first-match precedence: reversed at least 10%, or copy-source at least 40%, goes to the copy-chain idea. Length-only at least 25% goes to the feedback ladder. Off-prompt at least 50% together with REGFIT at most 20% closes the writer line.

4. State the prior up front so the result is not post-hoc. From existing donor data, word_filter, list_stats and fewshot_number_rule carry the donor answer (normalised carry of about 100, 106 and 81), but table_lookup does not (full-state donor match 3.8%, about 13 normalised). So the expected outcome for table_lookup is 'registers do not carry a transferable answer'. Say which REGFIT range would contradict this.

5. Rule 7: raw answers only. Skip rows with answers over 8 characters and report the count. Never use gold() (silent cut at ledger.py:447).

6. Power and rule 4. Missed GEN rows are only about 62-78 per seed (estimated, untested), and the six seeds reuse one dev set, so the union of unique rows is the real n. Report intervals. Seeds 200 and 201 alone are a screen. Do not route on fewer than six seeds. The report is a measurement, not a method claim.

7. Autonomy handoff. Label every threshold and class as research-only. For ideas 4, 5 and 12-14, require a deploy-time check with no answer key (a learned self-check head trained before shipping on the model's own tries, or an outside tool the model chooses to call). The gold-based classes may pick which idea to build; they must not be a runtime gate.

8. Scope notes for the Opus lead. This probe says little about sentence-length English talking (B2 caps at 8 characters with independent per-register argmax); it ranks B2's writer against its thinker. Rule 9: keep B2 claims apart from the 1.2B English line. The T1 screen ran on rented GPUs; check rule 6 before treating T1 as a baseline. Cost is about 1.5-2 CPU hours (the idea's own estimate, untested).

plan.title: Talker D1: read-only probe of B2's wrong answers (revised)
plan.ben_line: We look inside B2's saved model to see why it gets some answers wrong: is the right answer lost in its thinking, in its choice of answer type, or in how it writes the letters? We only read the saved models on a regular computer and change nothing in them.
plan.question: On the six saved B2 checkpoints (seeds 200-205), for in_dist rows B2 gets wrong: does the gold answer sit in B2's final GEN registers (read by a shared free readout fit on train rows, with controls), or is it lost to the wrong answer path (NUM/WORD vs GEN), or is it absent from the thinker state? Labels: shown = RESULT.json and code lines checked this session; suggested = reasoned; untested = not run.
plan.one_change: No change to B2, to any checkpoint, or to training. The one thing under test is a read-only diagnostic: B2's 9 final GEN registers are read through the real copy path (gen_copy) and scored with a fixed-recipe free readout, with controls. Only existing-code edit: diag_ledger.py:21 changes from model.readout(R) to gen_copy(R, X, xm, prompt_ids). ledger.py is not edited.
arms: Harness: copy-path output versus model.talk(state, batch, return_modes=True), string for string on all 1,360 in_dist rows; vocab path (gate forced to 1) versus talk(lesion='nocopy').

2x2 mode table on the 1,360 rows: gold mode (progparse.row_targets rule, progparse.py:196-208) by decoded mode (talk). W = gold GEN, decoded GEN, wrong. C = gold NUM or WORD, decoded GEN, wrong. N = gold GEN, decoded NUM or WORD, wrong.

Stage 1, no fit, on W rows: rank of each gold character (units-first, EOS at gold length) per register under the copy mixture and under the vocab path; reach_GEN against a different-row null from the same family; gate strata (mean gate at least 0.5 versus below 0.5).

Stage 2, REGFIT (primary): ONE shared free 256x108 head plus bias on ln_t(R), fit on the first 10,000 TRAIN gold-GEN rows with answers up to 8 characters. Per-register heads are reported only as an upper bound. Controls: donor-state registers, label-shuffled fit, loops:0 registers (row-independent by construction, ledger.py:302-305), and a per-family train-majority prior floor. Second probe class: one hidden layer (256, GELU) on the same data and controls.

Stage 3, swaps: register-only swap on same-family donor pairs (evalx.py donor pairing: same family, different answer) where both gold answers are GEN, at most 8 characters. Pointer-only swap is reported only on NUM/WORD pairs, as a descriptive number. The full donor swap is cited from RESULT.json lesions.donor, not re-run.
Stage 4, conditional: per-round register readability at t=1..7 with the Stage 2 recipe, run only if Stage 2 or Stage 3 shows a register signal.
plan.seeds: Screen first on seeds 200 and 201 (harness, 2x2 mode table, Stage 1). Decision on all six seeds 200-205, pooled over seeds, with 95% intervals from a bootstrap over the 1,360 dev rows (the same dev rows repeat across seeds, so seeds are not independent). Nothing is routed on fewer than six seeds.
plan.machine: Ben's PC, CPU only, fp32, the same device for the probe and for talk(). Needs CUSTOM_IO_DATA set to the sk200k data root (data.py:7-9; the root is absent in this container, so no dev or train row was run here). Checkpoints: scratchpad code/b2ckpt B2_s200 to B2_s205, sha256 matched in this container (shown). No GPU.
pass_marks: VOID (harness): the copy-path output equals talk() string for string on all 1,360 in_dist rows for all six seeds, and the vocab path equals talk(lesion='nocopy'). Any mismatch voids the probe. Reference only, not a gate: seed-200 nocopy in_dist is 78.97 in RESULT.json (shown); a CPU fp32 rerun should land within 1.0 point (suggested, about 14 rows).
VOID (sanity): REGFIT exact on dev rows B2 gets right with mean gate below 0.2 is at least 90% (suggested). If it fails, the free head lacks power and nothing is routed.

VOID (controls): donor-state REGFIT and label-shuffled REGFIT exact on vocab-path W rows are each at most the prior floor plus 5 points. Unique vocab-path W rows across the six seeds must be at least 60 (suggested), or the result is 'not shown'.

PRIMARY, registers hold the answer (go to writer ideas, routed by error class): REGFIT exact on vocab-path W rows, pooled over six seeds, is at least 60%, is at least 20 points above the prior floor, has a bootstrap lower bound of at least 50%, and the MLP class also reaches at least 60%. REGFIT exact means every register argmax, read units-first and reversed, equals the gold string.

STATE PROBLEM (no writer screen): REGFIT exact at most 20% and MLP exact at most 20%, and reach_GEN minus its different-row null at most 10 points. This says the registers do not linearly carry the gold. It does not say whether the thinker or the reader is at fault.

CHOOSER FAULT: the share of all in_dist misses that are N or C rows (decoded mode differs from gold mode) is at least 30%. The chooser hypothesis is dead at 10% or below. Measured from decoded mode and gold mode directly, not from reach_NUM or reach_WORD (see depends_on).

ERROR ROUTING for wrong GEN-decoded rows, first match wins in this order: reversed (output equals gold reversed) at least 10%, or copy-source (output and gold both prompt substrings) at least 40%, goes to the copy-chain idea; length-only (edit distance equals the absolute length difference) at least 25% goes to the feedback ladder; off-prompt (edit distance at least 2 and not a prompt substring) at least 50%, together with REGFIT at most 20%, closes the writer line. All thresholds are suggested and fixed before the run.

REGISTER-ONLY SWAP (descriptive, not a gate): at least 50% of same-family GEN pairs have output equal to the donor's gold, reported by gate stratum. There is no 2x ratio against the pointer swap, because pointers are read only in NUM and WORD modes (ledger.py:380-406), so the pointer swap cannot move a GEN-decoded row.

PRIOR, stated before the run, not a mark: fewshot_number_rule W rows predicted at most 20%. Shown reason: its full-donor carry is 80.7 (donor match 27.9 against intact 34.6, six seeds, RESULT.json), so the output tracks the state and a wrong state is the likely cause. A fewshot REGFIT at or above 60% would contradict this and point at the tied readout, which is the untie gate. The table_lookup prior is open: its full-donor match is 3.8 (intact 28.7, carry 13.0), but 31% of its gold rows are WORD, so only the register-only arm can speak to it.
Everything else is 'not shown'. Fixed next step: one pre-registered refit with twice the TRAIN rows and the same recipe, with no tuning.
plan.proved_wrong: The writer hypothesis (B2's misses are register or writer faults) is proved wrong if, on vocab-path W rows with controls passing, REGFIT exact is at most 20%, the MLP is at most 20%, and reach_GEN minus its null is at most 10 points. That means the gold is in neither the registers nor the top-5 vocabulary path, so the thinker state is the bottleneck and writer ideas are dead. The chooser hypothesis is proved wrong if N and C rows are at most 10% of all in_dist misses. The probe is void, not proved wrong, if the harness, sanity or controls fail.
plan.null_risk: Yes, the marks could pass with no real change, at moderate risk (suggested). (a) A readout can learn each family's answer prior: families with few answers (yes/no, small integers) can reach 60% without reading the registers. Guarded by the prior floor (+20 points) and by the label-shuffled and loops:0 controls. (b) Six seeds share one 1,360-row dev set, so the pooled numbers come from fewer unique rows than 6 x 60; guarded by the bootstrap over dev rows and the 60-row minimum. (c) The free head is fit on TRAIN rows that B2 trained on, so their registers may be cleaner than the registers of rows B2 gets wrong (suggested). The donor control partly guards this; if REGFIT passes, a cross-fit on dev rows B2 gets right (folds stratified by family, scored on W rows) is the robustness check before any writer build. (d) The harness can pass trivially if the probe calls talk() itself, so the probe must compute its own copy path. The 60 and 20 thresholds are far apart, so a chance pass after prior-floor subtraction is unlikely.
plan.autonomy: Research only. The probe reads frozen checkpoints and changes nothing in the deployed model. It adds no parameters and no runtime step. Its gold labels, the 2x2 mode split, the error classes and every threshold are research-only and must never become a runtime gate (rule 10). PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md line 100 lists tests, scoring and pass marks as ours, so Ben should confirm that exemption before sealing. Any writer or chooser build picked from this must keep its runtime method self-run: the model checks its own registers with a learned head or with an outside tool it chooses to call, using no answer key. A REGFIT-fitted untied readout would be a trained parameter, fixed before shipping, which is not a deploy-time step. It costs +27,648 params (108 x 256; +0.84% of B2's 3,302,481), and B2-untied would be 3,330,129, which is +2.6% over plain_tf S = 3,244,544, inside rule 3's +-3% band (shown arithmetic).
steps: Pre-run checks (done in this session, shown): ledger.py:340 snapshots only when t <= n-2, that is t=1..6, so the 7th write and the post-loop state are not captured by run(rounds=True); ledger.py:387 talk() calls gen_copy when copy=True; ledger.py:447 gold() silently cuts answers to 8 characters, so the probe must not use gold() for targets; ledger.py:351-352 run() returns X and xm when copy=True, and talk() reads the same X (ledger.py:284, 386); all six checkpoint sha256 files match; seed 200 in_dist over 1,360 rows: exact 90.51, nocopy 78.97, loops:0 0.00, donor exact 3.24, donor match 58.24. In_dist misses per seed are 115 to 141 (mean 128.8). Shown: table_lookup and fewshot_number_rule hold 328 of 773 six-seed in_dist misses (42.4%). Suggested and approximate: about 68 gold-GEN misses per seed, about 65% of them in those two families. Rule 5: only TRAIN and the dev in_dist rows are touched; no protected panel.

Seal the spec before any run: the marks above, the row sets (1,360 final-eval in_dist as primary; the 6,800-row big-root in_dist only as a family-level power check), the REGFIT recipe, the controls, and the priors. Ben confirms the rule-10 exemption for research probes.

Edit diag_ledger.py:21 to use gen_copy. Write diag_talker.py as a hooked copy of run() that records registers after each write (t=1..7) and checks bit-for-bit that the post-loop state equals the t=7 record (they are the same state, not separate snapshots). Apply ln_t to the raw registers (ledger.py:341 stores raw Z).
Harness on seeds 200-201, then 202-205: copy-path and vocab-path strings against talk(return_modes=True). Void on any mismatch.

Build the 2x2 mode table and the W, C and N sets on the 1,360 rows. Gold mode comes from progparse.row_targets, the same rule gold() uses. Decoded mode comes from talk(return_modes=True). Exclude and count any dev row whose gold answer is over 8 characters (rule 7; the T1 fact-check reports none, untested here).

Stage 1 on W rows (seeds 200-201 first): per-register gold-character ranks under the copy mixture and the vocab path, reach_GEN and its different-row null, gate strata, error classes in the stated first-match order, and per-register P(EOS at gold length).

Stage 2 REGFIT on all six seeds: the first 10,000 TRAIN gold-GEN rows with answers up to 8 characters (count and skipped count reported; raw answers only, never gold()). One shared head, multinomial cross-entropy, fixed L2, fixed full-batch epochs, with 10% of train held out for convergence only. Controls and the MLP class as in arms. Optional robustness (suggested): cross-fit on dev rows B2 gets right, scored on W rows.

Stage 3 swaps: register-only swap uses the donor's R with the current row's vals, valid, lmode, lans and lword, passed to talk() with the current batch; report by gate stratum. The pointer-only swap is reported on NUM/WORD pairs only.
Stage 4, only if Stage 2 or Stage 3 gives a register signal: per-round REGFIT on the t=1..7 records with the same recipe.
Apply the decision table and write the result to a new results folder. No checkpoint, ledger.py or train.py write.
files_to_touch: reader/custom_io/diag_ledger.py (line 21 only: readout(R) becomes gen_copy(R, X, xm, prompt_ids); run() already returns X and xm when copy=True, ledger.py:351-352)
reader/custom_io/diag_talker.py (new, read-only; a hooked copy of run() that mirrors ledger.py:278-356 without editing it)
reader/custom_io/results/41-talker-d1/ (new results folder for the sealed run)
Read-only references: reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py, models/progparse.py:186-208, evalx.py:93-125, results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200..B2_s205/RESULT.json, scratchpad code/b2ckpt checkpoints
Not touched: models/ledger.py, any checkpoint, train.py
plan.depends_on: Prerequisites: (1) Ben's ruling that research probes (scoring and marks) are exempt under rule 10 (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md line 100 lists them as ours); (2) the PC with CUSTOM_IO_DATA and the sk200k data root; (3) nothing from T1, EGE or the calculator work. Corrections to the draft, all checked in the files: (a) reach_NUM and reach_WORD are true by construction on gold-mode rows (progparse.py:196-208 assigns mode 0 when the gold equals a slot value and mode 1 when it equals a prompt word, compared case-insensitively), so the chooser test uses the 2x2 mode table instead; (b) the pointer-only swap cannot change a GEN-decoded row (talk() reads pointers only in NUM and WORD modes, ledger.py:380-406), so the 2x ratio rule is dropped; (c) the 'post-loop plus t=1..7' list double counts, since the post-loop state equals the t=7 record; (d) donor_match and exact in RESULT.json are percentages, not counts (the donor-carry ratios here weight them by n); (e) per-register heads would add 248,832 params (+7.5%), outside rule 3, so the primary head is shared. T1 is not a baseline here: it is a different model (no NUM mode), its screen was NOT SHOWN (write_copy S3 FAIL, architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md), and it ran on two rented RTX 5090s, which rule 6 must clear before T1 counts as a baseline.
plan.confirm: If the screen (harness, 2x2 mode table and Stage 1 on seeds 200-201) gives a clear branch with controls passing, the six-seed confirm is the full run on seeds 200-205 with the bootstrap intervals above, and it is the only routing run. The build that follows is a separate spec with its own runs. If registers hold the answer: a shared untied readout (+27,648 params, +0.84%), B2-untied against B2-tied on six paired seeds (rule 4). If the state is the problem: the thinker-side ideas (W2 scratch tokens, H1 stop), each on its own two-seed screen and six-seed confirm. If chooser fault: the mode chooser, on the same pattern. The probe claims none of these builds.

issues: Sanity check has the gate backwards (shown). The plan says 'REGFIT exact on dev rows B2 gets right with mean gate below 0.2'. In gen_copy the vocab path is weighted by the gate: ledger.py:249 returns gate * p_vocab + (1 - gate) * p_copy, and copy_gate_eval reads 1 - gate as copy share (ledger.py:658-660). A gate below 0.2 selects copy-dominated rows, where a register-only head should fail for reasons unrelated to probe validity. Use gate at least 0.8 (copy share at most 0.2).

'Vocab-path W rows' is undefined, and REGFIT reads only ln_t(R) so it ignores the copy mixture (shown). Copy matters for fewshot_number_rule: forcing the gate to 1 lowers its in_dist exact from 34.6% (intact, six seeds) to 25.8% (RESULT.json lesions.nocopy), although its mean copy share is only 4.6% (extra.copy_gate, seed 200). Gold characters supplied by the copy path will look like register failures and bias the result toward the STATE branch. Define W on the copy-path decode, report copy-supplied rows separately, and say which rows the primary covers.

The 2x2 mode table has no fourth cell. Only gold GEN/decoded GEN, gold NUM-or-WORD/decoded GEN and gold GEN/decoded NUM-or-WORD are listed. Gold NUM or WORD decoded NUM or WORD, wrong (slot or word pointer faults) is never classified, so N plus C does not partition the misses, and the chooser band from 10% to 30% is unassigned.

The N cell mixes chooser errors with value errors (shown from progparse.py:188-209). An integer answer is gold NUM only if it equals a slot value and the row has a program or the number is in the prompt. An integer no slot holds is labelled gold GEN, so B2 printing a wrong slot value is counted as a chooser fault. Also, rows with more than 7 steps lose their program (progparse.py:199) but keep integer answers as gold GEN, so gold-GEN sets include answers no program can reach. fewshot_number_rule is 0% program and 96% gold GEN in dev coverage (extra.coverage, seed 200), so this hits the primary family directly.

Undefined terms that the decision depends on. reach_GEN and its 'different-row null' appear nowhere in the code or project files (grep, shown). 'Top-5 vocabulary path' is undefined. 'Exact' over nine registers is ambiguous: vocab.decode stops at the first EOS (data.py:60-68) and gold() fills only up to EOS, leaving later registers at -100 (never trained). The plan must say exact means decode-to-EOS equals the gold string. Also missing: MLP settings, the Stage 4 'signal' gate, and the bootstrap method (it must resample dev rows with all six seeds' outcomes kept together).

Decision table gaps. REGFIT between 20% and 60%, or MLP between 20% and 60%, matches no branch ('everything else is not shown'), and the chooser band from 10% to 30% is unassigned. The error classes are first-match but overlap, so the first match hides the rest.

proved_wrong overreaches and contradicts the STATE branch. It concludes 'the thinker state is the bottleneck and writer ideas are dead' from the 9 final registers alone. Registers are only part of the state: controls 2-7 are used (zeroing them costs -1.6 pooled-5 and -7.8 chain-5, shown in redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 5b), and the workspace is not probed. The STATE branch itself says the probe does not show whether the thinker or the reader is at fault. The writer-is-dead conclusion only follows for writers that read registers alone.

Structural gap the plan does not mention (shown from code). The seventh program write happens in the last iteration (N_RES = 7, ledger.py:319). The controller blocks read S before each write (ledger.py:309), so the 9 GEN registers never see result 7. Only the post-loop answer pointer does (ledger.py:343 uses cat[S0, Rs]). Gold NUM rows whose answer is result 7 cannot be carried by the GEN registers. Report them separately, or the STATE branch will blame the thinker for a gap in the design. The T1 fact check reports the same gap for T1 (untested here).

Sample size is unknown and may void the probe. The primary rests mostly on fewshot_number_rule and table_lookup: 157 and 171 of the 773 six-seed in_dist misses, 328 together or 42.4% (shown from RESULT.json). Each family has 40 in_dist rows per seed, so unique W rows across six seeds are probably far fewer than six times the per-seed count (suggested). No PREDS.json exists in the container (shown), so the unique count cannot be read off the files. It must be measured in Stage 0. The 60-row void mark and the 60% pooled mark both depend on it, and two families limit what the primary can say about B2 generally.

The Stage 2 training sample is picked by file order ('first 10,000 TRAIN gold-GEN rows'), which can cluster by family. Use a seeded sample stratified by family, report per-family counts, and report no-program integer rows as a separate fit.

The head spec is incomplete. Registers differ per checkpoint, so there must be six heads, one per seed, not one shared head pooled across seeds. L2, epochs and learning rate are not given; they must be sealed before any run, or they become tuning on dev W rows. The MLP needs its held-out score reported, because it can memorise train registers.

The loops:0 control is degenerate (shown from ledger.py:303-304: at loops 0 the registers are the place-table rows, identical for every row). It reduces to a global constant, which the per-family prior already covers. Keep it as a floor or drop it.

The Stage 3 register-only swap threshold ('at least 50% of pairs output the donor's gold') measures dependence on registers, not correctness. The donor lesion already gives the fewshot carry: donor match 27.9% against intact 34.6%, carry 80.7% over six seeds (RESULT.json, shown). Make Stage 3 descriptive or drop it.

Cheaper evidence already in the files is not used. RESULT.json lesions.loops:16 gives mean in_dist 89.07 against 90.53 intact over six seeds, with fewshot 26.2 against 34.6 and table_lookup 27.9 against 28.8 (shown). loops:1 and loops:2 give fewshot 2.9 and 6.7. More rounds do not rescue the two families, and the plan should cite this. probe_loops.py (design/LOOPS-probe.md) already runs per-K in_dist on CPU and covers Stage 4's loop curve.

diag_ledger.py already writes per-row modes and a GEN column. Changing line 21 needs more than one line: gen_copy needs o['X'] and o['xm'] from run() (returned when copy=True, ledger.py:352) and batch['prompt_ids']. Stage 0 should use this existing tool before writing diag_talker.py, which is cheaper. The harness check (copy path equals talk) passes by construction because both call gen_copy (ledger.py:387). It is a consistency check, not an independent one.

Hours are underestimated. The 2-hour figure does not cover copying sk200k from the PC (absent in this container, shown), installing torch (absent here, shown), writing and bit-checking a hooked run(), about 70,000 CPU forward passes across six seeds plus donor and swap passes, the head fits, a clustered bootstrap and the conditional Stage 4. Suggested: about 5 hours of work, excluding queue wait. For scale, B2 seed 200 trained for 13,160 s on GPU (shown). CPU forward speed is untested.

Machine and schedule. The PC is queued for days: EGE q39 runs until about 9 PM to midnight ET, then 8a's 3M rung (about 9 hours), 10M (about a day) and 30M (4 to 5 days) (whole-model-roadmap addendum C, shown). A CPU probe on the PC will compete with the queue. Rule 6 makes the M1 Pro a first-line machine: use it if torch is installed there (untested), or schedule the PC job after the 8a 3M rung.

The rule-10 exemption is a disclosed reading, not Ben's ruling (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md line 8 and line 100, shown). It must be confirmed before sealing. Any build that follows (untied readout, learned mode or stop) must run inside the deployed model with no answer key.

Scope and rule 4. 8a addendum G changes B2 to 12 rounds, 36 answer registers and 106 slots (whole-model-roadmap section 8a, shown). This probe is about the 8-round, 9-register B2 only, so the findings may not transfer to the 8a model. The untied build is a second change on top of 8a and must be its own one-change test.

Rule 7 exclusions. Dropping gold answers over 8 characters from W and from training is a selection, not truncation, but it changes the population. Report them as a separate cap-limited class. The T1 fact check reports no pooled-5 answer over 8 characters (not re-run here, untested).

The '6,800-row big-root in_dist' label is not supported. RESULT.json extra.n_dev is 6,800, and coverage shows 200 rows per family across 34 families, while in_dist is 1,360 rows at 40 per family (shown). Name the root and its counts.
The CPU fp32 reference is compared with RESULT numbers from a bf16 GPU eval (config.bf16 true, shown). The 1.0-point tolerance is suggested, not measured.
Stage 4 needs seven per-round fits, and the 'same recipe' is not specified. Gate it on a pre-named Stage 2 pass and reuse probe_loops.py where possible.

Multiple looks at one dev set. Stages 0 to 4, plus the pre-named refit with twice the TRAIN rows, are a sequence of decisions on the same 1,360 in_dist rows. Treat them as one pre-registered sequence with a fixed budget.

Brief correction: T1 has run. architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md shows two rented RTX 5090s, seeds 200 and 201, and write_copy S3 FAIL (shown). The brief's 'sealed, not run' is stale; the plan's note that T1 is not a baseline is correct.

Checked and holding (shown): seed 200 in_dist 90.51 (1,231 of 1,360), nocopy 78.97, loops:0 0.00, donor exact 3.24 and donor match 58.24; 328 of 773 misses (42.4%); fewshot carry 27.9 / 34.6 = 80.7%; diag_ledger.py:21 uses model.readout; ledger.py:340 snapshots only for t 1 to 6; gold() cuts answers at 8 characters (ledger.py:447); the six B2 checkpoint sha256 files match; untied readout +27,648 (0.84% of B2), B2-untied 3,330,129 (+2.6% over plain_tf S, inside the 3% band), per-register heads +248,832 (+7.5%).

fixed_plan.title: D1 (fixed): read-only register and answer-choice probe on the six saved B2 checkpoints
fixed_plan.ben_line: We look inside B2's saved model to see why it gets some answers wrong. Is the right answer still in its final memory slots, is it picking the wrong kind of answer, or was it never there? We only read the saved models on a regular computer and change nothing in them.
fixed_plan.question: On seeds 200-205, for in_dist rows where B2 is wrong and the gold answer is at most 8 characters: (a) can a fixed head read the gold answer from the 9 final GEN registers, scored through the copy mixture, against controls; (b) how much of the miss is answer-kind choice (NUM/WORD vs GEN) and how much is value or writer error; (c) is the state or the writer the limit? Labels: shown = RESULT.json or code line checked; suggested = reasoned; untested = not run.

The chooser hypothesis is wrong if N plus C is at most 10% of in_dist misses. Rows whose gold is result 7, or an integer that no slot or prompt number holds, are reported separately and count toward neither.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Moderate (suggested). (a) Family priors: fewshot and table_lookup answers repeat; guarded by the per-family majority prior and the label-shuffled control. (c) The head is fit on TRAIN registers that B2 was trained to fit, so registers on W rows may be off-distribution; this biases toward STATE; guarded by the donor and label-shuffled controls and the cross-fit check. (d) Copy-supplied characters look like register failures; handled by scoring on the copy mixture and reporting copy-prompt-copyable rows separately. (e) The MLP can memorise train registers; check on the held-out split and report it. (f) The harness check passes by construction, so it is a code-consistency check only.

idea.title: Sentence scoring kit: slot referee, chance floor, thinker-decision table
idea.summary: No sentence answer can be scored today (english.score is set membership on exact strings), and the planned leak mark (donor state at most 10%) is below the question-only chance level on two of the four English sets. Build a hand-written slot checker validated on planted right and wrong sentences, set the leak mark per set from a question-only floor, and score every sentence against the thinker's own decision, not the gold answer. CPU only.
idea.change: (a) slot_pass(sentence,row): recall = every gold slot present as a whole-word run (canonical or accepted answer, or yes/no polarity words); extra = a passage name or number that is not a gold slot appears. Validate on 150 planted wrong-slot sentences (gold swapped for the passage's other candidate, at least 3 frames) and 100 planted correct-slot sentences in frames the scorer code never saw; Ben hand-checks 30; regression: on the 768 bare-answer rows of the four English sets slot_pass must agree with exact match on every row. (b) Chance floor per set = best of three fixed question-only rules (constant No on yes/no rows, first capitalised passage name, last capitalised passage name). Leak mark becomes: donor-state score <= floor+3 on the 6-seed mean and <= floor+6 on every seed, per set. A trained zero-state control is reported only as a diagnostic. (c) Thinker-decision table: D = B2's own predicted answer (re-scored from the saved checkpoints since predictions were not saved); fidelity = slot_pass(talker sentence, D); report a 2x2 of thinker right/wrong (against gold, scoring only) by fidelity yes/no; talker-caused error = thinker right and fidelity 0. Donor arm: fidelity against the donor's decision. For the later sentence talker (idea 3).
idea.why: Computed floors are 6.0% on the unseen pair (23/384), 16.7% on FRESH-EN-R3 (32/192), 15.1% on GEN-HELDOUT-R4 (29/192) and 10.9% pooled, so a fixed 10% donor mark is below chance on two sets and a non-leaking talker can fail it. B2's loops:0 leak over seeds 200-205 is 0.00, 10.81, 0.00, 5.66, 3.53, 0.00 (mean 3.33, SD 4.35, 6-seed half-width 4.6), too noisy for a 3-point mean mark, hence the per-seed maximum rule. B2 is right on only about 90.5% of in_dist, so about 129 rows per seed are thinker errors that no talker can fix and must not be charged to the talker.

evidence.claim: english.score() passes only if en_norm(output) equals a normalised accepted answer; there is no sentence scorer. The four English sets give 768 rows (686 short-answer, 82 yes/no); 74 rows have a capitalised passage name as the answer with 2.14 candidate names on average.

test.pass_mark: Fixed before building: false pass <=2% (<=3 of 150); false fail <=3% (<=3 of 100; Ben's 30 hand checks agree on >=28); 100% agreement with exact match on bare-answer rows; the floor+3 ceiling passes the state-ignoring heuristic on unseen rows (6.0 <= 9.0) and fails shuffled-core allptr (73.2 > 9.0). Later, for the sentence talker: talker-caused error <=3% of in-family rows, fidelity to D >=97% on thinker-right in-family rows and >=90% on unseen-kind rows, donor arm carries donor's decision >=90%.
test.proved_wrong: Referee unusable if >=5% of planted wrong-slot sentences pass, or >=5% of correct ones fail, or any bare-row disagreement. Mark unusable if it passes the shuffled-core allptr (73.2% vs a 9.0 ceiling). Translator premise fails if fidelity to D is below 80% on in-family thinker-right rows.

problems: [shown] The core reason for replacing the 10% donor mark is wrong. The idea says a non-leaking talker can fail 10%. But the English donor arm pairs donors with judged_pairs (english.py:139, used at english.py:276-283), which drops any donor whose canonical answer is in row i's accepted set. evalx.donor_pairs does the same (evalx.py:75-79: 'a donor-answer hit can never also be an exact hit'). So a state-following talker scores about 0 on exact by construction. Even with unrestricted same-family donors, my recount from english_eval/*.json gives donor-answer collision with the current gold of 3.8-7.9% (same family) and 0.9-1.7% (all pairs), both under 10%. The 'below chance' argument uses the question-only floor, which is the wrong null for a state-follower.

[shown by recount; the floor code is not in the container] The floors do not reproduce. A plain reading of the three named rules (constant No on yes/no rows; first or last capitalised non-initial passage word) gives FRESH 9.4% (18/192), NEW-KINDS-R5 6.2% (12/192), NEW-KINDS2-R6 5.2% (10/192), GEN-HELDOUT 8.9% (17/192), pooled 6.0% (46/768). The idea reports 16.7, 6.0 (for the pair; I get 22/384 = 5.7%), 15.1 and 10.9 pooled. A per-row union of the three rules reaches 22.9% on FRESH, but that uses the gold answer, so it is not a question-only floor. On the plain reading the 10% mark sits 0.6-1.1 points above the FRESH and GEN floors, not below them. grep found no w1g-2 code in the container. The 'below chance on two sets' claim depends on an extractor the idea does not state.

[suggested] Replacing the 10% mark with floor+3 (mean) and floor+6 (each seed) loosens the gate. With the idea's FRESH floor that is a 19.7 / 22.7 ceiling; with my floor it is 12.4 / 15.4. The floor is a heuristic, which the idea itself calls a lower bound on a trained question-only reader, and the trained zero-state control is demoted to a diagnostic. A question-reading talker that beats the heuristic floor by more than 6 points would pass. The shuffled-core allptr (73.2%, RESULTS-CT.md:29-31) would be caught, but weaker leaks are not bounded. B1-b already uses donor <= 10% on new kinds (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:422, sealed in PR #41 addendum 3), so changing that mark's meaning conflicts with a sealed test.

[suggested, untested] The slot rules would reject correct sentences. The 'extra' rule fails any sentence with a passage name or number that is not a gold slot. A correct contrastive sentence ('not Tom, Ann') or a restatement ('Dax tossed the plum to Hale', gold Dax) fails. The spec does not require negated, contrastive or restating frames among the 100 correct planted sentences, though the orchestrator note asks for negation scope. Number handling is unspecified: 41 of 384 gold questions have number-word answers (my count from english_eval/*.json), and the spec does not say how 'two' and '2' match or whether a passage number in a correct sentence counts as an extra.

[suggested, statistics] The pass marks are observed rates, not bounds. 3 false passes in 150 is 2%, but the 95% exact (Garwood) upper bound for 3 events is about 5.8%. 3 false fails in 100 has an upper bound of about 8.8%. The pass band (<=2%, <=3%) and the kill band (>=5%, i.e. 8 of 150 or 5 of 100) leave 4-7 of 150 and 4 of 100 with no verdict. Ben's 30 hand-checks agreeing on >=28 allows 2 of 30 disagreements (6.7%), above the 3% false-fail limit the check is meant to confirm.

[shown from the spec] The regression tests the wrong thing. The 768 bare-answer rows contain no sentences, so they test that the referee accepts gold strings, not that it handles sentence wording. The decisive use is stage 4b on B2's exact answers (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:429), where NUM answers are 42% of B2 dev rows (brief, from results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json extra.coverage). Digits, separators and computed results are absent from the English sets, so the referee is validated on a different answer domain from the one it would gate.

[shown] Legality of the planted sentences is unresolved and blocks steps (a) and (b). Roadmap line 190 says 'No Claude-written or Claude-judged text' and line 502 (the web-text ruling) says 'No Claude-written text' without a training qualifier. The idea's 250 planted sentences are Claude-written. The idea lists this as open for Ben, but as written it cannot be built before a ruling.

[shown + suggested] Row population and rule 9. The thinker-decision table uses 'B2's own predicted answer' on rows the idea never names. B2 is trained on skill questions (family split 1.6%, RESULT.json), and the English sets belong to the 1.2B line. Evaluating B2 on English rows would leave the 'thinker right' cells nearly empty; evaluating on skill rows puts the referee on a domain it was not validated on. The idea also borrows B2's loops:0 variance (in_dist, seeds 200-205) to set the English-line per-seed rule, mixing two lines that rule 9 keeps apart. Re-scoring B2 needs the sk200k data root, which the container lacks (director summary), so this runs on Ben's PC, not as a container job.

[shown] Vague terms. 'Passage name' (capitalisation rule; sentence-initial words), 'yes/no polarity words', 'whole-word run' (punctuation, case, number words), 'frames the scorer never saw' (no frame list; 'at least 3 frames' not named), 'per set' floors (the 6.0% is a pair figure; NEW-KINDS-R5 and R6 separately are not given), and 'in-family' vs 'unseen-kind' rows in the 2x2. The '74 rows with a capitalised passage name as answer' figure cannot be reproduced without the extractor; a plain count of capitalised short answers gives 46 questions (92 rows over two panels).

[shown] Rule checks. Pass: R1 (scoring and floors are test code), R2 (no teacher), R7 (no cap), R10 (test only, nothing at deploy). R5 holds (the English sets are not protected, though earlier runs read them, as the idea says). Rule 4 is strained: the stage 4b and 9 marks (roadmap:429, 441) are proposed, not sealed, so changing them is allowed only as an explicit revision, but B1-b is already sealed at 10% (roadmap:422).
critiques.rescue: Revise, do not run as written. (1) Keep the slot referee and its regression, but freeze the matcher text first: number-word and digit equivalence; a passage name is not an extra if it sits in a negation or contrast clause ('not', 'rather than', 'instead of'); write the 100 correct planted sentences with contrast and restatement frames. Use exact binomial upper bounds, close the verdict gap with one band per threshold, and require Ben's 30 hand-checks to agree 30/30 or revise the referee. (2) Drop the floor-based leak mark. Keep the existing judged-pair donor arm with its 10% absolute ceiling (chance is about 0 there by construction), measure state-following with donor_match plus slot fidelity to the donor's answer, and set any question-only ceiling from a trained zero-state control of the same size.
