critiques.expected_effect: Revised as above, the screen would say whether a closed-gate reader on B2's frozen state follows the state for state-written non-digit answers: the gate opens and donor-follow reaches the recomputed slice baseline minus 3. It would say nothing about digits until the probe passes, about open English (the frames are templates), about T1 states, or about deploy autonomy. As written, the screen would give an uninterpretable result: either the gated slice cannot reach the bar, or the bar passes trivially on a near-zero baseline. Chance passing of the donor-follow metric is low once the baseline is fixed, because constant predictors score only on the few binary families (about 6% of rows, suggested). The design's strongest parts are the zero-state arm, the gate-off arm and the explicit proved-wrong clauses, and these should be kept.

chair.reasons:
Verdict: plan, but only as a heavily narrowed two-step screen. As written the idea is not testable and would give an uninterpretable result. Four problems stand even after discounting the Haiku critics. I checked each in code or result files this session.

(1) Wrong donor baseline [shown]. Ledger.state() (ledger.py:359-362) returns (R, vals, valid, lmode, lans, lword). R is only the 9 registers (ledger.py:344, R=Z[:, N_CTRL:]). The 8 control vectors are never returned, so the "17 vectors" and the P10 arm need a hooked copy of run(). donor_eval (evalx.py) swaps the whole tuple, so the exact int64 vals and the pointer logits move too. I split B2's saved by-family donor results on seeds 200 and 201 by family NUM share (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s*/RESULT.json, lesions.donor.in_dist.by_family joined to extra.coverage.by_family). Families with NUM share of 50% or more (600 of 1,360 rows) score donor_match 93.7 and 93.8. All other families (760 rows) score 30.3 and 30.7. Copy_word, table_lookup and cipher_map score 0 by design, because the donor's word is not in the current prompt. So the 57-59 headline is mostly the vals channel, which a 17-vector read excludes. Pass mark (i), at least 54.1 and 55.3, would fail on the NUM rows by construction. On the non-NUM slice it sits about 25 points above B2's own value. The zero-state control zeroes the whole tuple (models/base.py:55-57), so its 0.0 does not show that the vectors carry the answer.

(2) Frames [shown/unruled]. About 40 frames per kind need an author. The roadmap bars Claude-written training text (lines 190, 358, 502). Ben's frame ruling is not in any file. Frames built from gold steps also contradict B2's own answer on its 8.5-10.4% of in_dist misses (89.6-91.5 exact, shown). A 5-step frame is 80 to 111+ characters, which does not fit the 64-position table without a cut (rule 7). Talker120 (313 of 500 unfaithful) was the same method class and is missing from closest_prior.

(3) Rule 10 [shown]. The frozen thinker runs the exact executor inside the forward pass (ledger.py:76-86, called at :333), the hand place code, the regex spans and the fixed 8 rounds. T1 and H1 replace these. A pass on B2's state therefore says nothing about the deployed interface until it is re-run on T1's state. The talker's own path is autonomous: learned reads, learned gate, learned EOS, left-to-right characters, no str(), reversal or slicing. B2's talk() text is used only to build training targets before ship, which is allowed.

(4) Mark defects [shown from idea text]. Pass (ii)/(iii) set the bound max(5, C+1) with C taken from a trained arm, so it is not fixed in advance and exceeds the project limit of 5. The P10-below-P17 "proved wrong" clause is inverted, because it supports reading all 17. The gate-value mark |tanh g| >= 0.1 is weak, since a gate can open on useless slots. There is no sentence-to-answer scorer. The 5 hours is not derived. The copy-talker claim overstates: the core-real check is NOT SHOWN (+0.7, CI -2.0 to +3.4), not "unused".

Why not cut. Everything that breaks a rule is fixable. The idea's core is the only concrete stand-in for the missing stage 4b on B2's card line (suggested): a left-to-right gated decoder on B2's frozen registers, with zero-state and gate-off controls and explicit kill clauses. It also fixes B2's real structural gap, that each of its 9 registers takes an independent argmax (ledger.py:387-390, shown). Zero B2 answers are over 8 or 32 characters in pooled-5 or train (T1 fact check (e), shown), so an answer-string-only target needs no cut. Dropping the frames from step A removes the frame-authorship ruling, the gold-step contradiction, the 64-position conflict and the sentence-extractor problem. Frames and English then wait for Ben's ruling. Cost is low: sequences of 9 or fewer characters, about 2 PC-hours for step A (untested estimate). A check is not needed. The decision hinges on judgment, and I verified the hinge facts above.

Overlap for Opus: merge with Sonnet-director idea 3 (frozen-B2 sentence talker screen) and gate it behind idea 1 (probe suite). The probe answers in minutes whether the registers and controls hold the answer string, and whether NUM digits are in the vectors at all (untested). Expected value: moderate for the talker area. A pass shows only in-dist state-following on B2's current interface. It does not show English, unseen kinds or deploy autonomy.
chair.revised_idea:
talker-D3 revised. Test: does a small left-to-right decoder that sees B2's frozen thinker state only through gates that start closed write B2's own decided answer, and does it follow the state when the state is swapped? This is a screen only. Any claim needs 6 paired seeds (200-205). Build-time label: deploy-blocked on the B2 interface, re-run on T1 state before it counts.

ORDER AND GATES
0. Run idea 1 (CPU probe suite) first. Checkpoints for seeds 100/101 are on the PC (checkpoints/29-b2-screen); 200-205 are copied here. Fixed gate: a linear or small-MLP probe on the 17 final vectors (Z[:, :8] controls plus R, 9 registers) recovers B2's talk() string exactly on at least 90% of held-out GEN and WORD rows. If not, stop. The decoder cannot read what the vectors lack. NUM digits stay ungated until the probe or the T1 write_copy check (at least 99.0) passes.
1. Step A, no frames. Needs no Ben ruling on frame authorship.
2. Step B, frames and English. Starts only after Ben rules on frame authorship. Options: Ben writes the frames, or use skeletons already in the project's own English generator; never Claude-drafted frames unless Ben allows it.

STATE (named tensors)
Hook a copy of run() to return Z[:, 0:8] (controls) and Z[:, 8:17] (registers) after the last round. Exclude vals, valid, lmode, lans, lword and the executor outputs. The zero-state arm zeroes only these 17 vectors.

MODEL (shapes from the original idea)
Two causal blocks, width 256, MLP ratio 2. Readout tied to the reader's character table. Copy head with the query from the talker's hidden state over the current prompt's characters. Each block gets a gated cross-attention to the 17 vectors (Q,K,V 256 to 64, O 64 to 256), multiplied by tanh(g) with g starting at 0. Positions: a fixed design-constant table, at least 64 for step A. Step B needs at least 111 for the longest 3-4 digit chain frame, so recompute params and the +-3% band from the table actually built. Decoding stops on a learned EOS, with a fixed safety cap that is the same on every run and every night. Log the cap hit rate; it should be at most 1% of rows.

DATA
Fresh generator draws (new seed, not in B2's 200k train file), in_dist only for training. Target = B2's own talk() string for the row, placed in no frame (step A). Assert zero cut targets and report how many rows were kept, so there is no silent skip. No row filter. Step B frames use equations from B2's own executed program (run() returns prog and vals), never gold steps. Rows with no program get a no-step frame, not a skip.

ARMS
G17 (gated read of 17); G0 (a separately trained arm with gates forced 0, the state-blind floor); zero-state eval of G17; donor eval of G17 using evalx.donor_pairs seed 0 and the same pairs as B2's saved donor result. Rerun B2's donor_eval with return_preds=True on seeds 100/101 so B2's baseline is computed per row on exactly the same rows as the talker. The q33 result folders keep only by-family numbers.

SLICES (defined before the run, by B2's own decoded mode on the row, from talk(return_modes=True))
S1 = rows B2 answers in GEN or WORD mode. Report S1 split by copy share (1 - gate) below and at or above 0.5. NUM rows are reported separately and are not gated. Copy-heavy families (copy_word, table_lookup, cipher_map) are reported but donor-follow on them is capped near 0 by design, and B2 has the same cap.

PASS MARKS (fixed now; both seeds 100 and 101)
(i) G17 donor-follow on S1 >= B2's donor-follow on the same S1 rows minus 3.
(ii) G17 donor-follow minus G0 donor-follow >= 10 on S1. This shows the state is used. For reference, B2's by-family value on the non-NUM families is about 30 on seeds 200/201 (shown).
(iii) Own-answer exact under the donor state on S1 <= 5.
(iv) Zero-state exact on non-copy S1 <= 5, the project leak limit, not max(5, C+1). Report G0's value and the best constant answer's rate as context, not as the bound.
(v) Flip rate (G17 text differs from B2's own decided answer on intact in_dist S1 rows) <= 2 percent of rows.
The gate value |tanh g| is reported as a diagnostic only. It is not a mark.
Follow-up P10 vs P17 (control 1 plus the 9 registers, via one 256-to-256 projection plus LayerNorm, vs all 17): same marks, one change at a time.
Per-slot patching audit: 17 single-slot swaps, the 10 readout slots, all 17. Reported, not gated, until step A passes.

PROVED WRONG
G17 donor-follow on S1 below B2's S1 value minus 10 on either seed; or G17 minus G0 under 3 (it ignores the state); or zero-state or own-answer above 5 on non-copy S1 (it answers from its own prior, a second solver); or the step-0 probe fails. Fixed inverted clause: if P10 scores at least 5 below P17, that supports reading all 17, so it kills only the cheaper P10 read. If P10 is within 2 of P17, the scratch slots add nothing and the 10-slot read is enough.

STEP B EXTRAS
Fixed test-side sentence-to-answer extractor written before the run (the final "so the answer is X" clause), with the same donor/own/zero/flip metrics scored on the extracted answer. Add a same-size plain decoder arm (rule 3) before any beat-plain claim. Add a variant-split donor arm. Report raw output before any brake or template fallback (rule 1).

AUTONOMY (rule 10)
At deploy the talker uses only learned reads, a learned gate and a learned EOS, and writes characters left to right. Residuals, stated openly: (a) the frozen B2 thinker still runs the in-forward executor, the hand place code, regex spans and fixed 8 rounds, until T1/N1/P1/H1 replace them, so the result must be re-run on T1 state; (b) there is no learned abstain or stuck head here; (c) the talker cannot learn a new sentence shape after build (ST1/L1 area); (d) the training target generator (B2 talk() and frames) is a build-time step and is allowed, but targets must be rebuilt from gold or the T1 writer after O1 deletes the renderers.

PRIOR ART TO CITE
talker120/120b (reader/design/v3/30-modes/120-talker-mouth-finetune-prep-muse.md: 313 of 500 unfaithful raw, a hand brake supplied the passing text); exp 53 (296 of 500 unassisted); reader-talker-compare/armB/lit-talker.md section 2; copytalk RESULTS-CT.md, reworded to "core-real NOT SHOWN on unseen kinds (+0.7, CI -2.0 to +3.4)", with a large core effect on practised kinds (97.4 vs 41.6).
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right, in this order.

1. Gate on idea 1 first. A probe on the 17 final vectors (controls Z[:, :8] plus the 9 registers) must recover B2's talk() string on at least 90% of held-out GEN and WORD rows before any decoder is trained. Do not use state() as it stands: it returns only the 9 registers plus vals, valid and logits (ledger.py:359-362, shown). Use a hooked copy of run() and name the exact tensors. Zero-state and donor arms must act on those 17 vectors only, not on the tuple (models/base.py:55-57 zeroes the whole tuple).

2. Fix the donor baseline before running. B2's 57-59 donor_match is mostly the vals channel (shown here: families with NUM share of 50% or more score 93.7/93.8 on seeds 200/201; the rest score 30.3/30.7; copy_word, table_lookup and cipher_map score 0 by design). Recompute B2's donor-follow per row with return_preds=True on seeds 100/101, on the same S1 rows (B2's own decoded mode GEN or WORD) and the same pairs. The mark is "B2's value on S1 minus 3", plus G17 minus G0 of at least 10. Do not gate NUM rows.

3. Step A has no frames. Target = B2's own talk() string, with zero cut targets asserted and the row count reported. Frames and English (step B) wait for Ben's ruling on frame authorship. Equations in frames must come from B2's own executed program, never gold steps. Position table and output cap must cover the longest frame (111+ characters for 3-4 digit chains) with no cut (rule 7). Use a fixed design-constant cap with a logged hit rate of at most 1%. Do not use the generator's longest sentence.

4. Keep every mark fixed in advance. Leak limit is 5 (zero-state and own-answer on non-copy S1). Report G0 and the best constant answer as context, not as a loosened bound. Make the gate value a diagnostic only. Fix the inverted P10 clause: P10 at least 5 below P17 supports the 17-vector read. Define donor-follow for sentences with a fixed test-side extractor written before the run (step B only). Add a same-size plain decoder arm and a variant-split donor arm before any claim.

5. Label results honestly. A step-A pass shows only in-dist state-following by a sequential gated decoder on B2's current interface (executor in forward pass, so deploy-blocked, rule 10). It is a 2-seed screen. It says nothing about English, unseen kinds, digits or T1. Re-run on T1 state, then on 6 seeds (200-205), before any claim. Keep old 1.2B-line results (copytalk, 350M swap) as motivation only (rule 9). Quote copytalk's core-real check as NOT SHOWN.

6. Cost and compute. Step A is about 2 PC-hours (untested estimate: 9-character sequences, two arms, two seeds, plus the reader re-run for copy keys). State cache is about 1.7 GB in fp16 (shown arithmetic). Do not cache reader outputs (about 21 GB). Recompute the +-3% parameter band from the actual build. The original count (talker 1,104,365; gate 132,994; whole 4,539,840) reproduces for the stated layout, and the position table grows if frames need more than 64 positions.

7. Give Ben a plain-language summary. The question is whether the small writer listens to the thinker's notes or just guesses. Use the swap test: give it another question's notes and see whether it writes that question's answer. Say plainly that this does not yet test real English, only whether a writer that can speak in sentences listens to the thinker.

plan.title: Gated-read talker screen on B2's frozen state (talker-D3 step A)
plan.ben_line: We are checking whether a small writer that turns B2's answer into letters actually listens to B2's notes or just guesses. We hand it another question's notes and see whether it writes that other question's answer. This does not test real English yet; it only tests whether the writer follows the thinker.
plan.question: Does a small left-to-right letter decoder, which reads B2's frozen 17 state vectors only through gates that start closed, write B2's own decided answer, and does its output follow the state when the state is swapped for another row's?
plan.one_change: Add a gated cross-attention read of B2's 17 frozen state vectors (one tanh gate per block, starting at 0) to a small causal letter decoder. The only comparison that counts is against the same decoder with its gates held at 0 (same parameter count, no state read).
arms: G17: the decoder with the learned gated read of the 17 vectors (8 controls, 9 registers) plus a B2-style copy head over the current prompt, with its own query. Size: talker 1,104,365 + gated read 132,994 + B2 3,302,481 = 4,539,840 for the stated layout (shown arithmetic). With the copy head's own key projection and LayerNorm recounted, about 4,556,800 (suggested). Both are inside the +/-3 percent band 4,403,645-4,676,035.
G0: the identical module with tanh(g) forced to 0 at train and test. Same parameter count, no state read, trained separately on the same data and draw order. This is the size-matched floor (rule 3).
G17 zero-state eval: zero only the 17 vectors (not the whole B2 state tuple, which base.py:55-57 would zero).
G17 donor eval: donor_pairs(rows, seed 0), the same pairs as B2's saved donor result. The talker receives the donor's 17 vectors and the current row's prompt.

B2 comparator, per row, on the same rows: B2 with only the donor's 9 registers swapped in, keeping the current row's mode, executor values and pointers. This matches the channel the talker reads. The saved full-tuple donor (donor_match 57.3-59.4 on in_dist, seeds 200-205, shown) also moves the executor values and the mode, so it is reported as context only.
Step-0 probe (before any training): a linear probe on the 17 vectors for the gated rows, with no decoder.

Reported, not gated: NUM rows, WORD rows, GEN rows with copy share at or above 0.5, and the gate values |tanh g|. The P10 vs P17 comparison and the 17-slot patching audit wait until the screen passes.
plan.seeds: Screen: B2 seeds 100 and 101. Their checkpoints are on Ben's PC (custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen, as named by the code-reading agent); this container holds only their RESULT files (shown). Confirm: B2 seeds 200-205. Six checkpoint.pt files with sha256 files are in the scratchpad b2ckpt folder (shown). Training draws use a new generator seed, deduplicated against every dev row and the 200k B2 training file.
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB PC for every step. The 100/101 checkpoints and the sk200k data root are only on the PC. The state cache is 17 x 256 in fp16 for 200k rows, which is 1.74 GB (shown arithmetic). Reader outputs for copy keys are recomputed each batch, not cached (about 21 GB, suggested). The M1 Pro is optional for the step-0 probe on a 20k-row subset. Nothing in this container is run, and torch is not installed here (from the brief).
pass_marks: Changes from the panel direction, flagged. (a) The gated slice is B2 GEN rows on in_dist whose per-row copy share, taken from B2's own gate on that row, is below 0.5. WORD rows and copy-heavy GEN rows are reported, not gated. Reason: a WORD answer is copied from the current prompt (ledger.py talk(), WORD branch), so own-answer under donor is high by design and donor-follow is zero by construction; the old S1 mixed these with the state-written rows. (b) Marks (iii) and (iv) use the same slice; the panel direction had them on different slices. (c) The B2 comparator is the registers-only donor described in arms. (d) The step-0 probe reads registers and controls only, because B2's word pointer uses the prompt's word keys (ledger.py:345, shown), which the probe would not have.

Gated slice size: suggested about 300 in_dist rows per seed (GEN share x 40 rows per family, from seed 200 coverage). The table_lookup copy share on GEN registers is 0.06-0.09 across seeds 200-205 (shown), so it is not copy-heavy on GEN rows; the family label is replaced by the per-row rule. Row floor: at least 150 gated rows per seed, otherwise the run is reported as untestable and not scored. All marks are sealed before the run and not loosened after it.

Step 0 (gate to training): a linear probe on the 9 registers and 8 controls recovers B2's talk() string exactly on at least 90 percent of held-out gated rows, on both seeds. Report B2's own exact on the same rows. B2's readout is linear in the registers, so this passes whenever the registers hold the answer; it is a stop condition, not a test of the talker.

(i) Follow: G17 donor-follow on the gated slice is at least B2's registers-only donor-follow on the same rows minus 3 points, on both seeds. Family-level proxy only (not the gated baseline): B2's donor match on the 12 families with GEN copy share below 0.5 is 43-47 on seeds 200-205, computed here, but it includes NUM rows.
(ii) Use: G17 donor-follow minus G0 donor-follow is at least 10 points on the gated slice, on both seeds.
(iii) No second solver: G17 own-answer exact under the donor state is at most 5 on the gated slice, on both seeds.
(iv) No prior answer: G17 zero-state exact is at most 5 on the gated slice, on both seeds. Report G0's zero-state exact and the best constant answer's rate as context, not as bounds.
(v) Translator: flip rate (G17 output differs from B2's own decided answer on intact gated rows) is at most 2 percent, on both seeds.
Verdict: pass only if step 0 and (i) to (v) all pass on both seeds. The gate value |tanh g| is a diagnostic, not a mark. Report G0's spread across the two seeds beside every gap.
plan.proved_wrong: On either seed: step 0 below 90 percent (the registers and controls do not hold the answer in a readable form). G17 donor-follow below B2's registers-only donor-follow minus 10 (the talker reads the state worse than B2's own readout). G17 minus G0 donor-follow below 3 points (the gated read adds nothing; it ignores the state). Zero-state or own-answer exact above 5 on the gated slice (a second solver answering from the prompt). Flip rate above 2 percent (not a translator of B2's decision). Gaps between these lines and the pass bar, such as 3 to 10 points in (ii), are reported as not shown, not as wrong. If training cannot fit its own targets (exact below 90 percent on training gated rows after the fixed budget), the screen is inconclusive, not a disproof.
plan.null_risk: Suggested, untested: under 10 percent chance that all marks pass with no state reading. A decoder that ignores the 17 vectors cannot beat its own prior on donor-follow, and donor pairs are same-family with different answers, so family cues only match at chance. Mark (iii) is what stops constant answers: on yes/no rows a constant 'yes' has about 50 percent donor-follow but fails own-answer. Weak spots: (i) is nearly free if B2's gated baseline is low, so it proves nothing alone. Step 0 is nearly free too (see pass marks). With about 300 rows per seed and two seeds, a 10-point gap in (ii) can come from G0 training variance, so G0's spread is reported beside it. What a pass cannot show: wording generalisation (in_dist only; the old copy talker failed on unseen kinds, shown in the brief), English fluency, digits (NUM rows are not gated), or anything about T1. Also: the 17 vectors are not executor-free. ledger.py:333-337 executes each step and writes its result back into the controller state through vcode (shown), so a pass may partly be the hand calculator's value carried in the vectors. The marks cannot separate that; any pass must say so.
plan.autonomy: What would ship: the decoder reads the 17 vectors by learned attention; its gates, copy query and EOS are learned; it writes characters left to right by argmax (no sampling temperature, no dev-tuned threshold); it stops on the learned EOS or at a fixed design-constant cap that is the same on every run and every night. No str(), reversal or word slicing in the talker path. Build-time only, allowed and not deploy: the fresh draws, B2's talk() strings as targets, the probe, the marks and the donor pairs. Deploy-blocked, stated openly: (a) the vectors carry executor output (ledger.py:333-337, shown); (b) the thinker runs a fixed 8 rounds (ledger.py:130, shown), uses hand place code and regex spans, and its copy keys come from B2's reader on the prompt; these are replaced only by H1, N1, P1 and O1 (sealed, not run); (c) there is no learned abstain or stuck head, and the talker cannot learn a new sentence shape after build. So a pass counts only after a re-run on T1 state, and the targets must be rebuilt from T1 or gold after O1 removes the renderers.
steps: 1. Seal the marks, the slice definition and the row floor in PASS-MARKS before any run (rule 4). Nothing is edited after results are seen.

2. Build the B2 comparator on the PC for seeds 100 and 101: donor_eval with return_preds=True on donor_pairs seed 0 (evalx.py:91-130, shown), plus a new registers-only lesion that swaps the 9 registers and keeps the row's own mode, executor values and pointers. Save per-row predictions, decoded mode and per-row copy share. The lesion is new code; forward math is unchanged.

3. Step-0 probe: a hook that returns Z[:, :8] and R after the last round. state() returns only R, vals, valid and the logits (ledger.py:359-362, shown), so the hook is needed. Fit a linear probe on gated rows from fresh draws; score exact match on held-out gated in_dist rows. Stop if below 90 percent.

4. Build fresh draws: a new generator seed, deduplicated against every dev row and the 200k training file. Keep every row (no row filter, rule 7). Target = B2's talk() string plus EOS, so targets inherit B2's errors (B2 in_dist exact is 89.6-91.5, shown in the brief); the talker translates the decision and does not correct it. Assert that no target exceeds 24 characters, a fixed cap chosen before the run; if one does, stop and report, do not cut. Gold in_dist answers should be 8 characters or fewer (data.py:109 strict assert for training data).
5. Cache the 17 final vectors per draw row in fp16 (1.74 GB for 200k rows). Recompute the reader's copy keys each batch.

6. Train G17 and G0 on seeds 100 and 101 (four runs) with the same data, draw order and recipe. Recipe copied from B2 and fixed in advance (24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16; suggested, untested here). Decoder: 2 causal blocks, width 256, MLP ratio 2, 64 learned positions, readout tied to B2's character table, B2-style copy head over the current prompt, one gated cross-attention per block to the 17 vectors (gate initialised at 0). Loss: teacher-forced cross-entropy over the target characters plus EOS. Decoding: greedy argmax to EOS or the cap.

7. Evaluate on in_dist (1,360 rows per seed): gated-slice donor-follow, own-answer exact under donor, zero-state exact, flip rate; the B2 comparator on the same rows; G0's values; the spread across seeds. Scoring uses the existing norm() and is_hit(). Step A outputs strings, so no sentence extractor is needed.
8. Apply the sealed marks. A pass on both seeds moves to step 9. Any fail stops the line and is reported with the numbers.
9. Only after a screen pass: confirm on seeds 200-205 with the same arms, marks and comparator and a new draw seed. A claim needs every mark on all six seeds; otherwise report 'shown on k of 6'.

10. Before anything counts toward deploy: re-run on T1 state (calculator as an outside tool; sealed, not run). Step B (frames, English, sealed extractor, same-size plain arm, variant split) waits for Ben's ruling and is not part of this plan.

fixed_plan.title: Talker-D3 step A, revised: no-training channel check, then a matched 9-register gated decoder screen
fixed_plan.ben_line: We ask whether a small letter writer can read the notes B2 keeps while it thinks and write the answer B2 chose. First we test the notes with no training: we swap another question's notes in and see whether B2's answer moves with them. Only if the notes really carry the answer do we train the writer, and then we compare it with the same writer with its note-reading switched off. It is a practice step toward an English talker, not English itself.
fixed_plan.question: With B2 frozen, does B2's own answer follow a donor row's 9 register notes when only those notes are swapped in, and, if so, does a small left-to-right letter decoder with a gated read of the same 9 notes follow them better than the same decoder with the read switched off, on the executor-free donor-held slice?
fixed_plan.one_change: Training stage: one change between G9 and G0 only, the gated cross-attention read of the 9 register vectors (one tanh gate per decoder block, starting at 0). G0 is identical with the gate forced to 0. The input channel is the 9 registers in both arms. Stage P0 changes nothing; it only measures.
arms: P0a (no training, seeds 100 and 101): B2 registers-only donor swap, keeping the row's own lmode, lans, lword, vals and valid; donor pairs from donor_pairs with seed 0. Scored by family on the donor-held executor-free slice. This is the comparator and the stop gate.

G9: 2 causal blocks, width 256, MLP ratio 2, 64 learned positions, readout tied to B2's character table (state whether the input embedding is tied too), B2-style copy head over the current prompt, and one gated cross-attention per block reading the 9 registers. G0: identical module with the gate forced to 0 at train and test. Same data, draw order and recipe.

idea.title: Feed each answer register the character before it
idea.summary: B2 writes its 9 answer letters as independent argmaxes, so spelling and length cannot depend on earlier letters. Add one learned 256-vector that adds the embedding of the previous register's character (from the existing tied table) to the next register, at +256 parameters. It is the cheapest test of whether a sequential writer is needed, and it opens only if the probe suite finds wrong-length or order errors.
idea.change: models/ledger.py gen_copy and readout (lines 239-249, 365-366) and talk() (380-390): decode registers j=0..8 in order with h_j = ln_t(R_j) + s * E[c_(j-1)], E = reader.tok.weight (tied, no new table), c_(-1) = BOS, s a 256-vector initialised 0 (created last so step 0 equals B2 exactly). Teacher-forced training on gold characters (EOS then EOS fill, targets unchanged), free-run greedy decode over the model's own characters. B2 becomes 3,302,737 (margin 39,143 to the band top 3,341,880); T1 3,277,649. Cheapest variants of the same rung: one learned scalar alpha (+1 parameter). Named fallbacks if the exposure check fails: a second refine pass over the 9 registers whose input adds the mean embedding of first-pass characters (+256 with a vector, 33,632 with a rank-32 block); a register chain through a 256->64 projection (about 16.7k). T1 variant (only if T1 write_copy is below 99.0 at lengths 6-9): 31 zero-initialised learned scalar gates (9 answer registers plus 2 x 11 call cells, tool.py:37, 110-117), +31 parameters.
idea.why: The 9 registers are independent argmaxes (ledger.py:387-390) with independent losses (521-525), so no readout change can make register j depend on register j-1; order and length errors are out of reach of any readout-only change. A full 256x256 feedback matrix would put T1 1,049 over the band top, so only the diagonal form fits. The diagonal adds a rank-256 bigram term E diag(s) E^T to the logits (algebra). The causal plain_tf beats B2 on seq_next (95.4 vs 86.7) and letter_ops (97.9 vs 95.4) but the cipher result is confounded by the missing letter window, so the evidence for causal writing is weak. Caution: the largest-miss families have copy share near 0, which is a content problem the probe may place in the thinker.

problems: Mechanism (shown, algebra from ledger.py:365-366, readout = F.linear(ln_t(R), tok.weight) + bias): the +256 feedback adds logits E diag(s) E^T. The idea's 'rank-256 bigram' label is wrong: E is 108x256, so the bigram matrix is 108x108 with rank at most 108.

Direction (shown, ledger.py gold(): ids = encode(answer[:GEN_MAX][::-1]) + [EOS]): registers are units first, so 'previous register' is the character that comes AFTER it in the answer. Any directional fix must say this, or it learns the reverse transition.

chair.reasons:
CUT as a stand-alone test; keep one free piece, fold the rest into idea 1 and O1a.

1. The mechanism is weak (shown by shape and code). The +256 vector adds E diag(s) E^T to the logits. E is the 108x256 tied letter table (ledger.py:365-366), so this is a symmetric 108x108 letter-pair term of rank at most 108. The idea says "rank-256", which is wrong. Symmetric means "u after q" gets the same boost as "q after u", so it cannot learn a directional order rule. The feedback also goes into the copy query and copy gate (gen_copy builds q_cp and g_cp from the same h, ledger.py:245-247), which the idea does not isolate. Registers are decoded units-first and reversed (ledger.py:390), so "previous register" is the letter that comes AFTER it in the answer. The idea does not say this.

2. The premise is overstated (shown, ledger.py:117-124). The 9 register tokens sit in the 17-token controller. Each CBlock self-attends over all 17 tokens, in all 8 rounds. Registers can already coordinate through the state. Only the readout and the per-register loss (ledger.py:387-390, 521-525) are independent. A null result would show only that a symmetric letter-pair term on the readout does not help. It would not show that a sequential writer is unneeded. A pass would show only that a bigram helps.

3. The ceiling is small (shown, computed here from the six B2 RESULT.json files, in_dist 8,160 rows). B2 has 773 misses. Weighted by each family's GEN share, about 410 misses are GEN-attributed. 266 of those come from fewshot_number_rule (150.7) and table_lookup (115.4), which look like wrong-value (content) errors, as the idea itself warns (suggested). The two families that are almost all GEN and could plausibly have order or length errors are seq_next (32 misses) and letter_ops (11). Together that is 43 rows, about 0.5% of in_dist rows, or at most about 1.75 GEN-row points if every one were fixed. The +2.0 GEN-row mark is reachable only if the content-heavy families have writer-type errors, and that is exactly what the gate has to show. My estimate (suggested) is +0.5 to +1.5 GEN-row points, about +0.2 to +0.5 pooled-5. With a per-seed SD of about 1.4 on GEN-heavy families, the screen would most likely return "not shown" for 2 to 8 PC-hours, and the true-effect pass rate at +2.0 is only about 35-40%.

4. The T1 variant is dead (shown). T1 has already run: architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md records S3 write_copy failing (operand 29.3 and 30.9, answer 42.1 and 42.4; about 0% at 6-9 digits). MARKS-D0-T1 Amendment 3 sealed one change, span copy, "nothing else", with R1-R4 as the re-screen marks. The cause named there is untrained place rows at 4 or more digits, not independent registers. A previous-character gate gives no source position, so it cannot fix that. Adding it would be a second, unsealed change to the same writer (rule 4). Drop the T1 variant.

5. The gate and metrics are unrunnable or loose as written. "Probe 2", the one-edit and order classes, the five-class split and M2/M8 are defined in no file I could find (reported by 3 critics; shown by absence). No B2 per-row predictions exist (the q33 folders hold only RESULT.json). diag_ledger.py:21 uses the readout without the copy gate, so it is the wrong decode for B2. The mark leaves gaps: free-run between TF-5 and TF-2, and GEN gain between 0 and +2 with the order share in the middle. "EOS fill" conflicts with gold(), which masks post-EOS targets at -100 (ledger.py:437, 523). The leak rule max(5, B2+1) would accept 11.8 on seed 201, above the limit of 5. "Gold-GEN rows" include mode errors that D4 cannot touch.

6. It is off the problem area and overlaps a planned rung. The area is an English talker. This changes the 8-letter GEN grid and cannot show that a sentence talker needs, or can use, a sequential decoder. PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:149 already plans O1a, an autoregressive writer, as the conditional rung. It would also build on the units-first reversal, a hand renderer Ben's deploy rule wants removed (INVENTORY A15). Rules 1 to 3, 7, 9 and 10 are not broken as written, and the 256-parameter cost fits the size band (B2 3,302,737, T1 3,277,649; shown, arithmetic checked by two critics). The cut is on value, not on a rule.

7. Compute is busy. The PC runs EGE (queue 39) until about midnight ET, then q40, U0 and the 8a 3M rung (from the brief). The 4.5 h figure is not derived. The confirm runs took 0.99 to 4.21 h each (shown, by the test critic).

What survives: the forward-only error-class split of wrong decoded-GEN rows on the six existing B2 checkpoints. It needs no training and is idea 1's job, not this idea's.
chair.revised_idea:
No stand-alone D4. Fold into idea 1 (CPU probe suite) as a free kill-first measurement, and into O1a as the real sequential-writer test.

(a) Free probe, forward only, no training, on B2 seeds 200-205 from b2ckpt, decoded through talk()/gen_copy (never diag_ledger.py:21 as written; change it to use gen_copy first). Save per-row predictions (evalx.evaluate(return_preds=True) or --save-preds). Write the exclusive error classes and their precedence into a file BEFORE running. Suggested precedence: (1) wrong mode, (2) wrong length, (3) same letters in a different order, (4) one substitution at equal length, (5) other content. Report per seed, report seq_next and letter_ops alone, and count decoded-GEN rows, not gold-GEN rows. Report the units-first reversal as the reading order.

(b) Decision rule (suggested), fixed before running: if length plus order plus one-edit errors are under 25% of wrong decoded-GEN rows on either of two seeds, D4 and any register-feedback variant is dead, and the result is recorded as "registers are not the bottleneck". The expected outcome is that fewshot_number_rule and table_lookup are mostly content or rule errors, which would also send those two families to the thinker or the data, not the talker.

(c) Only if the gate opens, run ONE sequential-writer rung. Fold it into O1a (PLAN-AND-MARKS line 149), written in normal reading order so it also deletes the reversal renderer. Do not use the symmetric diagonal. Use an asymmetric low-rank term or a causal 1-layer decoder over the 9 registers. For example h_j += U(V^T E[c_(j-1)]) with rank 32, which is 16,384 parameters, so B2 3,318,865 and T1 3,293,777, both inside the band (arithmetic by the mechanism critic, shown by shape). EOS is a feedback input only. Targets stay exactly as gold() makes them (-100 after EOS). Report copy share per family.

(d) Drop the T1 31-gate variant. T1's writer is covered by the sealed span-copy re-screen (Amendment 3, R1-R4).
chair.plan_guidance:
Not a plan; guidance if the lead folds the surviving pieces into idea 1 and O1a.

1. Order of work: first the free forward-only error-class probe, then at most one sequential-writer rung, and only if the kill-first rule leaves it open.

2. Probe requirements:
 - Decode through talk()/gen_copy.
 - Define the error classes and their precedence in a file before the run.
 - Use decoded-GEN rows, with gold-GEN rows reported separately.
 - Report per seed, and report seq_next and letter_ops alone.
 - The plain_tf versus B2 gaps on seq_next (95.4 vs 86.7) and letter_ops (97.9 vs 95.4) are confounded by plain_tf's lack of the letter window and its whole-question attention, so do not read them as evidence for causal writing (shown: the cipher result falls from about 97 to about 4 when B2's window is removed).

3. Kill and pass marks, fixed in advance:
 - Kill if order, length and one-edit errors together are under 25% of wrong decoded-GEN rows on either seed. This 25% is a suggested threshold, not a project-sealed number.
 - If the rung runs, give every middle zone the label "not shown" (project convention in PLAN-AND-MARKS section 3a). Do not leave gaps, and do not add a "borderline" arm.
 - Use a flat thinker-off leak limit of 5 on every seed, reported as a separate flag.
 - The sequential-writer test must be one change.

4. Scale and noise:
 - If the asymmetric term is tried, state its effective scale at init. The tied table is initialised at std 0.02, so an identity feedback starting at 0 may stay negligible against ln_t(R), whose norm is about 16 (suggested).
 - The 2-seed noise on GEN-row exact is about 1.4 SD, so a gain of +2.0 is only about 1.4 SD (suggested).
 - Any claim needs 6 paired seeds (rule 4).
 - A cheap pre-step, if the gate opens: cache the 9 registers and gold letters for about 20k B2 training GEN rows, and fit only the feedback term. This is a lower bound, not a kill.

5. Hard constraints:
 - The talker must score on raw output, with no hand brake.
 - The units-first reversal and the first-EOS cut are hand renderers that O1 must delete, so build the writer in reading order.
 - Any English-length (over 8) work must lift the GEN cut at ledger.py:447 and the 32-character drop, or it breaks rule 7.
 - Keep B2 claims separate from the 1.2B English line (rule 9).

6. Plain-language summary for Ben: B2 writes its answer letters all at once, not one after another. This idea added a tiny hint of the neighbouring letter. Most of the answers B2 gets wrong look like wrong values (the rule or the lookup was wrong), not wrong spelling. At most about 43 of 773 in-dist misses come from families where spelling could be the problem. So the hint probably cannot help much, and it would not teach us how to build an English talker. The useful, free thing to do is to sort B2's wrong answers into kinds, using the checkpoints you already have. If spelling or order errors are rare, we stop. If they are common, we build a proper letter-by-letter writer as the O1a step.

idea.title: Learned keep-or-abstain head with self-made labels
idea.summary: B2 always answers, yet it scores 31.9-37.1 on the variant split and 0.6-2.5 on brand-new families. Train a 514-parameter keep-or-abstain head on B2's final control state with right-or-wrong labels, and test whether labels the model makes itself (does its final answer agree with its own round-6 answer) work nearly as well as gold labels. The head's argmax replaces a hand-set 0.5 break-even or retry cap. CPU first, six seeds.
idea.change: Stage 1 (CPU, frozen B2 seeds 200-205): new Linear(256,2) on zf=ln_z(Z[:,1]) (ledger.py:342) = 514 parameters, fit on about 8,000 FRESH skills-generator rows (new seed, 13-gram-filtered against train and dev, the 62-word-piece/208-char filters off or logged so nothing is silently cut). Arms: (a) head with gold labels (B2 exact match; gold used pre-ship only); (b) free baseline = mean of the nine per-register max probabilities from gen_copy, no training; (c) head on zf plus the pooled reader output of the written answer string (+256), the string-only hear-back arm; (d) head with self-labels: 1 if the final GEN answer equals the GEN answer read at round 6 (run(rounds=True) snapshot), else 0. Decision = argmax of two logits, no threshold. Stage 2 (PC, only if stage 1 passes): mode_head Linear(d,3) -> Linear(d,4) with an ABSTAIN mode that writes '?' then EOS through the existing GEN registers (+257 parameters); abstain training rows = rows where B2's own no-grad greedy pass is wrong; scoring +1 right / 0 abstain / -1 wrong (break-even exactly 0.5, no tuned threshold); placebo arm with shuffled abstain labels.
idea.why: B2's final state is what produced the answer, so a head on it can rank answers without an outside cut-off. The free baseline shows whether any learned head is needed at all. Self-agreement labels are the rule-10 test: a deployed model has no gold, so it can keep learning when to abstain only from labels it makes itself. Risk: B2's round-6 readouts were never trained (round_readout defaults 0.0), so agreement may be near-constant; the label share is reported first.

evidence.label: shown

evidence.label: shown

evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: H1 (planned, not run) already has a confidence readout and a 'settled' label on the thinker state, so the signal is expected to be in the state.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Under a +1/0/-1 rule, abstaining when P(right)<0.5 maximises expected score; a string-only re-read cannot carry more correctness information than the registers plus prompt it was computed from (data-processing argument).

test.where: Six frozen B2 checkpoints (scratchpad code/b2ckpt, seeds 200-205), CPU; fit rows from the generator on the PC; held-out = dev variant and family pooled (1,480 rows) and in_dist (1,360) per seed. Stage 2 on the PC GPU only after a pass.
test.arms: (a) gold-label keep head; (b) free register-confidence baseline; (c) head plus answer-string re-read; (d) self-labelled head. Stage 2 (+2.5 h): B2 vs B2+ABSTAIN vs shuffled-label placebo, seeds 200-201.
test.pass_mark: Six seeds, marks written before any run. Gold head (a): AUROC >=0.70 on each seed; mean AUROC(a)-AUROC(b) >=0.03 with >=5 of 6 seeds positive; on variant, exact among kept rows >=45% with keep share 20-80%; on in_dist, exact among kept rows >=97% with keep share >=80%. Self-label head (d): AUROC against gold correctness >=0.65 each seed, mean gain over (b) >=0.8x the gain of (a), self-label share between 10% and 90% each seed (else 'not shown'). (c) beating (a) by >=0.05 AUROC means answer-string hear-back is not redundant. Stage 2, both seeds: variant score (+1/0/-1 per 100 rows) >= +10 over B2; in_dist score down <=3; abstain rate on in_dist <=15%; loops:0 leak within 1.0 of B2; placebo does not reach the gain. A pass earns a 6-seed confirm, not a claim.
test.proved_wrong: Head (a) AUROC below 0.60 on >=3 of 6 seeds, or no better than baseline (b) on average; mean AUROC of (d) below 0.55 (agreement across own rounds carries no signal); stage 2 variant score gain below +2 on either seed, or ABSTAIN on >50% of variant rows with gain below +5.

idea.rules_check: R1: GEN registers only; no NUM/WORD renderer used. R2: no teacher; gold only for training labels and scoring. R3: +514 (probe) or +257 (ABSTAIN mode) parameters, inside the band. R4: six-seed probe, marks fixed now, 2-seed screen for stage 2. R5: dev scored not trained; fit rows 13-gram checked against train and dev. R7: no target cut; '?' is a short teaching target. R9: B2 only. R10: see autonomy.
idea.closest_prior: H1's stop head (257 parameters, decides how many rounds, redesign-ideas 8b-8c) and the learned notebook gate (PLAN section 4, D6). This decides keep or abstain on a finished answer with no extra rounds and replaces the 0.5 break-even.
idea.autonomy: Model: reads its own state, decides keep or abstain by argmax, writes '?'. Labels for later learning come from its own round agreement, with no gold, tool or threshold. Developer residues: round 6 as the comparison point (a constant; idea 10's learned pointer could replace it), the '?' abstain string (teaching target), and gold labels in pre-ship training only.
idea.director_note: Cheap and rule-10 clean, and it gives the talker something English-like to say beyond an answer (I don't know). Critics should check hardest: untrained round-6 readouts may make (d) degenerate; fit and held-out rows must not overlap by 13-gram; AUROC on variant+family pooled mixes two shifts.

problems: Stage 2 pass is reachable by abstaining on every variant row. shown: B2 variant exact mean is 34.7 (n=1320 per seed; results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200..s205 RESULT.json final_eval.variant). Under the +1/0/-1 rule B2 always-answer scores about -30.6 per 100 variant rows, and always-abstain scores 0. So the mark 'variant score >= +10 over B2' passes always-abstain, and the proved-wrong clause 'ABSTAIN on >50% of variant rows with gain below +5' does not fire. No comparison is made against always-abstain or against baseline (b).

Stage-1 marks contradict the stage-2 scoring. shown: in_dist exact is about 90.5 (n=1360). suggested arithmetic: keeping 80% of rows at 97% exact scores 0.8 x (0.97 - 0.03) = 75.2 per 100, against about 81.0 for B2 always-answer. That is a drop of about 5.8, which fails the stage-2 guard 'in_dist score down <= 3'. The variant stage-1 mark (kept rows >= 45% exact) is below the 50% break-even that the idea itself uses, so each kept row has expected score -0.10 (suggested).

Arm (d), the rule-10 self-label test, is confounded with program length. shown: the round snapshot is taken at t <= n-2 = 6 (ledger.py:340). Steps are written only for 1 <= t <= N_RES (ledger.py:319; N_RES = 7 at models/progparse.py:8). So round 6 holds steps 1-6 only, and any row whose answer needs step 7 disagrees with the final answer by construction. The label then tracks program length and whether the answer has settled, not correctness. shown: round readouts are untrained (round_readout default 0.0, ledger.py:131 and 140). Test LR already failed on stability and leak (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:292). 'GEN answer' is undefined on NUM and WORD rows, so agreement must be defined on the full talk() output with its mode (ledger.py:380-406).

Baseline (b) is mode-mismatched. shown: gen_copy register probabilities (ledger.py:239-249) are read only when talk() takes the GEN path (ledger.py:380-406). shown: dev rows are NUM 42.2%, WORD 27.9%, GEN 30.0% (RESULT.json extra.coverage.all, n=6800, seed 200). So about 70% of rows never use the register confidence that baseline (b) measures. Mode and family are also predictable from the state, so a head can beat (b) by learning family identity.

Pooled AUROC on variant plus family mixes split identity with correctness. shown: family exact is 0.6-2.5% (n=160 per seed) and variant exact is about 34.7% (n=1320). suggested arithmetic: a head that ranks family rows below variant rows, with chance ordering inside variant, reaches pooled AUROC of about 0.58 with no within-variant skill. The 0.70 mark then needs within-variant AUROC of about 0.65. The spec needs within-split AUROC, and a family-prior baseline built from fit-row accuracy per family.

The fit-row filters are not feasible as written. shown: data.py:107 asserts prompt length <= 208, so 'filters off' is impossible without dropping rows. shown: PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:63 says the generator silently drops questions over 62 estimated word pieces, which B2 was trained with; turning that off moves the fit rows away from B2's training distribution. shown: data.py:109 asserts answers <= 8 characters, and strict=False truncates answers (data.py:116). Truncation breaks rule 7. B2 cannot write answers over 8 characters, so those rows are wrong by construction and bias the labels. The spec must drop and count such rows.

Rule 5 gap. shown: /mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md:23 and :128 say GOLD-PRIVATE and every reserved or blind panel are not yet cleared or merged. The idea filters fit rows only against train and dev. The fit must also be checked against those hashes, or wait until they are merged.

Rule 10 is only partly met. Arm (d) is the one self-labelled path. Arm (a) and all of stage 2 use gold labels (stage 2 labels are 'rows where B2's own greedy pass is wrong'). That is a pre-ship build, which is allowed, but it does not show a deploy-time behaviour. The fit rows are generator rows, not the model's own question stream. The deploy-time loop for (d) is unspecified: which tries it learns from, how often, what replay it uses, and when it trains.

Stage-2 spec gaps. The abstain positives are not named. If they come from B2's training set, the wrong set is probably small: 24,000 updates x 256 / 200,000 questions is about 31 passes, and training accuracy is not shown (suggested). The idea does not say whether a wrong row keeps its gold mode and answer targets or switches to ABSTAIN. A fourth mode also changes talk() (ledger.py:380-406) and the mode loss (ledger.py:517).

The argmax is a fixed 0.5 cut on a probability calibrated only on the fit distribution, which is in-family and about 90% right. suggested: on variant the head may keep almost every row, so keep share and calibration on variant should be reported before any mark is read.

Parameter count in arm (c). A head on 512 inputs (zf plus a 256-wide string vector) has 1,026 parameters, which is +512 over 514, not +256. The stage-1 count of 514 (Linear(256,2)) and the stage-2 count of +257 (Linear(256,4) minus Linear(256,3)) are correct, from the shapes at ledger.py:149.

Overlap with prior plans. shown: H1's 'settled' stop head is a 257-parameter head that predicts whether the current readout is already right, on the same final-round state (/mnt/project-files/architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:136, 161-162). The learned notebook gate (/mnt/project-files/creative-roadmap/creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:853-870; no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:186) is another self-labelled learned gate. No abstain, AUROC or keep-head work exists in /mnt/project-files (grep, no matches). The only abstain code is phrase matching for scoring in reader/scripts/fable_bench113c_run.py:55-110, which belongs to another bench.
