critiques.expected_effect: A roughly 2-hour CPU probe on six frozen B2 seeds (checkpoints present, verified). If it works, it shows whether B2's final control state carries right-versus-wrong signal inside each split. It does not show a talker gain, English speech, or a shippable abstain policy. Under the +1/0/-1 rule the variant gain depends on keeping rows over 50% right, which is untested. As written the marks would pass always-abstain, so a pass alone would not show a skill.

problems: No deploy-time learning loop is specified (untested gap). The idea says the head 'can keep learning when to abstain only from labels it makes itself', but it gives no trigger, buffer size, update rule, fit schedule or stop rule for after ship. The only fit described is the pre-ship probe on about 8,000 FRESH generator rows. PLAN-AND-MARKS.md:95-97 places when-to-learn in fast sleep (D8); the proposal does not connect to it.

Arm (d) self-labels rest on round-6 readouts that B2 as built never trains. round_readout defaults to 0.0 (ledger.py:131, 140) and the intermediate-round loss runs only when the weight is set (ledger.py:532-535; docstring 37-40). The snapshot at t <= n-2 (ledger.py:340-341, 355-356) is therefore read by an untrained readout, so the labels may be near-constant (the proposal names this risk; untested). The only trained version, Test LR, failed its marks: leak 15.9 at seed 200 and a 16-round drop of 0.51 against a 0.3 limit (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:292-293; redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:148, 152). The configuration that would make arm (d) meaningful has already failed.

The self-label is defined only for GEN answers ('1 if the final GEN answer equals the GEN answer read at round 6'), but the head reads zf (ledger.py:342), which is mode-independent, and it is applied to every row. Dev answer modes are NUM 42.18%, WORD 27.85%, GEN 29.97% over 6,800 rows (shown: results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json extra.coverage.all). About 70% of rows therefore have no defined self-label. The mode head is read only after the last iteration (ledger.py:344), so no round-6 mode exists either.

Stage 2 ABSTAIN labels are gold: 'rows where B2's own no-grad greedy pass is wrong'. Pre-ship that is a build step, but the autonomy claim covers only the head, so the ABSTAIN mode has no deploy-time learning path. Its training rows are also the generator kinds B2 fails on, so the mode learns generator-specific difficulty. Rule 10 names 'knowledge taken from the test generator (which kinds exist)' as not counting. Whether a pre-ship fit on generator rows is build or learning needs Ben's ruling (untested).

The 'no tuned threshold' claim holds only if the head is calibrated on the traffic it sees (suggested). Argmax of a 2-class head is a 0.5 cut on posterior probability only under calibration. The implicit cut moves with the label share in the fit mix, which is a developer choice (B2 is about 90% right on in_dist and about 35% on variant, RESULT.json). A deployed model has no calibration check of its own except the self-labels, which are the degenerate ones named above.

Developer gates remain in the probe: the 10-90% self-label share check, the keep-share bands, and the note about '62-word-piece/208-char filters off or logged'. The deployed model has no equivalent, so the idea needs its own autonomous degeneracy test (for example the head's own label variance) or must state that a fixed constant is used. The '62-word-piece' filter was not found in the custom_io *.py files I could search (untested reference).

Fixed constants: round 6 (n-2 of the 8 fixed rounds, ledger.py:340), the 8-round count, the '?' string and the 0.5 break-even. Fixed design constants are allowed if they stay the same every night, and the proposal flags round 6 itself. The 8-round count is different: PLAN-AND-MARKS.md:90 already lists the fixed 8 rounds as a researcher's run-time choice that H1 must replace, so D5 inherits that residue.

The rules check R1 says 'GEN registers only; no NUM/WORD renderer used'. That is not true for the answers the head judges: about 70% of B2 answers come through the NUM str() and WORD copy renderers (shares above). The deploy rule (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md section 4) lists those renderers for replacement through O1 after K1, so the keep decision depends on hand renderers for most rows until then.

The closest prior, H1, has the same training-time gold dependency. Its stop label is computed 'from the model's own per-round readouts against the target' in training (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:136, 162). The proposal cites H1 as evidence that the signal exists, but H1 is also trained against gold and then frozen. The proposal should apply the same standard to itself: a frozen-at-ship head is a build step, and 'keeps learning' is a separate claim that needs its own spec.

After an abstain nothing happens: there is no retry, tool call or check. Rule 10 covers deciding that the model is stuck, whether to try again and when to stop (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:382; PLAN-AND-MARKS.md:92). D5 covers the decision but not the action after it. The creative try budget (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:965) is the existing counterpart and is not referenced.

Rule 5 (not autonomy, but a rule gap): fit rows are checked by 13-gram filter against train and dev only. Protected-panel hashes are not merged (per the brief; data-pool plan not re-opened here), so the fit rows cannot yet be checked against protected panels. The idea should say so.
critiques.rescue: Choose one claim and specify it. (A) Build-time only: keep stage 1 arms (a)-(c) as a pre-ship fit of a frozen 514-parameter head, state that it is frozen at ship, and delete the 'keeps learning' sentence. The deployed step is then argmax of a fixed head with no run-time gold, gate or tuned value, which meets rule 10 without further work. (B) Learn after ship: write the deploy loop. It needs a fixed buffer size and fit interval (the same every night), rows taken only from the model's own questions and tries, and labels from a label-free source. For NUM answers that could be a calc tool call that re-evaluates the chosen program's value (an outside tool the model calls; it checks arithmetic on the chosen program, not whether the program answers the question, suggested). For other modes, round agreement may be used only after the round-6 readout is shown non-degenerate on B2 as built. The degeneracy check should be the model's own (label variance), not the developer's 10-90% gate, and the fit decision should attach to fast sleep D8. Before any arm (d) run, a no-training CPU probe on seeds 200-201 can measure the label share and the AUROC of round-6 agreement, which answers the degeneracy question first. Drop gold-labelled ABSTAIN training from the deploy path (keep it build-time and frozen), and get Ben's ruling on whether a pre-ship fit on generator rows counts under rule 10.
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior tests: Test LR (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:292-293; redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:148, 152) for trained intermediate readouts, which failed on leak and stability; H1 stop head (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:134-137, 157-168) for a head on the thinker state with a self-computed label, itself gold-trained; creative C9 (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:965) for a learned 'can't do this yet' signal from the model's own failed checks; PLAN-AND-MARKS.md:84 (ST1) for a check tool at deploy time. No file tests self-agreement labels on B2 as built (untested).
critiques.expected_effect: Checked against the files: the parameter counts are right (514 = Linear(256,2); +257 for the ABSTAIN mode = Linear(256,4) minus Linear(256,3)), and the baseline numbers match RESULT.json (in_dist n 1,360, variant n 1,320, family n 160; variant exact 31.9-37.1; family 0.6-2.5). Under (A), the deployed keep or abstain step is fully autonomous and costs +514 parameters, with no claim of learning after ship. Under (B), the autonomy claim becomes testable, but nothing is measured yet: the round-6 label share, AUROC of the gold head, and self-label AUROC are all untested, so no gain can be expected until the no-training probe runs.

problems: Stage-2 variant gate (score >= +10 over B2) is passed by random abstention. Shown from the per-seed variant exact values in /tmp/.../results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s20N/RESULT.json (31.9-37.1, mean 34.7): B2's score per 100 rows is 2*34.7-100 = -30.6, so abstaining at random on a fraction f gains f*30.6. A random abstainer at 28-39% (mean 33%) clears +10 on every seed. The gate needs a matched-rate random placebo, not a shuffled-label one.

The stage-2 in_dist gate (score down <= 3 at abstain <= 15%) is passed only by a head that abstains on about 3.7% or fewer in-dist rows at random. A head that abstains more on variant-like rows and less on in-dist rows passes both score gates with no within-split correctness skill. The stage-1 variant precision mark (>= 45% among kept, random kept precision 34.7%) is the real test, and stage 2 does not repeat it. Stage 2 should require that mark too.

The 0.5 argmax is break-even only under the training prior. The head is fit on FRESH rows where B2 is about 90% right (shown: in_dist 89.6-91.5), but variant is 34.7% right. The prior odds ratio is about 0.056 (computed here). A head calibrated on in-dist puts its 0.5 cut at a variant-equivalent P of about 0.05, so it keeps rows that are mostly wrong on variant (suggested, Bayes prior-shift arithmetic). Ovadia et al. 2019 (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv 1906.02530; found by search, abstract text checked) report that post-hoc calibration that works in-distribution can fail under mild input shift. If stage 1 misses the 20-80% keep-share mark, the only fix is a variant-tuned threshold, which breaks the autonomy rule. The idea's claim of 'no tuned threshold' does not hold under shift.

The stage-1 in-dist mark and the stage-2 in-dist gate disagree. Keep share 0.80 at precision 0.97 passes stage 1 but gives score about 75.2 against B2's about 80.8 (mean in-dist 90.4). That is down about 5.6, which fails the stage-2 'down <= 3' gate. Stage 2 needs precision near 0.986 at keep 0.80 (suggested, computed from the RESULT.json means). The marks should be checked on the same rows.

The pooled variant+family AUROC is confounded by split. Family has only 1-4 correct rows per seed (shown: 1.875%, 2.5% and 0.625% of 160, from RESULT.json). A pure novelty detector with no within-variant skill gets pooled AUROC of about 0.57 (suggested pair count, about 458 variant-right, 862 variant-wrong, 157 family-wrong per seed). So the 0.70 pooled gate needs only about 0.65 within-variant AUROC. Family AUROC per seed has a Hanley-McNeil SE of about 0.17 with 3 positives (suggested), so it cannot carry a per-seed gate. Report within-split AUROC for variant and in_dist separately, and treat family as descriptive.

The self-label arm (d) and the free baseline (b) are undefined for most rows. Shown in RESULT.json extra.coverage.all (n=6800): NUM 42.2%, WORD 27.9%, GEN 30.0%. talk() in ledger.py emits GEN only when the mode head says GEN or a NUM/WORD pointer is invalid. Arm (d) compares 'final GEN answer' with 'GEN answer read at round 6', so it is undefined on NUM and WORD rows, which are 70% of dev. Arm (b) (mean of nine register max probabilities) is mode-blind, so for NUM and WORD rows it scores registers the model never emits. A fair baseline needs confidence of the chosen mode head or pointer, for example softmax max of lmode, lword or lans.

Round-6 readouts were never trained, so arm (d) may be degenerate by construction. Shown: round_readout defaults to 0.0 (ledger.py __init__), and the confirm RESULT.json config contains only cfg copy:true, so the default applied. The round-6 registers were never trained to be readable. The label share may fall outside the 10-90% band, which makes the arm 'not shown' by design. The arm also mixes units: run() stores the raw Z[:,1] in snaps, while the head expects ln_z(Z[:,1]); arm (d) must apply ln_z to the snapshot.

Agreement between rounds tests stability, not correctness. A model can settle on a wrong answer, and that is exactly the case the head must catch on the held-out families (B2 family accuracy is 0.6-2.5%, shown). The proved-wrong line (mean AUROC below 0.55) and the pass line (0.65 per seed) leave a 0.55-0.65 band that is not decided. The H1 'settled' label cited as support (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 8c) is computed against the target, so it is gold-based and untested. It is not evidence that self-agreement carries signal.

The head reads the wrong state. Shown in ledger.py run(): out['R'] = Z[:, N_CTRL:] and talk() takes the GEN answer from those 9 registers. The head on zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]) (control 1) feeds only the mode, answer-pointer and word-pointer heads. So the claim 'the talker reads only control 1' is true only for those heads. Arm (a) cannot see the registers that produce a GEN answer, and arm (c) (string re-read) is the only route to that information. The data-processing argument is therefore muddled: (c) can beat (a) because it adds register information, which says nothing about hear-back redundancy. Also, arm (c) on zf plus 256 features is Linear(512,2) = 1,026 parameters, not 514.

Stage 2 trains the ABSTAIN mode on gold labels (rows where B2's greedy pass is wrong). That is pre-ship supervision, which rule 10 allows only before shipping. The autonomy paragraph claims a deploy-time loop that learns from self-agreement, but no such loop is specified or tested. The round-6 comparison point is a developer constant. The ABSTAIN class is about 10% of in-dist rows, so its head learns the in-dist prior (see the prior-shift point).

Rule 5 gap: the FRESH fit rows are 13-gram filtered only against train and dev. Shown in /mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md (line 128): protected panels (GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind) are not yet merged, and the pool must not be used for training until the merge. The idea must check the 8,000 FRESH rows against the protected-panel hash file, or mark them not cleared for training. Line 125 also says generator-row 13-gram results are reported, not gated, which conflicts with the idea's gating.

Factual error: the idea cites 'the 62-word-piece/208-char filters'. No 62 constant exists in the code. The word cap is W_MAX = 64 word tokens (progparse.py:8), and MAX_PROMPT = 208 characters (data.py:11). Dataset asserts on prompt length (data.py:107) rather than cutting, so the FRESH rows need an upstream filter, not a silent cut.

The probe's gate for the abstain choice is a single-seed-style statistic on 1,320 rows. A binomial SE for one split is about 2.6 points per 100 rows per seed (suggested). The 'matched random' comparison is paired, so its SE is lower, but the probe still needs six seeds before any claim (rule 4). The +10 gate is about four SE from zero per seed while being passable at random, so it proves little.

Unverified: whether the B2 control state carries correctness information on held-out kinds. Not measured here or in any file. The mode-share and head-input facts above are shown; the value of the head is untested.
critiques.rescue: Keep stage 1 (CPU, six seeds, cheap) but change the marks and the baselines. (1) Replace the stage-2 score gate with a matched-rate random abstention placebo per split and seed; a pass needs the head to beat random at the same abstain rate by at least +5 per 100 rows on variant, plus the stage-1 variant precision mark (>= 45% among kept). (2) Report AUROC within variant and within in_dist separately; drop the family AUROC gate (1-4 positives per seed) and report family as descriptive. (3) Decide the keep cut without variant tuning: fit with class weights so that the cut is break-even under a prior the model can estimate from its own tries (its running accuracy), and report the prior-corrected keep share. Do not tune the cut on dev. (4) Define the answer for every mode: score NUM and WORD rows with the chosen mode's own confidence (softmax max of lmode, lword or lans) and compare the head against that baseline; define arm (d) for all modes, or restrict every arm and the baseline to GEN rows and say so. (5) Apply ln_z to round snapshots. Say in advance that arm (d) may be 'not shown' because round-6 readouts are untrained, and treat any test of it on a checkpoint trained with round_readout > 0 as a separate single change. (6) Give the head the register vectors (or per-register gen confidence) as well as zf, so arm (a) can see the state that writes the answer. (7) Make the stage-1 and stage-2 in-dist marks agree on the same rows. (8) Before fitting, check the FRESH rows against the protected-panel hash file, or label them not cleared. (9) Fix the 62-word-piece reference to W_MAX = 64 word tokens and MAX_PROMPT = 208 characters, and fix arm (c) to 1,026 parameters. (10) Cite Ovadia et al. 2019 (arXiv 1906.02530) as the shift risk. Keep stage 2 pre-ship only and say so; the self-labelled deploy loop needs its own idea and marks.
critiques.already_tried: Checked against the code and files: no prior keep-or-abstain head on B2 exists. Closest prior work: H1's stop head (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 8b, 257 parameters, not run); the Test LR round-loss probe (failed on stability and leak, seeds 200-201, shown in the roadmap section 2); the planned notebook gate D6 (no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md section 4, not run). None measures correctness from the B2 control state on held-out kinds. The parameter arithmetic in the idea is correct: mode_head is Linear(d,3) (ledger.py __init__), so Linear(d,4) adds 257, and the 514-parameter probe is Linear(256,2). Only the arm (c) count is wrong.
critiques.expected_effect: Honest estimate, computed here with a binormal model at variant prior 0.347 and no prior shift: a head with within-variant AUROC of 0.60, 0.65, 0.70 and 0.75 at about 40% keep share gives about +6, +10, +13 and +17 score per 100 variant rows over matched-rate random abstention (suggested; the keep share is set by hand in this calculation, and the deployed argmax may land elsewhere). AUROC 0.5 gives 0. The idea's +10 gate over B2 is passed by random abstention, so a pass on it is not evidence. Prior shift and untrained round-6 readouts could push the real effect toward zero. The effect size is therefore plausible but low-to-moderate in probability, and the expected gain is small against two-seed noise. Untested: whether zf carries correctness on held-out kinds.

problems: Arm (d) self-labels cannot be built as written, and the round-6 heads are untrained. shown: the B2 confirm config is {"copy": true} (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json, config), so round_readout keeps its default 0.0 (reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py:131, 140; the round loss runs only when it is above 0, ledger.py:500, 532-534). The rounds=True snapshot at ledger.py:341 is (t, Z[:,1], registers, Rs, valid) with no vals, but talk() needs vals for NUM answers (ledger.py:384-399). 'The final GEN answer' is defined only for GEN rows, which are 30.0% of dev rows (NUM 42.2%, WORD 27.9%; RESULT.json extra.coverage.all). So arm (d) needs new decode code and a label-share check before any fit. untested: whether round-6 agreement is near-constant.

Arm (a) gets the wrong inputs for the comparison. shown: zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]) (ledger.py:342) feeds only the mode, answer-pointer and word-pointer heads (ledger.py:344-345). GEN characters come from the 9 register tokens through gen_copy (ledger.py:239-249, 387-390). So the idea's claim that the talker reads only control 1 is wrong for characters, and the 514-parameter head never sees what baseline (b) scores. A failure of (a) cannot tell whether the state lacks the answer or the head got the wrong input. Add an arm with the registers pooled into the head, so it has the same information as (b) (suggested: a few hundred more parameters, inside the 3% band).

The pooled AUROC mark mixes two shifts and is almost entirely the variant split. shown: family has 1 to 4 correct rows per seed (family exact 0.62-2.50 on 160 rows; RESULT.json final_eval.family). suggested (arithmetic on those counts): a score that only separates variant from family, with no within-split signal, reaches pooled AUROC 0.571-0.578 across seeds 200-205, so the 0.70 bar is not met by split identity alone. But family cannot be measured by AUROC at all with 1-4 positives. Mark within-variant AUROC instead (1,320 rows, 421-490 correct per seed, shown), with a null SE near 0.017 (suggested), and report family as counts only.

The 'no tuned threshold' claim is false. A two-logit argmax is a 0.5 cut on the head's own probability, the same 0.5 break-even the idea says it replaces. That cut follows the fit set's base rate and class weights, which are developer choices. Fresh generator rows should resemble in_dist (suggested), which is 89.6-91.5% exact (shown), while variant is 31.9-37.1% exact (shown). A head fit on fresh rows will therefore move on variant, and the keep share will move with it. Report keep share per split and name the class weighting as a design constant.

A random abstainer passes the stage 2 variant bar. suggested arithmetic: on variant, abstaining on a random row gains P(wrong) minus P(right) per abstained row, about +0.36 at seed 200 (31.9% exact) and +0.26 at seed 202 (37.1% exact). At a 25% abstain share that is about +9.1 (seed 200) and +6.4 (seed 202) per 100 rows, against a +10 bar. The shuffled-label placebo does not match abstain share, so it is not a control for this. Add a random-abstain arm at matched share on each split. The in_dist guard does rule out random abstention (about -12 per 100 at 15% abstain on in_dist, suggested arithmetic), and it implies that abstained in_dist rows must be at least 40% wrong at the 15% cap. That is the useful part of the mark.

Stage 2 labels need the gold answer, so the path is not autonomous under rule 10. shown: the abstain training rows are 'rows where B2's own no-grad greedy pass is wrong', which is a comparison with gold. Only arm (d) uses self-labels, and the idea does not carry (d) into stage 2. Either label stage 2 as pre-ship gold training, which is not evidence for rule 10, or drive the stage 2 labels from arm (d). The stage 2 row pool (which rows, from which generator sample) is not specified.

The stage 2 cost of +2.5 h holds only for a head-only fine-tune on frozen B2. shown: each B2 confirm run had wall_s 13,318 (about 3.7 h) under the queue's --par 3 (RESULT.json wall_s; results/33-pc-confirm-b2/33-pc-confirm-b2.txt lines 2 and 6). Two seeds of B2+ABSTAIN and a placebo are four retrains, about 5 h of device time (suggested: about 1.2 h each if three share the GPU). The brief's 'about 1 hour per run' is suggested, not measured. The idea does not say whether the arms retrain or fine-tune. A 3.3M-parameter model fits in 16 GB (suggested).

The loops:0 leak guard (within 1.0 of B2) is either trivial or noisy. shown: B2 loops:0 in_dist exact by seed is 0.00, 10.81, 0.00, 5.66, 3.53, 0.00 (RESULT.json lesions). A head on frozen B2 cannot change the thinker, so the guard passes by construction. A retrain would move the leak by an unmeasured same-seed amount; across-seed spread is 0 to 10.8 (shown), far above 1.0. Say which path is used, and measure paired retrain noise before using a 1.0 bar.

The guards skip three dev splits. shown: pooled-5 is 6,040 rows including answer (1,200 rows; 73.1-74.9 exact), frame (1,360; 85.9-89.0) and vocab (800; 86.3-88.8) (RESULT.json final_eval, per seed). The stage 2 guards cover only in_dist and variant, and stage 1 covers only in_dist and variant. A keep head could cut the other three splits and no mark would notice. Add a pooled-5 no-drop guard covering all five splits.

Some bands are left open and one mark inverts. The arm (a) AUROC between 0.60 and 0.70 and the stage 2 gain between +2 and +10 are neither pass nor proved wrong. The arm (d) mark 'mean gain over (b) at least 0.8 times the gain of (a)' passes a negative (d) gain whenever (a) is zero or negative, since 0.8 times a negative number is above the gain. Write explicit 'not shown' bands and make the (d) rule sign-safe, for example gain(d) above 0 and above gain(b), plus gain(d) at least 0.8 times gain(a) only when gain(a) is above 0.

The closest prior gives no evidence yet. shown: H1 has not run ('No H1 result exists', architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:163). Its 'settled' label is computed from the target answer (line 162), so it is gold-labelled and is not a self-label precedent. The H1 stop head is 257 parameters (line 136), not the 514-parameter head here. The claim that the signal is 'expected to be in the state' rests on an unrun design.

The filters cannot be switched off, and fit rows must match dev. shown: the Dataset class asserts prompts of at most 208 characters and, in strict mode, answers of at most MAX_ANS = 8 (reader/custom_io/data.py:101-110; MAX_PROMPT and MAX_ANS at data.py:11). A prompt over 208 characters cannot be read at all, so 'filters off' is not an option. Fit rows must pass the same caps as dev and be logged as a selection, not truncated (rule 7). The '62-word-piece' filter named in the idea was not found by grep in the custom_io code or docs. The dev family split has answers up to 12 characters that an 8-slot model cannot emit (data.py:102-103). Those rows should be wrong by construction (suggested; the scoring code was not read), so flag them in the labels.

Rule 1 and the R1 line are inaccurate for the keep decision. The keep decision applies to B2's final answer, which comes from the NUM or WORD path for about 70% of dev rows (shown: RESULT.json extra.coverage.all; ledger.py:384-405). 'GEN registers only; no NUM/WORD renderer used' is true only for the new code. The head's labels and scoring still depend on the renderers the deploy rule says to replace.

Arm (c) carries an information argument that does not fit arm (a). suggested: the data-processing argument says the answer string cannot carry more information than the registers and prompt it was computed from. Arm (a) has no registers, so a 0.05 AUROC gain of (c) over (a) shows learnability, not redundancy. Also, feeding answer strings through the reader is off the prompt distribution the reader was trained on (suggested). Drop the redundancy reading, or add the registers to (a) first.

The held-out splits are reused, and rule 5 needs the panel check. shown: variant, family and in_dist dev were scored in every B2 confirm run (RESULT.json per seed), so they are not fresh for a new decision. The 13-gram check is against train and dev only, and protected-panel hashes are not merged yet (shown: data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md lines 23, 128, 164). Fit rows must also pass the overlap13 index for the protected panels before use. If the generator can make fresh variant and family rows, use them for the held-out (untested).

Stage 1 cannot run in this container, and its cost is understated. shown: the default skills data root is a path not present here (reader/custom_io/data.py:7-9; the brief says sk200k is absent), and no skills generator is in the three code folders (grep found none). Stage 1 must run on Ben's PC. The 2 h estimate covers forward passes only. The fresh-row generation, the 13-gram index and the data copy are not costed (suggested: 3-4 h in all). CPU speed of B2 at 8 rounds and 208 characters is untested.

A cheaper gate should come first. On the six existing checkpoints, with no training, compute (i) within-variant AUROC of the free baseline (b), (ii) a mode-only keep rule (keep when the answer came from NUM or WORD, which control 1 can encode through the mode head), and (iii) random-abstain curves at matched share. If (i) already reaches 0.70 within variant, the learned head is unneeded. If (ii) reaches 45% exact among kept with a 20-80% keep share, arm (a)'s variant mark is confounded by answer mode. Per-mode accuracy on variant is not saved in the results (shown, by absence in RESULT.json), so this is untested. These checks cost minutes once dev rows are on the PC.

The stage 1 keep marks are not passable by chance, so the risk is confounding. suggested: a random keep at 50% gives about 35% exact among kept on variant with a standard error near 2 points, so the 45% mark sits about five standard errors above chance. The in_dist mark at 97% is similarly far from chance. The live risk is that answer mode or answer length drives the keep decision, which the mode-only check above tests.
critiques.rescue: (1) Run a no-training precheck on the six existing B2 checkpoints on CPU: within-variant AUROC of the free baseline, a mode-only keep rule, and random-abstain curves at matched share. Gate the rest on these. (2) Write the snapshot decode for arm (d) and report its label share before any fit. (3) Stage 1 arms: (a) head on control 1 (514 parameters); (a+) control 1 plus pooled registers, so it sees what (b) sees; (b) free register-confidence baseline; (c) string re-read; (d) self-labels. Pass marks on within-variant AUROC (at least 0.70 on each seed, and at least +0.03 over (b) on 5 of 6 seeds), with family as counts only and a pooled-5 no-drop guard across all five splits. (4) Report keep share per split, and name the class weighting and fit base rate as design constants. (5) Stage 2 as a head-only fine-tune on frozen B2, with a random-abstain arm matched to the abstain share on each split, the in_dist guard kept, and labels from arm (d) if the autonomy claim is kept. If retraining is needed, budget about 5 h. (6) Write explicit 'not shown' bands and a sign-safe (d) rule. (7) Use fresh generator variant and family rows for the held-out if the generator can make them.
critiques.already_tried: None of the probe or head has been run: the H1 stop head is unrun (architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:163) and the round readout is off in the B2 confirm (RESULT.json config). Nearest prior: the learned notebook gate in no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md (line 186), which is labelled by correctness against gold, so it is no self-label precedent. Dev numbers checked from results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200..s205/RESULT.json: in_dist 89.6-91.5, variant 31.9-37.1, family 0.6-2.5, answer 73.1-74.9, frame 85.9-89.0, vocab 86.3-88.8, loops:0 in_dist 0.00-10.81. critiques.expected_effect: If run as rescued, stage 1 would show whether the thinker's control state or its registers carry correctness on unseen variant kinds, against a free baseline and a mode-only rule, with no threshold claimed. A pass would support a keep head on B2 at 3.3M only (shown scope: B2 card experiments, rule 9). A fail on (a) with a pass on (a+) would point to the input, not the idea. Arm (d) passing would be the first evidence for rule-10 self-labels, but only at the AUROC level. Stage 2 would show a gain only above a matched random-abstain control. Nothing here shows the idea at hundreds of millions of parameters (shown: no such evidence in the brief). The expected outcome is uncertain (untested). chair.reasons: Worth a cheap sealed CPU probe, but not as written. (1) Cost and rules: the probe is CPU-only on six frozen B2 checkpoints (present at scratchpad/code/b2ckpt, seeds 200-205), adds 514 params (Linear(256,2); 1,026 if the 512-wide arm is used), and breaks no rule. R1 holds for new code (a head, no renderer). R2 holds (no teacher). R5 is fine because fit rows are fresh skills-generator rows scored on dev only; dev is never trained on. R7 holds if over-208-char prompts and over-8-char answers are dropped and counted, never cut. R9 holds (B2 only). Rule 10 holds only for the frozen-at-ship reading: argmax of a head fitted before ship is a build step, which rule 10 allows. The 'keeps learning from self-made labels' sentence has no deploy loop behind it and must be dropped or made a separate idea. (2) Value: it measures something nobody has measured, namely whether B2's own state or confidence separates right from wrong answers inside a split. No abstain, AUROC or keep-head work exists (all four critics grepped). A label-free 'I am stuck' signal is also what rules 8 and 10 need before creative tries can be triggered by the model (suggested). It is a modest English-talker idea: the only English it adds is '?'. It earns its place on cost, not on talker progress. (3) Checked in the code this session (shown, ledger.py): round_readout defaults to 0.0 (line 131); the round snapshot is (t, Z[:,1], Z[:,N_CTRL:], Rs, valid) taken only for t <= n-2 and holds no vals (line 341), so a NUM answer cannot be decoded from it without a hooked run(); zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]) feeds only mode_head (Linear(d,3)), the answer pointer and the word pointer (lines 342-345); GEN characters come from R = Z[:, N_CTRL:] through gen_copy (talk(), lines 380-406). So the critics are right that a head on zf alone cannot see the registers that write GEN answers, and that baseline (b) as written scores registers the model does not use on about 70% of rows (NUM 42.2%, WORD 27.9%, GEN 30.0%, shown in RESULT.json extra.coverage.all). (4) The marks as written are unsound, shown by arithmetic from the confirm RESULT.json means (variant exact 34.7, in_dist about 90.5). B2 scores about -30.6 per 100 variant rows under +1/0/-1, so 'variant score >= +10 over B2' is reached by random abstention at about 33% and by always-abstain. Keep share 0.80 at precision 0.97 on in_dist gives about 75.2 against about 81.0 for B2, which fails the stage-2 guard of -3. The 45% kept-exact mark is below the idea's own 50% break-even. Pooled variant+family AUROC is about 0.57 from split identity alone, and family has only 1-4 correct rows per seed. 'No tuned threshold' fails under shift: an argmax fitted on ~90%-right fresh rows is break-even only under that prior, so it may keep nearly every variant row. The arm (d) mark 'gain >= 0.8x gain of (a)' passes a negative gain. (5) Arm (d) is confounded with program length (steps are written at t=1..7 but the snapshot is at t<=6, so any 7-step row disagrees by construction) and its round-6 readouts are untrained. Test LR, the trained version, already failed on leak and stability (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:292). It is worth one report-first look and nothing more. (6) Stage 2 as written does not work. With B2 frozen, the registers cannot be made to write '?', and a constant '?' printed by code would be a renderer. A real ABSTAIN mode needs a retrain (about 3.7 h per run at par 3, shown by wall_s 13,318 in RESULT.json) or a full-model fine-tune. It must be a separate sealed idea after stage 1 passes. (7) Overlap: H1's 'settled' stop head (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md 8b-8c, unrun, also labelled against the target) and the D6 notebook gate. Opus should treat this as the measurement half of the same question and share the state-dump script. No fact-check by Haiku is needed; the open points are design fixes, not file facts.
chair.revised_idea:
talker-D5 (revised): a no-training precheck, then a six-seed CPU head probe, on frozen B2 seeds 200-205. Stage 2 (ABSTAIN mode) is removed from this idea and becomes a separate sealed idea that opens only if stage 1 passes.

Scope claim: only whether B2's own state or confidence separates right from wrong answers inside a split. It is not an English-talker gain and not a shippable abstain policy.

Step 0 (no training, minutes once dev rows are on the PC). For each seed, on dev in_dist (1,360), variant (1,320) and family (160, counts only):
- Record gold correctness and the decoded mode (talk(return_modes=True)).
- Compute a mode-aware free confidence c_b: the confidence of the path that actually emitted the answer. That is the max softmax of lans for NUM, the max softmax of lword (and lwend if span) for WORD, and the mean of the nine per-register max probabilities from gen_copy for GEN. Also compute the max softmax of lmode.
- Compute three more baselines. (i) A mode-only rule. (ii) A kind-prior from fit-row accuracy per generator family. (iii) A random-abstain curve at matched keep share.
- Report within-split AUROC for in_dist and variant separately. Pooled AUROC is not a gate.
- Report the round-6 label share for arm (d) by the model's own program length (non-noop ops written), using a hooked copy of run() that saves vals, applies ln_z to the snapshot Z[:,1], and decodes the full talk() output with its mode at round 6.
- Gate: if c_b already has within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 on >= 5 of 6 seeds, the learned head is not needed. Report 'free baseline suffices' and stop. That is a good outcome, and the baseline is itself autonomous.

Stage 1 (CPU, only if the gate does not stop it).
- Fit rows: about 8,000 fresh skills-generator rows from a new seed, through the same generator path B2 trained on, so its built-in filters stay. Drop and count prompts over 208 chars and answers over 8 chars. Do not cut them (data.py:107-109, rule 7). Log the 13-gram overlap with train and dev as a report. Fit with fixed L2 and fixed class weights, named as design constants. Cross-fit within the fresh rows for the in_dist numbers.
- Held-out: dev in_dist, variant and family, scored only, never trained on.
- Arms:
 (a) head on zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]), 514 params, gold labels (B2 exact match), used pre-ship only.
 (a+) head on zf plus pooled registers, Linear(512,2) = 1,026 params, gold labels.
 (b) the Step 0 mode-aware free baseline, no training.
 (d) self-label head on the same inputs as (a+). The label is 1 if the full decoded answer, including mode, at round 6 equals the final answer, else 0. Report-first: if the label share is outside 10-90% on any seed, or labels track own program length, mark (d) 'not shown'. Also fit a step-count-only control head.
 The hear-back arm (c) is dropped from this idea as a separate change. If it is ever run, its count is 1,026 and it must be given the registers first.
- Decision = argmax of two logits. Report keep share per split. Prior shift is expected, so a head fitted on ~90%-right rows may keep almost all variant rows.

Pass marks (fixed now, six seeds, within-split):
- M1: (a+) within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 on each of 6 seeds.
- M2: mean within-variant AUROC of (a+) minus the best of the free baselines (b), mode-only and kind-prior >= 0.03, with >= 5 of 6 seeds positive.
- M3 (in_dist, same rows): at the head's own argmax, in_dist score (+1/0/-1 per 100) within 3 of B2's always-answer score, with abstain share <= 15%.
- M4 (variant): at the head's own argmax and own keep share, variant score >= matched-rate random abstention + 5 per 100 on each seed, and kept-row exact >= 45%. Keep share must be 20-80%. If the AUROC marks pass but keep share is outside 20-80%, report 'ranking transfers, cutoff does not' and do not claim a threshold-free rule.
- M5: pooled-5 no-drop guard. Report all five splits (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab, variant) under the head's decisions. Do not gate on family AUROC.
- M6 (d): within-variant AUROC against gold correctness >= 0.65 on each seed, and mean AUROC beats the step-count-only control by >= 0.03. Report gain(d) over (b). The 'gain(d) >= 0.8x gain(a)' clause applies only when gain(a) > 0.

Proved wrong:
- (a+) within-variant AUROC < 0.60 on >= 3 of 6 seeds.
- (a+) no better than the best free baseline on average.
- Mean AUROC of (d) < 0.55 (round agreement carries no signal).
Between the pass and wrong lines the result is 'not shown'. A pass earns a 6-seed confirm of the same marks, not a claim.

Autonomy (rule 10). The deployed step is argmax of a head frozen at ship, with no run-time gold, threshold or gate. Gold labels are used pre-ship only, which is a build step. Arm (d) tests only whether a label-free signal exists. Round 6 is a fixed design constant. No 'keeps learning after ship' claim is made. That needs its own spec, tied to fast sleep D8, with a fixed buffer and fit interval and rows only from the model's own questions and tries.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must get these right.
1. Run Step 0 first. It needs no training and tells whether a learned head is needed at all. Gate the rest on it.
2. Score within split, never pooled. Variant has 421-490 correct rows per seed (shown). Family has 1-4 correct rows per seed (shown), so report family as counts only. Add a matched-rate random-abstain control and a mode-only rule to every comparison. The old +10 variant mark is reached by random abstention (variant score about -30.6 per 100 for B2, shown from RESULT.json means).
3. Baseline (b) and arm (d) must be defined for NUM, WORD and GEN rows. 70% of dev rows are not GEN, so use the confidence of the path that emitted the answer. Arm (a) must see the registers (arm a+), or its failure cannot be told apart from the wrong input.
4. For arm (d), write a hooked run() that saves vals per round, applies ln_z to the snapshot, and decodes the full talk() output with its mode. Report the label share by the model's own program length first. Include a step-count-only control. B2's round-6 readouts were never trained (round_readout 0.0, shown), so 'not shown' is a likely and acceptable outcome.
5. Fit rows: new-seed generator rows through B2's own generator path. Drop and count prompts over 208 chars and answers over 8 chars, with no truncation. Report the 13-gram overlap with train and dev. The data root sk200k is not in this container, so run on Ben's PC, and budget about 3-4 h including the build (suggested), not 2 h.
6. State that 'no tuned threshold' holds only if the keep share on variant lands in 20-80%. Otherwise report 'ranking transfers, cutoff does not'. Do not tune any cut on dev. Ovadia et al. 2019 (arXiv 1906.02530) is a suggested reference for the calibration-under-shift risk.
7. Keep stage 2 out of this test. A frozen B2 cannot write '?' through GEN registers, and a constant '?' printed by code would be a renderer. A real ABSTAIN mode needs a retrain (about 3.7 h per run at par 3, shown by wall_s) and its own sealed idea. That idea would use fresh generator rows named as abstain rows, gold answer targets kept separate from the ABSTAIN target, and a matched-rate random placebo.
8. Share the state-dump and extraction code with the H1 'settled' head (unrun, queue 49). Opus should dedupe the two as one probe on the same saved states.
9. Keep this on B2 (rule 9). Do not read it as evidence at hundreds of millions of parameters (none exists). Do not read it as talker progress: the only English added is '?'. A suggested extra use is a label-free stuck signal for the C1/C2 creative tasks under rules 8 and 10 (untested).
10. Label every number shown, suggested or untested. Everything about whether the control state or the registers carry correctness on held-out kinds is untested.

plan.title: Frozen B2 keep-or-not-sure probe (talker-D5, revised)
plan.ben_line: We test whether the model's own inner state can tell when its answer is probably wrong, using a tiny add-on that says keep or not sure. We count it only if it beats simple shortcuts like 'this kind of question is usually hard', and it does not make the model talk any better yet.
plan.question: Does frozen B2's final state (or its own answer confidence) separate its right answers from its wrong ones inside a split, beyond what question kind, answer mode, program length and answer length already predict? Scored only within split: in_dist (in-family, about 90% right, shown) and variant (unpractised sub-tasks, about 35% right, shown). Family (brand-new kinds, 1-4 right per seed, shown) is reported as counts only.
plan.one_change: One frozen linear keep-or-not-sure head on B2's final control state: arm (a), 514 parameters, and arm (a+), the same state plus the mean of the nine register vectors, 1,026 parameters (+0.02% to +0.03% of 3,302,481, inside rule 3). B2, its answers, its training and its scoring are unchanged. Step 0 changes nothing and trains nothing.
arms: Step 0 (no training, all six seeds, dev rows only). Free per-row scores: (c_b) mode-aware confidence of the path that emitted the answer: max softmax of lans for NUM, max softmax of lword for WORD, mean over the nine registers of the max of gen_copy p for GEN (ledger.py:239-249, 380-406); (lm) max softmax of lmode; (mode) accuracy prior by decoded mode; (len) accuracy prior by non-noop program length; (alen) accuracy prior by decoded answer length; (kind) accuracy prior by family. Priors use in_dist per-row accuracy as a stand-in for fit rows. Control only, not a baseline for marks: (plen) prompt length in characters.

Stage 1 (only if Step 0 does not stop; blocked until the panel check, see depends_on). (a) head on zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]), 514 params, gold labels (is_hit), pre-ship build only. (a+) head on [zf ; mean over k of ln_t(R_k)], 1,026 params, gold labels. (d) head on the same inputs as (a+), trained on self-labels only: label 1 if the decoded output at round 6, mode included and compared with the same norm as is_hit, equals the final decoded output; plus a step-count-only control head.

Matched-share comparators at each seed's own keep share q: random abstention (mean over 1,000 draws), kind prior, mode prior, and c_b. Each keeps the top q of rows by its own score, with ties broken at random and averaged over 1,000 draws. Scores are +1 right, 0 not-sure, -1 wrong, per 100 rows.
plan.seeds: B2 checkpoints 200-205, the six confirm seeds (s200 sha256 re-checked here: 94057436...). Step 0 and Stage 1 both run on all six seeds, so rule 4's six-seed count is met by the probe itself. An optional code screen on seeds 200-201 may run first; it is a screen only, since M2 needs 5 of 6 seeds. The confirm (after a pass) uses the same marks on the same six checkpoints with fresh fit rows and fresh variant and in_dist rows drawn with a new generator seed. If the generator cannot draw variant rows, the confirm reuses dev and is labelled lower weight.
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC. The dev data root and the skills generator are there, not in this container: data.py:8-9 points at another session's scratch folder (sk200k), which is absent here (shown). CPU is the planned device for the 3.3M-parameter model; forward-pass timing is untested. No GPU or rented compute is needed.
pass_marks: Gate (Step 0, no training): stop and report 'free signal suffices' if any free baseline (c_b, lm, mode, len, alen, kind) reaches within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 AND within-kind AUROC >= 0.60 on >= 5 of 6 seeds. The kind prior cannot pass the within-kind half, because it is constant inside a family.
M1: head (a+) within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 on each of 6 seeds. Pooled AUROC is not used as a gate.

M1b (added): head (a+) within-kind AUROC >= 0.60 on each seed, pooled over the mixed variant families only (families with 1 to 39 correct; 23 to 28 per seed, about 6,200 to 7,100 within-family pairs, shown from RESULT.json counts). Pairs are counted inside a family only.

M2: mean over seeds of [(a+) within-variant AUROC minus the best free baseline on that seed] >= +0.03, and positive on >= 5 of 6 seeds. Baselines are every Step 0 score except the prompt-length control.

M3 (in_dist guard): at the head's own argmax, in_dist score >= B2 always-answer in_dist score minus 3 on each seed (always-answer is about +79 to +83 per 100, shown from exact 89.6 to 91.5); not-sure share on in_dist <= 15%.

M4 (variant): at the head's own argmax, keep share q in [0.20, 0.80] on each seed; variant score >= matched-share random + 5, >= matched-share kind prior + 5, and >= matched-share mode prior + 5, each on each seed; kept-row exact >= 45% on each seed. If only the keep-share window fails, report 'ranking transfers, cutoff does not' and claim no rule.
M5 (pooled guard): pooled-5 score under the head's decisions >= B2 always-answer pooled-5 score minus 3 on each seed. All five splits (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab, variant) are reported.

M6 (arm d): round-6 self-label share between 10% and 90% on each seed (else 'not shown'); (d) within-variant AUROC against gold correctness >= 0.65 on each seed, and its mean >= the step-count-only control's AUROC + 0.03.
plan.proved_wrong: (i) (a+) within-variant AUROC < 0.60 on 3 or more of 6 seeds; (ii) mean within-kind AUROC of (a+) <= 0.55, i.e. no within-kind skill; (iii) mean M2 difference <= 0, i.e. no better than the best free baseline; (iv) mean within-variant AUROC of (d) < 0.55, i.e. agreement across rounds carries no correctness signal. Between the pass and wrong lines the result is 'not shown'. A pass earns the fresh-row confirm, not a claim: the dev splits have been scored in every B2 confirm run (shown), so a pass is a probe result.
plan.null_risk: Partly yes, if the marks are sealed as first drafted. (1) M4 against random abstention alone is passed by a kind prior. Using B2's own in_dist per-family accuracy as a stand-in for fit-row priors (computed here from RESULT.json counts; a proxy, not the fit-row prior, shown), keeping the top 40 to 60% of variant rows by family gains +6 to +16 per 100 over matched-share random on all six seeds. That is why matched-share kind and mode comparators are required. (2) Correctness on variant is concentrated by kind: 2 to 3 families are all right and 3 to 7 all wrong per seed (shown). The in-sample per-family oracle gives within-variant AUROC 0.87 to 0.90 (shown; in-sample, so an upper bound on kind identity, not a fair baseline). The in_dist-prior proxy gives within-variant AUROC 0.62 to 0.69 (shown proxy). So M1 is a near miss for a kind-only head, and M1b is the mark a kind-only head cannot pass, since a kind prior is constant inside a family. (3) The M1b null is about 0.50 with SE about 0.02 (suggested, from about 24 mixed families with about 20 right and 20 wrong each). (4) Residual: within-kind skill can come from prompt length, number count, or digit-loss errors (D0 shows place-9 loss in the pooled span, 65 to 83%, shown in no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT) rather than from knowing the answer. The controls report this; it is a limit, not a pass. (5) M3 and M5 are passed by a head that keeps nearly everything. The 20 to 80% keep window in M4 blocks that. (6) Round-6 labels are untested. round_readout defaults to 0.0 (ledger.py:131, 140; shown), so the heads were never trained on round-6 states and the label may be near-constant. (7) The variant split and in_dist have been reused in every confirm run (shown), so the marks are fixed but the data is not fresh. My estimate (suggested, not measured): a kind-only head sits below 0.70 on most seeds and fails M1b on all; a head with no real state signal fails M1b and M4 on most seeds. Whether any within-kind state signal exists is untested.
plan.autonomy: The deployed model does every step itself. It reads the prompt with its own reader, runs its fixed rounds (8 today, a design constant to be replaced by H1 later), writes its answer with its own heads as it does now, and then the frozen keep head reads its own final control state and returns keep or not-sure by argmax. No run-time gold, threshold, gate or dev-tuned value is used. Build-time only, before ship: fitting the head on generator rows with gold labels (arms a and a+), and the fixed L2 and class weights written in the sealed queue file. Probe-only, never shipped: the kind, mode, length and answer-length priors (the kind prior needs family names the deployed model does not have), the round-6 label, and the hand scorer is_hit (allowed as a test under rule 1). Arm (d) is the only label-free head; it tests whether a self-label signal exists and claims no learning after ship. What not-sure does at deployment is not defined here and needs its own spec, with no hand-written string. Residues: the fixed 8 rounds, and the argmax equals a 0.5 cut only if the head is calibrated on the deployment distribution. That calibration is untested on variant (suggested: an in-family fit usually keeps too many out-of-family rows). After any T1 or O1 change the state moves, so the head is re-fit as a build step, not at deploy.

Write a hooked, read-only copy of run() in a new probe file; ledger.py is not edited. It must: (a) add vals to each round's snapshot, since the existing snapshot tuple at ledger.py:341 omits vals and the NUM path needs them in talk() (ledger.py:384-399); (b) apply ln_z to the raw Z[:,1], because ledger.py:342 does this only at the final round; (c) index snapshots by t, since the list starts at t=0 (ledger.py:340 has no lower bound); (d) decode round 6 with the same logic as talk() (mode_head at ledger.py:149, then NUM, WORD or GEN). Step 0, per row, dev only (family as counts only): split, family, is_hit (evalx.is_hit against row['accepted']), decoded mode, non-noop program length (ops != NOOP in out['prog']; steps are written only at t=1 to 7, progparse.py N_RES = 7), decoded answer length, prompt length, number count, c_b, max softmax of lmode, and the round-6 self-label (norm-equal to the final output). Save per seed in a results folder.

Step 0 scores, no training. Within-variant AUROC, within-kind AUROC (pairs inside each mixed family only), and in_dist AUROC for every baseline; matched-share scores for random, kind, mode and c_b; the round-6 label share by program length, with the step-count AUROC against the label. The priors (mode, length, answer length, kind) use in_dist per-row accuracy as the stand-in for fit rows. Apply the Step 0 gate. If it stops the run, report 'free signal suffices' and do not claim a learned head.

Extract per row: zf (256, after ln_z), the mean over the nine registers of ln_t(R_k) (256), gold label = is_hit, self-label = round-6 decoded output equals the final decoded output. Report the self-label share on fit rows first. Arm (d) needs 10% to 90% on each seed.

Fit with fixed L2 and fixed class weights written in the queue file: (a) 514 params, (a+) 1,026 params, (d) on the same inputs as (a+) using self-labels only, plus the step-count-only control head. No dev row is used for any choice. No cross-fit is needed, because every scored row is dev and never trained on.

Score held-out dev (never trained on): within-variant AUROC, within-kind AUROC and in_dist AUROC; the baselines with fit-row priors; keep share and kept precision per split; matched-share comparisons at each seed's own keep share; the M3 and M5 guards; family as counts only. Apply M1 to M6 and the proved-wrong lines in the sealed order.
Screen first on seeds 200 and 201 as a code check, not a claim (M2 needs 5 of 6 seeds). Then run all six seeds with the same marks.

Confirm after a pass: the same marks on the same six checkpoints, with fresh fit rows and fresh variant and in_dist rows from a new generator seed, sealed before the run. If the generator cannot draw variant rows, reuse dev and mark it lower weight.

fixed_plan.title: B2 keep-or-not-sure probe, staged (frozen B2)
fixed_plan.ben_line: We check whether the model's own final state can tell when one of its answers is probably wrong, using one tiny frozen add-on. We count it only if it beats simple shortcuts such as how hard a question family usually is and how long the prompt is, and it does not claim to make the model talk better.
fixed_plan.question: Does frozen B2's final control state separate right answers from wrong ones within the same question family on the variant split (scored within family), beyond what prompt length, number count, answer length, answer mode, program length and family prior already predict?
fixed_plan.one_change: One frozen 2-class linear keep head (514 params = 2x256+2) on B2's final control state zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]). B2's weights, answers and scoring are unchanged. Arm (a) is the only primary arm. Arms (a+) and (d) are secondary, with their own marks, and cannot rescue (a).
arms: Step 0 (no training, dev rows only, all six seeds, after a 200-201 screen): free baselines c_b (registers up to first EOS only), lm, mode, len, alen, kind, plen (prompt length), number count. Each is scored within variant and within kind.
Primary (a): head on zf, 514 params, labels is_hit, fit on generator train-pool rows only. Hard overlap gate against all scored dev rows and protected hashes.
Secondary (a+): head on [zf ; mean over the nine registers of ln_t(R_k)], 1,026 params. Own marks, no rescue.

Secondary (d): same inputs as (a+), self-labels only (round-6 decode equals final decode), with a step-count-only control head of 2 params. Reported as the only label-free candidate. Claims no learning after ship.

Comparators at the head's own keep share q, with q set on the variant split and stated in the sealed file: random (1,000 draws), kind prior, mode prior, c_b, plen, number count, alen. All priors fit on the same fit rows.
fixed_plan.seeds: B2 checkpoints 200-205 (all six sha256 match, checked here). Code screen on seeds 200-201 is only a screen (rule 4). A pass claim needs all six seeds with identical marks.
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's PC. Reproduce the RESULT.json counts on the GPU in bf16 (the RESULT path, shown). A CPU fp32 path is allowed for head fitting only after features are saved from the GPU run, or after a measured bf16-vs-fp32 flip count sets the tolerance. Respect the GPU-BUSY lock while queue 39 or 40 runs.
pass_marks: M0 reproduction: per-split correct counts match RESULT.json within a tolerance set from measured flips (default 5 rows for in_dist and variant, 2 for family), on the GPU bf16 path. The hooked final-round decode equals talk() on 100% of rows of every split and seed, else stop.

HARD GATE (new): zero exact prompt matches and zero shared 13-word windows between fit rows and every scored dev row (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab, variant, family), and zero protected-panel hits. Counts reported per split.
Step 0 gate: stop with 'free signal suffices' if any free baseline (c_b, lm, mode, len, alen, plen, number count) has within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 AND within-kind AUROC >= 0.60 on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
M1 (a): within-variant AUROC >= 0.70 on each seed. Near-miss for a kind-only head (proxy 0.622-0.685, shown), so M1 alone never passes the probe.
M1b (a): within-kind AUROC >= 0.60 on each seed AND >= the best of plen, number count and alen within-kind AUROC + 0.03 (new numeric control).

M2 (a): mean over seeds of [within-variant AUROC minus the best free baseline, over ALL listed baselines including plen, number count, kind] >= +0.03, positive on >= 5 of 6 seeds, and the family-cluster paired bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 (new).
M3 in_dist guard (unchanged): in_dist score >= always-answer in_dist score minus 3 on each seed; not-sure share on in_dist <= 15%.

M4 variant (unchanged, q now stated): keep share q in [0.20, 0.80] on each seed; variant score >= matched-share random + 5, >= kind + 5, >= mode + 5, >= plen-based + 5, on each seed; kept-row exact >= 45% on each seed. If only the window fails, report 'ranking transfers, cutoff does not' and claim no rule.
M5 pooled guard (unchanged): pooled-5 under head decisions >= always-answer pooled-5 minus 3 on each seed. All five splits reported.
M6 (d): round-6 self-label share between 10% and 90% on each seed, else 'not shown'. (d) within-variant AUROC >= 0.65 on each seed and its mean >= the step-count-only control AUROC + 0.03.
Secondary (a+): the same marks as (a), reported as secondary.

Between the pass and wrong lines the result is 'not shown'. A pass earns the fresh-row confirm, not a claim.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Recomputed from RESULT.json (shown): in-distribution kind-prior proxy gives within-variant AUROC 0.622 to 0.685, within 0.02 to 0.08 of the 0.70 mark, so M1 can be passed by family identity. A kind prior alone beats matched-share random by +6.3 to +16.2 per 100 rows at keep shares 0.4 to 0.6, so a random-only M4 is weak. Family oracle (in-sample) AUROC 0.874 to 0.902 is an upper bound on family identity only. Mixed families 23 to 28 per seed and within-kind pairs 6,194 to 7,095 (shown). Two to three families are all right and three to seven all wrong per seed (shown); 920 to 1,120 of 1,320 variant rows sit in mixed families (shown). Suggested: the M1b null SE is about 0.02 from about 24 family clusters, but the honest CI is a family-cluster bootstrap. Residual: within-kind skill may be prompt length, number count or digit loss (D0 place-9 loss, shown). The numeric controls in M1b and M2 are what separate that from state signal.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Build-time only: the head is fit on generator fit rows with gold labels (pre-ship training, allowed). The deployed model runs its fixed 8 rounds (a design constant), reads its own final control state, and returns keep or not-sure by argmax of frozen weights. No runtime gold, no dev-tuned threshold, no hand-written not-sure string. Argmax equals a 0.5 cut only if the head is calibrated on deployment-like rows; that is untested on variant and is what the M4 window checks. The not-sure action has no deploy spec and must get one before any shipping claim (rule 10). Arm (d) is the only label-free candidate, and its round-6 label is untested (round_readout default 0.0, ledger.py:131, 140). Any change to T1 or O1 moves the state, so the head is refit as a build step.
steps: Step 0a, seal first: write a dated queue file with all marks; the L2 value (chosen by family-grouped CV on fit rows only); balanced class weights; 8 fixed rounds; round 6 used only for the label; 1,000 draws; tie rule; keep window; the split that sets q; the step-count-control definition; and the not-shown bands. Nothing runs before this file exists.

Step 0b, reproduce counts: evalx.evaluate(..., return_preds=True) on the GPU in bf16 (matching the RESULT run's --bf16 on cuda) for in_dist, variant and family, seeds 200-205. Compare with RESULT.json. Any CPU fp32 run first measures its flip count against the GPU run on seed 200 and sets the tolerance from that.

Step 0c, hooked read-only run() in a new probe file (ledger.py untouched): snapshots at t=1..6 (not t=0; ledger.py:319 skips t=0); add vals to each snapshot (ledger.py:341 omits it); apply ln_z to Z[:,1] per snapshot (ledger.py:342 does this only at the end); decode round 6 with the talk() logic, including NUM which needs vals. Check: the final-round decode equals talk() on 100% of rows for every split and seed, else stop.

idea.title: One traced pass: does B2's own NOOP or confidence give a free stop?
idea.summary: Run each screen checkpoint once for 16 rounds, keep every round's answer, op, NOOP probability and confidence, then replay stop rules offline. It measures NOOP onset against program length, the cost of freezing at the NOOP round, and the AUROC of the model's own confidence. It says whether a zero-parameter stop exists for program rows (the NOOP B2 already trains) and for the 59% of rows with no program, before any stop is built. Shown ceiling for any stop inside 8 rounds is about 2 in-dist points, so the value is compute saving and the rule-10 path, not accuracy.
idea.change: New script custom_io/probe_trace.py (copy of probe_loops.py; no edit to ledger.py). Per batch of 128 rows sorted by prompt length, call m.run(batch, loops=16, rounds=True) once under no_grad. Snapshot t is the state after K=t+1 loops, so one run holds all K. Re-apply mode_head, the answer pointer (q_ans, k_slot, valid) and word pointer to ln_z(Z[:,1]) of each snapshot; take op argmax from out['steps'] (rounds 2 to 8 only). Save per-row arrays (probe_loops.py computes them in memory but writes aggregates only): exact_r, answer string per round, mode_p_r, pointer top-1 and entropy, noop_p_r, op_r, and gold program length L (used for grouping only). Arms scored offline: (a) round 8; (b) NOOP stop, t* = first non-NOOP-after-write round, answer read at K=t*+1 and K=t*+2, rows with no t* read at 8; (c) answer-agreement stop for no-program rows (first K>=4 with identical answers at K-2, K-1, K); (d) rows whose step-1 op is NOOP read at pass 6, others at 8; (e) AUROC of conf_r (mode_p times pointer top-1; GEN rows use mean top-1 over the 9 registers), mode_p, ans_top and step-1 NOOP probability for 'already right at r' and 'settled by r' on the 4,007 no-program rows; (f) argmax-confidence over passes 2 to 8 as a selection arm. Extend scoring from in_dist to the five dev splits and chain-5, and add a robust overthinking count (wrong at 8, right at both K and K+1) to price the prize on variant, answer, frame and vocab. Self-check: per-K exact from the trace must equal untraced evaluate at K=8 and 16 on the same machine. Params 0.
idea.why: Halting alone is capped near 2 in-dist points and about 0.6 pooled-5 points, and 94 to 95% of the overthinking rows and the whole 16-minus-8 loss sit in no-program rows, which carry NOOP targets only at weight 0.1. For program rows the model already trains NOOP after the last write at weight 1.0 but nothing reads it. Freezing program rows at the NOOP round itself costs -3.4 and -5.7 points because the answer heads are only trained at round 8, while one settle round later is nearly free (-0.1 to -0.24 points, 15% of rounds saved). So the open question is whether the model's existing outputs mark the right stop round on each row type; this probe answers it in about an hour on CPU and decides whether ideas 5 and 7 are worth building.

P1: first post-write NOOP at round L+1 on at least 90% of L=1..6 rows, premature at most 2%, false-freeze (L=0 rows that write then say NOOP) at most 2%. problems: [shown] Index convention is inconsistent and P2 is ambiguous. ledger.py:307 runs `for t in range(n)` (0-based). Step t is written at loop index t=1..7 (ledger.py:319). Snapshot t is taken after t+1 loops (ledger.py:340, t<=n-2). The idea reads op argmax at 'rounds 2 to 8' (1-based) but writes P1 as 'round L+1' (0-based). Under 0-based, the NOOP after L writes is index L+1, so K=t*+2 = L+3, which PROBE.json M1 already measured (-0.24 and -0.10 overall). Under 1-based, t*+2 = L+4, which M1 never measured. Rule 10 allows hand code only as an outside tool the model chooses by writing text. The idea's 'no threshold' claim does not cover the fixed offset or the fixed pass cap. A deployable stop must be learned (for example a stop head trained on the model's own per-round readout, as H1 in redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 8b) or a text action the model writes.

critiques.expected_effect: If the spec is fixed and the marks are sealed: on the two screen checkpoints, a per-row NOOP-based stop would show whether program rows (41% of in_dist) can stop at L+3 for about 0.1 to 0.3 points, saving 37.5% of their rounds (15.4% of all in_dist rounds at gold L, shown from PROBE.json by_len n counts). The no-program signal would be measured but not established. The accuracy prize is bounded near 2 to 3 in_dist points (oracle 2.5-2.7, shown, not deployable). Expected outcome: the program-row stop is cheap, the no-program stop is uncertain, and the H1 verdict is untested here.

problems: Step 1, program rows (L=1..6). The stop decision is the model's own op argmax with no threshold, so it is autonomous in form (shown: NOOP is op index 0, progparse.py OPS; trained at weight 1.0 via w_row at ledger.py:501). But the chosen offset, 'read at K=t*+2' (one settle round after the NOOP), is a constant taken from the dev curve. The figures behind it (-3.38/-5.69 at K=L+2, -0.24/-0.10 at K=L+3) come from PROBE.json M1 by_len on the same 6,800 dev rows the arm is scored on. A constant tuned on dev answers does not count under the rule. Not autonomous as written.

Round indexing is not pinned, and an index slip is worth about 3 points by the idea's own numbers. Shown: the loop index t is 0-based (ledger.py:307; snapshot at :341 is the state after K=t+1 loops; docstring ledger.py:6-8 says K iterations give K-1 writes). Step s is predicted at K=s+1, so the first NOOP after L steps appears at K=L+2. The idea writes P1 as 'round L+1', the op list as 'rounds 2 to 8', and the change section as 'first non-NOOP-after-write round', which inverts 'first post-write NOOP' in the test section.

Coverage hole: no NOOP stop exists for 7-step programs. Shown: gold() builds op with N_RES=7 columns (ledger.py:435-436) and the step loop covers steps 1..7 only (ledger.py:319, :324). So L=7 rows never get a NOOP target: 28 of 6,800 rows (PROBE.json M1 n_by_len). That is small here, but 'the NOOP B2 already trains' overstates it, and under the 8a rung (11 steps) the longest programs would again have no stop target.

The answer at the stop comes from a head never trained at that round. Shown: round_readout defaults to 0 (ledger.py:131, :140), so the answer, mode and word heads train only at the final round K=8 (ledger.py:500, :532). Reading at K=t*+1 or t*+2 uses an untrained readout, which is why the freeze costs 3-6 points. The model decides when to stop by itself, but the answer it gives then is one it was never trained to give. The autonomous fix is a per-round answer loss restricted to the NOOP round and one round later. The idea does not propose it.

Freeze and saving are not built. Shown: run() passes every row through all n rounds with no per-row stop (ledger.py:306-307, :341-345). The '15% of rounds' figure is a per-row count from probe data, not a batch saving. A batch early exit saves nothing while any row in the batch is still running. A per-row mask is a build step, allowed, and once built the model's own NOOP drives it. The value is compute, not accuracy.

No-program rows (L=0; 4,007 of 6,800 rows, 59%) have no trained stop. Shown: their NOOP is trained at weight 0.1 (ledger.py:130 w_noop default, :501). Arm (d), 'step-1 NOOP then read at pass 6', therefore relies on a signal given at one-tenth weight. The 6.82-pass cost estimate is a gold-branch reanalysis, and the predicted-branch test is untested (the idea says so). Pass 6 is a dev-picked number.

Arm (c), answer agreement over three rounds starting at K>=4, is autonomous in form (the model compares its own answers). But the window of 3 and the start K>=4 are hand constants with no design source. The start looks taken from the no-program curve (PROBE.json M1 by_len['0'], K=1..8: 51.8, 68.8, 77.3, 81.8, 83.4, 83.7, 83.9, 84.0). Under the rule these must be fixed before the run with a stated reason, or learned.

Arm (f), argmax of confidence over passes 2-8, has a developer-chosen window (the idea's own rules_check calls it a developer-chosen selection). The confidence at K!=8 comes from heads trained only at K=8 (item 4), so it is not a score the model was taught to calibrate. Argmax needs no threshold, but both the window and the untrained readout must be fixed first.

Arm (e), AUROC of four confidence scores, measures ranking only. Any deployed use needs a cutoff. A cutoff chosen so that some rule passes P3 is a threshold tuned on dev answers, which the rule forbids. The idea names no cutoff that is set without dev answers. H1 uses a fixed 0.5 'not tuned on any data' (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 8b), but this idea does not adopt it. So the no-program path has no autonomous stop in sight beyond the hand constants in (c) and (d).

P3 is a 'some zero-parameter rule' gate. Whichever of (c), (d) or (f) passes is picked on dev and then deployed with its dev-picked constants, which is the pattern the rule excludes. The screen seeds 100/101 are also the seeds whose M1 curves produced the arm design, so the test is in-sample. A verdict needs one rule fixed in advance and scored on held-out seeds (200/201 on Ben's PC).

Measurement mismatch on the no-program path. Every K!=8 readout here is untrained (item 4). A deployed model trained with per-round answer loss would have a different K-curve; the brief reports that Test LR moved loops:0 leak to 15.88 on seed 200 (shown per brief; RESULTS-EG2.md not reread here). A P3 pass on these checkpoints says nothing about the model a per-round build would ship. The idea must name which training it describes.

Generalisation is not tested. The NOOP onset is learned from the same generator family as in_dist, and the probe's lengths come from progparse on the same rows. P1 names L=1..6 rows without naming a split, and P2 names in_dist and chain-5 only. No mark covers variant, frame or vocab, where B2 is reported to miss most (shown per brief; not rechecked). For a new kind the NOOP head has no training, so the stop is not shown to transfer. This is the 'learning a new kind' part of the rule (PLAN-AND-MARKS section 0).

Transfer to the rule-1 build. The NOOP stop is read from B2's in-forward executor (ledger.py:76-86, inside the forward pass). Ben's rule 1 says the calculator moves outside as a tool (T1). In tool.py the NOOP means 'no call' (op 0 is skipped at tool.py:175-176). The loop is still 8 fixed rounds with calls at rounds 1-7 (tool.py:162). So a B2 pass does not carry to T1 without a rerun, and T1 is the build the rule applies to.

The trace cannot be built with 'no edit to ledger.py' as the idea says. Shown: the snapshot tuple (ledger.py:341) holds the control-1 vector, registers, Rs and valid but not vals. talk() prints NUM answers from vals (ledger.py:380-392). So per-round answer strings (the V check and arms a-d) need either a changed run() or a re-implemented executor, and the idea must say which. Snapshots also stop at t<=n-2 (ledger.py:340), so K=16 must come from the final output, not a snapshot.

Scope against the autonomy goal. The idea only stops early inside a fixed cap of 8. It cannot test 'think longer when stuck': the 16-round run is negative (PROBE.json M1 all, K=16 88.2 and 89.7 vs K=8 89.4 and 90.5; shown). Plan 2a row 1 ('fixed 8 thinking rounds' must become learned halting) stays open for the 59% no-program rows. Calling the cap 'a fixed architecture constant' reclassifies that row without the plan's sign-off.

Verdict wording overclaims a two-seed screen. 'FREE STOP EXISTS' and 'NO-PROGRAM SIGNAL EXISTS' would gate building ideas 5 and 7 on seeds 100/101, which rule 4 treats as a screen only (6 or more paired seeds for a claim). These should read as screen verdicts, with no build decision until a held-out confirm exists.
