idea.title: Which parts of B2's loop are used: blocks, reader, scratch
idea.summary: Zero-training hooks on the two screen checkpoints: skip or swap each controller block, blind the thinker to the reader from round 2, 5 or 9, zero controls 2 to 7 on seeds 100 and 101, and record per-round relative state change, per-slot norm profile and participation ratios. Each outcome gates a named later run: unique-block depth, scratch room, late reader attention, a narrower MLP.
idea.change: One probe script, no model edit. (a) Replace core[b].forward by identity at all rounds, or at rounds 2-8 only, or replace core[1] by a second copy of core[0]. (b) Pre-hook each CBlock with a per-block call counter and set mask[:, 27:] = False from round r on (r = 2, 5, 9), and recompute the softmax mass on the 27 workspace columns versus reader columns per round. (c) evaluate(m, rows, lesion='ctl27') on seeds 100 and 101 (already coded, ledger.py:315-316, 410). (d) Forward hook on core[-1] and pre-hook on core[0] on a 512-row sample for rounds 1-16: relative change ||Z_t[i]-Z_{t-1}[i]||/||Z_{t-1}[i]|| for control 0, control 1 and the mean of registers; RMS of each of the 17 slots with max/median ratio; participation ratio of the MLP GELU input, reader output and controller state. Outputs reported per stratum (L=0, L>=1, chain-5). Params 0.
idea.why: The 8a plan spends on depth-first growth (8 blocks), W2 asks for 16 scratch tokens, W1 changes reader features, and none of these has a usage measurement. The A register loop lost its chain-5 when the prompt was cut after round 1, but B2 was never tested that way. Only the small-cost outcome of a lesion is decisive because a removed part also shifts the residual scale.

Internal contradiction in the decision rule. The why-field says only the small-cost outcome is decisive because lesions shift the residual scale, but 'late reader needed' (cost at least 2.0 and share at least 0.5) and 'scratch used' (in_dist change at most -1.0) are decided on large costs. The project already calls eval-only read-stop lesions confounded (custom_io/design/design-latent-reread.md:213; custom_io/research/code-map.md:124-127, the zero_pool note), and names trained read_once as the clean route (design-latent-reread.md:215-216). Round 9 arm is a no-op at the default 8 loops. Iteration indices run t = 0..n_loops-1 (custom_io/models/ledger.py:6 docstring; the loop is range(n) with n = 8 at ledger.py ~306-307), so reader blind from round 9 never fires. The idea also mixes 1-based round labels (rounds 2-8, round 9) with the code's 0-based t, so 'skip core[1] at rounds 2-8' is ambiguous at the last round. (shown)

The 'settled' mark measures residual scale growth that the heads ignore. Relative change ||Z_t - Z_{t-1}|| / ||Z_{t-1}|| counts norm growth. PROBE.json results[].M5.ctrl_rms (seeds 100 and 101, 512 rows) gives the eight-control RMS as 28.0 to 32.4 (+16%) at round 7 to 8 and 32.4 to 36.8 (+14%) at round 8 to 9 (seed 101 has the same pattern: 23.6, 27.3, 31.0). By the triangle inequality, norm growth of that size alone forces a relative change of about 0.13 to 0.16 if controls 0 and 1 grow with the mean, above the 0.10 'not settled' line. M5 averages over controls 0-7, so the applicability to controls 0 and 1 is untested. The heads read ln_z(Z[:,0]) and ln_z(Z[:,1]) (ledger.py run()), so scale does not reach them. Use a LayerNorm-centred cosine change instead. (shown from PROBE.json and ledger.py; bound computed)

The reader-share mark has a uniform-attention baseline. Reader columns are every prompt character (mask = cat(valid, xm) in run(), ledger.py ~311), and the workspace has at most 27 valid columns. Uniform attention gives a reader share of T/(T+V), which is above 0.5 whenever the prompt has more characters than valid slots. So 'needed: share at least 0.5' is passed by near-uniform attention, and 'not needed: share below 0.2' needs strong focus on slots. Report share against the uniform baseline, per head. (shown by code; baseline arithmetic computed)

Confounds the marks do not name. (a) Masking reader columns renormalises the softmax over the 27 slots, so the cost mixes 'not read' with 'attention mass moved'. (b) S0, built before the loop, already holds the pooled reader term for every number (run(), before the loop), so a reader blind leaves number values reachable; the lesion tests only controller letter reads. (c) The per-block pre-hook needs a round counter that resets per batch (each block runs once per round per batch, ledger.py:313-314), which the idea does not mention. Effect sizes are untested. (shown by code)

problems: Autonomy overclaim (shown: the idea's autonomy field). It says a deployed loop 'could skip late reader attention and the model would decide that itself'. A skip or blind fixed at build time is a researcher's design constant, not a self-decision. A per-row decision would need a learned gate, which D4 neither builds nor measures. D4 reports batch averages at fixed rounds (mean blind cost, mean reader share), so it cannot show that any row needs or skips late reader reads. As a pre-ship diagnostic it adds no deploy-time step, so it passes rule 10 on that basis (suggested; the directive treats build-time steps as not deploy steps).

The reader-blind arm does not blind the numbers (shown: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py:199-208 parses numbers with progparse.py:14 NUM_RE; ledger.py:292-296 puts the exact values and a pooled reader term into S0 before the loop; ledger.py:311 builds mask = cat([valid, xm]), so mask[:, 27:] = False removes only the per-round cross-attention to reader letters). So 'late rounds do not read the prompt' or 'loop needs text after round 2' can only mean letters and words. The regex number step is hand-written code between question and answer (rule 1; the code notes flag it). D4 leaves it in place and does not record it as an unmeasured hand step.

Round indexing is ambiguous and one arm is a no-op (shown: ledger.py:307 runs t = 0..n-1 with n = 8; steps are written only for 1 <= t <= 7 at ledger.py:319). At 8 rounds there is no round 9, so 'reader blind from round 9' is identical to the intact run and wastes a run. 'Skip core[1] at rounds 2-8' and 'reader share at rounds 5-8' also change meaning between 0-based and 1-based counting. The per-block call counter must map call index to round (two block calls per round, ledger.py:313-314).

Middle zones are undefined for every gate. Block skip: core[1] cost between 1.0 and 5.0. The reader-share criterion is not calibrated. Prompt length is capped at 208 characters per the code notes (data.py:11). That share is above 0.5 for any prompt longer than 27 characters. So 'share at least 0.5' is met by spread attention, and 'share below 0.2' needs strong preference for workspace slots. Suggested fix: report share minus the uniform baseline T/(T+27), per prompt-length bucket.

The marks exist only in this idea text. Project practice is a dated addendum in custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md before a run, and probe_loops.py records that its gates were fixed before it ran. Seal D4's marks there, with the data set for each, before running. Otherwise the 'fixed in advance' claim cannot be checked.

The hour estimate is untested. results/40-loops-probe/probe.log records no timing. At 8 rounds the design has 8 new arms x 2 seeds = 128 round-passes per row, or 144 with the intact arm. The two-seed M1 probe is 272 (136 per checkpoint, K = 1..16), so D4 is about half of M1. Intact can be reused from M1's K = 8 column (89.4 and 90.5). The 16-round readouts on 512 rows are negligible. It fits in 16 GB trivially (3.3M params; CPU is enough). Shown by arithmetic. The brief's 'B2 at 3M about 1 hour per 24,000 updates' conflicts with the fact-check median of 1.54 PC-h and the logged 1.0 to 4.2 h. Use about 1.5 PC-h for any gated follow-up training run.

Hook mechanics need care. (a) An instance-level forward override is dispatched through self.forward, so it should work. Suggested: confirm by counting calls. (b) Per-block call counters must reset at each run() call. evalx.evaluate calls generate, and so run(), once per batch (evalx.py:37-48), so round indexes drift across batches otherwise. (c) The mask is edited in place on a tensor shared by both blocks in a round. This is correct because the mask is rebuilt each round (ledger.py:311). (d) The real signature is evalx.evaluate(model, rows, batch_size, device, lesion, return_preds) (evalx.py:37), not evaluate(m, rows, lesion=...).

Only round 8 is in the trained regime. Label rounds 9-16 as out of regime.

Missing wiring checks. There is no null control that must give exactly zero change. Add a pass-through hook that must reproduce intact on every row, and a loop-blind-from-round-0 arm that should collapse chain-5. These show the hooks act at all.

chair.reasons:
Verdict: plan, as a narrower sealed probe. It is cheap (CPU only, 0 params, no training, nothing on the answer path), and it breaks none of Ben's rules. Rule 10 holds only if the autonomy text is rewritten (see the revised idea). It is the first usage measurement of B2's blocks, late reader reads and scratch controls, and no result like that exists (all four critics agree and found no block-skip or reader-blind run anywhere).

Confirmed by me from the code and files (shown): (1) CBlock.forward is fully residual (ledger.py lines 111-124: Z + attn, Z + self-attn, Z + MLP), so replacing a block's forward with identity is a clean skip. (2) The loop is range(n) with t = 0..7 at 8 loops (ledger.py:307); steps are written only for 1 <= t <= 7. So 'blind from round 9' never fires and is dropped. (3) ctl27 on results/d0 reproduces: in_dist change -2.57, -0.74, -0.22 and chain-5 change -7.8, -0.6, -1.0 on seeds 200, 201, 202. Only seed 200 clearly uses the scratch. (4) Checkpoints B2_s200 to B2_s205 are all in the scratchpad b2ckpt folder, so the critics' 'seed 200 is not available' caveat is wrong, and ctl27 can be completed to six seeds on the confirm checkpoints.

Flaws in the idea as written, all accepted from the critics (shown unless noted):
- The 'state settled' mark (<= 0.02) cannot pass. Controller RMS grows 14-16% per round at rounds 7 to 9 (PROBE.json M5), and the heads read ln_z(Z[:,0/1]), so scale never reaches them.
- Marks leave undefined bands (1.0 to 5, 1.0 to 2.0, -0.3 to -1.0, 0.02 to 0.10). Seed 201 (-0.74) already sits in the middle.
- Marks mix data sets (pooled-5 on 6,040 RESULT rows vs the 6,800-row in_dist big build).
- Several arms have no mark, and the 'narrower MLP' gate has no arm or mark.
- The reader-share mark has a uniform baseline T/(T+valid slots) above 0.5 for any prompt over about 27 characters.
- Rule 4 wording: 'proved wrong' on two checkpoints is not allowed.
- The 'one hour decides the 8a premise' claim overreaches. The probe measures usage at test, not benefit at matched size.
- The marks are not sealed in PASS-MARKS.md.

Expected value: modest. My prediction (suggested, untested) is that skipping core[1] costs a lot, so 'block 1 used' is the likely outcome. A large cost is ambiguous because removing a block also shifts the residual scale. So the main gain is the small-cost outcomes: idle block, late reader reads not needed, or scratch not generalising beyond seed 200. The probe can only shut or add a control. It cannot open any 8a, W1 or W2 build.

Rule 4: the cutoffs below were chosen after seeing seeds 200-202 for ctl27, so only seeds 203-205 are fresh for that arm. Disclose this in the sealed addendum.
chair.revised_idea:
D4 (revised): a zero-training usage probe, a pre-ship diagnostic. It adds no deploy-time step. Rule 10 does not apply to it, and the idea must not claim that the model decides to skip anything. A per-row self-decision would need a learned gate, which this probe neither builds nor measures. The only link to autonomy is the per-row answer-flip table below, which sets a ceiling for any later learned gate.

Checkpoints: the six confirm checkpoints B2_s200 to B2_s205 (from branch claude/b2-confirm-checkpoints, sha256 pinned). This gives 6 paired seeds under rule 4. ctl27 already exists on 200-202 (results/d0), so 203-205 are the new ctl27 seeds. Seeds 100 and 101 are optional.

Data: the 6,800-row in_dist big build, the same as results/d0 and probe_loops.py, plus its 1,000-row chain-5 subset. Drop pooled-5, since the RESULT.json splits are a different row set. Run on Ben's PC or Mac CPU. Confirm no overlap with protected panels (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md).

Indexing: use the loop index t = 0..7 everywhere (steps are written at t = 1..7). Drop the round-9 arm. Reuse the d0 intact numbers for 200-202 and recompute 203-205.

Hook mechanics:
- Wrap the model's run() on the instance so a block-call counter resets at the start of every batch, then map call index to round (2 block calls per round).
- Edit the mask inside a pre-hook only; the mask is rebuilt every round (ledger.py:311).
- Use the real signature evalx.evaluate(model, rows, batch_size, device, lesion, return_preds).

Arms:
- W0, a pass-through wrapper that must reproduce intact on every row exactly. Wiring check.
- B1, skip core[1] at all t.
- B1late, skip core[1] at t >= 4.
- B0, skip core[0] at all t.
- BC, core[1] replaced by core[0]'s forward.
- Rlate, 'late letter reads blind': mask[:, 27:] = False for t >= 4.
- Rmid, the same from t >= 2.
- Rall, the same from t >= 0. Positive control: chain-5 should collapse (mark at most 10); if it does not, the hook is not applied.
- ctl27 on 203-205 (ctl27 on 200-202 already exists).

Caveats to print with the results:
(a) The blind arm only removes per-round cross-attention to reader letters. Number values still enter through S0, via the pooled reader term plus the regex-parsed values (a hand-written step under rule 1 that this probe does not test). The word keys and the talker's copy path also still read the reader. So the arm is 'late letter reads', not 'text'.
(b) Masking renormalises the softmax over the 27 workspace slots, so a cost mixes 'not read' with 'attention mass moved'.
(c) Removing a block shifts the residual scale, so a large cost proves little.

Descriptive readouts (no pass marks, not gates), per stratum (L=0, L>=1, chain-5):
- Per-row answer-flip fraction versus intact, for each arm.
- Per-round 1 - cosine of LayerNorm-centred controls 0 and 1 (what the heads read), with norm growth printed beside it.
- RMS of each of the 17 slots, with max/median.
- Participation ratios, with the formula stated: (sum of eigenvalues)^2 / sum of squared eigenvalues of the activation covariance.
- Reader share minus the uniform share T/(T+valid slots), per head and per prompt-length bucket.
- Label rounds 9-16 out-of-regime, because step_emb[7] is re-added each round and training never sees that.
Drop the 'narrower MLP' gate.

Marks (seal in a PASS-MARKS.md addendum before any run; paired change versus intact, in_dist and chain-5, on 6 of 6 seeds; anything between is 'inconclusive, gate stays shut'):
- Block 1 idle: B1 costs at most 1.0 in_dist and chain-5 stays at least 99.0. The only follow-up is a one-block-control training run, which is a separate sealed test. 'Used (suggestive only)': cost at least 5.0.
- Late letter reads not needed: Rlate costs at most 1.0 in_dist and chain-5 stays at least 99.0. 'Needed (suggestive only)': cost at least 2.0. Rall chain-5 at most 10 on 6 of 6.
- Scratch, per seed: 'used' means ctl27 in_dist change at most -1.0 AND chain-5 change at most -2.0 (only seed 200 qualifies so far). Used on at least 4 of 6 seeds supports W2's premise. Used on at most 1 of 6 means seed-specific: W2 stays unqueued. 2 or 3 of 6 is inconclusive.
- 'B2 uses its second block' is wrong only if B1 meets the idle mark on 6 of 6. 'Late rounds read letters' is wrong only if Rlate meets the not-needed mark on 6 of 6. Nothing is called 'proved wrong' on fewer than 6 seeds.

Scope statement: this measures usage at test on trained weights. It does not show whether more blocks, rounds or scratch help at matched size. The 8a depth-first premise stays untested whatever the outcome. The cheap matched-size tests are ideas 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 in the area summary.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must get these right.

1. Seal before running. Write the marks into a PASS-MARKS.md addendum (pattern: addenda 16-19) before any run. Disclose that the ctl27 cutoffs were chosen after seeing seeds 200-202, so only 203-205 are fresh for that arm.

2. One data set per mark.
- Use the 6,800-row in_dist big build (same as results/d0 and probe_loops.py) plus its 1,000-row chain-5 subset.
- Do not use pooled-5; its splits are different rows.
- Use all 6,800 rows for verdicts. A 1,000-row subsample has a paired standard error of about 0.9 points against a 1.0-point mark, so use it only for staging and timing.

3. Seeds and checkpoints.
- Use the six confirm checkpoints 200-205 (b2ckpt copies, sha256 pinned) for 6 paired seeds under rule 4.
- Reuse d0 intact and ctl27 numbers for 200-202; run ctl27 and the intact baseline fresh on 203-205.
- Seeds 100 and 101 are optional.

4. Hook correctness.
- Use 0-based t = 0..7 (the loop is range(n); steps are written at t = 1..7). Drop the round-9 arm, which is a no-op at 8 loops.
- Reset the block-call counter at the start of each run() call, by wrapping run() on the instance. evalx.evaluate calls it once per batch.
- Include a pass-through wrapper arm that must equal intact exactly on every row.
- Include a blind-from-t=0 positive control (chain-5 should collapse; mark at most 10).
- Confirm the instance-level forward override fires on every round, for example by counting calls.
- Hook the real evalx.evaluate signature (model, rows, batch_size, device, lesion, return_preds).

5. Decide only on small costs.
- Skipping a block shifts the residual scale, and masking renormalises the softmax. A large cost is therefore 'suggestive only' and never gates a build.
- Every mark needs an explicit 'inconclusive, gate stays shut' band.
- Drop the 'state settled' mark (cannot pass: norm grows 14-16% per round, M5). Use 1 - cosine of LayerNorm-centred controls 0 and 1 as a descriptive readout only.
- Drop the narrower-MLP gate.
- Make the participation ratio and slot-norm readouts descriptive only, with the formula stated.

6. Reader-blind wording.
- Call it 'late letter reads'.
- State that number values still reach the thinker through S0 (regex spans, a hand-written step under rule 1) and that word keys and the talker's copy path still read the reader. The arm cannot test whether the loop needs the text.
- Report reader share minus the uniform baseline T/(T+valid slots), per head and prompt-length bucket.

7. Add per-row answer-flip fractions versus intact for each arm, by stratum (L=0, L>=1, chain-5). This is the ceiling for any later learned per-row gate, and the only autonomy link. Rewrite the autonomy field as 'pre-ship diagnostic, no deploy step'.

8. What each outcome gates.
- Nothing can open an 8a, W1 or W2 build.
- An idle block 1 only adds a one-block-control training run, which needs its own sealed test.
- A scratch-used verdict (at least 4 of 6) only supports W2's premise.
- State plainly that 8a's matched-size benefit stays untested. The cheap tests are ideas 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11.

9. Time and cost.
- Do a 512-row timing run first; the old '1 hour' was for 2 checkpoints and was never timed.
- Six seeds with about 9 arms is roughly 3x that, so the cost is a rough estimate (suggested, untested).
- Run in staged order: B1, then Rlate, then B0 and BC, then ctl27 on 203-205, then the readouts.

10. Give Ben a plain-language summary: 'we switch off parts of the trained model one at a time and see which parts it actually uses. A part it can lose without trouble is a part we don't need to build more of. A part it can't lose only tells us the model uses it, not that making more of it would help.' Label every claim shown, suggested or untested.

plan.title: B2 usage probe: which trained parts it uses at test (D4 revised)
plan.ben_line: We switch off one piece of the trained model at a time and see whether its answers get worse. If a piece can be switched off with almost no harm, the model is not using it, so we should not build more of it. If switching it off hurts a lot, that only shows the model uses it, not that more of it would help.
plan.question: On the six trained B2 checkpoints, with no training and no model change: (a) does switching off the second controller block cost little (idle) or a lot; (b) does blinding the reader-letter reads from round 4 onward cost little; (c) do controller slots 2-7 carry row-specific content, or does zeroing them only act as a constant or a scale shift?
plan.one_change: No model or training change. One new zero-training hook script wraps the frozen B2 forward pass during evaluation and reports the effect of test-time lesions on six checkpoints. Every arm is a test-time lesion; none is a build.
arms: I (intact): recomputed for every seed on the run machine; the reference for every paired change.
W0 (wiring): hooks installed as identity wrappers, then removed; predictions must equal I on every row.
B1 (gate, block 1 idle): core[1] replaced by identity at all rounds t = 0..7 (ledger.py:313-314).
Rlate (gate, late letter reads): reader-letter columns of the attention mask set to False for t >= 4 (in place, mask[:, 27:], shared by both blocks of the round).

C27 (gate, scratch): controls 2-7 zeroed after each round's blocks, the existing lesion at ledger.py:315-316. Because step_emb is added to all 17 vectors at the start of the next round (ledger.py:312), the slots become a constant step_emb row, not zeros.
Cshuf (content check): controls 2-7 replaced by the next row's controls (roll by 1 within the batch) after each round, so norms stay typical and only the row match is broken.
Rall (wiring, positive control): reader columns off for t >= 0. The hook must fire on every call and must change at least one prediction per seed. Chain-5 collapse is a prediction, not a gate.
B1late (descriptive): core[1] identity at t >= 4.
B0 (descriptive): core[0] identity at all t.

BC (descriptive): block 1 uses block 0's weights. Override both core[1].forward and core[1].kv_of, because keys and values come from block-specific projections (ledger.py:113-115, 302, 310); overriding forward alone is not a copy.
Rmid (descriptive): reader columns off for t >= 2.

Readouts (no marks, open no gate): answer-flip fraction versus I by stratum (L=0, L>=1, chain-5); per-block write size |out - in| / |in| per round; 1 - cosine of LayerNorm-centred controls 0 and 1 by round (the vectors the heads read, ledger.py:321 and :342), with norm growth printed beside it; per-slot RMS with max/median; participation ratio (sum of eigenvalues)^2 / sum of squared eigenvalues of the stated activation covariance; reader share minus its uniform share T / (T + V_t), per head and prompt-length bucket. T = the row's prompt characters (sum of xm); V_t = the row's valid workspace slots at round t (valid changes each round, ledger.py:336-337).

plan.null_risk: Moderate. Every gate pass needs a reading before it is believed. (1) Block 1 idle can pass because the block is inert. Its output projections start at std 0.02/sqrt(3*2*8) = 0.0029 (ledger.py:160; arithmetic shown), so a small trained write costs little when skipped. That is a true fact about this checkpoint, not evidence that a deeper model would not need the block. Print per-block write size beside the verdict. (2) Late letter reads can pass because the answer path reads pre-loop keys that Rlate does not mask: number pools (ledger.py:291-296), word keys (ledger.py:299-301) and the talker's copy path. Rlate tests only per-round letter re-reads. (3) Scratch "used" can be a shape effect. After the lesion the slots hold step_emb, a row-independent constant (ledger.py:312, 315-316; shown by code, effect untested). Cshuf is the control for this. (4) Hook errors can fake a pass or a fail. Counting every block call instead of core[0] doubles the round index. Editing a copy of the mask does nothing. BC without kv_of is not a copy. The wiring checks catch these. (5) Statistics. At about 8% of rows flipping (suggested), the paired standard error is about 0.9 points at n = 1,000 and about 0.35 at n = 6,800 (suggested arithmetic). The chain-5 set is a 5-family subset of the same 6,800 rows (evalx.py:11, 141-147; 5 x 200), so the in_dist and chain-5 marks are not independent evidence. (6) Machine. The d0 seed-200 and seed-201 numbers came from another machine, and the same seed gave different plain-B2 loops:0 leak values on different machines (RESULTS-EG2.md lines 12 and 22: 1.40 vs 0.00 on seed 200; shown). If the seed-200 scratch effect does not reproduce, the scratch verdict falls. (7) Post-hoc cutoffs. The ctl27 thresholds were set after d0 showed seed 200; the fresh-seed rule is the guard. (8) Passing wiring checks shows the hooks act, not that the model uses the part.

fixed_plan.title: B2 usage probe, corrected and reduced: which trained parts it uses at test
fixed_plan.ben_line: We switch off one part of the trained model at a time and see whether its answers get worse. If switching a part off barely hurts, the model is not using that part, so this test does not support building more of it. If switching it off hurts a lot, that only shows the model uses the part, not that more of it would help.
fixed_plan.question: On the six trained B2 checkpoints, with no training and no model change: (a) does switching off the second controller block cost little; (b) does blinding per-round letter reads from round 4 on cost little; (c) do controller slots 2-7 carry row-specific content, or only a constant or a scale shift?

C27: built-in lesion ctl27 (no hook needed; ledger.py:315-316, routed at ledger.py:409-411).
Cshuf: after each round, controls 2-7 replaced by a fixed random donor's controls 2-7 (donor map fixed across arms and seeds; forward hook on core[1]).
Readouts with no marks, intact pass only: per-round write size |out-in|/|in| for both blocks; control norms per round; reader-column attention share per head and prompt-length bucket.

pass_marks: WIRING (void the run if any fails): W0 equals I exactly on all 512 seed-200 rows; the C27 hook (if built) equals lesion='ctl27' exactly on every row where both run; reader-column attention mass is exactly 0 at each hooked round in both blocks (direct assertion); the B1 identity returns its input unchanged on every call.

REPRODUCTION (seed 200, CPU): intact chain-5 99.4 and ctl27 chain-5 91.6, each within 0.2 points of d0. A miss is reported as a machine difference, and the gates then run on the reproducing device. The in_dist value 90.588 is not a target unless the 1,360-row small root is also run.
NOISE FLOOR: two runs of I on seed 200 give identical predictions. If not, the paired SE is measured from those runs and no arm difference below 2 SE is judged.
BLOCK 1 IDLE (gate): B1 minus I, in_dist change >= -1.0 AND chain-5 change >= -1.0 AND chain-5 level >= 99.0, on 6 of 6 seeds. Reported bound: at most about 1 point of loss.
BLOCK 1 USED (suggestive only): in_dist change <= -5.0 on 6 of 6 seeds. Between the two bands is inconclusive and the gate stays shut.

LATE READS NOT NEEDED (gate): Rlate in_dist change >= -1.0 AND chain-5 change >= -1.0 AND chain-5 level >= 99.0, on 6 of 6 seeds. NEEDED (suggestive): in_dist change <= -2.0 on 6 of 6. Scope: controller re-reads only; number pools, word keys and the talker copy path are untouched.

idea.title: Frozen 257-parameter heads for 'settled' and 'right' on B2's state
idea.summary: Fit a logistic head on B2's frozen controller readout state to predict (a) the answer is already final through round 8 and (b) the answer is right, using fresh generated training-split rows. At deploy the stop is the sign of the head's own logit, no gradient enters the loop, and B2's numbers are unchanged when the stop is not taken. It is the only stop candidate for the 59% of rows that have no program and no useful NOOP.
idea.change: Add head(s) Linear(256,1) on ln_z(Z[:,1]) at each round (257 params each; 3,302,738 total with one head, 0.008% over B2), computed under no_grad from the rounds=True snapshots. Labels from the model's own answers against gold on about 20k fresh rows from the same generator (new seeds, none of the 200k train rows, no dev or protected rows): settled(K) = right at K and at every round from K to 8; rows get label 0 before round L+2 so the head never stops before the program's last write is read. Fit 16k, test 4k; score in_dist and variant dev. Deploy rule: stop at the first K in 2..8 where the settled logit is positive, otherwise 8. Second label: right at the final round. Compare against idea 1's best zero-parameter score on the same rows.
idea.why: Oracle stopping at each right-at-8 row's settle round averages 2.54 and 2.70 rounds against 8 (a compute bound of about 3x), but the accuracy ceiling is only 1.7 to 1.9 in-dist points. The settle round is 1.69 and 1.74 for string families and 3.09 and 3.33 for number families, so a stop has to depend on the row. Test LR trained answers at every round and leaked; a detached head reads the loop without changing it. Joint gate training is reported to distort the loop while post-hoc readouts match or beat gates (abstract-level, second-hand). The correctness label doubles as the 'am I stuck' signal that rule 8 allows creativity to use.

test.arms: A: round 8 for all rows. B: settled-label head stop. C: idea 1's best zero-parameter rule. D: right/wrong head versus the best zero-training confidence AUROC from idea 1.
test.pass_mark: Fixed now, both seeds. Held-out AUROC for settled(K), K in 3-8, at least 0.75; B vs A: in_dist change at least -0.3 with mean rounds at most 6.0 and loops:0 in_dist unchanged within 1.0 (a gain of +0.3 pooled-5 is a bonus, not required, given the 2-point ceiling); right/wrong head AUC at least 0.80 on in_dist and at least 0.70 on variant, and at least 0.05 above idea 1's best zero-parameter AUC on variant.
test.proved_wrong: Settled AUROC below 0.65 on both seeds, or B loses 1.0 or more in_dist against A, means a linear readout cannot find a stable stop and idea 7's trained stop is needed. Right/wrong head gains 0.02 or less over the zero-parameter score on variant: the final state holds nothing the heads do not already show.

idea.rules_check: Rule 1: the loop break is control flow like today's fixed count; the decision is the head's own sign. Flag for Ben's ruling: is a logit>0 cutoff inside the forward pass a hand-set switch (it is the natural logistic boundary, not tuned). Rule 2: labels come from the model's own answers against gold, no teacher. Rule 3: +257 params (+0.008%). Rule 4: two checkpoints is a screen. Rule 5: head fitted on generated training-split rows. Rule 7: no positive label before round L+2.
idea.closest_prior: H1 (redesign section 8b): joint per-round supervision plus a stop head with cap 32, needs T1 first, no code. Test LR (tried, failed). StreamPonder (design only). This freezes B2 and changes no loss.
idea.autonomy: At deploy the model stops on the sign of its own head; no threshold we pick. Fitting the head is a build step; a deployed model could refit it on its own self-generated practice rows (suggested), since gold labels there come from the generator that produces the practice questions. Cap stays 8.
idea.director_note: Cheapest route to a model-decided stop for no-program rows without retraining. Critics: (1) the head reads untrained mid-loop states, so check AUROC per round and per stratum, not pooled; (2) labels need fresh rows (30 passes over the 200k set); (3) whether the sign cutoff counts as a hand-set switch under rule 10; (4) accuracy gain should be near zero by the ceiling, so judge on rounds saved at flat accuracy; (5) the first positive label at round L+2 uses gold L in training, deploy uses the model's own view.

problems: [shown] Prior-art overlap. The 257-parameter stop head is H1's head (/mnt/project-files/architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:136-137). Section 8c (about lines 165-170) already switched H1's stop label to 'settled', defined as '(right now, or no later round of this turn is right)'. D5's label is 'right at K and at every round K to 8', which differs. It gives label 0 to every turn the model never gets right, which is the defect 8c fixed ('a calibrated stop head thinks to the cap on exactly those turns'). D5 does not cite 8c. It also gives label 0 to right-then-wrong turns, the overthinking rows that are the only accuracy prize (1.7-1.9 in_dist points, PROBE.json M4). So D5 can only stop rows that stay right, and its accuracy gain is near zero by construction. Its 'closest_prior' and 'no code' statements are out of date: 8c reports settled-label code tested for function on the build thread (not in this copy; queue 49-pc-h1-screen is not in queue_local, which ends at 44). D5's real novelty is only the frozen, no-retraining version of H1's head.

[shown] The labels cannot be computed from the rounds=True snapshots as the idea says. The snapshot holds control 1 and registers, not vals (ledger.py:340-341). talk() decodes NUM answers from vals (ledger.py talk(), about lines 380-406). So 'right at K' for NUM rows needs per-round values, via replay() (ledger.py:89-99, from logged ops and pointers) or a probe-only edit that adds vals to the snapshot tuple. Round 8 comes from the final output (zf), not from the snapshots. The idea needs that code change stated.

[shown] Round numbering is a trap. The loop variable t is 0-based (ledger.py run(), for t in range(n)). Writes happen for 1 <= t <= N_RES, and the snapshot is skipped at t=0 (the continue comes before the snapshot append). For n=8 the snapshots keep t=1..6 (completed rounds 2..7), and the final state is separate. D5's 'K in 2..8' and 'label 0 before round L+2' are correct only under completed-round counting. The spec must say which numbering it uses.

[shown] Labels are correctness of answer readouts that were never trained at intermediate rounds. Answer heads train on the final state only unless round_readout > 0 (ledger.py:140 default 0; round_loss runs only when round_readout is set, ledger.py ~497-520). D5's label is therefore the correctness of accidental intermediate readouts. The deploy stop reads the same readout, so label and output agree, but the head learns which accidental readouts are right. The brief's freeze costs (-3.4 and -5.7 at the NOOP round) show these readouts are weak. Say this limit in the spec and keep the readout-trained variant (Test LR, which failed) out of this probe.

[shown] Wrong control signal, and an uncovered deploy-time truncation risk. The head reads control 1 (Z[:,1], the final readout). Step and NOOP decisions read control 0 (ledger.py run(): z = ln_z(Z[:,0]) feeds op_head and the pointers, about lines 321-324). The program-finished signal (NOOP after the last write, trained at weight 1.0 for program rows, ledger.py loss() w_row) lives in control 0 and is not a D5 input. The label forces 0 before L+2 using gold L, so the head can avoid early stops only by inferring program length from family identity. Nothing enforces this at deploy, so a stop at round 2 or 3 on a 4 to 7 step row can cut its program. This is not a rule 7 breach in the training-target sense, but it is an accuracy risk that no mark covers. Rescue: require op-head NOOP at round K (zero parameters) as a stop condition, and add a program-row mark.

[shown] K=2 is trained only on no-program rows and is never measured. Label 0 before L+2 with L=0 for no-program rows means K=2 positives come only from no-program rows that stay right, so the K=2 head is a no-program-family detector. The pass mark is AUROC for K in 3-8 only, but deploy stops at K in 2..8. Pooled AUROC is also confounded by family: PROBE.json M2 gives mean settle rounds of about 1.7 for string families and 3.1-3.3 for number families. Rescue: stratified AUROC per family and per program length, K=2 included, plus a family-only baseline (predict the stop from question family alone). That baseline is cheap and shows whether the head learns more than family.

[shown] The compute bound is overstated. PROBE.json M2 'all' n = 6076 (seed 100) and 6156 (seed 101) equals the right-at-8 rows (M1 K=8 accuracy 89.35% and 90.5% of 6800). The oracle mean of 2.54 and 2.70 covers only those rows. The wrong-at-8 rows (724 and 644) still take 8 rounds. Overall the oracle averages about 3.1 and 3.2 rounds, so the bound is about 2.5 to 2.6 times, not about 3 times (suggested arithmetic on PROBE.json). The no-program group has little slack at fixed K (seed 100, M1 by_len 0: K=4 81.78, K=5 83.38, K=6 83.70, K=8 83.95). Stopping all no-program rows at K=6 costs about 0.25 in-group (about 0.15 pooled), K=5 about 0.57 (about 0.34 pooled), K=4 about 2.2 (about 1.3 pooled). So the flat-accuracy saving there is at most about 25% of rounds unless per-row stops do better (suggested; one seed only). 'Mean rounds at most 6.0' is too weak to act as a compute gate.

[shown] Pass-mark gaps, and one mark that cannot fail. AUROC: pass at 0.75, proved wrong below 0.65; the 0.65 to 0.75 band gets no verdict. In_dist: pass at -0.3 or better, proved wrong at -1.0 or worse; the band between has no verdict. 'loops:0 in_dist unchanged within 1.0' is true by construction, because the head does not change the loop, so it cannot fail. 'At least 0.05 above idea 1's best zero-parameter AUC' refers to a result that is not in this brief and cannot be checked. The correct-at-final head is a second 257-parameter head. The 3,302,738 total counts one head. Seven per-K heads (K=2..8) give 3,304,280 (about 0.05%, suggested arithmetic). The count should name the head design.

[suggested] Rule 10 (autonomy) does not clear the deploy-time refit. Gold labels exist only where a generator has answer keys. A deployed model on real questions has none. The idea's self-generated practice rows get gold answers from a hand-written generator, which rule 10 may exclude as generator knowledge or a hand-picked practice set (Ben's ruling needed). The build-time fit is allowed, since rule 10 says building before shipping is not a deploy step. Drop the refit claim, or require answers the model verifies itself (for example through its calculator tool) and test that separately (untested).

[shown] Data source and rule 5. The 'same generator' is not in the code copy: data.py:9 points to sk200k, which does not exist here, and no skills generator was found under /home/user/learner to depth 4. The idea gives new seeds and 'no dev or protected rows' but no overlap check. The protected-panel hash merge is not done (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md; PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md), and generator templates can repeat across seeds and dev splits. Require a 13-word overlap check of the about 20k fresh rows against the dev splits and the protected hashes before the fit. Presence of the generator on Ben's PC is untested.

[shown] 'The only cheap candidate' is overstated. No-program rows are not NOOP-free. Their gold op is NOOP at every step (ledger.py gold(), default op 0), trained at weight w_noop = 0.1 (ledger.py loss(), w_row). So 'no usable NOOP' is untested here, not shown (no file measures NOOP probability on those rows). Zero-parameter stops are also cheap: answer unchanged for k rounds, or a max-answer-probability threshold (the brief's probe hook). The idea itself lists these as arm C. The phrase 'only cheap candidate' should be removed.

[shown] Rule 1 and implementation. 'Stop at the first K where the logit is positive' is hand-written control flow inside the forward pass. The 0 boundary is a fixed constant (the same rule as H1's p >= 0.5, redesign 8b H-f), so it is probably acceptable, but Ben should rule on it as D5 asks. Deploy needs per-row freezing that run() does not have (ledger.py run() has no freeze, about lines 277-341). A probe can select per-row rounds offline without changing the loop.

[shown] History risk. The repo's earlier learned stop head 'always quit after round 1' (/mnt/project-files/design/JUDGES.md:49; design/design-streaming-ponder.md:48 and :259). Section 8c names the same early-collapse risk for H1 and asks for a check (H-c). D5 has neither check. Add a stop-round distribution per family as a mark, and H-c's chain-5 versus one-step gap.

[shown] Rule 8 scope creep. 'The correctness label doubles as the am I stuck signal' adds a second use that rule 8 limits to stuck creativity. It has no test in this idea. Remove it, or label it as a separate, untested later use.

[suggested] Literature support is second-hand here. The Popescu 2607.20519 'match or beat' claim is abstract-level (no-hardcoding-papers.md:281-289, per the idea and the brief). The LoopViT entropy-exit result is an abstract-level scout note. Treat both as motivation, not evidence for this head.

[shown] Checked and holds: settle statistics (PROBE.json M2: number families 3.09 and 3.33, string families 1.69 and 1.74); overthinking 1.91% and 1.66% (M4); H1 stop head 257 parameters and p >= 0.5 (redesign 8b); no halt or stop code in ledger.py or tool.py (grep); Test LR seed 200 stability -0.51 and loops:0 leak 15.88 (results/RESULTS-EG2.md:28, :32); 257 is +0.008% of 3,302,481.
critiques.rescue: Re-scope D5 as the frozen-state readout test of H1's stop head, and say so in the spec. (1) Adopt 8c's 'settled' label as ruled (right now, or no later round is right), or write the stricter label in the spec, state that it differs from 8c, and report both labels; the accuracy prize needs the 8c 'right now' part. (2) Make the probe-only code change: add vals to the per-round snapshot, or rebuild values with replay() from logged ops and pointers; take round 8 from the final output; state completed-round numbering and skip t=0 explicitly. (3) Add zero-parameter arms: op-head NOOP at round K (control 0), a family-only baseline, and idea 1's best rule; report AUROC stratified by family and program length, with K=2 to 8 all inside the mark. (4) Close the verdict bands: AUROC pass at 0.75 and proved wrong below 0.70, with 0.70 to 0.75 labelled not shown; in_dist pass at -0.3 or better and proved wrong at -1.0 or worse, with the band labelled not shown. (5) Replace the loops:0 mark with a program-row mark: count program rows stopped before their last write and report their in_dist change. (6) Restate the compute bound as about 2.5 times for the oracle over all rows, and about 25% of rounds on no-program rows at flat accuracy (suggested, one seed). Make mean rounds a real gate. chair.reasons:
PLAN, ranked low to medium and only as a re-scoped screen. It is cheap (CPU, no training, no loop change) and it is not a duplicate of a run. No frozen post-hoc stop probe exists anywhere. It is also the only test that checks whether H1's 257-parameter stop head can be learned from B2's state without per-round answer training, the thing that made Test LR leak (loops:0 15.88 on seed 200, shown, RESULTS-EG2.md). The deploy-time part passes rule 10: the model stops on the sign of its own head's logit, with no researcher step. The head is fitted at build time, which rule 10 allows.

Four things in the idea must change before it is queued.

1. It is H1's head, and the label is not the ruled one. I read redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 8c (shown). H1's label was switched to "settled" = right now, or no later round is right. D5's label ("right at K and at every round K..8") gives 0 to never-right rows and to right-then-wrong rows. That reintroduces the cap problem 8c fixed, and it cannot reach the 1.7-1.9 point overthinking prize. D5 does not cite 8c.

2. The marks cannot fail or cannot be read.
- A family-only score reaches AUROC about 0.91 for right-at-8 and about 0.86-0.88 for right-at-3, in-sample, derived from PROBE.json M1 and M3 (suggested). The AUROC marks 0.75 and 0.80 therefore pass on family identity alone.
- "loops:0 unchanged within 1.0" is true by construction, because the head is never consulted at zero rounds. Drop it.
- Three mark bands have no verdict: AUROC 0.65-0.75, in_dist change between -0.3 and -1.0, and a gain over the zero-parameter score between 0.02 and 0.05.
- "Mean rounds at most 6.0" cannot bind. The oracle averages about 3.1-3.2 rounds over all rows, or about 3.7 with the L+2 floor (suggested arithmetic from PROBE.json M2). The ~3x claim counts right-at-8 rows only; the honest bound is about 2.2-2.6x.
- Chain-5 and program rows have no gate. A stop before a program's last write costs that row, and chain-5 is 0.0-2.9 at loops:1 (shown).

3. The labels need code the idea does not mention.
- Snapshots keep completed rounds 1-7 and carry no workspace values, so NUM answers cannot be decoded per round from them (ledger.py:340-341; shown).
- The fix is to rerun loops:K for K=1..8, as probe_loops.py does, and save per-row hits. Equivalence of loops:K to the first K rounds of an 8-round run is suggested from ledger.py (the step embedding clamp and the write rule do not depend on n). It must be checked bitwise.
- K<8 labels use answer heads trained only at round 8 (round_readout=0). The label therefore measures an untrained readout's accidental hits (shown). Say so in the spec.

4. Rule 10 and rule 5 gaps.
- Drop the deploy-time refit claim. Gold answers from the generator are not available to a deployed model.
- The cap stays 8, so this head only shortens thinking and never lengthens it. That is a partial answer to Ben's "model decides how long to think", and the spec should say so.
- The 'only candidate' wording and the 'am I stuck' use (rule 8) go.
- Whether a loop break on logit > 0 counts as a hand-set switch is Ben's call. It is the same fixed boundary as H1's p >= 0.5 (H-f).
- Fresh rows need an overlap check, and the generator's presence on Ben's PC is untested.

Value for Ben, honestly: the accuracy prize is about 0 to 0.6 pooled-5 (shown ceiling). Compute savings are not realised, because run() loops all rows to n and has no per-row freeze. They would be counted as mean rounds and per-row exit at batch size 1. The result is mainly design information for H1 and for idea 1: is a stop readable from frozen state beyond what the family already tells you. Run it after idea 1 and reuse the same per-row fixture. Treat a pass as a screen only (rule 4).

Marks, fixed now, both seeds (verdicts close every band):
- M1 learnability. Pass: head minus family-prior AUROC on held-out rows has a mean over K in 3..8 of at least +0.05 with no K below 0, and macro within-family AUROC is at least 0.70. Proved wrong: the mean margin is below +0.02 on both seeds. In between is "not shown".
- M2 accuracy. Pass: in_dist change B minus A at least -0.3, with a paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound at least -0.8; chain-5 at least 99.0; no dev split down more than 2.0. Proved wrong: in_dist -1.0 or worse on either seed, or chain-5 below 99.0. In between is "not shown". Variant change is reported.
- M3 compute. Pass: mean rounds over all in_dist rows (wrong-at-8 rows count as 8) at most 5.5, AND B saves at least 0.5 more rounds than the best of C or D at the same in_dist change (within 0.1). If not, the 257 parameters are not earning their place. Also report per-row exit at batch size 1 and the variant rounds.
- M4 program safety. Pass: at most 0.5% of program rows (L>=1) stop before their last write is read, and chain-5 mean stop round is at least 2.0 above the one-step families (H-c's line). Proved wrong: a stop-round collapse to round 1 or 2 on chain-5 (the JUDGES.md failure).
- M5 confidence head (right at final round). AUROC at least 0.80 on in_dist and 0.70 on variant, within-family and at least 0.05 over the best zero-parameter score. A gain of 0.02 or less is proved wrong ("the state holds nothing the heads do not show").

Drop the loops:0 mark. Drop the deploy-time refit and 'am I stuck' claims. Ask Ben for a ruling on whether a fixed logit>0 loop break is allowed under rules 1 and 10, since it is the same switch as H1's H-f.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. Order and scope.
- Run only after idea 1, on the same per-row fixture.
- Keep it separate from H1/T1. This is the frozen B2 state, with no per-round loss.
- Mark every claim shown, suggested or untested.
- A pass is a two-seed screen, not a claim (rule 4).

2. Fixture, probe-only.
- Rerun loops:K for K=1..8 and save per-row hits and ln_z(Z[:,1]).
- Do not rely on rounds=True snapshots. They keep completed rounds 1-7 and carry no vals, so NUM answers cannot be decoded (ledger.py:340-341, shown).
- Verify bitwise that loops:8 matches the normal answers.
- State completed-round numbering. The loop variable t is 0-based, and writes happen at 1<=t<=7.
- probe_loops.py asserts n_loops==8 and saves aggregates only, so extend it to save per-row data.
- Run it on Ben's PC. The dev rows are not in project files (shown); the presence of data and the generator is untested.

3. Labels.
- Primary is 8c's "settled" (right now, or no later round is right).
- Report D5's strict label too.
- Rows get 0 before round L+2 (gold L is used in training labels only).
- The head is fitted on fresh generated rows, never the 200k train rows (B2 made about 30 passes over them; shown, 8A-SPEC addendum B1). Run the 13-word overlap check against dev and protected hashes.

4. Baselines before the head. Family-prior, answer-unchanged-for-k, margin or entropy of the model's own readouts, state cosine, and control-0 NOOP. Family alone gives about 0.91 AUROC in-sample (suggested), so AUROC is judged within-family and as a margin over the family prior.

5. Marks. Use M1-M5 in revised_idea. Every band needs a verdict ("not shown" counts). The paired bootstrap on in_dist is required. Mean rounds counts wrong-at-8 rows as 8, and the oracle is about 3.1-3.7, not 3.

6. Hours. The idea says 2 h. Allow about 3-4 h on the PC for 2 seeds x 8 K x (6,800 in_dist + variant + 20k fresh) CPU passes. This is suggested and untested.

7. Pitfalls to name in the spec.
- Untrained mid-loop readouts, so the labels are accidental hits.
- Control 1 does not see the answer keys, registers or copy inputs.
- The JUDGES.md precedent of a stop head collapsing to round 1.
- The 8c risk of "settled" labelling everything as stop early.
- Batch code has no per-row freeze, so savings are measured in rounds, not wall-clock.

8. Rule 10, to be written into the spec.
- Fit is build-time only.
- The head's logit>0 is the only runtime switch, and Ben rules on it.
- Cap 8 is a fixed constant, so the head shortens thinking only. Ben's rule 0 (the model picks how long) is only partly met.
- Drop the deploy-time refit and 'am I stuck' claims.

9. Rank low to medium. The accuracy prize is about 0 to 0.6 pooled-5 (shown ceiling). Its worth is as design information for H1 and a model-decided stop on the current B2.

plan.title: D5 re-scoped: frozen settled-stop heads on B2 (CPU screen)
plan.ben_line: We ask whether the thinker can look at its own state after each round and tell that it already has the answer, so it can stop early and save thinking. We test this with a tiny extra reader on two saved models, without changing or retraining them.
plan.question: Can a frozen linear readout on B2's controller state, one per round, tell from that state alone when the answer has settled, so that a stop rule saves rounds at flat in-distribution accuracy, beats zero-parameter rules and a family-prior baseline, and does not cut programs short? (suggested that the state carries the signal; untested that it does.)
plan.one_change: Add seven frozen heads, one per round K=1..7: Linear(256,1) on ln_z(Z[:,1]), 257 parameters each, 1,799 in total (+0.054% on B2's 3,302,481 shown; inside rule 3's +-3%). Fit at build time on fresh generated rows with the settled label (8c). Deploy rule: stop at the first K in 1..7 whose logit is above 0, otherwise run all 8 rounds. Report-only heads (strict label, round-8 confidence) are not shipped and do not count toward rule 3 unless they ship. Nothing else changes: no loop, loss, weight or training-data change.
arms: A: fixed 8 rounds, the normal B2 answer (reference).
B: settled heads, first K in 1..7 with logit > 0, else 8 (the test arm).
B-strict: same heads fitted on the strict label (right at K and at every later round). Report only.

B-E: B, plus the op head's argmax must be NOOP at that round (K 2..7). Control 0 stands in for gold L. No op is read at completed round 1 (run() skips t=0), so E cannot stop at K=1. Report only; also report how often NOOP is argmax on no-program rows.
C1: answer unchanged for the last two rounds (k=2 fixed in advance; no fitted value; K>=3).
C2: margin of the mode head's softmax (top-1 minus top-2) at round K >= one shared threshold fitted on the fit split.
C3: cosine between Z[:,1] after round K-1 and after round K >= one shared threshold fitted on the fit split.
D: family prior: per-family settled rate at K from the fit split; stop when it is >= one shared threshold fitted on the fit split. Comparator only. It uses family labels and is never shipped.
R: random control: B's per-row stop rounds permuted across dev rows with a fixed seed (same histogram, no row information).
F: report only, family holdout (fit heads on 27 families, test on the other 7).
plan.seeds: Screen: B2_s100 and B2_s101 from /mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/ (present, shown). Confirm: B2_s200 to B2_s205 under the scratchpad code/b2ckpt/ folder (present with sha256 files, shown). Rule 4: two seeds is a screen only.
plan.machine: Ben's PC, CPU forward passes only (no training, no GPU). Data that must be on the PC: dev in_dist (probe_loops.py uses the big build, 6,800 rows, shown), variant, chain-5 (1,000 rows, shown in RESULT.json), and about 20k fresh generated rows. The skills generator is not in the code copy and its presence on the PC is untested. The M1 Mac is a fallback only if the data is there (untested).
pass_marks: M1 learnability, fresh test rows (4k), K=2..7, label settled(K). W = macro within-family AUROC of the head logit, over families with at least 20 test rows and both classes. PASS: mean W >= 0.70 on both seeds AND pooled AUROC(head) minus pooled AUROC(family prior) averages >= +0.05 over K=2..7, with no K below 0, on both seeds. PROVED WRONG: mean W < 0.60 on both seeds. Otherwise NOT SHOWN. The family prior is 0.50 within families by construction. Its in-sample pooled AUROC is 0.86-0.88 at K=3 and 0.91-0.92 at K=8 (computed here from PROBE.json M1 by_family and M3 n_by_family; shown inputs, computed result).

M2 accuracy, dev in_dist, paired, B minus A. PASS: mean change >= -0.3 points on both seeds, with a paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound >= -0.8 (10,000 row resamples, fixed seed); chain-5 for B >= 99.0 and within 1.0 of A on the same machine; no dev split (in_dist, variant, or any other present) below -2.0. PROVED WRONG: in_dist change <= -1.0 on either seed, or chain-5 < 99.0 on either seed. Otherwise NOT SHOWN. Variant change is reported with its CI.

M3 compute. Mean rounds over all in_dist rows, with rows wrong under A counted as 8 (the conservative convention); the actual per-row mean is reported next to it. PASS: mean <= 5.5 on both seeds AND B is at least 0.5 below the best matched comparator (C1, C2, C3, D; a comparator is matched when its fit-split change is within 0.1 of B's and its dev change is within 0.3 of B's; best = lowest mean among matched; no match = NOT SHOWN) AND B's dev change beats R by >= 0.5 points. PROVED WRONG: B's mean at or above the best matched comparator on both seeds. Otherwise NOT SHOWN. Per-row exit at batch size 1 and variant rounds are reported, not gated.

M4 program safety, dev under B. PASS: at most 0.5% of program rows (gold L >= 1) stop before round L+2 on both seeds, AND chain-5 mean stop round is at least 2.0 above the mean for one-step families (gold L = 1). PROVED WRONG: chain-5 median stop round <= 2 on either seed (the JUDGES.md collapse pattern). Otherwise NOT SHOWN.

M5 round-8 confidence (report only; does not gate deploy). A 257-parameter head on the round-8 state for right(8), within-family macro AUROC: PASS if >= 0.80 on in_dist and >= 0.70 on variant, and >= 0.05 above the best zero-parameter score (C2 margin at round 8). PROVED WRONG: gain of 0.02 or less over that score on variant. Otherwise NOT SHOWN.

Fixture checks (void, not a fail of the idea, if any breaks): (a) loops:8 answers equal the normal answers row by row; (b) the state after round K in a K-round run equals the same round in the 8-round run, on 200 rows; (c) batch-size-1 answers at K* equal the table on 200 sampled rows; (d) a head fitted on shuffled labels gets within-family AUROC 0.50 +/- 0.03; (e) the overlap check drops any fresh row sharing a 13-word shingle with a dev split or protected hash, and reports the counts.
plan.proved_wrong: The idea is wrong on the screen if, on both seeds, (a) mean within-family AUROC W is below 0.60, meaning the frozen state holds no row-level stop signal; or (b) B's mean rounds are at or above the best matched zero-parameter rule, meaning the 257-parameter heads add nothing; or (c) on either seed the in_dist change is at or below -1.0, or the chain-5 median stop round is at or below 2. A failure on one seed is reported as a seed-level result, not a verdict (rule 4). Any band that the marks leave open is reported as NOT SHOWN, never as a pass.
plan.null_risk: Partly. Routes to a false pass, and what guards each. (1) A head that never fires gives zero change and passes M2; M3 fails it (mean rounds 8). (2) M2 alone can pass on rows whose answer barely moves, so M3 and the R control carry the test. (3) M1 within-family can pass on surface difficulty (digit count, answer length) that the state encodes. That is not settledness; it pays only if B beats C, D and R on rounds, which M3 checks. (4) The family prior is a strong comparator (pooled AUROC 0.86-0.92 in-sample, computed here), so the pooled margin in M1 is hard to pass even for a useful head. The within-family W decides, which is why the proved-wrong line uses W. This changes the chair's margin-only proved-wrong rule and should be sealed explicitly. (5) Dev rows were already read for PROBE.json (the halting-prize analysis), so this is a second look. Marks are fixed now, and the heads use fresh rows only. (6) The -2.0 variant floor is loose: B2 scores 31.9-37.1 on variant (RESULT.json, shown), so -2 is about 6% of its score; report the CI. (7) The accuracy gain is small. The 8c label lets heads stop on right-then-wrong rows, so the ceiling is the overthinking share, 1.91% and 1.66% of in_dist (PROBE.json M4, shown), not zero. (8) Under 8c, never-right rows will stop early, which lowers the actual mean; the forced-8 M3 convention is conservative and the actual mean is reported beside it. (9) The floor-adjusted oracle (label floor L+2 for L>=1) comes to about 3.4 rounds on both seeds (computed here from PROBE.json M2 by_len; pre-floor 3.12 and 3.20). The critic's figure of about 3.7 is not reproduced. Verdict: M1 and M2 can pass with no real change; M3 and R are what keep the claim honest.
plan.autonomy: Deploy: the model reads its own round-K controller state (the same vector its answer readout uses: zf = ln_z(Z[:,1]) after the loop in run()) and stops when a fixed head is positive. Option E also uses its own op head (control 0, NOOP). No gold, no family label, no threshold chosen on dev, no refit at deploy. Build time only: head weights are fitted on fresh generated rows with gold answers. Rule 10 allows building before shipping, but the fit needs the generator. Comparators C, D and R use family labels or dev permutation and are never shipped. Two items need Ben's ruling: (a) whether a fixed logit > 0 loop break is hand-written control flow under rule 1 (the same kind of switch as H1's p >= 0.5, redesign-ideas section 8b); (b) the cap of 8 is fixed, so the model decides when to stop but not how long beyond 8, and rule 0 is only partly met. Limit, not a rule break: answers read at K below 8 come from readouts never trained at that round (round_readout defaults to 0, ledger.py:130 and :140, shown), so those answers are accidental hits; the table measures this.
steps: Before any run: seal the arms, marks and fit rules above. Ask Ben to rule on the logit > 0 loop break (rules 1 and 10). On the PC, confirm the generator, the dev rows and the chain-5 rows exist. If the generator is missing, report BLOCKED, not failed.
Order: run idea 1 (the zero-parameter rules on the same fixture) first. This test reuses its K-sweep table and rules C1 to C3.

Build the K-sweep table with a new probe-only script. Do not use probe_loops.py as is: its n_loops == 8 assert in probe() and its aggregate-only output rule it out. For K = 1..8, run the loops:K path (K=8 is the normal path) on in_dist, variant, chain-5 and the 20k fresh rows. Save per row: hit (is_hit), decoded answer, mode-head softmax margin at K (C2), op-head argmax at K for K >= 2 (E), and Z[:,1] after round K (float16), captured with a forward hook on m.core[-1]. Do not use run(rounds=True): its snapshots cover completed rounds 1-7 only and carry no vals, so NUM answers cannot be decoded (shown in the code).
Run fixture checks (a) to (d). Stop if any fails.

Labels, build time, from the model's own answers against gold. right(K) per row. settled(K) = right(K) OR no round in K+1..8 is right (8c; primary). strict(K) = right at K and every later round (B-strict, report only). Floor: for gold L >= 1 set the label to 0 when K < L+2; for L = 0 there is no floor. The floor matches the model's own NOOP: at completed round K the op head predicts step K-1 (1-based), which is NOOP exactly when K >= L+2 (the op target at loop index t is gold op index t-1, and writes run only for 1 <= t <= 7). Gold L is used only in these labels, never at deploy.

Overlap check: 13-word shingles of the 20k fresh rows against every dev split and every protected hash. If the protected-hash merge is not present, write 'protected check not done' in the result; no protected-panel claim can pass without it.

Split the 20k fresh rows into 14k for fitting, 2k for threshold matching and 4k for testing (family-stratified). Fit one logistic head per K=1..7 for settled, with L2 fixed in the spec before the run. Strict heads and the round-8 head are report only. Arm F (family holdout) is report only.
Fit C2, C3 and D thresholds on the 2k matching split so each matches B's change there within 0.1 point. Apply each once to dev.

Dev simulation (in_dist, variant, chain-5, and any other dev split present): per row K* for each arm; the answer is read from the table at K*; paired bootstrap of change versus A (10,000 resamples, fixed seed). Spot-check K* answers at batch size 1 on 200 rows (fixture check c).

Compute M1 to M5 on the stated rows. Write per-row files and a verdict file to results/41-settled-probe/, with each band marked pass, proved wrong or not shown. Label each claim shown, suggested or untested.

Hours: about 4 PC CPU-hours for both screen seeds (suggested; untested; probe timing is not in the files read). The 8 K-runs with hit and state capture cost more than probe_loops' aggregates pass, which ran 16 K-runs on 6,800 rows per seed.
Read only the marks. A pass on both seeds is a screen (rule 4), not a claim. The next step is the 6-seed confirm.

Pitfalls to name in the write-up: untrained intermediate readouts (labels and answers are accidental hits); the head reads control 1 only, not the key, register or copy inputs the answer heads also use; the JUDGES.md precedent of a stop head collapsing to round 1; the 8c risk that never-right rows stop early (report the stop-round distribution per family); batch code has no per-row freeze, so savings are counted in rounds, not wall clock.

plan.depends_on: Idea 1 (zero-parameter per-row fixture and rules), run first on the same table. No dependence on any training run, H1, T1 or W1. External blockers: (1) the skills generator and dev rows on Ben's PC (untested; not in project files); (2) Ben's ruling on the fixed logit > 0 loop break (rules 1 and 10); (3) the protected-hash merge for the overlap check (status unknown).
plan.confirm: If both screen seeds pass M1 to M4 and every fixture check holds, run B2_s200 to B2_s205 with the same code, marks and fit rules, fitting the heads separately per checkpoint on the same fresh rows. Six-seed pass: mean in_dist change for B >= -0.3 with a paired t-based 95% lower bound (over seeds) >= -0.8; M3 saving >= 0.5 rounds over the best matched comparator on at least 5 of 6 seeds; mean W >= 0.70 on all six; M4 on all six. A confirm pass is a claim only if the fixture checks hold on all six. What it would show: a frozen readout can shorten B2's thinking on today's tasks at flat accuracy. What it would not show: adaptivity on longer chains (ideas 2, 15-17), any gain on the variant split, or anything about H1's trained stop. Rank: low to medium. The accuracy prize is small (overthinking share 1.66-1.91 in_dist points, shown). Its value is compute saved and design information for H1.

issues: Rule 5 (shown: /mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md lines 23 and 128): Stage 1 fits seven heads on about 20k fresh rows before the protected-panel overlap check. Rule 5 bars training on GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind panels whatever a later claim says, so 'no claim can pass without it' is not enough. The last recorded status is 'not yet cleared'; the plan records it as unknown and proceeds.

Training-set overlap is unchecked. B2 trained on the 200k seed-1 build for about 30 passes (shown: 8A-SPEC addendum B1 as cited; RESULT.json s200 final_train_loss 0.021). Fresh rows from the same generator can repeat training items, so the 'settled' labels would partly record memorised answers. The overlap check covers dev splits and protected hashes only. Fix: a new seed, plus a shingle check against the training build.

Rules 1 and 10 (suggested, from the code and the plan): the stop is a fixed sign test (logit > 0 breaks the loop inside the forward pass), not a model-written token or a tool call. For the 59% no-program rows (shown: PROBE.json M1 n_by_len, L=0 is 4,007 of 6,800) no NOOP stop exists. 'No threshold tuned on dev' is true, but 0 is the logistic decision point for the fit-set prevalence, which the generator sets. Ben's ruling must come before any deploy claim; it does not block a measurement.

Floor-induced confound in W (suggested from the label definition; shown in coverage). The label is 0 on every program row before round L+2, so labels split by program presence in mixed families and by program length within program families, and the op head exposes that as NOOP. Shown (B2_s200 RESULT.json extra.coverage, counted here): 19 families have no programs, 12 are all-program, and 3 are mixed: list_stats 29.0%, verify_claim 68.5%, arith_bare 99.0%. W can therefore pass on program presence, which is not settledness. The plan's null-risk names surface difficulty but not this.

Late-K heads have few negatives and no minority count is gated. Under 8c, label(7) is 0 only when the answer is wrong at 7 and right at 8. Shown (PROBE M1 by_len): the net accuracy change from 7 to 8 is about 0.1 point for no-program rows and about 0 for program rows. The flip count is not measured. 'At least 20 rows and both classes' admits families with one or two minority rows, so macro W at K=6 and K=7 can be noise.

Comparator matching is fragile (shown in the plan's rules; suggested as a risk). C1 has no free parameter, so it cannot be matched within 0.1 on the fit split and 0.3 on dev; the strongest zero-parameter rule can drop out of 'best matched'. If nothing matches, M3 is NOT SHOWN for a matching reason. C2 reads the mode head at K below 8, which was never trained there (shown: round_readout default 0 at ledger.py:130), so it is weak by construction. Use a dominance check against every zero-parameter rule that meets M2.

Gold L is the builder's L, not the generator's (shown). progparse.py:199 returns no program for more than N_RES=7 steps, and row_targets returns none when program_for is None. The floor and M4 therefore treat those rows as no-program, and M4 cannot see a stop that cuts their programs. The 528 train rows with 9-11 steps (cited in the plan, not recounted) will also appear in fresh rows. Use len(row['steps']); data.py:25 keeps 'steps'. Whether 'steps' is populated for the no-program families is untested.

M3's absolute mark is nearly automatic (computed from PROBE M1 n_by_len: L=1..7 counts 1073, 1018, 447, 151, 69, 7, 28). With the L+2 floor, program rows average about 4.0 rounds. With wrong rows counted as 8, the 5.5 mean needs no-program right rows to average only about 6.2 rounds. The 5.5 mark does not discriminate; the margin over zero-parameter rules is the real test.

A rule-clean zero-parameter candidate is missing from the comparators (shown: the plan's arms list has only B-E, which needs the head plus NOOP). Standalone E (stop at the first NOOP, K = L+2) is reported in the source notes as costing -3.4 and -5.7 points; that is untested here, since PROBE.json has no freeze run, so E should fail M2. E+1 (stop one round after a NOOP is read) is described there as near free with about 15% of rounds saved; also untested here. The 15% matches program rows alone: 0.41 x 3/8 is about 15% (computed). E+1 is absent from the comparator list and should be Stage 0's main arm.

Whether E+1 acts on no-program rows is untested. The code trains NOOP targets on no-program rows at weight 0.1 (shown in code notes: w_noop, ledger.py:130 and about :501). The source notes say those NOOPs are not usable. If the op head does read NOOP there, E+1 stops those rows at K=3, where no-program accuracy is 76-77% against 84-85% at round 8 (shown: PROBE M1 by_len), so M2 would likely fail. This must be measured, not assumed.

Dev builds are mixed and unnamed (shown: B2_s200 RESULT.json: in_dist n 1,360, variant n 1,320, chain-5 n 1,000; PROBE in_dist n 6,800 from data_big). The plan does not name the variant or chain-5 files. Paired comparisons within a run stay valid, but the numbers cannot be read against RESULT figures (s200 in_dist 90.5 on 1,360 rows vs probe 89.4 on 6,800).

Compute and hours are unsourced. PROBE.json and probe.log record no wall time. Counting round-passes (computed from the K values): probe_loops did 136 per row over 6,800 rows per seed (about 0.92 M); the full plan does 36 per row over about 29,100 rows per seed (about 1.05 M), so about 1.1 times the probe per seed before fresh-row generation (untested). Stage 0 is about 0.36 of the probe per seed, or 0.31 of the full plan. The '4 PC CPU-hours' figure is untested.

Parameters are unsealed. The L2 value is said to be 'fixed in the spec' but no value is given, and class weighting is not stated. Under 8c, label prevalence rises from about 30% at K=1 (shown: right(1) is 30.6% and 30.2%, plus never-right rows) to about 95% at K=7 (suggested, from M1 accuracies). An unweighted logit > 0 rule therefore stops more rows at later rounds by construction. Seal the L2 value and weighting before fitting.

The head is build-time only (suggested from rule 10). Fitting needs gold labels, which the deployed model does not have. Any deploy-time weight change (sleep or learning) makes the heads stale, and no gold-free refit label is tested. F (family holdout) is report-only, yet it is the only check on new kinds, so deploy wording must stay within the 34 generator families until F passes.

Marks were set after reading dev outputs (shown: the plan cites PROBE.json settle means and the family prior). The 5.5 mark, the 0.5-round margin and the family-prior margin therefore carry dev information. Thresholds should be set on fresh rows only and recorded in the seal.

The family-prior comparator is on the wrong label (computed here from PROBE M1 by_family right(K) rates and M3 n_by_family): K=3 gives 0.861 (s100) and 0.880 (s101); K=8 gives 0.906 and 0.915. These reproduce the plan's 0.86-0.88 and 0.91-0.92 within rounding. But the test label is settled(K), whose family rates are higher than right(K) rates, and the figure is in-sample on dev. Compute it on the fit split with settled labels.
The 13-word shingle check can drop most rows on templated prompts (untested): shared template text, not items, may match. Report drop counts per family and per source, not just the total.

fixed_plan.title: Stage 0: zero-parameter stop rules on B2 (CPU), then gated frozen heads
fixed_plan.ben_line: We check whether the thinker can stop early by reading what it already produces: the NOOP token it writes, and whether its answer stops changing. We test those simple rules first with no new training, and add a tiny frozen reader only if they leave a gap.
fixed_plan.question: On B2's two screen checkpoints, does any stop rule the model can run by itself (its own NOOP token, or its answers across rounds, with no fitted weights) save rounds at flat in-distribution accuracy? If none does, does a frozen 257-parameter readout close the gap when fitted only on clean fresh rows?
fixed_plan.one_change: Stage 0 changes nothing in the model: it measures stop rules on a saved 8-round sweep (measurement only). Stage 1, run only if Stage 0 leaves a gap, adds seven frozen Linear(256,1) heads on ln_z(Z[:,1]) at rounds 1 to 7 (1,799 params, +0.054% of 3,302,481, computed), fitted with an unweighted logistic loss at an L2 value written into the sealed spec.
arms: A: fixed 8 rounds (reference; the normal B2 answer).
E+1 (zero parameters; Stage 0 main arm): stop at the first completed round K >= 3 at which the op head read NOOP at round K-1; otherwise 8. Uses only the model's own op head.
E (zero parameters; Stage 0, reported): stop at the first completed round K >= 2 whose op-head argmax is NOOP (K = L+2 on program rows). Expected to fail M2 per the source notes.
C1 (zero parameters): stop at the first K >= 3 where the answers at K-2, K-1 and K are equal (k = 2 fixed in advance).
Oracle (report only): gold-picked any round K in 1..8 at which the answer is right.
Stage 1 only: B (seven frozen heads; first K in 1..7 with logit > 0, else 8), fitted on clean fresh rows with settled labels; B-strict and the round-8 head are report-only.
Stage 1 only: R (B's per-row stop rounds permuted across dev rows, fixed seed) as control; F (family holdout, 27 vs 7 families) report-only.
C2, C3 and D are descriptive only and do not gate; their thresholds are fitted on the matching split and never shipped.

Stage 0 gap rule: Stage 1 runs only if no zero-parameter rule (E+1, C1, E) meets M2 with a mean saving of at least 0.5 rounds (wrong rows counted as 8) on both seeds. If one does, Stage 1 must beat it by at least 0.5 rounds at M2 to count.

Stage 1 M1 (learnability, stratified): W = macro within-family AUROC of the head logit, computed separately on no-program families and within L-matched program strata; families need at least 10 minority rows per class; K values with under 2% minority rows are reported, not averaged. PASS: mean W >= 0.70 on both seeds AND the head beats the zero-parameter P(NOOP) score by >= 0.05 on program strata. PROVED WRONG: W < 0.60 on the no-program strata on both seeds.
Stage 1 M2 (accuracy of B): same bands as Stage 0 M2, paired, on dev in_dist, chain-5 and variant.

Stage 1 M3 (compute): mean rounds over in_dist, wrong rows counted as 8. PASS: mean <= 5.5 on both seeds AND B is at least 0.5 rounds below every zero-parameter rule that meets M2 on that seed (dominance, no matching); B's dev change beats the R control by >= 0.5 points. The 5.5 band is nearly automatic under the floor, so the margin is what counts.

Stage 1 M4 (program safety), with gold L = len(row['steps']) and any row where builder L differs from len(steps) reported: at most 0.5% of program rows stop before round L+2 on both seeds; chain-5 mean stop round at least 2.0 above one-step rows. PROVED WRONG: chain-5 median stop round <= 2 on either seed.
Stage 1 F (family holdout): report with CI. Any deploy claim beyond the 34 generator families is blocked until F passes.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Stage 0: none (it is measurement only; a null result is reported as a result). Stage 1: W < 0.60 on the no-program strata on both seeds; or B's mean rounds at or above the best M2-passing zero-parameter rule on both seeds; or an in_dist change <= -1.0 on either seed; or chain-5 median stop round <= 2 on either seed.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Routes to a false pass. (1) W can pass on program presence, because the floor labels program rows 0 before L+2 and the op head exposes NOOP; stratify W and compare with the P(NOOP) score. (2) Late-K heads have few negatives (label(7)=0 only when wrong at 7 and right at 8); gate a minimum minority count and report it. (3) The 8c label marks never-right rows as stop-ok, so W partly measures hopelessness; also report W on right-at-8 rows. (4) M3's 5.5 band is nearly automatic under the floor (computed), so only the dominance margin is informative. (5) Matching to C2, C3 and D is fragile and C1 cannot be matched; use dominance. (6) C2 reads an untrained mode head at K below 8 (shown: round_readout default 0), so it is a weak comparator. (7) Marks were set after reading dev outputs; thresholds should come from fresh rows only and be stated as such. (8) The ceiling is small: overthinking gives 1.7 to 1.9 points of in_dist at most (shown, PROBE M4), so the value is mainly rounds saved, and the 15% saving from E+1 is about program rows only (computed).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Stage 0 rules use only the model's own op head (NOOP) and its own answers across rounds, with one fixed design constant (k = 2 for C1). Stage 1 heads are frozen weights fitted at build time on gold-labelled generator rows: allowed as build (rule 10), but the deployed model cannot refit them without gold labels, so any deploy-time learning makes them stale. The logit > 0 break is a hand-written sign test inside the forward pass; Ben must rule under rules 1 and 10 before any Stage 1 deploy claim. The cap of 8 is fixed, so the model decides when to stop only within 8 rounds.
