Do not reuse rules_real.reference or fewshot.find_reference. They parse only example-pair prompts, omit CMP, and return None for both 'not found' and 'budget hit'. Any new multi-slot search must report found, not-found and budget-hit separately. Drop the 6M-state arm unless timing on 20 questions per cell shows it is feasible (the roughly 5-6M depth-2 candidates at 8 items could need several GB).

Count steps, numbers, words and letters from the raw text and the generator's executor-verified trace, not from progparse. progparse truncates at 16 numbers and 7 steps, and Try.make silently keeps only the first 7 steps. Keep every generated row in the denominator.

Move the build after the T1 re-screen (span copy) and the crafting contract (world verbs, per-episode state, tape size, round budget of at least 17 for 16 writes). Otherwise the counts describe the wrong interface. Keep the K1 16-write column conditional, since T1 has not passed its confirm.

idea.title: Mid-loop prompt cut: does B2's state keep a binding?
idea.summary: B2 re-reads the whole prompt every round, so a binding written inside one prompt never has to be remembered. This CPU probe swaps a donor's prompt-derived inputs in at round 4 while keeping the 17 state vectors, and asks whether the state still holds the original question's value. It is the cheapest test of whether any in-state memory exists before anything is built.
idea.change: Diagnostic script beside probe_loops.py, no model change. At round 4 replace reader output X and mask, number-slot embeddings and validity, and word keys with a donor's (same family, different answer; evalx.donor_pairs), keep Z. Fit a ridge probe on uncut round-8 states (label: last digit of the first step's first prompt-number operand, 10 classes) on train rows and score cut states against the original and the donor digit on dev in_dist. Cuts at rounds 0, 2, 4, 6; each run with executed results Rs kept and zeroed; controls: untrained same-size B2 and reader-slot ceiling.
idea.why: Whole-state donor swaps already show the state matters (donor_match 58.2% on seed 200) but they replace the state too, so they cannot say whether Z holds the old prompt. Cutting only the prompt separates 'Z still holds the old value' from 'Z only mirrors the new prompt'. Controls 2-7 are used memory (zeroing them costs 7.8 chain-5 points), so some state use is already visible.

test.where: PC CPU (needs custom-io/work/data and data_big copies); raw B2 seeds 200-205 from code/b2ckpt.
test.arms: Uncut vs cut at rounds 0/2/4/6; Rs kept vs zeroed; untrained control; reader ceiling. Six seeds, no screen needed.
test.pass_mark: On 6 of 6 seeds: uncut round-8 accuracy at least 40% (chance about 10%); after the round-4 cut the original digit at least 30% and the donor digit at most 15%, in both Rs variants.
test.proved_wrong: On at least 5 of 6 seeds the donor digit is at least 30% and the original at most 15% after the cut (Z only mirrors the current prompt), or uncut round-8 accuracy is at most 20% on at least 5 of 6 seeds.

problems: [shown] Missing closest prior: the register-loop model A ran a mid-loop state interchange at round 1 (donor registers swapped in, rounds 2..R run on them). It matched the counterfactual on 1.8% of rows (mark 40), and the team read this as 'A's rounds recompute from the prompt instead of carrying the intermediate value' (custom-io/REPORT-custom-reader-talker.md ~line 82; custom-io/gpt-b2-leak-and-credit-2026-10-05.md ~line 103). The idea's closest_prior line omits it. The intervention differs (prompt-only swap with Z kept), but it asks the same question on a sibling model.

[shown] Expected outcome conflicts with the team's own lesson, 'Exact intermediate values beat latent ones' (REPORT-custom-reader-talker.md ~line 80). B2 keeps step values exactly in Rs and vals (ledger.py 337-339), not in Z. A Z-only test with Rs zeroed is likely to fail by design, so a fail says little about B2's memory and a pass would be surprising. The prediction should be written down before the run.

[shown] 'Round' is undefined. The loop is `for t in range(n)` (ledger.py 307), and steps are written at t=1..7 (`1 <= t <= N_RES`, line 319; vals[:, R0+t-1] at 337). design-B2.md line 28 says 'Round t = 1..7 writes program step t'. 'Round 4' could mean loop index 3 or 4. By the cut, steps 1-3 are already written, so a negative result may mean the binding is no longer needed rather than not held. Pin the index, and add a cut before step 1 is written and a case where a later step still needs the original first operand.

[shown] Label coincidence: donor_pairs (evalx.py 75-91) pairs by family and different answer only. Nothing stops the donor's first-operand last digit from matching the original's. On those rows 'original digit at least 30%' and 'donor digit at most 15%' test the same label, so the pass cannot be met there. Pair on different labels and report how many rows that leaves.

[shown] Label set: 4,007 of 6,800 in_dist rows have no program (design/LOOPS-probe.md line 43), so only about 40% of rows are labelled. Step-1 operands can be constants (CONSTS 1,2,10,100 in progparse.py 8-9; row_targets 201-203), which have no prompt-number last digit. Parser-dropped rows with more than 7 steps also fall into L=0 (progparse.py 197-199). The idea gives no n per seed and no exclusion rule.

[shown] The probe is fit on uncut states and scored on cut states, which is a distribution shift. After the cut, rounds 4-7 read donor S0 and X, so a probe fit on uncut states can map cut states to a class whatever they hold. Add a probe fit on cut train-row states (label = original digit), or the result is confounded. Also say which split 'uncut round-8 accuracy' is measured on; the probe is fit on train rows the model trained on, so use dev held-out.

[shown] The ceiling is undefined for the path the loop actually reads. D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md (table lines 6-13; control row) gives the reader window at 99.997-100% for the lowest digit place, but the pooled number slot that enters the loop (ledger.py 291-296) keeps the lowest place at 72.2, 67.2, 81.9, 83.2, 70.4 and 65.2% across seeds 200-205 (control 74.2%). The 40% uncut bar and 30% cut bar need a reference of about 65-83% for that path, not 100%.

[shown] The Rs-zeroed arm is not a Z-only test. The executor reads vals inside the loop, and vals keeps the pre-cut results (ledger.py 337). Writes after the cut (338-339) are built from those executed values, so later Rs entries carry pre-cut information even after Rs is zeroed. Zero the pre-cut result entries in vals too, or label the arm 'Z plus executed history'.

[shown] Implementation gaps: kvx is computed once before the loop (ledger.py 302), so the cut must rebuild kv_of for every block. The mask is rebuilt each round (311). S0 is built once from pooled X (291-296), so the number slots must be rebuilt from the donor X. Word keys Kw (299-301) are read only after the loop (345, 350), so cutting them has no effect on Z; drop them or say so. Donor and current batches need a common padded length (evalx.py docstring 95-98).

[shown] Controls evidence is thin in the idea. 'Zeroing controls 2-7 costs 7.8 chain-5' is seed 200 only (architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md 5b; RESULT.json for B2_s200 has no ctl27 key). The six-seed numbers are in D0-RESULT (line 20): pooled-5 -0.6 to -13.6 and chain-5 -0.6 to -36.9, uneven across seeds. Cite D0. ctl27 zeroes controls only, not the 9 registers, so it shows that controls are used, not which carrier holds the binding.

[shown] Overclaim: 'the cheapest test of whether any in-state memory exists' is not what the test covers. It tests Z with Rs zeroed, and it leaves vals (exact results) and the rebuilt S0 as other carriers. Narrow the claim to 'whether Z holds the prompt binding after rounds 4-7 read a donor prompt'.

[shown] Pass and fail bands are incomplete. Pass needs 6 of 6 seeds. 'Proved wrong' needs 5 of 6 on one pattern. Seed counts of 1-4 of 6 and mixed patterns get no verdict. Add an inconclusive band, fixed before running (rule 4). 'Chance about 10%' is untested: the chance level is the majority-class rate of the actual label distribution, and that needs computing.

[suggested] No behavioural arm, so the probe is indirect. The model needs the binding only if a later step or the answer uses it. Add: cut at the same round, then score answers on rows where a later program step needs the original first operand (uncut vs cut vs donor_match, using donor_eval logic at evalx.py 93-110). That measures what the model uses, not whether a probe can read a digit.

[shown] Rule check. R1 passes (diagnostic only, no answer-path change). R4 is satisfiable (b2ckpt has seeds 200-205; the untrained control needs six random inits). R5 passes only if rows come from dev in_dist and train, and not from blind_*.jsonl or GOLD-PRIVATE-v1.json (data-pool/PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md lines 28-33); the idea names no files. R6 passes. R9 passes. R10 cannot be checked: the 'deploy version' ('carry-state') is undefined, so say what the model would learn, with no outside step.

[untested] The 0.5 h CPU estimate is unchecked. It covers 6 seeds x 4 cut rounds x 2 Rs arms, controls, and a ridge fit on train states, with torch not installed here. The LOOPS probe needed 6,800 rows per checkpoint for M1-M5.

[shown] Loop-state context: the LOOPS probe (results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json) shows controller-token RMS growing 3.4-3.9x from iteration 1 to 8 (gate G3 closed). The state changes a lot each round, so a Z value from round 4 may be overwritten in rounds 5-8 regardless of memory. The untrained control should run at the same cut rounds, and the idea should say so (suggested).
critiques.rescue: Revise, do not kill. (1) Cite the register-loop round-1 interchange (1.8% vs mark 40; REPORT-custom-reader-talker.md ~line 82) as the closest prior and predict a Z-only failure by design, since B2 keeps exact values in Rs/vals. (2) Define the round index against ledger.py 307-339 and design-B2.md line 28. Add a cut before step 1 is written, plus a row set where a later step needs the original first operand. (3) Pair donors with different first-operand labels (evalx.py 75-91 checks answers only) and report n per seed. Restrict labels to prompt-number first operands (exclude CONSTS slots 16-19) and state the no-program and dropped-row exclusions (4,007 of 6,800 rows are L=0). (4) Fit the probe on uncut states and also on cut train-row states, and report uncut accuracy on dev held-out. (5) Set the ceiling per path from D0 (pooled slot 65-83%, reader window 100%). (6) Zero pre-cut result entries in vals as well as Rs, or call the arm 'Z plus executed history'. (7) Add a behavioural arm: answer accuracy on rows where a later step needs the original first operand, uncut vs cut vs donor_match. (8) Add an inconclusive band and the majority-class baseline, fixed before running. (9) Cite D0's six-seed ctl27 numbers instead of seed 200 alone. (10) Narrow the claim to Z with Rs and vals zeroed. (11) Drop the word-key cut (no effect on Z, ledger.py 299-301, 345), rebuild kvx, mask and S0 at the cut, and pad donors as evalx.py 95-98 does. (12) Define the deploy version as a learned mechanism the model runs itself (rule 10). Rules 1, 4, 6 and 9 already pass, and rule 5 holds if only dev in_dist and train rows are used.

critiques.expected_effect: If run as written, the likeliest result is that the Z-only arm (Rs zeroed) fails: after the cut the original digit stays below 30%. B2 keeps exact values in Rs and vals, and the team's register-loop result says latent carry is weak, so the failure is predicted by the design rather than new. A pass would be new: Z would hold the prompt binding after four rounds read a donor prompt. The run would then move the memory question from 'unknown' to 'latent carry exists or does not'. The result would not decide any roadmap item by itself. It is cheap (CPU, about 0.5 h estimated, untested) and worth running only after the revisions above, with the behavioural arm.

problems: Score 6 is the rule-10 autonomy score the director asked for. The probe itself is a measurement, so it adds no step to the deployed model (the idea's R10 line is right). What fails is the stated deploy path: 'if it passes, the carry-state idea is the deploy version' (idea.autonomy). That version is never specified, and on B2 as built it rests on hand-written steps that rule 10 forbids. Labels: shown (code), suggested (scoring). Code base: scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/ (ledger.py below).

Deploy step 1, reading the prompt numbers, is hand code that runs on every question with no model choice. A regex takes the first 16 numbers, int() parses them, and the digit spans are mean-pooled into the number slots S0 (ledger.py:200-217, 289-291, 296). INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md rows A1-A3 and A7 list these, along with the int64 executor (ledger.py:76-86). The cut the probe tests replaces exactly these slots, so a carry-state built on them inherits rule 1 and rule 10 violations. Labels: shown. Autonomous version (suggested): remove the regex reader (planned as N1/T1 in the inventory), or make the parser a tool the model chooses to call by writing text.

Deploy step 2, the mid-loop input change, does not exist in B2. The prompt keys and values are computed once before the loop (ledger.py:302, kvx), and the batch is fixed for all 8 rounds. A mid-loop change can only come from the planned T1 design, where tool replies are appended to a tape that the reader and thinker re-read (tool.py:21, 188). That is autonomous only if the model chooses to call the tool. Labels: shown for B2 code; untested for T1 (the brief reports its write_copy screen failed, so it has no passing screen).

Deploy step 3, the carry itself, has no decision rule. The same controller rewrites Z every round (ledger.py:312-314), and the idea names no keep or forget gate and no learning signal. The only signal it names is the donor pairs from evalx.donor_pairs (same family, different answer), which is generator knowledge. Pre-ship training may use generator data (rule 10: building before shipping is not a deploy step), but a deployed model that must learn new bindings from its own tries cannot. Labels: shown (code), suggested (autonomous version). Autonomous version (suggested): label post-cut recall with the model's own pre-cut program, checked by the exact executor, and train on the model's own checked tries during sleep.

Scope: Z is reset to learned constants for every question (ledger.py:304; shown), so the carry works only inside one question. Nothing here covers memory across questions, which is what 'learns like a person' needs. A passing probe would not show that the model can keep a note across sessions. That needs a store the model writes itself, such as a tool or notebook, which the idea does not test. Label: shown (code); untested (the store).

Probe check 1, the executed-value path (orchestrator check). The cut list omits vals, the int64 values read by the executor and the NUM talker (ledger.py:293, 333-337). If vals is not swapped, results written after round 4 carry the original prompt's numbers into Rs (ledger.py:336-339) and into the result-slot valid bits (ledger.py:337). Those bits stay in the attention mask (ledger.py:311), and zeroing Rs does not clear them. The idea also does not say which states the ridge probe is fit on. Uncut states keep Rs, so a zeroed-Rs run is a shifted distribution, and the probe must be fit separately per Rs variant. Labels: shown (code); suggested (fix).

Probe validity, binding definition. The probe reads the digit, but B2's natural binding is a pointer. S0 gives each number an ordinal embedding (ledger.py:296), and operands are slot pointers (ledger.py:323-331). A Z that holds 'slot 0 is the first number' reads the donor's digit after the cut, because slot 0 now holds donor values. The proved-wrong rule (donor at least 30 percent and original at most 15 percent on 5 of 6 seeds) would then fire on a working pointer memory. Fix: add a second read for which ordinal the first operand is, and report both. Labels: shown (code); suggested (failure mode, not run).

Probe check 3, the binding label (orchestrator check). Step-1 operands cannot be results: result slots are invalid at t=1 (ledger.py:294, 323), so the worry about later operands being results applies only to steps 2-7. The label still has three holes. (a) ADD, MUL, MIN and MAX are commutative (progparse.py:12), and the loss accepts either operand order (ledger.py:510-512), so 'first operand' is undefined for them. (b) A constant operand (slots 16-19 hold 1, 2, 10, 100; progparse.py:8) has a fixed last digit, so it must be excluded. (c) progparse's Builder lists every slot with the same value as a candidate, so a value that appears twice in a prompt is ambiguous. Labels: shown.

Probe check 2, the untrained control (orchestrator check). 'Sits near chance' is untested. An untrained B2's Z is dominated by learned constants and small init scales (ledger.py:153-160, 304). But the ordinal and place embeddings are inputs (ledger.py:296, reader place rows), so a ridge probe can beat 10 percent on an untrained state. Also, 10 percent assumes uniform labels, which is untested. Fix: report a label-permutation floor and a majority-class baseline, and make the pass mark relative to the untrained control (trained minus untrained). Label: untested.

Missing built-in floor and transfer check. The probe is fit on uncut states and applied to cut states, so it may not transfer at all. Cutting at round 0 removes all original prompt information before any computation, so the original digit should read at chance and the donor digit should read high. If the donor digit does not read high at round 0, the probe is not transferring and the other cut rounds mean nothing. Suggested: make round 0 a required pass.

Implementation: 'no model change' is not quite accurate. A mid-loop cut means re-implementing Ledger.run (ledger.py:278-357), because kvx (line 302) and S0 (lines 289-297) are built before the loop. Before any cut, the script must reproduce run() exactly on the dev rows, with the same predictions and states. Also, the word keys Kw do not enter the loop (used only at lines 345 and 350), so cutting them at round 4 changes nothing in Z and is a no-op for this probe. Labels: shown (code); suggested (the reproduction check).

Pass-mark ambiguity: 'uncut round-8 accuracy at least 40 percent' does not say whether it is the ridge probe's digit accuracy or B2's answer accuracy. B2's own in_dist exact on seed 200 is 90.5 (RESULT.json final_eval), so if the mark means the answer, it is trivial. Specify it as probe accuracy and set it relative to the controls (see the untrained-control item). Label: shown (RESULT.json).

Verified claims. Z starts from learned constants (ledger.py:304), and each round cross-attends to the full prompt (ledger.py:302-311, 117-121). Seed 200: donor exact 3.24 and donor_match 58.24 over 1,360 rows, skipped 0, zero_state 0.0 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json). Controls 2-7 cost -1.6 pooled-5 and -7.8 chain-5 on seed 200 (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md line 82). The six checkpoints exist with sha256 sidecars (code/b2ckpt). The probe needs the data copies, which sit on Ben's PC (RESULT.json config paths), so it cannot run from this snapshot. The 0.5-hour estimate is untested. Six seeds, train and dev in_dist only, and CPU only meet rules 4, 5 and 6 as written.

Note on the lesion family. zero_state zeroes the whole state tuple, including vals and valid (models/base.py:55-56), not Z alone. The idea's claim that donor and zero lesions show the state matters is therefore about the whole state, not about the thinker's own memory. Label: shown.
critiques.rescue: (1) Keep the probe as a diagnostic, and first: check that the re-implemented loop reproduces run() exactly with no cut; add a round-0 cut floor, a label-permutation floor and an untrained control; swap vals and valid together with the prompt slots at the cut; fit a separate probe per Rs variant; read both the digit and the ordinal pointer; exclude constant operands and use the unordered pair for commutative ops (or restrict the label to SUB, DIV, MOD and CMP); set the pass mark relative to the controls, not as an absolute 40 percent. (2) Do not treat a pass as a deploy method. Write the autonomous path first. The mid-loop input is a tool reply on T1's tape (tool.py:21, 188). The number reading is the model's own reader or a tool it chooses to call, not the regex slots. The carry signal is the model's own pre-cut program, checked by the exact executor, so sleep can train recall from its own checked tries without generator data. All of this is untested.
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior work: donor_eval (custom_io/evalx.py:93-133) swaps the whole state, not the prompt. Seed 200 gives donor_match 58.2 and exact 3.2 (RESULT.json, B2_s200). zero_state and shuffle_state zero or roll the whole state tuple (models/base.py:55-56). ctl27 zeroes controls 2-7 after each iteration (ledger.py:315-316; diag_d0.py --ctl27). probe_loops.py varies the loop count, not the inputs. None cuts the prompt mid-loop, so none tests whether Z keeps the original value after the input changes. No mid-loop cut run exists in the snapshot.
critiques.expected_effect: If run as written on six seeds (about 0.5 hour of CPU per the idea, untested here), it gives a digit-accuracy table per seed, cut round and Rs variant. Without the fixes it can false-fail a working pointer memory (binding-definition item) and can false-pass through a label or distribution artifact that the untrained control and round-0 floor would expose. With the fixes it tests whether Z keeps information from the old prompt after the input changes, which is useful for choosing T1's tape design. It does not show an autonomous deploy method, and it changes nothing in the deployed model. The carry-state deploy path still needs its own design and a test on the tape interface.

problems: [shown] Cut spec is incomplete. The executor reads vals (exact int64; prompt numbers are the regex values set before the loop), and each new step's result embedding is computed from value_code(v) (code/reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py, run() about lines 288-294 and 335-339). The idea swaps only 'number-slot embeddings and validity'. Unless vals[:, :R0] and valid are also replaced, steps written after the cut (t=4..7, since steps are written at t=1..7 at ledger.py:319) execute on the ORIGINAL numbers, and their results carry original digits into Rs. That leaks the original into the 'donor' condition. S0 (ledger.py:295) also holds vcode(value_code(vals)) (the exact digits) plus a pooled reader term, so both parts must be recomputed from the donor.

[shown] The claim that 'only the Rs-zeroed variant tests Z alone' is wrong. Z is updated by cross-attention to S = [S0, Rs] at every round (ledger.py:307-318). The first step is written at t=1 (ledger.py:319-322), so the results of steps 1-3 are already absorbed into Z before a round-4 cut. Zeroing Rs after the cut removes only later inputs. Z can therefore hold step 1's RESULT, which for ADD, SUB and MUL depends on the first operand's last digit. The probe could read the operand digit through the result.

[suggested] The label is confounded. Use the first-operand last digit only on rows where it differs from the step-1 result's last digit and from the donor's. Add a control probe on the result's last digit. Also, the first operand may be a constant (1, 2, 10, 100), so define which operand is used and drop rows without a prompt-number operand.

[shown] Donor pairs are chosen on answers, not first-operand digits (code/reader/custom_io/evalx.py:75-91). About 1 in 10 pairs (suggested; digit distribution not in the snapshot) will share the original's and donor's label. Those rows make the two readings identical and must be dropped. A 10% chance level holds only if digits are uniform; use the majority-class baseline instead (untested).

[shown] The pass and proved-wrong marks are asymmetric and leave the likeliest outcome unscored. The pass needs donor at most 15%, meaning the state must exclude the current prompt. But rounds 4-7 cross-attend to the donor prompt (ledger.py:302 and 311), so a state holding both original and donor digits is the natural result. 'Both' (original at least 30%, donor at least 30%) fails the pass and does not meet the proved-wrong rule (original at most 15%). Score the margin original minus donor on the same rows instead.

[shown] The round-0 cut is a free null, because Z starts from learned constants (ledger.py:304) and nothing original is in the state before round 0. The idea runs round 0 but gives it no mark. Add a mark: the round-0 original readout should sit at the chance or majority level, and the carry effect is original(cut 4) minus original(cut 0).

[suggested] The untrained control is undefined. Output projections are initialised at 0.02/sqrt(3*blocks*n_loops), about 0.003 for B2 (ledger.py:160), so untrained Z hardly depends on the prompt. The orchestrator note's 'sits near chance' is untested. Report the untrained number and the probe's standardisation, rather than assuming it.

[shown] Round indexing is undefined. 'Cut at round 4' must say which iteration index is meant. Steps are written at t=1..7 (ledger.py:319), so a cut at 4 falls after steps 1-3. Also specify the probe features (17x256 = 4,352 dims, or control 1 only), and choose ridge regularisation on held-out rows. The probe is currently fit on train rows the model was trained on (24k updates), so its states differ from dev states. Use held-out generator rows if they exist (untested; the generator is not in the snapshot).

[shown] The ctl27 evidence is understated. The idea says 'seed 200 only'. D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md (/mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md) shows ctl27 on all six seeds: pooled-5 -0.6 to -13.6, chain-5 -0.6 to -36.9. Seed 200 is -1.62 and -7.8, which matches results/d0/B2_s200.json. Cite D0-RESULT. Zeroing controls shows that the state is used, not that it holds a prompt binding.

[shown] The 40% gate is ambiguous. It is unclear whether 'uncut round-8 accuracy' is the probe's accuracy or the model's answer accuracy. Intact seed-200 in_dist exact is 90.5% (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json, final_eval). If it is probe accuracy, its ceiling is not given. Name the metric and the rows.

[shown] The closest prior is missing from the idea. diag_register.py ('round-1 register interchange', about lines 134-160; PASS-MARKS.md line 59) is a mid-loop state swap, but on the register-loop design, not B2. Its results are not in results/. The statement 'none cuts the prompt mid-loop' is true for the prompt, but the interchange should be cited as the nearest prior.

[shown] Verified: Z starts from learned constants (ledger.py:304); each round cross-attends to the full prompt (CBlock.forward at ledger.py:117; mask at 311); seed-200 donor exact 3.24 and donor_match 58.24 (RESULT.json lesions.donor.in_dist); zero_state 0.0 (lesions.zero_state); all six B2 checkpoints exist and their sha256 matches the sidecars (code/b2ckpt/B2_s200..205).

[suggested] Pass gate: six of six seeds on fixed marks with no pilot. Seed-to-seed spread is large (ctl27 -0.6 to -36.9 on chain-5), so a 6/6 rule can fail from heterogeneity rather than from the absence of binding. Sampling noise is small by comparison: about 1.5 points SE on roughly 1,000 dev rows (1,360 in_dist rows per seed in RESULT.json). A 5-of-6 rule may be fairer, but the rule must be fixed before the run.

[suggested] Autonomy and relevance. The probe is a diagnostic and fits rule 10. But 'if it passes, the carry-state idea is the deploy version' is undefined. The probe tests within-question memory after the prompt leaves the window. It does not test memory across episodes or a learned choice of what to keep. Do not count it as a deploy-time mechanism.
critiques.rescue: Keep the probe, but fix it before running. (1) Cut the whole prompt side at round k: X, xm, kvx, the S0 number part (exact value code and pooled term), valid[:R0] and vals[:R0]. Say so in the spec. (2) Score the margin original minus donor on the same rows, with the round-0 cut as a null. (3) Use labels only on rows where the first-operand digit differs from both the donor's digit and the step-1 result's last digit. Add a result-digit control probe. (4) Define the round index and the probe features. Report the untrained control as a number. (5) Proposed marks, to be fixed before running (suggested): pass on 5 of 6 or 6 of 6 seeds if original-digit readout is at least 30%, original minus donor is at least 15 points, and the round-0 original readout is at most chance plus 5. Proved wrong if original readout is at most 15% on at least 5 of 6 seeds, or donor exceeds original on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Keep both Rs variants. Cite D0-RESULT for ctl27 and diag_register.py for the interchange prior.
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior on the prompt: none cuts the prompt mid-loop on B2 (checked in code/reader/custom_io/). Whole-state donor swap: evalx.py donor_eval (def at line 93; the state swap is the model.talk(model.state(don), cur) call at line 116, not 93-102 as the idea says). Round-1 register interchange: diag_register.py interchange() (about lines 134-160) and PASS-MARKS.md line 59, on the register-loop design, not B2. Lesions on B2 seed 200 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json): zero_state 0.0, shuffle_state in_dist 7.8, donor in_dist exact 3.24, donor_match 58.24. Controls 2-7 zeroed (ctl27), six seeds: results/d0 and D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md. No result file for the proposed cut was found.
critiques.expected_effect: Diagnostic only, no gain claimed. Labels: suggested, untested. Under the marks as written, the most likely outcome is an unscored 'both' pattern: some original-digit readout (partly from step-1 result information already in Z) and some donor-digit readout (rounds 4-7 re-read the donor prompt). My rough guess is a 10-20% chance of a sealed pass on 6 of 6 and a 20-30% chance of a sealed proved-wrong, with the rest unscored. Sampling noise is small (about 1.5 points SE on about 1,000 rows per seed). The decision risk comes from the marks, the uncut control and seed-to-seed spread. Cost is about 0.5 CPU hours, plausible but not measured here. Passing would show that within-question state keeps some prompt-derived value after the prompt is removed. It would not show a cross-episode memory or a deploy mechanism.

problems: Wrong target for B2's architecture (shown). The answer path reads exact values from the executor, not from Z: NUM mode prints vals[i][k] (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py lines 396-399), and the step heads read only Z[:,0] to output op and pointers (ledger.py 321-331). Suggested: a working B2 need not store an operand's digit in Z. So the uncut gate (at least 40%, 6 of 6 seeds) can fail for a design reason, and the proved-wrong clause (uncut at most 20% on 5 of 6 seeds) can fire without the cut being tested. A null would be a readout artifact, not evidence about memory.

Z is not the model's whole per-question memory (shown). The controller re-reads S = [S0; Rs], 27 slots, every round (ledger.py 309-311, 322). S0 holds exact value codes of the prompt numbers (295-296) and Rs holds executed results (336-339). The redesign note 'The 17 vectors are the whole of the thinker's own memory' (/mnt/project-files/architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md, section 5b) is contradicted by the code. A Z-only probe cannot show that no in-state memory exists before anything is built.

The cut list is incomplete and partly a no-op (shown). It does not say whether vals and valid (the executor values that NUM answers read) are swapped, or whether the value-code term of S0 (vcode(value_code(vals)), ledger.py 295-296) is swapped or only the pooled reader term. Word keys Kw are never read inside the loop (used only at lines 299-301, 345, 350), so swapping them at round 4 cannot change Z. The swap list must name X and xm (lines 302, 311), all of S0 for slots 0-15, and vals and valid.

Rs leak or out-of-distribution (shown). Step t writes its result into Rs at iteration t (ledger.py 336-339) and the controller reads Rs every round (309-311). By the round-4 cut, steps 1-3 results are already in Z's history. If Rs is zeroed only after the cut, step-1 results (functions of the first operand) can carry the label into Z. If Rs is zeroed from round 0, the model runs out of distribution: on seed 200 the noexec lesion gives chain-5 2.9 and in_dist 52.2 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200/RESULT.json, lesions and chain5). The zeroed arm is therefore leaky or degraded, and 'zeroing Rs tests Z alone' does not hold for a round-4 cut.

Missing controls and sanity bars. (a) No uncut Rs-zeroed baseline, which is the right comparator for the zeroed cut arm. (b) The untrained control and the 'reader-slot ceiling' have no pass bar, and the ceiling is undefined. A ceiling on the reader output X would sit near 100% (D0 per the brief, not re-read here) and says nothing about Z. The untrained model's out-projections are scaled to about 0.003 (ledger.py 158-160), so its Z is nearly input-independent (suggested). Near-chance is therefore likely but unverified. (c) No round-0 donor sanity bar. A donor-only state must read the donor target well; if it cannot, the target is wrong for B2 (see item 1) and no round-4 result means anything.

Pass and proved-wrong clauses leave a gap (shown in the idea text). Results such as uncut 20-40%, or original and donor both at 10-25%, match neither clause. It is not stated whether the proved-wrong clause applies in one or both Rs variants, or whether 'both variants' must pass together. Rule 4 needs a pre-registered three-way outcome table with the variant rule written in.

Chance and labels are not fixed (untested; the dev and train rows are not in the snapshot). 'Chance about 10%' assumes a uniform last-digit prior, and no prior or majority-class baseline is given. The label must exclude constant first operands (slots 16-19 hold 1, 2, 10, 100; ledger.py 292-293). Pairs whose donor digit equals the original's (suggested: about one in ten) make the 'original at least 30%, donor at most 15%' rules overlap, so exclude or report them separately. Give n per cell: in_dist is 1,360 rows per seed (shown, RESULT.json donor.in_dist.n), and the labelled subset is smaller.

Probe spec not fixed (Rule 4). Missing: the ridge lambda and how it is chosen (fixed in advance, not tuned on dev), feature standardization, whether the probe reads raw Z or ln_z(Z) (ledger.py 342), one-vs-rest or multinomial, the number of train rows, and whether the probe is fit on states the model memorised in training (suggested: fit on a held-out slice of dev-like rows).

Round indexing is undefined. The loop runs t = 0..7 (ledger.py 307-308) and writes steps at t = 1..7 (319-337). 'Cut at round k' must be defined as the state before iteration t = k, and 'round 8' as Z after t = 7.

The hook does not exist, and building it is not in the estimate. run() has only the lesions noexec, opswap, nowordc and ctl27 (ledger.py 300-334); no mid-loop prompt swap exists (shown, so the idea's closest-prior claim holds). The diagnostic needs a copy of run() with the swap, plus a check that the copy with no cut reproduces B2's intact outputs (reference: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/results/d0/B2_s200.json, intact in_dist 90.59, chain-5 99.4). That build is not in the 0.5 h estimate.

Compute and GPU (suggested unless marked). The 0.5 h CPU estimate holds only with a cap on train rows (suggested: about 20k). Uncapped 200k rows per seed would take on the order of 1-3 h of CPU for six seeds (untested; torch is not installed here). No GPU is needed. On the RTX 5070 Ti a forward-only pass of a 3.3M-param model at batch 256 fits well under 1 GB of the 16 GB (suggested), so the probe costs a small fraction of the roughly 1 h B2 training run. The data is on the PC only (config paths in RESULT.json), so nothing can run in this snapshot.

What the donor evidence shows. donor_match 58.2 on seed 200 (shown, RESULT.json lesions.donor.in_dist) means the answer follows the donor's whole state, including the donor's executor values. That supports items 1 and 2 (answers come from workspace values) and says nothing about Z holding the old prompt. The ctl27 numbers are shown (results/d0/B2_s200.json: chain-5 99.4 to 91.6, pooled-5 73.01 to 71.39): controls 2-7 carry information across iterations (ledger.py 315-316), but the lesion does not show what they hold.

Pass by no real change would come through leaks (items 3 and 4), not chance. With several hundred rows and a 30% bar against 10% chance, chance passing is negligible (suggested). Rules: no break found. Rule 5 is met (dev in_dist, not a protected panel), Rule 1 holds (diagnostic only), Rule 9 holds (card line only). The deploy-time 'carry-state' version would need a learned objective for what to keep across a cut, which is untested and not yet specified.
critiques.rescue: Cheapest decisive version (suggested, untested): read the answer-pointer head B2 actually uses (lans, ledger.py 343-345) instead of a digit probe. Steps: (1) Pairs: reuse donor_pairs (evalx.py 75-91) but keep only rows whose gold answer is a NUM prompt slot (index below 16, mode 0) and whose donor's gold answer slot index differs. (2) Cut: at iteration k, replace the whole prompt-derived input for the rest of the loop: X, xm, S0 (both terms), vals and valid for slots 0-15, and Kw only if the talker is scored. Run the kept-Rs variant and the zeroed-Rs variant, and say which one is out of distribution. (3) Score: the share of rows where the argmax answer slot equals the ORIGINAL gold answer slot (Z kept the role binding) versus the DONOR's gold slot (the question was re-read from X). Chance is 1 over the number of valid prompt slots, computed per row, with the majority-slot baseline reported. (4) Bars fixed before running: a round-0 donor sanity check (the answer pointer must hit the donor slot on at least 80% of pairs, else stop and report the target as unreadable); uncut answer-pointer accuracy at least 80% (bar set now, untested); the untrained model at most 15%; a three-way outcome table for the 6-seed claim. (5) Run seed 200 first as a screen, and go to six seeds only if the sanity and uncut bars pass. If the digit probe is kept, make it secondary and apply the same round-0 sanity gate, with the target restricted to the labels in item 7.";
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior, checked: donor_eval (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/evalx.py lines 93-125) swaps the whole state after the loop (shown; seed 200 in_dist exact 3.2, donor_match 58.2, RESULT.json lesions.donor). The run() lesions zero_state, shuffle_state, noexec, opswap, nocopy, nowordc and ctl27 act on the whole state or on controls, never mid-loop on the prompt (ledger.py 300-337; shown). probe_loops.py varies only the loop count and trains nothing (shown). zero_state gives 0.0 in_dist, and noexec gives 52.2 in_dist and chain-5 2.9 (shown, seed 200). The idea's claim that no mid-loop prompt cut exists holds. No probe of Z for prompt digits or pointers was found in the code tree.
critiques.expected_effect: As written, the most likely outcome is a readout artifact (suggested). For a working B2 the uncut digit probe may sit near chance, which can trip the proved-wrong clause, or the zeroed-Rs arm may leak step-1 results into Z. Neither outcome would show whether the state holds a prompt binding. Under the answer-pointer readout with the sanity bars above, a pass would show that Z keeps which slot the answer refers to after a mid-loop prompt swap, and a fail would show that the question's role is re-read at the end. Both outcomes are untested. A seed-200 screen would take CPU time only, once the mid-loop copy of run() is written and checked against intact outputs (suggested, under 1 h of compute).

chair.reasons:
Cut as a stand-alone item. It breaks no rule, since it is a read-only CPU measurement on the six saved B2 checkpoints. The problem is that no outcome changes what Ben builds, and the probe as written cannot give a clean answer.

1. No decision hangs on it (suggested). The idea's own deploy line, "if it passes, the carry-state idea is the deploy version", names no mechanism. Rule 10 sends Minecraft-style memory through a tool the model chooses to call: the T1 tape and a notebook. A pass would not change that design, and a fail would not either. B2 keeps exact step values outside Z, in the vals and Rs workspace (shown: ledger.py lines 333-339), and the NUM talker prints from vals, not from Z (shown: ledger.py lines 396-399). So a Z-only miss is predicted by the design and says little about memory.

2. The sibling result already points the same way (shown). The register-loop interchange at round 1 matched the counterfactual on 1.8% of rows against a mark of 40, and the team read it as "A's rounds recompute from the prompt instead of carrying values forward" (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/REPORT-custom-reader-talker.md line 82). The idea omits this prior. That model is not B2, so for B2 the result is suggested, not shown.

3. The probe has confounds that several critics each found. I checked them against ledger.py lines 286-345 (shown):
- The loop writes a step at every t=1..7. Steps 1-3 and their results are already in Rs and in Z's history before a round-4 cut. Zeroing Rs afterwards does not make it a Z-only test.
- vals, valid and the value-code half of S0 (vcode(value_code(vals))) are built once before the loop. If they are not swapped too, post-cut steps execute on the original numbers and leak them into the donor condition.
- kvx is computed once before the loop, so a cut has to rebuild it.
- The word keys Kw are never read inside the loop, so cutting them does nothing to Z.
- The digit label has holes: constant operands, commutative ops (ADD, MUL, MIN, MAX), duplicate values, and donor pairs that share the same last digit (donor_pairs matches on answers only). Also about 4,007 of 6,800 in_dist rows have no program (design/LOOPS-probe.md line 43; shown by a critic, not re-read here).
- A ridge probe fit on uncut states and scored on cut states is a distribution shift.
- B2's natural binding is a slot pointer, not a digit. A working pointer memory would trip the proved-wrong clause (donor digit read, original digit not).
- The marks leave the likeliest outcome, "original and donor both partly readable", with no verdict. The untrained control and the 10% chance level are untested.

4. Fixing all of this is a rewrite, not a revision. The probe needs a re-implemented run() that matches intact outputs, a round-0 null, a margin metric, filtered labels, an inconclusive band, an untrained control and a behavioural arm. The 0.5 h estimate does not include writing and checking that script (untested). The data rows are on the PC only, not in this snapshot.

5. The value of the Minecraft-area work lies elsewhere: expressibility of crafting, the T1 span-copy re-screen, a Crafter pip speed gate, and data variety for scaling. This diagnostic competes with none of those and unblocks none of them.

Cheap rescue if the lead wants to keep the kernel: fold a behavioural round-k prompt swap into the H1 / learned-stop loop probe, which already needs a run() copy and a loops sweep. It needs no separate item, no 6-of-6 pass mark and no deploy claim. See revised_idea.
chair.revised_idea:
Do not run as written. If the lead keeps any part, it is a small behavioural add-on to the planned H1 / learned-stop loop probe (CPU, B2 seeds 200-205), as a measurement only and with no deploy claim.

- Question, narrowed: after a swap of every prompt-derived input at iteration k, does B2's final answer follow the original question or the donor's? This asks whether B2 commits its plan early. It does not ask whether Z stores a digit.
- Cut set, all of it: X, xm and kvx; the S0 pooled term and the value-code term; vals[:, :16] and valid[:, :16]; Kw only if the talker is scored. Rs and vals[:, 16+:] keep their pre-cut results, and the Rs-zeroed arm is labelled "Z plus executed history" unless the pre-cut results are zeroed too.
- Define the index: the cut happens before iteration t=k of the loop at ledger.py line 307. Include k=0 as the null (the answer must follow the donor) and k=1, before step 1 is written.
- Readout: the answer pointer lans, restricted to rows whose gold answer is a prompt slot (mode NUM, slot below 16) and whose donor gold slot differs. Report the share that hits the original slot, the donor slot, or neither, with a majority-slot baseline. A digit ridge probe is secondary and only after the k=0 sanity check passes.
- First check: the no-cut copy of run() must reproduce intact outputs (seed 200 intact in_dist 90.59, chain-5 99.4 in results/d0/B2_s200.json).
- Seed 200 is a screen. Go to six seeds only if the k=0 null and the uncut accuracy pass. Fix a three-way outcome table with an inconclusive band before running.
- Drop the "carry-state is the deploy version" line. The autonomous memory path for a world is a tape or notebook the model writes to by calling a tool (T1 contract), which is a separate design question gated on the T1 span-copy re-screen.
chair.plan_guidance:
Not planned, so this is only for the case where the lead overrides the cut. A test plan must:
(1) Reproduce intact B2 outputs with the re-implemented run() before any cut.
(2) Swap the whole prompt side, not only the slot embeddings: X, xm, kvx, both parts of S0, vals[:, :16] and valid[:, :16]. Say which Rs / vals variants are used.
(3) Define "round k" as the state before iteration t=k, and include a k=0 null and a cut before step 1.
(4) Read the answer pointer (original slot vs donor slot, restricted to rows where the two differ) rather than only a last-digit ridge probe.
(5) Fix before running: a three-way outcome table with an inconclusive band, a majority-class baseline, and an untrained-model control reported as a number.
(6) Use only train and dev in_dist rows, never the blind or protected panels. Report n per seed after filtering.
(7) Screen seed 200 first and go to six seeds only if the k=0 null and the uncut accuracy pass.
(8) Label every claim shown, suggested or untested, and keep it a B2 card-line diagnostic with no deploy claim.
(9) Cite the register-loop round-1 interchange (1.8% against a mark of 40) as the closest prior, and D0-RESULT for the six-seed ctl27 numbers (pooled-5 -0.6 to -13.6, chain-5 -0.6 to -36.9).
(10) State the prediction beforehand: the answer follows the donor at early k, because B2 keeps exact values in vals and Rs, not in Z.

idea.title: Crafter by pip: spec check and steps-per-second gate
idea.summary: Install the base crafter package (no JAX, no WSL2) on the PC and the M1 Pro, check the spec the roadmaps quote (17 actions, 22 achievements, 9x7 local view, info keys, shape and id map of info['semantic']), and time the default image step against a text-only step. The timing sets the step budget for every later real-game test. No model is trained.
idea.change: New folder creative/crafttext/ with gate_spec.py: import crafter, read data.yaml, assert counts, print the shape and id map of info['semantic'], time 10,000 random steps per path on one core. The text view must be cut on the environment side to exactly the 9x7 local view the player sees plus the 16 inventory counts (no full-map leak). Params 0.
idea.why: Every later test costs environment steps: 10M steps is about 2.8 core-hours at 1,000 steps/s and about 13.9 at 200. The verify-craftax-run fact check shows the cheapest real game is pip-only Crafter; Craftax needs JAX (CPU-only on the Mac, no native Windows GPU wheel, WSL2 experimental, Blackwell unverified), so roadmap row 12a is not the first step.

problems: [shown: PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md section 0, rule 1; INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md line 3] Rule 1 is broken as written. The text view is applied automatically to every observation (the view is 'cut on the environment side', and the 16 inventory counts are always present). Rule 1 allows hand code between question and answer only inside a tool the model calls by writing text. The idea's rules_check says 'R1 the environment is a tool', but the model never calls it. The project already counts the reader's regex number slots and place code as breaches (INVENTORY A1-A7), so the same bar applies. Fix: make observation a model call (for example a `look` action returning the 9x7 text and a `inventory` action returning the 16 counts, with a fixed reply format), or get Ben's written ruling that per-step observations are the question stream.

[suggested: model cost per decision; shown: the idea's own arithmetic] The step budget is set by the wrong bottleneck. Every later test has the model decide at each step (the talker writes action text, and the thinker runs 8 loops over a prompt of up to 208 chars). The env step is likely a small part of the cost per decision, so 1,000 env steps/s per core does not set the budget. Fix: add an arm C that times the env step plus one forward pass of a random-init model at B2's 3.3M shape, on the same seeds, reporting decisions per second. Random weights are fine for timing (suggested). Set the budget from the slower arm. Example (computed): 10M decisions within 48 h needs about 58 per second.

[untested: upstream Crafter source is not in the snapshot and cannot be installed here] The 'text-only step' arm may be no faster than the image arm. My recollection (untested) is that Crafter's step() always renders the frame, so a text arm that keeps env.step() differs only by slicing. Skipping the render means forking upstream code, which R2 (upstream only) seems to forbid. Fix: time env.render() on its own, report the render share, and drop 'text-only' as an arm name unless a fork is allowed.

[suggested from upstream Crafter layout; untested here] The view spec is incomplete. The player's facing direction shows in the local view (the player sprite), and do/place depend on it, but the idea omits it. Night darkness changes what the player sees, so 'exactly the 9x7 view the player sees' is false at night unless darkness is encoded. The leak test is also incoherent. A full map can be cut around player_pos, so 'cannot be cut to the local view without leaking' is the wrong condition. The real risks are cells outside the window and extra fields (player_pos, reward, discount, achievements). Fix: proved wrong = any text cell that does not match the rendered frame at the same cell over 500 random states, or any field outside a fixed allow-list.

[untested: data.yaml not installed here; find and find_spec found no crafter package] The spec check has no proved-wrong branch. The counts (17 actions, 22 achievements, 16 items, 9x7 view) come from the idea's memory and a relayed fact check. If the installed package differs, the idea does not say what happens. Fix: record the installed values from data.yaml and let later tests use them, with a mismatch rule set before running. Rule 4 (one change at a time) also argues for separate marks for the spec check, the speed check and the view check.

[shown: whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md line 450; relayed fact check, untested here] The 'why' overstates the Craftax blocker. Line 450 says JAX on the PC 'likely needs WSL, untested'. The relayed fact check says CPU JAX runs on both machines and only GPU speed is untested. So Craftax is not blocked, and Crafter first is a speed and install choice. Also, the idea's order (Crafter text before Craftax-Classic) changes the written order in creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md line 244 (C10) and whole-model-roadmap row 12 (line 449). That needs a roadmap amendment, not a silent change.

[shown: grep of /mnt/project-files, papers/creative-model-papers.md D24 lines 147-150] Two figures used as evidence are not in the project files. '1,580 steps/s' appears in no file under /mnt/project-files. 'EMERALD 58.1 vs 50.5 at 27 FPS' is not in D24, which gives only 'surpass human experts within 10M steps'. Mark both untested here. problems: [shown] Autonomy walk-through. The gate itself (install, read the spec, time the env, pick the step budget) is developer work before ship, so rule 10 is fine for it. The text view, though, implies three deploy-time steps that need an outside driver: (a) the observation is cut and pushed on every step, with no model choice (hand code between world and model; under rule 1 it should be the reply to a model-written action or look call, as in T1's tool contract, tool.py:1-5); (b) an outer episode loop re-invokes the model per game step and carries history; (c) something decides when to continue and when to stop. A learned stop (H1/2d) is specified but unbuilt (brief), so the deployed text track has no autonomous path for (b) or (c) yet. The gate does not need one, but the idea should say who runs the loop.

[shown] The observation cannot fit the tool contract the idea says it reuses. T1 entries are cut at LE = 40 chars (tool.py:38, entry() at tool.py:57) and the tape holds N_RES = 7 entries (progparse.py:8; tool.py:2 'rounds 1..7'). A 9x7 grid is 63 cells, about 69 characters with newlines, before the 16 inventory counts. One observation cannot fit one entry, and the tape holds seven entries in total. The test has no pass mark for this; it needs a size check, or a named reply-cap and tape change.

[shown] Nothing carries across calls inside the model. Each forward pass starts from learned controller tokens and zero registers (ledger.py:298 Rs = zeros; ledger.py:304 Z from ctrl.weight plus place rows), and runs a fixed 8 rounds (tool.py:68 n_loops=8). History therefore has to be fed back by the harness on each game step, which is a harness step under rule 10 unless the model writes its own notes or memory tool. The idea does not mention this.

[untested] The pass and kill bands leave a gap. Pass is at least 1,000 steps/s per core and proved wrong below 200; the band from 200 to 1,000 has no verdict. Rule 4 needs every outcome to have one. The 1,000 mark itself is untested: the only speed figure in the brief is 1,580 steps/s aggregate, with no per-core number, so the bar may fail on one core.

[suggested, from memory of Crafter's env.py, not checked here] The 'text-only step' arm may not be cheaper. Crafter's step() renders the image each call, so the text path skips nothing unless the render is patched. Time env.step as shipped (with its render), and time the text cut as a separate cost, or show a render-free path before claiming the text arm is faster. problems: [shown, from fetched engine.py on GitHub main; not byte-checked] info['semantic'] is SemanticView(world), which starts from world._mat_map.copy() (full world area, default 64x64) and overwrites object cells with object ids. The idea's proved_wrong clause ('a full-world map that cannot be cut to the local view without leaking') is logically wrong: a full map can be cropped to the 9x7 window around info['player_pos']. The leak test that matters is whether the text output changes when cells outside the window change; the idea has no such test.

[shown, fetched engine.py and objects.py] Darkness leak: LocalView.__call__ always calls _light(canvas, world.daylight); at low daylight it adds noise and blends toward blue; when player.sleeping it calls _sleep (desaturate plus tint). The image hides the local map at night and while sleeping, but info['semantic'] does not. The pass condition 'text view built only from what the player sees' fails on night steps as written. Fix: apply the same daylight and sleep rule to the text tiles, or measure the share of low-daylight steps and disclose the text track as more informative.

[shown, fetched env.py] info keys are inventory, achievements, discount, semantic, player_pos, reward. The text view must exclude player_pos (absolute position), achievements, reward and discount; the gate should assert this key list. Player facing is not in info, but the image shows facing through the player sprite (suggested from texture naming, untested), so the text view loses a cue the image has.

[shown, EMERALD Table 2 caption via fetched arxiv HTML; a table value read by a summariser] EMERALD's 27 FPS is defined as total environment frames collected divided by training duration, so the paper's throughput is set by the whole learning loop, not by the game's Python step. The idea times only env plus text render on random actions and never times a policy in the loop. A looped thinker running 8 rounds per step is plausibly the binding cost on CPU (suggested; untested). The gate needs a policy-in-loop arm: a random-weight model of about the planned size, one forward per step, no training.

[shown arithmetic, checked] 10M steps at 200 steps/s is 13.9 core-hours and at 1,000 steps/s is 2.8 core-hours. The proved_wrong clause ('text track drops to 1M steps') treats core-hours as the budget. Wall time divides by parallel workers (6 to 10 cores on the M1 Pro), so at 200 steps/s on 8 cores 10M steps is about 1.7 h before policy cost. The kill rule should be in wall-clock hours at the measured worker count.

[shown, from the idea's own marks] Verdict gap: pass is at least 1,000 steps/s per core and proved_wrong is below 200. The 200 to 1,000 band has no verdict, and a plausible result sits there. Add a middle band with a named action (for example, run N workers and re-set the 10M budget) and fix thresholds before running.

[suggested] Timing protocol is thin. One 10,000-step random run is essentially one episode, and object-update cost depends on how many objects are near the player (from memory of env.py; untested). Use at least 3 seeds, a scripted policy as well as random, report the spread, and record machine load. The PC queue (q39, then q40 to q44 in queue_local) runs back to back and the M1 runs job 9 until about 4 PM ET, so 'PC CPU between queue jobs' has no idle window. The gate must check load before timing.

[untested] Like-for-like timing is not guaranteed. The fetched summary did not quote the body of step(). If step() calls render() on every call, as I recall the source does, a text-only path cannot skip the image cost without a wrapper, so 'image step vs text-only step' must say how the render is removed.

problems: [shown, from the idea's own change field] The gate times only environment steps on random actions. No model is in the loop, so the budget (2.8 and 13.9 core-hours for 10M steps) covers the environment alone. A deployed model needs one forward pass per environment step, and the design never times it. By rough arithmetic from the cited shapes (208-position reader, 8 loops, 2 blocks, width 256; ledger.py and reader.py under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/models/), one forward is on the order of 1-2 GFLOP. On one CPU core that is plausibly 10x or more slower than the environment step (suggested; untested).

[shown by file read] The observation length is not tested, and the text view as specified may not fit B2. B2's prompt cap is MAX_PROMPT = 208 with an assert (reader/custom_io/data.py lines 11 and 107). The specified view (63 grid cells, 6 line breaks, 16 named inventory counts) is about 237 characters by my count (suggested arithmetic; the 16 inventory names alone total 120 characters). The number regex reads the first N_NUM = 16 integers in the prompt as slots (models/progparse.py lines 8 and 14; ledger.py spans()), so the inventory digits compete with the question's own numbers. The 8A build already uses max_prompt 280 and n_num 91 (/mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/8a-results/8a-3M-s405-pool/caps.json), so which cap binds is not set.

[shown by reasoning] The proved-wrong clause for leakage cannot fire. Cropping a full semantic map to a 9x7 window is trivial, so 'cannot be cut to the local view without leaking' is never true. The test needed is a perturbation check: change cells outside the window and every other info field, then require the text string to be byte-identical. The idea names only info['semantic'] and does not say which other info keys the text view may read (achievements, reward and player position are likely present, as I recall the Crafter info dict; untested here).

[untested] The text view is not what the player sees. As I recall Crafter's source, the rendered local view is darkened with noise at night, while a semantic crop is not. The text view would then be richer than the image at night. The spec must either name it a privileged view and report it, or mask it the same way.
