chair.reasons:
Worth running, but only as a cheap prerequisite and only after revision. It is CPU only, 0 params, about 0.5 h, so it costs none of Ben's GPU time. It is pre-deploy, so rule 10 is not broken by the measurement itself. No hard rule is broken that cannot be fixed.

What it buys: it pins the Crafter spec (shown on main by one critic, untested here: crafter is not installed in this sandbox, `import crafter` fails) before any sealed mark uses it. It gives a measured per-core speed (no per-core figure exists anywhere; '1,580 steps/s' is in no file under /mnt/project-files, verified by grep). And it tests whether a text view can feed B2 at all.

The most decision-relevant output is the length gate, and the original idea does not have it. B2 asserts prompts of at most 208 chars (reader/custom_io/data.py line 11 and line 107, shown). T1 cuts tape entries at 40 chars (tool.py LE=40 line 38, entry() line 57) and has 7 rounds (progparse.py line 8 N_RES=7), shown. A 9x7 grid is 63 cells plus line breaks plus 16 inventory counts, about 237 chars by a critic's count (suggested, arithmetic, not run). So the specified view probably does not fit B2's current cap or T1's reply cap. That fact blocks every T1-gated world idea.

The original has real faults that the critics found and I confirm:
1. The leak clause is logically wrong. A full 64x64 semantic map can always be cropped to 9x7 (suggested, from upstream source read by a critic, untested here). The real test is a perturbation test: change cells outside the window and every non-allow-listed info field, and require byte-identical text.
2. Night and sleep are not applied to the semantic crop, so the text view is richer than the image at night (suggested, from upstream source, untested here).
3. The timing is environment-only. A decision needs a forward pass too, so budget from the slower arm.
4. The 'text-only step' arm may time the same code, because step() probably renders every call (suggested, untested). Do not claim a cheaper text environment unless a render-free path is shown.
5. The verdict bands have a hole between 200 and 1,000 steps/s, and the kill rule is in core-hours rather than wall-clock hours at the measured worker count.
6. Rule 1 and rule 10: a per-step push of the observation is hand code between world and model that the model never calls. Make the observation the reply to a model-written look/inventory call, or get Ben's written ruling.
7. Label hygiene: Crafter and JAX spec facts and the EMERALD numbers (58.1 vs 50.5, 27 FPS, 103 h) are external or untested here. creative-model-papers.md D24 gives no numbers (the critics say so; I did not re-read it). '1,580 steps/s' is in no project file. The roadmap '65% human' and 'Crafter is solved' (creative-roadmap line 160, row 12 line 449, C10 line 244, shown) mix metrics; the anchor is Crafter score with human 50.5.
8. Arithmetic: 10M steps at 200/s is 13.9 core-hours, not 'over 14'.
9. The gate is not on the critical path. It moves none of the open questions (scaling, new kinds, breadth, creativity), and a pass only makes a later Crafter text track affordable. The order change (Crafter text before Craftax-Classic) needs a roadmap amendment and Ben's sign-off before any game claim. Rank it below ideas that move scaling or new kinds, and run it only on an idle machine: the Mac is busy until job 9 ends, about 4 PM ET, and the PC queue q39 to q44 runs back to back.
chair.revised_idea:
Crafter by pip: spec record, view-leak check, length gate and speed gate. CPU only, 0 params, no training, about 0.5 h per machine, on an idle machine with the load average logged. Not progress on the north star. Output is a recorded spec plus a step budget plus a go or no-go on the text view format, nothing else. Put the code in its own top-level folder (for example crafter_gate/), not creative/, so rule 9 keeps this line apart from the C1/C2 card experiments and the village.

Four separate marks (rule 4), each fixed before running:

S, spec record. pip install crafter on the PC and the M1 Pro. Pin and log the installed version and a hash of data.yaml. Read, do not assume: number of actions, achievements, inventory items, recipe costs and the 'nearby' rule, local view size, image size, episode cap. Expected, from main-branch source read by a critic (suggested, untested here): 17 actions, 22 achievements, 16 inventory items, 9x7 world window. Mismatch rule: any difference is recorded and every later mark uses the installed values. This is a record, not a pass or fail.

V, view check (leakage). Build the text view only from a crop of info['semantic'] around the player, following the image view's own centring and out-of-bounds rule, plus the inventory counts. The allow-list is exactly {window tiles, inventory counts}; player_pos, achievements, reward and discount stay out. The facing direction is visible in the image through the player sprite, so state how the text carries it (or that it does not). Test on 1,000 random-policy states: mutate every cell outside the window and every non-allow-listed field, and require byte-identical text. Pass: 0 differences. Proved wrong: any difference. Separately report the share of steps at low daylight or sleeping, when the image is dimmed but the semantic crop is not; any later claim must label the text track as more informative than pixels at night, or mask the same way.

L, length gate. On 1,000 random-policy states, render the chosen encoding and report the length distribution (p50, p99, max) against B2's 208-char prompt cap (data.py 11, 107), the 8A caps (max_prompt 280, per a critic's read of 8a-results/8a-3M-s405-pool/caps.json, to be re-read), and T1's 40-char entry and 7-entry tape (tool.py 38, progparse.py 8). Pass: p99 at most 280 with all 16 counts kept. Proved wrong for the format: no encoding that keeps all counts fits 280, so move the counts out of the prompt into a separate inventory call, or raise the cap, before any run. State that the T1 contract cannot carry this as built (reply cap, round budget and per-row state all need changes), so the gate must not be read as T1 support.

T, speed gate. Three seeds, full episodes with resets (death or the cap), at least 10,000 steps per seed, one pinned core, median of 3 repeats with the spread. Arm A: env.step as shipped (it probably renders the image every step; if so, say so and do not claim a cheaper text environment unless a render-free path is shown). Arm B: the text formatter alone. Arm C: env step plus formatter plus one forward pass of a raw B2 checkpoint (code/b2ckpt/B2_s200/checkpoint.pt) on one CPU thread, on a real text observation padded or cut to 208 (a lower bound on cost, say so), at batch 1 and at batch 32. A GPU forward is out of scope here. Report steps per second per core and the machine's core count. Bands, fixed before running: A+B at least 1,000/s per core means the environment is not the bottleneck; 200 to 1,000 means run N worker processes and set the budget in wall-clock hours at the measured worker count, with no pass claim; below 200 per core means re-plan the budget (text track to 1M steps, or use Craftax-Classic row 12a). For arm C: at least 100 decisions/s per core fits a 10M-step plan, 20 to 100 fits 1M, below 20 means act every k steps or wait. Budget from the slower arm.

Observation as a tool reply (rule 1 and rule 10). Specify that at deploy the model writes an action or look/inventory call as text and the environment tool returns the fixed-format reply. Ask Ben for a written ruling if he prefers per-step push as the question stream. The outer episode loop (calling the model once per game step, carrying notes) is a harness step; the gate does not solve it and a later design must say how history lives in the model's own notes or a memory tool.

Labels and metric. Crafter facts (version, counts, recipe costs) and JAX platform facts are suggested until S runs. '1,580 steps/s' and the EMERALD figures (58.1 vs 50.5, 27 FPS, about 103 h) are untested here; D24 in papers/creative-model-papers.md gives no numbers. Use the Crafter score (geometric mean of 22 success rates, human expert 50.5) as the metric anchor, not reward points or the roadmap's 65%. Do not repeat 'Crafter is solved'. Corrected arithmetic: 10M steps is 2.8 core-hours at 1,000/s and 13.9 at 200/s.

Roadmap record. The order change (Crafter text before Craftax-Classic, rows 12/12a and C10) needs a written amendment and Ben's sign-off before any game claim. Any later model test on Crafter needs its own sealed mark (6 or more seeds, same-size plain arm).
chair.plan_guidance:
Write one test plan with four independent marks (S spec record, V view leak, L length, T speed) and a decision table, each fixed before running, as in revised_idea.

Compute and fit: CPU only, one core per timing arm, 0 params, about 30 min per machine. Run only on an idle machine and log the load average with every number. The Mac is busy until job 9 ends, about 4 PM ET. The PC queue q39 to q44 and the 8A jobs run back to back, so ask Ben for a gap. Do not time under load.

Do not claim a faster text-only environment unless a render-free path is shown. First check whether Env.step renders every call (not verified here: crafter is not installed in this sandbox). If it does, time env.step as shipped, the formatter alone, and env.render() alone, and report the render share.

View check, V. The correct leak test is mutation, not cropping. Mutate cells outside the 9x7 window and every non-allow-listed info field, and require byte-identical text over 1,000 states. Fail on any difference. Note the facing direction and the night or sleep dimming (suggested from upstream source, untested here) and label any resulting text-vs-pixel difference in every later claim.

Length gate, L. This is the most valuable output. State up front that p99 length is compared with 208 (data.py, shown), 280 (8A caps.json, to be re-read) and T1's 40-char entries (tool.py, shown). Say plainly that T1 as built cannot carry a world reply, so the gate neither supports nor refutes T1 and does not unblock the T1-gated world ideas by itself. Offer a compact encoding variant (inventory as a separate call, or nonzero items only) as a second encoding, not a silent change.

Speed gate, T. Include the model-in-loop arm C with a raw B2 checkpoint (b2ckpt/B2_s200, sha-checked), batch 1 and batch 32, and a lower-bound caveat for prompts longer than 208. Do not use the original single pass bar of 1,000/s as a verdict; use the three bands with named actions. Express budgets in wall-clock hours at the measured worker count.

Autonomy and rules. Say that the gate is pre-deploy and adds no deployed method. Specify observation-as-tool-reply (look/inventory), or request Ben's ruling. Say who runs the episode loop. This line stays separate from B2 card claims and the village (rule 9).

Labels. Mark every external Crafter, JAX and EMERALD fact as suggested or untested until the gate or a read of the paper settles it.

Honest ranking note for the lead. This tests no model and moves none of the open questions (scaling, new kinds, breadth, creativity). Rank it as a cheap prerequisite and run it after the higher-value tests; it can fit idle gaps. The one result that could change other plans is L, which says whether B2's 208-char cap and T1's 40-char reply can carry any world observation.

plan.title: Crafter text gate: spec, view leak, length and speed
plan.ben_line: Before we ask the model to play a small survival game, we run cheap checks on your two computers: can the game screen be written as text that fits the model's reading limit, does that text reveal anything a player could not see, and how fast do the game and the model run? This trains nothing and does not show the model can play.
plan.question: With pip-only Crafter (no JAX, no WSL) on BensPC and the M1 Pro: what does the installed Crafter spec say (S); can a text view of the 9x7 local window plus the 16 inventory counts be built with zero leakage (V); does that text fit the prompt caps, B2 at 208, the 8A build at 280, and a T1 entry at 40 (L); and how many environment steps and B2 decisions per second per core can each machine run (T)?
plan.one_change: Add one pre-deploy measurement folder, crafter_gate/ at the repo top level, that records the installed Crafter spec and measures view leakage, observation length and CPU speed. No model is trained or changed, no score is claimed, and no existing model code is edited.
arms: S spec record (record only, no pass or fail): installed crafter version, sha256 of data.yaml, actions, achievements, inventory items with max value, recipe costs and the nearby rule, view and image size, episode cap, info keys, and whether env.step() renders the image on every call (read from the installed env.py, not assumed).

V view leak: the text view (9x7 window of info['semantic'] centred on the player, one printable-ASCII character per tile, a void character for out-of-bounds, plus the inventory counts) compared with copies where every cell outside the window and every non-allow-listed field is mutated; 1,000 random-policy states.

L length: E0 grid only (69 characters with newlines, computed); E1 grid plus 16 counts as fixed-order digits (86, computed); E2 grid plus named counts (about 237, computed from the 16 item names, suggested); E3 nonzero-only counts (variable length, offered as the second encoding, not a silent change); 1,000 random-policy states; report p50, p99 and max.
T-A env.step as shipped (image render included), 10,000 steps per seed, random policy with episode resets.
T-R env.render() alone on the same states (gives the render share of T-A).
T-B text formatter alone on the same states, no env step.

T-C env.step + formatter + one B2 decision (Ledger.generate, ledger.py line 409) on the raw B2_s200 checkpoint, loaded with load_model (models/__init__.py lines 28-33), batch 1 and batch 32, one torch thread, prompt padded or cut to 208 (timing only, not scored), 2,000 decisions per seed.

T-C8 (optional, only if the 8A build is on the machine): a random-init model at the 8A shape (280 characters, 12 rounds, 36 registers), the same decision loop, timing only. If the build is absent, the output says so.
plan.seeds: Env seeds 200, 201 and 202 for T-A, T-R, T-B and T-C, with 3 repeats each. 1,000 random-policy states over env seeds 200 to 203 (250 each) for V and L. Checkpoint B2_s200 for T-C; its speed barely depends on the weights, so one checkpoint is enough. No dataset rows are read, so rule 5 is not engaged. The six-seed version (200 to 205) is the confirm.
plan.machine: Two machines, one at a time. BensPC (Windows, RTX 5070 Ti): CPU timing only, record the CPU model and core count, pin one core with psutil affinity if that is installed. M1 Pro Mac: record the core count; macOS has no CPU affinity API, so use one torch thread and a logged load average instead. Run only on an idle machine: record load average and running jobs before each repeat, and drop repeats that ran under load. The Mac's job 9 must have ended (board ETA about 4 PM ET on 10-07, not confirmed in the snapshot). The sandbox here has 4 cores and no crafter or torch installed, so nothing is timed here.
pass_marks: S: record only, no pass or fail. Suggested expected values from upstream Crafter (untested here until step 5): 17 actions, 22 achievements, 16 inventory items, 9x7 local view, 64x64 image, 10,000-step episode cap. Mismatch rule: any installed value that differs is recorded, and every later mark uses the installed value.

V: PASS if all 1,000 states give byte-identical text before and after mutation, AND the centre cell of the text window is the player object on all 1,000 states. FAIL on any difference. Report separately the share of steps at low daylight or asleep (no mark). Any later claim must say that the text sees hidden map cells at night when the pixel view is dimmed, unless the text is dimmed the same way.

L: PASS for an encoding that keeps all 16 counts if its p99 length is at most 280 (8A caps.json, max_prompt 280, shown). Report every encoding against 208 (B2 cap, data.py line 11, shown) and 40 (T1 entry, tool.py line 38, shown). This mark has no 40-character question reserve, following the chair's direction. If Ben wants room for a question inside the 280, the mark becomes 240; E2 (about 237) would then pass only just, and with a 40-character reserve it needs 277 of 280.

T bands, arms A and B, per core, median of 3 repeats: at least 1,000 steps/s means the environment is not the bottleneck. 200 to 1,000 means run N worker processes and set the budget in wall-clock hours at the measured worker count, with no pass claim. Below 200 means re-plan the text track to 1M steps or use Craftax-Classic symbolic (roadmap row 12a).

T bands, arm C (B2 decisions/s per core, median of 3, batch 1 and batch 32, the slower counts): at least 100 fits a 10M-step plan; 20 to 100 fits a 1M-step plan; below 20 means act every k game steps or wait. Budget in wall-clock hours = game steps x k / (rate per core x workers x 3600). k (calls per game step) is set by the design and is not measured here. Computed reference: 10M env steps at 1,000/s is 2.8 core-hours and at 200/s is 13.9 core-hours; 10M decisions at 100/s is 27.8 core-hours and at 20/s is 138.9 core-hours.
plan.proved_wrong: V: any byte difference between the original and mutated text, meaning the text reads something outside the window or the allow-list (a leak, or a coding error). L: no encoding that keeps all 16 counts has p99 at most 280; then the counts move to a separate inventory call, or the cap changes, before any run. T: arms A and B below 200 steps/s per core on both machines (the environment track is re-planned), or arm C below 20 decisions/s per core at both batch sizes with no k-step plan. A CPU miss re-plans the CPU budget only; the deployed budget needs a GPU timing, which is a separate gate. S: nothing can fail; it is a record.
plan.null_risk: High for S and L. A fixed-width grid has one length, so L is arithmetic on the installed names and counts, not a sample: it passes or fails on paper. The 1,000 states check only count width (counts above 9, suggested max 9) and E3. V is the only mark that can fail on real content, and it fails only on a coding leak, so a pass says the code is right, not that the model can use the text. T can move between bands with load noise; repeats and load logs guard against that. Suggested expectation, untested: B2 at 208 characters with 8 rounds runs near 10 to 60 decisions/s per core, so the 100 mark is probably missed and the 20 mark is borderline. The likely result is an act-every-k plan or a GPU timing, not a clean pass. All marks could pass with no change to the model. A pass is infrastructure, not progress on the north star, and the gate moves none of the open questions (scaling, new kinds, breadth, creativity).
plan.autonomy: Pre-deploy measurement only: it adds no deployed method and the model learns nothing here. At deploy the model does each step itself by writing text calls (look, inventory, legend, act), and the environment returns a fixed-format reply, the same tool contract as T1 (tool.py header). The grid and counts are the reply to a call the model chose to make, so they are tool output, not hand code between question and answer (rule 1), provided the model writes the call. Not solved here: (a) the outer episode loop that calls the model once per game step and carries history is a harness step; a later design must keep history in the model's own notes or a memory tool. (b) The learned stop (H1 / 2d) is unbuilt. (c) T1 as built (40-character entries, 7-entry tape, stateless calc) cannot carry a 69 to 237 character reply, so a reply-cap change is a separate design change. Ben's ruling is needed on the observation contract: a call reply (recommended, rule 10) or a per-step push (then the push is a harness step).
steps: Before any run, Ben gives two rulings in writing. (a) The observation is the reply to a model-written look or inventory call (recommended), or a per-step push. (b) The game track moves from Craftax-Classic symbolic (whole-model roadmap row 12a, line 450; C10 in the creative roadmap, line 244) to Crafter text first. That needs a roadmap amendment and sign-off before any game claim; row 12 is at line 449.

Save the marks above, with the expected values and the mismatch rule, in crafter_gate/MARKS.md before the first run (rule 4). Mark external Crafter facts as suggested, and mark the EMERALD figures (58.1 vs 50.5, 27 FPS, about 103 h) untested and unused. D24 in papers/creative-model-papers.md (about lines 147-150) gives no numbers (shown). The figure 1,580 steps/s appears in no .md under /mnt/project-files (grep, shown), so it is not used. The creative roadmap's 'Crafter is solved' (line 160) overstates D24 and is not repeated. The metric anchor is the Crafter score with human expert 50.5, from design/02-options.md line 46 (shown; citing Hafner 2021, suggested), not the 65% stretch in roadmap row 12.

Idle check on each machine. Record load average, CPU model, core count and running jobs. Confirm the Mac's job 9 has ended. Pause or log the PC queue: queue_local jobs 39 to 44 (shown) and the 8A jobs run back to back, so ask Ben for a gap. Time nothing under load.

On each machine, Ben runs pip install crafter at a pinned version (no JAX, no WSL). Log the version, the Python version, and the sha256 of data.yaml, env.py, engine.py and objects.py. Dependencies are whatever the installed setup lists (suggested: numpy and imageio).

S: read data.yaml and env.py from the installed package and write the results into crafter_gate/RESULTS.md. Record actions, achievements, inventory items with max value, recipe costs and the nearby rule, view and image size, episode cap, info keys, and whether step() renders every call. Do not assume any of these.

Build the text view in crafter_gate/view.py. Centre = player_pos; window = the installed local view size. Each tile is one printable-ASCII character (codes 32 to 126) from a fixed legend: B2's vocabulary gives each printable ASCII character its own id, and any other character becomes UNK (shown: data.py ASCII set and CharVocab.build). Out-of-bounds is a void character. Counts are E1 (fixed-order digits) or E2 (named). Facing is included only if the image shows it and it is read from the player object (suggested: facing is not in the info dict). If facing is included, check once that the four facings give four different player sprites (untested).

V: mutation test on 1,000 states (env seeds 200 to 203). idea.title: Fewshot-gap diagnosis panel: example count, order flips, multiplier readout
idea.summary: B2 trails the step-writing transformer on fewshot_number_rule by 14.9 points pooled over six seeds (behind on 6 of 6). Three eval-only checks say why: a learning curve over 2, 3 and 4 shown examples, an answer-flip test when the examples are permuted, and a ridge readout of the hidden multiplier from controller state at each loop.
idea.change: CPU probe, no model change, on raw B2 seeds 200-205 (code/b2ckpt) and plain_tf_steps (tfsteps s100/101, C0 s200/201). Hand-written rows in the dev format ('12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?', integer multiplier 2-9): 100 items per k; 3 random permutations of the shown pairs (query last); a few thousand generated rows for ridge fits (256 inputs) of A from control-token-1 state at loops 1-8 via run(rounds=True), top 20% of A values held out, with the reader digit-position fit as control.
idea.why: Fewshot has no written program (prog 0%), so the answer is generated from the registers; copy share is only 3.7-8.2% across seeds. The executor-off equality (34.6% either way) is trivial because the family has no program rows, so it says nothing about the calculator. A flat k curve would mean the answer route, not evidence, is the limit; high flips would point to the per-absolute-index slot vectors; a readable multiplier would mean only a writing or arithmetic step is missing.

chair.reasons:
Worth a plan, after revision. It is a CPU-only, eval-only probe on the six saved B2 q33 checkpoints (seeds 200-205, sha256 checked). It changes no model, so rules 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10 are safe. It targets a gap that is shown on 6 of 6 seeds: fewshot_number_rule pooled 22.71 vs plain_tf_steps 37.60, -14.90, per-seed -10.0 to -19.4 (33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json, verified by two critics and the fact check). It bears on the north star, because inducing a rule from a few shown examples is the skill a game world needs. Its cost to Ben is low: one script, about 1 CPU hour (suggested; torch is not installed here, so untested). It does not need the sealed 8a ladder.

It is not a 'check', because the disputed facts are mostly settled in the files. I confirmed: (1) the real family uses 2 or 3 shown pairs, written with spaces around '->', in framed prompts ('Examples:', 'Quick one:', 'Be brief.'), with pair_sum rows as tuples (/mnt/project-files/model-audit/probe_prefix_cpu.py lines 41-44; research/data.md line 36 shows the 2-pair form; rules_real.py docstring shows 3 pairs). No 4-pair row appears anywhere, so k=4 is out of distribution (suggested; the train shot mix lives only in the generator on Ben's PC, which is not in this snapshot). (2) ledger.py:340 keeps round snapshots only for t <= n-2, so t=1..6 at 8 loops. Each snapshot holds control-token-1 and the 9 registers, and out['R'] holds the final registers. Loop 8 control-token-1 is not returned. The idea's 'loops 1-8 via run(rounds=True)' is wrong as written. But the registers are what feed the GEN digit writer, so reading them needs no code change. (3) The training skills variants are add (y=x+B), mult (y=A*x) and pair_sum (rules_real.py docstring), so the hidden 'multiplier' exists only on mult rows.

Critic defects I accept (all four critics agree on most): the k=4 cell is a format shift and not evidence; only 100 items per k gives a standard error of about 6-7 points on a k-difference, so the +15 and +5 marks leave a wide undecided band; the ridge reads the wrong state and mixes three rule types; the 256-wide control-token-1 fit does not match the registers (9x256) that the digit writer reads; the slot inputs carry a hand-built 93-feature digit code, so a readable A could come from that; the plain side has no 6-seed cap-64 checkpoints (tfsteps s100/101 have none; C0 s200/201 is cap 107, so the caps are mismatched), so a plain-side mark is a screen at best; the flip test needs a defined denominator and a null; marks must be sealed in a file before the run; rule 5 needs a hash check of the fresh rows against the protected-panel list (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md). I discount the critics' loop-indexing complaint only partly. It is right that loop 8 is missing. It is wrong that the probe is blocked, because loops=K sweeps and the rounds=True registers cover t=1..6 and the final state. I also advise against using the 8A 3M partial fewshot numbers as a comparator. That would be a peek at a sealed ladder, and that B2 is a different arm (n_loops 12, a different pool).

Honest value: moderate, not high. It diagnoses the 3.3M q33 B2 as it is today. If T1 (outside calculator), the learned stop or the 8A shape replaces that design, the verdict does not carry over without a rerun. The most likely result (suggested, about 50-60% for a clean reading once fixed, from the mechanism critic) is a partial reading that picks between two already-specced next steps. It does not by itself move any score. Minor housekeeping: the rules critic left a stray scratch file at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/readfew.py, which has no effect on the repo.
chair.revised_idea:
Fewshot-gap diagnosis, B2 only, three measurements on in-distribution rows, run on Ben's PC (where the skills generator and the C:\Users\benja\custom-io\work\data folder live). No model change, no training, no GPU. Scope of the verdict: B2 3,302,481 params, q33 seeds 200-205 (33-pc-confirm-b2), 8 loops. It does NOT cover the 8A B2 (n_loops 12, different pool), T1, or B3.

Step 0 (before any run; written to a sealed marks file, as in the PASS-MARKS pattern). Read the skills fewshot_number_rule generator on the PC for: the train mix of 2-shot vs 3-shot rows, the variant mix (add, mult, pair_sum), the A and B ranges, and the frame wordings. Draw fresh rows from the generator's own seed space. Drop any prompt whose hash is in the train set or in the protected-panel hash list (GOLD-PRIVATE, blind, reserved; PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md). Keep prompt numbers off the constant slots 1, 2, 10 and 100. Check that each row has exactly one consistent answer across add, mult and pair_sum. Hand-write only the scorer. Use the generator's exact prompt string (spacing, frames). Report k=4 only as a labelled out-of-distribution point, or drop it if training has no 4-pair rows.

M1, evidence use. For each seed, 300 fresh rows per cell, with a different item seed for each model seed (so 1,800 items per cell). Cells: variant (add, mult, pair_sum) x k in the shot counts that occur in training. Rows are paired: the same rule and query with one more shot added. Report the paired k-up minus k-down difference with a bootstrap CI over items. Also report an error taxonomy of wrong answers: (a) equals the answer under another variant; (b) right rule, wrong digits or small arithmetic slip; (c) copies a shown y, a shown x or the query; (d) other.

M2, order flips. For every row, all orderings of the shown pairs (2 for k=2, up to 6 for k=3), query last, since the rule and answer are unchanged. Denominator: rows B2 gets right in the original order. Statistic: right-to-wrong rate, bootstrap CI. Null: the same statistic under a content-neutral change that is already in training (swap the frame wording), so a position shortcut can be told from general fragility.

M3, readout. At least 8,000 mult rows per seed (B on add rows as a second target). Features are the 9 registers (9x256 = 2,304 dims, the input of the GEN digit writer) at t=1..6 from run(rounds=True) and at the final loop from out['R']. A random 80/20 split gives R^2; alpha is chosen by CV on the train part only; a one-hidden-layer MLP readout is added so 'not linear' is not read as 'absent'. The extrapolation error on the top 20% of A is reported separately as MAE, not R^2. Controls: shuffled labels; an input-only floor (the pooled reader and number-slot features before any loop, which includes the hand-built 93-feature digit code); an untrained-init B2 with the same readout; and a readout from the registers to the answer digits (the talker side). The reader digit-position fit (D0) is not a sufficient control, because it covers the reader output only. Optional, labelled as a code change: return the final control-token-1 vector.

Comparator. None in the pass marks. If Ben wants a contrast, run plain C0 seeds 200/201 (cap 107, 3,271,424 params; /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/43-c0-s200 and 43-c0-s201) on the same rows, paired with B2 s200/201, labelled as a 2-seed screen. Do not read the sealed 8A per-family numbers.

Pass marks, fixed first. Each outcome names the ONE next change (rule 4); no two changes together.
- Outcome E (the evidence is used and the gap is in the answer route): pooled paired k-up minus k-down on mult rows at least +10 with CI lower bound above 0; flip rate at most 5% (CI upper at most 10%) and not above the neutral-change null by more than 3 points; A random-split R^2 at least 0.60 at t=6 or final on at least 5 of 6 seeds and at least 0.30 above the input-only floor; and at least half of the errors are type (b). Next single change: worked-program teaching rows for fewshot (hand-written trace: DIV on one shown pair, then MUL by the query; the model chooses the pair and checks it against the other shown pairs through its own written steps). 6 seeds, F1 mark kept.
- Outcome R (the rule is not extracted): R^2 at most 0.20 for ridge AND MLP at every t on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and most errors are type (a) or (d). Next single change: the W2 scratch-token test (marks already written, redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 5b).
- Outcome P (a position shortcut): flip rate at least 15% and at least 10 points above the neutral-change null. Next single change: random-order fewshot training rows (a data change), 6 seeds.
- Anything else, including a flat k curve with a readable A, is reported as undecided and Ben acts on none of it. Proved wrong for the idea's own hypothesis ('more evidence helps'): paired k-up minus k-down CI upper bound below +3 on unique-answer mult rows.

Rules and autonomy. R1 holds (hand-written rows and scorer are tests). R2 holds (no teacher). R5 holds (hash check, fresh rows). R9 holds (B2 card line only; the creative notebook M gain of +8 to +12 on fewshot is a separate claim and stays out). R10: measurement only at build time; the generator labels A and B are never a deploy-time step. Any fix this points to must have the model pick the pair, write the program, and check it against the shown pairs by itself (the same self-check shape as C2's example checker, kept separate under rule 9). That path still reads the numbers through the regex slots (INVENTORY A1), which is a separate open item. Cost: about 1 CPU hour (untested).
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.
1. Source of rows (shown gap): the skills fewshot generator and dev splits are not in this snapshot. They live on Ben's PC (path in RESULT.json config). Rows must be drawn from the generator's own seed space. Each prompt must be hash-checked against the train set and the protected-panel list (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md) before scoring. Copy the exact prompt string (spacing around '->', frame words, pair_sum tuples). Read the real 2-shot vs 3-shot train mix first. In the files, only 2- and 3-pair rows exist (suggested for 'no 4-pair rows'), so k=4 is a labelled out-of-distribution point or dropped.
2. Variants (shown): the family trains on add, mult and pair_sum. A hidden multiplier exists only on mult. Stratify every cell by variant, read A only on mult rows and B only on add rows, and say the variant mix.
3. Which state to read (shown, ledger.py:340): rounds=True gives t=1..6 snapshots of control-token-1 and the 9 registers. The final registers are out['R']. Loop 8 control-token-1 is not returned (optional one-line code change, to be labelled). The GEN digit writer reads the 9 registers, so use the registers (2,304 dims, at least 8,000 rows per seed). loops=K sweeps are lesions, not snapshots; label them.
4. Controls for M3 (shown/suggested): shuffled labels; an input-only floor that includes the hand-built 93-feature digit code; an untrained-init model; a readout to the answer digits; an MLP as well as ridge; random-split R^2, with extrapolation reported as MAE only.
5. Noise: 100 items per k is too few (standard error about 6-7 points on a k-difference, suggested). Use 300 fresh rows per cell per seed, a different item seed for each model seed, paired items, bootstrap CI over items, and per-seed values shown. Single dev cells (40 rows) are noise: B2 seed 200 scored 15/40 in q33 and 12/40 in the first-look rerun.
6. Flip test: define the denominator (rows right in the original order), use all orderings, and include a neutral-change null. Without a null the 5% and 15% marks mean little.
7. Comparator: B2-only for the marks. No cap-64 plain_tf_steps checkpoints exist for any 6-seed set. C0 s200/201 (cap 107) is a 2-seed screen, only paired with B2 s200/201. Do not peek at the sealed 8A per-family numbers.
8. Scope and labels: say which B2 each verdict covers (q33 3.3M, 8 loops). Label every claim shown / suggested / untested. Pre-register the single next change for each outcome (E, R, P) and an 'undecided, act on nothing' band, then seal the marks before running.
9. Priority: low-to-medium. It is cheap and rule-safe, but it diagnoses a design that T1, the learned stop or the 8A shape may replace. Rank it below anything that moves scaling or new-kind scores, and above anything that needs GPU or new code. Ask the lead to bundle it with the Crafter pip gate and the shape-vs-digit variety test as one CPU afternoon, not as a separate project.

plan.title: Fewshot-gap diagnosis: B2 on 6 seeds, CPU, eval only
plan.ben_line: B2 loses to a simpler model on questions where it has to work out a rule from a few examples. This test asks the model we already have, with no training and no changes, three questions: does it use more examples, does its answer change when the examples are shuffled, and can we read the rule from inside it. The next step is chosen before the test runs, so whatever it finds, we know what to do next.
plan.question: On the six saved B2 checkpoints (q33 seeds 200-205), why does fewshot_number_rule trail plain_tf_steps (pooled over four splits: 22.71 vs 37.60, shown; recomputed from RESULT.json counts 218/960 and 361/960)? Does B2 fail to use extra examples (outcome E), never extract the rule (outcome R), or lean on example position (outcome P)?
plan.one_change: No model change and no training. The one addition is an eval-only fewshot panel: fresh rows at the trained shot counts, a paired one-shot-more comparison, shown-pair order flips against a frame-swap null, and ridge/MLP readouts of the multiplier from the 9 register tokens. Scope: B2 at 3,302,481 params, q33 seeds 200-205, 8 loops, in-distribution rows only. It says nothing about the 8A B2 (12 loops, different pool), T1, B3, or unseen rule kinds. Each outcome names one next single change, which is not run here.
arms: B2 (ledger.py, copy=True): 3,302,481 params. Raw checkpoints at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 through B2_s205/checkpoint.pt, 13,243,510 bytes each. sha256 matches the sidecar for all six (checked here; shown).

Input-only floor: the workspace S0 before any loop (ledger.py lines 295-297; 27 slots x 256 = 6,912 dims flattened, per the ledger.py docstring as reported in the brief). It holds the hand-built digit code and the pooled reader span, so it is the fair input yardstick. Same readouts as the registers (shown code; the flattening is a suggested choice).
Untrained-init B2, same architecture, fixed seed, same readouts (suggested control, built on CPU).
Shuffled-label null for every readout. Frame-swap null for the flip test, using training frame wordings from the generator (suggested).

Plain comparator: none in the pass marks. The plain step-writer (tfsteps_s200 through tfsteps_s205, 3,260,928 params, -1.3% vs B2, inside the +-3% band; shown) has six-seed RESULT.json scores but no checkpoint, so it cannot be scored on fresh items. Optional screen only: C0 cap-107 (3,271,424 params, per brief) at seeds 200-201; checkpoints/cio-1007/43-c0-s200 (13,103,797 bytes, shown) and 43-c0-s201 exist. It is labelled a 2-seed screen and never pooled with the 6-seed claim.
plan.seeds: Six paired B2 model seeds, 200-205, as in the 33-pc-confirm run. Each model seed scores its own fresh item panel (item seed recorded per model seed), so pooled claims rest on six item sets; per-seed values are reported too. The optional C0 screen covers seeds 200-201 only and is not pooled with the 6-seed claim.
plan.machine: Ben's Windows RTX 5070 Ti PC, CPU mode for the probe (no GPU). The skills generator and data (C:\\Users\\benja\\custom-io\\work\\data, from the RESULT.json config) exist only there, so the probe runs there. The Mac is not needed.
pass_marks: Sealed first: the marks, the answer-free rule (step 3b) and the decision table go in a dated addendum to reader/custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md before any item is scored. Record the file's sha256 in the results folder.

Outcome E (the answer route is the limit; the extra evidence is used). All four must hold. (a) Paired k-up minus k-down on mult rows, pooled over six seeds, is at least +10 with a bootstrap CI (resampling items) whose lower bound is above 0. (b) Right-to-wrong flip rate is at most 5% with CI upper bound at most 10%, and at most 3 points above the frame-swap null. (c) At some answer-free loop t, the A readout (the better of ridge and MLP, stratified 80/20 split) has held-out R^2 of at least 0.60 and is at least 0.30 above the floor's A readout, on at least 5 of 6 seeds. (d) More than half of wrong answers are type (b). If no loop is answer-free, clause (c) cannot pass. Next single change: worked-program teaching rows for fewshot_number_rule covering every trained variant (hand-written traces, allowed by rule 1), 6 seeds, F1 mark kept.

Outcome R (the rule is not extracted). The A readout has R^2 at most 0.20 for both ridge and MLP at every loop t=1..6 and at final, on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and more than half of wrong answers are type (a) or (d). Next single change: the W2 scratch-token test (16 learned tokens, about 4k params; marks cited in architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 5b, not re-read here; untested).
Outcome P (position shortcut). Flip rate at least 15%, and at least 10 points above the frame-swap null. Next single change: random-order fewshot training rows (a data change), 6 seeds.
Undecided, act on nothing: any other pattern, including a flat k-curve with a readable A at an answer-free loop (see null_risk).
plan.proved_wrong: The idea's claim that extra shots help the answer route is proved wrong if the paired k-up minus k-down on unique-answer mult rows has a CI upper bound below +3 over six seeds. The claim that a readable multiplier means only a writing or arithmetic step is missing is proved wrong if the A readout is at most 0.20 for both ridge and MLP at every loop, with its shuffled-label null at chance. Neither result proves B2 cannot learn fewshot in general: the probe reads one checkpoint family on in-distribution rows. If the whole-prompt hash gate (step 0b) cannot be run, the result is no verdict, not a pass.
plan.null_risk: Medium, and it sits in the readout rather than the behaviour. Could the marks pass with no real change? Partly, yes. For mult rows the target A equals the true query answer divided by the query input (A = y_q / x_q). The 9 registers are tied one-to-one to the talker's answer characters (redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 5b, line 82, shown; gen_copy at ledger.py lines 239-249, talk at line 380), so a readable A at the final loop can be the answer leaking into the registers, with no rule extracted. The input floor does not block this, because the answer is not in the input. Clause (c) and the answer-free test (3b) are the guard; without them the readout clause is not decisive. Second risk: a right answer reached by luck flips easily under reordering, so the frame-swap null is needed and the flip denominator is right-in-original rows only. Third: the trained shot counts are unknown until step 0a. If training has only 2-pair rows, the k=3 cell is out of distribution and clause (a) measures a shift. Behaviour clause (a) is much harder to pass with no real change: with about 1,800 paired items per cell, the standard error of the k-gap is roughly 1-2 points (suggested, from the discordant-pair share), so +10 and +3 are separable. The 6-7 point estimate in the critic notes applies to unpaired 100-item cells, not to this design. Gap in the decision table: a flat k-curve with a readable A at an answer-free loop is the case the original idea hoped to diagnose, and under the current rule it is undecided with no named change. The owner should name one before sealing, or accept that this probe can end with no action. Low risk: a rule held in a code that neither a ridge nor a one-layer MLP can read would give a false R.
plan.autonomy: Measurement only, at build time; nothing here ships. The generator's A and B labels are used only to score items and fit the readout, never at deploy time (rule 10). Each outcome's next change is the part that must work at deploy time. E's teaching rows train the thinker to pick a shown pair and check its candidate against the other shown pairs in its own written steps, the same self-check shape as the C2 example checker (kept separate under rule 9). Not changed here: the example numbers still reach B2 through regex digit-run slots and int() (INVENTORY A1, /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md; progparse caps 16 numbers). That is a hand step on the answer path under rule 1 that already exists. No fewshot result can be called hand-code-free until A1 is replaced, and this probe does not add to it.
steps: 0a (read-only, on the PC): read the skills fewshot_number_rule generator and its training config. First it proves our scoring code gives the saved numbers. Then it asks whether B2 uses the extra examples, whether the rule can be read from inside it, and whether its wrong answers are slips in writing the number. fixed_plan.question: On the six saved B2 checkpoints (q33 seeds 200-205), on fresh in-distribution fewshot_number_rule items, where does B2's gap to plain_tf_steps come from? Outcomes: E (the extra evidence is used, and the wrong answers are writing slips), U (the rule is readable but the evidence is not used), R (the rule is not readable), P (position shortcut), or undecided. Preliminary, shown: in-distribution exact match 34.6% for B2 vs 60.8% for plain_tf_steps (83/240 vs 146/240, from RESULT.json).

Test-side solver ceiling (rule 3, scoring only): a small program search over the skills variants add, mult and pair_sum. It marks which k-down items have two or more fitting answers and reports the solver's score on them. If not, stop and check precision (bf16 vs fp32), the prompt string and the data path.

Stage 0 (descriptive; no pass or fail): on the big-dev in-dist fewshot rows, exact match by variant, answer digit count, shot count and solver ambiguity, with per-row predictions saved. Its only use is to fix the primary variant and cell before the seal. If failures sit mostly in add or pair_sum, the primary changes before the seal, with the reason recorded.

E (evidence used; the writing route limits), all four must hold: (E1) on ambiguous k-down items (at least 150 per seed, or E cannot be judged), B2's k-up minus k-down is at least +10 points, pooled over six seeds, item-bootstrap CI lower bound above 0, with the solver's own gain shown beside it. (E2) On unambiguous items, k-up minus k-down is at least -5 points (CI lower bound above -5). (E3) More than half of wrong answers are class W. (E4) At some answer-free loop t (talker-decode exact match at most 2 points above the floor and at most 2 points above the shuffled null), the A readout has held-out R^2 at least 0.60 and at least floor + 0.30, on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Loop t and readout type are fixed on the training split.
U (rule readable, evidence not used): E4 holds and E1 fails. Next change: none named here; the owner names one before the seal.

R (rule not readable): the A readout (ridge and MLP) is at most 0.20 at loops 1 to 6 and at the final loop, and at most floor + 0.10, on at least 5 of 6 seeds; and more than half of wrong answers are class (a) or (d).
P (position shortcut): flip rate at least 15% on right-in-original rows, and at least 10 points above the frame-swap null, on at least 5 of 6 seeds.

Precedence: if P fires, it is reported first; R may hold alongside P and is reported too. E, U and R cannot all hold (their thresholds exclude each other). Otherwise the result is undecided, with no action.
Shuffled-label null: each readout's shuffled-label R^2 must be at most 0.05, or that readout is void.

Class order (sealed): W first (the answer has the same digit count as the true answer and differs in exactly one digit position); then (a) equals the output of another variant's rule that fits all shown pairs; then (c) equals a shown x, a shown y or the query; then (d) everything else.

idea.title: Shape variety versus digit variety at fixed row presentations
idea.summary: Today's B2 sees each of its 200,000 skills rows about 31 times. A deep 10M B2 on the same data was flat on the one seed read so far while the plain 13-layer gained, so data variety is the suspect. Keep the 6.1M row presentations fixed and fill them with about 1.5M shape-distinct rows (S) versus the same skeletons redrawn with fresh digits (D) versus today's rows (C), first on the cheap plain step-writer.
idea.change: Build two row sets: S, about 1.5M rows distinct on the digit-masked shape and capped per family at its shape count; D, the same 200,000 skeletons redrawn with fresh digits to about 1.5M. The skills generator (branch claude/project-thread-y0sxwe) is not in this snapshot, but data-pool/built/own72.tgz holds skills.jsonl with 1,583,731 rows at rung 30 and steps (suggested to be the shape-unique pool; overlap with dev variants must be checked). Train plain_tf_steps with C0 settings (cap lifted) on S, D and C, 24,000 updates, 2 seeds; then B2 on six seeds if the plain screen passes.
idea.why: First look at 10M (seed 201 only): B2 deep 74.65 vs 74.93 for B2 3M, flat, while plain 13-layer 70.17 vs C0 67.98 (+2.19); B2's own rerun differs from its confirm run by 0.66, so the flat reading is within noise but not encouraging. Variant misses are not explained by shape count (group_induct 77 shapes scores 43.8, compare_numbers 769 shapes scores 6.7), so the arms test structure directly. B1 ran about 22 passes per row in both arms and never tested variety at a fixed presentation budget.

chair.reasons:
Verdict: plan, but only as a rebuilt, gated, low-to-medium priority screen. All four critics said revise, and the main problems hold. I re-read the readout and the data notes myself.

Why it is not a cut:
- The cost is small. Plain C0 runs take about 0.37 h each on the rented 5090s (shown, first-look-10m-results/readout.json, train_h). The census is CPU-only.
- The question is real and unanswered. B2 grown to 10M gained little on the same 200k rows while the plain 13-layer gained (shown, readout.json). No run varies shape or digit variety at a fixed presentation budget.
- The 8A plan has a gap. The sealed 8A stop rule says there is no 30M rung if 10M minus 3M is below 0, and the quarter-pool variety diagnostic is a 30M run (shown, 8A-SPEC section 7; stop rule per the brief). So if B2 is flat at 10M, the variety question gets no readout. A cheap plain-model precursor would then be the only variety evidence before any money is spent.

Why the idea cannot run as written:

1. The premise is stale (shown, readout.json).
   - Seed 200 exists: B2 10M is 74.82 against 73.39 for B2 3M on the same box, a gain of +1.42. Seed 201 is -0.28.
   - The sealed marks (as given in the brief) call a gain under +1.0 on both seeds flat, and +3.0 on both encouraging. Seed 200 is +1.42, so the pre-fixed reading is unclear, not flat.
   - The lead over plain fell by 1.31 and 2.47. The plain 13-layer gained +2.73 and +2.19.
   - The deep model also rose on variant: +1.67 and +1.82. The plain 13-layer rose more on variant: +4.62 and +3.64. I computed both from readout.json.

2. The first look does not show that the data is saturated (suggested).
   - The same 200k rows gave the plain model a size gain, so the data can still carry size.
   - Competing explanations are untested and specific to B2: the width stays 256, the 17-vector state stays fixed, and the reader is unchanged.
   - A plain 3.27M screen cannot separate these. It can only say whether repetition costs a small plain model something.

3. The S arm cannot hold family mix constant, and its source is wrong.
   - Shape counts per family are small (shown, DATA-POOL-PLAN line 36): group_induct 77, digits_parity 231, verify_claim 231, odd_one_out 308, backward_solve 462, compare_numbers 769, list_stats 923, fewshot_number_rule 1,009, arith_bare 1,078, seq_next 1,592.
   - Capping each family at its shape count drops these families by up to 98% against C. C probably already contains all of their shapes (suggested). So S minus C and S minus D mix shape variety with family starvation.
   - own72 is not a shape-unique pool (reported by two critics from the manifest and sampling, not re-checked by me). The manifest shows a 25.5% duplicate share, the critics counted about 59-65% distinct digit masks, and the 62-token length filter is off. The realistic ceiling is about 1.0M rows, not 1.5M.
   - own72 is also 8A's sealed pool, so S and D must be built from the generator on the PC with the same filters as the q33 200k build. The generator is not in this snapshot.

4. The variant split cannot be fixed by more shapes or digits (shown, reader/custom_io/research/data.md lines 44 and 53).
   - 1,078 of 1,320 variant rows use a never-trained variant, and only 16% of variant prompts have an exact train template after masking numbers and names. Frame and family are 0%.
   - A train-clean S cannot contain those forms. S can help only on layout-only rows (242) and on recombinations of trained pieces. So the original +3.0 variant mark is unrealistic.
   - A critic estimated S minus C on variant at about 0 to +2 (suggested). The right mark is on pooled-5, with variant read in strata.

5. The dev-shape filter (R5) is a leak-removal confound if it is applied to S alone. It must apply identically to all arms, or to none.

6. Two seeds are too few (computed by two critics).
   - With the original marks, the chance of a pass with no true effect is 2-4%, a true +2 passes only 23-26% of the time, and about half to two-thirds of outcomes land in the undecided gap.
   - The "D minus C at least S minus C" proof-wrong clause fires about half the time on a true tie.

7. Hygiene: rule 5 (protected-panel overlap hash on every new row; DATA-POOL-PLAN says panels are not cleared), one machine for all arms (B2's same-box rerun drift is 0.39-0.66 pooled-5), and rule 7 caps.
   - Rule 7: the C0 step cap of 107 does not bind in the samples (steps max 104), but rows over 208 characters (0.09%) must not be skipped.

Autonomy (rule 10), shown and suggested.
- The test only changes pre-ship training data. Hand-built parts (shape mask, dedupe, per-family quotas, dev-overlap filter, marks) are build-time and scoring tools. Rule 10 allows them and none runs at deploy.
- There is no deploy-time autonomous path yet. A pass justifies putting variety into the pre-ship corpus only.
- The deploy-time version is a separate, untested idea. The model writes its own practice questions, calls an outside shape-key tool by writing text (rule 1), keeps its shape counts in its own notebook, and picks novelty with a fixed constant that is the same every night, not tuned on dev.

Link to the north star: weak. This is a scaling and data diagnosis, not a world stepping stone. Rank it below the crafting expressibility audit and the Crafter timing gate. Its value is as a cheap hedge for the 8A stop-rule gap.
chair.revised_idea:
Rewrite D5 as a build-time repetition-versus-variety probe on the plain step-writer (C0 settings, 3,271,424 params). It is a precursor to the sealed 8A quarter-pool diagnostic, not a new variant lever, and its result is pre-ship only. One change at a time: the number of distinct training rows at a fixed family mix and a fixed 6.14M presentations (24,000 x 256).

Step 0, CPU census on the PC, no GPU, minutes. Marks are sealed before it runs.
- Per family: shape supply (digit-masked shapes in the generator) against C's row count and C's distinct-shape count.
- Distinct digit-masked shapes in the q33 200k build. Do not assume 200k; the estimate is about 120-135k.
- Which dev splits have templates in C. Already known (shown, data.md line 44): in_dist 82%, vocab 89%, variant 16%, frame 0%, family 0%.
- For each arm, the count of rows over 208 characters and over the plain step cap of 107. No row is skipped.
- The 13-word protected-panel overlap hash on S and D rows (rule 5), plus the dev-shape overlap counts.
- Gate, fixed in advance. Drop the S arm if S_fm holds fewer than 50% new shapes relative to C overall, or if the dev-shape overlap makes it unfair. In that case keep only the D-versus-C contrast.

Arms. All three come from one generator build on the PC, with the same 62-token length filter, the same held-out and dev-prompt exclusions, the same caps lifted (K1), and one machine, with C re-run on that machine.
- C: today's 200k rows, about 30.7 passes.
- D: C's skeletons with fresh digits only, drawn up to the same number of distinct rows as S_fm (about 1.0-1.5M, whatever S_fm reaches). This keeps family mix, shapes and dev overlap identical to C.
- S_fm (family-matched shape-distinct): per-family presentation counts are copied from C, so family mix is identical by construction. Within each family, distinct skeletons = min(shape supply, presentations / 4). A family with too little supply keeps its full supply and repeats it. The shortfall is not refilled from other families. Report each family's share in S_fm, D and C.
- Apply the dev-shape exclusion identically to all three arms (or to none), and report the counts.

Readout. Primary is pooled-5 (all five splits). Variant is read in strata: never-trained-variant rows (predicted flat) against layout-only and recombination rows (the only place S can help). Add per-family tables with the predicted pattern written first: families with large shape supply move, and the small-supply families (group_induct, digits_parity, verify_claim) do not move, because C already holds their shapes. Record train accuracy within one machine only.

Seeds and cost, staged. Start with seeds 200-201 for D and S_fm (4 runs, about 2 h at 5090 speed, plus the C re-runs on the same box). Add seeds 202-203 only if the stage-1 stop rule is not met. Total is about 6 h at 5090 speed, so budget 6-9 h because the 5070 Ti speed is untested.

Marks, suggested values to be sealed by Ben before any run (pass marks are per rule 4):
- Pass: S_fm minus C on pooled-5 is at least +1.5 on the 4-seed mean with a paired CI above 0 and at least +0.5 on each seed, and S_fm minus D is at least +1.0.
- Proved wrong: at the 2-seed stage, S_fm minus C is under +0.5 on pooled-5 on both seeds; or after 4 seeds the mean is under +0.75.
- Report D minus C as a separate finding. If D minus C is within 0.5 of S_fm minus C, shape variety adds nothing beyond digit variety.
- Report the variant delta as secondary. Do not use +3.0 on the whole variant split.

Follow-ups. Only if the plain screen passes, run B2 3M on S_fm against C for six seeds (the existing B2 build needs the 7-step cap lifted, 528 rows). A B2 10M arm needs a memory fix because it reserved 17.0 GB on a 16 GB card (untested). The 8A own72 pool stays untouched. If 8A's 3M or 10M rung shows B2 gaining +3.0 per rung, drop D5. Read D5 together with the 8A quarter-pool diagnostic so there is one readout on the variety question. Label every result pre-ship only.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. State the 10M first look correctly. Seed 200 exists. B2 10M gained +1.42 on seed 200 and -0.28 on seed 201. The plain 13-layer gained +2.73 and +2.19. The lead over plain fell 1.31 and 2.47. The deep B2 rose on variant by +1.67 and +1.82, and the plain 13-layer rose by +4.62 and +3.64. The pre-fixed category is unclear, not flat. All of this is shown in first-look-10m-results/readout.json.

2. Hold family mix constant by presentation count. This is the main design fix.
   - S_fm and D both copy C's per-family presentation histogram. A shape cap per family must not change the mix, and shortfalls must not be refilled from other families.
   - Report each family's share and shape supply.
   - Write the predicted per-family pattern before running. Large-supply families should move. The small-supply families should not, because C probably already holds their shapes.

3. Build from the generator on the PC, not from own72.
   - own72 is 8A's sealed own-text pool. Its shape-unique count is about 1.0M at most (a critic's estimate), and its 62-token length filter is off.
   - S_fm size is whatever digit-only dedupe allows. Do not target 1.5M by assumption.
   - Use the same filters, held-out exclusion, dev-prompt exclusion and 62-token filter in all arms.

4. Use a staged plain screen on one machine with C re-run there. Run 2 seeds first, then 4. The original 2-seed marks give pass 2-4% at no effect and mostly land undecided (computed by two critics). The first-look rented-5090 runs differ from the PC by 0.39-0.66 pooled-5 for the same B2 seed, so do not mix machines.

5. Do not use +3.0 on the whole variant split.
   - 82% of variant rows use a never-trained variant, and only 16% of variant prompts have a train template after masking (shown, data.md lines 44 and 53). More shapes cannot supply those forms.
   - Make pooled-5 the primary mark and read variant in strata. Use the suggested marks in the revised idea, to be sealed by Ben before any run.

6. Apply the dev-shape exclusion identically to all arms. Run the protected-panel 13-word overlap hash (rule 5) on S and D before training. Do not skip the 0.09% of rows over 208 characters. Confirm that no row exceeds the plain cap of 107.

7. Tie it to 8A. D5 is a 3.3M plain precursor of the sealed 30M quarter-pool diagnostic, and it covers the case where the 8A stop rule (10M minus 3M below 0) cancels that diagnostic. Do not alter 8A data. Drop D5 if 8A shows B2 gaining at least +3.0 per rung. Keep a single readout on the variety question.

8. Do not claim anything about B2 from the plain screen. The B2-specific flat reading (width 256, 17-vector state, unchanged reader) is a separate untested explanation. The B2 follow-up is six seeds at 3M, and a 10M B2 arm needs a memory fix because it reserved 17.0 GB on a 16 GB card.

9. Run the census first and stop if it says the S arm cannot differ meaningfully from C. It needs the dev splits and the generator, which are on the PC and not in this snapshot.

10. Autonomy. Label the result pre-ship only, and write the deploy-time analogue as a separate untested idea. The model writes its own practice questions, calls an outside shape-key tool by writing text (rule 1), keeps its shape counts in its notebook, and picks novelty with a fixed same-every-night constant. It must have no dev-tuned thresholds, no generator knowledge, and no hand-picked practice set.

11. Plain-language summary for Ben (a high-school senior). The model sees each practice question about 30 times, and making it bigger did not help it the way it helped the plain model. The test asks whether showing it many more different questions, instead of the same ones again, helps. We keep the mix of question types the same so the answer is not an accident. The test uses cheap small models first. The result may say little about the hard split, because that split uses wordings the model never trained on. It is a side check, not the main road to Minecraft.

plan.title: Shape variety at a fixed practice budget (plain screen, pre-ship)
plan.ben_line: The model sees each practice question about 30 times, so this asks whether showing it many more different question shapes, with the same mix of question types and the same number of practice steps, helps a small plain model. It is a cheap side check before any big build, and it may say little about the hard split.
plan.question: With the same family mix and the same 6.14M presentations (24,000 updates x 256), does a plain step-writer score higher on pooled-5 when its training rows have more distinct question shapes (S) than when the same shapes come back with new digits (D), and than today's rows (C)? Labels: the first-look facts below are shown in /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/first-look-10m-results/readout.json; the 10M look is read as unclear (seed 200 +1.42, seed 201 -0.28), not flat, under the sealed rule in FIRST-LOOK-10M-2026-10-07.md lines 17-22.
plan.one_change: The number of distinct question shapes at a fixed number of passes and a fixed family mix: S versus D. D is the control with the same passes. C is the reference; it differs from S and D in passes too (about 30.7 passes per row against about 4), so C-versus-S is not the one-change contrast.
arms: C (reference): today's 200,000 q33 skills rows, plain_tf_steps at C0 settings (3,271,424 params), about 30.7 passes per row, restricted to the family set P below. The queued q43 C0 seeds 200-201 on BensPC may serve as C's stage-1 runs if the build and box match.

D (digit control): C's own shapes, each redrawn with fresh digits. Per-family presentation counts copied from C (about 4 passes per row). Per-family distinct rows set equal to S's, so D and S have the same row budget and differ only in how many distinct shapes they contain.

S (shape arm): per family, one row per distinct shape, sampled uniformly over distinct shapes with a fixed seed (never chosen on dev), up to the per-family presentation count divided by 4. Same presentation counts as C and D. Shape key sealed before the census: primary = the research/data.md template mask (numbers, names, nouns and made-up words masked, the key behind the 82% and 16% overlap figures); fallback = digit-only mask (DATA-POOL-PLAN section 2). If the template key is used, S minus D also contains name and noun variety, and that must be said in the readout.
plan.seeds: Stage 1: seeds 200 and 201 (three arms x two seeds = six runs). Stage 2, only if the stage-1 kill rule does not fire: seeds 202 to 205 (twelve more runs). A claim needs all six seeds 200 to 205 (rule 4). Pairing is by seed (same seed per column across arms).
plan.machine: BensPC (RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GB) for the census, all builds and all three arms, including the C re-run. No rented-5090 or Mac runs in the comparison: the first-look runs were rented and differ from the PC by 0.39 and 0.66 pooled-5 on the same B2 seed (shown, readout.json 'machine' field).
pass_marks: Seal first (Ben, as a new addendum in PASS-MARKS.md, before any build): the shape key, the family set rule, the gates, these marks, and the predicted per-family pattern written down. These are suggested values. They differ from the earlier suggestion in two places (see null_risk): the 4-seed CI rule cannot pass at +1.5, and the every-seed +0.5 rule halves power.

Gates (no training if any fails): (a) family set P holds at least 60% of C's presentations (suggested); (b) within P, S has at least 1.5 times C's distinct shapes (this replaces the ambiguous 'fewer than 50% new shapes' gate); (c) zero answer-only step targets and zero skipped rows in every arm; (d) identical per-family presentation counts across arms.

Stage-1 kill (seeds 200-201): if both seeds have S minus D below 0 on the primary score, stop and report. Under a true +1.5 this fires about 2% of the time; under a true zero about 25% (computed, planning SD 1.33).

PASS (six seeds 200-205, paired): mean S minus D at least +1.5 with the paired 95% CI lower bound above 0; AND mean S minus C at least +1.5 with its CI lower bound above 0; AND S minus D above 0 on at least 4 of 6 seeds. Primary score = pooled-5 over the dev rows of families in P (the families every arm trains on). Suggested change: the roadmap convention is all 6,040 rows; the all-family pooled-5 is reported beside it, not as the mark, because out-of-P families are zero-shot in every arm and only dilute differences.

PROVED WRONG (six seeds): mean S minus D below +0.5 on the primary score. Also proved wrong: S minus C at least +1.5 while S minus D is below +0.5, because then the gain comes from the passes change or family mix, not from shape.
UNDECIDED: any six-seed mean between +0.5 and +1.5, or a CI that crosses 0. No claim; report it as unclear. Do not extend seeds unless the sealed marks already said 12 seeds.

Reported with no mark: D minus C (passes and digits at fixed shapes); the variant split in two strata, layout-only rows (242 per seed) and never-trained-variant rows (1,078 per seed) (research/data.md, shown); recombination rows only if the census labels them (no labels in the snapshot); per-family table against the predicted pattern; rare-shape share and step and answer length per arm.
plan.proved_wrong: Six-seed mean S minus D on the primary score below +0.5, or stage 1 with both seeds S minus D below 0 (stop). Also proved wrong: S minus C at least +1.5 with S minus D below +0.5, since the gain then comes from passes or family mix rather than shape.
plan.null_risk: Labels: shown = checked in the files named; computed = my arithmetic on shown files; suggested = reasoned. Could the marks pass with no real change? Noise alone almost never passes. The planning SD of 1.33 is the paired pooled-5 difference between B2 and the q33 plain step-writer over six seeds (computed from 33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json; the per-arm six-seed SDs are 1.01 plain and 0.63 B2). Under a true zero effect, a six-seed mean of +1.5 or more happens about 0.3% of the time (computed, normal approximation). Two of the earlier suggested marks are wrong. First, at four seeds a CI above 0 needs a mean above about 2.1, so +1.5 with CI above 0 cannot pass at four seeds (computed); the six-seed rule is the one that is consistent. Second, the every-seed +0.5 rule cuts power: at a true +2.0, all six seeds clear +0.5 only about 44% of the time (computed), so it is replaced by at least 4 of 6 seeds positive (about 99% at +2.0). The real false-pass routes are confounds, each with a control in the steps: (a) family starvation: if C is family-balanced (suggested; C's family counts are not in the snapshot), a small-supply family such as group_induct (77 shapes at 400k draws, shown in DATA-POOL-PLAN line 36) would repeat each row about 2,350 times under S, and seq_next (1,592 shapes) about 110 times, so the family set P excludes them; (b) more distinct rows give more chances of 13-word or template matches with dev, so exclusion counts are reported per arm, and the same shape set is removed in all arms; (c) a truncation in one arm (the 64-character default in models/plain_tf_steps.py makes 840 var_chain rows answer-only, shown in PASS-MARKS.md line 518); (d) mixed machines. Also, S samples uniformly over distinct shapes, not over draws, so its rare-shape share and answer lengths differ from C; this is reported, not controlled. The likelier error is a false null: 82% of in_dist prompts already have an exact train template and only 16% of variant prompts do (research/data.md, shown), so pooled-5 is mostly insensitive to shape variety, and a real variant effect may be too small to move the pooled mark.
plan.autonomy: Pre-ship, build-time data test only. Under rule 10 a build before shipping is not a deploy step, so the test is allowed, but the deployed model does nothing new here. The census, the shape key, the family quotas, the 13-word exclusion, the cap and the marks are all researcher or build steps, and none of them may run at deploy. Rules 1, 2 and 7 hold for the arms: the generator is hand-written teaching data, no LLM is involved, and no target is truncated (the cap is the arm-wide maximum). The deploy-time version is a separate, untested idea and must not be claimed from this result: the model writes its own practice questions, counts its own shapes in its notebook, calls an outside shape-key tool by writing text (rule 1), chooses its next practice kind by a novelty score, and stops when a fixed same-every-night constant says its shape coverage is enough. It needs no dev-tuned threshold, no generator knowledge and no hand-picked family quota.
steps: Seal (Ben): write the addendum in PASS-MARKS.md with the shape key, family-set rule P, gates, marks, and the predicted per-family pattern (large-supply families in P move up on S minus D; layout-only variant rows move up; no prediction for families outside P). This is the CPU-first step, no GPU.

Census on BensPC, CPU only, minutes to about an hour (suggested): for each of the 34 families, distinct shapes under both keys at 50k, 100k, 200k and 400k draws, to show saturation (shape supply is a finite template space, so it should plateau); C's per-family rows and distinct shapes; per-arm counts of prompts over 208 characters and step targets over 107 characters (the q33 200k build's train prompts top out at 204 characters, shown in research/data.md; the cap 107 was measured on the 200k rows, shown in PASS-MARKS.md lines 517-518); per-arm 13-word hits against every dev split. Merge the protected-panel hashes first (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md; DATA-POOL-PLAN section 6 says the pool must not train until that merge is done).

Gate (a): compute P = families whose saturated shape supply is at least C's per-family presentations divided by 4 (about 45,000 if C is family-balanced, suggested). If P holds less than 60% of C's presentations, stop and report; no training. Families outside P are excluded from training in all three arms and from the primary score.
Gate (b): S's distinct shapes within P must be at least 1.5 times C's distinct shapes within P. Otherwise stop.

Build C, D and S from one generator build with one seed, the same length filter, and the same exclusion: any row whose shape key or 13-word window matches a dev row is dropped in all three arms, and the excluded shape set is identical across arms. Set one step-target cap for all arms to the largest step target across the three arms, and raise any prompt limit (data.py MAX_PROMPT is 208 for B2) to the arm-wide maximum, so no row is skipped or falls back to the answer alone. Assert zero answer-only fallbacks (models/plain_tf_steps.py target_text) and identical per-family presentation counts. Save the counts.

Stage 1 on BensPC, seeds 200 and 201, all three arms, same batch 256, lr and 24,000 updates as q33. Record pooled-5 on the 6,040 rows, the primary P-only score, the variant strata, per-family tables, and the step and answer length distributions per arm. Time per run from the PC's own RESULT.json (shown: plain step-writer runs took 1,679 s and 2,271 s, i.e. 0.47 to 0.63 h).
Apply the stage-1 kill rule. If it does not fire, run stage 2: seeds 202 to 205, same arms.
Read the six-seed marks exactly as sealed. Anything in the undecided zone makes no claim.

Only if the six-seed plain result passes: a separate B2 check at 3,302,481 params on S and C, six seeds. It needs the 7-step cap lift first (the 528 rows, reported in the brief; not re-checked here). This is a second claim, not part of the plain pass.

Keep one readout with the 8A quarter-pool diagnostic (8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md section 7): this test is its 3.3M plain precursor. Drop this test if 8A shows B2 gaining at least +3.0 per rung (the 8A pass rule).

issues: KEY CONTRADICTION (shown + computed): the plan's primary shape key is the template mask (research/data.md section 1: numbers, names, nouns and made-up words masked). A coarser key cannot have more distinct shapes than the digit-only key. DATA-POOL-PLAN section 2 (shown, line 36) already lists 10 families with 1,592 or fewer digit-shapes at 400k draws: group_induct 77, digits_parity 231, verify_claim 231, odd_one_out 308, backward_solve 462, compare_numbers 769, list_stats 923, fewshot_number_rule 1,009, arith_bare 1,078, seq_next 1,592. All 10 fail the ~45,000-per-family gate under the template key too. The plan switches to the digit key only if the template key fails, which is a post-census key switch. Seal the digit key now and keep the template key as a report only.

THE DEV-OVERLAP EXCLUSION CHANGES THE BENCHMARK (shown): step 4 drops every train row whose shape key or 13-word window matches a dev row. 82 percent of in_dist prompts already have an exact train template (research/data.md section 1). 21,830 of 200,000 q33 train prompts (11 percent) share a 13-word window with the skills dev panels, mostly prop_eval 5,027, object_track 3,888, state_update 2,222, rule_apply 1,665, distance_units 1,537 (DATA-POOL-PLAN section 6). DATA-POOL-PLAN itself recommends reporting this, not gating it. The plan also does not say whether gate (a) is counted before or after removal. The arms would then be scored on a different dev coverage than q33's, so in_dist and frame would no longer be comparable. Use exact-duplicate removal only and report template coverage.

COVERAGE CONFOUND: S (uniform over the whole shape pool) and D (C's frequency-weighted shapes) differ in how many dev templates each arm's training rows contain. That coverage is the mechanism for variant, but it is a confound for in_dist and frame. The plan reports coverage but has no rule for it. Add a per-split coverage table and mark any split where S and D differ by more than 3 points as confounded (reported, not judged).

D IS NOT A CLEAN CONTROL: D samples C's skewed shape frequencies while S samples uniformly over distinct shapes. S-D therefore also changes the rare-shape tail and answer length; the plan admits this only for S versus C. Under the template key, D keeps names and nouns fixed while S varies them, so S-D is not template variety alone. Fix: D = the same uniform sampler restricted to K random shapes per family (K = C's distinct count), each shape repeated with fresh digits and with fresh names and nouns wherever the key does not mask them.

POWER IS TOO LOW FOR THE MARK: the planning SD of 1.33 is the B2-minus-plain paired SD (computed from the six 33-pc-confirm RESULT.json files; the CONFIRM-ANALYSIS CI implies it). S-D compares two separately built plain arms. The plain per-arm six-seed SD is 1.01 (computed from RESULT.json, shown), so the paired SD for two independent plain arms is about 1.4 (suggested). Monte Carlo with the mark as written (mean at least +1.5, CI above 0, at least 4 of 6 positive) passes about 41-43 percent of the time at a true +1.5 and 70-76 percent at +2.0 (computed, SD 1.33 to 1.45), before the S-C condition. At a true +1.0, about 18 percent of six-seed runs would have a mean below +0.5 and be declared proved wrong (computed, SD 1.33).

S-C CONDITION IS CONFOUNDED: C has about 30.7 passes per row over 200,000 rows (computed: 6.144M / 200k). S and D have about 4 passes over about 1M rows. S-C therefore mixes repetition with shape variety. Requiring S-C at least +1.5 as a second pass condition can fail for reasons unrelated to shape and lowers power further. Make it report-only.

PRIMARY DILUTES THE MECHANISM: pooled-5 over P is dominated by in_dist (1,360 rows, 82 percent template-covered), frame and vocab. The plan's own null_risk says pooled-5 is mostly insensitive to shape variety, so a real effect may not move it. The mechanism predicts gains on the variant split (1,320 rows; 1,078 never-trained-variant rows and 242 layout-only rows per dev file, not per seed, shown in research/data.md section 3). Make variant a co-primary with its own mark.

ONE DATA DRAW: all seeds share one generator build and one sampler seed. Six seeds then measure training noise only, and the 0.3 percent false-pass figure assumes the data draw is fixed. A shape-variety claim needs at least two independent sampler builds, with seeds split across them, or it must be scoped to that build.

C IS NEITHER THE QUEUED RUN NOR THE q33 BASELINE: queue 43 (C0, seeds 200-201) trains on the full q33 200k rows at cap 107, with no P restriction and no exclusion (queue_local/43-pc-c0.txt, shown). The q33 six-seed plain_tf_steps is cap 64 with 840 answer-only var_chain rows (PASS-MARKS addendum 20, shown), so it is not a reference for this build either. C must be rerun in the test build.

HOURS AND MACHINE ARE UNDERSTATED: the plan cites plain step-writer runs of 1,679 s and 2,271 s (0.47-0.63 h). Those are seeds 200 and 205. THE B2 SECOND CLAIM IS ONE CHANGE TOO MANY: B2 writes at most N_RES = 7 steps (progparse.py line 8, shown), runs 8 thinker rounds with the step embedding clamped at n_loops - 1 (ledger.py line 308, shown), and holds at most N_NUM = 16 numbers.
