CALCULATOR LESION IS HAND CODE (rule 1): plain_tf_steps.py calc_fill forces exact results into the decode for the 'calc' lesion, and queue 43 reports calc-on scores through --final-eval (shown). Calc-on must never be part of a mark or a claim. Report calc-off only.

GATES ARE WEAK OR MISSING: (i) gate (b), S at least 1.5 times C's distinct shapes, is almost certainly met because C has only 200k rows, so it tests nothing (suggested). fixed_plan.title: Distinct surface variety at fixed passes (plain step-writer, 12 seeds)
fixed_plan.ben_line: We test whether showing a small plain model many more different practice questions, each seen about four times, teaches it more than showing fewer different questions with new numbers, using the same total practice steps. If variety helps, it is a cheap lever to try before building a bigger model.
fixed_plan.question: At equal presentations (6.14M = 24,000 updates x 256) and equal per-family rows, does a plain step-writer at 3.27M score higher on pooled-5 over the families with enough distinct digit-masked shapes (set P), and higher on the variant split, when its rows come from a uniform sample over many distinct shapes (S) than from the same sampler restricted to fewer shapes (D)?
fixed_plan.one_change: Number of distinct shapes per family: S (full uniform sample) versus D (the same sampler restricted to K shapes, K = C's distinct count per family). Presentations, passes (about 4), family set P, sampler, digit and name refresh, step cap, model and optimizer are held fixed. C is reference only.
arms: S: for each family in P, one row per distinct digit-masked shape from a uniform sample of the shape pool (sampler seed sealed in advance). Rows = family presentations / 4 (about 1 million rows if P holds about 24 families; suggested). plain_tf_steps at C0 settings: cap set to the maximum step target over all three arms (107 if g2 holds), 3,271,424 params, 24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, final eval with --save-preds, calc lesion off in every mark.

D: the same sampler restricted to K random shapes per family (K = C's distinct count in that family, a sealed random subset of S's pool). Each shape is repeated with fresh digits, and with fresh names and nouns wherever the key does not mask them, to the same row count and presentations as S.
C (reference only, seeds 300-301): q33's 200k rows restricted to P and rebuilt in the test build (not the queued q43 run). Reported, never judged.
fixed_plan.seeds: 12 new training seeds 300-311 (never used before). Seeds 300-305 use sampler build A and seeds 306-311 use sampler build B, so the data draw varies across seeds. S and D are paired on the same seed and build. The claim needs all 12; per-build results are reported.
fixed_plan.machine: Rented RTX 5090, one per seed (or 6 boxes with 2 seeds each). All arms of a seed run on one box, from one hash-checked build per sampler build. Renting needs Ben's approval under rule 6 (PC and Mac both full). Fallback: BensPC, about 10-25 h of PC time for 26 runs at the q33 timings.
pass_marks: Gates before any training (no run if one fails). g1: P is the set of families whose digit-masked shape supply from the census is at least C's per-family presentations / 4, counted from the actual q33 family counts in the build manifest; P must hold at least 60 percent of C's presentations. g2: zero answer-only step targets, zero skipped rows, zero answers over 8 characters, zero prompts over the arm's limit, identical per-family presentation counts in S and D. g3: zero rows whose strings match held-out families, held-out openers or closers, or held-out layouts. g4: exact-duplicate prompts removed in both arms; no dev-overlap removal. g5: hash-only protected-panel check passes on the new rows (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md). g6: per-split template coverage reported for S and D; any split with a difference over 3 points is marked confounded.

PRIMARY (all 12 seeds, paired): mean S minus D on pooled-5 over the dev rows of P families is at least +1.0; paired 95 percent CI lower bound (t with 11 df, 2.201) is above 0; S is above D on at least 8 of 12 seeds.
CO-PRIMARY (all 12 seeds, paired): mean S minus D on the variant split of P families is at least +1.5, with CI lower bound above 0.
CLAIM ('more distinct shapes help at fixed passes') only if PRIMARY and CO-PRIMARY both pass. Neither alone is enough.
PROVED WRONG: the PRIMARY 95 percent CI upper bound is below +0.5, or D beats S on pooled-5 with the CI upper bound below 0.
UNDECIDED: anything else. No claim; report the means and CIs.

Reported with no mark: S minus C and D minus C (2 seeds, reference only); template coverage per split per arm; per-family table; variant strata (layout-only and never-trained variant); answer and step length by arm; calc-off scores only.
No stage gate and no seed extension beyond 12. Run all 12 in parallel; a stop after 2 seeds would fork the design.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: PRIMARY 95 percent CI upper bound below +0.5, or D above S on pooled-5 with the CI upper bound below 0. If PRIMARY passes but the CO-PRIMARY CI upper bound is below +0.5, the gain is not on the variant split: report it as not variety-specific, with no claim.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Computed by Monte Carlo under stated SD assumptions. PRIMARY (12 seeds, SD 1.4 per paired difference, 8-of-12 rule): about 0.6 percent pass at zero, about 47 percent at +1.0, about 88 percent at +1.5. CO-PRIMARY (12 seeds, SD about 2.1 = plain variant SD 1.46 x root 2): about 1 percent at zero, about 48 percent at +1.5, about 78 percent at +2.0. The joint pass is lower than either alone (not computed; the two are correlated because variant is inside pooled-5). Risks: (i) the coverage confound (S can raise dev-template coverage); (ii) one sampler per build, reduced by two builds; (iii) P may hold only about 20-24 families, so the test says little about the excluded families; (iv) a real effect below about +1.5 will mostly read as undecided; (v) the S and D SDs may differ from the q33 plain SD of 1.0 (untested). The old 2-seed stage is dropped because its kill rule would fork the design.

idea.title: Sub-task signature census and held-out-signature meter
idea.summary: Before training anything, classify every variant row by a sub-task signature (op sequence and answer form where worked steps exist, a digit- and name-masked template where they do not) and count how many already appear in training. Then score the existing B2 checkpoints on about 1,500 held-out-signature rows against matched in-signature rows, giving a sharper variety meter than the 40-row family cells.
idea.change: New CPU scripts (custom_io/census_subtask.py and subtask_meter.py): signature from progparse.program_for plus answer form; masked template otherwise; output per family the share of variant rows whose signature is in train, joined to six-seed variant means. Meter: load B2 s100/s101 (29-b2-screen) or the 200-205 b2ckpt files, score held-out-signature vs matched in-signature rows.
idea.why: Per-family variant accuracy does not track program coverage (table_calc 100% coverage scores 0.4, kin_chain 0% scores 89.2; Spearman about 0.29), so a better structure measure is needed. A large in-signature minus held-out gap says the variant miss is a structure gap; a small gap kills every structure-based data idea. Per-family cells have seed spread up to 25 points, so a 1,500-row meter is the readable instrument.

Seal the signature list (or a separate panel) before any census-driven data change. Measuring alone does not break rule 10, since the deployed model does not run it.

[shown] Compute and hours. No GPU is needed. The census is pure Python over rows, and the meter is CPU inference of a 3.3M-parameter model (13.2 MB; b2ckpt checkpoints match their sha256 sidecars), well under 1 GB, so the 16 GB limit does not bind. The brief's run times are off at the top end: the six confirm runs took 0.99 to 4.21 h (train_s 3,559 to 15,164). This test does not need training. The 0.5 h CPU estimate is untested, because torch is not installed here.
critiques.rescue: Replace the signature meter with a data-first split test on the PC, no new generator, one change at a time, marks written before the run. Step 1 (data only, minutes): for each family, split its 40 dev variant rows per seed by the row's own 'variant' key (trained or never-trained) and by layout (held-out or not), and compute each family's majority-train-answer floor on the same rows. Step 2 (CPU, six b2ckpt checkpoints, seeds 200-205): B2 six-seed accuracy on (a) never-trained-variant rows, (b) layout-only rows, (c) the same family's in_dist rows as the reference. Marks: computation-novelty gap = in_dist minus never-trained-variant, pooled over families with at least 10 rows in each group. A gap of at least +20 with the CI above +5 means new computation is the miss. A gap under +5 means it is not. Layout gap at most +5 means layout is not the miss; at least +20 means it is. A family whose B2 variant accuracy is within 3 points of its label floor on all six seeds is reported as a shortcut and kept out of the means. Step 3 (same rows, CPU): teacher-forced program accuracy on variant rows that have a parsed program, using the ledger.extra_evals harness pointed at dev/variant.jsonl instead of in_dist. At least 90% teacher-forced with free-run answer at most 40% means the miss is in writing the program. At most 50% teacher-forced means the miss is in reading or executing the given steps. Proved wrong for the structure/variety idea: computation-novelty gap under +5 and teacher-forced program accuracy under 50%. Note the 7-step exclusion and the NUM/GEN/WORD mode when reporting. Hours: 0 GPU, about 0.5 h CPU once the PC has the dev variant rows and torch. Seal the signature and family lists before any census-driven data change, so the variant split stays held out.
critiques.already_tried: Nothing in the snapshot runs a variant-row probe. Closest prior: research/data.md:44 (template match 16% for variant under the broader mask), data.md:53 (1,078 never-trained variant rows, 242 layout-only), data.md:68 (split rule); DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md section 2 (digit-masked shape uniqueness); own72 MANIFEST digit_or_name_shape_duplicate_share (20.5%, 23.1%, 25.5% at rungs 3, 10, 30); RESULT.json extra.op_acc (in_dist, n=400: teacher-forced program 98, free-run answer 98); extra.opswap (ADD/SUB swap gives the swapped value on 99.9%, so the executor is used). Not tried anywhere in the snapshot: a per-family split by the variant key, teacher-forced program accuracy on variant rows, or a label-floor baseline on variant rows.
critiques.expected_effect: If run as written, the census gives a per-family table of signature-in-train shares and two gaps whose meaning depends on the signature definition. Most variant rows would count as held-out, because only about 16% match a train template under the broader mask and 82% are never-trained variants (suggested from data.md:44 and :53). The meter's gap would mix wording with structure, so it cannot separate structure from wording, and its +20 pass could fire on a wording-only miss (reasoned from the idea's own definitions, untested). The revised test uses the generator's own variant key and layout, a label floor and teacher-forced program accuracy. It would separate computation novelty from layout and from program writing, with fixed marks, on six existing checkpoints, with no generator and no GPU (untested).

chair.reasons:
CUT as a standalone idea. The question it asks is mostly answered by files that already exist, and the meter as written would pass trivially. It is CPU-only, so no GPU time is wasted, but it also does nothing for the Minecraft north star.

1. The census was already done, and the idea's closest_prior omits it. [shown] custom_io/research/data.md line 44: after masking numbers, names, nouns and made-up words, an exact train template matches 82% of in_dist prompts, 89% of vocab, 16% of variant, and 0% of frame and family. Line 53: 1,078 of 1,320 variant rows use a never-trained variant, 242 are layout-only. Line 68: the split is defined as 'variant not in train variants'. So a held-out signature is the variant split by construction, and the meter's gap restates how the split was built.

2. The +20 validity mark cannot fail. [shown, computed from the six q33 RESULT.json files] B2 in_dist is about 90.5 and variant 34.7, a raw gap of about 56 points. Any in-signature versus held-out comparison clears +20 without saying anything about structure. 'Matched in-signature rows' names no matching keys. The bands 5-20 (meter), 30-70% (census) and 0.3-0.5 (Spearman) have no verdict. [suggested, critic computation not rechecked] At n=33 the Spearman cut-offs 0.3 and 0.5 cannot be told apart (95% interval around 0.5 is about 0.19 to 0.72), and the current coverage measure already reads about 0.28.

3. The signature is the wrong instrument. [shown, from critics' reading of code] program_for keeps programs over 7 steps that training dropped (528 train rows, progparse.py line 199), returns None for both 'no steps' and 'parse failed', and has no WORD mode. On the template path a pure wording miss would make the +20 'structure' pass fire. The motivating coverage figure is a per-family 'has worked steps' flag measured on in_dist rows, not on variant rows.

4. I read the six-seed variant cells myself. [shown, computed from results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200-205 RESULT.json final_eval.variant.by_family, 40 rows per family per seed] Pooled over six seeds: the layout-only families (state_update 90.8, story_chain3 100.0) score 95.4% on 480 rows. The families data.md line 53 lists as new computation (list_stats, letter_ops, seq_next, compare_numbers, fewshot_number_rule, rule_apply, digits_parity, object_track) score 2.2% over 1,920 rows. The families it lists as recombinations score 36.9% and split sharply: chain_ops 100, kin_chain 89.2, percent_rate 79.6, arith_bare 57.5, copy_word 31.7, distance_units 25.4, div_exact 6.2, table_calc 0.4. So layout and wording are not the miss (frame costs only about 2.8 points, shown in the confirm numbers), new computation is about 0 by design, and the one open puzzle is why some recombinations fail. A signature census does not resolve that puzzle.

5. The decision it gates is already covered. [shown] B1-a (teacher variety) was proved wrong at +0.78 against +15 (RESULTS-B1.md). 8A-SPEC lines 126-127 queue a quarter-pool diagnostic asking whether data variety rather than size limits B2. A 'structure gap' verdict would point to a data step already tested in its teacher form.

6. It cannot run from the snapshot. [shown] The q33 train.jsonl (a Windows PC path) and the dev splits are absent. own72 is the 8A training pool with held-out items already rejected (heldout_flag 5,572,497), so it is neither the q33 train set nor a clean scoring set. [untested] Whether the 29-b2-screen seeds 100-101 used the same 200k rows; the six b2ckpt seeds 200-205 are the right checkpoints.

Rules: no breach as a measurement (R1, R2, R6, R7, R9 fine). R5: any rows drawn from own72 or the generator would need clearing against GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved and blind panel hashes, which are not yet merged. R4: a two-checkpoint go/no-go is only a screen. R10: the deployed model never runs it, so it passes, but the census output must never become a practice-kind picker or a stuck detector.
chair.revised_idea:
Do not spend a slot on the census or the held-out-signature meter. The useful remainder is a small diagnostic of variant cells that explains why some recombination families score near zero. Fold it into the existing variant and fewshot diagnosis panel, and do not run it as a separate idea. 

Measurement only, CPU, on the PC where the dev variant rows exist, using the six sha-checked b2ckpt checkpoints (seeds 200-205).

(a) Group the 1,320 dev variant rows by the rows' own (family, variant key, layout flag). Do not build new signatures and do not use own72.

(b) Mark each cell trained or never-trained from the q33 200k train file's variant keys. Rebuild that file from skills_curriculum.build --train 200000 --dev-per-cell 40 --seed 1 and check it against the FULL-BUILD-MANIFEST-200k-seed1.json hashes. Add a train-majority-answer floor per cell.

(c) Report B2 six-seed accuracy per cell, and teacher-forced program accuracy next to free-run answer accuracy on the rows that have a parsed program. Rows over 7 steps are reported separately, not dropped. This separates 'cannot write the program for the new wording' from 'cannot read or execute it'.

(d) Target cells: table_calc cost (0.4 despite full coverage), div_exact (6.2), distance_units time (25.4), copy_word distractor (31.7), list_stats sum (0.0).

Autonomy: nothing here may feed a deploy-time rule. The cell labels come from the generator, so they may not choose practice kinds or decide 'stuck'. The deploy-time analogue would be a novelty check on the model's own program writes against its own earlier tries. That is a different idea and untested.
chair.plan_guidance:
n/a for the cut. If the lead keeps a slot for the residue, the plan must get these right:

1. Seal before running. The prediction is that never-trained cells that only recombine known ops (the cells in the target list in revised_idea) score at least 50% pooled over six seeds, and that cells with a new instruction word score at most 5%. The result that proves the 'new computation is the whole miss' story wrong is any recombination cell scoring under 10% with teacher-forced program accuracy at or above 90%.

2. Fix every verdict band before the run. No gaps, such as the undefined 5-20 band in the original.

3. Score all six seeds. Report cells with at least 10 rows pooled across seeds, because per-seed cells of 40 rows swing 8 to 25 points. Use a bootstrap over rows within cells, not a Spearman cut-off at n=33.

4. Control for answer length (8 chars or fewer), prompt length (208 chars or fewer), step count (7 or fewer) and level. Exclude degenerate or shortcut cells: syllogism 47.5 equals the 'starts with No' shortcut, word_filter and var_chain are identical on every seed, and several families have a single answer string. Use the label floor.

5. Keep the cell labels measurement-only (rule 10), and take no rows from own72 or from any panel that has not cleared the protected-hash overlap check (rule 5).

6. Read B2's per-row predictions by re-scoring the checkpoints, because q33 did not save PREDS.json. The 0.5 h CPU estimate is untested because torch is not installed in this snapshot.

7. State which decision it gates. The answer should be either program-language growth (stage 4) or the 8A web-text mix. Without a named decision, drop it.

8. Keep it on the skills line only. It says nothing about the village model or Minecraft (rule 9), and it should not be presented as a Minecraft step.

idea.title: Block-use census: skip-one-block and per-round share on saved checkpoints
idea.summary: Before buying more depth, measure on trained checkpoints whether each controller block and each round actually changes the answer. Skip one block (all rounds, early rounds, late rounds), halve it, and log each application's update size relative to the state; later repeat on the 8-block first-look checkpoints, and log the same matrix every 1,000 updates in 8a runs. No training.
idea.change: Off-by-default hooks in Ledger.run() (skip_cells, half_cells, rec list) plus a probe script using load_model and evalx. Cells: intact; skip block j all rounds; skip j in rounds 0-3 or 4-7; skip every block in a half; half-strength j. 11 cells at 2 blocks, 35 at 8 blocks. Log teacher-forced loss, in_dist exact, McNemar counts, chain-5, and per-(round, block) update norm over state norm. Run on b2ckpt B2_s200..s205 now; ask for checkpoint.pt in the first-look collection list before the rented boxes are destroyed. Optional --usage-every N logger for the 8a runs. 0 params.
idea.why: Residual writers moved 10-18x from init during training (0.0505 vs 0.00289), and the control state RMS grows 3.4-3.9x over 8 rounds (shown), so Pre-LN dilution is possible but unmeasured per block. The 30M block count is otherwise set only by band arithmetic (9 blocks at mlp 6.0 or 11 at mlp 4.8; the spec's 14-16 do not fit). Skipping biases toward showing use, so a small cost is strong evidence of idleness and a large cost is only an upper bound.

evidence.claim: Six q33 checkpoints exist: b2ckpt/B2_s200..B2_s205/checkpoint.pt, 13,243,510 bytes each, step 24000, cfg copy=True, 101 tensors summing to 3,302,481. Seed identity is shown only for 200-202 (d0 result paths); match each file's dev in_dist to its RESULT.json first.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Trained residual-writer std 0.0505 (block 0) and 0.0520 (block 1) vs init 0.00289 on B2_s100; control-state RMS after round 8 is 3.92x and 3.38x round 1 on B2_s100/s101.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Each CBlock has three residual writers (o, p, out); the same blocks run every round; no existing lesion removes a single block (loops:K truncates rounds, ctl27 zeroes controls).
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: In LLMs late Pre-LN layers add little (2502.05795) and second-half layers contribute less (2505.13898); not shown for B2 or at 3M-30M.

test.where: PC or Mac CPU with torch (torch is not importable in the reading session); needs the dev in_dist rows from the PC data folder (not in the snapshot); first-look 8-block checkpoints after collection
test.arms: 2-block q33 checkpoints B2_s200..s205 (11 cells each); the two 8-block first-look checkpoints (35 cells each); intact reproduction check first
test.pass_mark: Reproduction: intact in_dist within 0.05 of RESULT.json, else stop. Labels: USED = teacher-forced loss rises at least 10% on both seeds, IDLE = under 2% on both. Decision rows: 3 or more of 8 blocks IDLE on both seeds at 8 blocks means do not order 30M at 9-11 blocks, re-solve the shape by width; all USED and 10M minus 3M at least +3.0 on both seeds means order 30M per the ladder; all USED with gain under +3.0 means run the data/size screen first; late rounds IDLE and early USED means test the stop head.
test.proved_wrong: Reading 'cheap to skip so block unneeded' is wrong if retraining without that block (one fewer block, same width) loses 3 or more points on both seeds; probe is invalid if reproduction fails.

idea.rules_check: Rules 1, 3, 4: measurement only, no claim; marks fixed here. Rule 5: dev in_dist and chain-5 only. Rule 6: CPU or PC minutes. Rule 9: B2 only. Rule 10: developer diagnostic, nothing in the answer path.

idea.director_note: Cheapest decisive test for the 'does depth help' risk and it gates the 30M money. Critics should check: skip bias, whether 2-block results say anything about 8 blocks, that first-look checkpoints will actually be collected, and that the 10%/2% thresholds on loss are sensible. The Csordas and MIDAS papers disagree, so do not trust either as a prior.

critiques.already_tried: Loop-count lesions in q33 RESULT.json; loop sweep in results/40-loops-probe/probe.log lines 1-2; ctl27 lesion in ledger.py run(); forward hook on m.core[-1] in probe_loops.py:64 (M5, last block only). problems: Rule 10 walk-through (suggested reading; Ben to confirm): the census is build-time analysis of saved weights, and no step runs in the deployed answer path. Steps: (a) add hooks, developer code; (b) choose cells, halves and thresholds (10%, 2%, 3-of-8), developer constants fixed before the run; (c) run the probe on checkpoints and dev rows, offline, developer; (d) pick the 30M block count, Ben or developer, a build-time choice that the brief says is not a deploy-time step; (e) the 8a logger, training-time and logging only; (f) the follow-up stop head, which would be a deploy-time method and needs an autonomous version (see item 4). Only (f) would touch deployment, and the idea does not build it. On this reading rule 10 is met.

Hooks in Ledger.run() (skip_cells, half_cells, rec list) stay as hand branches in the forward pass (ledger.py:278-357). They are inert when off, and the repo already uses this pattern (lesion argument at ledger.py:278, 315-316, 332-335; rounds snapshots at 340-341; shown). The idea adds no parameters, which is true by inspection. Needed: strip or gate these hooks in the shipped build so the deployed forward carries no test-only code.

The 8a logger (--usage-every N) runs teacher-forced loss and in_dist exact on dev rows every 1,000 updates, about 24 logs per 24k-update run (arithmetic, shown). It is logging only, so it passes rule 10. It breaks rule 10 if any automatic step reads it to add a block, stop a run or choose a round count, because that is a gate on dev answers. Its compute cost, and whether it changes RNG state or training, are untested. Keep it read-only and say so in the write-up.

The stop-head branch ('late rounds IDLE and early USED means test the stop head') proposes a deploy-time halting method. It needs an autonomous version: the model decides to stop from signals it can check without answers, and any threshold is learned or a fixed design constant, never tuned on dev. The census per-round update norm over state norm is answer-free (computable from ledger.py:307-318), so it is a candidate signal (suggested). Prior evidence to check first, shown in results/40-loops-probe/PROBE.json: gate G2 halting is closed (overthinking_pct 1.91 and 1.66, open false), while gate G1 more loops is open (7.3 and 8.4 percent of wrong answers right later).

Metric validity: the USED/IDLE rule uses 'teacher-forced loss' only. Under gold, run() executes the gold op (ledger.py:328) and takes the pointer argmax over gold-valid slots (ledger.py:329-330). So a block whose job is choosing the op is invisible on answer-side terms. The total loss does include op CE (ledger.py:507) and pointer NLL (ledger.py:513), and aux logs them separately (ledger.py:527). Fix: decide on total loss and on each component, and on free-running exact match (gold=None). Confirm that generate() at ledger.py:409 is the free-running path. The deployed model has no gold program, so the free-running measure is the one that matters for rule 10. Suggested; untested.

Round-count mismatch: q33 B2 runs the default 8 rounds (33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT config cfg is copy only; ledger.py:130 default n_loops=8; shown). The 8a 3M B2 runs n_loops 12 (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-box/box.json, cfgs.B2 and cmd; shown). The rounds 0-3 and 4-7 halves and the 11/35 cell counts assume 8 rounds. The cell arithmetic is correct (1 + B + 2B + 2 + B gives 11 at 2 blocks and 35 at 8; shown). Define the halves for 12 rounds before the 8a logger runs. The first-look 8-block checkpoints are 8-round, so they are not directly comparable to 8a.

Rule 4 and the 30M gate: the decision rows use two 8-block checkpoints (seeds 200 and 201). shown: whole-model-roadmap/FIRST-LOOK-10M-2026-10-07.md says two seeds are below the project's 6-seed noise rule and that no reading there is a verdict. The 'do not order 30M' rule is therefore a screen gate. Label it as a screen, and do not treat the census as a claim until six seeds.

Dev overlap: the census decides from dev in_dist (test pass_mark), and the 8a rung marks are read on pooled-5, which includes in_dist (FIRST-LOOK 'Readout, fixed now'; shown). The same panel picks the shape and scores the rung. Suggested: choose the 30M block count on a panel outside pooled-5, such as the family split. shown: the B2D_s200 RESULT.json final_eval has a 'family' key outside pooled-5. The 160-row count comes from the brief and is untested here.

Checkpoint survival: the six q33 checkpoints are present and match their sha256 (shown: code/b2ckpt/B2_s200..B2_s205/checkpoint.pt, 13,243,510 bytes each, sha256 check passed on all six). The 8-block first-look folders (whole-model-roadmap/first-look-10m-results/B2D_s200 and B2D_s201) hold RESULT.json, rc.txt, stdout and result.tgz.sha256, but no checkpoint.pt and no tgz (shown). Whether the tgz held checkpoint.pt, and whether the rented boxes still exist, is untested. FIRST-LOOK says the boxes are destroyed once results are collected (shown, Amendment 2). Ask for checkpoint.pt now. If it is lost, a re-run costs about 1.6 h (B2D train_s 5708 s at 4.2 steps/s; shown).

Redundancy blind spot: single-block skips show removability but not redundancy. Two equivalent blocks can each look idle alone and matter together. The 30M block count is a removability decision, so add pair skips for the three lowest-cost blocks (3 pairs at 8 blocks; suggested). The proved_wrong retrain test covers one block on two seeds only.

Undefined and unpinned cells: 'half-strength j' has no code path. CBlock.forward returns Z + o + p + out (ledger.py:117-124; three residual writers, shown), so the cell must say which writer(s) to scale by 0.5, or scale the whole block delta. The 10% and 2% thresholds do not say relative to what (intact loss on the same rows?) or on which loss term. Pin these before the run, since they are the pass marks.

Residual-writer claim has no source in the snapshot: 'moved 10-18x (0.0505 vs 0.00289)'. No result file has a weight-std key (PROBE.json has none; shown). The two numbers give 17.5x and 18x, not 10x. The init value is right: 0.02/sqrt(3 x 2 x 8) = 0.00289 (ledger.py:158-160; shown). Recompute from 29-b2-screen B2_s100 and B2_s101 checkpoint.pt with torch before citing it as shown (untested).

The control-state claim is correct but weak: PROBE.json results[].M5.ctrl_growth_8_over_1 is 3.918 (B2_s100) and 3.382 (B2_s101) (shown). The RMS rises almost linearly over rounds (8.26 to 32.36 on B2_s100), which residual accumulation alone would produce. It does not show that any block is idle.

Transfer to a shippable design (rule 1): the census measures the B2 controller, which runs hand code (regex number spans at ledger.py:214, in-forward int64 executor at ledger.py:76; shown). Its USED/IDLE results may not carry over to the calculator-as-tool design (T1, brief queue 40, not run; queue file not in this snapshot). Suggested: repeat the census on the T1 checkpoint before fixing the shippable 30M block count.

The decision rule is not validated. The proved_wrong test needs retraining without one block, but the test plan does not include it, so IDLE-by-skip is only a proxy. The thresholds have no null (suggested). The 10% and 2% teacher-forced-loss thresholds are not calibrated. Add a cost floor: replace block j with a freshly initialized block of the same init, or perturb its output by a fixed small amount, and place IDLE above that floor. The idea also leaves undefined which loss terms make up teacher-forced loss (op, pointer, mode, answer), which rows are used, and what half-strength scales (the o, p and out writers, or the whole block update).

Rows that bypass the controller may bias IDLE (shown, partly). loops:0 in_dist is 12.06 on the 8a 3M B2 seed 401 and 0 to 10.8 on the q33 seeds, above the leak limit of 5 (brief; PASS-MARKS.md lines 56 and 176). Rows answered without rounds may change little under any block skip, which would push blocks toward IDLE. The census should report skip effects separately on rows that depend on rounds (for example, rows where loops:0 is wrong and intact is right).

The cited papers were checked through WebFetch of the abstract pages (suggested priors only). Csordas et al. 2505.13898: second-half layers contribute much less, and no evidence of multihop composition. Sun et al. 2502.05795: Pre-LN variance growth makes deep blocks contribute little; LayerNorm Scaling is the proposed fix. Saunshi et al. 2409.19044 (MIDAS): 1B, 2B and 8B models, up to 40% faster pretraining, reasoning gains with similar or slightly worse perplexity. Kapl et al. 2512.08819: depth-grown models use layers more evenly. The idea's note that the Csordas and MIDAS papers disagree is inaccurate: both describe under-use of late layers in non-grown Pre-LN models and differ on whether growth fixes it. None of them studies 3M to 30M, and Kapl et al. grow depth during training by middle stacking, which 8a does not do (fresh init at a larger depth).

chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test, but only in a narrower form than written. It trains nothing and adds no parameters. It passes rules 1-3, 5-7 and 9. For rule 10 it is a build-time analysis of saved weights, nothing runs in the deployed answer path (suggested reading), so it passes.

What is real (shown):
- The six q33 checkpoints are in code/b2ckpt, sha256 checked.
- No per-block or per-application skip lesion exists. Only loops:K, noexec, opswap and ctl27 do (ledger.py run(); train.py lesion_names).
- CBlock has three residual writers, o, p and out, and the same blocks run every round (ledger.py lines 102-124 and 306-318).
- The cell counts (11 at 2 blocks, 35 at 8) are right.

What breaks it as written, which the critics found and I confirmed (the file checks are mine):
1. The 8-block half probably has no subject (shown).
   - first-look-10m-results/B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 hold only RESULT.json, rc.txt, stdout.events.txt and result.tgz.sha256. There is no checkpoint.pt and no tgz.
   - FIRST-LOOK line 65 says the boxes are destroyed once results are collected.
   - Whether the lost tgz held checkpoint.pt is untested, and no file in the folder can settle it. Only Ben can answer, so a Haiku file check would not help.
   - The 8a runs do pass --out (RESULT.json shows out=/job/g8a/w/8a-3M-s401-B2), so the file exists on the box. The folders collected so far hold only RESULT.json, stdout.events.txt and sha256 files, so no collected folder holds a checkpoint. A named collection step is missing.
2. The reproduction gate cannot pass (shown). in_dist has 1,360 rows, so one row is 0.074 points and a 0.05 tolerance means zero flipped rows.
   - The PC and the rented box already differ by 13 rows on seed 200 (1231 vs 1218 of 1360).
   - Training used bf16 autocast on CUDA only, so a CPU fp32 reproduction will flip rows.
   - The checkpoint stores no seed, so matching a file to a seed by in_dist is ambiguous (seeds 202 and 204 are 2 rows apart).
3. The USED/IDLE rule is uncalibrated and mislabelled.
   - The 10% and 2% loss bands have no null, no stated loss terms, and nothing for the 2-10% gap.
   - Teacher-forced loss hides a block whose job is choosing the op, because gold executes the gold op (ledger.py:328-330).
   - The idea's own proved_wrong clause says reading a cheap skip as an unneeded block is wrong, yet the decision rows do exactly that.
   - A single-block skip cannot tell idle from redundant (Hydra effect, suggested).
4. The state-norm metric is confounded (shown). Control RMS grows 3.4-3.9x over the 8 rounds (PROBE.json M5: 8.26 to 32.36), so a fixed-size update looks smaller late in the run. Use the norm only as a descriptive number, divided by per-round state RMS.
5. The q33 and first-look checkpoints are not the 8a shape (shown). They use 8 rounds, 9 registers and the 200k skills rows. The 8a B2 arms use 12 rounds, 36 registers and the 60M and 190M pools. A block that is idle on small synthetic data may be idle because of the data, which the spec names as a risk. Init also differs: writer std is 0.00289 at 2x8 and 0.00144 at 8x8.
6. The 8a logger would change a sealed build (addendum and bit-identity check needed) and arrives too late for 3M seeds 401, 402 and 405, whose results are already in. A post-hoc census on saved checkpoints gives the same information with no build change.
7. The two-seed 8-block census cannot gate a 4-5 day rung under rule 4. At most it can slow or stop 30M as a screen. It cannot choose a new width or block count without a dated addendum.
8. The 'stop head' branch is a deploy-time method. It is not built here and needs its own autonomous design. The existing halting gate G2 is closed (PROBE.json: overthinking 1.91 and 1.66). Drop that branch from this idea.
9. The residual-writer figures (0.0505, 0.0520) are not in any result file (grep finds nothing). They give 17.5x and 18x over init, not '10-18x'. Recompute them from the checkpoints before citing them as shown.

Value (suggested): modest. It cannot show bigger is better, and it cannot by itself justify ordering 30M, because skipping biases toward USED. Its main use is diagnosing the likely case where 10M minus 3M is under +3: is added depth idle (change the growth axis) or used but data-limited (run the quarter-pool diagnostic)? The Haiku critics put the chance it changes the 30M shape at 20-30% (suggested). The 1.5 h CPU estimate is untimed. The pilot is cheap, at most about 1.5 CPU hours or 20-60 GPU minutes, and risk-free, so it is worth running in the narrowed form, but it ranks below ideas that change what gets trained.
chair.revised_idea:
Block-use census, split into a pilot that can run now and a conditional part that waits for checkpoints. It is diagnostic only: no training, no new parameters, nothing in the answer path, so rule 10 is met as a build-time analysis.

PILOT (now, q33, six seeds). Run on b2ckpt/B2_s200..s205 (2 blocks, 8 rounds, 9 registers, 200k skills rows). Label it 'q33 baseline, not the 8a shape'.
- Add off-by-default skip hooks inside the block loop at ledger.py:313, taking a set of (round, block) cells. The intact path must stay bit-identical.
- Cells, 2 blocks x 8 rounds: intact; skip block j in all rounds; skip j in rounds 0-3; skip j in rounds 4-7; skip both blocks in a half; scale one writer (o, p or out) of block j by 0.5, or drop half-strength; a null cell (intact with a tiny perturbation, e.g. writers x1.001, plus a re-run for noise); a fresh-init-block floor (replace block j with a same-init block); a positive control (skip all blocks, must read USED).
- Measures per cell:
  (a) free-running exact match on the dev in_dist rows (gold=None via generate()), with the paired flip count (McNemar);
  (b) teacher-forced loss in nats per token with a row-bootstrap CI, with op CE, pointer NLL, mode CE and answer CE reported separately and the total;
  (c) chain-5 exact;
  (d) the same measures on rows where loops:0 is wrong but intact is right (the rows that depend on rounds);
  (e) update norm over per-round state RMS, descriptive only.
- Reproduction check. Use an in-machine intact reference run in the same precision as training (bf16 autocast on the PC GPU, or fp32 on both sides). Compare to RESULT.json only as a sanity check with a 1.0-point cross-machine tolerance, and report the flip count against the RESULT.json number. Stop only if the gap is above 1.5 points. Match files to seeds by reproduction, never by in_dist value alone. Optionally run the PC once with --save-preds for a row-level match.
- Marks, fixed now (suggested). A block-cell is IDLE on a seed if the skip flips under 1% of rows (fewer than 14 of 1,360) and the nats change sits inside the null CI. It is USED if the skip flips at least 5% of rows (at least 68 of 1,360). Otherwise it is UNCLEAR. A block is IDLE only if IDLE on at least 5 of 6 seeds and also IDLE under the pair and cumulative skips. Label all of this 'shown on 6 seeds, q33 only'.
- A positive control that does not read USED, or a null that flips more than 1%, voids the probe.

CONDITIONAL PART (8-block and 8a-shape checkpoints).
- Step 0, ask Ben: does result.tgz for first-look B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 contain checkpoint.pt? If yes, run the census with 8-round halves (0-3, 4-7) as a labelled 2-seed screen, adding pair skips for the three lowest-cost blocks (35 cells + pairs) and an init-scale note (2-block writer std 0.00289 vs 8-block 0.00144). If no, do not re-run B2D just for this and make no 8-block claim.
- Step 1, add checkpoint.pt (with sha256) to the collection list for every 8a B2 run that uses --out: the 3M seeds 401-405 if the tgz still exists on a live box, and the 10M deep arm (8 blocks) seeds 400-405. 8a runs have 12 rounds, so use halves 0-5 and 6-11 and do not compare with the 8-round numbers.
- No new --usage-every logger in the sealed 8a build. The census is run post hoc on collected checkpoints, which needs no addendum or bit-identity check.

DECISION USE.
- A census result can slow or stop the 30M rung as a screen. It cannot choose a new width or block count without a dated addendum.
- USED cannot justify ordering 30M, because skipping biases toward USED. The ordering gate stays the 8a marks: 10M minus 3M of at least +3.0 on 6 paired seeds with CI above 0, and the stop rule that no 30M follows if 10M minus 3M is below 0.
- If the 10M gain is under +3: late blocks IDLE on at least 5 of 6 seeds means depth-only growth is not being used, so re-think the growth axis (width or data) as a screen. Blocks USED but no gain means run the quarter-pool data diagnostic first.
- IDLE-call validation: retrain with one block removed, same width and data, on 2 screen seeds (about 2 h). The IDLE call is withdrawn if removing the block loses 3.0 or more pooled-5 on both seeds. Run this only if a block is called IDLE.
- Drop the 'late rounds IDLE means test the stop head' branch. It is a separate deploy-time halting idea that must be designed autonomously (the model decides from answer-free signals, constants fixed and the same every night).

Strip or gate the skip hooks out of the shipped build.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. Order of work. Run the six-seed 2-block pilot first, time one cell before accepting the 1.5 h estimate, and report it as the q33 baseline (8 rounds, 9 registers, 200k rows), not the 8a shape.
2. Reproduction gate. Use an in-machine intact reference at training precision. A 0.05-point tolerance is below one row, since 1,360 rows make one row 0.074 points, so it fails by construction. Report the flip count against RESULT.json. Use a 1.0-point sanity tolerance and a 1.5-point stop. Do not match seeds by in_dist value.
3. Primary measures. Use free-running exact match with paired flip counts, plus loss reported by component (op, pointer, mode, answer) with bootstrap CIs. Teacher-forced total loss alone hides op-choosing blocks. Add a null cell, a fresh-block floor and a skip-all positive control.
4. Marks fixed in advance.
   - IDLE: under 1% flips and inside the null CI.
   - USED: at least 5% flips.
   - Otherwise UNCLEAR.
   - A block counts as IDLE only if IDLE on at least 5 of 6 seeds and also under pair and cumulative skip.
   - Wrong-result clause: an IDLE call is withdrawn if removing the block (1-block retrain, same width and data, 2 screen seeds) loses 3.0 or more on both.
5. Checkpoint availability. Do not assume the 8-block checkpoints exist. Ask Ben whether result.tgz for B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 contains checkpoint.pt, and add checkpoint.pt (with sha256) to the collection list for the 8a 10M deep arm (seeds 400-405) and any live 3M B2 runs. The 8a runs already pass --out, so the file only has to be named when collected.
6. Rounds. Define rounds halves per rung and never compare across them. Use 0-3 and 4-7 for 8-round models, and 0-5 and 6-11 for 12-round 8a models.
7. Keep the decision narrow. A census only informs the shape and growth-axis choice for 30M as a screen. USED never justifies spending 4-5 days, only the 8a marks do. A change to the 30M shape needs a dated addendum. The 8-block census is a 2-seed screen under rule 4.
8. No changes to the sealed 8a build. No usage logger, only a post-hoc census. Hooks are inert when off and are stripped from the shipped build. No automatic step may read census output.
9. For Ben (a high-school senior), write a plain-language summary. The idea asks whether the extra layers do any work, by turning each one off and seeing whether answers get worse. Explain that 'turning off barely matters' is a clue, not proof, and that the real proof is retraining without the layer.
10. Label all claims shown, suggested or untested. Separate the small-card B2 claims from the village model.
11. Offer an outside prompt for Astra (read-only, no edits, tests, training or GPU) if the pilot gives a surprising result, for example a block that is idle on some seeds and used on others.

plan.title: Block-use census for the six q33 B2 checkpoints
plan.ben_line: We switch off one of B2's two thinking layers at a time, on models we already trained, and check whether its answers change. If almost nothing changes, that is a clue the layer may not be needed, not proof; only training a model without that layer can show it.
plan.question: On the six saved q33 B2 checkpoints (2 controller blocks, 8 rounds), does skipping each block, or one half of the rounds, change answers by more than the probe's own noise, and do the controls show the probe can tell a real change from none?
plan.one_change: At test time only, skip one controller block (or one half of the 8 rounds) on each saved checkpoint. Weights, training, data, scoring and the answer path stay unchanged.
arms: C0 intact: reproduction reference only; must match the PC RESULT.json (M0), not a result
C1 precision null: intact in fp32 versus bf16 autocast; sets the numerical noise floor. Replaces the brief's x1.001 writer scaling, which bf16 may round to no change (suggested, untested)
C2 skip block 0 in all 8 rounds; C3 skip block 1 in all 8 rounds
C4 skip block 0 in rounds 0-3; C5 skip block 0 in rounds 4-7
C6 skip block 1 in rounds 0-3; C7 skip block 1 in rounds 4-7
C8 skip both blocks in rounds 0-3; C9 skip both blocks in rounds 4-7

C10 block 0 replaced by a fresh block with the same init rule (ledger.py:160), all rounds; C11 the same for block 1. Descriptive only: residual writers start near 0.003, so these may look like skips (suggested)
C12 positive control: skip both blocks in all 8 rounds; must read USED (M2)
Dropped on purpose: half-strength writer cells (the question is removability, not scaling) and the rounds-dependent subset (almost every correct in_dist row depends on rounds, so it adds nothing)

Conditional 8-block screen (only if checkpoint.pt was kept; first-look seeds 200 and 201): intact; precision null; each block all-round and in two halves (24); both blocks in each half (2); fresh block (8, descriptive); skip-all control (1); pre-set adjacent pairs 0-1, 3-4, 6-7 (3); pre-set prefixes 0-1, 0-3, 0-5 (3). About 43 cells. Pairs are not chosen by single-skip cost, which would bias toward IDLE.
Conditional 8a 3M B2 (12 rounds, 36 registers; seeds 401, 402, 405 are in the snapshot but their checkpoints are not): halves 0-5 and 6-11, only with the 8a build code and a settled answer cap
plan.seeds: Pilot: q33 seeds 200-205 (six). Match each checkpoint file to its seed by the 1,000-row chain-5 flag pattern in RESULT.json, never by folder name or in_dist total (seeds 202 and 204 differ by only 2 in_dist rows: 1,221 and 1,219, shown). Retrain screen, only if a block is called IDLE: seeds 200 and 201. Conditional 8-block: first-look seeds 200 and 201 (2-seed screen, only if checkpoints were kept). 8a 3M B2 seeds 401, 402 and 405 appear in the snapshot without checkpoints.
plan.machine: BensPC (RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GB): forward passes only, small memory, can share the card with the queue. Copy the six b2ckpt folders to the PC and check each checkpoint.pt.sha256 first (all six match here, shown). Use the PC's own data folders named in the q33 RESULT configs (data and data_big). Not the Mac, because the gate needs CUDA bf16 as in train.py:132. Not a rented box.
pass_marks: M0 Reproduction (C0, PC, bf16, eval batch 128): each checkpoint's chain-5 per-row flags match RESULT chain5.intact.hits on at least 995 of 1,000 rows, and its in_dist total is within 13 rows (about 1.0 point) of final_eval. Warn at 14-20 rows off. Stop at 21 or more rows off (about 1.5 points) or more than 5 chain-5 mismatches. Report the 34 in_dist family counts without gating on them. The cross-machine tolerance is not the test here: the first-look box was 13 and 9 in_dist rows off the PC for seeds 200 and 201 (shown in readout.json and RESULT.json), so a PC run should sit much closer.

M1 Precision null (C1): on every seed, at most 13 of 1,360 in_dist rows, 13 of 1,320 variant rows and 10 of 1,000 chain-5 rows change. More than that means the probe is void. If the precision null already sits above this band, report void rather than loosen the band (suggested).

M2 Positive control (C12): on every seed, at least 68 of 1,360 in_dist rows (5 percent) change. Fewer means the probe is void. Most rows should flip, because the q33 loops:0 lesion (no rounds) leaves in_dist at 0-10.8 percent (shown in q33 RESULT lesions, per the brief).

M3 Cell call per seed: IDLE if in_dist flips are at most 13, variant at most 13 and chain-5 at most 10, and the paired 95 percent row-bootstrap CIs of the change in total nats and in op CE both include 0. USED if any panel has at least 68 in_dist, 66 variant or 50 chain-5 flips. Otherwise UNCLEAR. The variant and chain-5 conditions are added to the brief's in_dist-only rule to close the false-IDLE gap (suggested).

M4 Block call over six seeds: IDLE only if the all-round skip and both half skips are each IDLE on at least 5 of 6 seeds. USED if the all-round skip is USED on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Otherwise UNCLEAR. With two blocks the pair cell is the positive control, so the brief's 'IDLE under pair' rule cannot apply. If both blocks are IDLE singly while C12 is USED, neither is called IDLE (joint use).
M5 Mixed pattern: a block IDLE on some seeds and USED on others is reported as UNCLEAR and triggers the outside-prompt step. It is not called either way.

M6 Wrong-result check: an IDLE call is withdrawn if the 1-block retrain (width 256, q33 data, 24,000 updates, same recipe) scores at least 3.0 pooled-5 points below its paired q33 two-block result on both seeds 200 and 201 (paired values 73.00 and 74.27, shown from RESULT.json).
M7 Conditional 8-block and 8a: same cell rules; labelled a 2-seed screen (rule 4); pairs and prefixes fixed in advance; 8a checkpoints read only after the answer cap is settled (rule 7).
plan.proved_wrong: Proved wrong: an IDLE call (M4) that passes the cell rules but costs at least 3.0 pooled-5 points when the block is removed and the model retrained at the same width and data, on both screen seeds 200 and 201 (M6). Proved invalid, which is different from wrong: C1 flips above 1% (M1), C12 flips under 5% (M2), or the reproduction gate stops (M0). A USED call proves nothing about need, because skipping biases toward USED, so the census can only suggest that a block is unneeded; only the retrain can test that.
plan.null_risk: Partly. Two no-change failures are caught by the controls: a hook that does nothing makes every block IDLE and fails C12 (M2), and a hook that breaks the forward flips the precision null past 1% and voids the run (M1). The live risk is a false IDLE: a block whose work sits in rows outside in_dist, variant and chain-5 (the answer, frame and vocab splits, or the 160-row family split, per the brief) still passes M3. Skip-testing also measures reliance inside one trained model, not usefulness, so an IDLE call is only a hint until the M6 retrain. The chance of a false IDLE is not measurable here (untested). A separate risk: the 1% band may sit inside bf16 numerical noise. If C1 flips more than 13 in_dist rows, the probe should be reported void, not loosened (suggested).
plan.autonomy: Build-time analysis only (rule 10). The census is a developer script that runs on saved weights after training. No step of it runs in the deployed model's answer path. The skip argument defaults to off and is stripped from the shipped build. Every choice (cells, halves, pairs, marks, checkpoints) is fixed before the run. Nothing the deployed model does changes because of it. A later change to the 30M block count would be a build-time architecture choice, logged in a dated addendum, and the 8a marks would still be read on their sealed panels. Caveat: the census reads dev rows, so its output must stay out of any runtime value. The dropped 'late rounds idle, so test a stop head' branch is a deploy-time method and is not part of this plan; if it returns, it needs an autonomous design (answer-free signals, fixed constants) and its own test. The census measures B2 with its hand parts still in (regex spans and the in-forward int64 executor, shown in ledger.py), so block use may not carry over to the T1 calculator-as-tool design (suggested, untested).
steps: 1. Ask Ben before any conditional compute. (a) Does result.tgz for first-look B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 hold checkpoint.pt? The snapshot has only RESULT.json, rc.txt, stdout.events.txt and result.tgz.sha256 (shown), and the boxes are destroyed once results are collected (FIRST-LOOK-10M-2026-10-07.md lines 64-65, shown). (b) Did the 8a boxes keep checkpoint.pt for seeds 401, 402 and 405? The 8a B2 command passes --out (shown in 8a-3M-s401-box/box.json). Future 8a collection should name checkpoint.pt with its sha256.

2. Copy the six q33 checkpoints to the PC and verify each against its .sha256 (all six match here, shown). Load each with models/__init__.py load_model and check step = 24000 and cfg = {copy: true}. The checkpoint stores no seed (train.py:201 saves model, name, cfg, chars and step only), so seed identity comes from the chain-5 match in step 5.

3. Before editing, save the intact outputs of the unedited Ledger on one fixed batch (R, vals, lmode, lans, lword, loss). Then add the off-by-default skip argument to run() and the check in the block loop (ledger.py:313-314), so a skipped block is passed over for listed (round, block) pairs. The default path must reproduce the saved tensors exactly (equality, not a tolerance). Use the PC copy of the code that produced the q33 RESULT files: the FIRST-LOOK note says ledger.py, train.py and data.py are unchanged from 085431a7f (shown).

4. Write probe_census.py (new file). Per-row predictions come from the same path eval_all uses (train.py:72-73, return_preds) with the free-running generate (base.py:50-58, gold None). Teacher-forced components use the loss code's own pieces: op CE (ledger.py:507) and pointer NLL (510-513) reported separately (the aux dict at 527 adds them together), plus mode (517), answer and word pointers (518) and GEN (526), total at 531. Report each in the units the code uses (op per step, pointer per row, GEN per target token, ledger.py:519), not one 'nats per token' scale. Op CE on rows without a gold program gets weight 0.1 (ledger.py:501), so report op CE on program rows separately.

5. Reproduction gate M0 on the PC, C0 only, with bf16 autocast on CUDA as in train.py:132 and eval batch 128 as in the RESULT configs. Match each checkpoint to its RESULT.json by the 1,000-row chain-5 flag pattern (chain5.intact.hits has 1,000 per-row 0/1 flags summing to 994 for seed 200, shown). Also record the in_dist total and the 34 per-family counts. Run C0 twice to measure run-to-run noise. If M0 stops, end the pilot here and report it.
6. Time one cell (C0 on seed 200): seconds and peak memory. Update the hours figure before the full run.
7. Run the controls first on all six seeds: C1 (precision null) and C12 (skip both blocks, all rounds). If M1 or M2 fails, stop and report the probe as void. Do not read any block cell first.

8. Run C2 to C11 on all six seeds. Save per-row 0/1 flags for in_dist (1,360), variant (1,320) and chain-5 (1,000), McNemar exact two-sided paired counts, the teacher-forced components, and the paired 2,000-resample row-bootstrap CIs. Use only dev panels (in_dist, variant, chain-5), the same dev panels the q33 RESULT files score; no GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected panel (rule 5).
9. Apply M3 per seed and M4 per block. Report each block's seed-by-seed pattern. Any mixed pattern (IDLE on some seeds, USED on others) is UNCLEAR under M5 and triggers step 13.

10. If any block is IDLE under M4, run the wrong-result check M6: train a 1-block model at width 256 on the q33 data, same recipe, 24,000 updates, seeds 200 and 201. Budget about 0.5 to 0.8 hours each (suggested, from the first-look B2 train_h of 0.78 h, shown). Withdraw the IDLE call under M6 if it applies.

11. Write the outputs to a new results folder (do not overwrite RESULT.json). Label every output 'q33 small-card B2; 8 rounds; 9 registers; six seeds; descriptive; not the 8a shape; not the village model'. Mark each claim shown (with its file), suggested or untested.

12. Conditional, only if step 1 says yes: run first-look B2D seeds 200 and 201 as a 2-seed screen with the 43-cell set (8-round halves 0-3 and 4-7, pre-set pairs and prefixes). Note the init scale: the residual writer std is 0.002887 at 2 blocks x 8 rounds and 0.001443 at 8 x 8 (ledger.py:160, arithmetic shown). The 8a 3M B2 checkpoints (12 rounds, 36 registers) need the 8a build code, which is not in this snapshot (ledger.py:62 has N_REG = 9; the 8a box caps have n_reg 36, shown). The 8a RESULT config says max_ans 35 while the command passes --max-ans 8 (shown), so settle the answer cap (rule 7) before reading any 8a census.

13. Surprise rule: if a block is IDLE on some seeds and USED on others, or a control sits near its line, write a read-only prompt for Astra, save it under reviews/ and give it to Ben (Claude cannot message Astra). The prompt forbids edits, tests, training and GPU use. It asks for shown, suggested and untested labels, a plain-language summary for Ben, one change at a time, marks M0 to M7 fixed in advance, and the q33 small-card B2 kept apart from the village model.

14. Before any shipped build: remove the skip argument and probe code from the forward pass; no runtime path reads census output; any change to the 30M block count is a build-time choice logged in a dated addendum; the 8a marks are read on their sealed panels, not on the dev rows that informed the choice.

plan.confirm: The pilot is six seeds, q33 only, and is a descriptive census (rule 4). An IDLE call is confirmed only by the M6 retrain on seeds 200 and 201, a screen of roughly 1 to 1.5 hours in total (suggested). A claim that the 30M block count can change needs six paired seeds of the depth comparison at 3M, about 6 hours (suggested), and a dated addendum. The conditional 8-block census (about 43 cells, about 1 hour, suggested) is a 2-seed screen and needs six seeds before any claim. Extra hours not in the 2.5 figure: about 1 hour for the conditional 8-block screen, and about 1 hour per retrain.

issues: Stale premise on machine and status: the plan says 8a runs on BensPC and that the 3M rung is not rented. The 8a 3M rung already ran on rented 5090s for seeds 401, 402 and 405 (8a-results/8a-3M-s40x-*/RESULT.json and box.json; box cost_usd 0.674; addenda H and I of 8A-SPEC). The orchestrator's line that 8a runs on the home PC and not rented GPUs is wrong (shown). Only .sha256 files for those boxes are in the snapshot, so whether any checkpoint.pt survived is unknown (shown).

Conditional deep stages are probably dead on arrival: the first-look B2D folders hold only RESULT.json, rc.txt, stdout.events.txt and result.tgz.sha256, and its box was destroyed after collection (FIRST-LOOK Amendment 2, shown). The 8-block census, which is the only piece that bears on the 30M block count, depends on those checkpoints.

Dev leakage that step 14 denies: step 14 says the 8a marks are read on sealed panels, not on the dev rows that informed the choice. 8A-SPEC section 7 says the marks are pooled-5 = dev in_dist, answer, frame, vocab and variant (shown). The census scores in_dist and variant (and chain-5, the 8a guard). Choosing the 30M block count from that output and then scoring 30M on the same dev rows leaks into the marks. Rule 5 bars reserved and blind panels, so the only clean route is fresh generator rows after the protected-hash merge (DATA-POOL-PLAN section 6; PROTECTED-HASH-JOB), or fixing the 30M shape in a dated addendum before any census output is read.

Wrong shape: the census measures q33 B2 (2 blocks, 8 rounds, 9 registers, 27 slots; ledger.py:62 N_CTRL, N_REG = 8, 9). The 8a B2 at 3M runs 12 rounds, 36 registers and 106 slots (8a box.json b2_extra n_loops 12, caps n_reg 36; addendum G). A 2-block result cannot inform the 30M choice, which is 9 blocks at mlp 6.0 or 11 at mlp 4.8 (shown, recounted: 985,273 non-block + 1,158,604 per d=256 block gives 3,302,481 at 2 blocks and 10,254,105 at 8; 2,016,185 + 9 x 2,957,952 = 28,637,753 at width 384).

Code-version premise is unproven: the plan says the PC code is unchanged from 085431a7f (shown). That git-diff claim is about the first-look branch, not the q33 runs. In the snapshot's history, ledger.py (257 changed lines), train.py (50), reader.py (31), evalx.py (37) and data.py (7) changed after the queue-33 commit 883663c55 (git diff --stat 883663c55 HEAD, shown). The default B2 path looks unchanged (new flags default off; data.set_max_ans defaults to 8), but the commit that produced the q33 RESULTs is not identified. M0 is the only check, so it must name that commit.

The IDLE test has no equivalence margin: M6 withdraws IDLE only if a 1-block retrain drops at least 3.0 pooled-5 on both seeds 200 and 201. That is a superiority test on two seeds. A block worth 2.9 points still counts as IDLE, and 3.0 is exactly 8a's per-rung mark. Showing a block is not needed needs an equivalence test (90% paired CI inside a fixed margin, here 1.0) on six seeds (rule 4).

Split coverage: M3 checks only in_dist, variant and chain-5. Answer (1,200 rows), frame (1,360) and vocab (800) are part of pooled-5 and the 8a marks but are not checked. A block that serves only answer or vocab would be called IDLE.

Loose and mis-derived tolerances: the 13-row M0 tolerance comes from comparing two different training runs on different hardware (PC seed 200 in_dist 1,231 correct vs first-look box 1,218; PC seed 201 1,245 vs 1,236; shown). That is training variation, not evaluation reproduction; the same checkpoint on the same code should match within a few rows. The M1 precision band (13 flips, about 1%) is the same loose number and may sit inside bf16 noise, which would void every cell.

Units: M3 uses 'change in total nats', but step 4 says the loss parts are in different units (op CE per step, pointer NLL per row, GEN per target token; ledger.py:519, 531). Their sum is not one nats measure. Use per-part CIs or one defined per-row answer NLL.

Zero-skip is biased toward USED: removing a Pre-LN residual block (ledger.py CBlock.forward) pushes the residual stream off distribution, so almost any block will look used, which the plan admits. Mean-ablation (replace the block's residual update by its average over training rows) is the standard fix. Training rows, not dev rows, should set the average.

Hours sit in the wrong place: the forward-only cells are cheap. The q33 runs' final eval plus its 11 lesion sweeps took 36 to 158 s per run (RESULT.json wall_s minus train_s; shown). So the 42-cell q33 pilot and the 43-cell 8-block set are minutes of forward time per seed. The real cost is the six 1-block retrains (0.5 to 0.8 h each solo, suggested; q33 seed 200 took 3.66 h on the shared PC, shown).

Wrong reference for precision: cells compare bf16 ablations with bf16 intact, while C1 is fp32 intact. Run the census cells in fp32, measure deltas against fp32 intact, and keep bf16 only for the M0 reproduction (q33 config: bf16 true, eval_batch 128, shown).

Ablation plumbing is under-specified: step 3 adds the skip only to run() (ledger.py:278-318). Evaluation reaches the model through state() and generate() (ledger.py:359-362; models/base.py:50-58), and loss() calls run() directly. If the skip is not threaded through all of them, cells silently equal intact. C12 would catch that, but only after the run. Add a unit check that a one-block skip changes the output tensors.

The first look's own pre-registered readout is unclear, not flat. Gains are +1.42 (seed 200) and -0.28 (seed 201); the lead over plain shrank by -1.31 and -2.47, beyond the -1.0 bound (readout.json verdict rows; shown). So neither the 'encouraging' nor the 'flat' rule holds. The census is motivated by a screen that did not pass its own rule.

Leak confound: the 8a 3M B2 has loops:0 in_dist of 12.06 and 14.26 on seeds 401 and 402, and 1.03 on 405 (8a RESULT lesions; shown). Rows answerable with no rounds can read as 'the block is idle' or distort flip counts. The census must report loops:0 rows separately.

8a answer-cap conflict: box.json's command for 8a-3M-s401-B2 passes --max-ans 8, while the RESULT config and the run's own caps event say max_ans 35 (stdout.events.txt; shown). fixed_plan.title: Descriptive block ablation on six q33 B2 checkpoints (reduced; later stages conditional)
fixed_plan.ben_line: We switch off one of B2's two thinking layers at a time, on models we already trained, and see whether its answers change. If almost nothing changes, that hints the layer may not be needed. Only training a model without that layer can prove it, and we do that only if the first check points that way.
fixed_plan.question: On the six saved q33 B2 checkpoints (2 blocks, 8 rounds), does removing one controller block, or replacing its work with its training-set average, change pooled-5 or chain-5 by more than 1.0 point (a margin fixed now), with the probe checked by controls and all deltas taken against fp32 intact?
fixed_plan.one_change: At test time only, replace one controller block's residual update for all 8 rounds, either with zero or with its training-set mean. Weights, training, data and scoring stay fixed. Nothing is retrained in Stage 1.
arms: A0 M0 reproduction (gate, not a result): intact, bf16, eval batch 128, per seed; compare with RESULT.json in_dist counts and chain5.intact.hits.
A1 intact in fp32: the reference for every delta and the precision null (M1).
A2 block 0 zero-ablated, all 8 rounds; A3 block 0 mean-ablated, all 8 rounds.
A4 block 1 zero-ablated, all 8 rounds; A5 block 1 mean-ablated, all 8 rounds.
A6 both blocks mean-ablated: the positive control (M2).
D1 descriptive only: residual-update norm divided by residual-stream norm, per block and per round, on dev rows. No pass or fail.
Mean references: per block and per round, the mean residual update over 1,000 q33 training rows drawn with a fixed seed. No dev row sets any constant.
fixed_plan.seeds: 200 to 205 (six), paired with the q33 RESULT.json files. Match each checkpoint to its seed by the chain-5 flags in M0, not by folder name alone.
fixed_plan.machine: BensPC RTX 5070 Ti, forward passes only. fp32 for A1 to A6, bf16 only for A0. Use the PC's original checkpoint.pt files in results/33-pc-confirm-b2 (the snapshot copies match their .sha256 files, shown). Record the commit the PC used for queue 33, identified before the run (not assumed to be 085431a7f).
pass_marks: M0 reproduction gate (bf16, six seeds): in_dist correct count within 3 rows of RESULT final_eval (seed 200: 1,231; 201: 1,245; 202: 1,221; 203: 1,238; 204: 1,219; 205: 1,233), and chain-5 per-row flags match chain5.intact.hits on at least 995 of 1,000 rows. If it fails, stop, bisect commits with M0 on seed 200 (seconds per evaluation), and run no ablation until M0 passes.
M1 precision null: fp32 intact minus bf16 intact pooled-5 is within 1.0 point on every seed. Otherwise the probe is void and no block call is made.

M2 positive control: A6 (both blocks mean-ablated) drops pooled-5 by at least 15 points on every seed (suggested; the q33 noexec lesion drops in_dist about 38 points, shown). Otherwise the probe is void, which also catches a skip that never reached evaluation.

M3 per block and per mode (zero, mean), on six-seed paired deltas vs A1 in fp32: CANDIDATE IDLE only if, for both modes, the 90% paired t-interval of the mean delta lies inside (-1.0, +1.0) for both pooled-5 and chain-5, and no split (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab, variant, held-out family) has a six-seed mean delta below -2.0. USED if either mode's 90% interval for pooled-5 or chain-5 lies entirely below -1.0. Otherwise UNCLEAR. Per-split deltas are reported in full.

M4 Stage 2 (only if at least one block is CANDIDATE IDLE, and only with Ben's OK on compute): six 1-block retrains at width 256 on the q33 data, same recipe, 24,000 updates, paired by seed with the q33 two-block RESULTs. NOT NEEDED at this size if the 90% interval of (2-block minus 1-block) paired pooled-5 lies inside (-1.0, +1.0) and the chain-5 interval does too. NEEDED if the interval lies entirely above +1.0. Otherwise UNCLEAR. This is one 3M recipe on one dataset, and it is not size-matched (the removed block carries about 1.16M parameters).

M5 Stage 3 (conditional on surviving checkpoints; two seeds, a screen only): the same cells for each block of the first-look 8-block checkpoints, or the 8a 3M 12-round checkpoints if kept. No 30M block count is chosen from it unless the shape is fixed in a dated addendum before any readout, and the 30M marks are re-scored on fresh rows after the protected-hash merge (rule 5 bars reserved and blind panels).
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: A block called CANDIDATE IDLE whose Stage 2 retrain shows the 2-block model ahead by more than 1.0 with the 90% interval entirely above +1.0 (the call was wrong). Also, if M1 or M2 fails, every block call is void. A two-seed Stage 3 screen cannot prove a 30M block count, so any such claim is wrong until six seeds exist.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Zero and mean ablation are both out of distribution, so the probe is biased toward USED and can miss a block that matters only on rare rows. Two redundant blocks can each look idle at test time while both help in training; only Stage 2 partly catches this. Stage 2 is one 3M recipe on one dataset and is not size-matched. Untested: how often redundancy hides use, and whether a q33 result transfers to the 12-round, 36-register 8a shape at all.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Build-time analysis only (rule 10). It runs on saved weights and changes nothing in the deployed model. The mean references come from q33 training rows, fixed before the run. All thresholds are fixed now and no runtime value is tuned on dev rows. Any change to the shipped block count is a build-time choice recorded in a dated addendum before the 30M marks are read. The skip argument is removed from the forward pass before any shipped build. The learned-stop branch stays out.
steps: 1. Ask Ben one question: did the first-look B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 checkpoint.pt files, and the 8a-3M s401, s402 and s405 checkpoint.pt files, survive in their result.tgz archives? The snapshot holds only .sha256 files (shown). Also settle the 8a answer cap: box.json says --max-ans 8, while the RESULT config and the caps event say 35. Only the conditional stages wait on the first answer.
2. On the PC, identify the commit that ran queue 33 from that machine's git log. Check it out in a separate worktree for the probe and record its hash in the results. Do not assume 085431a7f.
3. Hash-check the PC's original results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200..205/checkpoint.pt against the six .sha256 files. Use the PC originals; no copy step.

4. Write probe_ablation.py (new, PC only). Thread an off-by-default ablation argument through run(), state(), generate() and loss(). Add a unit check that a one-block skip changes the output tensors on one batch, and that the default path reproduces saved tensors exactly.
5. Build the mean references once per seed from 1,000 q33 training rows with a fixed seed. No dev row is used.
6. Run A0 (intact, bf16) on six seeds and apply M0. If it fails, stop and bisect the commit (M0 on seed 200 only); run no ablation until it passes.
7. Run A1 (fp32 intact) and apply M1. Run A6 and apply M2. If either fails, report the probe as void and stop.
8. Run A2 to A5 in fp32 on six seeds. Compute deltas against A1, apply M3, and report per-split deltas and the family split.
9. Compute D1 (norm ratios per block and round on dev rows). Report only.
10. If any block is CANDIDATE IDLE, ask Ben for compute for Stage 2 (six 1-block retrains, about 3 to 6 hours solo, suggested). Run it only on Ben's OK, and apply M4.

11. If checkpoints survived (step 1), run M5 with the same cells on each block, labelled as a two-seed screen. Do not choose a 30M block count from it without a dated addendum written before any 30M readout.
12. Before any shipped build, remove the ablation argument from the forward pass.

13. Write outputs to a new results folder and do not overwrite RESULT.json. Label every output 'q33 small-card B2; 2 blocks; 8 rounds; 9 registers; six seeds; descriptive; not the 8a shape; not the village model', and label each claim shown, suggested or untested.
