A 30M block-count claim needs deep-shape evidence (8 or 9 to 11 blocks) on six seeds and a dated addendum fixed before the readout. None of that exists today.

final.why: The idea is rule-safe and cheap, about 1 forward-only hour (suggested, untimed). The six-seed census runs on the 2-block q33 checkpoints, which do exist (shown: code/b2ckpt). Only the 8-block checkpoints could inform the 30M shape, and the first-look B2D folders hold only RESULT.json, rc.txt, stdout.events.txt and result.tgz.sha256, so no checkpoint was collected (shown). With only 2 blocks, skipping one almost certainly reads USED, because zero- and mean-ablation are out-of-distribution (suggested, untested). So Stage 1 is unlikely to change any decision (guess about 10% or less), and the useful 8-block half waits on checkpoints that do not exist. Park it with one trigger: if the 8a 10M-minus-3M gain is under +3.0 on the 10M deep arm (seeds 400-405), run the 8-block census on its collected checkpoints as a labelled screen. The one thing to do now is nearly free and does not depend on this idea. Add checkpoint.pt plus its sha256 to the collection list for every 8a B2 run, because the 8a runs already pass --out (shown: box.json) but no collected folder holds a checkpoint.
final.ben_line: The idea is to turn off one of B2's thinking layers at a time and see if its answers get worse, but with only two layers that test will nearly always say "needed", so wait until the bigger 8-layer models are saved and test those instead.
plan_fixes: Stage 1 is on 2 blocks and cannot inform the 8 to 11 block question behind the 30M shape. Either fold it into the 8-block census (run only when checkpoints exist) or label it a controls-and-tooling rehearsal. Do not present it as evidence about depth (suggested).

Checkpoints are not collected: first-look B2D_s200 and B2D_s201 have no checkpoint.pt or tgz in the folder (shown, ls). No collected 8a folder has one either. Add checkpoint.pt and its sha256 to the collection list for the 8a 10M deep arm (seeds 400-405) and any live 8a B2 box. Do not re-run B2D just for this: 8 blocks costs about 1.6 h per seed on the box, shown in readout.json train_h.

M0 tolerance of 3 in_dist rows is arbitrary. Run intact twice on the PC at training precision (bf16, eval batch 128) to measure run-to-run flips, then set the tolerance from that. Keep the chain-5 flag match of at least 995 of 1,000 for seed identity.

The mean reference for mean-ablation is underspecified. Say whether it is averaged per (round, controller token, channel) over the 1,000 fixed training rows, or over tokens too. Averaging over tokens would break the 8 control tokens and 9 register tokens, which play different roles (ledger.py lines 303-304 and 306-318). Also write down that zero- and mean-ablation both push the Pre-LN stream off distribution, so USED is the expected outcome (suggested).

The IDLE rule (90% interval inside +-1.0 on pooled-5 and chain-5, six seeds) is the right shape. Chain-5 sits near 99.5, so a ceiling effect can make almost anything look IDLE there; require the pooled-5 interval and the per-split floor of -2.0 to carry the call.

Report loops:0 leak rows separately. B2 at q33 seeds 201 and 203 already answer 5.66 to 10.8% of in_dist with no rounds (shown, RESULT.json lesions), and the 8a 3M B2 leak is 12.06 and 14.26 on seeds 401 and 402 (Haiku red team, not re-checked by me). Those rows can read as a block being idle.

Dev-row reuse: choosing a 30M block count from census output on pooled-5 dev splits and then scoring 30M on the same splits leaks into the marks. Fix the 30M shape in a dated addendum before any readout, or rescore on fresh generator rows after the protected-hash merge. A 2-seed 8-block screen cannot choose a shape under rule 4.

Stage 2 (six 1-block retrains) is real compute, about 3 to 6 GPU hours (suggested), and the only part that can show a block is not needed. Run it only on Ben's OK and only if a block reads CANDIDATE IDLE. The equivalence margin of 1.0 on six seeds is correct. The earlier 3.0-on-two-seeds withdrawal rule should stay dropped.

Settle the 8a answer-cap conflict separately, since it matters more than this idea. The 8a box.json commands pass --max-ans 8 while the B2 RESULT.json config says max_ans 35 (shown by grep; I did not read train.py in the 8a build). If 8 was used, targets were cut (rule 7). Do not probe 8a checkpoints until it is settled.

Identify the exact commit that ran queue 33 on the PC before running M0. Do not assume 085431a7f, which is the first-look branch base. The census must also use fp32 deltas against fp32 intact, with bf16 only for M0.

Keep the ablation argument off by default, thread it through run(), state(), generate() and loss(), add a unit check that a one-block skip changes the tensors, and strip it before any shipped build. No automatic step may read census output (rule 10).

idea.title: Spelling gate: can B2 write 9-12 letter cloze answers?
idea.summary: The 62% web share asks B2 to spell blanked words of 3-12 letters, mostly absent from the prompt, with a parallel one-character-per-register generator that today caps answers at 8 letters and cuts longer ones silently. Run a no-training audit of GEN spelling on existing checkpoints, then a 2,000-update pilot on a closed set of 200 frequent 9-12 letter words before any 8a rung is started.
idea.change: Step 0 (CPU): run B2_s100/s101 (or b2ckpt) on answer-split rows of word_filter, seq_next, digits_parity, fewshot_number_rule, table_lookup, list_stats, order_chain; per wrong row record edit distance to gold, whether gold occurs in the prompt, answer length. Step 1: pilot 2 seeds x 2,000 updates with N_REG=13 and GEN_MAX=12 (13 registers fit the existing 16-row place table; only the constant in ledger.py line 62 changes) and an assert in gold() that fails instead of cutting; train on web cloze rows whose blank is one of 200 frequent 9-12 letter words, test on held-out docs with the same words; control set of 200 frequent 3-8 letter words in the same job. Closed vocabulary tests spelling, not prediction. 0 params beyond the 8a shape.
idea.why: GEN decodes each register in parallel with no conditioning on earlier output characters, answers are cut at GEN_MAX=8, and about 10.4% of 3-12 letter blank positions are 9-12 letters (about 40% if length is drawn uniformly; the spec is ambiguous). If long words break, the 62% web share cannot train and the 9-hour 3M rung fails for a reason unrelated to size.

evidence.claim: GEN_MAX = N_REG - 1 = 8; gold() cuts answers to GEN_MAX silently; train.py skips the max_ans check for B2.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: N_REG=13 (12 letters plus EOS) fits the 16-row place table with no new parameters; the 36 registers of addendum G need N_PLACE of at least 36 (+5,120 params) or the gather fails.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Blank-length share on slice_rung3: 3-8 letters 89.6%, 9-12 letters 10.4%; 28.4% of 3-12 letter blanks repeat elsewhere in the chunk (30.2% for 3-8, 12.5% for 9-12).
evidence.label: shown
evidence.source: streaming measurement of web_slices_8a.tgz by w2f ideas (my packing rule, not cloze.py)

evidence.claim: Answer-split means (six seeds): word_filter 0.0 with copy gate 0.00006; seq_next 30.4 (GEN 100%); fewshot_number_rule 28.3; table_lookup 20.4. cipher_map (GEN-only, 8 letters) scores 39-40 of 40 in_dist, so short spelling works.
evidence.label: shown
evidence.source: custom_io/results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json final_eval and extra.copy_gate, extra.coverage

test.where: Step 0 on Mac or PC CPU (torch needed); step 1 on BensPC after the speed probe and before any 8a rung
test.arms: Step 0: B2_s100, B2_s101. Step 1: B2 with N_REG 13 on the 200-word 9-12 letter closed set plus 3-8 letter control, seeds 410 and 411
test.pass_mark: Step 1 passes if held-out 9-12 letter exact is at least 25% and length-right share at least 80% (2-seed mean) and 3-8 letter exact at least 40%. Step 0 reads: spelling limit if 60% or more of wrong answer-split GEN answers are within edit distance 1; value limit if under 30%.
test.proved_wrong: 9-12 letter exact under 10% and length-right under 50%, or under half the 3-8 letter exact: the parallel generator cannot carry long words, so do not start the 3M rung; test the GRU decoder. Step 0: under 30% within edit distance 1 means misses are wrong values and a spelling fix would not move the answer split.

idea.rules_check: Rule 7: the assert makes any cut an error, the opposite of the silent cut. Rule 2: human web text. Rule 5: test docs from a slice with overlap13 checked; no protected panel. Rule 4: pilot, not a claim. Rule 10: n/a; the generator is the model's own.
idea.closest_prior: 8A-SPEC section 4 names the problem and its risk list mentions it, but no test is planned; the G build raises registers to 36 without a spelling check.
idea.autonomy: Probe before shipping. At deploy the talker spells with its own registers; no outside step.
idea.director_note: This is the largest unmeasured risk to the 8a web share and costs under 2 hours. Critics should check: the closed 200-word set might be solved by memorising words (so it overstates open spelling), the threshold values are suggested, and whether the 8a build (not in checkout) changes the register path. A pass does not show web cloze teaches skills.

problems: 1. Timing premise is false (shown). The idea gates the pilot 'before any 8a rung is started', but the 3M rung has already run: /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/8a-results/ holds status-ok RESULT.json files for 8a-3M-s401, s402 and s405 (B2, PT and LLM arms). s403 and s404 are not there yet. 8A-SPEC section 19 (addendum I, 4:35 PM ET) says the boxes started before any 3M result. A spelling check can now only be a post-hoc audit of a finished rung.

2. The 13-register pilot is not the 8a shape (shown). The sealed 3M B2 runs 36 registers, 12 rounds and max_ans 35 (8a-3M-s401-pool/caps.json: n_reg 36, max_ans 35; 8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json: n_loops 12, max_ans 35, n_params 3,346,513). 8A-SPEC addendum G (section 17) requires the 36 registers. The idea's '0 params beyond the 8a shape' and 'only the constant in ledger.py line 62 changes' are wrong. 36 registers need N_PLACE raised from 16 (reader.py:13) to 36, and the 8a count is 44,032 above q33 (3,302,481). N_REG is also read at ledger.py:303 (register slice) and ledger.py:437 (gen target width), so this is not a one-line change. A 13-register pilot tests a different model.

3. Step 0 on the q33 checkpoints cannot test 9-12 letter answers (shown). q33 has 9 registers and GEN_MAX 8 (ledger.py:62-63), and gold() cuts answers at ledger.py:447. Any 9-12 letter answer is wrong by construction. The 8a 3M checkpoints are needed for that audit. Their result.tgz files are not in the snapshot (only result.tgz.sha256 files are present).

4. The Step 0 families are mostly not spelling tests (shown, from research/data.md). word_filter answers are counts 0-7 (line 41), and its answer split is the constant '2' on all 40 rows (line 50; design/design-B2.md:11 'word_filter answer split 0/40'). list_stats (line 15), seq_next (line 17) and fewshot_number_rule (line 36) have numeric answers. digits_parity (line 16) answers even/odd labels. order_chain (line 21) gives yes/no or names, and table_lookup (line 24) gives numbers or words. Under the idea's own rule, 'within edit distance 1' would count one wrong digit (2 vs 3) as a spelling error.

5. cipher_map is copy-driven, not vocabulary spelling (shown). RESULT.json extra.copy_gate for cipher_map is 0.99992 to 0.99998 on seeds 200-205 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s20N). copy_gate_eval (ledger.py:658-661) reports 1 minus the vocabulary gate, and its docstring says '1 = the register copies from the prompt'. So cipher_map's correct letters are copied from the prompt and say nothing about spelling unseen words from the vocabulary. The idea's six-seed answer-split means recompute as stated (word_filter 0.0, seq_next 30.42, fewshot 28.33, table_lookup 20.42), but they come from count and number families, not spelling.

6. The pilot tests memorisation, not spelling (reasoned). The idea trains and tests on the same 200 words ('held-out docs with the same words'), so a pass measures recall of 200 strings. The word list is hand-picked by a 'frequent' rule that the idea does not define. Rule 10 says a hand-picked practice set does not count as evidence of learning. A valid test needs disjoint words, for example 150 to train and 50 unseen 9-12 letter words with matched letter frequency.

7. WORD-mode hits come from a hand renderer (shown). In WORD mode the talker prints a hand-sliced prompt word (ledger.py:402-403, from word_spans; span defaults to False at ledger.py:130). The 8a copyable share is 27.9% of web rows (8a-3M-s401-pool/MANIFEST.json web.copyable_share 0.279, on slice_rung30). PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:36 already lists word slicing as a hand part. The spelling pass mark must count GEN-mode rows only and report WORD hits separately (rule 1). The idea does not mention rule 1.

8. The verdict bands leave gaps (shown in the idea text; reasoned). Pass: 9-12 exact at least 25%, length-right at least 80%, 3-8 exact at least 40%. Proved wrong: 9-12 exact under 10% and length-right under 50%. Between them (9-12 exact 10-25%, or length-right 50-80%) there is no verdict. Step 0 reads a spelling limit at 60% or more within edit distance 1 and a value limit under 30%, and says nothing for 30-60%. Rule 4 requires the outcome that would prove the claim wrong, so these bands must be closed before any run. The thresholds are suggested, not derived, and no baseline supports them.

9. No comparison arm (reasoned). The idea's concern is the parallel GEN decoder (ledger.py:385-390: gen_copy runs over all registers in one pass with no conditioning on earlier characters). No causal arm runs on the same rows, so a fail cannot be read as 'parallel decoding costs spelling'. The 8a PT and LLM arms exist for seeds 401, 402 and 405 on the same web rows (8A-SPEC section 4 'identical rows').

10. Budget mismatch (reasoned). The pilot runs 2,000 updates, while the rung runs at least 24,000 (8A-SPEC section 4 and addendum B1). A kill at 2,000 updates does not show failure at 24,000. Either run the pilot at 24,000 or log a curve at 2k, 8k and 24k.

11. Rule 5 is not established, and two documents disagree (shown). The idea says 'no protected panel' and 'overlap13 checked'. DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md section 6 says GOLD-PRIVATE and every reserved or blind panel are 'not yet cleared' and 'the pool must not be used for training until that merge is done'. 8A-SPEC addendum A1 (section 11, line 168) allows training before the check. The 8a 3M runs have already trained on the pool. Any held-out doc must pass the overlap13 check after the protected-hash merge (data-pool/PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md).

12. The closest-prior claim is overstated (shown). The idea says 8A-SPEC section 4 'names the problem' and has a risk list that mentions it. The spec contains no 'risk' section and no spelling or GEN test. The known dev-side cut is recorded at PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:59 (dev answers up to 12 characters cut to 8 and unanswerable, not in pooled-5; 5 of 160 family rows, 25 of 800 in the big dev build), and the idea does not cite it. The silent cut in q33 code is real (ledger.py:447; train.py:142-143 skips the guard for B2 because getattr returns args.max_ans). The 8a build removes it (8A-SPEC addenda E, E2 and G; caps.json max_ans 35).

13. The real gap is unmeasured (shown). No 8a 3M RESULT file has a cloze or web split. final_eval keys are in_dist, answer, frame, vocab, variant and family only (8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json). chair.reasons:
PLAN, but only as a rewritten idea. The original pilot and Step 0 should be cut, and all four critics are right on these points.

(1) The gate is late. Shown: whole-model-roadmap/8a-results/ holds finished 3M runs for seeds 401, 402 and 405 (B2, PT and LLM, all status ok). Their B2 runs already used the real 8a shape (stdout.events.txt 'caps' event: max_ans 35, n_reg 36; RESULT.json n_loops 12, n_params 3,346,513) and trained on the 38/62 web mix without breaking. Pooled-5 recomputed from RESULT.json: B2 73.21 / 74.14 / 71.42 (mean 72.92, versus q33 74.0), PT 66.23 / 66.42 / 66.14 (mean 66.26), LLM 47.9 / 48.7 / 42.0. B2's lead over PT is about +6.7. So 'long words break and the 3M rung fails' is no longer a live risk. The web rows did not stop the skills score. The open question is whether the 62% web share teaches B2 anything, and whether it is worth 13-14 h a seed at 30M (spec addendum I2/I3, about $42 for six seeds). Pooled-5 cannot answer that.

(2) Step 0 on the q33 / s100 checkpoints is dead. Shown: those checkpoints have 9 registers and GEN_MAX 8 (ledger.py:62-63), and LIMIT-COUNTS / PLAN-AND-MARKS line 59 say no train or pooled-5 dev answer is over 8 characters. Most of the named families have numeric answers, so 'edit distance 1' would count a one-digit value error as a spelling error. cipher_map's copy_gate of about 0.9999 is the stored mean of (1 - g), which means prompt copying (ledger.py copy_gate_eval docstring), so it does not show vocabulary spelling. word_filter is a count family. Drop both as evidence.

(3) The 13-register, 2,000-update, 200-word closed-set pilot is a different model from the 8a shape (36 registers, 12 rounds). Shown: N_PLACE would need to rise and the build adds 44,032 params. The pilot trains and tests on the same 200 words, so it measures memorisation, and a hand-picked word list is a practice set under rule 10. Cut it. The 8a 3M B2 run took 3,384 s for 24,000 updates on one 5090, so a real-shape rerun is cheap enough that a shortcut shape is not needed.

(4) The stake is smaller than written, and the arithmetic needs correcting. The critics reproduced it on a 6 MB prefix of slice_rung3 (suggested; cloze.py is not in the checkout). About 10.4% of blanks are 9-12 letters if a word is drawn at random from the chunk, and 40% if the length is drawn uniformly. About 28% of blanks repeat elsewhere in the chunk. That puts up to about 44% of training rows (not 62%) on vocabulary spelling of unseen words, mostly 3-8 letters. The manifest's web copyable_share is 0.279, so the shared slices agree.

(5) A better and nearly free test exists. B2 and PT trained on identical rows at the same seeds, and PT is a left-to-right decoder, so it is a built-in control for the parallel-register worry. Auditing both on held-out web cloze rows, split by blank length, copyable or not, and how often the answer word occurred in training, separates spelling from prediction and from the hand word-copy path. It also gives a smooth size curve for the web share (3M to 10M), which pooled-5 does not.

Still unknown (untested): whether the 8a result.tgz files contain checkpoint.pt (only .sha256 files are in the snapshot, and the boxes are destroyed after collection), and whether a held-out cloze file can be built (cloze.py is not in the checkout). Neither can be settled from the files, so this is a plan with a fallback, not a check.
chair.revised_idea:
scale-D3 revised: Held-out cloze audit of the 8a checkpoints, B2 against PT on identical rows. Not a pilot, and no new training unless the checkpoints are gone.

WHAT IT ASKS: on web fill-in-the-blank rows whose answer is NOT in the chunk, can B2's parallel character registers spell 9-12 letter words as well as 3-8 letter words, measured against the left-to-right PT arm on the same rows? Ben should know the answer before the 10M and 30M web shares are paid for.

STEPS (the first is zero compute):
0. Find out whether the 3M result.tgz for B2 and PT (seeds 401, 402, 405, and 400/403/404 when they land) contain checkpoint.pt. If not, keep checkpoints from the 10M run (the PC run) and audit 10M and any re-run 3M seed instead. Fallback: re-run one 3M B2 and one PT seed at the exact 8a shape (36 registers, 12 rounds, caps.json, 24,000 updates; B2 took about 3,400 s on a 5090) with --out kept. Do not use N_REG=13.
1. Build a held-out cloze set with the 8a cloze script (same sizes: chunk up to 280 letters, one 3-12 letter blank) from FineWeb-Edu documents NOT in slice_rung30 (document-id disjoint, hash-checked), with a seed outside 400-405, passed through overlap13 against the panels already indexed. Do not score on any protected panel document. Draw about 2,000 rows each for 3-8 and 9-12 letter blanks (stratified, because the natural share of 9-12 is only about 10%), and also report the natural-share-weighted total. Tag each row by script, not by hand: copyable (answer word also in the chunk); and the answer word's count in the training web text (0-9 = rare, 10 or more = common). No hand-picked word list anywhere.
2. Run greedy answers from the saved checkpoints (CPU is fine for a few thousand rows). Score the way the training target is written. Report exact match, length-right, normalised edit distance and mean per-character log-probability (the last avoids an exact-match cliff), split by blank length, copyable or not, rarity bin and mode used (GEN or WORD). The primary cell is non-copyable and rare, so a pass cannot come from the hand word-slice copy or from memorised words. Require at least 300 rows in each primary cell, else draw more.
3. Verdict, bands fixed now and closed. Let rho_L = (B2 exact) / (PT exact) in the primary cell for blank length L, averaged over the seeds available.
 - Floor: if PT's 9-12 exact is under 3%, verdict is 'unlearnable for both arms at this size'. This says nothing about spelling. Report it, and the 8a analysis decides whether to keep the web share.
 - Pass (decoder not the bottleneck): rho_9-12 is at least 0.8 x rho_3-8.
 - Fail (parallel decoder limits long words): rho_9-12 is below 0.5 x rho_3-8.
 - In between (0.5 to 0.8): inconclusive. Go ahead, do not claim, and re-read at 6 seeds and at 10M.
 Label: a screen on 3 to 5 seeds, not a claim (rule 4); a claim needs all six 8a seeds.
4. If Fail, make ONE change in a separate arm and say so: either a left-to-right GEN decoder (adds params, state them against the size band) or cap web blanks at 3-8 letters. The cap changes the data mix between rungs, so the 3M rung must be re-run. Do not do either before Ben reseals the spec.
5. Optional, same files: run the same audit on the 10M checkpoints and report the 3M-to-10M change in cloze exact and log-probability for B2 and PT, as a smooth size signal on the web share (suggested, untested as a predictor of pooled-5).

RULE CHECK: rule 1 and 2 fine (human web text, scoring is hand-written and allowed). Rule 5: held-out docs go through overlap13, and the protected-panel hash merge (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB) is still open, so label the set 'pre-merge' until it lands. Rule 7: the 8a caps already raise max_ans to 35, so there is no silent cut. Rule 10: this is a build-time diagnostic, not a deploy step; word bins come from a script over the model's training data. Say plainly that B2's regex word splitter, place code and word-slice copy still run between question and answer, so WORD-mode hits are reported separately and never counted toward the pass. The GEN step itself is learned.

chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. State the premise as a post-hoc audit. The 3M rung has run on seeds 401, 402 and 405, so do not say 'before any 8a rung'. Cite 8a-3M-s40N-B2/RESULT.json (pooled-5 recomputed as 73.21, 74.14, 71.42; PT 66.23, 66.42, 66.14). The first thing to establish is whether the 3M result.tgz files hold checkpoint.pt, since only .sha256 files are in the snapshot and the boxes are destroyed after collection. Tell Ben to make the 10M run keep checkpoints. If none exist, the fallback is a real-shape rerun (36 registers, 12 rounds, caps.json, 24k updates), never N_REG=13.

2. Do not test memorisation. No hand-picked 200-word closed set, and no training and testing on the same words. Use held-out documents that are disjoint from slice_rung30 by document id. Tag every row by script with: blank length (3-8 vs 9-12), copyable (answer in the chunk), rare vs common (count of the answer word in the training web text), and mode (GEN vs WORD). Score the pass marks on non-copyable, rare rows only. This removes both the memorised words and the hand word-slice copy (ledger.py:402-403). Stratify the draw so there are at least 300 rows in each primary cell, because the natural share of 9-12 letter blanks is about 10.4%.

3. Use PT, the left-to-right arm on the same rows and seeds, as the control. Judge B2 by a ratio to PT, not by absolute 25%/40% thresholds that have no baseline. Fix the bands before running, with no gaps: rho_9-12 at least 0.8 x rho_3-8 passes, below 0.5 x fails, and the middle is 'inconclusive, re-read at 6 seeds and 10M'. Add a floor: if PT's 9-12 exact is under 3%, the verdict is 'unlearnable for both' and says nothing about spelling. Say which result would prove the worry wrong (ratio at least 0.8) and which would prove it right (below 0.5). Also report edit distance and per-character log-probability so a flat exact-match number does not hide a smooth trend.

4. Do not repeat any of the dropped evidence. Drop Step 0 on the q33 or s100 checkpoints: they have 9 registers and GEN_MAX 8, and no pooled-5 dev answer exceeds 8 characters. Do not cite cipher_map (copy_gate is the mean of 1-g, about 0.9999, so it is prompt copying) or word_filter (a count family) as spelling evidence. Do not use edit distance 1 on numeric families.

5. Label every number shown, suggested or untested. The 10.4%, 28.4% and 40% figures come from a streaming recount (not cloze.py) and are suggested. The 8a manifest's web copyable_share of 0.279 is shown. Note that the training-log 'gen' loss (about 0.72-0.92 at step 24,000, normalised over the whole batch, mixed own-text and web) cannot separate length bands and should not be read as spelling.

6. Rule 4: 3 to 5 seeds is a screen. A claim needs all six 8a seeds. Do not let a screen gate the 10M or 30M start by itself; the 'inconclusive' band must not block the rungs.

7. Rule 5: the protected-panel hash merge is still open, and DATA-POOL-PLAN section 6 conflicts with spec addendum A1 on whether training may precede it. Run overlap13 on the held-out docs and mark the set 'pre-merge'. Ask Ben to rule on that conflict.

8. If it fails, the next step is one change in a separate arm: a conditioned decoder (adds params, so state the size band) or a 3-8 letter blank cap (changes the data mix, so the 3M rung must be re-run). Neither may be done silently.

9. Keep the village model out of it. Everything here is the B2 and PT card experiments.

10. Say plainly in the autonomy line that the GEN step is learned but B2's regex word splitter, place code and word-slice copy are hand steps that run between question and answer. This is a build-time probe with no deploy step.

11. Ask Ben to confirm the 10M run (PC) keeps checkpoint.pt, and that a held-out web file can be built. The 8a build (cloze.py, analyze_8a.py) is not in this checkout, so whether it already reports cloze exact by length is untested.

plan.title: Held-out cloze spelling audit, 3M B2 vs PT
plan.ben_line: The 3M models learned to fill in blanks in web sentences. This test checks, on new pages they never saw, whether B2 spells long words (9 to 12 letters) about as well as a same-size plain model, and it trains nothing new.
plan.question: On held-out web fill-in-the-blank rows whose answer word is not in its chunk and never occurs in the 3M training text, does B2 lose more on 9-12 letter answers than the same-size plain model PT does, compared with its own 3-8 letter results?
plan.one_change: No training. The one change is the test: score the already-trained 8a 3M B2 and PT checkpoints on held-out web rows that were never in training. Only if the checkpoints are gone: re-run one B2 and one PT per seed at the exact 8a shape (36 answer registers, max answer 35, 12 rounds, 24,000 updates, taken from caps.json); never at 13 registers.
arms: B2 at 3M: ledger, width 256, 2 blocks, 12 rounds, copy talker on, 36 answer registers, max answer 35, 3,346,513 params (shown: 8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json). It is 3,346,513 minus 3,341,880 = 4,633 above the top of the plus-or-minus 3 percent band, and 3.1 percent above the 3,244,544 plain-S reference (shown: stdout.events.txt size event, inside false). Pooled-5 on seeds 401, 402, 405 is 73.21, 74.14, 71.42 (shown, recomputed from final_eval).

PT = plain_tf_steps_g at 3M: width 256, 4 causal layers, 3,297,536 params, inside the band (shown: 8a-3M-s401-PT/RESULT.json; size event inside true). Pooled-5 on the same seeds is 66.23, 66.42, 66.14 (shown, recomputed).
Report-only, not in the verdict: plain_lm (the LLM arm) on the same rows, if its checkpoint exists.
plan.seeds: Screen on seeds 401, 402 and 405, the three 8a seeds in the snapshot (shown). Seeds 400, 403 and 404 are not in the snapshot. Under rule 4 this is a screen; a claim needs all six 8a seeds. Both arms are scored on identical rows in identical order.
plan.machine: Scoring only, on Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC or the Mac CPU (torch needed; not installed here). No GPU rental for the audit. A re-run, if one is needed, goes where the 8a rung runs. The spec's newest addendum says rented 5090s (shown: addendum I, 4:35 PM); the orchestrator brief says the PC (unverified, a later decision may exist).
pass_marks: Frozen before scoring. Primary cell: answer word absent from its chunk AND never occurring in the 3M training text (training web text = the first 38,158 docs of slice_rung30.jsonl, suggested from the 3M manifest docs count and addendum I1; plus the rung10 own-text prefix, shown as own_rung 10). Secondary cell: 1-9 occurrences. Each primary length cell (3-8 and 9-12) needs at least 1,000 rows; a smaller cell is reported with no verdict.

rho_L = B2 exact / PT exact in the primary cell for blank-length band L, pooled over the seeds present. R = rho_9-12 / rho_3-8. The verdict uses point estimates; 95 percent intervals from a bootstrap over documents are printed beside them.
Unlearnable (says nothing about spelling): PT exact on the 9-12 primary cell below 3 percent.

Pass (worry proved wrong): R at least 0.8 AND B2 exact on the 9-12 primary cell at least 10 percent. The 10 percent floor is added here (suggested): without it both arms can fail alike and R near 1 passes with no spelling.
Fail-relative (worry proved right): R below 0.5.
Fail-absolute (worry proved right): B2 exact on the 9-12 primary cell below 10 percent while PT is at least 3 percent.
Inconclusive (re-read at six seeds and at 10M; does not block any rung): every other result, including R from 0.5 to 0.8.

Reported, never gated: mean copy weight (1 minus the copy gate) per cell; a Pass with a primary-cell mean above 0.5 is labelled copy-assisted, not vocabulary spelling (suggested). WORD-mode hits, excluded from every cell. Exact by character position for both arms (a steeper B2 fall with position fits parallel decoding; suggested). Normalised edit distance. Per-character log-probability. The natural-share-weighted total: about 10 percent of blanks are 9-12 letters (shown by my reproduction on a 6 MB prefix of slice_rung30: 10.4 percent by occurrence, 30.7 percent by distinct word, 40 percent if lengths were uniform; regex [A-Za-z]+, not cloze.py).
plan.proved_wrong: The worry (B2's parallel character registers cannot spell long unseen words) is proved wrong by a Pass: R at least 0.8 with B2's long-word primary exact at least 10 percent. It is proved right by Fail-relative (R below 0.5) or Fail-absolute (B2 long-word primary exact below 10 percent while PT is at least 3 percent). If the 1,000-row cells cannot be filled, the test gives no verdict and says so.
plan.null_risk: Medium without the added floors, lower with them. False-pass routes: (a) both arms near floor on 9-12 letters, so R is near 1 (blocked by the added 10 percent B2 floor); (b) recall of words the model saw (blocked by the zero-count primary cell, which may be small; untested); (c) spelling by copying prompt characters rather than from the vocabulary (copy_share in the 8a training events is 0.27 to 0.38 at step 24,000, shown; reported, and a Pass is labelled copy-assisted above 0.5). False-fail routes: B2 and PT differ in more than the decoder (12 rounds, 36 registers, the reader, the copy gate), so a fail cannot be pinned on parallel decoding without a causal B2 arm; the per-position curve is only a hint. Power: with suggested rates of about 0.10 on 9-12 and 0.30 on 3-8, the 95 percent interval on R spans a factor of about 1.6 either way at 400 rows per cell and about 1.3 at 1,000 rows (shown by arithmetic, summing (1-p)/(n p) over both arms). The log gap between the 0.8 and 0.5 lines is 0.47, so the 300 to 400 rows proposed in the brief cannot separate them.
plan.autonomy: Build-time probe with no deploy step, so the deployed-model rule is not triggered by the audit itself. The learned part is the GEN spelling step, which needs no outside tool at deploy. B2's path still has hand code between question and answer: the regex number and word splitter (ledger.py spans and talk, data.word_spans), the hand place code (reader.py, 16-row table in the q33 code, shown), and the WORD copy of a prompt word (ledger.py lines 402-403, shown). The audit reports WORD hits separately and never counts them toward a verdict. Rows are chosen and tagged by script from human-written web text; rarity comes from the training text; no hand-picked word list is used, so the test is not a practice set (rule 10). Plain line for Ben: the spelling step is learned; the rest of B2's path is still hand-written.
steps: 0. Zero compute, first. Ask Ben whether each 8a result.tgz (seeds 401, 402, 405; B2 and PT) holds checkpoint.pt. The snapshot holds only the .sha256 files (shown), so this is unknown here. train.py saves checkpoint.pt when --out is set (shown: train.py lines 199-201), and the earlier checkpoint folders keep checkpoint.pt beside a .tgz.sha256 (shown: checkpoints/cio-1007), so the 8a archives probably do too (suggested, untested). Boxes are destroyed after collection (shown: addendum H). If no archive holds it, go to 0b.

0b. Only if missing: one B2 and one PT per seed at the 8a shape (caps.json: n_reg 36, max_ans 35; n_loops 12; 24,000 updates; lr 1e-3; batch 256; bf16), with --out kept. Timing reference (shown: box.json): B2 3,423 s and PT 589 s on one rented 5090. A re-run is a new run with the same seed, not bit-identical (suggested).

1. Before any scoring, post the pass_marks in the thread and record the held-out row hash. Record these discrepancies beside them: (i) box.json logs --max-ans 8 for B2, while caps.json and RESULT.json say 35 (shown), so the scorer must take N_REG and the max answer from caps.json and the checkpoint shapes, not from argv; (ii) the web-slice manifest budgets rung30 at 123.35M tokens, while data-pool plan section 10 says 117.8M (shown both); (iii) the 3M schedule ran 4.33 passes with max_row_draws 5, above the spec's no-more-than-4 rule, which addendum B1 allows with the count reported (shown); (iv) the brief's 44 percent is by word pieces, not rows: non-copyable web rows are 437,510 of 1,418,702 training rows, 30.8 percent (computed from the manifests; about 45 percent of pieces if the two kinds are equal length, suggested).

2. Build held-out rows (no training). Take documents whose id is not in slice_rung30.jsonl (match the id field of every line). Candidates: the unread remainder of shard 000_00000, since about 286k documents were dropped while building rung30 (shown: manifest drops 235,045 + 51,152 + 109) and shard 0 holds 726,000 documents (shown: data-pool plan section 6); or shard 1, which the 8a slice manifest does not use (shown). Apply the same grade and quality filters as the slice (the filter code is not in this checkout: untested). Build rows with the 8a cloze builder at a seed other than 400 (400 built the rung30 rows, shown in 8a-3M-s401-pool/caps.json). Draw by script until each primary length cell has at least 1,000 rows. Run overlap13 against every panel already indexed, and against the 3M training documents to drop shared-text documents (suggested). Label the set pre-merge until PROTECTED-HASH-JOB merges (no protected index file in the snapshot, shown).

3. Tag each row by script. (a) Copyable = the answer word, lowercased, also appears as a whole word elsewhere in the chunk. This is the rule progparse uses for WORD mode (progparse.py _targets, shown in the q33 code); the 8a builder's rule is untested. (b) Training count = occurrences of the answer word, lowercased, in the 3M training text: the first 38,158 web docs of slice_rung30.jsonl (suggested) plus the rung10 own-text prefix (shown: own_rung 10 in the 3M manifest). Bins: 0, 1-9, 10 or more. Primary = non-copyable and count 0; secondary = count 1-9. If the zero-count cell cannot reach 1,000 long-word rows, the switch to 1-9 must be written into the marks before scoring. Chunks average about five 9-12 letter words (suggested arithmetic), so the zero-count rule, not the draw, is the binding constraint.

4. Score both arms on identical rows (CPU is enough for a few thousand rows; untested at this count). Greedy answers. A non-copyable row can only be right through GEN, because a WORD copy cannot equal an answer absent from the chunk. For B2, force GEN mode for the log-probability and record the decoded mode separately. Record per row: prediction, decoded mode, copy weight per GEN character (copy_gate_eval in ledger.py uses 1 minus the gate, shown), per-character log-probability of gold plus EOS (teacher-forced for PT; register distributions for B2), and exact match by position. B2 registers are stored units-first and reversed at decode (ledger.py talk(), shown); the scorer must do the same. Assert zero truncated gold answers: 12-letter answers against a 35-character cap. The q33 silent cut is ledger.py line 447; the 8a build's behaviour is untested.
5. Apply the pass_marks to the primary cell, with per-seed results and document-bootstrap intervals beside them. Write the verdict and the reported items into the thread.

6. Only if Fail-relative or Fail-absolute: one change, in a separate arm, stated before running. Either a left-to-right GEN decoder for B2 (adds parameters; state them against the 3M band) or a cap on web blank length at 3-8 letters (changes the data mix, so the 3M rung must be re-run). Neither is done silently or before Ben reseals the spec.

7. Optional (suggested): if the 10M checkpoints are kept, run the same audit and report the 3M-to-10M change in exact match and log-probability for both arms. This is a smooth size signal on the web share, not a predictor of pooled-5 (untested).

idea.title: Remove host stalls from the B2 step, phase timer first
idea.summary: B2 at q33 caps runs about 105-121 ms per update against about 28 ms of matmul time, and B2 is 4x slower than plain at the 8a caps on a 5090 (0.092 s vs 0.023 s at 3M). Measure where a step goes with a per-phase timer, then remove syncs (cached constant tensors, one pinned non_blocking copy, equality-based one-hot) and move collate, span parsing and gold-target building into DataLoader workers. Outputs stay bit-identical.
idea.change: Step 1, measurement only: synchronize around collate, tokenize, gold, forward, backward, step for 200 updates. Step 2 if prep is at least 15% of the step: (a) ledger.py value_code uses (digs[...,None]==arange(10)).float() instead of F.one_hot; (b) cache OMEGA, CONSTS, COMM per device; (c) pack tokenize and gold numpy arrays into one pinned int64 array with one non_blocking copy; (d) DataLoader with 2-3 workers, pin_memory, prefetch 4, precomputed int32 spans per worker replacing the 20,000-entry spans cache that thrashes at 200,000 rows. 0 params.
