problems: Claim (a), that F.one_hot forces a host sync, is probably wrong. ledger.py:72 calls F.one_hot(digs, 10) with num_classes given. A WebFetch of upstream aten/src/ATen/native/Onehot.cpp (main branch; a small-model summary, not a raw read, so recheck on the installed torch) says the CUDA path with explicit num_classes skips the host min/max and relies on scatter device asserts ('rely on device asserts from scatter to avoid sync'). So the one_hot change is at most a suggested gain, and likely none. Shown by grep: the real host-to-device copies without non_blocking are at ledger.py:217 (tokenize, 5), 222 (OMEGA), 292 (CONSTS), 454 (gold, 8) and 502 (COMM), 16 in total, which matches the idea's count. Their cost is mainly the first drain of the GPU queue per step, not the count.

The step-1 phase timer (synchronize around collate, tokenize, gold, forward, backward, step) removes the overlap it is meant to measure. Shown from train.py: after opt.step() is queued, the loop calls next(batches) (collate, data.py:119) and then loss(), where gold() (ledger.py:433-454) does Python row_targets work before its first blocking copy at ledger.py:454. So the CPU work runs while the previous backward is still on the GPU. Sync-bracketed timers would count that work as serial and inflate the prep share used for the 15% gate. The fix is a cached-batch replay: precompute 200 batches in RAM, time the step on them, and compare with the live step. The gap is the real upper bound on what workers can gain.

Where prep is probably on the critical path: tokenize() (ledger.py:214-217, called from run() after gold()'s drain) runs spans() (ledger.py:200-211) on the main thread while the GPU is idle. The cache at ledger.py:203-204 clears above 20,000 entries. With 200,000 shuffled training rows, a random row is in the cache with probability about 5-10% (suggested arithmetic), so most prompts are re-parsed every batch. This is the most credible part of the idea. Its size is untested: suggested 256 regex parses per batch, roughly 5-25 ms against a step of 100-600 ms.

The speed baseline mixes GPUs and shared runs. The 8.24 steps/s figure (results/29-b2-screen/B2_s100) comes from BensPC with queue 32 at --par 2, so two jobs shared the card. The 9.56 figure (results/40-egw-s200/B2V_s200) is from a rented 5090 pair (queue 36-pc-eg2 header; data path /job). Both are shared, so neither is solo. The q33 confirm the idea calls 'q33 caps' (results/33-pc-confirm-b2, --par 3 on BensPC) ran B2 at 1.58-6.74 steps/s, which is 148-632 ms per update, not 105-121 ms. Shown from RESULT.json steps_per_s and queue_local/33-pc-confirm-b2.txt.

The plain range 24.5-28.5 steps/s is a selected subset. The same plain arm in the same shared queue ran 13.0 (tf_s205) and 16.6 (tf_s200) steps/s (results/33-pc-confirm-b2, shown). The 28.5 figure is a calibration run (02-calib-long/tf3m_24k), not a matched solo run. The 3x and 4x B2/plain ratios therefore depend on which runs are picked.

The '28 ms of matmul time' and the 'about 30 TFLOP/s for plain' figures have no source in the files I opened (8A-SPEC addendum I2, notes/speed-5090-2026-10-04.txt, and the RESULT files). My rough count (suggested, not measured): B2 at about 0.75 TFLOP per update (forward about 0.25, times 3 for training) gives about 6-7 TFLOP/s at 8.24-9.56 steps/s, which fits the idea's 7-8. Plain at about 25 steps/s with 100-150 character prompts gives about 12-20 TFLOP/s, not 30. Both are far below bf16 peak, so the gap is mostly small kernels and eager-op count, not only syncs. My estimate is about 1,000 forward kernels (16 block applications of about 20 ops, plus 7 steps of about 50-80 ops each); suggested, not counted. If so, the cost is kernel-launch overhead, which removing syncs does not address. The idea's own rejection clause (under 1.03x means launches, see CUDA graph) concedes this.

The 4x B2/plain ratio is close to the depth ratio alone. plain_tf.py:43 sets n_layers=4 applied once; plain_tf_steps inherits it. B2 applies 2 CBlocks for 8 loops, so 16 block applications per forward (ledger.py:147 and 306-318), each with cross-attention over the reader memory. A 4x ratio in per-update time is therefore roughly what the block count predicts, and attributing it to host overhead is not shown.

Arithmetic error on the 30M time. I2's 30M row is 0.679 s per update and 58,594 updates, which gives 39,781 s, about 11.1 hours for B2 alone. I2's 16.0 hours is for all three arms (0.679+0.148+0.154 per update). The idea's '13-14 h a seed' matches neither. The 30M figures also come from gradient accumulation in 4 parts at 15 GB (I2), so per-part overhead is multiplied. Attributing 30M time to syncs or prep is untested, and the 8a micro-batch build is not in this snapshot.

'Multiplies across all 8a rungs' is overstated. The expected gain is largest at 3M, where GEMMs are small and overhead is a large share. Per update the rungs go 0.092, 0.327 and 0.679 s (I2), so GPU work grows about 3-4x per rung and the host share falls. Gain at 10M and 30M is likely smaller (suggested). This should be measured per rung, not assumed.

The pass mark is not valid on a shared card. The test runs 200 updates, 3 repeats, median, on BensPC. The queues show sharing cuts B2 steps/s by 3-10x (shown, RESULT files above). Without an idle GPU the 1.10x comparison measures other jobs. The first 50 or so updates (autotune, allocator warm-up) are not excluded. The band between 1.03x and 1.10x is undefined. The 15% prep gate is not anchored to any measurement.

'Outputs stay bit-identical' is probably not testable as written, and the pass mark uses a different standard ('equal to 6 digits'). On CUDA, gather backward uses scatter_add with atomics (suggested), and bf16 autocast is on (train.py --bf16). So two runs of the current code may not match bit for bit. The test must first measure the run-to-run spread of the current code on one seed, and only then define 'identical'. The 6-digit check is weaker than the summary claims.

Scope: the ledger.py lines I verified (72, 203-204, 217, 222, 292, 454, 502) match the q33 code. Line 338 and line 295 were not checked. The 8a build (cloze, 36 registers, 280-letter prompts, 12 rounds, micro-batching; addendum G) is not in this snapshot, so the sync and prep sites may differ there, and the gains on q33 code may not carry over. The speed test is on the 5070 Ti, while the I2 numbers are from a 5090, so the baselines are on different cards.

Rule check: no rule is broken. The change is training-side (rule 10 does not apply), it truncates nothing (rule 7), costs about 0.6 PC hours (rule 6), and adds no parameters. The idea cites no papers, so none needed checking. Rule 4 does not apply, since it makes no quality claim. The equivalence claim is what must hold for rule 3 (same function) to stay true, which is why the replay and determinism checks above matter.
critiques.rescue: Keep the idea but cut and reorder it. (1) Run torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('warn') for 20 updates on the installed torch to count the real syncs, and drop the one_hot change unless it reports one. (2) Measure the run-to-run spread of the current code (two runs, same seed, same GPU, idle card, first 50 updates excluded). Define 'identical' as within that spread. (3) Run the cached-batch replay (200 batches precomputed in RAM) against live batches on an idle card. That gives the upper bound on what moving collate, gold and tokenize off the main thread can gain. Stop if the bound is under 10%. (4) If the bound is at least 10%, first precompute the spans (ledger.py:200-211) for all training rows once, which removes the cache thrash. Then test DataLoader workers. (5) Use torch.profiler or nsys over 50 steady-state updates to measure GPU-idle fraction and kernel count, instead of synchronize-bracketed phase timers. (6) Pass mark: at least 1.10x median steps/s over 5 repeats on an idle card of the rung's type, with the 1.03-1.10x band reported as inconclusive and no claim made. Report the 30M gain separately, as its own measurement. (7) Put CUDA graphs in a separate idea. They are the likely launch-overhead fix and need this work as a prerequisite, as the idea says.
critiques.already_tried: None in this project for B2 host overhead. The idea's own closest_prior says torch.compile and CUDA graphs were only suggested. The nearest prior measurements are 8A-SPEC addendum I2 (per-update times at 3M, 10M, 30M on a 5090, no breakdown) and the q33 queue runs (--par 2 and --par 3 on BensPC, with no solo timing). I found no profiler output or per-phase breakdown in the files I opened. The search was not exhaustive: the 28 ms figure, the matmul claim and the profile terms were checked only against the notes and RESULT files named above.
critiques.expected_effect: Suggested, not measured. At 3M, a total speedup of about 1.00-1.15x is most likely, with the spans precompute and removal of the first-drain stall contributing most. Removing the syncs alone gives about 0-5% (the one_hot sync is probably absent). The 1.10x mark is at best a coin flip. The gain is likely smaller at 10M and 30M, where GEMM work grows. Model outputs should be unchanged to within the run-to-run spread of the current code. Nothing changes in parameters, data or marks. Cost is about 0.6 PC hours for the measurement, plus the replay test, which should come first.

problems: Not the cheapest decisive test. The step-1 phase timer puts a sync around every phase, which removes the overlap it should measure. In the live loop, the next batch is prepared (CODE/train.py:159-167) while the previous step's GPU work is still queued, and the sync only happens at to_device. So 'prep at least 15% of the step' measured with syncs overstates prep on the critical path (shown: train.py loop order; suggested: pageable-copy sync behaviour). CODE = /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io.

The CPU-only check that settles the workers question is missing. collate (data.py:119-130), gold (models/ledger.py:433-454), tokenize (ledger.py:214-217) and batch_places (models/reader.py:26-40) can be timed on CPU alone for 50 batches of 256 at q33 caps in minutes, with no GPU and no checkpoint. Against the first-look step of 117 ms (8.52 steps/s, first-look-10m-results/readout.json, shown), prep under about 17 ms (15%) would drop the workers arm. The spans cache clears above 20,000 entries (ledger.py:203-204), so with 200k rows the hit rate is about 5% (suggested: average fill about 10k of 200k). Prep is 10-30 ms per batch by my estimate (suggested, untested).

The sync count is undercounted, and non_blocking=True gives false comfort. Each update has at least 21 pageable host-to-device copies: 4 in to_device (train.py:167, data.py:132, non_blocking=True on pageable memory), 1 in reader.py:40 (batch_places), 8 in gold (ledger.py:454), 5 in tokenize (ledger.py:217), and one each for OMEGA (ledger.py:222), CONSTS (ledger.py:292) and COMM (ledger.py:502). The proposal counts 16 (shown). There are also 8 F.one_hot calls (ledger.py:72 via 295 and 338), which I believe range-check on CUDA and so sync (suggested: PyTorch behaviour as recalled). Pageable copies stall the stream even with non_blocking=True (suggested: CUDA runtime sync rules as recalled), so the pinned-memory change (step c) is the fix that matters. The one-hot and packing edits are value-identical (0/1 floats; no float reordering), so outputs can stay the same.

The baseline numbers come from shared or unrecorded runs, and they disagree. The 105-121 ms figure comes from 29-b2-screen (8.24 steps/s) and 40-egw (9.56 steps/s); neither RESULT.json records sharing (shown). The q33 PC B2 runs were 1.58 and 1.82 steps/s in the 3-job queue (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s201 and B2_s200: train_s 15,164 and 13,160; shown). The first-look B2 at q33 caps ran 8.52 steps/s with four runs sharing each rented 5090 (FIRST-LOOK-10M amendment 2, shown). The same B2 config varies about 5-6x across queues. The proposal says 'no solo timing exists yet', but addendum H says the probe ran alone on a seventh 5090 (/mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md line 397; shown).

B2's probe and sustained speeds disagree at G caps, while the plain arms do not. Probe (I2, 200 updates, one 5090): B2 0.092 s per update, PT 0.023, LLM 0.032. Sustained 8a runs (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2, -PT, -LLM RESULT.json): B2 7.09 steps/s (0.141 s; train_s 3,384 for 24k updates), PT 42.3 steps/s (0.024 s), LLM 31.2 steps/s (0.032 s). The plain arms match their probes within 3%; B2 is 53% slower sustained, and its sustained ratio to PT is about 6.0, not the 4x the proposal uses (shown). Either the probe or the sustained run is unrepresentative. A host-side cost that varies by machine would explain it (suggested). The test must state which number it replaces.

The pass mark has no noise floor and can pass by chance. The design uses three repeats of 200 updates, arm A then arm B, with no current-vs-current control and no discard of warm-up updates. Within one queue the same B2 config varied 15% (1.58 vs 1.82 steps/s; shown), and a 1.10 mark sits inside that range. Needed: ABAB order, at least 500 updates with the first 50-100 discarded, at least 4 repeats per arm, and a current-vs-current pair that sets the noise band before the edit is judged.

The identity gate ('equal to 6 digits' over 200 updates) is undefined for unchanged code. train.py never sets deterministic algorithms (grep finds none, shown). gen_copy uses scatter_add_ on CUDA (ledger.py:248), and the reader's conv and embedding backward run CUDA kernels; run-to-run float differences with identical code are then likely (suggested, untested). Fix: rerun the current code with the same seed to measure its divergence, and require the edit to stay within it. Or run the identity check in deterministic mode, keeping speed in a separate run.

Bundled edits break one-change-at-a-time (rule 4). Steps (a) to (d) are tested together, so a result under 1.03 cannot say which part failed, and the 1.03-1.10 band has no verdict at all. Test the sync edits (a to c) alone first, and the workers (d) only after the prep check in item 2.

The key question, whether the step is host-bound or GPU-bound, is not tested. B2's controller matmuls are small (17 tokens per row at q33 caps, 44 at G caps). Batch-size scaling at 128, 256 and 512 with fixed caps separates the two: flat time means host-bound, so syncs and prep matter; time proportional to batch means GPU-bound, and sync removal buys little. A torch.profiler window (busy GPU time vs wall time) gives the same answer without editing code.

The '28 ms matmul' and '7-8 TFLOP/s' figures appear in no file (grep shown). My count from ledger.py block sizes (2.04 MFLOP per controller token per block application; 2 blocks x 8 rounds x 17 tokens x 256 rows at q33 caps; forward plus backward) gives about 0.65 TFLOP per update at q33 caps and about 2.6 TFLOP at G caps with 280-character reads (suggested: my arithmetic, untested). So 28 ms implies about 23 TFLOP/s, an assumed efficiency, and the 'most of the gap is dispatch' conclusion rests on that assumption.

Hours and memory. The 0.6 h is roughly right as GPU time for the proposed run (about 10-15 min with startup), but only on an idle card. The PC runs several jobs at once under a GPU-BUSY.txt convention (CODE/PC-JOB.md, shown), so the test needs a slot. A valid version (items 5 and 6 plus a profile) is about 1-1.5 h of GPU (suggested). The '1 hour per 24k run' figure holds only when solo: 8.52 steps/s is 0.78 h in the shared first look, and the PC queue ran 3.7-4.2 h (shown). Memory fits in 16 GB: q33-cap B2 peaks at 2,873 MiB allocated and 4,696 MiB reserved (first-look-10m-results/B2_s200/RESULT.json, shown); G-cap B2 at 6,463 MiB allocated and 6,986 MiB reserved (8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json, shown). Two G-cap runs at once would be about 14-15 GiB reserved with CUDA contexts (suggested), so one process at a time.

int32 spans (step d) are a silent correctness risk. ledger.py:205-208 stores numbers as int64, clipped at 10^18, so the code expects values past 2^31. int32 would wrap them (4294967297 becomes 1) and the executor would run on wrong values with no error (suggested, follows from the dtype). Keep numbers int64; word spans can be int32.

Benefit transfer. The 10M and 30M rungs run on rented 5090 boxes (8A-SPEC addendum H, shown), whose host CPU is not recorded. A PC-only speedup does not show the rung gain. Record CPU model, core count and GPU clock on both machines. Any edit must be bit-identical, because the 3M rung is sealed (8A-SPEC addenda A to G).

Shape mismatch. The test runs at q33 caps (8 rounds, 9 registers, 27 slots). The rungs run at addendum G caps (12 rounds, 36 registers, 106 slots, reads to 280; 141 ms per update sustained, shown). n_loops=12 is a config value and can be tested now (8a-3M-s401-B2 config shows n_loops 12). The register and slot counts need the 8a build, which is not in this snapshot (shown).
Arithmetic slip. 0.679 s x 58,594 updates is about 11.1 h, not the proposal's '13-14 h a seed' (8A-SPEC addendum I2 and I3, shown; I3's 13 h has no derivation in the file).
critiques.rescue:
Replace the test with a gated sequence on one idle PC card (check nvidia-smi and GPU-BUSY.txt first; record CPU model, core count, GPU clock and other running processes). Write the pass and kill marks before any run.
(0) CPU only, no GPU, about 10 min: time collate, gold, tokenize and batch_places over 50 batches of 256 at q33 caps. Drop the worker arm (d) if prep is under 15% of a current step (about 17 ms at 117 ms).
(1) About 20 min, current code, no edits: batch-size scaling at 128, 256 and 512 (100 warm-up updates, then 400 timed); live vs prebuilt batches at 256; a torch.profiler window (busy GPU time vs wall time) or torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('warn') to count syncs per step (suggested API, untested here). Kill the sync work if time scales with batch (GPU-bound). Continue only if time is flat and prebuilt batches are clearly faster.
(2) Control: current code vs current code, same seed, ABAB, 4 repeats of 500 updates (first 100 discarded). Record the step-200 loss divergence and the steps/s spread. These set the identity tolerance and the speed noise band.
(3) One arm: sync edits only (a, b, c). Pass: median steps/s at least 1.10x the control median and step-200 loss within the control divergence, at q33 caps and again at n_loops 12. Kill: median ratio under 1.03 with the repeats inside the noise band. Between 1.03 and 1.10, report a small gain, not a pass.
(4) Only if (0) shows prep at least 15%: the worker arm alone, numbers kept int64, same sampler order, first 200 batches identical.
(5) Before any 10M or 30M rung uses the edit, repeat (3) on the rented 5090 box type that rung will run on.
critiques.already_tried: Nothing on syncs, prep or batch-size scaling has been run. Speed evidence on file: the first-look B2 readout (8.52 steps/s at q33 caps, four runs sharing each rented 5090; readout.json), 33-pc-confirm-b2 B2 seeds 200 and 201 (1.82 and 1.58 steps/s, shared PC queue), 29-b2-screen (8.24) and 40-egw (9.56) (no sharing recorded), addendum I2 (one 200-update probe per arm on one 5090 at G caps: B2 0.092 s, PT 0.023, LLM 0.032), and the sustained 8a 3M runs (B2 7.09, PT 42.3, LLM 31.2 steps/s). The closest prior speed test is I2: a single short probe with no spread and no host/GPU split. Other design notes already flag launch counts as a likely limit (CODE/design/design-recursive-refine.md:113 and design-latent-reread.md:112, shown), but none of them measures B2.
critiques.expected_effect: If the syncs and prep sit on the critical path, removing them could take B2 at q33 caps from about 8.5 to roughly 10-14 steps/s, and the G-cap rung from about 7.1 steps/s sustained by a similar amount (suggested, untested). It is a speed-only change: outputs stay identical and no size, data, arm or mark changes, so it cannot move a rung verdict. If the step is GPU-bound at these small shapes, the gain is under about 5% and the idea should be dropped in favour of shape-level work (fewer, larger kernels) rather than host tuning. Stage (1) decides which case holds, in about 20 minutes of GPU time.

chair.reasons:
PLAN, with the test rebuilt as a decision ladder: profile first, edit later. The idea is worth about 1.5 PC hours because it is training-side only (rules 1, 3, 7 and 10 untouched; the deployed forward stays the same function), costs no params, and every later 3M screen and rung would run faster if it works. Critics were right that the original test and pass marks were weak, but there is one strong new piece of evidence that none of the four critics put together.

Strongest evidence (shown). B2 alone runs much slower in the sustained 8a runs than in its own probe. B2 at 3M took 0.145 s per update for 24,000 updates, very steady across 500-step intervals (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/stdout.events.txt; steps_per_s 7.09, 7.14, 6.41 on seeds 401, 402, 405 in the RESULT.json files). The addendum I2 probe, at the same caps on a 5090, says 0.092 s (8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md line 419). The plain arms match their probes: PT 0.024 s sustained vs 0.023 probed, LLM 0.032 vs 0.032. So about 53 ms per update (37% of the sustained step) appears only for B2. B2 is the only arm with a per-row Python path (vocab.encode in collate, spans(), gold(), batch_places()). The sustained run draws from a 1,418,702-row pool (stdout start event). Against that pool all three host caches miss: the spans cache clears above 20,000 entries (ledger.py:202-204), the place-code cache above 400,000 (reader.py:34-36), and row_targets keeps an unbounded dict (progparse.py:185-193). The probe's batch source is not described in the spec, and q45 is not in the checkout, so this explanation is suggested, not shown. It is cheap to test and it is the better reason to run this idea than the original sync argument.

What to drop or fix from the idea.
(1) The claim that F.one_hot forces a host sync is recalled from PyTorch, probably false with an explicit num_classes on CUDA, and untested. Do not credit step (a) with sync removal; run torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode on the installed torch to count real syncs. Keep one-hot-by-equality only if the profile shows launch cost.
(2) The copy count is 21, not 16. The idea missed the 4 tensors in to_device (data.py:131-132, pageable memory) and the 1 in batch_places (reader.py:40). Two critics counted this independently and I read both sites.
(3) A phase timer that synchronizes around each phase removes the CPU/GPU overlap it is meant to measure, so it overstates prep on the critical path. Use CUDA events plus torch.profiler, and a replay test (200-300 batches prebuilt in RAM versus live batches) to get a true upper bound.
(4) The int32 span change is a correctness bug for the number values. nv is int64, clamped at 10**18 (ledger.py:209), and int32 would wrap numbers of 2**31 or more, turning prompt numbers into wrong small ones with no error. Only the offsets ns, ne, ws, we may be int32.
(5) The precompute-for-all-rows version is too big. At the 1.42M-row pool it needs several GB; compute spans, gold and places per batch in workers.
(6) DataLoader shuffle changes batch order. Use a batch_sampler that replays train_batches' RandomState(seed).permutation order (data.py:135-143), or no gain can be compared.
(7) Timing baselines are mixed: the 105-121 ms figure comes from two single screens, the six q33 runs on the shared PC queue ran 1.6-6.7 steps/s, and the 28 ms and TFLOP/s figures appear in no file (untested). The 30M time is 0.679 s x 58,594 updates = 11.1 h for B2 alone (arithmetic on the I2 table), not 13-14 h.
(8) The 3M rung is mostly done (seeds 401, 402, 405 exist). The gain is for later 3M screens and arms (T1, U0, W1, B3 catch-up, EGE, all about 24k updates), the 10M rung and the 30M rung. The host share should shrink with size (suggested): about 53 ms of 327 ms at 10M, about 8% at 30M. Expected gain is suggested at roughly 1.2-1.5x at 3M, 1.05-1.15x at 10M and at most about 1.08x at 30M; none of this is measured. Prior work: none for B2 host time; AUDIT-ranked-2026-10-05.md T4 plans the same method for another model with no result, and armB-report.md says torch.compile could not be tested there. grep finds no DataLoader, pin_memory, compile, CUDA graph or deterministic setting in the code.

Rule check. Rule 10 neutral: training speed only. The one caution is a single code path: the deployed forward must still compute spans itself when no precomputed arrays are passed (tokenize ledger.py:214-217 and talk() at ledger.py:392). Rule 4 does not apply (no accuracy claim), but inputs must be exactly identical. Rule 6: PC only, and only when idle. The PC is busy with q39 until about midnight ET 10-07, then the first look and C0 are queued, so the GPU steps must wait for an idle card (check nvidia-smi and GPU-BUSY.txt).
chair.revised_idea:
scale-D4 (revised): find out whether the B2 step is host-bound, then remove only the host cost the profile shows. Training-side only, 0 params, same function.

Question: is the 53 ms per update that B2 pays in sustained 8a runs (0.145 s) but not in the I2 probe (0.092 s) host-side per-row prep (collate/encode, spans, gold, batch_places, pageable copies) on a 1.42M-row pool?

Step 0, CPU only, no GPU, about 10 min, on BensPC. Time 50 batches of 256 rows from the real data order: next(batches) (collate and vocab.encode), tokenize(), gold(), batch_places(), cold caches and warm caches separately. Use the 8a pool at 8a caps (rebuilt with g8a.get_data) and also the 200k-row q33 data at q33 caps. Report ms per batch and a count of cache hits for spans, places and row_targets. Divide by that machine's sustained step time for the same config (not another machine's).

Step 1, GPU, idle card only, about 30 min, current code unchanged, at 8a caps (12 rounds, 36 registers, 280 letters) from the 8a pool.
 (a) A/A control: same code vs same code, same seed, ABAB, at least 4 repeats of 600 updates, first 100 discarded. Gives the noise band and the loss divergence floor (train.py sets no deterministic mode, so the code may not repeat itself bit for bit).
 (b) Replay upper bound: live batches versus 300 prebuilt batches held in RAM (spans, gold, places and encodings precomputed for exactly those rows), ABAB, 4 or more repeats. r = median replay steps/s over median live steps/s.
 (c) torch.profiler over 50 steady updates: GPU-busy fraction, kernel count, CPU-side time between kernels. Also torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('warn') for 20 updates to list real syncs.
 (d) Batch-size scaling 128/256/512 at fixed caps: flat time per update means host- or launch-bound; time proportional to batch means GPU-bound.
 Record CPU model, core count, GPU clock, other processes.

Step 2, only if the ladder below says so. Edits, each flag-gated and off by default, measured one at a time in this order:
 1. cache OMEGA, CONSTS and COMM per device; one pinned int64 buffer and one non_blocking copy for the tokenize and gold arrays; reuse t in gold() (it calls row_targets twice); equality-based one-hot only if (c) shows launch cost.
 2. only if the ladder allows: DataLoader with 2-3 workers, pin_memory, prefetch 4, and a batch_sampler replaying train_batches' RandomState(seed) permutation. Workers compute spans, gold and places per batch (no all-rows precompute), keep nv int64 (only ns, ne, ws, we may be int32), and put the arrays in the batch dict. The model uses them when present and otherwise computes them in the forward (one code path, so deployment is unchanged).
 Equality gates: (i) first 200 batches from the new path exactly equal (np.array_equal on every tensor) to the old path; (ii) step-200 loss and grad norm within 2x the A/A divergence; (iii) run()/talk() outputs on 500 dev rows from one existing checkpoint identical with and without the change. Sealed 8a rungs use the flag only if (i)-(iii) pass on the 8a pool, and the flag is recorded in box.json.

Decision ladder, fixed before any run:
 - Step 1(b) r below 1.05 or inside the A/A band: stop. Host prep is not the cost; the step is launch-bound. Cut this idea and send the launch problem to a separate fewer-ops / CUDA-graph / torch.compile idea (check that the PC has a compiler first).
 - 1.05 <= r < 1.15: do edit 1 only; no workers.
 - r >= 1.15 and Step 0 prep share >= 15% of the sustained step: do edit 1, then edit 2.
 - Final pass: median steps/s over at least 5 ABAB repeats at least 1.10x the A/A control, outside the A/A band, with gates (i)-(iii) met. Between 1.03x and 1.10x: report a small gain, no claim, no workers. Under 1.03x or inside the band: proved wrong, drop.
Report separately per rung shape (3M q33 caps, 3M G caps, 10M, 30M if it fits), not one number. Check the 10M and 30M claims on the rented-box type before using the edit there.

Cost: Steps 0 and 1 about 0.7 PC hours, edits plus final test up to about 1.5 more, one process on the card at a time, idle card only. Wait for q39 and the first look to finish.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.
1. Lead with the shown 3M gap: B2 sustained 0.145 s per update (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/stdout.events.txt, steady across 48 logged intervals) against 0.092 s in the I2 probe (8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md line 419). PT and LLM sustained 0.024 and 0.032 match their probes. The idea is a test of that gap's cause, not of syncs. The host-prep explanation (3 caches miss on a 1.42M-row pool) is suggested, untested.
2. Do not use a synchronize-bracketed phase timer as the main measurement; it removes the CPU/GPU overlap. Use the replay upper bound (prebuilt batches versus live) plus CUDA events or torch.profiler, plus batch-size scaling to tell host-bound from GPU-bound.
3. Always include a same-code A/A control first (ABAB, at least 4 repeats, 600 updates, discard the first 100). Define "identical" two ways: exact np.array_equal on every input tensor for the first 200 batches (deterministic, CPU-checkable), and loss within 2x the A/A divergence (train.py sets no deterministic mode, so CUDA gather/scatter backward may not repeat bit for bit). Do not demand "bit-identical and 6 digits" at once.
4. Run at the 8a shape (G caps, 8a pool), not only q33 caps; also run q33 caps on the 200k-row skills data since most coming screens (T1, U0, W1, B3, EGE) use that shape. The benefit transfers differently: expected to shrink with size (about 53 ms of 327 ms at 10M, under 10% at 30M, all suggested, untested). Report per shape.
5. Fix every range's verdict beforehand (ladder in revised_idea): r under 1.05 stop and cut; 1.05-1.15 cheap edits only; at least 1.15 and prep at least 15% build workers; final pass median at least 1.10x over at least 5 interleaved repeats outside the A/A band; 1.03-1.10x report as small gain, no claim; under 1.03x drop. State the result that proves it wrong: r under 1.05 means launch-bound, not host-bound.
6. Hard constraints on the edits: keep prompt numbers int64 (int32 wraps values of 2**31 or more and changes the executor input silently); only offsets may be int32; do not precompute spans for all 1.4M rows (several GB); use a batch_sampler that replays train_batches' RandomState(seed).permutation; keep one forward code path so deployed inference still computes spans itself (add a run()/talk() equality check on 500 dev rows from an existing checkpoint); edits are flags, off by default, recorded in box.json, and used on sealed 8a rungs only if the equality gates pass.
7. Drop the F.one_hot sync claim unless set_sync_debug_mode reports it. Correct the host-to-device copy count to 21. Correct 30M to 11.1 h for B2 alone (0.679 s x 58,594). Drop the 28 ms and TFLOP/s figures unless the profiler produces them. Do not cite q33 PC steps/s (1.6-6.7, shared queue) or the 7.8x ratio as solo timings.
8. Resource rules: idle PC card only (nvidia-smi, GPU-BUSY.txt; q39 runs to about midnight ET and the first look follows), one process at a time, CPU also idle because workers use cores; record CPU model, core count, clocks and other processes. Step 0 can run on the Mac only for order-of-magnitude prep ms; the share verdict must use the same machine's step time. Budget about 0.7 h to the decision and up to 1.5 h more if edits go ahead (the original 0.6 h was too low).
9. Plain summary for Ben: "B2's step takes about 145 ms when the 8a pool is used but about 92 ms in the quick speed probe. The plain models don't show that gap. This test finds out whether the missing 50 ms is the computer preparing each batch of questions one at a time, and if so moves that off to helper processes so the GPU never waits. If the GPU is already the limit, we stop and look at a different fix."
10. Keep this separate from the quality claims: it changes speed only, so no accuracy mark moves and no 6-seed claim is needed, but nothing in 8a's sealed build may change unless inputs are shown identical. Offer an outside review (reviews/ file for Astra) only if step 1 gives a surprising result, such as r near 1.0 with a large A/A band.

plan.title: Find whether B2's 3M step waits on per-batch prep (replay bound first, one flag-gated edit only if it passes)
plan.ben_line: B2 takes about 0.14 seconds per training step on the real 8a settings, but an earlier quick speed check said 0.09. This test checks whether the missing 0.05 seconds is the computer preparing each batch of questions while the graphics card sits idle. If it is, a later, separate change can move that work off the main path. If it is not, we stop and look somewhere else.
plan.question:
Does the B2 step at 3M on the 8a settings (about 0.146 s per update, mean of three rented-box seeds) take about 50 ms more than the I2 probe (0.092 s) because host-side per-batch prep (collate, gold targets, place ids, spans, pageable copies) runs while the GPU waits, rather than because the probe timed less work or ran under other conditions?

Facts checked against the files:
- (shown) I2 probe, 200 updates at G caps, 15 GB cap: B2 0.092, PT 0.023, LLM 0.032 s per update (8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md lines 414-419). B2 is about 4x PT in the probe.
- (shown) Sustained 8a 3M, seeds 401/402/405, rented 5090: B2 median logged interval 0.1400, 0.1394, 0.1552 s per update (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/stdout.events.txt, 47 intervals each); steps/s 7.09, 7.14, 6.41; peak 6,462.6 MiB (RESULT.json). The 3-seed mean of train_s/24,000 is 0.146. B2 is about 6x PT sustained.
- (shown) PT sustained medians 0.0236 to 0.0258 and LLM 0.0320 to 0.0336 match the probe within 0 to 12%, so the gap is specific to B2.
- (shown by arithmetic) The box's arms sum to its wall time: 3423.4 + 589.4 + 790.4 + pool build 254.9 = 5058.1 s (box.json wall_s). The arms ran back to back, not sharing the GPU. The FIRST-LOOK B2 runs (8.5 steps/s) did share their card four ways (FIRST-LOOK-10M amendment 2), so they are not a solo baseline.
- (shown) The names plain_lm, plain_tf_steps_g and g8a used by the 8a runs do not appear anywhere in this checkout (grep), so the 8a code path cannot be read here.
- (shown) The checkout makes 21 host-to-device copies per update: to_device 4 (data.py:132), batch_places 1 (reader.py:40), tokenize 5 (ledger.py:217), OMEGA 1 (ledger.py:222), consts 1 (ledger.py:292), gold 8 (ledger.py:454), COMM 1 (ledger.py:502). The idea's count of 16 is an undercount.
- (shown) --big-data feeds only the post-training chain-5 eval (train.py:215-217), not the timed loop.
- (suggested, uniform-sampling arithmetic, 1,418,702 rows) Spans cache (cleared above 20,000, ledger.py:203-204) hits about 0.7%. Place-id cache (cleared above 400,000, reader.py:36-37) hits about 14% at steady state and about 2% in a fresh 200-update run. Gold-target cache (progparse.py:185-193, unbounded) misses only the first 5,542 steps of the 24k run, and every row in a fresh run.
- (suggested) So a host-prep-only story predicts the fresh 200-update probe carries at least as much prep as the sustained run, i.e. the probe should be slower. The observed direction therefore needs one of three explanations: the probe timed less prep (prebuilt or reused batches), it used different rows (padded length, words and numbers per row), or it ran on another host. The probe script is not in the snapshot, so which one holds is untested.
- (suggested) B2 per-step prep may also include a per-word torch loop in place_ids (reader.py:17-23). Its cost per uncached prompt is untested and could be large; Step 0b must measure it.
plan.one_change: No model or code change to start. The one thing measured is the per-batch input path: live batches (current code) against the same batches prebuilt in RAM, with the non-batch copies (OMEGA, consts, COMM) left in. This replay is a bound, not a fix. Only if the decision ladder allows: one flag-gated edit (cache per-device constants and send the batch arrays through one pinned buffer). The worker loader (edit 2) is a separate, later test.
arms: A live: current code at 8a G caps (12 loops, 36 registers, 280-char prompts, n_num 91, n_res 11), 3M B2 (3,346,513 params), data-order seed 401 from the rebuilt 8a 3M pool.
A/A control: the same code as A, run in ABAB order with A. Sets the noise band and the loss-divergence floor. Needed because train.py sets no deterministic mode.

B replay bound: same seed and order, 300 prebuilt batches. Test-only harness monkeypatches tokenize, batch_places and gold to return precomputed GPU tensors built before the timer. The forward code is unchanged. Removes 18 of the 21 copies; OMEGA, consts and COMM remain.

C premise check on the PC: the sustained command at 200 updates and at 600 updates (log every 50). Also the I2 probe's own script if it can be recovered from the 5090 box or its result archive (not in the snapshot); if not, record the probe's batch source and bf16 setting as unknown.
D batch-size scaling, live: 128, 256 and 512 at G caps (100 warm-up updates, 300 timed). If 512 does not fit 16 GB, use 128 and 256 only.
E profiling: torch.profiler over 50 steady updates (GPU busy fraction, kernel count, CPU time), plus torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('warn') for 20 updates to list real syncs.
F only if the ladder allows: edit 1 with its flag on versus off (same code otherwise).
plan.seeds: Timing uses data-order seed 401 only (the seed of the 8a 3M B2 run). The timing claim rests on repeats, not seeds: at least 4 ABAB pairs per comparison, 600 updates each, first 100 discarded. The equality gates use six seeds (400-405): the CPU prep check on 200 batches each, and the GPU step-200 check in the confirm. This is not a model-quality claim, so rule 4's six-seed rule gates only the equality claim.
plan.machine: BensPC, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB. One process on the card at a time, with nothing else on the GPU or CPU (check nvidia-smi, GPU-BUSY.txt and top before and during each run). Record CPU model, core count and clocks. Step 0b is CPU-only on the same PC. Rented 5090s (Vast, $0.48/h, box.json) are a different machine: the 8a baselines come from them, and any 10M or 30M speed check needs Ben's OK before renting.
pass_marks: Mark 1 (premise, step C): short is the mean of all 200 updates; long is the median of updates 101 to 600, same command on the PC. Within 10%: the short probe is representative on this machine, so the 53 ms is a real condition difference. Short at least 20% below long: the I2 probe is biased low and the gap is partly a probe artifact. Either way, marks 2 to 9 still decide the edit.

Mark 2 (prep share, step 0b, CPU): prep ms per 256-row batch at warm-cache steady state (collate, gold CPU part, batch_places, spans), divided by the PC's live steady step ms from mark 1. At least 15%: edit 1, then the worker test, may run. 5% to 15%: edit 1 only. Under 5%: stop, host prep is not the cost. The 5% line is suggested; the 15% line is the chair's.
Mark 3 (noise band): the ratios of median steps/s over at least 4 ABAB A/A pairs. The band is the minimum to maximum of those ratios. Differences count only outside this band.

Mark 4 (replay bound): r = median steps/s of B divided by median steps/s of A, at least 4 ABAB pairs. r inside the A/A band or below 1.05: stop, host prep is not the cost, the step is GPU- or launch-bound. 1.05 to under 1.15: edit 1 only, no workers. At least 1.15 with prep share under 15%: edit 1 only, since the gain then comes from copies or syncs, not prep. At least 1.15 with prep share at least 15%: edit 1, then the worker test.

Mark 5 (scaling, D): t(512)/t(128) at G caps. At most 1.5: host- or launch-bound. At least 3.0: GPU-bound. Between: no verdict. If 512 does not fit, use t(256)/t(128): at most 1.3 host-bound, at least 1.8 GPU-bound. These thresholds are suggested and fixed here. Scaling separates host from GPU, not prep from launch overhead; mark 2 and mark 4 separate those.

Mark 6 (gate i, equality of inputs): first 200 batches, seeds 400-405, CPU only. np.array_equal is true on every tensor of the batch dict and the gold dict, the place ids and the five span arrays. A counter must show the new path ran on every batch (count above zero). Any mismatch drops the edit.
Mark 7 (gate ii, GPU): step-200 loss and grad norm within 2x the A/A divergence on seed 401; on all six seeds in the confirm.

Mark 8 (gate iii, inference): run() and talk() on 500 dev rows are identical, exactly, with and without the flag. Use a seeded random-init model (same weights both ways) and, if it loads, the q33 screen checkpoint /mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 (its config matches q33 B2 per a critic, untested here).

Mark 9 (final speed, edit 1 only): median steps/s over at least 5 ABAB pairs of 600 updates, flag on versus off, on the PC at G caps. At least 1.10x and outside the A/A band: pass. 1.03x to 1.10x: small gain, reported with no claim and no workers. Under 1.03x: drop.
plan.proved_wrong: Host prep is not the 50 ms if the replay ratio (mark 4) is inside the A/A band or under 1.05 on the PC. Then the step is GPU- or launch-bound and this idea is dropped. The idea is also proved wrong as a speed fix if edit 1 gives under 1.03x on five ABAB pairs (mark 9) even when the replay gave 1.15 or more, because then the replay bound is not reachable by caching and the worker test is not justified.
plan.null_risk: Yes, in three places. (1) Mark 4 can pass with no fix that edit 1 could reach. The replay removes all per-batch prep and 18 of the 21 copies, and it reuses 300 warm batches, so r of 1.15 or more is plausible even when the live cost is mostly launches (suggested). The replay is therefore a bound, and the final pass is measured on edit 1 alone. (2) Mark 9 (1.10x) can pass by chance on a noisy host or in a fixed run order. The same 3M B2 config spans 6.41 to 7.14 steps/s across three seeds on rented boxes (shown, RESULT.json), about an 11% spread, so one pair proves nothing; ABAB and the A/A band guard against this. (3) Gates 6 to 8 can pass trivially if the new path never runs (flag default off, or precomputed arrays ignored in favour of the in-forward code). The call counter in mark 6 guards this. With the ABAB and A/A controls the chance of a false speed pass is low (suggested). The equality gates check the function, so they cannot show a speed gain.
plan.autonomy: Training-side speed only. What the deployed model does is unchanged: its forward still tokenizes numbers and words, places characters and builds the executor from the prompt inside the model. The ledger.py tokenize and reader.py batch_places paths remain the one code path whenever no precomputed arrays are passed. No orchestrator, worker or researcher step runs at deploy; DataLoader workers, if ever used, exist only in training. Rule 1 status is unchanged: the regex and word-split hand code stays in the forward path, which is a separate, already-known issue, not fixed or worsened here. Rule 10 is neutral because building and pre-training happen before the model ships.
steps: Step 1, preconditions (about 0.1 h, CPU). The PC and its CPU are idle (q39, the first look, C0 and PT13 finished). Record the CPU model, cores and clocks. Confirm the 8a build commit is checked out, because the names g8a, plain_lm and plain_tf_steps_g are absent from this checkout. Rebuild the 3M pool and check its train sha256 against box.json (910485f16cc6aa5a546bacf8d53f735b4ce00a6a44ecd9be84cfac5505829a8b). Stop if it differs.

Step 2, premise check C (about 0.1 h GPU). Run the sustained command on the PC at 200 and at 600 updates, log every 50. Compute mark 1. If the I2 probe script is recoverable, read how it built batches (prebuilt or reused, fresh process, bf16, memory cap) and record it; otherwise record the probe's batch source as unknown. Record the PC's steady live step ms for mark 2.

Step 3, Step 0b CPU only (about 0.2 h). Time 50 batches of 256 at 8a caps for collate, gold CPU part, batch_places and spans, in a fresh process (cold) and on a second pass (warm). Record padded length, mean words, numbers and program steps per row. Compute mark 2. The CPU timing is not a GPU claim.

Step 4, GPU timing on an idle card (about 1.2 h, suggested; PC speed at G caps is not measured). (a) A/A, ABAB, at least 4 pairs of 600 updates. (b) Replay, same seed and order, at least 4 pairs, via the test-only monkeypatch described in arm B. (c) torch.profiler over 50 steady updates and set_sync_debug_mode('warn') over 20 updates. (d) Scaling at 128, 256 and 512 (or 256 only if 512 does not fit). Log per-run CPU and GPU state.

Step 5, decide with marks 3 to 5, fixed before any run. Write one verdict per shape: 3M at G caps is the measured shape; 3M at q33 caps only if time allows; 10M and 30M are not measured here (rented boxes need Ben's OK).

Step 6, only if the ladder allows edit 1: a flag, default off and recorded in box.json. Cache OMEGA, CONSTS and COMM per device. Pack the tokenize and gold arrays into one pinned int64 buffer with one non_blocking copy. Keep prompt numbers int64. Drop the one_hot change unless set_sync_debug_mode shows a sync. Run gates 6 to 8, CPU first, then GPU. Edit 2 (worker loader, batch sampler replaying train_batches' RandomState(seed) permutation, only offsets as int32) runs only if the ladder allows, with the same gates.
Step 7, final pass (mark 9): at least 5 ABAB pairs of 600 updates, flag on versus off, on the PC at G caps. Report with the A/A band beside it.

Step 8, write-up: parameters unchanged (same n_params), gates 6 to 8 passed, the copies removed listed by line, the profile split reported, and the note that the deployed forward still computes spans and places itself. Speed-only: no accuracy mark moves. The benefit is also bounded. A constant 50 ms host cost is about 35% of a 3M step (50/140), about 15% of a 10M step (50/327 on the probe times) and about 7% of a 30M step (50/679), about 0.8 h of an 11 h 30M seed (suggested, assumes the cost does not depend on model size).

issues: WRONG HARDWARE FOR THE QUESTION. The 50 ms gap is between the rented-5090 probe (0.092 s per update, 8A-SPEC addendum I2) and the rented-5090 sustained 8a runs (interval medians 0.1400, 0.1394, 0.1552 s over 47 intervals each, seeds 401/402/405; shown from stdout.events.txt). The plan tests only on the PC (RTX 5070 Ti). The 5090 boxes are destroyed after collection (addendum H; shown), and renting is barred while the PC is free (rule 6). So the planned runs can say whether the PC's B2 step is prep-bound, not whether the box gap was prep. As worded, the question cannot be answered by the planned runs.

THE SIGN OF THE GAP CUTS AGAINST THE PLAN'S OWN EXPLANATION. A fresh 200-update probe has all caches cold (spans 0% hits, place 0%, gold 0%; ledger.py:203-204, reader.py:36-37, progparse.py:185-193), so under a host-prep-only story it should be equal or slower than the sustained run, not about 50 ms faster. The probe (0.092) is faster than the first 500-step interval of seed 401 (about 0.145; shown). Only three explanations fit: the probe used prebuilt or repeated batches, a much smaller or cache-resident row set, or another host. Its peak memory (6.3 GB, I2 table) matches the sustained peak (6,462.6 MiB; shown in RESULT.json), which suggests the same config, so the data path is the likely difference. The plan lists these explanations but has no test that separates them, and the probe script is not in the snapshot.

MARK 2 AND STEP 3 USE A WARM SECOND PASS. A second pass over the same 50 batches (12,800 rows, under the spans-cache clear limit of 20,000 at ledger.py:203-204) is about 100% cache hits. Training hits about 0.7% of spans and, by the plan's own arithmetic, about 14% of place ids (suggested). So 'warm steady state' underestimates the prep the training loop pays, and biases the test toward stopping. Only cold (unseen) rows represent training.
STEP 4 (about 1.2 h of GPU) IS NOT GATED BY STEP 3 (CPU prep). Mark 2 says stop below 5%, but the step list runs Step 4 unconditionally. Step 4 must be conditional on Step 3.

EDIT 1 CANNOT REACH THE REPLAY BOUND. Mark 4's replay removes CPU compute (regex in spans, word and place code, gold array fills, collate) and 18 of the 21 host-device copies. Edit 1 only caches three constants and packs arrays into one pinned copy. The 21 copies are small transfers (shown: ledger.py:217, 222, 292, 454, 502; reader.py:40; data.py:132), each tens of microseconds (suggested), so edit 1 saves well under 2 ms of a 146 ms step. A mark-4 result of 1.15 or more therefore leads to an edit that will almost surely fail mark 9. The edit that matches the replay is a per-row precompute at load (or a worker), which needs a memory check.

MARK 5 MISREADS PER-ROW HOST WORK. Host prep scales with rows, as GPU work does, so a prep-bound step gives t(512)/t(128) near 4, and mark 5 would call it GPU-bound (at least 3.0). Scaling separates fixed overhead (launch) from per-row cost, not host from GPU. The plan's sentence 'Scaling separates host from GPU' is wrong.

MARK 1 COMPARES A MEAN WITH A MEDIAN. The short probe uses the mean of all 200 updates (including start-up); the long run uses the median of updates 101 to 600. Use the same statistic and window. The 10% band has no measured PC noise basis; the 8a boxes differed by about 11% in steps/s (6.41 to 7.14; RESULT.json, shown), but that spread is between hosts.

THE DECISION RULES CONFLICT. Mark 2 allows the worker test at 15% or more prep share; mark 4 allows only edit 1 with no workers when the replay is 1.05 to 1.15. No precedence is given. The replay (mark 4) should override the prep-share mark.

MARK 9 STATISTICS ARE WEAK. The 'outside the A/A band' rule uses the range of 4 to 5 A/A pairs. For exchangeable ratios, a new ratio exceeds the maximum of 4 with probability about 1/5 (suggested), so the band adds false negatives and gives little protection against false passes. Use 'every ABAB pair at least 1.10 and median at least 1.10' instead.
MARK 6 USES np.array_equal, WHICH IGNORES DTYPE, DEVICE AND CONTIGUITY. A packed or precomputed array can pass the value check and still change dtype or device. The gate must check all four.

MARK 7 IS LOOSE AND MOSTLY REDUNDANT. A 2x band on the A/A loss divergence is wide. If gate 6 holds (identical inputs) and no other code changes, training is identical up to GPU nondeterminism. Keep gate 6 as the gate and treat mark 7 as a check.

MARK 8 CANNOT USE THE q33 CHECKPOINT AT G CAPS. The reader position table is nn.Embedding(MAX_PROMPT, d) (reader.py:72). q33 uses MAX_PROMPT 208 and G caps use 280 (box.json caps; addendum G), so the checkpoint's table shape cannot match. The 'if it loads' clause is void. Only a seeded random-init model is a meaningful identity check.

NUMBERS THAT DO NOT RECONCILE. (a) The 30M per-seed time in the plan (about 11 h) conflicts with addendum I3 (about 13 h) and the I2 table (16.0 h for all arms). I3's own B2 figure does not reproduce: 0.503 s x 58,594 updates is about 8.2 h (two parts), and 0.679 s x 58,594 is about 11.05 h (four parts). (b) Updates: I2 uses 58,594; addendum C says about 62,000. (c) The 10M percentage uses the two-part time (327 ms) and the 30M percentage the four-part time (679 ms). If prep runs once per micro-batch under accumulation (untested; accumulation code not in the checkout), four parts times 50 ms is 200 ms, about 30% of 679 ms, not 7%.

THE PREMISE IS STALE AND THE PAYBACK IS AT 30M, NOT 3M. Three 3M seeds are already complete on rented boxes (401, 402, 405; RESULT.json, shown). The brief's 'has not run' is out of date. Approximate pooled-5 from final_eval and the brief's split sizes (my arithmetic, approximate): B2 about 73.2, 74.1, 71.4 against plain_tf_steps about 66.2, 66.4, 66.1. At 3M, a 35% cut to B2 saves about 0.33 h per box (3,423 s x 0.35), so the remaining seeds (400, 403, 404; status not checked here) save about 1 h, less than the test's 1.5 h. The payback case is the 30M rung on the PC, which is sealed and awaiting Ben.

ZERO-COST EVIDENCE THE PLAN DOES NOT USE. In each B2 log, steps 500 to 5,000 (the first epoch, when every gold lookup and almost every place lookup misses) run 6 to 8 ms per step slower than steps 5,500 onward: seed 401 0.1454 vs 0.1390, seed 402 0.1446 vs 0.1383, seed 405 0.1615 vs 0.1538 (shown, stdout.events.txt). This caps the cache-sensitive share at about 8 ms per step. The plan's claim that the gold cache misses only the first 5,542 steps is correct (data.py:135-143 uses one permutation per epoch; shown). So the gap, if it is prep, sits in the uncached spans, collate and array-fill path.

LOCAL CPU CHECK (this session, not the PC). The NUM and word regexes on 256 synthetic 240-character prompts take about 5 ms per batch (suggested; synthetic text on this CPU). The regex is therefore not the 50 ms by itself. The likely heavy item is place_ids' per-word torch loop (reader.py:17-23), which is untested; Step 3 must time it cold.

THE CODE FACTS ARE FROM THE q33 CHECKOUT, NOT THE 8a BUILD. plain_lm, plain_tf_steps_g and g8a are absent from the code (grep; shown), though they appear in the 8a run logs. The 21-copy count, cache sizes and code paths were read from the q33 code. The 8a build raises MAX_PROMPT to 280 and uses 36 registers and 91 numbers (box.json). The plan labels these '(shown)' without that qualifier; verify them on the 8a commit first.

PROBE SOLO STATUS IS UNVERIFIED. Addendum H (line 397) plans that 'a seventh 5090 runs the probe alone'. That is a plan, not a result, and the I2 text does not say solo (shown). Sharing would make the probe slower, so this does not rescue the prep explanation, but the plan must not cite it as clean.

HOURS ARE UNDERSTATED. Step 1 (0.1 h) assumes the 3M pool can be rebuilt on the PC from FineWeb-Edu shards 0 and 1. The box built the pool in 254.9 s once its data was present (box.json; shown), but the PC's shard download and build time is unknown (untested). The 1.5 h figure also leaves out the final pass (about 0.5 h), which is counted only in the edit branch.

RULE 5 AND THE POOL. The 8a pool (train sha256 910485f1...) has not passed the protected-panel overlap check. Ben's 'Start now' and addendum A1 allow training before the check, so this is not a new violation. The plan should still say its gates trained on an unchecked pool, and that any flagged document must leave the pool before 8c. caps.json also lists 'dev' in its source (shown); it is a design constant and not used by this timing test. Separately, the 8a B2 shape is outside the plus-or-minus 3% size band (events 'size': inside false, vs_plain_tf_pct 3.14; shown). That does not change a speed test but does matter for the rung's marks.
NAMING INCONSISTENCY. Mark 2 refers to 'Step 0b' while the step list calls it Step 3. Low risk, but an operator could run the wrong step.

VERIFIED AND NOT ISSUES. box.json arm wall times sum to the box wall time (3,423.4 + 589.4 + 790.4 + 254.9 = 5,058.1 s), so the arms ran back to back and B2 is solo in the 8a runs (shown). Steps per second, the 0.146 s three-seed mean, the peak of 6,462.6 MiB, and the PT (0.0236) and LLM (0.032) medians all match (shown). The 21-copy count, the spans-cache clear at 20,000 and the place-cache clear at 400,000 match the q33 code (shown). The first-look B2 runs shared their card four ways (FIRST-LOOK amendment 2; shown). A/A control: P1 against P1 in ABAB order (noise band).
C1 cold CPU prep timing: per-batch time of collate, gold CPU part, batch_places, spans and place_ids on 50 batches of rows not yet seen in the process. No second warm pass.

pass_marks: M1 (cache sensitivity): median steps/s of P2 divided by P1 is at least 1.15, AND each of the 4 ABAB pairs is at least 1.10. Stop the 3M speed work if the median is under 1.05. Between 1.05 and 1.15: input prep is a minor cost; no code edit.
M2 (noise): A/A median ratio within 0.97 to 1.03. If it falls outside, repeat the A/A once; if it still falls outside, the timing is not usable and the test is reported as failed.
M3 (prep share, cold rows): cold prep ms per 256-row batch divided by the PC's live P1 step ms. An edit is considered only if M1 passes AND the share is at least 15%.

M4 (probe mechanism, from Z0): the probe gap counts as explained by cache residency only if Z0 shows the probe used a small or repeated row set, or prebuilt batches. Otherwise the probe gap is reported as unexplained.
M5 (scaling): batch-size scaling (128/256/512) is not used as a host-or-GPU verdict, because per-row costs scale with batch for both prep and GPU.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: If P2 over P1 is under 1.05, cache-resident rows do not speed up B2, so input caching is not the 50 ms and the 3M speed work stops. If Z0 shows the probe had the same row source and cache state as the sustained runs, the gap is not explained by prep and is reported as unexplained.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Low to moderate. A P2 speed-up could come from something other than input work (the smaller pool also changes gold targets and collate, which are input work too, so this is acceptable). Thermal drift is controlled by ABAB order. The 4-consistent-pairs rule limits false passes. A false 'not prep' result is possible if the PC's cache behaviour differs from the 8a boxes; that is stated as a limit.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Training-side timing only. The deployed model is unchanged: at deploy the forward still tokenizes numbers and words, places characters and builds the executor from the prompt itself (ledger.py tokenize, reader.py place_ids). Any later edit is a training-only precompute that must not change the model's inputs. No orchestrator or researcher step at deploy, so rule 10 is neutral. Step 2 (about 0.1 h GPU): idle-check the PC (nvidia-smi, top). Run P1 for 200 and 600 updates and record the live steady step ms as the median of updates 101 to 600 (same statistic as the probe comparison).

Step 3 (about 0.2 h CPU): cold C1 timing on 50 batches of unseen rows, timing collate, gold CPU part, batch_places, spans and place_ids separately. Report ms per batch and the share of Step 2's step. No second warm pass.

Step 4 (about 0.8 h GPU): 4 ABAB pairs of 600 updates, P1 against P2, G caps, identical config; first 100 updates discarded; median steps/s per run. Plus 4 A/A pairs of P1 against P1. Optional PT control (2 pairs) if time allows.

Step 5 (decision, marks fixed in advance): apply M1 to M5. If M1 fails, stop the 3M speed work and report the 50 ms as not explained by input caching. If M1 passes but M3 is under 15%, no code edit; report the P1/P2 result as the cache effect only. If M1 and M3 both pass, go to Step 6.

Step 6 (only if Step 5 passes; training-side, flag off by default, recorded in box.json): precompute per-row spans, place ids and gold targets once at load into arrays, instead of copy packing. Memory check on the 16 GB PC with the full pool (shard by row index if needed). Keep the forward code and the deploy path unchanged. Gates: every array's values, dtype, shape, device and contiguity equal on 200 batches for seeds 400 to 405 (CPU); run() and talk() identical on 500 dev rows for a seeded random-init model (not the q33 checkpoint). Then 5 ABAB pairs at G caps: every pair at least 1.05 and median at least 1.10.

Step 7 (write-up): report the P1/P2 ratio, the cold prep share, the A/A band, the probe status (explained, unexplained or unknown), and these limits: the rented-5090 gap is not re-measured (those boxes are gone); 10M and 30M shares are not measured; no accuracy claim.

Step 8 (only if the 30M rung is to run on the PC): a 200-update 30M probe on the PC to get the PC's 30M step, and the share of the cold prep ms in it. This is the payback test, since prep ms is roughly the same at every rung (same caps).

The fixed plan is the right shape: it uses unchanged code, a real-versus-cache-resident pool contrast and an A/A control, and it stops the speed work early if the pools run at the same speed. The expected saving is only suggested, not measured. If the cost is a constant ~50 ms of host prep, it is worth about 35% of a 3M step, 15% of a 10M step and 7% of a 30M step, roughly 8-10 PC hours over the remaining 10M and 30M seeds and the coming 3M screens. The cost is 1.5 to 3 PC hours, with a roughly 40% chance the cause is host prep at all (suggested). Training-side only, so rules 1, 3, 7 and 10 are untouched. idea.title: Build workspace keys and values once per forward
idea.summary: Every round recomputes the key and value projections of all workspace slots, including the number and constant slots (20 at q33, 95 at addendum-G caps) that never change within a forward. Compute those once and recompute only the result slots each round. Same numbers, fewer FLOPs, less saved activation memory, which matters for fitting 30M in 16 GB.
idea.change: ledger.py run(), lines 307-310: before the loop compute kvs0 = [b.kv_of(S0 + src.weight[0]) for b in core]; each round compute kvsR from Rs only and concatenate in the order [S0, Rs] as today. Same for the per-step pointer keys k_slot(ln_k(cat(S0, Rs))) at lines 326 and 345 (split S0 and Rs parts). 0 params.
idea.why: I read the code: S0 is built once before the loop and S = cat(S0, Rs) with a constant src offset, so S0 keys and values are identical every round. S0 keys and values are 7.5% of fwd+bwd FLOPs at q33 (20 of 27 slots) and 15.7% at G caps (95 of 106), and about 16% of saved activations at G 3M (suggested model that overshoots measured peaks by about 1.4x). B2 runs at about half of plain's achieved rate on the 5090 at G caps.

evidence.claim: S0 is computed once before the loop; kvs = kv_of(S + src.weight[0]) with S = cat(S0, Rs) is rebuilt every round for every block; k_slot(ln_k(cat(S0, Rs))) is rebuilt at each program step.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: S0 share of fwd+bwd FLOPs: 7.5% at q33 caps, 15.7% at addendum-G caps (arithmetic from slot counts; not timed).
evidence.label: shown

problems: Not new in the snapshot (shown): models/tool.py:138 already builds kvs0 = kv_of(S0 + src.weight[0]) once before its loop, tool.py:155 concatenates kvs0 with the per-round tape KV (torch.cat(..., 3)), and tool.py:192 rebuilds the tape KV only when a tape entry is written. The T1 model (queue_local/40-pc-t1-screen.txt, 3,277,393 params) carries this pattern and has not run. The proposal's closest_prior field misses it. The real change is a port of tool.py's pattern into ledger.py, with no measurement in the snapshot.

The stated memory mechanism is only partly right (mechanism shown from code; size suggested). ledger.py:120 (CBlock.forward) concatenates the S and X keys and values every block and every round, and attention keeps k and v for backward, so the S0 rows of K and V are still saved every round under D5. What D5 removes is the per-round LayerNorm input and projection input for the S0 rows (ledger.py:113-115 kv_of). Rough arithmetic (suggested): at G caps that is about 2 x 95 x 256 values per example per block-round, roughly 10-15% of the about 1 MB per example per block-round implied by 6.3 GB / (256 x 24) (8A-SPEC section 19, I2). The 16% figure is the wrong quantity, though its size may be in range. The 0.90x memory bar is a fair test.

Speed does not follow the FLOP share (suggested). The 15.7% figure is FLOP arithmetic. The measured 3M B2 step at G caps is 0.092 s per update on a 5090 (8A-SPEC section 19, I2). My estimate of about 2.8 TFLOP per update (from the ledger shapes, reader length assumed 150, untested) gives about 30 TFLOP/s, a small fraction of peak, so the step is probably memory- and launch-bound. As written, D5 adds a second torch.cat per block per round (the proposed S0 plus Rs concatenation, on top of ledger.py:120), so the copy traffic can cancel the saved projection. The 1.08x steps/s bar is optimistic, and a no-gain or slower result is plausible.

The test checks only forward logits (shown in the proposal). D5 changes the autograd path: the S0 key and value gradients now sum across rounds in a different order. 8A-SPEC section 17, addendum G2, sets the bar for the same kind of change: loss and gradients within 1e-5 relative, and identical predictions on 1,000 dev rows. D5 should use that bar, including gradients.

The mask changes every round. ledger.py:336-337 sets valid for each written result, and ledger.py:311 builds mask = cat([valid, xm]) every round. The proposal does not say the mask must be rebuilt per round. A version that reuses one mask would attend to unwritten result slots and be silently wrong.

The G-caps test cannot run from this checkout (shown: the q33 shape here has 27 slots, 8 rounds and 9 registers; addendum H cites build commit 50ee171632, which is not present). The 106-slot, 44-token, 12-round shape needs that build. The q33 shape (20 S0 slots, 7 result slots) can be tested now.

Citations and details are off (shown). The pointer-key computations are at ledger.py:322 and ledger.py:343, not 326 and 345 (326 is the no-gold argmax line; 345 is the answer and word pointer line that uses the keys). The concatenation axis is not given. The stacked kv tensor is (2,B,h,T,dh), so the T axis is dim 3, as tool.py:155 uses; dim 2 would be wrong on the stacked tensor.

Lesion paths checked (shown). shuffle_state and zero_state act on the final state in models/base.py:55-56, not inside the loop. ctl27 changes only Z (ledger.py:315-316). noexec zeroes result writes (ledger.py:334-335). opswap changes only the op (ledger.py:332). None alters S0 or Rs per round, so the premise holds for ledger.py as it stands.

Unsourced ratio. The proposal says B2 runs at about half of plain's achieved rate at G caps. The I2 table gives B2 0.092 s against plain 0.023 s per update at 3M, a 4.0x time ratio (shown). No plain FLOP count is in the snapshot, so the half-rate figure is untested here.

The decision-relevant number is missed. At 30M, B2 runs in 4 parts at 15 GB (0.679 s per update) or 2 parts at 18.5 GB (0.503 s) (8A-SPEC section 19, I2). Under the 15 GB limit, a 2-part run needs about a 19% cut per part (suggested arithmetic). D5 alone is suggested at 10-15%, so it probably does not change the part count alone. The proposal does not name this threshold.
critiques.rescue: Port tool.py's precompute into ledger.py, in a better layout. Once per forward, per block, build fixed = cat(kv_of(S0 + src.weight[0]), kv_of(X + src.weight[1])) (keys ordered [S0, X]). Each round, compute kv_of(Rs + src.weight[0]) only, then one cat per block of [fixed, kvRs], which is the same copy count as CBlock's cat today. Rebuild mask = cat(valid0, xm, validR) every round. This removes the S0 LayerNorm and projection each round and adds no extra cat. Pre-registered tests: (a) q33 shape now, fp32 CPU, 1,000 dev rows: max abs logit difference at most 1e-5, identical argmax, and max relative gradient difference at most 1e-5 on every parameter (the G2 bar), with identical predictions. (b) PC bf16, 200 updates, 3 repeats: peak allocated at most 0.90x and median steps/s at least 1.05x, both fixed before running. Proved wrong: gradients or predictions beyond the bar, peak above 0.95x, or steps/s at most 1.0x. (c) Run the G-caps version only from the build commit, and report the number of 30M micro-batch parts under a 15 GB limit as the decision number.
critiques.already_tried: Partly, in the code. models/tool.py:138 (kvs0 once before the loop), tool.py:155 (per-round concatenation with the tape KV), tool.py:192 (tape KV recomputed only on write). The T1 model is queue_local/40-pc-t1-screen.txt, not yet run. models/ledger.py:302 already computes the reader KV once per forward (kvx). models/register_loop.py:75 does the same for X. No speed or memory measurement with or without the S0 precompute exists in this snapshot. Addendum G2 (8A-SPEC section 17) is a related allowed speed-up (per-batch slot sizes) and sets the equality bar this idea should use. Peak memory for B2 at q33 caps is 2,872.9 MiB (results/40-egw-s200/B2V_s200/RESULT.json, shown).
critiques.expected_effect: Same function, 0 new parameters, no mark changed, so the rules are not broken: rule 3 (same function and size), rule 4 (an equality and speed test, not a model claim), rule 6 (about 0.4 h on the PC), no teacher, no truncation, no deploy-time step. Expected (suggested, untested): peak activation memory at G caps down by roughly 5-15%, and steps/s between about 0.95x and 1.1x. The change matters only if it changes the 30M micro-batch part count under 15 GB, which needs about a 19% per-part cut, and D5 alone is unlikely to reach that. Worth running only after the equality test with gradients is in place.

problems: AUTONOMY WALK-THROUGH (rule 10): PASSES. Build time: one edit to run() in ledger.py (engineering, before shipping). Deploy time: each forward builds the S0 key and value rows once, then runs the same rounds and steps as today. No value is tuned, no tool is added, no data is read, and no orchestrator step exists. The only human steps are the equality and timing checks, which run before shipping. shown: ledger.py 295-297 (S0 built once), 307-310 (kvs rebuilt per round from cat(S0, Rs)), 322 and 343 (pointer keys).

SAME-FUNCTION PREMISE HOLDS. S0 is fixed inside one run(): vals and valid for slots 0..R0-1 are set at ledger.py 293-297 and never rewritten; only Rs and result-slot validity change. kv_of is LayerNorm then Linear per token (ledger.py 113-115), so splitting S into S0 and Rs is exact in real arithmetic. The attention mask (valid, xm) is not in the K/V path. No dropout exists in ledger.py, reader.py or CBlock (grep shows only .eval()/.train() calls). Lesions ctl27, noexec, opswap and nowordc do not touch S0 (ledger.py 315-337). shown.

CACHE SCOPE. The cache must live only inside one run() call. A module-level or cross-call cache would be wrong if a future tool wrote into number or constant slots (for example a calculator-as-tool design). Writes to result slots (Rs) are safe. suggested.

PREMISE ERROR. 'B2 runs at about half of plain's achieved rate on the 5090 at G caps' is not supported. 8A-SPEC addendum I2 (lines 417-419, shown): solo 5090 at G caps, B2 0.092 s per update vs PT 0.023 (B2 about 4.0x slower) and plain LLM 0.032. The 8a event logs (shown): 8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2, s402-B2 and s405-B2 run at 7.09, 7.14 and 6.41 steps/s against their PT arms at 42.32, 42.06 and 38.89 (about 6x). box.json has no field saying whether the arms shared the card, so treat the event-log ratio as indicative. If 'half' means FLOP utilisation, the snapshot has no source for it (untested). Correct the premise before reading the 1.08x speed mark.

FLOP SHARE. The 7.5% (q33) and 15.7% (G caps) figures do not state the reader length T_X, which sets the cross-attention cost. My recount (suggested, my arithmetic, not timed): S0 key, value and pointer-key work is about 10% of block plus pointer forward MACs at q33 (17 tokens, 27 slots, T_X about 208) and about 17% at G caps (44 tokens = 8 control + 36 registers, 106 slots, 12 rounds, 2 blocks, T_X about 280). That is consistent with the idea's figures, but T_X must be stated. The rest of the controller (44 tokens x 12 rounds x 2 blocks) is untouched, so the realised speedup is probably nearer 1.1-1.2x if compute-bound. The extra cat and split ops per round and per step add kernel launches on a launch-bound 3M model, which may cut the gain further (suggested). The 1.08x mark is plausible but not assured.

MEMORY CLAIM OVERSTATED. The cache removes only the LayerNorm input and output saves and the k_slot input saves for S0 rows (ledger.py 113-115, 322). The S0 keys and values are still saved every round, because CBlock.forward concatenates them with the reader's K and V (ledger.py 120) and SDPA saves the concatenated tensors. The fp32 key copies made inside ptr (ledger.py 229) are also rebuilt per call. My count (suggested, untested) at G caps: about 190 d saved per block-round and per pointer call, about 6.3k d of about 50-53k d saved per forward, so the peak ratio is about 0.88-0.89. The idea's '16% of saved activations' is its own model, which it says overshoots measured peaks by about 1.4x. At q33 caps the saving is about 6% (about 0.94x). The 0.90x mark passes only narrowly, and the '<5% = proved wrong' line is the likelier fail if the count is off. Weights and optimizer state are small (about 50 MB at 3M against a 6.3 GB peak), so activations dominate the peak. The idea's two measured peaks are real: 8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json line 10394 (6,462.6 MiB at G caps) and 40-egw-s200/B2V_s200/RESULT.json (2,872.9 MiB; config copy=true, 3,302,481 params, batch 256, bf16, shown).

CITATION ERRORS. The idea cites ledger.py lines 326 and 345 for the per-step pointer keys. Line 326 is the greedy argmax on the inference branch. The in-loop key build is line 322, and the post-loop key build is line 343 (used at line 345). Lines 295-297, 307-310 and 113-124 are correct.

SKETCH DETAIL. The src.weight[0] offset is added to the whole S (ledger.py 310), so the Rs part needs the same offset in kv_of(Rs + src.weight[0]). The sketch as written would change the function. The equality test would catch this, so it is a fix to the text, not a flaw in the idea. suggested.

TEST DESIGN. The fp32 CPU equality test (max abs logit difference at most 1e-5, 1,000 dev rows) is a valid hand-written engineering check under rule 1. It adds no parameters and no RNG draws. problems: Premise checks out (shown, ledger.py): S0 is built once before the loop (lines 295-297). The memory claim is overstated about 2x (shown by my count, magnitude suggested). The change removes only the LayerNorm input and output for the S0 rows, 2*S0*d per block-round. Calibration (suggested): my G-cap count gives about 13.4M saved values per example, about 6.4 GiB at batch 256 in bf16, close to the measured 6.3 GB (8A-SPEC addendum I2).
