chair.reasons:
PLAN, low priority. It is cheap, exact and breaks no rule, but the payoff is small and the stated reasons for it are partly wrong.

Premise (shown). I re-read ledger.py. S0 is built once before the loop (about lines 293-297). Each round it rebuilds kvs = kv_of(cat(S0, Rs) + src.weight[0]) for every block (lines 308-310). The pointer keys k_slot(ln_k(cat(S0, Rs))) are rebuilt at line 322 inside the step loop and at line 343 after it. Nothing in the key/value path depends on the round for the S0 rows, so caching is exact in real arithmetic. models/tool.py lines 137-138 and 155 already do this (kvs0 once, per-round cat on dim 3 of the stacked kv). The idea is a port of that pattern into ledger.py, and the T1 design (queue 40) already carries it.

Rules (rules, autonomy and mechanism critics agree). It adds 0 params and keeps the same function. No deploy-time step, tuned value or truncation is involved. Rule 10 passes. The cache must live only inside one run().

Why only low priority, from the critics:
(a) The memory story is mis-stated (shown mechanism). CBlock.forward (line 120) re-concatenates the S0 keys and values with the reader's every block and round, and SDPA saves that concatenation. D5 removes only the S0 LayerNorm input/output saves (plus part of the pointer-key saves). Estimates range from 4% to 16% of saved activations, central about 10% (suggested, untested).
(b) The speed ceiling is small. The S0 share of forward MACs is about 7.5% at q33 and 15.7% at G caps (suggested arithmetic that needs T_X stated). That caps the compute-bound speedup at about 1.07x and 1.17x. The step is probably launch- and memory-bound. I2 in 8A-SPEC (shown) puts B2 at 4.0x the plain time per update at 3M (0.092 vs 0.023 s), 4.7x at 10M and 4.6x at 30M. That gap comes mostly from rounds, steps and executor clones, which D5 does not touch. The idea's premise 'about half of plain's rate' is wrong.
(c) It will not change the 30M part count (suggested). I2 (shown) gives 0.679 s per update in 4 parts at 15 GB, and 0.503 s in 2 parts needing 18.5 GB. Fitting 2 parts under 15 GB needs about a 19% cut, which D5 alone does not give. The motivation 'fits 30M in 16 GB' is not supported.
(d) The value only arrives if the 30M rung runs. 8a stops if B2's 10M minus 3M is below 0, and the 2-seed first look was weak (+1.42 and -0.28). A 5-12% speedup at 30M is worth about 0.7-1.5 h per seed of about 13 h (suggested).
(e) The ship design is B3/T1 on tool.py, which already has the pattern. 8a's B2 cannot ship (roadmap 4.1), so the benefit stays inside 8a.
(f) It overlaps addendum G2 (slot trimming) on the same S0 term. The two do not stack in marginal gain.
(g) The 3M rung is already training on rented 5090s without D5. Adopting it later puts the 10M and 30M B2 runs on a different code version. That is the same function, but bf16 rounding differs, so it needs a sealed addendum.

The staged test below keeps the zero-GPU parts first and gates the GPU parts on the 30M rung actually being run.
chair.revised_idea:
Port the tool.py precompute into ledger.py run(), as an exact-equality speed and memory change with 0 params. Do it only as a sealed addendum that applies to rungs not yet started.

Implementation. Once per forward and per block, build fixed = cat(kv_of(S0 + src.weight[0]), kvx), with keys ordered [S0, X]. Each round, compute only kv_of(Rs + src.weight[0]), including the src offset, then do one cat per block of [fixed, kvRs] on the token axis. That is dim 3 of the stacked [2,B,h,T,dh] tensor, or dim 2 of kvs[0] and kvs[1]. This is the same number of cats as today. Rebuild the mask each round as cat(valid_S0, xm, valid_Rs), so unwritten result slots stay masked. Split the pointer keys at ledger.py 322 and 343 into a cached S0 part and a per-step Rs part. Keep the cache local to one run() call. Cite the pointer-key lines as 322/323/343/345. All arms of a rung must use one commit.

Staged test with pass marks fixed now:
(1) Mac or PC CPU, minutes, no GPU. Use the trained q33 checkpoint code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 at the q33 shape (the G build is not in this checkout). Check fp32, and float64 for the gradient step: loss, and the gradient of every parameter, within a relative difference of 1e-5 by tensor norm (the G2 bar). Predictions must be identical on 1,000 dev rows. Run it intact and with the lesions noexec, nocopy, ctl27, opswap, nowordc, loops:16 and rounds=True. Proved wrong: any gradient or prediction beyond the bar.
(2) CPU, minutes. Count saved-tensor bytes with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks, old vs new, at the G-caps shape (T_X about 280, 106 slots, 44 controller tokens, 12 rounds, batch 8) once the G build commit is available. Pass: new is at most 0.92x of old. Kill: at least 0.96x. In between: report only, and judge speed alone.
(3) Gate for the GPU steps: run (3) and (4) only if the 8a 3M-to-10M result (when it arrives, alongside the speed probe) leaves the 30M rung going. In the speed probe, profile one 30M step with torch.profiler. Kill if the S0 key/value path takes under 7% of CUDA time.
(4) Solo box, interleaved A/B/A/B at the I2 probe shape (5090, 15 GB limit), at least 5 pairs plus an old-vs-old null pair. Record seconds per update, allocated and reserved peak, and the micro-batch part count. Pass: median paired speedup at least 1.05x and outside the null band, with allocated peak at most 0.93x. Kill: speedup at most 1.00x, or allocated peak at least 0.96x. In between: report only, no adoption.

Do not claim it changes the 30M part count. Re-measure after G2 if G2 is adopted. If it passes, record it as an addendum to the sealed spec with the equality result before any 10M or 30M B2 run uses it.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must get these right.

1. Premise and precedent. The S0 key/value premise holds (shown, ledger.py about 293-297, 308-310, 322, 343). tool.py:137-138 and 155 already do this. The change is a port, not a new mechanism.

2. Correct the stated mechanism and numbers. Memory saved is mostly the S0 LayerNorm in/out saves, not S0 K/V, which the per-round cat and SDPA still save. Expect about 4-16% of saved activations, central about 10% (suggested). The speed ceiling is about 1.07x at q33 and 1.17x at G caps if compute-bound (suggested). State T_X (about 200 at q33, 280 at G caps) next to the 7.5% and 15.7% FLOP shares.

3. Remove the false premise that B2 runs at about half of plain's rate. Use I2 (shown): 4.0x at 3M, 4.7x at 10M, 4.6x at 30M per update. Do not claim D5 fixes the 4x gap, because most of it comes from rounds, steps and executor clones.

4. Equality. Use the G2 bar: loss and all gradients within a relative 1e-5, identical predictions on 1,000 rows. Use the trained checkpoint, not random init, because the residual init is tiny. Include the lesion paths and loops:16. bf16 will not be bitwise equal, so do the equality in fp32 and float64 only. Reorder the mask with the key order, and keep the src.weight[0] offset on the Rs keys.

5. Gating and cost control. Do the zero-GPU parts (1) and (2) first. Run the GPU timing only if the 30M rung will run (8a stops if B2's 10M minus 3M is below 0), and use the same box and memory limit as I2. Time it solo with interleaved A/B pairs and an old-vs-old null pair, because shared-GPU spread in this project is 1.6-6.7 steps/s.

6. Keep marks fixed in advance, with kill, report-only and pass bands. Report reserved as well as allocated memory. Do not claim it fixes the 30M micro-batch count (it needs about 19%, and D5 alone gives less).

7. 8a bookkeeping. This is a cost and engineering change, not a size or learning result, so no 8a mark changes. The 3M rung is already training without it, so adopt it only as a sealed addendum. All arms in a rung must share one commit. Note its overlap with G2 and that the ship design (T1/tool.py) already has the pattern.

8. Plain-language note for Ben: this makes the model faster to train without changing what it computes, so it is safe if the equality test passes. It is not a way to show that bigger is better, and the gain is probably a few percent.

plan.title: D5: cache B2's number-slot keys once per forward (same function)
plan.ben_line: This is a speed and memory fix that should not change what the model answers or learns. We first check on the trained models that answers, losses and gradients match the old code exactly, and we keep the change only if it also saves memory and time.
plan.question: Does caching B2's number and constant slot keys and values once per forward, recomputing only the result slots each round, leave the loss, every gradient and every answer on the six trained q33 checkpoints unchanged, and does it cut saved activations and step time at the 8a caps?
plan.one_change: In ledger.py run(), compute the S0 (number and constant) key/value rows and their pointer keys once per forward, as tool.py already does (tool.py lines 137-138 and 155), and recompute only the result-slot rows each round. CBlock takes the joined keys and values, so attention keys are ordered [S0, X, Rs] and the mask is rebuilt each round to match. Nothing else changes.
arms: A: current run() (reference; one commit for all of A).
B: the D5 port (the one change above).

Mutants, harness check only, never adopted: M-a result-slot keys without the src.weight[0] offset; M-b mask in [S0, Rs, X] order against [S0, X, Rs] keys; M-c one round-0 mask reused in every round. The harness must fail all three.

Timing shapes: q33 3M (2 blocks, 8 rounds, 9 registers); q33 8-block deep (B2D, 10,254,105 params; the first look measured it at 4.20 steps/s and 9,672.7 MiB allocated, shown in first-look-10m-results/B2D_s200/RESULT.json); G-caps 3M (12 rounds, 36 registers, 106 slots) and G-caps deep 10M after the build; the 30M probe only if 30M goes.
Null: A vs A, interleaved with the same batches.
plan.seeds: No training, so no training seeds. Screen: checkpoint B2_s200 (sha256 verified, shown). Six-seed confirm: B2_s200 to B2_s205 (the six q33 seeds). Dev rows: 1,000 q33 dev rows in a fixed order, row ids recorded; q33 dev only, never GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind panels (rule 5). Timing: the same seeded batches on A and B; discard 20 warm-up updates, then time 200 (fixed harness constants, not tuned).
plan.machine: CPU checks (M1, M3): BensPC CPU, where the B2 data lives (the q33 config names a Windows data folder on Ben's PC, shown), or the M1 Pro after copying the 1,000 rows and checkpoints. GPU screen (M5 at q33): BensPC RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB when idle. G-caps and 30M timing: one solo rented 5090 only with Ben's approval (addendum H precedent). Compare A and B only on the same box and the same micro-batch split.
pass_marks: M1 equality (fp64 CPU; screen B2_s200 and B2_s201, then confirm B2_s200 to B2_s205): loss, logits and every parameter gradient within 1e-5 relative (gradient compared by tensor norm, denominator floored at 1e-12); generate() answers identical on 1,000 dev rows; run(rounds=True) snapshots identical. Required under intact, noexec, opswap, ctl27, nowordc and loops:16. Pre-registered tie rule: an answer flip counts as a failure unless the fp64 top-2 margin is below 1e-6, in which case it is reported as a tie.
M2 harness check: all three mutants (M-a, M-b, M-c) must fail M1. If any passes, the harness is too weak and no other mark is read until it is fixed.

M3 saved bytes (CPU fp32, batch 8, one loss forward, torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks, bytes deduplicated by storage): pass if B/A is at most 0.92 at G caps; kill if at least 0.96; between is report only. The q33 run is a cross-check, reported only.

M4 profile gate (one 30M-shape step on an idle box, torch.profiler, run only if the 30M rung is going): S0 key/value and S0 pointer-key work at least 7% of CUDA time, else stop before timing. Suggested addition, to seal before running: also report GPU-busy fraction (kernel time over wall time); under 0.8 means launch-bound, which predicts little speed gain.

M5 timing (solo box, A and B interleaved, at least 5 pairs plus an A/A null band, same micro-batch split): pass if the median paired speedup is at least 1.05x, lies outside the null band, and allocated peak is at most 0.93x; kill if the median is at most 1.00x or allocated peak is at least 0.96x; between is report only, not adopted. Suggested addition: if the null band is wider than plus or minus 3%, speed is unreadable and the result is report-only. Report reserved peak next to allocated peak.
Screen stop (suggested, q33 8-block shape on the PC): stop before any G-caps run if the median speedup is at most 1.00x or allocated peak is at least 0.96x.
plan.proved_wrong: Any M1 difference beyond the bar on any checkpoint or lesion (the port would change the function); any mutant passing M1; saved bytes at least 0.96x at G caps (the memory saving is not real); S0 work under 7% of CUDA time; median speedup at most 1.00x, or allocated peak at least 0.96x. A median speedup inside the null band is not a gain, even if it is above 1.00x.
plan.null_risk: M1 passes for an unchanged file, so it is a correctness check, not a benefit check; M2 is what shows it can fail. M3 and the memory part of M5 cannot pass with no change, since a no-op gives 1.00x. The speed part of M5 can pass by noise: the same B2 config ran at 1.6 to 6.7 steps/s in one shared queue (shown, results/33-pc-confirm-b2), so the null band may be too wide to read. Real risks: (a) M3 sits near its line. Suggested count: about 0.91 to 0.92 for a block-only port and about 0.88 to 0.89 with the pointer-key split, so the pointer split must be in step 1. (b) Speed: at G caps B2 runs about 3 TFLOP per update in 0.092 s (shown timing; suggested arithmetic), about 30 TFLOP/s, a small share of a 5090's peak, so the step may be launch- or memory-bound. D5 removes about 15% of forward arithmetic at G caps (suggested; S0 is about 18% of block MACs) and keeps the kernel count nearly the same, so a 1.05x speed mark is less likely than not, and a speed kill is a plausible outcome. Premise correction (shown, 8A-SPEC I2): B2 is 4.0x slower per update than plain at 3M (0.092 vs 0.023 s), not about half the rate. Payoff (suggested): at most 1 to 2 hours of a roughly 16-hour 30M seed; no size, learning or 8a mark effect.
plan.autonomy: Passes rule 10. This is a same-function rewrite of B2's forward pass. A deployed model runs the same rounds, writes, pointers, mask, executor and stop logic, with no added step, no tuned value, no data read and no researcher action. The caching is internal arithmetic, not learned or tuned. The equality, memory and timing checks are build-time acceptance tests run before any rung uses the code. Rule 1: no change; the hand parts (regex spans, in-forward executor, str() printer, word splitter) stay, so this is not progress on rule 1. Rule 3: zero new parameters. Rule 7: no target is truncated. Rule 5: q33 dev rows only. No dropout or torch.compile in the ledger code (grep, shown), so both arms are deterministic on the same inputs.
steps: 1. Port (build time, in the B2 branch, not the read-only scratchpad copy). In run(): once per forward and per block, build fixed = cat(kv_of(S0 + src.weight[0]), kvx) on the token axis (dim 3 of the stacked [2,B,h,T,dh] tensor), and once per forward build the S0 pointer keys ks0 = k_slot(ln_k(S0)). Each round: kvR = kv_of(Rs + src.weight[0]) (the offset must also be added to Rs; shown: ledger.py 309-310 adds it to the whole S), keys = cat(fixed, kvR) on dim 3, and CBlock.forward uses these keys without its own cat with kvx (ledger.py line 120). If CBlock still cats kvx, X is counted twice and the mask length fails, so the run crashes rather than silently changing. Mask per round = cat(valid_S0, xm, valid_Rs). Pointer keys per step = cat(ks0, k_slot(ln_k(Rs))) with valid kept in [S0, Rs] order (ledger.py 322-323 and 343-345). Keep rounds=True snapshots and every lesion path. Reference pattern: tool.py lines 137-138, 155, 192. Per block-round this is one stacked cat instead of two (ledger.py 120), a small launch saving (suggested).

2. Harness mutants (CPU, minutes). Plant M-a, M-b and M-c. M1 must fail on each. If one passes, strengthen the harness (for example larger-norm inputs, or a direct gradient check on the offset) and repeat. Do not change the marks.

3. Screen equality (CPU fp64, B2_s200 and B2_s201, 1,000 q33 dev rows, all lesions). ptr() forces fp32 (ledger.py 227-229), so the pointer noise floor is about 1e-7, under the 1e-5 bar. Record M1 per seed and per lesion.

4. Saved bytes (CPU fp32, batch 8). Run at the q33 shape now as a cross-check (reported only). Run at the G-caps shape after the build as M3. Report the block-only and pointer-key savings separately so the effect of the split is visible.
5. Confirm equality on B2_s202 to B2_s205 with all lesions (the six-seed confirm for the checks).

6. q33 timing screen on the PC when idle: 3M and the 8-block deep shape; A and B interleaved, at least 5 pairs, plus an A/A null pair, solo; 200 updates each after 20 warm-up. Apply the screen stop. The deep shape is the better test because S0 keys repeat across 8 blocks x 8 rounds (suggested). The first look's 4.20 steps/s for the deep shape (shown) is a rough baseline only, since it was not measured as an A/B pair.

7. Only after the build commit exists (50ee171632 or b3d48f22e2; neither is in the local repo, shown): M3 and M1 at G caps. Use a trained G-caps checkpoint if one was kept (unverified; check the 8a result.tgz files). Otherwise use random init and note that the check is weak, since residual projections start at about 0.003 std at q33 (ledger.py 158-160, shown).
8. Gate: run M4 at the 30M shape only if the 8a 3M and 10M results leave the 30M rung going (spec stop rule: no 30M if 10M minus 3M is below 0; Ben decides money and time).
9. M5 at G-caps 3M and deep 10M on one solo box, same micro-batch split for A and B. Run the 30M probe (8A-SPEC section 13) only if 30M goes.

10. Adopt only if M1, M2, M3 and M5 pass; report only if a result is between bands. Record it as addendum J to the 8A spec, with the equality result, before any 10M or 30M run uses the code. All arms of a rung share one commit; the 3M rung keeps the old code, and this is disclosed. No 8a mark changes.

issues: VERDICT. The D5 port as written is not worth building now. Its best case removes about 16% of controller forward arithmetic (suggested, see item 9), which is roughly 2 to 3 h of a 30M seed, and it adds a code change between rungs that the marks cannot see. A short profile of the real training loop decides in under an hour whether any speed port can help, so that gate is worth running first.

TIMING PREMISE IS OFF (shown). The 3M B2 runs on the 8a boxes (seeds 401, 402, 405; RESULT.json and stdout.events.txt) run at about 0.145 s per update in steady state: the events at steps 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500 advance 72.6 s per 500 steps. Their steps_per_s are 7.09, 7.14 and 6.41. On the same boxes PT and LLM run at 0.024 and 0.032 s per update, which matches addendum I2 (0.023 and 0.032). Only B2 disagrees: its I2 probe figure of 0.092 s is 37% below the real loop (about 1.58x). So B2 costs about 6x plain per update in the real loop, not the 4x the plan states, and the 200-update probe reproduces a number the real run does not hit. The gap is more likely host-side work (per-batch Python in gold() and tokenize(), ledger.py 214-217 and 433-447 in the local copy) that D5 does not touch. This is suggested, not profiled.

FIRST-LOOK TIMING IS NOT A SOLO BASELINE (shown). The B2D figures (4.20 steps/s, 9,672.7 MiB) come from the first look, where FIRST-LOOK-10M Amendment 2 says all four runs of a seed share one RTX 5090. The numbers are as recorded, but they cannot anchor M5. The 3M box logs (arms run in sequence on one box) are the cleaner baseline.

THE 'OLD CODE' FRAMING IS WRONG AND CREATES A CONFOUND (shown). The 3M rung ran at build 50ee171632 (addendum H; box.json; the 'start' event), and seeds 401, 402 and 405 have finished all three arms. A port would make 10M and 30M run different code from 3M. train.py runs B2 under bf16 autocast on CUDA (train.py:132; --bf16 in the box command), and reordering a sum changes bf16 trajectories. So the 10M-minus-3M comparison (mark 1) would mix code with size. An fp64 forward and one-batch gradient check does not show that training is unchanged. Cheapest fixes: re-run the 3M rung on the new commit (cost per box $0.67 to $0.74 for all three arms, shown; about 1.4 h wall), or run a training A/A (same seeds, old and new commit, bf16) and show the gap is inside the seed sd (B2 sd 0.6 pooled-5, shown).

M1 CANNOT RUN AS WRITTEN (suggested from reading; torch is not installed here, so not run). M1 asks for fp64 CPU. But value_code returns float32 (ledger.py:72-73), OMEGA is float32 (ledger.py:65), and the S0 line applies vcode, an nn.Linear(93, d), to that output (ledger.py:295). A model.double() forward should fail at the first vcode call. No existing test runs a forward in fp64; the tests use .double() only for weight checksums (tests/test_ledger_copy.py:38-39). Options: patch the dtypes (which edits the code under test), or run fp32 with a noise floor measured by an A/A reference (same code, permuted key order), because 1e-5 relative on gradients may sit near fp32 noise. ptr() forces fp32 anyway (ledger.py:227-229), so pointer logits are fp32 in both arms.

THE EQUALITY CHECKS USE THE WRONG SHAPE (shown). The six q33 checkpoints have 8 rounds, 9 registers, 27 slots and a 16-row place table. The 8a shape has 12 rounds, 36 registers and 106 slots (addendum G; box.json cfgs). Those checkpoints cannot load into the G build. The snapshot holds no trained G-shape checkpoint: 8a-results has only result.tgz.sha256 files, and the tarballs are not here (unverified whether they hold checkpoint.pt). Plan step 7 falls back to random init, where residual outputs are small (about 0.003 std, per the plan), so mutant M-a (the missing src offset) may be too small to see. If M2 then fails, the harness is weak, not the code. Use a trained G-shape checkpoint (check the 8a tarballs on BensPC) or perturbed weights with larger offsets, and confirm each mutant moves outputs above the bar before trusting M2.

LINE NUMBERS AND COMMITS DO NOT MATCH (shown). The edit list cites the local copy (run() lines 295-310, CBlock 117-124, pointer keys 322-323, answer pointers 343-345). The rung ran build 50ee171632, and addendum G cites b3d48f22e2 with different lines (223, 287-291, 305). The port has to be made on the commit the 10M and 30M runs will use. Also, addendum G2 (per-batch slot sizing) changes the same S0 path and remaps result-slot indices, and it needs its own equality test (fp32, 1e-5, real pool batches). The plan does not say whether D5 and G2 are alternatives or can stack. G2 may remove more S0 work than caching does. The per-batch maximum number count can be measured on CPU from the pool before any GPU time is spent.

THE M3 BAR SITS ON THE PREDICTION (suggested arithmetic). Counting saved activations at G caps: S0's LayerNorm and linear inputs are about 8 to 9% of the controller's saved elements, and the reader is about 5% of the total. So the block-only port gives B/A of about 0.91 to 0.92, and the pointer split may bring it to about 0.88. The pass line is 0.92, so a block-only port passes or fails by noise. Set the line at 0.95, or report M3 only.

THE SPEED PAYOFF IS SMALL AND CONDITIONAL (shown dimensions; suggested count). At G caps S0 is 95 of 106 workspace rows (91 numbers plus 4 constants, shown). Its key/value projection is about 12.5M of about 68.6M MACs per block-round (about 18%, my count). Caching removes 11 of the 12 rounds' copies, which is about 16 to 17% of controller forward arithmetic. The 1.05x mark only holds if the step is arithmetic-bound, and the 3M gap in item 2 casts doubt on that. If it works, the payoff is about 16% of GPU time: roughly 2 to 3 h of a 16 to 20 h 30M seed, or about $1 to $1.50 per box at $0.48/h (suggested). No 8a mark changes, as the plan itself says.

A CHEAPER ROUTE FITS THE SHIP DESIGN BETTER (shown). tool.py already caches S0 once per forward (tool.py:137-138 and 155). The calculator-outside tool model (T1, the B3 path) has the same S0 structure and no result slots, so a speed port there avoids the offset and remap risks. If B3 is the design that ships (the brief's rule 1 note says B2 cannot ship), optimise B3's build rather than B2 mid-ladder.

HOURS ARE UNDERSTATED (suggested). The plan says 4 h. The port needs a harness, mutants, a dtype decision, CPU equality over six checkpoints times six lesions on 1,000 rows, real-loop timing, and a training A/A or a 3M re-run. Realistic work is 8 to 12 h. GPU time is under 1 h.

ADJACENT, HIGH PRIORITY FOR THE 8a LADDER (shown in the box records; mechanism shown in the local copy; G-build behaviour unverified). Every arm's box command passes --max-ans 8 (box.json cmd strings for B2, PT and LLM). The caps say max_ans 35, and addendum G says 35-letter answers come from own text. In the local copy, train.py:139 builds Dataset with strict=True, data.py:109 asserts answers are at most MAX_ANS, and data.py:116 cuts answers to MAX_ANS characters before EOS. PT and LLM still finished with rc 0, so either the G build differs from this copy, or the baseline arms trained on answers cut at 8 characters. That would break rule 7 and make the PT and LLM baselines unfair. B2's own GEN targets are cut at GEN_MAX (ledger.py:447), which is N_REG minus 1, so 35 in the G build (suggested). Check the G build's data path before any PT or LLM comparison is read.

THE 3M B2 IS OUTSIDE THE SEALED SIZE BAND (shown). The stdout 'size' event for seed 401 reads n_params 3,346,513, band [3,147,208, 3,341,880], inside false, vs_plain_tf_pct 3.14. Rule 3 says +/-3%. The gap is small, but the brief's note that addendum F3 allows +3% needs checking against this event.

THE BRIEF'S STATUS IS STALE (shown). 8a 3M results already exist for seeds 401, 402 and 405 (all three arms; RESULT.json and box.json). The brief's dph of 0.49 is 0.48 in box.json. The 30M cap is not set, because the section 6 caps are superseded (addendum C). Addendum H says 10M and 30M caps will be set from measured time.

NUMBERS THAT CHECK OUT (shown). All six b2ckpt checkpoints match their .sha256 files (computed this session). The first-look readout matches readout.json: gain +1.42 and -0.28; lead 5.50 and 6.95 falling to 4.19 and 4.49; B2D params 10,254,105; 4.20 steps/s; 9,672.7 MiB. The 3 TFLOP per update is consistent with my count (about 2.9 TFLOP for forward plus backward at G caps, suggested), which gives about 32 TFLOP/s at 0.092 s and about 20 TFLOP/s at 0.145 s.

THE 30M ESTIMATES CONFLICT AND RELY ON THE PROBE (shown for each figure; the combination is suggested). Addendum I2 gives 16.0 h a seed (all arms, 15 GB); addendum I3 gives about 14 h; superseded addendum C gives 4 to 5 days. The D5 payoff should be recomputed from the real-loop figure, and the 30M cap and MAXH must be re-set before any 30M run.

M5 IS FRAGILE (suggested). The speed rule uses five pairs on one box. If the A/A null band is about +/-3% or wider, a 5% gain cannot be read. Use at least six pairs on two boxes, and report the result as report-only when the band is wider than the gain.

fixed_plan.title: D5 gate: profile the real B2 step before any port
fixed_plan.ben_line: Before we rewrite B2's code to save time, we check on the real training run how much time the part we would change actually takes. We rewrite only if that share is big enough, and we then check that the rewrite keeps training the same.
fixed_plan.question: On the real 3M-shape B2 training loop (12 rounds, 36 registers, 106 slots, bf16, batch 256), what share of each update is GPU-busy, and what share is the S0 key/value and pointer-key work that D5 would cache?
fixed_plan.one_change: None to the model. Measurement only: time the existing train.py loop for 220 updates (drop the first 20) with torch.profiler and per-phase timers covering batch prep (gold() and tokenize()), forward, backward and optimizer.
arms: A: current build 50ee171632 (the 3M rung's code), real train.py loop, G-caps 3M shape, copy on, bf16, batch 256, with profiler and phase timers.

C: counting only (CPU, no GPU): per-batch maximum number and word counts over 20 pool batches, to see how much of the 91 number slots a batch uses. This decides whether G2 or D5 has anything to remove.
fixed_plan.seeds: No learning claim, so no training seeds. Timing repeated on two boxes (the pools for seeds 401 and 402) to see the spread.
fixed_plan.machine: One rented RTX 5090 at $0.48/h, solo, approved by Ben first (rule 6), about 0.5 h including the 255 s pool build (cost about $0.25). CPU counting on the PC or the M1.
pass_marks: GPU-busy fraction of the real loop (kernel time over wall time) at least 0.8. Below 0.8 the step is host-bound and no GPU-arithmetic port can reach the 1.05x mark.
S0 key/value plus pointer-key work at least 7% of CUDA time (the plan's bar). Below 7% D5 is not worth building.
Step time reproduces the 3M rung's 0.14 to 0.145 s per update within 10%. If it does not, stop and report, because the harness is not the real loop.
Per-phase timings repeat within 5% across the two boxes; otherwise the result is report-only.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: GPU-busy under 0.8, or S0 plus pointer-key share under 7% of CUDA time: then D5 cannot give the 1.05x speed mark and is dropped for this ladder. Also, if the per-batch maximum number count is near 91 in almost every batch, G2 has nothing to remove either, and speed is not a rung blocker.
fixed_plan.null_risk: The 220-update window may not reflect the whole run, but the 3M rung's step time is steady (72.6 s per 500 steps, shown), so the window is probably fine. The profiler adds overhead, so the shares are read, not the absolute times. Suggested: the gate's answer is most likely host-bound, which would close D5 for good.
fixed_plan.autonomy: No model change. Passes rule 10 and rule 1: nothing is added to the deployed model, and the hand parts stay as they are. Measurement only; no runtime value is tuned. Rule 5: the profile uses training batches only and scores no dev or protected rows.
steps: 1. Ask Ben for the single rented 5090 for about 0.5 h (rule 6). Do not start a box without his OK.

2. Run train.py's ledger config at the 3M G shape (copy on, bf16, batch 256, build 50ee171632) for 220 updates, dropping the first 20, with torch.profiler and per-phase timers around batch prep, forward, backward and optimizer.
3. Record the steady step time (expect about 0.145 s; if not, stop and report), the GPU-busy fraction, the S0 plus pointer-key share of CUDA time, and the per-phase CPU time.
4. On CPU, count the per-batch maximum number and word slots over 20 pool batches (no GPU).
5. Write the result as a measured, not-adopted addendum J to the 8A spec. If the gate fails (busy under 0.8 or S0 share under 7%), stop here and drop D5 for this ladder.

6. Only if the gate passes and Ben has approved a 10M or 30M rung: decide D5 versus G2 (or both, sequenced) on the commit that rung will use. Build the port there. Run the equality checks (fp32 with an A/A noise floor, or patched dtypes), the mutants, and the timing on the real loop, with at least six pairs on two boxes.
7. Before any rung uses the port, run a training A/A (same seeds, old and new commit, bf16), or re-run the 3M rung on the new commit (about $4 for three seeds at the recorded $0.67 to $0.74 per box).
8. Resolve the max-answer question first (issue 11): confirm the G build's PT and LLM arms do not cut answers at 8 characters before any G-caps measurement is read as an 8a result.
files_to_touch: None for the gate. A profiling harness goes outside the model code and outside tests/.
Port stage only, later: ledger.py on the rung's build commit (not the local copy); new harness files under tests/; addendum J to /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md.
fixed_plan.depends_on: Ben's OK for one rented 5090 (rule 6). The port stage depends on a go for the 10M or 30M rung, since the payoff only matters if 30M runs. The max-answer check (issue 11) should come before any G-caps measurement is read as an 8a result.
fixed_plan.confirm: Only if the gate passes: M1 on the rung's commit (fp32 with a measured noise floor, or patched dtypes; all lesions; trained G-shape checkpoints or perturbed-init weights), M2 mutants on that harness, M3 saved bytes at G caps with a pass line of 0.95, M5 timing on the real loop with at least six pairs on two boxes and an A/A band, and a training A/A on two seeds (or a 3M rung re-run on the new commit).

final.why: The premise holds (shown, ledger.py: the number and constant slots S0 are rebuilt into keys and values every round, and the pointer keys are rebuilt at each step; models/tool.py already caches them), the change is exact, adds 0 params and breaks no rule including rule 10. But the payoff is small and the speed case is weakened by the 3M rung logs (shown: B2 runs 6.4-7.1 steps/s, about 0.14-0.15 s per update, versus 0.092 in the 8A-SPEC I2 probe and about 0.024 for PT, so B2 is about 6x plain and the extra time is probably host-side or launch-bound work that caching does not touch). The compute-bound ceiling is about 1.07x at q33 and 1.17x at G caps (suggested), the saved-activation cut is roughly 4-16% (suggested), I2 (shown) says 30M needs about a 19% memory cut to drop from 4 parts to 2, which this does not give, and the saving is about 1-2 h of a 13-16 h 30M seed. A port also puts the 10M and 30M runs on different code than the 3M rung, which already ran on build 50ee171632, and bf16 rounding would differ, so it needs a sealed addendum; it only matters if 30M runs, and the first look (+1.42, -0.28 against the +3.0 mark) makes that uncertain. Park it, and fold a profile of the real training loop (GPU-busy fraction, batch prep time, S0 share) into the planned 8a speed probe. Revisit D5 only if that profile shows the step is GPU-arithmetic-bound and the 30M rung is a go.
final.ben_line: This is a safe way to make the model's training a few percent faster without changing its answers, but it will not show that bigger is better, so wait until we know the 30M run is happening.
plan_fixes: Do not fund D5 as a stand-alone job: move the profile gate (GPU-busy fraction, per-phase timers for gold()/tokenize(), S0 key/value plus pointer-key share of CUDA time) into the existing 8a speed probe, so one box visit answers it. Only open the port if busy is at least 0.8 and the S0 share is at least 7%.

Remove the premise that B2 runs at about half of plain's rate. Shown: I2 gives 4.0x (3M), 4.7x (10M), 4.6x (30M), and the real 3M rung logs (8a-results seeds 401, 402, 405) give about 0.14-0.15 s for B2 against about 0.024 for PT, so about 6x. The 0.092 s probe figure is not what the real loop does, and the 18 s per 200 updates arithmetic is wrong; use the real-loop rate.

State the mechanism correctly: CBlock.forward re-concatenates S0 keys and values with the reader's keys and values in every block and round, and SDPA saves that concatenation, so the saving is mostly the S0 LayerNorm inputs and outputs, not S0 keys and values. Expect about 4-16% of saved activations (suggested), and say T_X (about 200 at q33, 280 at G caps) beside the 7.5% and 15.7% FLOP shares.

M1 as written (fp64 CPU) probably cannot run (suggested, not run, torch is absent here): value_code and OMEGA are float32 (ledger.py about 65-73) and vcode is applied to that output, so a double() forward likely fails. Either patch dtypes (and say so) or run fp32 with a noise floor measured by an A/A reference (same code, permuted key order). Also check that 1e-5 relative on gradients is above the fp32 noise.

Equality must use a trained checkpoint, because residual init is about 0.003 std and the mutants (missing src.weight[0] offset, wrong mask order, reused round-0 mask) may not move outputs. The six q33 checkpoints fit the q33 shape only (8 rounds, 9 registers, 27 slots); the G-shape build (50ee171632 / b3d48f22e2) is not in the checkout, so the G-caps equality and the bytes check at G caps need a trained G-shape checkpoint from the 8a tarballs or perturbed weights, and each mutant must be shown to exceed the bar first.

M3 pass line of 0.92 sits on the predicted result (about 0.91-0.92 block-only, about 0.88 with the pointer-key split). Set the line at 0.95 or report M3 only, and require the pointer-key split in the first port.

M5 timing: use at least six interleaved pairs, ideally on two boxes, plus an A/A null pair; report only if the null band is wider than plus or minus 3%. Do not anchor on the first look's 4.20 steps/s or 9,672.7 MiB (four runs shared one 5090). Do not claim D5 changes the 30M micro-batch count.

Code-version confound: any adoption must be a sealed addendum, all arms of a rung on one commit, and it needs a training A/A (same seeds, old vs new commit, bf16) inside the seed sd (B2 sd 0.6 pooled-5), or a 3M re-run on the new commit (about $0.67-0.74 per box). An fp64 one-batch check does not show bf16 training is unchanged.

Address the overlap with addendum G2 (per-batch slot trimming) on the same S0 term and the remapped result-slot indices: decide G2 or D5 or both in sequence, using a CPU count of per-batch maximum number slots over about 20 pool batches. G2 may remove more than caching does.

Hours are understated: 4 h for the port, harness, mutants, six checkpoints times six lesions, and timing is more like 8-12 h of work, with under 1 h of GPU. The line numbers cited are from the local copy, not build 50ee171632, so redo the edit list on the rung commit.

Unverified and adjacent, check before reading any G-caps result: all three 3M box commands in box.json pass --max-ans 8 while the spec says answers go up to 35 letters (G build, E1 no-truncation rule). In the local code data.py cuts answers to MAX_ANS, so either the G build changes this or PT and LLM trained on answers cut at 8, which would break rule 7. Also the 3M B2 is 3,346,513 params, 3.14% above plain_tf S, outside the printed band (inside false); confirm addendum F3 covers it.

Ship-design note: tool.py (T1/B3) already has the S0 cache, and 8a's B2 cannot ship (roadmap 4.1), so any speed work that matters for the final model belongs on the tool.py path, not on ledger.py mid-ladder.

idea.title: Report pool4, no-executor subset, family classes and smooth scores
idea.summary: Add reported columns, all computed from the same checkpoints and rows, so a failed size mark can be interpreted: a four-split pool (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab; 4,720 rows) beside pooled-5, a no-executor family subset, family-class predictions fixed now for the first look, and two smooth scores (edit similarity and answer log-likelihood). Marks are not changed.
idea.change: Reporting in analyze_8a.py (not in this checkout) and a small eval function beside evalx.evaluate. Columns: pool4; the 20 families with program coverage under 50% (3,480 rows a seed) and the 14 above the cut, flagged as a rule-1 risk; per-family deltas for pre-registered classes (U: fewshot_number_rule, list_index, order_chain, table_calc, table_lookup should each rise 3.0 or more; S: 12 families with in_dist at least 85 and variant under 30 stay within 2.0); edit similarity and answer NLL (B2 NLL marginalises over modes and pointers that spell the gold; comparable within an arm only). Regression: new code must reproduce RESULT.json exact match (B2_s200 in_dist 90.51; tfsteps_s200 88.53). 0 params.
idea.why: Variant holds 54.9% of B2's lost pooled-5 points (14.27 of 25.98) and in_dist alone can add at most about 2.1, so the +3.0 per rung mark mostly tests variant, a data-limited split. Pool4 is 85.0, so +3.0 pooled needs +3.84 on pool4. The 20 no-executor families hold 20.13 of 25.98 lost points and are where size must show without a hand calculator. Exact match is 0/1 and could hide growth (2304.15004 argues metric choice drives apparent plateaus).

evidence.claim: B2 six-seed means: in_dist 90.5, answer 74.2, frame 87.7, vocab 87.4, variant 34.7; points lost per split 2.13 / 5.14 / 2.77 / 1.67 / 14.27 (total 25.98); pool4 85.0.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Correction: the 14 'executor-bound' families are a 50% program-coverage cut (ledger.py line 559); the code's own noexec set is 12 families (B2 87.63, loses 4.67). The 20 no-executor families score B2 65.07 vs plain_tf_steps 59.25 (not 59.3).
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Correction: the variant split has 33 families, not 34 (cipher_map is absent); odd_one_out has no vocab rows, so 'odd_one_out vocab is 0' is false; list_index figures 75 and 52 are percentages (75.4, 52.1).
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Plain size gain is +0.76 pooled and +0.28 in_dist at 24k vs the 4-seed 3.2M mean (+2.2 only seed-matched with the lowest 3.2M seed).
evidence.label: shown

test.where: q33 six-seed RESULT.json now (zero compute for pool4, subset, class table); smooth columns on CPU or PC for the q33 and first-look checkpoints
test.arms: B2 vs plain_tf_steps (and C0 if it passes), six paired seeds at 3M; 3M and 10M first-look seeds when they exist
test.pass_mark: Size claim on pool4: at least +3.8 per rung (equals +3.0 pooled), CI above 0, on six paired seeds; on the no-executor subset at least +5.2 per rung with B2's lead not down more than 1.0. Class prediction holds if 4 of 5 U families rise 3.0 or more, 9 of 12 S families stay within 2.0, on both first-look seeds. Smooth-score hidden gain: smooth slope per doubling at least 1.5x the exact slope, smooth CI above 0, exact CI includes 0, and the 3.3M ordering B2 over plain_tf_steps holds on 6 of 6 seeds.
test.proved_wrong: Pool4 rises under +1.9 per rung on six seeds (same-structure rows do not respond to size, so any pooled gain is variant-only data); at most 2 of 5 U families rise 3.0, or 5 or more of 12 S families rise 3.0; a smooth-score ratio under 1.5 means exact match is not hiding growth.

shown: the idea says 'Marks are not changed' but adds gates: pool4 at least +3.8 per rung, a no-executor subset at least +5.2 with a lead rule, a smooth slope at least 1.5x the exact slope, and new proved-wrong lines. shown (arithmetic): pool4 +3.84 equals +3.0 pooled only if the variant gain is zero. Pooled gain = (4720 x d_pool4 + 1320 x d_variant) / 6040, so the two gates can disagree (pool4 +3.84 with variant -2 gives pooled about +2.5). Pool4 = 85.0 is correct (1360 + 1200 + 1360 + 800 = 4720 rows).

shown: 'no-executor' is a mislabel. The 20 families are those where under 50% of training rows carry a gold program (ledger.py:559 tests coverage percent >= 50 from progparse.py:212-223). The executor runs on every row at test time: ledger.py:333 calls execute() unconditionally, and noexec is only a lesion switch at ledger.py:334-335. So the claim that size must show 'without a hand calculator' on these families is false, and the rule-1 question is not answered by this subset. The executor-off measure already exists as noexec.program_families (ledger.py:589-600).

shown: smooth scores do not exist yet. No eval-time answer NLL or edit similarity appears in evalx.py, ledger.py or train.py. The only logsumexp terms are training losses (ledger.py:459-516) and the cosine term is at ledger.py:540. B2 emits its answer by argmax over mode and pointers (ledger.py:342-345), so 'marginalising over modes and pointers' needs a new eval function. The 1.5x slope-ratio gate compares nats or characters with percentage points, so the ratio has no fixed meaning.

shown: the +1.9 'proved wrong' threshold is copied from PR #18's frozen-core result (a different design; results-digest row 11 as cited in the brief, not re-read here). The inference that a pool4 gain under 1.9 means 'any pooled gain is variant-only' does not follow from the weights in the item above.

shown (brief facts, addendum G): the q33 reference is not the 8a 3M rung. q33 B2 has 8 rounds and 9 registers (ledger.py:62-63 per the code notes). 8a B2 uses 12 rounds, 36 registers and 280-letter prompts, on seeds 400-405 (8A-SPEC line 86). A pool4 reading from q33 describes a different design. A 'six paired seeds at 3M' test cannot show per-rung growth, which needs two rungs of six seeds each.

untested: the '3,480 rows a seed' figure for the 20 families is not in any project file searched (grep for 3,480 and 3480 in /mnt/project-files finds only plan-b IDs). In the pooled in_dist split each family has 40 rows (1,360 over 34 families), so 20 families give 800 rows there. Source the count or drop it.

shown: much of the reporting already exists. Per-family by_family counts are in every RESULT.json (e.g. /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/8a-results/8a-3M-s401-B2/RESULT.json final_eval). problems: Autonomy (rule 10) is not engaged. The idea adds no deploy-time step and 0 params. Walk-through: (1) pool4, family sets, class labels, edit similarity, answer NLL and the regression check are computed by a research-side script (analyze_8a.py; not found in the checkout, shown by find); (2) the 20/14 split comes from the 50% coverage cut at ledger.py:559, a dev-derived threshold; (3) U and S class labels come from family names and dev results (test-generator knowledge, allowed for scoring only); (4) answer NLL needs new code that marginalises over modes and pointers (not written, suggested); (5) the gates are pre-ship build decisions. Caution: these labels and the NLL must never become a runtime signal (checking tries, deciding stuck, choosing practice kinds). The idea does not propose that; if it did, it would need an autonomous version.

Pre-registration is void for the first look. The idea says the class predictions are 'fixed now for the first look', but the first-look RESULT.json files and readout.json already exist (first-look-10m-results, file times 2026-10-07 21:14 to 21:24, shown). Scoring the idea's own class rule on them (shown, my recomputation from RESULT.json by_family): U rule (4 of 5 families at least +3.0 on both seeds): seed 200 passes at 4 of 5 (deltas +6.2, +7.0, +4.0, +8.5, -2.0); seed 201 fails at 0 of 5 (deltas -6.2, -1.5, -2.0, -4.0, -1.5). S rule (9 of 12 'stay within 2.0'): with |delta| <= 2, seed 200 gives 6 of 12 and seed 201 gives 9 of 12; with delta >= -2, the counts are 12 of 12 and 11 of 12. The rule as written fails on seed 201 for U under either reading. This is a post hoc reading, not a verdict.

Marks changed while the text says they are not. The idea says 'Marks are not changed', and its rules_check says a mark change needs a dated addendum and 'none is proposed'. But pass_mark adds four new pass conditions: pool4 at least +3.8 per rung with CI above 0; no-executor at least +5.2 per rung with the lead rule; the class prediction; and a smooth-score 'hidden gain' route. The sealed marks (8A-SPEC section 7, shown) gate on pooled-5 only: B2 rises at least +3.0 per rung with CI above 0; the lead holds within 1.0; B2 minus PT is at least +3.0 on 5 of 6 seeds at 30M. The smooth route could report growth even when the exact-match CI includes 0. That is a second escape route, not a reporting column.

Per-family thresholds sit inside sampling noise. Each family has 160 to 200 pooled-5 rows per seed (shown, RESULT.json by_family n). At mid-range accuracy a binomial SE for one family is about 3 to 3.5 points (suggested, my approximation). On the first look, 10 of 34 families moved by +3 or more on seed 200 and 3 on seed 201 (shown, recomputed), so per-family 3.0 marks mostly measure noise. Use a pooled class mean with a CI instead.

The S rule is undefined. 'Stay within 2.0' does not say whether it means |delta| <= 2 or delta >= -2. The two readings give different first-look passes (6 and 9 of 12 versus 12 and 11 of 12), so the rule cannot be applied as written.

Naming collision. The 20-family set is a program-coverage cut (families under 50%, ledger.py:559; 3,480 pooled rows per seed, shown). Calling it 'no-executor' suggests the noexec lesion, but the code's lesion covers a different set: extra.noexec.exec_families has 12 names and program_families has 14 (shown, RESULT.json). The 20 families were never run under noexec, so the claim that size must show 'without a hand calculator' is not measured by this set.

Pool4 is not a translation of the pooled +3.0 mark. Pooled = (4,720 x pool4 + 1,320 x variant) / 6,040 (shown arithmetic), so +3.84 on pool4 equals +3.0 pooled only if variant is flat. On the first look, pool4 moved +1.36 (seed 200) and -0.87 (seed 201), and pooled-5 moved +1.42 and -0.28 (shown, recomputed; matches readout.json verdict). The pool4 value is below the proposed +3.8 on both seeds, but these are 2-seed screens.

Smooth scores cannot be built from the snapshot. No NLL, likelihood or edit-similarity function exists in custom_io/*.py or models/*.py (grep, shown), and no RESULT.json carries a likelihood field (grep, shown). The first-look folders hold result.tgz.sha256 (B2D_s200 hash 3c7d8462...) but not the tgz, and FIRST-LOOK Amendment 2 says the boxes are destroyed after results are collected (shown). The six q33 B2 checkpoints are present in scratchpad code/b2ckpt (shown), so smooth scores on q33 are feasible once torch is available on the probe machine; first-look ones need the tgz from whoever holds it.

Class labels come from q33 (8 rounds). The 8a 3M B2 is a different design (12 rounds, 36 registers, 3,346,513 params; shown in 8a-results/8a-3M-s401-box/box.json) and already has RESULT.json for seeds 401, 402 and 405, with PT and LLM for 401 (shown). The idea does not mention these. Its labels therefore do not carry over to 8a, and the 8a 10M and 30M rungs (not yet run) are where the class and pool4 predictions could be pre-registered.

Adjacent, not part of this idea: the 8a 3M pool manifest (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-pool/caps.json, shown) says the 3M rung used the largest pool (own72 plus the rung30 web slice, 4,634,263 rows), while 8A-SPEC section 4 and addendum B1 give 3M the 60M pool. The brief already lists this as open. Flag it for the 8a owner.

Pass-mark identity is wrong (shown arithmetic). Pooled gain = 0.7815 x pool4 gain + 0.2185 x variant gain (4,720 and 1,320 of 6,040 rows). '+3.84 on pool4 equals +3.0 pooled' holds only when variant gains zero. Pool4 +3.84 with variant falling can pass while pooled is below 3.0, and pooled +3.0 can pass with pool4 below 3.84 if variant rises. So pool4 and the +5.2 subset mark are new pass routes, which contradicts 'marks are not changed'. The +5.2 figure is 3.0 x 6,040 / 3,480 and holds only if the 14 other families stay flat.

Proved-wrong inference is a non sequitur (shown arithmetic). Pool4 gain under +1.9 caps the pool4 contribution at about 1.5 pooled points. A pooled +3.0 would then need about +6.9 on variant. Nothing in that threshold shows that same-structure rows fail to respond to size, or that any pooled gain is variant-only.

Selection bias in the class predictions. The U class has no stated membership rule. Its members are low B2 scorers (fewshot 22.7, table_lookup 25.0, order_chain 43.6, table_calc 56.1, list_index 56.2 on the six-seed q33 means), but the bottom five by score would be fewshot, table_lookup, order_chain, digits_parity and seq_next. Family seed sd is 1.7-4.6 for U families and 2.2 median across 34 families (shown). The S rule tests stability at ceiling (in_dist 85-100), so it cannot count as evidence of growth.

Smooth-score rule is ad hoc. 'Smooth slope per doubling at least 1.5x the exact slope' compares slopes in different units (edit similarity in [0,1] against exact match in percent), so the ratio depends on scaling, and no source fixes 1.5. The cited paper (arXiv 2304.15004, Schaeffer, Miranda, Koyejo; checked by search) argues that nonlinear or discontinuous metrics produce apparent sudden jumps and that continuous metrics show smooth gains. It is about jumps, not plateaus, and gives no slope-ratio rule. Nothing in ledger.py, models/ or evalx.py computes answer NLL or edit similarity; the only log-softmax terms are training pointer and mode losses (shown by grep). Both are new builds and untested.

Multiplicity and rescue route. About six new tests (pool4 mark, subset mark, five U rises, twelve S stays, smooth ratio, 3.3M ordering) would be read on two-seed screens with no correction. chair.reasons:
VERDICT: plan, but only as a reporting-only rider on analyze_8a.py, not a standalone test. It costs no GPU time. It does not break a rule. Every critic found the same fixable faults, and I confirmed the key ones in files.

WHAT HOLDS (shown, recomputed by critics from the six q33 B2 and tfsteps RESULT.json files, not re-run by me): pool4 = 85.01 over 4,720 rows; variant = 14.27 of 25.98 lost pooled points (54.9%); the 20 families under 50% program coverage hold 3,480 rows a seed and 20.13 lost points (B2 65.07 vs tfsteps 59.25); the regression anchors match (B2_s200 in_dist 90.51, tfsteps_s200 88.53). I read ledger.py:559 myself: the cut is `c['prog'] >= 50`. Extra checks I ran: 8a-results holds only 3M seeds 401, 402 and 405; PREDS.json exists only for first-look C0_s200 and C0_s201, so no B2 per-row predictions exist anywhere; train.py has a `--save-preds` flag.

WHAT BREAKS AS WRITTEN:
1. Rule 4 timing (shown). The first look has already run. readout.json and the B2/B2D RESULT.json files are dated 10-07 21:24, and 8a 3M seeds 401, 402 and 405 already have RESULT.json. So 'class predictions fixed now for the first look' is not a prediction. The critics' post hoc recount of the idea's own class rule on first-look seeds 200/201 (suggested, critic arithmetic): U gets 4 of 5 on seed 200 and 0 of 5 on seed 201; S gets 6 of 12 on seed 200 and 9 of 12 on seed 201. The rule fails on both seeds. Pool4 moved +1.36 and -0.87, and pooled-5 moved +1.42 and -0.28.
2. 'Marks are not changed' is false. The idea adds pool4 +3.8, a subset +5.2, a class gate and a smooth 'hidden gain' route. The sealed spec gates pooled-5 only; everything else sits in 'Reported, not gated' (8A-SPEC line 117). Pool4 +3.84 equals pooled +3.0 only if variant is flat, because pooled = 0.7815 x pool4 + 0.2185 x variant. The 'smooth CI above 0 while exact CI includes 0' route is a rescue path for a failed rung, with no control arm.
3. 'No-executor' is a mislabel (shown). The 20 families are a program-coverage cut. The executor runs on every row at test time. The code's own noexec lesion set is 12 families (extra.noexec.exec_families), so the label would collide with it.
4. Per-family 3.0 thresholds sit inside sampling noise (suggested): about 160-200 rows per family per seed, binomial SE about 3 points, family seed sd 1.7-4.6. A family with a true +3.0 clears the bar only about half the time. U families are the low scorers, so regression to the mean also biases them upward.
5. Smooth scores do not exist (shown by grep; no NLL or edit-similarity code in evalx.py, ledger.py or train.py). Edit similarity needs saved predictions, and none exist for B2. 'Slope ratio >= 1.5x' compares different units and has no source. The cited paper (2304.15004) is about apparent jumps, not plateaus. The NLL 'marginalising over modes and pointers' is not computable exactly.
6. The reference design differs (shown from the brief). q33 has 8 rounds and 9 registers; the 8a B2 has 12 rounds, 36 registers and cloze data. The U/S labels come from q33 and are untested on 8a.

AUTONOMY (rule 10): not engaged. This is research-side scoring, which Ben's rules allow. The one fix: say in the addendum that no column, class label or smooth score may become a deploy-time signal (stuck detection, practice picking, sleep or stop timing). Any such use would need its own autonomous version.

VALUE (suggested): modest. The decision effect is small. The first-look echoes (pool4 +0.25, low-20 +0.10 on the two-seed mean) suggest the columns will mirror pooled-5. They make a flat rung readable. They do not show that size helps. Smooth scores are the only part that could reveal hidden growth; the critic's guess is a low chance (about 15%, suggested). Pool4 and the coverage split are one-line recomputations from by_split and by_family in existing RESULT.json files, about 0.3 h. Smooth scores add about 2-4 h (suggested) and need B2 predictions or checkpoints.
chair.revised_idea:
REPORTING-ONLY ADDENDUM (scale-D6r), dated and hashed before the 8a 10M rung (seeds 400-405) starts. It adds NO pass mark, NO proved-wrong line, NO 'hidden gain' route and changes NO sealed mark. It goes under 'Reported, not gated' (8A-SPEC line 117). It states that none of these columns can pass, fail or rescue a size claim. Only pooled-5 marks 1-3 decide.

Columns, for every arm (B2, plain_tf_steps or C0, and PT13C0 or the 10M plain arm) on the same rows, so the lead comparison is two-sided:
(a) Pool4 (in_dist, answer, frame, vocab; 4,720 rows) and variant (1,320 rows), with the identity written out: pooled-5 gain = 0.7815 x pool4 gain + 0.2185 x variant gain. Drop the '+3.84 equals +3.0' shortcut.
(b) 'Low program coverage', the 20 families under 50% of training rows with a gold program (3,480 pooled rows a seed), against the 14 at or above the cut (2,560 rows). Cite ledger.py:559. Keep the code's 12-family noexec set (exec_families and program_families) as its own separately named columns. Never call the 20 'no-executor' and never say they show size 'without a hand calculator'. The executor runs on all rows. The rule-1 flag stays on the whole in-forward executor.
(c) Class means with paired CIs, not per-family thresholds. U = {fewshot_number_rule, list_index, order_chain, table_calc, table_lookup}. S = the 12 families with q33 six-seed in_dist >= 85 and variant < 30. For each class report the mean rung gain and a paired CI across seeds. For S use |delta| <= 2.0 as the reading. Report the plain arm's class gain beside B2's so regression to the mean (U are low scorers) is visible. The class labels come from q33 seeds 200-205, an 8-round 9-register design, so they are labels, not predictions about the 8a design. The sealed 8a design (12 rounds, 36 registers, cloze data) differs.
(d) Smooth score: per-character edit similarity of the free-run answer string against gold, on the same rows and the same families. This needs `--save-preds` (or checkpoints) turned on for B2 and plain arms from the 10M rung on. Answer NLL is dropped, or kept only as a labelled teacher-forced value comparable within an arm. No slope-ratio rule. Report edit similarity beside exact match per class and per rung with a six-seed CI.
(e) Regression check: the new code must reproduce RESULT.json exact match (B2_s200 in_dist 90.51; tfsteps_s200 88.53) and the first-look pooled-5 values in readout.json before any new number is trusted.

Pre-registration rules: the first-look seeds 200/201 and 8a 3M seeds 401/402/405 are already read. Any class or pool4 reading on them is labelled POST HOC, with the recount above (U 4 of 5 then 0 of 5; S 6 of 12 then 9 of 12) as the honest result. Use them only as a labelled check of whether the q33 labels transfer to 8a. Any prediction about classes is written, dated and hashed before 10M seeds 400-405 run, and scored only there (and later at 30M). If Ben wants one written prediction, it is: U class mean gain >= +3.0 with paired CI above 0 on six seeds, S class mean change >= -2.0, with a plain-arm difference-in-difference beside it. Mark it as interpretation, not a gate. A 'proved wrong' reading is a U CI that includes 0 while the S class is stable. State the count of new tests (about 6 class and pool4 reads per rung) and say that nothing is multiplicity-corrected, so they are exploratory.

Scope limits: the 3M-to-10M step is depth only on identical rows, so the columns read cleanly there. At 30M, width, lr, updates and pool all change together, so the columns cannot attribute the cause. The quarter-pool diagnostic does that, not these columns.

Rule 10: scoring and tests are research-side and not a deploy-time step. No label, class or smooth score may be used as a runtime signal for stuck detection, practice picking, sleep timing or stopping. A runtime use would need an autonomous version.

problems: Step 0 (memorisation check on the six B2 checkpoints) is a research measurement, not a model method. Its pass marks use dev answers, which a deployed model never has. The deploy-time analogue ('am I memorising my own practice?') would need a self-check that needs no answers, such as accuracy on fresh self-generated items verified by an outside checker the model calls. The idea does not propose one. Shown: train.py logs only train loss and dev quick_eval (train.py lines 175-193, 189), and RESULT.json final_eval holds the dev splits only, so no train exact-match exists and step 0 must generate it. Step 1 (build the 1.7M shape-unique rows and train on them) is build-time. It passes rule 10 only under the reading that building before ship is not a deploy step. That reading is labelled suggested in the roadmap ('My reading (suggested; Ben can override)', whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md lines 364-366) and disclosed as Ben-correctable in no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md section 0. The idea should cite that reading and state that the data choice is fixed before ship.

The dedup and exclusion rules (drop pooled-5 dev shapes, held-out flags and protected shapes) use test-generator knowledge. That is acceptable as a build-time anti-leak step. It would not be acceptable as a deploy-time filter: if the deployed model ever chose its practice by 'shape-unique' or by the test's family list, rule 10's clause on test-generator knowledge (which kinds exist) would apply. The autonomous version is a novelty check the model calls as an outside tool, using only what the model has seen.

Transfer trap, sleep repetition knob. If D7 finds that repetition binds, the tempting deploy-time move is to cap sleep replay visits. The fast-sleep sleep already runs 80 visits per record (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md line 43; fast-sleep/gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md line 45). A visits cap set from D7's dev numbers would be a runtime value tuned on dev answers, which rule 10 bars. The autonomous form is a sleep that stops replaying when its own tool-checked tries on fresh replay prompts stop improving, with any fixed constant set before the run.

Transfer trap, deploy-time practice source. If the result is read as 'more fresh practice helps', the easy source is skills_curriculum. Its 34 train families are the test's kinds (data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md section 2, and the dev splits come from the same generator), so a deploy-time call to it breaks rule 10's clause on which kinds exist. Autonomous sources are the day's own questions (already the rule in the fast-sleep report lines 32-34) or free human-written web text (FineWeb-Edu, allowed by rule 2) used at build time.

The measured design is B2, which still has parts that run between question and answer: the int64 executor inside the forward pass (ledger.py line 76 execute, called in the forward), regex number spans (ledger.py line 206, NUM_RE) and the str() printer. A repetition result on B2 therefore describes a design that cannot ship as built. To carry it to a shippable design, the same comparison must be re-run on a design with the calculator outside as a tool (T1: queue_local/40-pc-t1-screen.txt, which is queued and not run in this snapshot). This is the largest autonomy gap, but it sits in B2's design, not in D7.

The step 2 gate (10.25M on 100k rows only if the first look shows at least +1.0 on one seed) is a research decision tuned on dev results. It is fine as research and must not become a deploy gate. One seed is only a screen under rule 4, so the gate should be presented as a research choice, not as evidence.

Outside autonomy, but it decides whether the result means anything: the shape-unique set keeps one row per digit-shape, and some families have few shapes (digits_parity 231, verify_claim 231, group_induct 77; DATA-POOL-PLAN lines 33 and 36, shown). So the 1.7M set has a different family mix from q33's 200k set. If q33 draws families evenly (untested here), arm B minus arm A measures family mix plus repetition, and the claim that the idea isolates repetition fails. Rescue: keep the family proportions fixed and remove only repeats, for example by sampling each family from its unique prompts in q33's proportions.

Outside autonomy, rule 5: the protected-shape exclusion is untested, and protected panels are not yet cleared (DATA-POOL-PLAN line 23, shown). Step 1 must not train on these rows until the overlap check (data-pool/PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md) has covered them.

What I confirmed (shown):

Where I weigh the critics:
1. The shape-unique arm B is a confounded contrast, because it changes family mix and removes number variety. The fix is an exact-unique full-prompt set drawn by the same builder at A's family proportions. I take that fix and drop the shape-unique set.
2. The title "separate data from size" is not delivered by a 3M-only test. A 3.3M null cannot clear 10M or 30M, since bigger models memorise faster (suggested). I take the critics' fix: run 10M on the same unique set, which also repairs the incoherent gated 2x2 (100k rows at 24k updates is about 61 passes, the opposite of the question). I also drop the proposal to cancel the 30M quarter-pool diagnostic.

5. Step 0 is nearly predetermined. Final train loss is 0.009-0.021 (shown), but a low loss is not the same as exact match on train rows. Step 0 is free and CPU-only, so I keep it as descriptive, gating nothing.

8. Rule 10: the test is a build-time data diagnostic. It passes only if no deploy-time constant (replay or visit cap, practice source) is read from its result.
