chair.revised_idea:
Title: Is B2's flat size curve caused by repeating the 200k rows? (skills data only, small-card B2 only; not the village model, and no claim about web cloze).

PART 0 (free, CPU, minutes; descriptive; gates nothing).
- Load the six code/b2ckpt B2_s200..s205 checkpoints. Seed identity is shown only for 200-202; the other three are inferred from folder names.
- Score a seeded 1,000-row sample of the q33 train file (same rows for all six checkpoints) against dev in_dist (1,360 rows) with the same exact-match rule. If train rows lack accepted lists, score both sets on answer equality only, and say so.
- Report the pooled gap and the per-family gap.
- Also report A's per-family train counts, and the exact-prompt and digit-shape overlap between A and each dev split. These come from the PC train file and need no training.
- Bands, fixed now:
  - memorised if train minus dev is at least +6.0 on 5 of 6 seeds;
  - not memorised if it is at most +2.0 on 5 of 6 seeds;
  - anything else is inconclusive.
- A memorised result is not evidence that repetition limits dev scores.

PART 1 (GPU; only if the gates below pass). A 2x2 on the skills data, seeds 200 and 201, with the q33 recipe: 24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, q33 caps.
- A3 = B2 3,302,481 params on the 200k rows (about 31 passes). Reuse the first-look same-box reruns (73.39 and 74.93).
- A10 = B2 grown to 8 blocks (10,254,105 params) on the 200k rows. Reuse the first-look runs (74.82 and 74.65).
- B3 and B10 are new: the same two models on about 1.3M exact-unique full prompts. That is about 4.7 passes, matching 8a's roughly 4.3.
  - Draw B with the same skills_curriculum builder, A's per-family proportions, the same length policy, and the same train-clean exclusions as A. Use full prompts, not digit-masked shapes.
  - If a family has fewer unique prompts than its A-matched count (prop_eval has 42k), cap it and report B's per-family counts next to A's.
- Optional, about 2.2 h: the plain arms C0 (3M) and PT13C0 (10M) on B, to see whether the size gain is B2-specific.
- Dropped from the original idea:
  - the digit-masked shape-unique set;
  - the 50k and 100k subsets;
  - the "10M on 100k rows" cell;
  - the claim that a 3M null lets the 30M quarter-pool diagnostic be dropped.

Marks (2-seed screen, fixed now; a claim needs six paired seeds):
- Repetition binds at 3M if mean(B3 minus A3) is at least +1.0 with both seeds above 0. Likewise at 10M for B10 minus A10.
- Size helps once repeats are removed if B10 minus B3 is at least +3.0 on both seeds (8a's rung mark). It is flat if under +1.0 on both seeds. Anything else is unclear.
- Proved wrong (repetition is not the cause) if B10 minus B3 is under +1.0 on both seeds and both B minus A differences are under +0.5. Then the flat B2 curve points to design or the variant ceiling.
- Any positive screen is followed by seeds 202-205 for the cells in question, including A10, which has only two seeds today.
- A mean in between is "unclear", never a pass or a fail.

Gates before Part 1 trains:
1. Part 0 and A's family-mix table are done.
2. The 8a 10M readout is checked. If 8a 10M minus 3M is already clear on six seeds, Part 1 is largely answered and should be skipped or demoted.
3. Rule 5: B comes from the same train-clean generator path as A, and its exact-prompt overlap with every dev split, held-out family and indexed panel is zero. Ben rules on the short-prompt gap (panels under 8 words contribute no 13-gram hashes).
4. The skills_curriculum builder (branch claude/project-thread-y0sxwe, not in the checkout) is present on the PC.
5. Run B on the same machine class as the first-look A cells. Otherwise rerun A3 seed 200 on the PC to measure the machine shift (+0.39 and +0.66 between q33 and the first-look reruns).

Rules:
- Rule 7: q33 caps (528 list_stats rows trained with no program) are the same in both arms. Label this a diagnostic, not a compliant pipeline.
- Rule 10: build-time data diagnostic only. Its result may set only fixed pre-ship constants. It must never set a deploy-time replay or visit cap, or a practice source. The deployed analogue would be the model practising on its own fresh tries and stopping by its own tool-checked tries.
- Rule 9: small-card B2 only. Rules 3 and 4: same shape, one change per contrast.
chair.plan_guidance:
What the test plan must get right (labels: shown = measured in this project, suggested = reasoned, untested = not run):

1. One change per contrast.
   - B must be exact-unique full prompts, not digit-masked shapes. It must keep A's family proportions and A's length policy (the 62-token redraw), and have the same train-clean exclusions.
   - Report B's per-family counts beside A's.
   - If any family cannot supply its A-matched count of unique prompts, cap it and report it. Do not silently change the mix. (shown: shape caps in DATA-POOL-PLAN section 2; A's mix is untested because the train file is on the PC.)

2. Hold the seen budget fixed.
   - Use 24,000 updates x batch 256 for every cell, so B3 and B10 get about 4.7 passes and A cells about 31. (shown: arithmetic.)
   - Do not use 50k or 100k subsets at fixed updates (about 123 and 61 passes). Do not drop the 30M quarter-pool diagnostic on any 3M or 10M null. (suggested: larger models memorise faster; the repeat-data paper is about LLM scale only.)

3. Machine control.
   - The first-look same-box reruns scored +0.39 and +0.66 above q33, so use them as the A3 and A10 cells.
   - Run B on the same machine class. Otherwise rerun A3 seed 200 on the PC to measure the shift. (shown: readout.json verdict.machine.)

4. Marks fixed before any run, with no gaps. Use the three-way marks in revised_idea and name the CI method for the six-seed follow-up (paired seeds, t interval, n = 6).
   - Part 0 bands are +6.0 and +2.0 on 5 of 6 seeds, and "inconclusive" for anything else.
   - Part 1 labels are "binds", "does not bind" and "unclear", defined in revised_idea.

5. Part 0 specifics.
   - Same exact-match rule on train and dev. Report the per-family gap too, because a pooled gap of +6 can hide memorisation in the number families.
   - Score a seeded 1,000-row sample with the same rows for all six checkpoints.
   - It gates nothing, and it is not evidence that repetition hurts dev. (shown: final train loss 0.009-0.021; train exact match is stored nowhere.)

6. Rule gates.
   - Rule 5: zero exact overlap with all dev splits, held-out families and indexed panels before training. The 13-gram tool cannot see panels under 8 words, so ask Ben to rule on that.
   - Rule 7: q33 caps are kept and disclosed (528 rows with no program). Label the run a diagnostic.
   - Rule 10: build-time only. The result may not tune a deploy-time replay or visit count.
   - Rule 9: small-card B2 only.

7. Do not oversell the effect.
   - in_dist can add at most about 2.1 pooled-5. Variant holds about 55% of lost points, and unique digit shapes are unlikely to fix it. (shown: the 14/20 family split and the pooled-5 weights.)
   - Expected P(B minus A at least +1.0) is about 25-35%, and a null is the likely outcome. (suggested.)
   - A skills-only result says nothing about web cloze.

8. Sequence by cost and overlap.
   - Part 0 first (minutes).
   - Check the 8a 3M and 10M readouts. 8a 3M seeds 401, 402 and 405 are already done: pooled-5 73.21, 74.14, 71.42, mean 72.92, versus q33 74.0. These runs are confounded and not a repetition test.
   - Run Part 1 only if the question is still open. It is 4 new B2 runs, about 4.8 h on a 5090-class card and 2-4x longer on a shared PC (suggested).

9. The brief's "8a has not run" and "no checkpoint" statements are stale. The six b2ckpt files are present with matching sha256, and the 8a 3M B2 runs on three seeds are finished.

10. Plain-language line for Ben: "Our small model has seen the same 200,000 practice questions about 31 times. The cheap check is whether it just memorised them. The real test gives the same model about 1.3 million different questions, with the same mix of kinds. If the scores don't move, repeating questions is not why it stops improving."

plan.title: Repeats or size? B2 with fresh practice prompts at 3.3M and 10M
plan.ben_line: Our small model has practised the same 200,000 questions about 31 times each, and making it bigger has stopped helping much. We will give it about 1.4 million different questions, with the same number of practice rounds, and see whether the bigger version then gets better.
plan.question: Is B2's flat gain from 3.3M to 10M caused by practising the same 200,000 skills questions about 31 times each? Test: the same 24,000 updates on about 1.4 million distinct questions (about 4.4 passes each), at the same per-family shares. Scope: B2 on skills data only, q33 caps, small-card rule 9.
plan.one_change: Distinct training prompts at a fixed seen budget. Control: the q33 200k rows (about 30.7 passes; shown: 24,000 x 256 / 200,000). Change: about 1.4M exact-unique prompts with the same per-family shares, the same 62-token rule and the same exclusions (about 4.4 passes). Fixed: 24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, q33 caps, and the 3.3M and 10.25M shapes.
arms: Part 0 (CPU, no training): the six q33 B2 checkpoints B2_s200 to B2_s205. Their sha256 values match the sidecars (shown). Scored on a stratified train sample of 40 rows per train family (34 families, 1,360 rows, the same design as dev in_dist, which has 1,360 rows; shown), with train rows over 7 program steps removed (528 list_stats rows; shown in LIMIT-COUNTS).

A3 (control, BensPC): B2 at 3,302,481 params on the q33 200k rows. Six-seed PC results on disk: pooled-5 73.00, 74.27, 74.74, 74.02, 73.63, 74.47; mean 74.02, sd 0.63 (shown, recomputed from the RESULT.json files).

B3 (new, BensPC): the same 3,302,481-param model on about 1.4M exact-unique prompts. Per-family quota = k x A's per-family quota, with k the largest integer that every family can fill. About 7 if prop_eval's 42k unique prompts still hold (shown in DATA-POOL-PLAN section 2, old generator; untested on the rebuilt generator). About 4.4 passes.

A10 (new, BensPC): B2 with 8 blocks at width 256, 10,254,105 params (shown in FIRST-LOOK and by ledger.py block arithmetic), on the q33 200k rows. Do not mix the first look's rented-box A10 values (74.82 and 74.65; shown) with PC runs.
B10 (new, BensPC): the same 8-block model on the B rows.

Optional, descriptive only, about 2.2 h (panel estimate, suggested): C0 at 3M and PT13C0 (10,379,264 params; shown) on the B rows, to see whether any B gain is B2-specific. On the q33 rows the plain models gained +2.73 and +2.19 from 3M to 10M (shown: first-look readout), so a repeat cost would have to be model-specific. Changes no mark.
plan.seeds: Part 0: checkpoints 200 to 205. Screen: seeds 200 and 201 (q33 BensPC runs exist for both). Six-seed claim: seeds 200 to 205 (q33 BensPC runs exist for all six). Not 400 to 405: those are 8a's mark seeds, and this diagnostic is not an 8a mark.
plan.machine: BensPC only (RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GB, as the brief states). The A3 controls are q33 BensPC runs, so no machine change enters the B-minus-A contrast. Part 0 runs on any CPU with torch and the q33 train file. Rule 6: rent only if BensPC is full, and then every Part 1 cell, including A3, reruns on the same box. Rented-box numbers differ from PC numbers on the same seeds by +0.39 and +0.66 (shown: first-look readout verdict.machine). Note: the 8a 3M seed-401 run also used a rented box at $0.48/h (shown: 8a-results/8a-3M-s401-box/box.json), which contradicts the brief's statement that 8a runs on the PC and Mac.
pass_marks: Preconditions, fixed now, all must hold before B3 trains: (a) Part 0 done and A's per-family train counts read from the PC file; (b) rule 5: zero exact-prompt overlap of B with every dev split (both the 40-per-cell dev and the 200-per-cell big dev), every held-out family and every indexed panel, plus Ben's ruling on panel items under 8 words, which the 13-gram check cannot see (shown: PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md line 45); (c) B's per-family counts reported beside A's; (d) the 8a 10M readout checked if it exists (not in the snapshot): if 8a 10M minus 3M is already clear on six seeds, demote this test.

Part 0 (descriptive; gates nothing): memorised if the train-matched minus dev in_dist gap is at least +6.0 on 5 of 6 seeds; not memorised if it is at most +2.0 on 5 of 6 seeds; otherwise inconclusive. Per-family gaps are reported, not gated (40 rows per family per seed, so noisy).

Mechanism check (void-if-failed): on each arm's own stratified sample, B3's train-minus-dev gap is smaller than A3's on both seeds. If not, B did not reduce memorisation and the screen does not test repetition.

Screen, seeds 200 and 201, paired by seed, BensPC only. R3 = B3 minus A3; R10 = B10 minus A10; S_B = B10 minus B3; S_A = A10 minus A3; I = S_B minus S_A (equal to R10 minus R3). Premise: S_A under +1.0 on both seeds. The first look's seed 200 (+1.42, rented boxes) breaks this premise by its own rule. If the premise fails, the verdict is 'premise not met' and H_rep is not tested.
Supports H_rep (go to six seeds): premise holds and S_B is at least +3.0 on both seeds (the 8a rung mark; shown in 8A-SPEC sections 6 and 7).
Repeats cost points but do not explain the flat curve: R3 or R10 at least +1.0 on the two-seed mean with both seeds above 0, while S_B is under +1.0 on both seeds.
Provisional against H_rep: S_B under +1.0 on both seeds AND both two-seed means R3 and R10 under +0.5. Provisional only (see null_risk).
Otherwise unclear: no claim, and no extra seeds are added to chase a mark.

Six-seed confirm (seeds 200 to 205, paired by seed, t interval with df 5 and t = 2.571 for 95%): support if mean(I) is at least +2.0 with the 95% lower bound above 0 and mean(S_B) is at least +3.0. Refute at the 8a bar if the 95% upper bound of mean(I) is below +2.0. Otherwise unclear.
plan.proved_wrong: Screen (provisional): S_B under +1.0 on both seeds and both R3 and R10 under +0.5. This says only that the screen did not look like repetition. Claim (six paired seeds): the 95% upper bound of the interaction I is below +2.0. That excludes the 8a-bar version of H_rep for this data and budget, so the flat 3.3M-to-10M curve is not explained by repeats here, and the owner should look at design or at the variant split (variant holds 54.9% of B2's lost pooled points, shown from the six q33 RESULT files; in_dist can add at most about 2.1 pooled points, shown). Why the claim-level mark is 'upper bound below +2.0' and not 'both means under +0.5': with six seeds the 95% half-width on I is about 1.3 (suggested, from a per-run sd of about 0.6), so 'under +0.5' cannot be shown, while the upper-bound mark has about 93% power if I is truly zero (suggested). Scope: this tests q33's 31-pass regime. The 8a rungs run near 4.3 passes, so a result here says what repetition does at q33's repeat level, not whether 8a's data is repetition-limited. The 8a quarter-pool diagnostic (8A-SPEC section 7) stays.
plan.null_risk: (1) Support mark: effectively no chance by noise when machines match. It needs +3.0 on both seeds; with a per-run sd of about 0.6, the per-seed S_B sd is about 0.85 (suggested). (2) Against mark: easy to hit by chance. With no real effect, 'S_B under +1.0 on both seeds' and 'both two-seed means under +0.5' together pass about a third to a half of the time (suggested, normal approximation). A two-seed 'against' is therefore provisional. (3) Machine bias: same-seed PC-versus-rented gaps were +0.39 and +0.66 (shown). A 0.5 bias on R3 would push the 'repeats cost points' mark to pass about 15 to 20% of the time under no effect (suggested), which is why every cell stays on one machine. (4) Coverage confound: B adds about 1.2M short generator prompts, which raises digit-shape overlap with dev, since both dev sets come from the same generator. A gain from that would pass the marks as 'repetition' but is really generator coverage, the rule-10 issue of test-generator knowledge. Guard: report dev digit-shape overlap of A and B by family, and check whether B's gains sit where overlap rose most. (5) Power on the interaction (suggested; per-run sd 0.6, S_A about +0.5): about 85% at a true interaction of +3 and about 15% at +2. (6) The per-run sd of 0.6 is an assumption: q33 seed sd is 0.63 (shown) and same-seed cross-machine gaps were 0.39 and 0.66 (shown). If PC reruns differ by about 1.0, six seeds cannot separate +2 from 0, so run the optional A3 seed 200 rerun first. (7) Prior: suggested 25 to 35% that the two-seed R3 reaches +1.0 (critic estimate, untested). (8) Rules: both arms keep the q33 caps, so 528 rows are trained answer-only (shown: LIMIT-COUNTS). That breaks rule 7 in both arms, so this is a diagnostic, not a compliant result. B2 keeps hand code between question and answer (regex number spans at ledger.py line 206, the int64 executor at line 76, the str() printer at line 399; shown), so any result covers B2 as coded. (9) 8a comparison: 8a 3M B2 at 4.3 passes averaged 72.9 on seeds 401, 402 and 405 (shown, recomputed), 1.1 below q33's 74.0 at 31 passes. It differs in web rows, 12 loops and a rented box, so it is not evidence either way.
plan.autonomy: Not a deploy-time method. No step here runs in the shipped model. Every step is a build-time measurement or a build-time data choice, which rule 10 allows (building and pre-training before ship). The most this can feed into the ship design is a pre-ship constant, such as how many distinct practice prompts go into pre-training. Forbidden at deploy time: setting a sleep visit count, a replay count or a practice source from these numbers, or drawing practice from skills_curriculum's family list or from dev answers (test-generator knowledge, rule 10). The deploy-time analogue, if repeats bind, would be the model writing its own fresh practice items and refusing its own exact repeats by calling an outside dedupe tool it chooses to call by writing text, with a stop rule based on its own tool-checked tries and no dev answers. That method needs its own autonomy check and is not claimed here. Rule 1: B2 still has hand code between question and answer (regex number spans, the in-forward int64 executor, the str() printer; shown), so results apply to B2 as coded. Rule 9: small-card B2 only, no village claim.

Read A's per-family train counts from the q33 train file on BensPC. The own72 build lists 50,935 skills rows for each of 34 families (shown: own72.tgz MANIFEST), which suggests equal quotas, about 5,882 per family at 200k (suggested). Report the counts; B's shares must match them.

Screen on BensPC only, seeds 200 and 201, 24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, q33 caps and the 62-token rule: B3 (2 runs), A10 (2 runs), B10 (2 runs). A3 is the q33 BensPC result for the same seeds. Log final_train_loss, chain-5, the loops:0 leak and per-family counts for every run.

Optional, recommended first (about 1.5 h): rerun A3 seed 200 once on BensPC. If it returns 73.00 exactly, same-machine reruns are repeatable; if it moves by more than 0.5, widen the marks before reading the screen.

Cheapest alternative if PC time is tight: B3 on seeds 200 and 201 only (about 3 PC hours, suggested). It gives R3 only. A small R3 does not rule out a 10M-specific effect, so it can defer the 10M cells but cannot close the question.

Readout from the RESULT.json files (pooled-5 = micro exact over the five splits, n = 6,040 per run; shown): R3, R10, S_B, S_A, I, the mechanism check, the premise check, the screen verdict, and per-split and per-family B minus A. Split sizes are 1,360 / 1,200 / 1,360 / 800 / 1,320 (shown).

If the screen supports H_rep, run seeds 202 to 205 for B3, A10 and B10 on BensPC and compute the six-seed marks. If the screen is against or unclear, stop and write the result. Do not add seeds to chase a mark.

fixed_plan.title: Gated repeats test: does fresh data lift B2's 10M-minus-3M gain?
fixed_plan.ben_line: Our small model has practised the same 200,000 questions about 31 times each, and the bigger version barely beat the smaller one. First we check on our own PC that the flat gain is real and that the plain model is not flat the same way; only if that holds do we give both sizes fresh questions and see whether the bigger one improves.
fixed_plan.question: Does B2's flat 3.3M-to-10M gain (q33's 200k rows, about 31 passes) come from repeated exact training rows, and is any repeat effect specific to B2 or shared with a plain transformer of the same size?
fixed_plan.one_change: Training rows only. A = the q33 200,000 rows. B = A plus about 1.2M new rows from the same skills generator, the same 34 families, per-family shares scaled by k, the same 62-token rule and exclusions (nested, so B contains A). Fixed: 24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, q33 caps. Plain arms are controls, not changes.

Screen, data B, BensPC, only after the gate and the rule-5 check: B3, B10, C0_B, P13_B on seeds 200 and 201.
Confirm, only if the screen passes: seeds 202 to 205 for B3, B10 and A10 (plus C0 and P13 on A and B if the readout needs them). A3 for 202 to 205 already exists on PC.

pass_marks: G0 (CPU, free): count exact duplicate rows in A's train file; expect 0 (the own72 builder rejects duplicate prompts, shown). If nonzero, recompute passes and report. Per-family digit-shape counts for A and for B are reported, not gated.

G1 (rule 5, before any B row trains): exact normalized-string match of every protected panel item (no length cut) against A, B and all dev splits gives zero matches, and Ben approves opening the panels. The 13-gram index does not count.
G2 (premise, PC gate): the two-seed mean of S_A = A10 minus A3 (seeds 200 and 201) must be under +1.0. If not, stop and write the result; no B arms run.
G2b (noise floor): the A3 seed-200 rerun. If the rerun differs from 73.00 by more than 0.5, the screen is marked unpowered and reported only.
G3 (screen go, seeds 200 and 201): I = (B10 minus B3) minus (A10 minus A3). Go to six seeds if mean(I) is at least +1.5 and both seeds' I are above zero. Otherwise stop and report.

G4 (six-seed claim, seeds 200 to 205, paired, t = 2.571 with df 5): support if mean(I) is at least +2.0, its 95% lower bound is above zero, and mean(S_B) is at least +3.0 (the 8a rung bar, 8A-SPEC section 7). Refute at the 8a bar if the 95% upper bound of mean(I) is below +2.0.

Readouts, pre-committed and not marks: Q = mean(P13_B minus C0_B) minus mean(P13_A minus C0_A). If Q is at least +1.0 and mean(I) at least +2.0, repetition is a shared cause. If Q is at least +1.0 and mean(I) under +1.0, repetition hurts plain but not B2, so B2's flatness is not explained by repetition. If mean(I) is at least +2.0 and Q under +0.5, the effect is B2-specific.
Per split (pre-committed): variant change is expected near zero (suggested). Any claim resting only on in_dist is capped at +2.13 pooled points (shown).
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Gate G2 fails (PC two-seed control gain at or above +1.0): the flat curve is not established on PC at this scale, so the test stops. Screen G3 fails: no repetition effect of the needed size at about 31 passes, so no six-seed run. Six-seed refute (95% upper bound of mean(I) below +2.0): repeats do not explain the 8a-bar flatness for B2 at q33's pass count.
fixed_plan.null_risk: suggested (simulated, per-run sd 0.6 assumed): the premise passes about 80% at a true +0.5 control gain on the two-seed mean; the screen false-go rate under null is about 4%. The noise sd is assumed; the cross-machine offsets of 0.39 and 0.66 (shown) suggest it may be larger. If run-to-run sd is about 1.0, six seeds cannot separate I=+2 from zero (suggested). Shape-level repetition is unchanged for about ten low-capacity families (shown counts; suggested arithmetic), so a null can reflect shape repetition. Variant is 55% of the loss and mostly never-trained variants (shown), so a null can come from there. Coverage: B adds digit-shape overlap with dev, so a gain could be generator coverage (suggested). Init and learning-rate effects (no depth scaling, shown) and the depth-usefulness literature remain untested alternatives. B2 as coded has hand code (shown), so the result describes B2 as coded. The data is q33's 31-pass regime, not 8a's 4.3 passes (shown). It inherits the 62-token filter and 528 answer-only rows (shown).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Build-time measurements and a pre-ship data choice only; no step runs in the deployed model. The gates are fixed constants written before the runs, and no dev answer sets any runtime value. Rule 10 is respected at build time. The deploy-time analogue (the model writing fresh items and refusing its own exact repeats through a tool it chooses to call) is not claimed and would need its own autonomy check. B2 as coded keeps hand code between question and answer (shown), so no result here is a ship result.

Check the 8a 10M readout (not in this snapshot). If 8a 10M already clears the bar on six seeds, stop: B is redundant. Apply G3. If it fails, stop and write the result. Do not add seeds to chase a mark.
If G3 passes, run seeds 202 to 205 for B3, B10 and A10 (plain arms if the readout needs them). Apply G4 and the readouts. Write the result with its noise floor and per-split tables.

idea.title: T1 tool-loop behaviour battery on q40 checkpoints
idea.summary: As soon as queue 40 writes T1_s200 and T1_s201, run one eval-only script on the calls list that run() already returns. It measures five things nobody has measured: what T1 does after a refused call, whether its stop holds in free run, whether any call writes after a no-call round, whether call operands come from the transcript, and how NUM-heavy answer rows fare now that T1 has no NUM mode. No training, no parameters.
idea.change: Eval hooks in models/tool.py only. (1) Add a 'dropop' lesion (LESIONS line 66, generate state-path tuple line 226, calc call site line 181) that makes the tool answer '?' for one op chosen from dev counts before the run; log the next-round op. (2) Count free-run calls written after a NOOP round and calls at round 7, and compare free-run vs teacher-forced no-call accuracy (extra_evals 356-389). (3) Stricter source test than sources() (311-321): an operand counts as sourced only if it equals a prompt number, an earlier result, or 1, 2, 10, 100. (4) Calls per family from the calls list, with the 19 zero-parse families listed. (5) Per-mode, per-split exact for the 13 families that B2 answers through NUM (520 answer-split rows per seed), against B2 on the same seed.
idea.why: T1 is trained only on gold tapes, so every free-run behaviour below is off-distribution and unmeasured. Gold never contains '?' (str(v) at tool.py 245-247); a NOOP round only skips a write (173-177) and gold programs are contiguous from slot 0 (263-264); calc does no source check (43-53); B2 with every call refused falls to 0.24-0.82 on program families. T1 also loses B2's NUM answer path, and the premise check found 13 answer-split families (520 of 1,200 rows) that B2 answers through NUM at 96.7 percent; the T1 screen has no per-mode breakdown, so a loss there would hide inside pooled-5. All five checks reuse the same checkpoints, so the marginal cost is minutes.

problems: AUTONOMY WALK (shown from the idea text and tool.py): the probe adds no step to the deployed loop, so it does not break rule 10 as a diagnostic. Its human steps are test-side only: choosing the dropped op from dev counts, adding the lesion, setting thresholds, and choosing a rung after a failure. These are allowed because a probe is not a model method, but the dropped op must be fixed and logged before the run.

Deploy-time refusals are real, not only lesion events (shown): calc returns '?' for an unknown op, a non-integer operand, |x| or |y| or result >= 1e9, an inexact DIV, or MOD by 0 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/models/tool.py:43-53). Gold tapes never hold '?' (tool.py:245-247), and progparse drops programs with an inexact DIV ('bad div' in Builder.op in models/progparse.py). So T1 meets refusal states at deploy that it was never trained on. This is the strongest case for running the probe, and its marks should be read as deploy marks, not only as lesion marks.

Lesion routing fails silently (shown): Tool.generate passes a lesion to state() only for the names in the tuple at tool.py:226; any other name goes to base generate, which calls self.state(batch, None) with no lesion (models/base.py:50-54). A 'dropop:<OP>' passed through generate would run unlesioned with no error. Add it to that tuple and to LESIONS (tool.py:66), or call run(lesion=...) directly, and assert that the count of '?' entries is above zero before any metric is read.

Mark (a) is confounded (suggested, from gold structure): 'the next op is NOOP or a different op on >=90%' counts a healthy same-op chain (for example ADD then ADD) as a failure. The dropped op is chosen by dev frequency, so it is probably a common op. Replace the clause with: the identical call (same op and both operands) repeated on <=5%, and report same-op continuation separately. Events at round 7, which have no following round, must be excluded. The '>=100 events per seed' count is untested because dev op counts are not in the snapshot.

The stop-gap metric does not exist (shown): extra_evals pools op accuracy over every step, NOOP steps included (tool.py:367-380), and call accuracy covers only gold call steps (tool.py:375-377). The mark 'free-run no-call accuracy within 1.0 of teacher-forced' needs a new split: NOOP accuracy on steps past the gold program length, free run against teacher forcing. Teacher forcing shows the gold entries (tool.py:171 sets shown from gold op), so the gap is partly exposure bias and should be labelled that way.

The round-7 mark has no baseline (shown for the mechanism; the rate is untested): round 7 is a legal call round (tool.py:162, with N_RES 7 from progparse.py:8), and progparse keeps programs of up to 7 steps (progparse.py:199), so any gold 7-step row needs a round-7 call. LIMIT-COUNTS-2026-10-07.json lists only programs over 7. The dev share of exactly-7-step rows is not in the snapshot, so '<=1% of dev rows at round 7' may fail a perfect model. Rewrite it as round-7 calls on rows whose gold program has <=6 steps, and report the gold 7-step rate next to it.

The sourcing check uses the wrong tokenizer and an uncalibrated list (shown): the prompt-number reference is NUM_RE = \d+ (progparse.py:14, prompt_numbers at 17-18), which drops minus signs, so a correct copy of '-27' would count as unsourced. The area fact check reports 1,431 of 200,000 train prompts with minus digits (reported, not re-counted here). The list 1, 2, 10, 100 is progparse CONSTS (progparse.py:8). Calibrate the check on gold teacher-forced calls first (the baseline should be about 0), because the inverse-op rewrite in Builder.op (about progparse.py lines 42-51) means gold operands can differ from the steps as written. sources() (tool.py:311-321) counts any integer literal as sourced, so the stricter test is needed, but it is not yet calibrated.

The 13 NUM families are defined by gold labels, not by B2's behaviour (shown): the NUM share comes from pp.coverage, which calls row_targets (progparse.py:212-223) on the 6,800-row big in_dist, and each of the 13 families shows NUM 100 percent in RESULT.json extra.coverage. B2's final_eval.answer.by_family records only correct and n (40 rows per family per seed) and no mode. The 96.7 percent is B2's exact accuracy on those 520 rows per seed (per seed 95.6 to 97.5, pooled 96.7; computed from results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json), not a measured share answered through NUM. The per-mode breakdown in item 5 needs a new B2 run with mode logging. Mark (d) itself can be computed now from the existing answer by_family numbers, with no new code.

Mark (d) granularity is unspecified, and per-family is noise-level (suggested; arithmetic on an assumed 10 percent disagreement between two models, untested): 40 rows per family per seed gives 80 over two seeds, so 3 points is about 2.4 rows, and the SD of a per-family difference is roughly 3 to 4 points. Equal models would often fail. Pool the 13 families (1,040 rows over two seeds, SD near 1 point under the same assumption) and state that in the mark.

The 528 list_stats training rows have no program and no calls (LIMIT-COUNTS-2026-10-07.json; progparse.py:199; tool.py:139-141). Item 4 will therefore show zero calls on list_stats by construction. Report this as a training artifact (answer-only rows for long programs, which is a rule 7 issue, shown) and not as a model behaviour, and keep list_stats out of any zero-parse conclusion.

Final-answer provenance is missing (suggested; autonomy): the battery measures the call reaction but not what the talker writes after a refusal. A deployed model has no person to ask, so the key behaviour is that its answer is a number some tool or prompt produced, or that it declines. Add, on lesioned rows, the share of final answers equal to a prompt number, an earlier tool result or a constant, and the share that match the intact answer. This needs no training.

A learned sourcing signal can replace the whitelist (suggested; autonomy rescue): gen_copy returns a copy gate, but run() discards it (tool.py:166, 'p, _ ='). The gate on each operand cell is a self-signal the model can read at deploy time with no answers. Test on dev whether a low gate share predicts an unsourced operand (AUROC). This is the autonomous form of the 'source check' rung.

Rung autonomy (suggested): a deploy-time source check written as code in the forward pass breaks rules 1 and 10, because it is hand code with a parser constant list. If it is built, it must be a learned signal (the copy-gate item) or an outside tool the model itself chooses to call. Failure-reply training is pre-ship building, which rule 10 allows, but its refusal set must be fixed at build time and not drawn from dev counts, or the dev probe stops being a test.

The hooks sit in the file that ships (shown): the lesion and logging would go at tool.py:66, 181 and 226, and B3 mark 8 audits that forward path. Keep them in a test subclass or a test file so the shipped Tool class stays clean.

Stop correctness is not measured, only stop holding (suggested): the battery checks calls after NOOP and calls at round 7, but not premature NOOP, where the answer comes before the gold program's steps are written. Add free-run calls per row against gold program length on dev, binned by length.

Dev reuse (suggested; process): the probe runs on dev, a failure triggers a rung, and the T1 confirm then uses the same dev splits. Record which dev results were seen before the rung was chosen, or hold out a split the probe did not touch.

Use an intact-arm baseline: the same-op and exact-repeat rates after a successful call, with the mark on the difference, fixed in PASS-MARKS before the run.

The stop-gap mark has no defined sample. shown: extra_evals samples only program rows (tool.py:349 prows; tool.py:357 subsample 400), so the code the idea cites cannot produce a no-call comparison. The phrase 'no-call accuracy' could mean no-program rows or rows where the free run wrote no calls, and the idea does not say which. On 400 rows, 1.0 point is 4 rows; whether that is inside the paired noise is untested.

Mark (c) cannot fail for a copy-pointer writer and does not test correctness. shown: sources() (tool.py:311-321) takes a prompt argument and never uses it, so every integer literal counts as a source. The stricter test is new code and needs a gold calibration (gold tapes should read 100 percent sourced) and a shuffled-prompt control. computed (arithmetic, not measured): a random two-digit operand matches one of about 20 available values roughly 1 time in 5 if values spread over 1-99, so small invented operands pass by chance. Correctness is already measured as call accuracy (tool.py:375-377).

Each mark has an unassigned band with no verdict: (a) repeat 5 to 25 percent; (b) 0.5 to 5 percent; (c) 1 to 5 percent; (d) 3 to 8 points; stop gap 1 to 3 points. Give each mark pass, not shown and proved wrong, and state that not shown means no action.

A cheaper probe on existing checkpoints does not exist for these questions. shown: no T1 checkpoint is in the snapshot (no results/40-* folder; queue 40 not run). B2's NUM use is inferred, not measured. shown: the 13 families come from gold-mode coverage (progparse.py:212-223, row_targets) on the big in_dist, and RESULT.json stores no per-row B2 mode. chair.revised_idea: Eval-only behaviour battery for the tool loop, kept in a separate test script (monkeypatching calc; no edit to tool.py), run on dev only. Part A, zero compute, from T1's RESULT.json and PREDS.json versus B2's RESULT.json on the same seed: the 13 NUM-labelled answer-split families pooled (520 rows per seed), exact T1 minus B2, 2-seed mean, then T1 alone split by gold answer digit length (1-3 vs 4+). Pass >= -3.0, proved wrong < -8.0, between = not shown. Part B, one forward pass per seed, on a named dev build (big in_dist, 6,800 rows, 2,793 with programs): (B1) refusal reaction. Arm 1 is noexec (every call refused) with all events read from the calls list. Arm 2 is a monkeypatched calc that returns '?' for one op chosen by gold dev frequency and written in the marks file before the run. Measure the exact repeat of the refused call (same op and both operands), against the intact rate of exact repeats after a successful call, and report same-op continuation and final-answer provenance (a prompt number, an earlier result, a constant, or other) separately. Round-7 events are excluded. Seeds with fewer than 300 events use the next most frequent op by a rule fixed beforehand. (B2) stop. Report calls written after a NOOP round, calls on rows with no gold program (4,007 rows), and calls past the gold program length, with NOOP accuracy past gold length free-run vs teacher-forced (label the gap partly exposure bias). Report round-7 calls only on rows whose gold program has 6 or fewer steps, plus the exact-7-step share. (B3) sourcing: an operand counts as sourced if it equals a sign-preserving prompt number, an earlier non-'?' result, or 1, 2, 10, 100. It is calibrated first on gold teacher-forced calls (expect about 100%) and on a shuffled-prompt control (the control must be much worse than the intact run, else the test is void); '?'-dependent operands are excluded. (B4) calls per family from the calls list; list_stats and the 19 zero-parse families are reported as training artifacts (no program, w_noop 0.1), not behaviour. First assert that lesion=None reproduces the screen numbers exactly and that '?' entries occur under the lesion.
chair.plan_guidance: Seal marks in MARKS-D0-T1 as a dated amendment before the record run; label results a screen with no verdict. Runs: (1) dry run on 40b-t1-s200/s201 for calibration only (gold calibration, lesion=None reproduces screen numbers, event counts per op); (2) record run on the R1-R4 re-screen checkpoints (or on the next T1 checkpoints if R1-R4 fail). Marks, all judgement, fixed now, both seeds: A (above). B1 pass = exact repeat of the refused call <= 5% of events, proved wrong >= 25%, in between not shown (report the intact baseline beside it). B2 pass = gap calls <= 0.5% of rows, calls on no-program rows <= 2% (compare with B2 on the same seed if readable), round-7 calls on gold <=6-step rows <= 1%, free-run vs teacher-forced NOOP gap within 1.0 point; proved wrong at gap calls > 5% or stop gap > 3.0. B3 pass = unsourced <= 1% of intact calls, proved wrong > 5%. Each mark has three verdicts: pass, not shown (no action), proved wrong. A proved-wrong result does not patch T1 before the confirm; it is written up as a named idea (failure-reply teaching rows made by our own tool, a stop head inside H1, an answer-writer change) with its own screen and pre-set marks. Feed-through: B2 stop readings inform H1 marks H-c/H-d and PLAN 3c item 9; zero-round leak (loops:0 in_dist 9.41/5.00 on T1) is H-e, not this battery. Do not claim novelty: free-run call accuracy, tool-off and opswap already come from the T1 result files. Keep any later source check as an outside tool the model chooses to call, or a learned signal such as the discarded copy gate (tool.py:166); never code inside run(). Cost is about 15-30 minutes per seed on the PC (suggested; untested). Plain-language line for Ben: this checks whether the calculator loop behaves sensibly when things go wrong, using only runs we have already trained, and it cannot change any score.

plan.title: T1 loop behaviour battery (refusal, stop, sourcing), eval-only
plan.ben_line: When the calculator says no, or the model should stop, does the model still act sensibly? This checks that with runs we already have and a few hours of PC time; it can only point to a later fix and cannot change any score.
plan.question: Does the T1 calculator loop, as trained, respond sensibly when a calculator reply is refused, stop when its program is done, and copy operands from the question or earlier results; and does its answer accuracy on the 13 NUM-labelled families hold up without a number mode? Screen-level only; no training.
plan.one_change: One test-only script that runs the T1 loop on dev rows, reads the loop's own calls list, and scores the marks below. It changes no model, data, loss, training run or queue entry; the only patch is to calc() inside the test process.
arms: Part A (no new run): T1 minus B2 exact on the 13 NUM-labelled answer-split families (520 rows per seed), read from the two RESULT.json files, plus T1 exact split by gold answer digits (1-3 vs 4+).
Intact: T1 with no lesion. Baseline for every mark and for the gold sourcing calibration.
B1 noexec: every calculator call returns '?' (the existing lesion), with events read from the calls list.
B1 drop-op: calc() returns '?' for one op named in the marks file before the run (the most frequent gold op on the big in-distribution dev set).
B2 same-seed control (optional): the B2 checkpoint on the same 4,007 no-program rows, counting non-NOOP steps. Needs one B2 forward pass.
plan.seeds: Dry run (calibration, no verdict): 40b-t1-s200 and 40b-t1-s201 (mounted). Record run (screen): seeds 200 and 201 on the R1-R4 re-screen checkpoints, or on the next T1 checkpoints if R1-R4 fail. Six-seed confirm (200-205): only after T1's own six-seed confirm exists.
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC (CUDA), after the jobs already queued there (41-44). No rented GPU: rule 6 allows one only when the PC and the Mac are both full. The T1 screen itself ran on rented 5090s and no mounted note records the rule 6 reason for that. CPU speed is untested.
pass_marks: A1 (13 families, mean of T1 minus B2 over seeds 200-201, exact): pass >= -3.0; proved wrong < -8.0; between = not shown. Print odd_one_out (no program, copy only) beside it, and the 12 program families without it. An 8-point loss on 520 rows is 41.6 rows, about 0.7 pooled-5 points (shown arithmetic).
A2 (report only): T1 exact on the same rows split by gold answer digits, 1-3 vs 4+. A slice under 20 rows on a seed is printed and not judged.

B1 refusal reaction: exact repeat of the refused call (same op and both operands) on dropped-op events, with round-7 events excluded (the thinker never reads a round-7 entry; tool.py run loop). Pass <= 5%; proved wrong >= 25%; between = not shown. Print the intact exact-repeat rate after a successful call beside it. Report same-op continuation and final-answer provenance (prompt number, earlier result, constant, '?', other) with no mark.
B2a gap calls (a call at round t when an earlier round wrote nothing), all 6,800 big in-dist rows: pass <= 0.5% of rows; proved wrong > 5%.
B2b calls on the 4,007 rows with no gold program: pass <= 2%; proved wrong > 5% (suggested, untested). Use the B2 same-seed control if it is run.
B2c round-7 calls on rows whose gold program has 1 to 6 steps: pass <= 1%. Print the exact-7-step share from the dev file (not mounted); no proved-wrong line (suggested: > 5%).

B2d stop gap: NOOP accuracy at steps past the gold program length, free run minus teacher-forced, within 1.0 point; proved wrong > 3.0 points. Label the gap as partly exposure bias, since teacher forcing shows gold entries (tool.py run loop).

B3 sourcing: an operand is sourced if it equals a sign-preserving prompt number, an earlier non-'?' result, or 1, 2, 10, 100 (progparse CONSTS). '?'-dependent operands are excluded. Pass: unsourced <= 1% of intact calls; proved wrong > 5%. Void unless (i) gold teacher-forced calls are >= 99% sourced and (ii) the cross-row control (each operand tested against another row's prompt numbers) is at least 20 points below the intact rate (suggested line).
B4 (report only): calls per family. list_stats (all 16 over-7 rows in the big dev set) and the 19 zero-parse families are reported as training artifacts, not behaviour.

Instrument checks, before any mark is read: lesion none reproduces the T1 screen figures to 0.1 point (call accuracy free run 98.3/98.6, loops:0 9.41/5.00, tool off 0.29/0.53, swap 95.9/96.5); the drop-op arm produces '?' entries (count above 0); events per dropped op are recorded. A failed check voids the marks, not the model.
plan.proved_wrong: The idea is proved wrong as a diagnostic if the drop-op and intact arms give the same reaction tables on every row (the refusal changes nothing the marks can see), or if an instrument check cannot be fixed. A void instrument reads no mark. Each mark's own proved-wrong line is listed in pass_marks. Any proved-wrong result becomes a named defect with its own screen and pre-set marks (for example: failure-reply rows built from the model's own tool, a stop head inside H1, or an answer-writer change). It never patches T1 before its confirm, per analyze_t1's rule and rule 4.
plan.null_risk: Honest read (suggested, untested). B1 repeat <= 5% will probably pass for any model that does not repeat calls, whether or not it reads the '?'; the reaction table carries the information, not the mark. B2a (gap calls) will probably pass because gold never trains a gap (program rows are contiguous from slot 0), so it cannot tell a good stop from a model that always stops early. B2b is the mark most likely to show a real defect: 4,007 of 6,800 big-dev rows (59%) have no program and train NOOP at weight 0.1, while program rows train ops at weight 1.0 (tool.py:280, shown). B3 can pass by coincidence, because 1, 2, 10, 100 and prompt numbers are small and common; it counts only with the cross-row control. Part A's -3.0 line is probably the wrong place to look on the 40b checkpoints: the T1 screen's random-string copy table already shows 59% at 4 digits and 1% at 5 digits (shown, T1-SCREEN-RESULT), so a fail there re-measures the known copy break, not the loop.
plan.autonomy: The deployed model does every step itself: it reads the question, writes each calculator call as text, reads the calculator's reply as text in its tape, writes NOOP to stop, and writes the answer from its registers. The battery adds no deploy-time step. It runs the same loop, reads the calls list the loop already writes, and swaps calc() only inside the test process. The lesion, the dropped op, the sourcing list and the marks are test-side scoring, which rule 1 allows; none of them ships. Keep it that way: a sourcing or refusal check built into the deployed loop must be an outside tool the model chooses to call, or a learned signal (the copy gate that run() discards near tool.py:166), never code between question and answer.

problems: Autonomy walk-through (shown from the idea text): D2 adds no step to the deployed model. Its steps (copy dev data from the PC, re-run the checkpoints, label rows, read the decision table, choose which fix to build) are all done by researchers before shipping, which rule 10 allows. Reword it so nobody reads it as a deploy-time step.

Exposure gate cannot pass (shown by reading models/ledger.py run() lines 325-336 and the op_acc block at 567-588). Under gold forcing, B2 takes the gold op and operands, executes them, and builds the next state from executed values, while the scored heads are computed before forcing. Program match is first-error scored, and a value-correct pick gives the same state under gold and free run, so teacher-forced and free-run program match are equal by construction. The RESULT.json files match this on 8 of 8 seed pairs: 29-b2-screen s100 97.5/97.5 and s101 98.75/98.75; 33-pc-confirm s200-s205 98.0/98.0, 97.5/97.5, 97.0/97.0, 98.0/98.0, 97.0/97.0, 98.25/98.25. The idea's 'why' reads this as 'compounding is unproven where measured', which is a misreading: the metric cannot show compounding. The pass mark 'exposure live if variant gap >= 5.0 points' is unreachable, and its 'dead' branch would drop check-and-retry, scheduled sampling and pick audit for a metric reason.

Replacement measure (suggested, from the same code): use the step-level gap after the first free-run error. For rows where free run first errs at step j, compare free-run step-k accuracy (k > j) with teacher-forced step-k accuracy on the same rows. In distribution this gap is near zero because errors are rare: op accuracy differs on only one seed (s204, 99.96 teacher-forced vs 99.93 free run, about one step in 2,800), so the test has room only on variant rows, which pool to 34.7 exact (2,749 of 7,920 over six seeds, shown from RESULT.json). Re-fix the marks before any run (rule 4).

Pick check (operand picks 50% or more of wrong rows): needs agreement between two writes or a probe trained pre-ship (arXiv 2608.03071 is the suggested model). Check-and-retry: the retry trigger must not use the answer; the calculator can recheck arithmetic only, so the trigger needs self-consistency. chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test, but only after a rescue. It costs no params and no training, and it breaks no rule (shown: measurement only, rules 1-3, 5-7 and 9 hold). Rule 10 holds for the probe, because a researcher runs it before shipping. Its output only decides which fix to build, and each of those fixes needs its own deploy-time signal.

I verified the critics' main points against the code and files.

1. The exposure gate cannot pass (shown: ledger.py lines 325-336 and 567-587). Program match is scored as "every step right". Under gold forcing and free run the state is identical up to the first free-run error. After that error the free-run row is already counted wrong. So teacher-forced and free-run program match are equal by construction, and the 8 of 8 equal seed pairs (97.0-98.75) say nothing about compounding. The "TF minus FR >= 5.0" mark can never be met, and its "dead" branch would drop scheduled sampling for a metric reason. The idea's 'why' text reads this equality as "compounding unproven", which is a misreading. The replacement is the gold-forced minus free-run ANSWER gap on variant rows, plus step accuracy after the first free-run error.

2. The T1 half is stale (shown: /mnt/project-files/architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md). T1 already ran on seeds 200 and 201 and is NOT SHOWN. S1 pooled-5 is +1.72/-0.31 and S2 chain-5 is 99.7/99.9, both pass. S3 write-copy fails at 29.3/30.9 (operand) and 42.1/42.4 (answer). Copy works for 1-3 digits and collapses at 4 or more digits, which matches the training lengths. A T1 checkpoint is mounted under /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/. MARKS-D0-T1 already requires the link-by-link diagnosis. A T1 variant diagnosis would also describe a model whose writer is about to change. Drop it from this idea and redo it after the writer fix.

3. The probe covers only part of the variant misses (shown, from the critics' RESULT.json counts). About 65% of variant misses sit in families with 0% in-dist program coverage. The 8 flagged families hold 31% of misses (1,591 of 5,171) and have no gold program, so program-level labels (op, pick) can explain at most about a third. The label set also lacks answer mode, word pointer, name, format, sign lost and answer-prior match. D0b needed some of these.

4. The "new computation" flag test is confounded and needs no run (shown). The 17.1 vs 40.3 split reproduces only with an inferred 8-family mapping (seq_next, list_stats, digits_parity, letter_ops, word_filter, syllogism, group_induct, fewshot_number_rule). Seven of the 8 have 0% in-dist program coverage. Within no-program families the gap is 17.1 (flagged) vs 32.3 (unflagged). So the flag cannot separate new computation from missing worked steps. Syllogism sits at 47.5%, equal to the shortcut rate in data.md line 44, so it needs an answer-prior baseline. A 33-family Spearman with the 0.3 mark has almost no power: the critics estimated it passes about 86% of the time under no relationship and has a 95% interval of about +-0.35.

5. Data is not in the snapshot. There are no dev files and no PREDS.json for any B2 run. So per-row labels need a checkpoint re-run after Ben copies the dev files from the PC. The six checkpoints for seeds 200-205 are in the snapshot (b2ckpt, sha256 checked), so a 6-seed run is possible and the plan should not use 2 seeds. Rule 4 wants 6. The 2-seed s100/s101 design mixes data builds.

6. The decision table has gaps and mixes models. Several bands have no outcome (exposure gap 2-5, pick share 25-50, call-choice gap 5-20, gold-forced under 60), and a sign disagreement between seeds is unhandled. The gold arm in tool.py and ledger.py forces op and picks together, so it cannot split op choice from operand writing. In ledger.py the pick mask comes from the gold slot sets.

7. Selection risk (rule 4). Variant is part of the sealed pooled-5. LIMIT-COUNTS has a separate big_dev_variant (6,600 rows) beside dev_variant (1,320 rows, shown). Diagnosing on one and scoring any chosen fix on the other limits selection on the sealed mark, but only if the two are disjoint. That disjointness is not shown and must be checked before the run.

Value to the lead: this is a gate, not a gain. It matters only if check-and-retry, pick audit, scheduled sampling or list ops would otherwise be built. Cheap, rank moderate. It carries a risk of finding that the dominant variant misses are in no-program families that none of those fixes touch (suggested, partly shown at family level).
chair.revised_idea:
tool-D2 (revised): a B2-only, six-seed, inference-only diagnosis of the variant split. It runs on CPU or the PC and trains nothing. It adds no params and no deploy-time step. It is a pre-ship research measurement that picks which learned fix, if any, is worth a GPU run.

Scope. Use B2 seeds 200-205 from the snapshot's b2ckpt folder (sha256 checked). Keep s100 and s101 only as a cross-check, and state which data build each seed used. Drop the T1 half. T1 is already NOT SHOWN at the screen because write-copy fails beyond 3 digits, and the sealed MARKS-D0-T1 already requires its link diagnosis. Re-do the T1 version only after the writer fix, with arms: free run, gold op only, gold operand strings only, full gold tape.

Step 0, no GPU, runnable now. Make a 33-family table for variant from the six RESULT.json files:
- B2 miss rate and in-dist program coverage;
- answer-mode share (NUM, WORD, GEN);
- a per-family answer-prior baseline (majority answer or the 'starts with No' shortcut for syllogism);
- the flagged set named in full (the 8 families above), with 17.1 vs 40.3 and the within-stratum numbers 17.1 vs 32.3 reported side by side.
Drop the Spearman mark. Report the share of variant misses that sit in program-bearing families (about 35%) vs zero-program families, so the lead sees how much any program-level fix can reach.

Step 1, on Ben's machine after he copies the dev splits. Rows to use:
- If big_dev_variant (6,600 rows) is disjoint from the 1,320 judged dev_variant rows, diagnose on big_dev_variant and keep dev_variant for scoring any later fix.
- If it is not disjoint, say so and treat the diagnosis as selection on the sealed split.
- Add in_dist as the control. Exclude the answer split's degenerate cells (data.md line 50) from label counts.
Save per-row predictions. Write a small helper that builds (R, tape, lmode, lword) from run(batch, gold=...) so talk() can score a gold-forced answer. Use batch size 1 for gold arms to avoid tape-layout changes.
Arms per row: free run; fully gold-forced; gold ops with free picks; free ops with gold picks. For each pair report paired counts (both right, gold-only, free-only) and an exact McNemar test. Add a planted-wrong-first-call positive control. Replace 'teacher-forced vs free-run program match' with (i) the gold-forced minus free-run answer gap on program-bearing variant rows, and (ii) step accuracy after the first free-run error, compared with teacher-forced step accuracy on the same rows. Also report the rank of the gold op (top-1, top-2, top-4) under teacher forcing.

Labels. Label every variant miss with its first wrong link, not only program rows: no program / op wrong / pick wrong split into key error (gold slot ranked low by its own pooled-span key) and query error / sign lost / answer mode wrong / word pointer wrong / name wrong / format wrong / matches the answer-prior baseline. Adapt diag_c1_links.py (D0b classes). Hand-check about 50 rows per class and report agreement. Report the 10 distinct chain-5 failing rows by id (8 recur; state_update-DI1-137 fails on all six).

Marks, fixed now. These are my suggested thresholds and are untested. They must be re-sealed by Ben before the run. Every outcome has a verdict and every seed pattern is covered.
- Program or call choice is a variant bottleneck if the gold-forced minus free-run answer gap on program-bearing variant rows is >= 10 points on >= 5 of 6 seeds. Reading or answer writing is the bottleneck if the gap is < 3 points on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
- A pick check is worth building only if pick errors are >= 50% of program-bearing wrong rows on >= 5 of 6 seeds. An op check is worth building only if the gold op is in the top-2 for >= 70% of op-wrong rows on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
- Anything else, including seeds that disagree in sign, is 'not shown', and nothing is built from it.
- Proved wrong for check-and-retry, pick audit and scheduled sampling: gap < 3 on >= 5 of 6 seeds AND pick share < 25%. Scheduled sampling is killed only by step accuracy after the first error showing no gap. Pick audit is judged only by first-link pick share.
- Whatever the outcome, state that program-level labels cover only the program-bearing share of misses, so a program-level fix cannot move the zero-program families.

Rule 10 and rule 5 conditions. The diagnosis is pre-ship research. Any fix it selects must name a deploy-time signal that needs no answer key (self-consistency between two reads, calculator recheck, or a probe trained pre-ship on the model's own tries), with fixed design constants and nothing tuned on dev answers. The designers' flag and the variant failures must not choose practice kinds, because the variant split is the source of ST1's held-out kinds (PLAN line 84). Name the split and seeds that will screen any chosen fix before the run, and do not reuse the T1 screen seeds as pass seeds for a changed model.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

(1) Do not use teacher-forced vs free-run program match as the exposure measure. It is equal by construction because it is first-error scored (ledger.py 325-336, 567-587). Use the gold-forced minus free-run answer gap on variant rows, plus step accuracy after the first free-run error. Include a planted-wrong-call positive control and paired counts with an exact McNemar test.

(2) Run on B2 seeds 200-205, not s100/s101, and keep B2 and T1 tables separate. T1 has run (NOT SHOWN, S3 write-copy fails beyond 3 digits, mounted under /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/). Defer the T1 variant arms until after the writer fix, with separate arms for gold op, gold operand strings and full gold tape.

(3) Data prerequisites. The dev splits and big_dev_variant are not in the snapshot, and no PREDS.json exists for any B2 run, so Ben must copy them from the PC. First check whether big_dev_variant (6,600 rows) is disjoint from the 1,320 judged dev_variant rows. If it is, diagnose on big dev and score any fix on dev_variant. If not, state the selection risk. Add a state-from-run helper for gold arms and use batch size 1.

(4) Cover all variant misses, not just program rows. About 65% of variant misses are in zero-program families and 31% are in the 8 flagged families (the 8 families are named in the revised idea). Use the 33-family answer-prior baseline and the label classes sign lost, answer mode, word pointer, name and format. Hand-check about 50 rows per class.

(5) Fixed marks must partition all outcomes. Treat sign disagreement between seeds as 'not shown' (build nothing), and require >= 5 of 6 seeds. Mark the thresholds as suggested and untested, and have Ben re-seal them. Drop the Spearman mark. Report the flag gap inside the zero-program stratum (17.1 vs 32.3) instead.

(6) Plain-language summary for Ben, as the repo's CLAUDE.md requires for outside prompts: "we ask the trained model the variant questions twice, once on its own and once with the right first steps handed to it. If handing it the steps barely helps, the mistake is in reading or writing the answer, not choosing steps, and no step-checker will help. If it helps a lot, step choice is the weak link." Label every claim shown, suggested or untested, and keep the B2 card experiments separate from the village model.

(7) Rule 10: name the deploy-time signal for each fix the table would unlock, and keep the designers' flag and the variant failures out of the choice of practice kinds.

(8) Cost. The "2 hours" estimate is untested. The probe is inference-only, and most of the time is setup and copying files.

plan.title: B2 variant misses: steps or answer? (six-seed forced-step diagnosis)
plan.ben_line: We ask the trained model the variant questions twice: once on its own, and once with the right steps handed to it. If handing it the right steps barely helps, the mistake is in writing the answer, so a step-checker will not help. If it helps a lot, picking the steps is the weak link.
plan.question: On B2's variant split (new layout and new wording), when the right operations and operand picks are handed to the model, does it answer correctly? That shows whether the misses come from choosing the steps or from writing the answer once the steps are right.
plan.one_change: Eval only, with no weight change and no training: add two forcing modes to B2's run() (gold operations only, and gold operand picks only, beside the existing mode that forces both) plus a state helper, then run four arms and three controls on the six existing B2 checkpoints (seeds 200 to 205).
arms: F (free): the model's own steps and answer, talk(state(batch)). This is the baseline.

O (operations forced): gold operations, the model's own operand picks. New mode 'op' in ledger.run(). Shown: today's gold branch (ledger.py ~lines 326-331) forces both the operations and the picks, so this arm needs a code change.
P (picks forced): the model's own operations, gold operand picks. New mode 'picks'.

G (both forced): gold operations and gold-valid picks, the existing gold branch. This isolates the answer stage on right steps. The helper builds (R, vals, valid, lmode, lans, lword) from run(batch, gold=g), the same tuple state() returns for B2 because span is False (shown: ledger.py ~lines 358-362).

C1 identity control: on in-dist and variant rows whose free program is fully right, G and F must agree on the answer for at least 99% of rows. Suggested: this follows from the code, since forced and free picks coincide when the free pick lies in the gold set. Untested as a check.

C2 planted-error control: on 500 in-dist program rows, plant one wrong operation or one value-changing wrong pick at step 1 (skip rows where the planted result equals the gold result). The answer must change on at least 80% of rows, which shows the answer stage reads the program. Suggested threshold.

C3 in-dist control: G minus F on in-dist program rows must be at most the in-dist program error rate plus 1 point. That rate is shown as 1.75 to 3.0 points on the six seeds (RESULT.json extra.op_acc, 400-row subsample, 100 minus free-run program match).
S compounding measure: step accuracy after the first free-run error, teacher-forced (G) versus free (F), on the same rows. Suggested measure.
L first-link labels: the first wrong link for every variant miss, program-bearing or not, with a 50-row hand check per class (step 8).
plan.seeds: 200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 205: the six B2 checkpoints in the snapshot at code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 to B2_s205. Shown: each checkpoint.pt matches its .sha256 file. Seeds 100 and 101 are a cross-check only and enter no verdict: their RESULT configs read /job/data, while 200 to 205 read Ben's C:\Users\benja\custom-io\work\data (shown), so the data builds may differ (untested).
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC for the forward passes, because the dev files exist only on the PC (inference only). M1 Pro CPU as a fallback for the labels and the planted control. No rented GPU (rule 6). No training and no weight change.
pass_marks: Before any run, Ben seals the arms, controls, verdicts, kill rules and the 8-family flag set. The thresholds here are suggested and untested; they are re-sealed by Ben and never loosened after a result.

Controls, all must pass before any gap is read: C1 agreement at least 99% on all six seeds; C2 answer change at least 80% on at least 5 of 6 seeds; C3 within its bound on all six seeds. A seed with fewer than 300 program-bearing variant rows is not counted (suggested).

Verdict A, step choice is the bottleneck: G minus F on program-bearing variant rows is at least +10 points on at least 5 of 6 seeds, with one sign, and the controls pass. Then O and P name the link: O at least +10 on at least 5 seeds means operation choice; P at least +10 on at least 5 seeds means operand picks; both means both.

Verdict B, answer writing is the bottleneck: G minus F is below +3 on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and the controls pass. Report 100 minus G per seed beside it, which is the answer-stage error on right steps.

Verdict C, not shown: any other pattern (gaps of 3 to 10 on most seeds, mixed signs, or a control failing on 2 or more seeds). Build nothing from this run and publish the numbers. With six seeds, A and B cannot both hold.

Inside A: a pick check is worth building only if pick errors are at least 50% of program-bearing wrong rows on at least 5 of 6 seeds. An operation check (two candidates) only if the gold operation is in the top 2 for at least 70% of operation-wrong rows on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and operation-wrong rows are at least 10% of program-bearing wrong rows on at least 5 of 6 seeds (suggested).

Denominators fixed in advance: program-bearing means the row's gold program (pp.row_targets) is non-empty, counted per row on the variant file, not per family. Program-bearing wrong means such a row whose free answer is wrong. A label class is used only if a 50-row hand check agrees with the automatic label on at least 85% of rows (suggested).

Statistics: exact McNemar on discordant pairs for each arm against F, reported with counts (both right, forced-only right, free-only right). Verdicts use effect size and seed count; p-values are reported, not gated (suggested).
plan.proved_wrong: Verdict B (G minus F below +3 on at least 5 of 6 seeds, controls passing) proves wrong that choosing steps is the variant bottleneck. It kills the operation check, the pick check and check-and-retry for variant. Pick audit is killed if its first-link pick share is below 25% on at least 5 of 6 seeds; the brief judges pick audit only by that share but also states a combined rule with the gap, which is inconsistent and should be re-sealed by Ben. Scheduled sampling is killed if the compounding measure S (teacher-forced minus free step accuracy after the first error) is below 2 points on at least 5 of 6 seeds. A control failure does not prove the idea wrong; it means the gap cannot be read, so the verdict is not shown.
plan.null_risk: Partly, so the controls carry the weight. (1) Identity bounds the gap: when the free program is right, the forced and free runs coincide, so the gap cannot exceed the share of program-wrong rows (suggested, from the code; C1 tests it). A pass therefore needs real program errors, but the 10-point line is an effect-size choice, not a noise limit (suggested). (2) Verdict B can pass when the answer stage ignores the program, for example when answers come from the prompt or a pattern; C2 guards this. (3) Verdict A can pass from a helper bug or from a distribution shift in the forced states; C1 and C3 guard this. (4) Labels can pass by convention, for example by calling ambiguous misses pick errors; the 85% hand-check gate guards this. (5) Eight variant families have identical correct counts on all six seeds (chain_ops 40, story_chain3 40, story_addsub 23, syllogism 19, var_chain 12, word_filter 15, letter_ops 0, list_stats 0; shown from RESULT.json), so cross-seed agreement counts fixed behaviour six times; report per family. (6) The flag gap (17.1 vs 40.3 for 8 vs 25 families; 17.1 vs 32.3 inside the low-coverage stratum) uses an inferred mapping: data.md line 53 names kinds 'count_above' and 'num_digits', which are not family names in the snapshot (shown), so digits_parity is an inferred match. Eight families is too few to separate new computation from missing worked steps. (7) The 34.7% and 65.3% program shares (shown from RESULT.json) use in-distribution coverage as a proxy, because RESULT extra.coverage is computed on the big in-dist file, not on variant; variant shares are unknown until counted. (8) The 3-to-10 band is not shown, which prevents false builds but can hide a real small effect.
plan.autonomy: This is pre-ship research. Nothing in it runs when the model answers. The forced arms, planted errors, hand labels and verdicts are researcher steps before shipping (rule 10 allows that), they add no parameters, and they change no weights. The deployed model does its own steps as before. Any fix this points to must name a deploy-time signal that uses no answer key, for example self-consistency between two independent reads of the question, a calculator recheck of arithmetic results only (not of picks), or a probe trained before shipping on the model's own tries (suggested; arXiv 2608.03071 in the papers list). Practice kinds may not be chosen from the designers' flags or from variant failures, because the variant split is the source of ST1's held-out kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS line 84, shown).
steps: 0. Ben seals the arms, controls, verdicts, kill rules and the 8-family flag set (families: seq_next, list_stats, digits_parity, letter_ops, word_filter, syllogism, group_induct, fewshot_number_rule; digits_parity is an inferred match to 'num_digits', data.md line 53) before any forced-arm run.

1. No GPU, already checked in this read from the six RESULT.json files (shown). Variant misses: 5,171 of 7,920 over six seeds. The 14 families with in-dist program coverage of at least 50% hold 1,794 misses (34.7%); the other 19 hold 3,377 (65.3%); the 18 families at 0.0% coverage hold 3,137 (60.7%); the 8 flagged families hold 1,591 (30.8%). Mean accuracy: flagged 17.1 vs 40.3 for the other 25; inside the low-coverage stratum 17.1 (8 families, including list_stats) vs 32.3 (11). Free-run accuracy on the 14 program families is 46.6% (1,566 of 3,360). list_stats has 29% in-dist coverage, but the 7-step cap explains only 16 of its 200 big in-dist rows (LIMIT-COUNTS), so the cause of its other no-program rows is untested. Chain-5 failures by id (chain5.intact.hits, shown): 26 misses on 10 distinct rows, 24 state_update and 2 story_chain3; state_update-DI1-137 fails on all six seeds, -99 on four, -111 and -303 on three, -257, -139, -328 and story_chain3-DI1-36 on two, -337 and -408 on one.

2. Ben copies from his PC: data/dev/variant.jsonl (1,320 sealed rows), data_big/dev/variant.jsonl (6,600 rows), data_big/dev/in_dist.jsonl (6,800 rows) and data/train.jsonl (for the answer prior; check its hash). None of these is in the snapshot (shown: no variant or in_dist jsonl found).

3. Overlap check by id on the PC. data.md line 5 says a scratch rebuild kept the old dev rows as a per-family prefix of the 6,600-row variant file (a note; untested on the PC files). If the first 40 rows of each family match the 1,320 sealed rows, the diagnosis uses only the 5,280-row suffix (160 per family), which leaves the sealed rows clean for scoring any fix. If the check fails, report the overlap and the selection risk. The brief's 'disjoint' test answers 'not disjoint' on the note's account.

4. Count on the PC: program-bearing variant rows per family (rows with a non-empty pp.row_targets prog); rows with a minus sign before a digit (the regex \d+ drops the sign, progparse.py line 14); and answer priors per family from the train file (most common train answer; syllogism's 'starts with No' rule, data.md line 44). Do not fit priors on dev. Answer-mode shares in RESULT coverage are in-distribution, not variant, so compute variant mode shares here. Also count variant rows whose gold answer exceeds 8 characters (LIMIT-COUNTS shows max answer 7 for big variant; expected 0).

5. Code, eval only: in ledger.py run() (gold branch, ~lines 326-331) add gold_mode 'both' (the existing behaviour), 'op' (gold op, argmax picks) and 'picks' (argmax op, gold picks). Add a state helper that returns (R, vals, valid, lmode, lans, lword) from run(batch, gold=g). The eval batch can stay at 128: B2's gold() pads to a fixed N_RES=7 steps and M=27 slots (shown: ledger.py gold(); progparse.py lines 8-10), so no layout depends on the batch. The same-answer check C1 at batch 128 will catch any batch effect. Batch size 1 is not needed for B2; the tape-layout concern applies only to T1.

6. Run per checkpoint: arms F, O, P, G on the suffix program-bearing variant rows; F only on the suffix non-program rows (for labels); C1 on in-dist and variant rows; C2 planted on 500 in-dist program rows; C3 on in-dist program rows. Save per row: free and gold programs, step logits (rank of the gold op), decoded mode, the four answers.

7. Analyse: per seed, the gap G minus F, the O and P gaps, 100 minus G, the control results, paired counts with exact McNemar, the rank of the gold op (top 1, 2, 4) under G, the compounding measure S, first-link shares among program-bearing wrong rows, and the prior-match rate. Apply verdicts A, B, C and the kill rules from pass_marks.

8. First-link labels (B2 classes; adapt diag_c1_links.py, whose a to x labels belong to the text baseline and should not be reused as they are). Program-bearing rows: no program written; operation wrong (split by gold op rank); pick wrong, split by the gold operand's digit count, since D0 shows the pooled number keys lose digits at place 9 (65.2 to 83.2%, shown in D0-RESULT); sign lost. Other rows: answer mode wrong (NUM, WORD or GEN); word pointer wrong; GEN copy wrong, split into one character off versus far; answer equals the family's train prior; gold program absent. Hand-check about 50 rows per class and report agreement.
9. Apply the verdicts. Controls first; then A, B or C. Only A or B may lead to a next step. C builds nothing.

10. If A: take the operation or pick check decision from pass_marks. Any chosen fix gets a new one-change plan, a named deploy-time signal and sealed marks before any model run. If B: the next step is an answer-stage label breakdown (mode, pointer, word, copy) and an answer-writer plan on the ladder (O1), not a checker. The answer stage also reads the pooled number keys (ledger.py ~line 291), so 'writing' here includes that reading (suggested).

11.
