fixed_plan.title: B2 variant misses: free-run decomposition first, then gated forced arms
fixed_plan.ben_line: We give the model the new-style questions it gets wrong, then hand it the right steps and see whether it now gets the answer. If the right steps fix most misses, choosing steps is the weak spot; if they barely help, turning steps into an answer is.
fixed_plan.question: On B2's variant split, does a wrong answer come from a wrong calculation chain (the steps) or from the answer stage after right steps, once the layout, answer-keyed label and reading confounds are separated?
fixed_plan.one_change: No model change and no weight change. One eval-only record added to B2's evaluation: for each variant row, the free run's final computed value against the gold answer, plus the answer-head error type (mode, pointer, copy). Forced arms run only if that record leaves the question open.
arms: F (free, baseline): the model's own steps and answer, as today.

D (decomposition from F, no forcing): a wrong final computed value is a step error; a right final value with a wrong output is an answer-stage error. Split answer-stage errors into mode, pointer on a slot holding the gold value, pointer with no gold slot, and GEN or WORD copy.
G (both forced, the existing gold branch): gold ops, picks restricted to slots holding the gold value; answer heads still read the model's own state. Run only after D. Do not read its S measure.
O (gold ops, free picks): new eval mode with unmasked picks.
P (free ops, gold-valid picks): new eval mode with masked picks.

Controls: R (reproduce RESULT.json for B2_s200 before anything else); C1 (G equals F exactly on rows where F's ops and picks are all gold-valid; must be 100 percent); C2 (planted step-1 error on in-dist rows where the recomputed gold final value changes and the gold answer is not a prompt number; answer changes on at least 80 percent); C3a (in-dist G minus F between 0 and (100 minus F's in-dist answer accuracy) plus 1 point; above that bound means the forced labels carry answer information); C3b (in-dist O minus F within 1 point of 0, since in-dist op accuracy is 99.93 to 100).

Strata: every verdict is reported on the primary stratum (gold program not answer-derived: no missing-operand rewrite, no MIN or MAX chosen from the answer, no integer-answer program dropped; and not held-out layout), and also on all rows, layout rows, answer-derived rows and syllogism shortcut-match rows.
fixed_plan.seeds: 200 to 205: the six B2 checkpoints in the snapshot (code/b2ckpt), the same six that produced RESULT.json. A diagnosis needs no new seeds. Any later fix is screened on seeds 300 and 301 and confirmed on 302 to 307.
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC for forward passes (inference only; minutes per checkpoint). Label analysis on the PC or the M1 Mac. No rented GPU (rule 6). No training and no weight change.
pass_marks: Gate R (before any arm): B2_s200 reproduces variant 421 of 1,320, chain-5 intact 994 of 1,000, and in-dist op accuracy 98.0 (free program) and 98.0 (free answer) on the same 400-row subsample. Any mismatch stops the run until the data build or checkpoint is explained (suggested).

Gate C (controls; all six seeds unless stated): C1 exactly 100 percent; C3a and C3b inside their bounds; C2 at least 80 percent answer change on at least 5 of 6 seeds (suggested). A failed control means the gap is not read; it is a bug or a leak to fix first.
Decomposition D (primary stratum, reported first): share of wrong rows with a wrong final value (step error) versus a right final value (answer-stage error), with answer-stage error types.

Verdict A (steps are the bottleneck): on the primary stratum, G minus F at least +10 on at least 5 of 6 seeds, the O or P arm carries the gain (at least +10 on at least 5 seeds), and at least 60 percent of program-wrong rows show a wrong final value under D (suggested).

Verdict B (answer stage is the bottleneck): on the primary stratum, G minus F below +3 on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and at least half of the G-stage answer errors are mode or copy errors rather than pointer errors on a slot holding the gold value. Pooled-key pointer errors are reported as reading, not writing (suggested).
Verdict C (not shown): any other pattern, including a gap of 3 to 10 on most seeds. Build nothing; publish the table.
Labels: a class is used only if a 50-row hand check agrees with the automatic label on at least 85 percent of rows (suggested). Reason codes come from progparse.program_for, not one catch-all class.

Statistics: family-level statements use a bootstrap over the 33 families; seeds are replicates on fixed rows, so five-of-six-seed counts are not independent evidence. Exact McNemar per arm against F, with counts. Effect sizes and seed counts drive verdicts; p-values are reported.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Verdict B proves wrong that step choice is the primary bottleneck on the primary stratum if D shows at least 80 percent of wrong rows have a wrong final value (suggested); it also kills the operation and pick checks for variant. Verdict A proves wrong that the answer stage is the bottleneck if G minus F is at least +10 on at least 5 of 6 seeds in the primary stratum, unless the gain sits only in the answer-derived stratum, which is then a label effect and not a finding. The pick audit is killed if its first-link pick share is below 25 percent on at least 5 of 6 seeds (one rule only; Ben re-seals).
fixed_plan.null_risk: Mostly confounds rather than noise: (1) answer-derived gold programs can pass G and O on label construction (the stratum guards this); (2) held-out layout rows (313 variant rows, all of state_update and story_chain3) can look like step error (the layout stratum guards this); (3) pooled-key pointer loss can pass verdict B as writing (the error-type split guards this); (4) the six seeds are replicates on one fixed set, and 8 families have identical counts across seeds, so family-level claims rest on about 33 families; (5) the 10-point and 3-point lines are effect-size choices, and the 3-to-10 band is the likely outcome, which returns not shown; (6) the in-dist operation accuracy of 99.93 to 100 predicts a near-zero O gain in-dist, which is a control, not a finding.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Research-only, before shipping. Forced arms, labels and the decomposition are researcher steps; they change no weights, and the deployed model does its own steps as before (rule 10 allows this). Any fix this points to must name a deploy-time signal that uses no answer key: self-consistency between two reads, a calculator recheck of arithmetic results only, or a probe trained before shipping on the model's own tries. Practice kinds may not be chosen from the generator's flags or from variant failures; PLAN-AND-MARKS line 84 (ST1 kinds named from the variant split) must be re-sealed before any ST1 run.
steps: 0. Ben seals before any run: the arms, controls, thresholds, strata and their definitions; the 8-family mapping (count_above has no family name among the 33 and needs a decision); the rule that the diagnosis does not choose ST1 kinds; and one pick-audit kill rule. 2. Copy to the PC: data/dev/variant.jsonl (1,320 rows), data_big/dev/variant.jsonl (6,600), data_big/dev/in_dist.jsonl (6,800), data/train.jsonl (check its hash). 3. Tag every variant row: answer-derived program (missing-operand rewrite; MIN or MAX chosen from the answer; integer-answer program kept or dropped), layout (Question and Facts), never-trained words, numbers over 16 or a minus sign, the program_for reason code, and the syllogism shortcut match.

4. Eval-only record on arm F for all six checkpoints: final computed value (last executed result slot), gold answer, output, mode and pointer validity. This gives D with no forcing and is the first result read.

5. Eval-only code: add gold_mode 'op' (gold ops, free picks) and 'picks' (free ops, masked picks) beside the existing 'both' path, plus the decomposition helper. Test that 'both' reproduces step 1 and that the default training loss is unchanged on a fixed batch (the gold argument is shared with training).
6. Run controls C1, C2 (restricted), C3a and C3b on in-dist rows; then G, O and P on the variant program rows (count the actual suffix rows per family; 160 suffix rows per family at most).
7. Analyse by stratum: per-seed gaps, D, answer-stage error types, paired counts with exact McNemar, the family bootstrap, and the flagged-family table as description only.
8. Labels: first wrong link from the reason codes; a 50-row hand check per class; at most six classes; a class is used only at 85 percent agreement or better.
9. Apply the gates, verdicts and kill rules. Publish the full table whatever the verdict.

10. Only after A or B: a one-change plan for the next step, with a named deploy-time signal and sealed marks. Any fix is screened on seeds 300 and 301 with fresh generator rows if the skills branch is available, because the sealed 1,320 rows share all 33 families with the diagnosis.

idea.title: Probe whether tape entries are read back digit-exact
idea.summary: T1 reads each calculator entry alone from position 0, and the whole claim 'the model reads the tool's reply back' rests on that. Two cheap checks: now on the mounted B2 reader (digit probe on 'add 12 5 = 17'-style strings, read alone vs after a question, plus a receptive-field check), and after q40 on T1 (thinker-state digit probe per round, joint-transcript swap eval). Together they say whether any read-back repair is needed.
idea.change: Stage A, CPU, B2_s100/s101, no change to the model: copy diag_d0.py features. About 6,000 calc-true strings in tool.entry() format (ops add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max, cmp; non-negative 1-9 digit operands), conditions A = reader(entry) alone, B = reader(question + ' ' + entry) at true positions, C = entry alone with position ids shifted. Linear probes per place 1-9, split by entry. Plus a perturbation check: states change only within 4 characters of a changed input, and an incremental append (re-read 8 characters before the junction, the entry, 4 after) matches a full re-read. Stage B, after q40, on T1_s200/s201: a copied loop that saves ln_z(Z[:,0]) after each round, probe the newest visible entry's digits (entry k at round k+2); and an eval flag that re-reads [question + visible entries] jointly, then scores pooled-5 and chain-5 with the same weights.
idea.why: D0 passed on question numbers (99.997-100 percent at every place, six seeds) but never read tool-format entries, never read them alone vs jointly, and did not look at the thinker state. T1's entries are normal digit order (calc returns str of an int), so the place labels count correctly from the right. The only open risks are the apart read (T1 differs from Ben's 'append to the transcript' picture by a position offset and a 4-character junction) and whether the controller state keeps the digits. The probe tells which, before six confirm runs are spent.

test.pass_mark: Fixed now. More important, B2 never reads a tape entry (the tape exists only in tool.py), while T1's reader was trained through entries, so B2's reader is not the reader T1 uses. The claim that B2 is a fair proxy until T1 exists is out of date. Probe T1's own reader (read_texts, tool.py:84-99) and use B2 as reference only.

STAGE B JOINT EVAL CANNOT RUN AS WRITTEN (shown from code, arithmetic checked): the reader's position table has 208 rows (models/reader.py:72; data.py:11). The 169-character question cap fits exactly one 38-character calc entry (169 + 1 + 38 = 208). Two visible entries need at least 247 positions, and seven need about 442. nn.Embedding cannot index past its size, so the eval would fail or need a longer table, which is a model change, not an eval flag. Capping questions also removes the long-question cases where a joint read would fail first (a selection bias), and it does not apply to T1's actual apart read at all.

STAGE B PROBES THE WRONG OBJECT (shown code path; mechanism suggested): the probe reads ln_z(Z[:,0]) (tool.py:164). In T1 the writer's digits come from copy attention: cell j's query is W_k(z) + reader place row j (tool.py:110-113, 166-167), and the keys are reader output over the prompt and the tape (ledger.py:239-249). A linear probe on z failing does not mean digits were lost, and passing does not mean the pointer finds them. gen_copy also returns the copy gate, which run() discards (tool.py:166-167). The missing link named in T1-SCREEN-RESULT ('(d) result reading') is never measured. The direct test is the copy-attention argmax per cell against the gold character of the newest entry, plus the gate.

SIGNS ARE NEVER PROBED (shown): calc takes operands matching -?\d+ (tool.py:40), sub returns a-b (models/progparse.py:24), so entries like 'sub 3 5 = -2' are normal; word_spans makes '-' its own token (data.py:149). The spec covers non-negative operands only and never mentions negative results. Signed operands and results must be in the probe set.

PASS MARK IS WEAKER THAN D0'S (shown): 'A-own >= 99.0' uses the own-character probe. The D0 mark that passed used the 9-character window ending at each number (code/reader/custom_io/diag_d0.py:1-8, 40-76; no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md). The own character keeps its token embedding in the residual stream (reader.py:86 plus conv residual blocks), so it is probably trivially decodable (suggested, untested). Use the window metric as the mark.

PERTURBATION CLAIM IS WRONG FOR INSERTIONS (shown): place_ids counts places from the right end of each word token (reader.py:17-23), so inserting or deleting a digit changes the place code of every digit in that token, up to about 9 characters away. The receptive field of +-4 (reader.py:5) holds for substitutions of equal length only. Restrict the perturbation test to substitutions, or state the expected radius.

'RESTART-POSITION' IS UNDEFINED (shown): the phrase appears in the area summary and in the idea's proved-wrong line, but no project file defines it (a search for 'restart' across /mnt/project-files finds only unrelated roadmap text). A pass or fail should not hinge on it.

Label Stage A and Stage B as screens, fix the marks before running, and keep them out of the sealed R1-R4 marks. Any repair the result suggests must be learned and deploy-autonomous (rule 10), not a hand fix. Rules 1, 3 and 5 are not broken: no parameters, no training, and dev is not on the protected list (GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind).

critiques.rescue:
Keep the idea as a no-training, CPU diagnostic, but re-aim it at the T1 checkpoints that now exist, and make the decisive arm the write-side pointer audit. Preconditions: confirm T1_s200 and T1_s201 load under models/tool.py with cfg default (n_loops 8); keep B2_s200 and B2_s201 (b2ckpt, sha256-checked) as reference only.

Arm 1 (decisive, replaces the z probe): replay the write_copy oracle (tool.py:449-482) on T1_s200 and T1_s201 with a copied loop. For each cell j of each call, record (a) the copy-attention argmax over the context, (b) whether it lands on the gold character of the newest visible entry, (c) the gate from gen_copy, and (d) whether the decoded cell is right. Split by digit count 1-9 and by place. Read the outcomes as: attention wrong = key or read-back break; attention right with a low gate = writer gate or vocabulary break; attention right with a high gate but the cell wrong = place-row or query break. Pass marks, fixed now (suggested): attention on the gold character at least 99% for 1-5 digit results on both seeds. Read-back is shown broken if it is below 97% at any digit count from 4 up.

Arm 4 (thinker state, secondary): probe all 17 control and register vectors per round, not only ln_z(Z[:,0]), to test whether digits are stored at all.

Sequencing: run Arm 1 before Amendment 3's span-copy build, so the chosen fix does not rest on an untested read path. Stage A probes the wrong model. It probes B2's reader, but B2 never saw a tape entry in training. T1's reader (models/tool.py read_texts, lines 84-108) is trained through the thinker and copy path on entries. A B2 result is a zero-shot number that does not predict T1's reader. The decisive reader check is now on the T1 checkpoints, which are CPU-cheap (reader forward only).

The probe labels do not separate what the copy uses. The writer's copy keys are the reader's per-character output (tool.py gen_copy line 239-249, k_cp(X)), and the cell query is W_k(z) + place row j (tool.py cells, lines 110-113). So a cell matches any character with place j in any context entry or prompt number. The D0-style per-place probe (diag_d0.py: 9-char window ending at a number, digit or none) does not label result versus operand digits in the same entry. A passing place probe can coexist with the writer copying an operand digit. Labels must include segment (result or operand, entry index).

The thinker-state probe does not test the link that is used. Copies are pointer reads from reader outputs, and the vocabulary path (gen_copy p_vocab from ln_t(R)) is the only route where state digit identity matters. The idea's pass and proved-wrong mapping (state probe below 99 with reader passing means read-back repairs are funded) does not follow: a state failure does not show that a read-back repair would fix copies, and copies can pass with an unreadable state. Dual labels are needed: oracle digits versus true-value digits on write_copy rows.

A cheaper decisive test exists and is missing: classify the failing write_copy operands and answers from the existing eval (tool.py lines 449-482; analyze_t1.py facts). Each wrong written string is either (a) the intact true result, which would mean the vocabulary path writes a remembered or in-state value rather than copying, (b) a string already in the context (wrong pointer), or (c) a digit-level mix. The T1 table gives 1-3 digit operand copy at 85-93%, which is most of training (about 99% of training results are 1-3 digits). The sealed span-copy story (untrained place rows at 4+) does not explain these short-length misses. Gate values (tool.py discards gate at run() line 166-167) should be recorded alongside.

The sealed re-screen marks in /mnt/project-files/architecture/MARKS-D0-T1-2026-10-07.md (Amendment 3) are internally inconsistent for the 1-3 digit cells. R1 requires write_copy at each length 1-9 to be at least 99 on both seeds. R3 only requires no length 1-3 cell to drop below its current value. The proved-wrong line covers only lengths 4-9 (below 90). So with span copy alone, the 1-3 cells sit in the between band (not shown) and R1 cannot pass without a fix that addresses 1-3 digits. The idea should say this before anyone spends the re-screen.

The joint-swap eval (question plus entries read together) tests a design nobody has chosen (B3). T1 is trained on apart reads, so a joint-swap drop is expected from the input shift and says nothing about apart reads. The pass mark (chain-5 within 0.5, pooled-5 within 1.0) is also below the noise of a non-retrained eval on 1,000 chain rows and 6,040 pooled rows. Drop it from this idea.

The ±4 window analysis cuts both ways. reader.py (CharReader, two k=5 ConvBlocks) gives an exact ±4 receptive field, and the place code counts from the right of each word token (word_spans regex at data.py line 149). Results of up to about 6-7 digits have their digits within 3 characters of either the '=' or the entry end, so local cues can separate them from operand digits. So key ambiguity alone does not explain the 4 to 5 digit failures. It is a candidate for 8 to 9 digit results only, not a general explanation.

Stage B requires a copied per-round loop. run() asserts rounds=False (tool.py line 124). B2's snapshot (ledger.py lines 340-341, 355-356) saves Z[:,1] and registers, not Z[:,0], which is the control token T1's writer reads (tool.py line 163). A copied loop must save Z[:,0] per round. Entry k is written at loop index t=k+1 and visible from t=k+2 (tool.py lines 184-194), which matches the idea's indexing.

The probe design lacks a control and a calibrated threshold. A linear probe with 99.0 as the pass line has no selectivity check. The D0 control (digits-only reader, lowest pooled place 74.2%) shows the method is not automatically at 100%. Hewitt and Liang (arXiv 1909.03368, checked here via WebSearch) propose control tasks with random labels and selectivity, meaning linguistic accuracy minus control accuracy. Each probe needs a random-init or shuffled-label control on the same features.

Arithmetic checks are correct. 481 rows = 208 + 7x39 and 495 rows = 208 + 7x41 (+69,888 and +73,472 params at d=256). 495 rows gives 8,985 over the band top from T1's 3,277,393. The joint probe on B2 is capped to one entry with a 169-character question (169 + 1 + 38 = 208), which is disclosed in the idea.
critiques.rescue: Re-aim the idea at the T1 checkpoints and the sealed write_copy link, and make it a zero-training gate before any further re-screen. (1) CPU, T1_s200 and T1_s201: classify every failing write_copy operand and answer string as true-value, context-string (report which entry or prompt number and place), or digit-mix, with gate values recorded. Pass if at least 80% of 1-3 digit misses are context-string or digit-mix. Proved wrong if most 1-3 digit misses equal the true value (that means a vocabulary-path shortcut, and span copy will not fix R1). (2) CPU, reader only: a linear probe on T1 reader output for random-digit entries, labelled per place and by segment (result or operand, with entry index), with a random-init reader control. Pass at 99 or above on both seeds for result digits at places 1-9. Proved wrong below 97 on result digits (reader loses entry digits). (3) Only if (1) and (2) pass, the thinker-state probe with dual labels (oracle digits and true digits, on the same write_copy rows) to see which the state carries. Drop joint-swap. Record the 1-3 digit cell problem in Amendment 3 before the span-copy re-screen.
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior: D0 (/mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md), which probed B2's reader output on question numbers only (linear probe, 9 chars ending at a number, six seeds, 99.997-100 pass; pooled span mean loses digits). Also the T1 write_copy eval already measures the apart read plus copy path with random digits (tool.py 449-482; T1-SCREEN-RESULT S3). Not tried: probing T1's reader on entries, a segment-labelled probe, the thinker-state probe on T1, and an error classifier on the existing write_copy outputs.
critiques.expected_effect: Zero score effect (diagnostic only, 0 params). Expected information: moderate. Two outcomes are likely: the reader probe on T1 passes (suggested, because D0 passed for B2 and T1 trained on entries), which confirms the writer is the failing link; and the classifier shows a large share of 1-3 digit misses are the true value or a digit mix, which would make the sealed span-copy fix insufficient for R1. Cost is CPU minutes on the mounted T1 checkpoints. Ben's rule 6 favours this. Estimated probability that the rescued version changes the next build decision: about 0.5 (suggested, not measured).

problems: Wrong seeds for the matched probe (shown): the idea probes B2_s100/s101, mounted at /mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/. The T1 screen runs seeds 200 and 201 (queue_local/40-pc-t1-screen.txt lines 7-8). B2_s200 and B2_s201 checkpoint.pt files (13,243,510 bytes each, with sha256 files) are in scratchpad/code/b2ckpt. Use 200 and 201. Their state dicts include g_cp, k_cp and k_wc, so the copy=True load is consistent (shown; the cfg was not decoded because torch is absent).

B2 is not a proxy for T1's reader (shown from code). models/tool.py:1-13 says T1 starts from B2's shared weights at the same seed. Nothing in tool.py or ledger.py freezes the reader (grep for requires_grad and freeze finds none), so T1's reader is trained by T1's loss. B2's reader never saw tape-entry strings; read_texts (tool.py:84-99) exists only in T1. A B2 probe on entries therefore measures an unseen input.

The Stage A kill ('A-own below 97.0 at any place') would stop T1 on the strength of a reader that never saw entries. T1 trains that reader on entries, so the kill is not a valid test of T1 (reasoned from the previous point). Stage A's pass is not a test of T1 either.

Stage A probably passes by construction (shown and suggested). D0 already measured the same reader's digit windows at 99.997-100 on six seeds (/mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md table). diag_d0.py:51-76 puts each digit in a fixed window slot (win[p-1] = char at place p), so a linear probe reads identity from the slot. The new information is only the apart/joint difference and the entry format.

Stage B's thinker digit probe targets the wrong quantity (shown from code, reasoned). The cell writer's query is W_k(ln_z(Z[:,0])) plus place row j, and digits are copied by pointer over reader outputs (tool.py:110-117, 164-167). The thinker state must say which entry and which place to copy, not hold digits. A probe below 99 would not show that read-back failed, yet the proved-wrong branch would fund a repair. Probe the gold source-entry index, or the pointer mass on the gold source character, instead.

The 7th entry is never seen by the thinker at 8 loops (shown). Calls are written at t=1..7 (tool.py:162-171). Entry k (0-based) is written at round k+1 and first read at round k+2 (tool.py:184-193). The last entry is written in the final round, so only the talker reads it (tool.py:194-198; mode and word heads read Z directly, tool.py:195-196). Stage B can probe entries 0-5 only. The 'entry k at round k+2' rule needs this restriction.

The joint-swap eval is underspecified and confounded. (a) Shown arithmetic: a question plus seven entries needs 481 to 495 positions (the idea's own numbers), but MAX_PROMPT is 208 (data.py:11, reader.py:72). The 169-character cap fits only one entry. The idea gives no rule for overflowing rows, and no prompt-length distribution is in the snapshot (LIMIT-COUNTS-2026-10-07.json has none). (b) If the joint string goes through tokenize, prompt-number slots (progparse.py:14-18, N_NUM=16) and WORD candidates (tool.py:217, W_MAX=64) pick up the entries' digits and words, so the test changes slot extraction, not only reading. (c) Where tape_emb[k] goes in a joint layout is not defined.

The joint-swap is out of distribution by design (shown: tool.py:84-108 trains entries read apart). A drop is the expected result and shows only that T1 is not layout-invariant. The proved-wrong text claims it shows the apart read loses digits, which it cannot show. Label it a B3 diagnostic with no T1 gate, or train a joint arm.

Arm C (offset only) has no mark. The arms list includes 'C offset only', but the pass and proved-wrong lines name only A, B and the joint-swap. Offset through the absolute position table (reader.py:72) is the likeliest cause of any B loss, so C is the arm that attributes it. Add marks: C minus A within 1.0 on each seed; B minus C within 1.0.

No inconclusive band (shown numbers in the idea). Stage A fails only below 97.0 and passes at 99.0, so 97 to 99 gives no verdict. The joint-swap passes at minus 0.5 and fails at minus 2.0 on chain-5, and nothing is said between them. Write explicit inconclusive ranges.

Power and chance (suggested, by arithmetic). Place 9 may have only a few hundred calc-true strings; the count is untested because the probe set is not built. At 99.0 with n=300, one error is 0.33 points. For B-own minus A-own within 1.0 with n about 500 per place, the SE of a difference of two independent 99% accuracies is about 0.6 points, so a no-change truth fails about 5% of the time. For chain-5 with 1,000 rows at about 99.6, the minus 0.5 line is about 5 extra errors, a false-fail rate of a few percent. Report n per place with Wilson intervals, and stratify by result length 1 to 9 as diag_d0.py does (copies, lines 21-37).

The perturbation claim is false as worded (shown from reader.py:17-23 and data.py:149). Place index runs from the right end of each word token, and '-' is its own token. Inserting or deleting one character re-indexes every character of that token, so states can change more than 4 positions away (up to 8 for a 9-digit token). The +-4 bound (reader.py:5-6, two k=5 blocks) holds only for same-class substitutions. Restrict the test to those, or state the token rule. The incremental re-read is exact only because the junction is a space.

Signed results are never tested (shown). rand_digits (tool.py:60-62) returns only non-negative strings for write_copy. INT_RE (tool.py:40) accepts '-', and calc returns str(v) (tool.py:53), so sub can write negative results. The idea's probe also limits operands to non-negative. Add signed strings to the probe and to write_copy, or the T1 screen cannot show sign-copy failure.

Existing T1 evals already test read-back end to end (shown). Call accuracy, teacher-forced vs free run: tool.py:356-381. Opswap, which changes answers only if the model reads entry values: tool.py:413-447. write_copy: tool.py:449-482. Tool-off: tool.py:390-399. Run these first. Stage B should keep only the source-index probe, not the digit probe.

Factual slip. The idea says the apart read differs from Ben's transcript picture by a 4-character junction. T1 has no junction, because each entry is read alone (tool.py:84-99). A junction exists only in the joint arm.

The incremental re-read (8 characters before, 4 after) is hand logic between question and answer if it runs at deploy time (rule 1). Allow it only as a bit-exact cache checked against a full re-read. The 1e-4 tolerance is not exact.

The joint-swap kill names a 'restart-position rung' that is not in the mounted ladder documents (grep for 'restart' in /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding and /mnt/project-files/architecture finds nothing; shown). Name the rung or drop the clause.

Cost and gating. Stage A is CPU-only, about 10 to 30 minutes per seed on the M1 by arithmetic (diag_eg.py:127-141 probe, 1,500 steps, batch 8,192; feature matrix about 55 MB for 6,000 by 9 by 256 in float32). Stage B is forward-only, under about 30 minutes on the 5070 Ti. Per-round states are about 140 KB per row, and 3.3M params fits in 16 GB easily. The 1-hour figure is the B2 training run and does not apply here. Stage B waits on queue 40, which runs after queue 39 (queue file line 1; queue 39 is the 274M EGE confirm), so the real wait is the queue.
The 169-character cap applies to eval inputs, not training targets, so it is not a rule-7 breach. It does bias the probe toward short questions, so disclose the excluded share.
Stage A reads the hand place code (reader.py:13-23), which P1 is meant to delete (shown in the ladder plan). Re-run Stage A after P1, or its result does not carry over (suggested).
critiques.rescue: Keep one new test and rewrite the rest. (1) Stage A, CPU, on B2_s200 and B2_s201 (matched seeds). Arms: A = entry alone, as read_texts does; C = entry alone with positions shifted by len(question)+1; B = question + ' ' + entry at true positions, with the question cap and excluded share reported. Probes: D0's window and own-char readings, split by operand pair (not by string), stratified by result length 1 to 9, with n and Wilson intervals per place. Marks fixed now: C minus A within 1.0 and B minus C within 1.0 on both seeds; A own-char at or above 99.0 reported but not a kill; an explicit inconclusive band. Kill only if B minus A is at or below minus 2.0 with at least 300 per place on both seeds, and say it kills only the joint layout, not T1. (2) Stage B after queue 40, with no digit probe: teacher-forced pointer mass on the gold source characters and a source-entry index probe on ln_z(Z[:,0]) for entries 0 to 5 only. Report these next to the existing call accuracy, opswap and write_copy numbers. (3) Joint-swap becomes a labelled B3 diagnostic with a question-only slot rule, tape_emb[k] on entry k, excluded rows reported, and no T1 gate. (4) Add signed strings to write_copy and to the probe. (5) Fix the perturbation claim to same-class substitutions, and re-run Stage A after P1.
critiques.already_tried: diag_d0.py:51-121 and /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md (window digit probe on question numbers, six seeds, pass on all). On T1 itself, models/tool.py:356-482 (extra_evals: call accuracy, tool-off, opswap, write_copy) already tests read-back end to end once queue 40 runs.
critiques.expected_effect: Corrected Stage A: most likely a pass on own-char and window readings. The informative outputs are the C-vs-A offset attribution and the B-vs-C junction reading, both on B2's reader as an unseen-input proxy, so they bound nothing about T1 except the joint-layout question. Corrected Stage B: the source-index probe should be high if the cross-attention and pointer work, and it duplicates what opswap and write_copy already report. The joint-swap most likely drops, which tells B3 whether joint training is needed; it does not show that the apart read loses digits. Cost: about 0.5 hours of CPU for Stage A; under 0.5 GPU hours for Stage B after queue 40; both fit in 16 GB by a wide margin. Every claim above is labelled: shown (file and line checked), suggested (arithmetic or reasoning), or untested (dev length distribution and place-9 counts are not in the snapshot).

chair.reasons:
PLAN, but only as a rewritten, re-aimed CPU diagnostic. The original design (Stage A on B2, thinker-state digit probe, joint-swap eval) is cut. The rewrite costs zero GPU and answers a question the sealed Amendment 3 leaves open.

Checked in the files (read-only; torch is not installed, so nothing was run):
- Shown (architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md): T1 HAS run. S1 pooled-5 is +1.72/-0.31 (pass) and S2 chain-5 is 99.7/99.9 (pass). S3 write_copy FAILS. Operand copy by digit count 1,2,3,4,5,6-9 is 86/93/85/14/1/0 percent. Answer copy is 96/98/98/59/1/0. The idea's 'after q40', 'T1 has not run' and 'closest prior: none' are stale.
- Shown: T1 checkpoints are mounted at /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/40b-t1-s200/T1_s200/checkpoint.pt and 40b-t1-s201/T1_s201/checkpoint.pt. Whether they load under models/tool.py is untested.
- Shown (tool.py docstring lines 1-30): T1's reader shares only its INIT with B2, then is trained through T1's loss, with tape entries read as separate strings from position 0. B2's reader never saw an entry, so a B2 probe on entries is an unseen-input number. It cannot pass or kill T1, and B2 is not a proxy any more.
- Shown (tool.py 110-113, 160-167; ledger.py 239-249): the writer's copy is a softmax over reader output on prompt plus visible entries. The cell query is W_k(z) + place row j. gen_copy returns the gate but run() discards it, and the attention vector is not returned at all, so a probe must recompute it from q_cp and k_cp. The thinker-state digit probe (ln_z(Z[:,0])) therefore probes the wrong object: the state has to say which entry and place to point at, not hold digits. Its proved-wrong branch would fund a repair the copy path does not use.
- Shown (tool.py 449-482): write_copy only COUNTS hits per length. It stores no wrong strings, no gate and no attention, so the misses cannot be classified from the existing outputs. A replay with recording is needed.
- Shown (MARKS Amendment 3): R1 needs write_copy >= 99% at EVERY length 1-9, on operand and answer. But 1-3 digit operand copy is only 85-93% today, and 1-3 digits are the trained lengths (99% of training results). The place-rows-untrained story explains 4+ digits only. Nothing in the sealed plan says how span copy lifts 1-3 digits from about 85-93 to 99. This is the real open question, and the audit speaks to it directly. (Suggested, untested: R1 may land in the 'in between' band.)
- Shown (tool.py 249-262): operand cells use W_k(z)+place row j, while the answer uses the 9 registers (init from place rows 0-8). Same pointer-generator, different query, and operand copy is worse than answer copy at 1-3 digits. That contrast is a free clue.
- Shown: the 'restart-position' rung is defined in no file in no-hardcoding/ or architecture/ (grep found nothing). Drop it.
- Shown (reader.py 17-23, data.py _WORD): the place code counts from the right end of each word token, so inserting or deleting a digit re-indexes the whole token. The 'no state changes beyond 4 positions' check is false for insertions and for numbers of 6+ digits. '-' is its own token (the \w/[^\w\s] split), and S3's random strings are unsigned, so sign copy is untested everywhere.
- Shown (arithmetic, per critics): a joint question plus entries needs 481 to 495 position rows and the table has 208, so the joint-swap cannot run without a model change. It tests B3's layout, which nobody has chosen, and T1 was trained apart. A drop would be expected and uninformative. Cut it.

Rule check: no training, 0 params, dev prompts only, CPU. The probe is developer-side measurement, which rules 1 and 10 allow. It ships nothing. Any repair it motivates must be learned and deploy-autonomous. Amendment 3 explicitly allows read-only diagnostics in parallel, and says they do not gate the span-copy fix.

Value (suggested): about 1-2 hours to write, under 1 hour of CPU per seed. It can change the next decision (about 0.3 to 0.5): whether the sealed span-copy re-screen can reach R1 at 1-3 digits, and which single follow-up to name in advance if R1 lands 'in between'. It cannot change the sealed R1-R4 marks. Untested: that T1 checkpoints load, and that the dev files on Ben's machines reproduce the S3 table.
chair.plan_guidance:
1. Aim it at the T1 checkpoints, which exist now (/mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/40b-t1-s200 and s201). Do not make B2_s100/s101 the gate. B2 never read a tape entry. B2_s200/s201 (scratchpad b2ckpt) are a report-only unseen-input reference.
2. Gate everything on a replay that reproduces the S3 per-length table within 2.0 points at every cell with n >= 100. Without it the harness is not trusted. The oracle strings are seeded per row id and round, so the replay is exact.
3. Record what write_copy discards: the wrong strings, the intact calc result, the gate, and the attention argmax. gen_copy returns only (p, gate), and run() throws the gate away, so the attention must be recomputed from q_cp and k_cp. A copied loop is needed because run() asserts rounds=False.
4. The decisive output is a per-length table with one row per link (reader, pointer, gate, cell). The first link below its pre-set mark is the cause. Report n and Wilson intervals. A cell with n < 100 on a seed is 'not read'.
5. Pay most attention to lengths 1-3. Amendment 3's R1 demands >= 99% there, but operand copy is 85-93% today and the 'place rows untrained' story does not cover it. Use the operand-versus-answer contrast (cell query versus register query) as the clue.
6. Use the D0 window metric as the reader mark, not the own-character probe (which is probably trivially decodable; suggested). Label segments (result digit versus operand digit in the same entry). Add a random-init control. Add signed results as a report-only stratum, since S3's random strings are unsigned.
7. Keep it outside the sealed marks. It is a 2-seed screen. It must not loosen R1-R4 or the proved-wrong line, and it runs in parallel with the span-copy build as Amendment 3 allows. It does not replace the planned diagnostic fine-tune on 4-9 digit rows (that stays a read-only parallel job on the GPU side). This audit is the zero-training half.
8. Run where the dev files are (Ben's PC or Mac). They are not in the snapshot. Say 'untested' about the checkpoints loading until someone has run it. Do not run it on the rented 5090s, because it needs none.
9. Plain-language summary for Ben: the calculator part passed, but the model fails to copy long numbers back correctly. This test looks inside the finished model to see whether it reads the number wrong, points at the wrong digit, or picks the wrong source, before we spend GPU time fixing the wrong thing. It also checks why even 1-3 digit copies are only 85-93 percent right.
10. Any repair this motivates must be learned and deploy-autonomous (rule 10). The attention mass and entropy logging is the only link to the 'model checks its own try' idea, and it stays report-only.

plan.title: tool-D3r link audit: where T1's exact copy fails by digit count
plan.ben_line: We look inside the finished calculator model at how it copies a calculator answer back into its writing, to find which step breaks for numbers with four or more digits. It uses no training and changes nothing, so we learn where the problem is before we spend compute on a fix.
plan.question: At which link does T1's exact copy of a calculator result fail at each digit length 1 to 9? Links as the code allows them: (1) the pointer, meaning the reader's keys plus the writer's query, which decide where it looks; (2) the gate, copy versus vocabulary; (3) the stop, the end-of-number token, which only the vocabulary path can write (shown: no EOS token is in the copy context, data.py:116, tool.py:89); (4) the cell or register decode; (5) for answers only, the mode head. The panel's four links fold (1) and (2) together in the code, and leave out (3) and (5).
plan.one_change: No model, data, loss or mark change. One new read-only measurement: a copied thinker loop that logs, for every copy event in the existing write_copy replay on the two T1 checkpoints, the copy mass on the gold character, the top-attended position and entry, the gate, and the raw argmax token of each cell or register. Shown: run() discards the gate (tool.py:166, p, _ = self.gen_copy(...)), and run() asserts rounds=False (tool.py:124), so a copied loop is needed.
arms: Arm 0a (loop check): the copied loop must return the same calls, answers and gen_copy outputs as Tool.run (tool.py:120-199) on 200 dev rows, exactly.

Arm 0 (harness replay): rerun the sealed write_copy replay (tool.py:449-482) on CPU fp32, same oracle (random.Random(row id + '|' + round), tool.py:452-453), same rows. Shown: in_dist dev has 1,360 rows (LIMIT-COUNTS-2026-10-07.json, /dev_in_dist/counts, a mounted file not checked as B2's dev file), so the 3,000-row cap (tool.py:454) never binds. Compare with the recorded T1 numbers (G0).

Arm 0b (label collisions): count events whose base-run operand or answer text equals a constant (1, 2, 10, 100; progparse.py:8) or a prompt number. Shown: sources() (tool.py:311-321, the text match at line 318) labels a text match to an earlier result first, so a correctly copied literal is scored as a miss. These events are class E and are reported beside the shares.

Arm 1 (classifier, by the first wrong cell of each event; units first, registers in order for answers): A remembered value (written string equals the intact calc result); B wrong source (another context string: another entry's result, a prompt number, a constant, or another entry's operand, sub-typed); C1 stop (right digits, wrong end point); C2 digit error at the right length; D other (including a WORD answer); E label artefact (Arm 0b). Shares exclude E; E is reported next to them.

Arm 2 (per cell below the event length, and per answer register below the answer length): the raw argmax token id (decode stops at EOS and silently drops other specials, data.py:60-69, so the decoded string hides them); copy mass on the gold identity summed over positions (ledger.py:248, scatter_add_ over raw ids); the argmax position, its entry and place; the gate g (vocabulary share), which reads only the query state h and not the context (ledger.py:239-249, shown); and the vocabulary probability of the gold character. Pointer identity hit: the argmax copy mass has the gold identity. Position hit reported too, since repeated digits make several positions correct. Wrong-source events are sub-typed as wrong entry at the right place, wrong place in the same entry, or wrong identity. Note: the sealed 'place rows untrained' reading (T1-SCREEN-RESULT, Reading) is suggested only. Shown: B2's reader reads places 1-9 at 99.997% (D0-RESULT, lowest place), and the same reader place rows are the cell queries (tool.py:112), which is what P-D tests.

Arm 2b (only if an answer cell has n below 100): replay the in_dist program rows with the oracle forced to each length (1-8 for answers, 1-9 for operands), same seeding. Reported as its own table; never gated. Shown: answer length 9 is excluded (tool.py:474-476) because GEN_MAX is 8 (ledger.py:63).

Arm 3 (report only): the D0 window probe (diag_d0.py:40-76) on read_texts(entry) strings 'op a b = r' with random-digit results, with a random-init reader of the same shape and B2_s200's reader beside it. Shown: copy writes raw context ids (ledger.py:248; tool.py:166 passes the ids), so reader identity reaches the copy only through the keys. This probe cannot clear or convict the reader link alone.

Arm 4 (report only): per-cell maximum copy mass and copy-attention entropy, and the AUROC of each for a wrong cell (suggested). Any later 'did my copy work' signal must be learned and run inside the model (untested).
Arm 5 (report only): signed results. Shown: the oracle draws are unsigned (tool.py:60-62). Negative results can be measured only in the intact run, as base-run copies of an earlier negative result.
plan.seeds: Two: T1_s200 and T1_s201, mounted at /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/40b-t1-s200/T1_s200/checkpoint.pt and .../40b-t1-s201/T1_s201/checkpoint.pt. Shown this read: each parts archive matches its .tgz.sha256 sidecar (46135f3c... for s200, 8f30ab93... for s201), and each mounted checkpoint.pt matches the checkpoint inside its archive (sha256 84e86bc2... for s200, 2a7f59e1... for s201). Loading under models/tool.py with default cfg (n_loops 8) is untested here (torch is absent). B2_s200 and B2_s201 (scratchpad b2ckpt, sha256 files present) are a report-only reference. This is a two-seed diagnosis, labelled a screen, with no design claim (rule 4).
plan.machine: BensPC on CPU (the dev data and torch are there; no GPU needed). The M1 Pro Mac on CPU works if the dev file is copied there. No rented GPU (rule 6).
pass_marks: G0a (copied loop, first): returns the same calls, answers and gen_copy outputs as Tool.run on 200 dev rows, exactly. Fail: stop, the logger is wrong.

G0 (harness; must hold before any class is read): the replay's event count n per cell equals the T1 result JSON's counts if that JSON is available (results/40-vast-t1 is not mounted, so this step may be blocked). Hit rates match the recorded T1 numbers within 2.0 points at every cell with n >= 100. Shown targets, T1-SCREEN-RESULT: seed 200 pooled operand 29.3, answer 42.1; seed 200 per length operand 86, 93, 85, 14, 1, 0 for lengths 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6-9; answer 96, 98, 98, 59, 1, 0; seed 201 pooled operand 30.9, answer 42.4 (per-length seed 201 not in the mounted file). Fail: the harness is wrong; no class is read.

G1 (label collisions, Arm 0b; threshold suggested): class E is 15% or more of the 1-3 digit misses on either seed. Then the sealed S3 1-3 digit figures are not a clean copy measure. Report both the all-events and the E-excluded rates, and declare the relabelling as a metric change before any re-screen is read (rule 4).

P-A (reader keys; report only): T1 window probe at places 1-9 and digit count at or above 99.0 on both seeds, with the random-init control beside it. Proved wrong: below 97.0 at any place on either seed (reader identity lost). If the control also reaches 99.0, the probe is non-selective and P-A says nothing about the reader.

P-B (4-8 digits, first wrong cell, class E excluded from the denominator): classes B and C2 together are at least 80% of misses on both seeds. Proved wrong: class A is at least 50% of 4-8 digit misses on either seed.

P-C (1-3 digits, same split): if class A is at least 50% of 1-3 digit misses on either seed, the sealed R1 at 1-3 digits is not a pointer problem, and the named follow-up (gate, or random-digit teaching data) is chosen before the re-screen is read. If classes B and C2 are at least 80%, the pointer explains 1-3 digits.

P-D (pointer by identity, cells below the event length only): identity hit below 90% at cells j >= 3 for 4-8 digit events, while at least 97% at j <= 2 on the same events, on both seeds. Proved wrong: identity hit at least 97% at j >= 3 while exact copy stays below 90%; then the break is the gate or the stop.

P-E (stop; not one of the panel's four links): the end token written at cell L with no digit after it, at least 95% for lengths 4-8 on both seeds (threshold suggested). Proved wrong: below 90% at any of lengths 4-8 with n >= 100 on either seed.

Verdict rule: per length and seed, the first failing link in the order pointer, gate, stop, decode, mode names the cause. Cells with n below 100 are reported as 'not read'. Class D above 15% of misses means the classifier is unfinished: report it, do not give a verdict.
plan.proved_wrong: The audit's premise, that one named link explains the 4-8 digit misses, is proved wrong if no mark among P-B to P-E fails on either seed and class D stays at or below 15%. The misses are then unexplained by these links, and no fix may be chosen from this audit. Separately, if G1 finds class E at least half of the 1-3 digit misses on either seed, the sealed S3 1-3 digit figures are a labelling artefact and cannot be read as evidence about copying.
plan.null_risk: The marks are the weakest part of this plan. P-A is near-certain to pass with or without training: the residual keeps each character's identity, and D0 gave B2 99.997% on a probe of this type (shown), so P-A is weak evidence and cannot clear the reader link. The class marks can pass with no real effect if class D absorbs the misses (capped at 15%) or class E is large (G1 guards this). P-D can pass on a handful of easy events if n is small, which is why the n >= 100 rule applies. Answer cells at lengths 4-8 may stay 'not read' on the in-distribution dev set alone: 1,360 rows over 9 oracle lengths gives at most about 150 answer events per cell (suggested arithmetic, not counted). Operand cells probably clear 100 at most lengths (suggested). The most informative output is the logged per-cell numbers (copy mass on the gold identity versus the gate and the vocabulary probability), which the table should show even when no mark fails.

fixed_plan.ben_line: The calculator model copies a calculator answer well for short numbers and badly for four or more digits. Before we pick a fix, we check that our scoring does not count correct copies as wrong, and we test whether the same failure happens when the digits come from the question. No new training is needed, and it runs on a normal computer.
fixed_plan.question: Is T1's copy failure at four or more digits a real limit of its writer, or partly a scoring error; and does the same failure happen when same-length digits are copied from the question instead of from a calculator result?
fixed_plan.one_change: No model, data, loss or mark change. Two metric changes, declared before any number is read: operand sources come from the gold program's slots instead of text matching, and the copy internals are read by wrapping gen_copy so that run() stays unchanged.
arms: Arm 0 (hook check): run() unchanged, with gen_copy wrapped to record the gate and the copy attention. On 200 big-dev program rows, calls and answers must match Tool.run exactly (fp32, same machine). Fail: stop.
Arm 0b (precision): the same 200 rows in fp32 and in CPU bf16 autocast; report the share of rows whose calls or answers differ. This sets G0's tolerance; it is not a model check.

Arm 2 (length control): synthetic prompts in which each prompt number is replaced by a random 1-9 digit number (the diag_d0.py substitution pattern); score operand copy from the prompt by length with the same writer. Also report the selection error (the copy argmax lands in the right number at all), since selection may differ between question and tape. Split rows by id: set any reading on one half, judge on the other.
Arm 3 (per-cell readout, report only): for tape copies, the gate, the copy-argmax identity and position, the entry index, and the EOS probability at the true length, per cell and per length.
Arm 4 (signed oracle, counted): the same copy scoring with random signed results, so minus signs are copied; the sealed S3 draws are unsigned (tool.py 60-62).

M2 (tape vs prompt, per seed): tape copy below 90% at 4-9 digits AND prompt copy at least 99% at 4-9 digits on both seeds = tape-specific. Prompt copy below 90% at 4-9 digits on either seed = general writer limit.

idea.title: Pair the zero-round leak line to B2 on each seed
idea.summary: The sealed T1 and B3 leak line (zero-round in_dist <=5 on every seed) is failed by B2 itself on seeds 201 (10.81) and 203 (5.66), so a perfect T1 could fail the confirm. Re-seal it before q40 runs as a paired line (T1 minus B2 on the same seed) and report the hits by answer type instead of counting them all as computation. This keeps the line honest without choosing families after the fact.

Add per-row loops:0 predictions to the saved outputs (PREDS.json holds intact predictions only), and print hits split into copy-type, binary-label, computed, and count families. 0 params; evaluation only.
idea.why: The orchestrator brief and the original proposal said computed families stay at 0-1.7 percent on every seed, but the fact check refutes that: on the 16 computed-answer families seed 203 has 43 of 640 hits (word_filter 22/40 = 55 percent, letter_ops 12/40 = 30 percent) and seed 204 has 13. The 13-family subset (9 of 520 on s203) excludes word_filter and letter_ops after seeing the results, which is moving the goalposts. Seed 201's 147 hits are 145 outside computed families (copy_word 35/40, prop_eval 30/40). The line should compare T1 with B2, which has the same leak mechanism, not with a fixed number B2 cannot meet.

idea.title: Two-layer B3 audit: bytecode scan and answer provenance
idea.summary: B3 mark 8 as written (patch re, int and str, loop in tools/) is fooled both ways on this code. Replace it with a bytecode scan plus call allow-list that is proved on 12 planted cheats, and a behavioural check that correct answers only contain digits from the question or the tool's replies. Both run on CPU.
idea.change: New test file (for example custom_io/tests/test_b3_audit.py), hand-written test code. Layer A: dis scan of every code object on the generate path (flag LOAD_GLOBAL of int, float, str, ord, chr, eval, type, getattr, re; LOAD_ATTR of split, strip, join, encode, decode, format, finditer, fullmatch, match, search, sub; FORMAT_VALUE and BUILD_STRING). Layer B: sys.setprofile with a runtime allow-list by file path (tools/ allowed; models/ functions allowed only if on the learned list). Layer C (untested on the real import): per-module builtins shadow. Red team: 12 planted cheats in a copy of tool.py (aliased int, f-string entry, compiled-pattern call, getattr(str,'split'), type(0)('3'), a hidden float on the answer path, others); each must be flagged. Behavioural check: for each correct dev answer with a digit run of >=3, the run must appear in the question or a transcript entry; compare T1 intact, T1 tool-off and B2 as control.
idea.why: Shown in memory on Python 3.13: sys.setprofile c_call events fired for str.split, Pattern.finditer, Pattern.fullmatch, Match.group, str.encode but not for int('3') or str(4); patching the module-level re.finditer caught 0 calls to the compiled NUM_RE.finditer; a bytecode scan did show LOAD_GLOBAL int for an aliased i = int. T1's generate path does call NUM_RE.finditer and int (ledger.py 206-207), INT_RE.fullmatch and int in calc (tool.py 45, 49), an f-string entry (57), vocab.encode (89), decode and reversal (117, 213), and word_spans (217). So mark 8 would pass the compiled-pattern calls and never see int. The provenance check is the behavioural second opinion, and B2 (whose answers are slot values printed with str, never in text) is the positive control that shows the check can see hidden arithmetic.

evidence.claim: Profiler test on Python 3.13.16: c_call events for str.split, Pattern.finditer, Pattern.fullmatch, Match.group, str.encode; none for int('3') or str(4); a module-level re.finditer patch was called 0 times by compiled NUM_RE.finditer.

problems: Rule 1 and rule 10 gap (shown): PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:167 exempts all of tools/ from the audit. INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md:82 puts the 16-call and 48-byte caps (E5) in tools/, and :83 puts the fixed 8-round loop (E6) there too. The INVENTORY itself says E6 is not allowed under Ben's rule 10. The audit certifies rule 1 only; it cannot certify rule 10, which the idea's rules_check implies it does.

Pass marks not fixed in advance (rule 4): 'all 12 planted cheats' names six and then says 'others'. 'Clean T1 flagged at exactly the expected sites' uses a site list the idea says is 'to be confirmed by the audit', so the mark would be set from the output.

Shown escape routes (python3 -I profile run in this read): (0).__class__('3') and (3).__add__(4) emit no c_call events under sys.setprofile. dis shows their call sites as LOAD_ATTR '__class__' and LOAD_ATTR '__add__', which are not on the idea's Layer A attribute list (split, strip, join, encode, decode, format, finditer, fullmatch, match, search, sub). Both escape Layers A and B as specified.

Shown: the Layer A name list misses aliases. A function calling i(x) after a module-level i = int compiles to LOAD_GLOBAL 'i' (dis run), not LOAD_GLOBAL 'int'. The alias is visible only in module-level code, which is not on the generate path, so the aliased-int evidence does not support Layer A as written. Layer C (per-module builtins shadow) is untested and does not cover attribute access.

Layer B design gap (suggested; torch is not installed here): C builtins called from models/ frames, such as torch tensor ops, emit c_call events, so a file-path rule would flag nearly every tensor op unless torch is exempted by module. The idea's 'models/ functions allowed only if on the learned list' names a list that is never defined. The tool's executor progparse.ex (tool.py:52; defined at models/progparse.py:21) lives in models/, so a models/-not-allowed rule conflicts with the tool itself. The rule has to be by caller frame.

Provenance check covers too little (shown by code; coverage untested): it tests only correct answers with a digit run of 3 or more. Word answers and answers of 1 to 2 digits are not tested. LIMIT-COUNTS-2026-10-07.json shows two-digit answers in the program-bearing examples (53, 57, 77, 45), so coverage may be small. Dev files are not mounted. At about 1,000 rows, 0.1 percent allows at most one novel run, so the mark is effectively zero-tolerance.

Provenance measures the wrong thing for rule 1: a learned in-model calculation also produces novel digits and would fail the mark, while hand copying (regex spans at ledger.py:206, place index at reader.py:17-23) passes because copied digits appear in the question. It measures arithmetic outside the transcript, not hand code. The idea should say so and keep the static layers as the rule 1 gate.

chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test in revised form. Cost: 0 GPU, 0 params, a few hours of author time (the 0.8 h is CPU run time only). It breaks no rule and it guards rules 1 and 10 at B3, where mark 8 as written (PLAN-AND-MARKS line 167) would give false assurance. All four critics said revise (score 6) and agree on the defects.

Confirmed defects (first two re-checked in this session on Python 3.13.16; the rest reproduced by 2-3 critics or read in code):
1. sys.setprofile cannot see int(), str(), type(0)(x) or (0).__class__(x), and it floods with torch frames (shown, three critics). Use it only as a diagnostic, never a gate.
2. On 3.13 a single-hole f-string compiles to FORMAT_SIMPLE (and a multi-part one adds BUILD_STRING). FORMAT_VALUE does not exist in 3.13, so the idea's f-string check cannot fire. (0).__class__ compiles to LOAD_ATTR __class__, not on the attribute list (shown here).
3. Layer A is a deny-list. It misses BINARY_OP on Python ints, '%d' % n, .item() and .tolist(), max/min/sum/abs, builtins.int and module-level aliases like I = int (the idea's aliased-int evidence holds only for a function-local alias). It must become an allow-list that fails closed.
4. 'Mark 8 never sees int' is overstated: a builtins.int patch does catch name-level int(). It misses aliases, type-object calls, and methods of str and compiled patterns (NUM_RE.finditer at ledger.py:206, _WORD.finditer at data.py:149-154).
5. Layers A and B disagree about tools/, so 'clean model flagged at 0 sites after the ladder' is unreachable: calc, the f-string entry, input encode and output decode all remain.
6. A directory exemption for tools/ would pass a hand router, hand caps and a fixed 8-round loop moved into tools/ (INVENTORY E5 and E6 put caps and the loop there). The audit can give rule 1 evidence only, not rule 10.
7. The digit-run provenance check is weak. It is laundered by a hidden result written as an operand ('add X 0 = X'; Tool.sources() at tool.py ~319 labels any integer literal as a value). It scores only correct answers with digit runs of 3 or more, so 1-2 digit hidden arithmetic and all non-numeric families are invisible. At about 1,000 rows 0.1 percent is zero tolerance. It also measures arithmetic outside the transcript, not hand code.
8. Pass marks are circular: 'exactly the expected sites' uses a hand-derived list that the idea says is 'to be confirmed by the audit'. The 12 cheats are only partly named and are written by the scan's own author.
9. Controls and dependencies: the B2 control is B2_s100 but the T1 runs are seeds 200 and 201 (use B2_s200/s201 from code/b2ckpt). No T1 checkpoint exists yet (q40 not run) and no tools/ directory exists. B2's own str() on the answer path is ledger.py:399, not 389-390 (INVENTORY A13 repeats the error). The int in spans() is ledger.py:208. PLAN line 167 says the only input tensor is byte ids, not 'tensors only'.

What survives: the static scan needs no torch and no checkpoint, and mark 8 does need replacing. Two stronger behavioural arms already exist in tool.py (write_copy counterfactual at 449-482, noexec tool-off at 390-399). Moderate value, very low cost, not urgent ahead of the T1 result: it matters at B3 and at each rung that deletes a hand part, because the scan output is the delete list for N1, P1 and O1.
chair.revised_idea:
Replace B3 mark 8 with a two-part audit (hand-written test code, 0 params, CPU only). It gives evidence for rule 1 only, and the test file must say so. Neither part sees tensor-level or learned hidden computation, torch internals, or rule 10 (stop schedule and caps).

PART 1, static, runs now with no torch and no checkpoint (compile() and dis over source files).
(a) One scan rule for whole files: models/, tools/, data.py, base.py, reader.py, progparse.py. 'Generate path' is defined by the whole-file scan, cross-checked against a recorded 200-row generate trace.
(b) An allow-list of builtins, global names, opcodes and attributes that fails closed. Use Python 3.13 opcode names (FORMAT_SIMPLE, FORMAT_WITH_SPEC, CONVERT_VALUE, BUILD_STRING). Flag BINARY_OP on non-tensor values (including %), every LOAD_ATTR starting with '__', and .item, .tolist, .float, partition, split, join, encode, decode and similar.
(c) An alias check on module globals: an AST scan of module-level assignments plus an identity comparison on the real import. Flag any module global that is a builtin, a type or a re callable and not on the allow-list.
(d) No exemption of tools/ by path. Pin sanctioned sites by function name and source hash (calc, the entry formatter, the call-grammar parser), plus one named I/O module (encode in, decode out). Every other flagged site must be deleted by the ladder.

(g) Red team: at least 16 named cheats in a copy of the code, with expected flags (cheat to rule) written first and the file hash committed before the scanner is final. Cheats: (0).__class__('3'); (3).__add__(4); module-level I = int called in a function; builtins.int; getattr(str,'split'); type(0)('3'); a single-hole f-string; a multi-part f-string; '%d' % n; compiled Pattern.finditer; str.join; a hidden float on the answer path; a + b on .item() values; max() or min() selecting a question number; a cheat inside tools/ in a non-allow-listed function; a cheat in a helper imported by calc. A second person writes at least 4, and that set is scored separately.
(h) The clean-code site list is generated by the scanner, frozen, each site labelled allowed or must-delete with the rule that flags it, and reviewed by someone other than the author. (iv) Keep the digit-run share only as a secondary detector, run on B2_s200 and B2_s201 (paired seeds, not B2_s100). It validates the detector for slot-printed answers only.
(v) Positive control: a copy of the real T1 checkpoint patched so the answer comes from hidden Python arithmetic that bypasses the tape. Arms (i) and (ii) must flag it.

plan.title: Two-part no-hardcoding audit (replaces B3 mark 8)
plan.ben_line: Before we say the model does its own math, we check two things: that no hand-written number or word trick of ours is secretly doing the work, and that the model's answer really changes when the calculator's reply changes. Passing these checks is good evidence, not proof.
plan.question: Can a fixed, pre-registered two-part audit (a scan of the answer-path code plus counterfactual checks on the T1 runs) catch planted hand-written number code and a hidden answer path, while passing a clean T1, so that B3 can cite it as evidence for rule 1?
plan.one_change: Replace PLAN-AND-MARKS mark 8 (line 167: patch re, int and str to raise outside tools/ on 200 rows) with this audit, sealed as Amendment 3 to MARKS-D0-T1 before any B3 run. No T1 screen or confirm mark changes.
arms: A. Static scan of whole files models/tool.py, ledger.py, base.py, reader.py, progparse.py and data.py, using AST and compile() only (no torch). Run on clean T1 (current tree) and on clean B2 as the control (expected flag includes ledger.py:399).

B. Answer-path reach: a name-based static call graph from generate, run, talk, read, tokenize, gen_copy, read_texts and decode_cells. Training-only and lesion-only sites are labelled in a frozen list and not scored as deploy sites.

C. Planted cheats: at least 16 in a committed file, expected flags written first. The author writes about 12 from the design doc; a second author writes 4 or more from the same design doc, before the scanner is coded.

D. Frozen site list for clean T1 and B2. Every line is labelled allowed (pinned function by name and source hash, or the character I/O codec) or must-delete, with the rule that flags it. A reviewer other than the author labels it.

E. Dynamic superset check (needs torch; random init is enough, no checkpoint): builtins shadows installed before import for int, str, float, type, chr, ord and eval; logging proxies for the module-level compiled patterns NUM_RE, INT_RE and _WORD; sys.setprofile for C method calls; 200 generate rows.
F. Tool-off (B1): extra.noexec.program_families and n from the queue-40 RESULT.json for T1_s200 and T1_s201. Read only, no new run.

G. Stale answers (B2): computed in the per-row run of arm H. Stale = share of injected rows whose answer still equals the original gold. The sealed write_copy answer_copy from RESULT.json is reported beside it.

H. Provenance (B3): a new per-row CPU run over dev call rows from the T1 checkpoints, giving calls, answers and injected results. Operand and answer provenance on correct call rows. The gold base rate is measured first, on gold program rows.
I. Positive control: T1_s200 with a wrapper that answers each program row from the prompt numbers using the gold program solver and ignores the tape. It must fail F and G.
J. B2 digit share on B2_s200 and B2_s201 (runs of 3 or more digits in correct answers that appear in neither the prompt nor the transcript). Report only.
plan.seeds: Static arms A to D: no seeds (one code tree). Behavioural arms F to J: the sealed T1 screen seeds 200 and 201; arm J also reads B2 seeds 200 and 201. When the audit backs a B3 claim it is re-read on seeds 200 to 205 (rule 4), and every seed must pass.
plan.machine: CPU only, no GPU. Arms A to D run on any Python with no torch, in minutes. Arms E, H and I need torch on Ben's M1 Pro or the PC CPU; H and I need the T1_s200 and T1_s201 checkpoints copied from BensPC after queue 40 finishes. F reads RESULT.json only. J uses the B2 checkpoints in scratchpad code/b2ckpt.
pass_marks: S1 (A, C): every planted cheat (at least 16) is flagged by at least one rule, with zero misses. A miss means fixing the scanner and re-running. The cheat file is never edited to pass.

S2 (A, C, second author): zero misses on at least 4 second-author cheats. A miss means fixing the scanner and scoring a fresh set of 4. Zero misses in 4 leaves a 95% upper bound on the true miss rate of about 53% (shown, arithmetic), so S2 is a sanity check, not coverage.
S3 (D): the site list is frozen by file hash, every line is labelled, and the reviewer is not the author. Both directions count: no unlabelled site, and no frozen site that stops being flagged.

S4 (E, needs torch): zero str, regex, int, float or type-constructor call sites on the answer path in the 200-row trace that the static scan did not flag. The profiler alone is not enough: shown in this read, sys.setprofile sees str.split and Pattern.finditer but not int() or str().

S5 (A, D): the clean T1 scan must flag tool.py 45, 49, 53, 57, 89, 117, 181, 213 and 217; ledger.py 206 and 208; data.py 64 and 154; base.py 10 and 11; reader.py 17 to 23 (through word_spans). The clean B2 scan must flag ledger.py 399. Any miss fails S5. Line numbers shown by grep in this read.

R10 (separate, not part of S1 to S5): explicit fail lines, each with its value, for the fixed round loop (tool.py 152, for t in range(n)), n_loops=8 (tool.py 68), the call cap N_RES=7 (progparse.py 8), the answer register GEN_MAX=8 (ledger.py 63), and N_NUM=16 and W_MAX=64 (progparse.py 8). They fail until H1 and the caps change. They do not change the rule-1 verdict but block any B3 ship.

F (B1, tool-off): noexec program_families at or below 2.0% on both seeds passes. Above 5.0% on either seed is a hidden-path fail. Between 2.0 and 5.0 is not passed and is reported, not called hidden-path. Reference: B2 is 0.24 to 0.82% on n = 2,085 per seed (shown, results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json). The all-families figure (n = 2,800) is report only, because B2 is already 5.39 to 7.11% on it. The sealed confirm line (under 5 on every seed, analyze_t1.py docstring) is unchanged; B1 is a separate audit line.

G (B2, stale answers): stale = 100 minus the injected-answer copy rate. Pass at or below 1.0% stale on both seeds; fail above 5.0% on either. Not judged if fewer than 100 denominator rows on a seed, or if path_changed exceeds 10% of call rows. Denominator: correct intact answers equal to a call result, at most 8 characters, with the injected string different from the original (collisions excluded and counted; about 1.1% of one-digit results collide, shown arithmetic from rand_digits in tool.py). This is the sealed write-copy line (at least 99.0) with two added exclusions, so it adds no new threshold.

H (B3, provenance): on correct call rows, operand provenance = operands that are not a prompt number (all prompt numbers, not progparse's first 16), a CONSTS value (1, 2, 10 or 100), or an earlier result. Answer provenance = correct numeric answers that match none of those. Pass when each share is at or below the gold base rate plus 1.0 point on both seeds; fail above base plus 5.0 points on either seed. The base rate is measured on gold program rows (the same population) before any T1 provenance is read, and written into the amendment. If the base rate is above 5%, H is not judged and the fix goes to the trace builder. Not judged below 100 correct call rows per seed.

I (positive control): the wrapper must fail F (noexec above 5%) and G (stale above 5%). If it passes either, the behavioural arms are blind to a wrapper-type hidden path and the audit cannot back rule 1, whatever F to H say. H is expected to pass the wrapper, since its answers match intact call results; this is reported, not gated.
J (B2 digit share): report only. No pass line until B2's share is measured on all six B2 seeds and a margin is sealed by amendment.
Verdict (evidence for rule 1, not a certificate): PASS only if S1 to S5 pass (S4 counts only after arm E runs), F, G and H pass on both seeds, and I is flagged. R10 is reported beside the verdict.
plan.proved_wrong: (1) Any planted cheat still unflagged after one fix round: the scanner is unfit as mark 8. (2) Clean T1 misses a named site in S5, or the second-author set misses after the fix (that set can then no longer be used to judge the scanner). (3) The positive control passes F or G: the behavioural arms are blind to a wrapper-type hidden path. (4) Clean T1 fails F or G on either seed for a legitimate reason (for example, a selection answer that is correct without the calculator, or a coincidence). That is a false alarm: the threshold goes back to a re-seal before any further reading.
plan.null_risk: Yes, the marks could pass with no real change, in these ways. (a) S1 and S3 are judged partly by the scanner's author; cheats and labels can be written to match what the scanner sees. The second author and the reviewer reduce this but do not remove it. (b) A clean sweep of 16 author-written cheats is not coverage: even if they were a random sample, 0 misses in 16 would leave a true miss rate of up to about 17% (shown, arithmetic), and they are not random. (c) The scanner sees named constructs only. Python int arithmetic written with plain operators, hand-built tables, torch-level or learned arithmetic, and repo helpers with innocent names are caught only if they are reached and named (suggested; untested). (d) F reads only the noexec set (n = 2,085 per seed: program rows whose answer slots are all result slots). A hidden path confined to other families is not measured. (e) G counts only correct intact answers that equal a call result and are at most 8 characters, and drops path-changed rows. An answer that matches no call result is outside G, and only H's answer provenance sees it. (f) H depends on the base rate and the membership set; a set that is too wide (all prompt numbers plus the constants) lets a hidden path that writes prompt numbers pass. (g) Two seeds are a screen. A pass means only that no hidden path is visible in these arms.
plan.autonomy: Nothing in this audit runs in the deployed model. It is an offline test of what the deployed answer path may contain. Under rule 1, the only hand code allowed there is the pinned tool functions (calc, entry and the call-text parser) and the character I/O codec. Units-first reversal slices (tool.py 117, 213, 252, 267; ledger.py 390, 447) and the regex number and word spans (ledger.py 206 to 208; reader.py 17 to 23; data.py 149 to 154) are not I/O and must be deleted by N1, P1 and O1. Under rule 10 the audit certifies nothing: the fixed round loop, the call cap and the 8-character answer register stay as explicit fail lines (R10) until H1 and the caps change. The harness loop that reads the op head's output and appends the result is a hand tool boundary. Rule 1 treats it as the tool, but Ben should sign that reading explicitly, because the model's op head, not the loop, chooses when to call. No village-model or creative-track claim is used.

Build the answer-path reach (arm B) from a name-based call graph starting at generate and the talk path. Label training-only and lesion-only functions and lines by hand in a frozen list. With torch on the Mac or PC (arm E), install the shadows before import, wrap the module-level compiled patterns after import (module globals are looked up at call time), run 200 generate rows with random init, and check S4. The inverse-op rewrite (progparse.py 42 to 51, 111 to 114) reads the answer to choose an operation, but its operands are prompt numbers or earlier values, so the base rate should be near zero (suggested; to be measured).

Run arm H on T1_s200 and T1_s201 dev call rows on CPU, giving per-row calls, answers and injected results. Compute the stale rate (G) on the same run and count collisions.
Build arm I's wrapper on T1_s200 (answers each program row from the prompt numbers with the gold program solver, ignores the tape). Run F and G and confirm they flag it.
Run arm J on B2_s200 and B2_s201 for the digit-share report only.

fixed_plan.proved_wrong: (1) any must-delete site reachable from generate at B3 (M1); (2) either positive control passes the arms it must fail, so the behavioural arms are blind; (3) a hand max() over prompt numbers, or a hand int/str answer path, passes arms C-G and is missed by arm A; (4) the span-copy build fails R1 at any operand length 1-9 or answer length 1-8 on any seed, by the rule Amendment 3 already sealed (then span copy is falsified and the next step is the sealed diagnostic, not a stack of changes); (5) a clean build fails M2 or M5 for a legitimate reason (for example a correct answer without the calculator): that is a false alarm, and the threshold goes back to a sealed re-seal before any further reading.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Yes, these can pass with no real change. (a) Arm A labels come from a reviewer; a reviewer who wrote the code will label it allowed. (b) Name-based reach misses dynamic dispatch (getattr, eval, module attribute lookup) and plain operator arithmetic (a + b) unless a reviewer reads it. (c) Arm C excludes verify_claim and compare_numbers by definition, so a hand max() over prompt numbers is seen only by arm A. (d) Arm G's membership includes all prompt numbers and any correct answer equal to one, so a model that copies a prompt number as its answer passes; the base rate is zero by construction and adds no information. (e) A hidden path confined to under about 2% of program rows and spread across families passes M2; the per-family cap catches only a family-sized path. (f) Two-seed runs are screens, not claims. (g) The partial cheat in arm H is one example, not the realistic hidden path. (h) A stale definition change could move a borderline seed.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Nothing here runs inside the deployed model. It audits what the deployed answer path may contain and how it behaves. Under rule 1 the only allowed hand code is calc, entry and the call-text parser (as tools) and the character codec. The tool loop in tool.py run() (reads the op head, formats the call, appends the result) is a harness boundary that Ben must sign off explicitly, because the op head decides when to call. The must-delete list is the list N1, P1 and O1 remove. Under rule 10 the audit certifies nothing about the fixed 8 rounds, the call cap of 7 (from the longest training program), the 8-character register, N_NUM 16 and W_MAX 64; those stay as R10 fail lines until H1 and the caps change. All thresholds are sealed before the run; none is tuned on dev answers.
