idea.title: Random-token control for EGE: content or wrapper
idea.summary: Run EGE with fixed random vectors per Gemma token id instead of Gemma's states (same tokenizer alignment, LayerNorm and zero-init 198,400-param adapter), plus a boundary-only arm (code from in-piece offset and piece length, no identity) and an optional wrapper-only arm (random table over the 108 letter ids). No 271M forward runs, so each run costs about a B2 run. It splits EGE's +1.59/+2.12 into wrapper, piece identity, segmentation and Gemma content, and decides whether further Gemma spending (q39-style runs, adapter repairs) is worth it. Path keys: CIO = /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io ; PF = /mnt/project-files.
idea.change: CIO/models/eg.py: split the tokenizer load from the AutoModel load (load(), lines 34-49) so the arm holds no 271M weights; new FrozenEG.static_states(prompts, T, mode) reusing align() (lines 51-67) and the char-to-token gather of encode() (lines 90-95), zero past each prompt. RAND table = mu + sigma*z, z ~ N(0,1), shape (len(tokenizer), 768), seed-0 generator; mu/sigma are Gemma per-dimension stats from one forward over 20k train prompts (fall back to N(0,1) only if that pass is unavailable, and report which). BND: code = 8*min(offset,7) + min(piece_len,8) - 1 into a random 64x768 table. WRAP: frozen random 108x64 table by letter id, LayerNorm(64) + zero-init Linear(64,256) = 16,768 trainable. CIO/models/ledger.py read() lines 255-267: new eg_control in {rand, bound, wrap}; ln_eg and eg_proj (lines 184-187) unchanged, so RAND/BND train 3,500,881 params like EGE. 24k steps, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, add --save-preds. Follow-up arms only if RAND lands in the 'identity' band: static per-token mean of Gemma states vs the same vectors permuted across ids (4 more runs).
idea.why: EGE keeps B2's own letter table, so Gemma's term only adds piece-level information, and Gemma's linear letter read is 22.99%, so the gain is not spelling. Its family pattern (order_chain +22.2, table_calc +15.0, list_index +15.0, kin_chain +13.0; seq_cycle -12.2, seq_next -6.2, list_stats -5.3) fits meaning, piece identity or plain extra capacity equally, and per-family seed signs agree on only 18 of 34 families. A random per-id vector keeps boundaries and identity and removes meaning and context, so it is the cheapest cut through those explanations.

Validity: chain-5 >= 99.0 on both seeds. loops:0 and variant are report-only (loops:0 SD 4.35 across seeds; variant 2-seed power about 30% at a true +2). Seal as a PASS-MARKS addendum before any run.

problems: [shown] Build-time steps are fine under rule 10. The idea's steps are: split the tokenizer load from the model load (eg.py:34-49); one stats forward over 20k train prompts; seed-0 random tables; BND caps; 4 to 6 training runs; scoring against sealed marks; the researcher's choice of follow-up arms. None of these runs in the deployed model, and building before shipping is not a deploy-time step. The control does not break rule 10 by itself, and nothing it adds ships.

[shown] Hand tokenizer on the question path. align() (eg.py:51-67) runs for each prompt in every train and test batch, through encode() (eg.py:69-98) and read() (ledger.py:255-267). This is hand code between question and answer, and it is not a tool the model chooses to call. RAND, BND and EGE all need it. The idea's R1 defers this to Ben, so no RAND, BND or EGE design can meet rules 1 and 10 as built. No autonomous replacement is built: U2 has no code (data.py:159 is a scatter/segment docstring, not a boundary scorer), and INPUT-UNITS lists U2 as a spec only.

[suggested, from the arm inputs] The decision tree has no rule-10 exit for three of four outcomes. 'Gemma content or context' means a Gemma-tokenized input (point 2). 'Identity' means a piece-id table keyed by tokenizer ids (point 2). 'Segmentation' means BND, whose boundaries come from the tokenizer (point 2). Only 'wrapper' avoids the tokenizer, and the idea makes that arm optional and width-mismatched (point 5). The addendum should state this before any run.

[shown, in the idea's own text] The stats step contradicts the 'no 271M forward' claim. The idea says 'No 271M forward runs' and 'the arm holds no 271M weights', but mu and sigma come from 'one forward over 20k train prompts', which needs the 271M model loaded once. Today load() loads the tokenizer and the model together (eg.py:34-49). This is acceptable as a build step only if the stats are saved to a named file. The fallback to N(0,1) 'only if that pass is unavailable' lets the machine choose which arm runs, so one choice must be pre-registered.

[shown, computed from ledger.py:174-187 and the idea's shapes] WRAP is not EGE's wrapper. WRAP trains 16,768 params (LN(64) 128 + Linear 64->256 16,640). EGE's adapter is 198,400 (LN(768) 1,536 + Linear 768->256 196,864). WRAP has about 12 times fewer adapter params and a 64-wide input, so it cannot say whether a wrapper at EGE's width carries EGE's gain. It is also the only tokenizer-free arm, and the idea makes it optional. Its letter ids come from B2's hand 108-id vocabulary (INVENTORY A16), so it is rule-10 clean only to the standard B2 already meets, which Ben must rule on. Fix: a frozen random 108 x 768 per-letter table through the identical LN and Linear (198,400 trainable).

[shown, computed] RAND's frozen table is missing from the size line. The Gemma word table is 134,217,728 = 262,144 x 512 (eg.py:5-6), so the vocabulary is about 262,144. RAND's table of len(tokenizer) x 768 is about 201,326,592 frozen values (about 0.8 GB in fp32). The idea says 'train 3,500,881 params like EGE' and leaves this out. It is not shipped, but rule 3 counts borrowed parts, so it should be disclosed.

[untested] Post-LayerNorm RAND vectors may collapse toward one vector. mu carries Gemma's per-dimension mean, and ln_eg then normalises each token's 768-vector. If a few dimensions have large means, RAND is nearly the same for every token. The arm would then score about B2 (g near 0) and be read as 'Gemma content needed' for the wrong reason. The idea's check (3) asks for this but sets no number. Measure before the run, on train prompts only: per-token post-LN spread and mean pairwise cosine for RAND versus EGE, with a fail rule if RAND is much less spread.

[shown: queue_local/39 staged; progress-board data.json updated 5:26 PM ET lists q39 as running, ETA 6-7 PM ET; no seed 202-207 result files in RESULTS-EG2.md] The same-seed EGE reference is not yet available. Seed 200 is cross-box (EGE on box C, base B2V_s200 on box A) and seed 201 is same-box (PASS-MARKS addendum 13, lines 308-325). The '+0.30' margin comes from plain-B2 rented-minus-PC offsets (RESULTS-EG2.md:125: +0.48, +0.12). That is not the offset between two rented boxes, so the margin is the wrong size. The 'mean +1.86' reference comes from seeds 200/201 and cannot feed a same-seed mark.

[untested] The BND caps have no source. min(offset,7) and min(piece_len,8) are not justified in the idea. They must come from train-prompt piece lengths (what the model saw) and be sealed before the run. If they are chosen after dev results, BND is dev-tuned. The offset cap also drops offset information for pieces longer than 8 letters, and the piece-length distribution is not measured here.

[shown] The repo already decided against a shuffle control for EGE. PASS-MARKS addendum 4 (PASS-MARKS.md:178-183) says 'EGE passing -> no shuffle control (the embedding ships inside the model, so its gain counts whatever its source)'. Under rules 1 and 10 the source decides whether a gain can ship, so the idea reverses that rule. The addendum should say so and why.

Its controls are native, LoRA, pooling, and zero or shuffled images. It has no random frozen embedding table. Drop it as precedent, or cite it only as a grafting-protocol reference. Missing capacity-matched wrapper control. WRAP is 16,768 params (LayerNorm(64) plus Linear(64,256)). A RAND gain therefore cannot be split into piece identity versus extra input-path capacity, and the verdict 'identity or wrapper' lumps those together. A wrapper control that matches capacity needs a fixed random 768-d vector per letter id (108 x 768) through the same LayerNorm plus Linear(768,256), 198,400 trainable. Label: shown (arithmetic from the idea and eg.py), suggested (fix).

Queue and timing estimate is unsupported. The idea's 4 hours assumes a solo PC B2 run of about 1 hour. Anisotropy could make the RAND arm uninformative. RAND vectors are mu plus sigma times z, with Gemma per-dimension mu. If Gemma states share a large common direction or a few massive dimensions (suggested by the Massive Activations scout paper, not checked here), LayerNorm over 768 dims can make different tokens nearly identical. A null RAND result would then be an artefact. Check before the run: mean pairwise cosine of the LayerNorm outputs for RAND and for real EGE states on one batch, and the share of per-token variance in the top five dimensions. Label: untested (suggested check).

The BND arm does not test what EGE supplies. EGE gives equality structure only: chars inside one token share a vector, with no explicit offset or length. BND gives explicit offset (capped at 7) and piece length (capped at 8) through a random 64-code table. A BND result therefore tests a different signal from EGE's. A cleaner segmentation arm is a fresh random vector per piece occurrence within a prompt (fixed seed), which keeps equality and drops identity. BND also uses tokenizer-derived piece length, which is hand code on the input path (rule 1), the same concern as EGE; the idea does note R1. Label: suggested (reasoning from the idea's own code description).

Content versus context stays undecomposed on the likely path. RAND is context-free, so RAND below EGE cannot separate Gemma content from Gemma context. The static per-token-mean arm that would split them is gated behind the identity branch, so the 'content or context' verdict is left as one bucket. Put that arm in the first batch or label the verdict as not decomposed. Label: shown (idea text), suggested (fix).

Sign-agreement motivation does not reproduce. Recomputing per-family pooled-5 gains for EGE minus B2V from the four RESULT.json files gives 23 of 34 families with the same sign on both seeds, not 18. Size and memory. The random table is (len(tokenizer), 768), about 262,144 by 768, or roughly 201M floats (about 805 MB fp32). Generate vectors only for ids seen, or hash ids. The arm is a control, not a shipped design, so rule 3 does not apply to it, but RAND minus B2 includes the 198,400 extra trainable params, about +6% over B2. chair.reasons:
PLAN, rewritten, not as submitted. All four critics asked for a revision and found the same flaws. I agree with them, and none of the flaws kills the idea.

Why it is worth a sealed test:
- EGE (+1.59 and +2.12 pooled-5, 2 seeds) is the only positive input result. Nobody knows what causes it (shown: RESULTS-EG2.md, and a grep finds no random-input or same-wrapper arm).
- The cut is cheap. A random-table arm needs no 271M forward, so it costs about one B2-class run. A solo PC B2 run is about 1.5 h median, from train_s of 5,446 / 5,473 / 5,583 / 3,559 s for seeds 202-205 (shown: results/33-pc-confirm-b2). Those runs shared the GPU three ways, so a solo time is untested.
- The answer sends Ben's effort in one of three directions (details in the plan guidance). The cut is also the cheapest check on Ben's question of why Gemma helps.

Flaws I confirmed:
1. Self-contradiction (shown, idea text; eg.py:34-49). The idea says no 271M forward, but takes mu and sigma from a Gemma pass, with a silent N(0,1) fallback. Fix: no stats pass and no fallback.
2. Capacity confound (shown arithmetic). RAND carries EGE's 198,400-param adapter. That is 159,001 above the band top of 3,341,880, so a RAND gain could be extra capacity.
3. Content and context stay merged (shown). RAND has neither. The follow-up arm "T0" is defined nowhere. Fix: add G0 in the first batch.
4. The preferred pairing does not exist yet (shown). EGE_s202/203 have no result files, and the repo has q39 only as a staged file. EGE_s200/201 were paired across rented boxes (addendum 13), so the +1.86 reference is not same-box. Fix: all thresholds are fractions of the same-seed PC EGE gain, sealed as such.
5. The sealed addendum 4 says "EGE passing -> no shuffle control" (shown). EGE has not passed, so the reversal is mild. A new addendum must say the control is diagnostic only and EGE's own verdict is unchanged.
6. Two-seed power is poor. The critics' simulations disagree on details but say the same thing: most outcomes land in "between", and a true +1.0 content effect is found about 25% of the time. So 2 seeds can only triage. The claim needs 6 seeds under the sealed 6-seed rule (mean >= +1.0 and >= 5 of 6 seeds ahead).
7. BND (code from in-piece offset and piece length) is a hand-segmentation diagnostic with no shipping path under rules 1 and 10. Its caps (7 and 8) are unexplained. Drop it from stage 1. Keep it conditional, with caps sealed from train piece lengths.
8. The 18-of-34 sign-agreement figure depends on how the four 0/0 families are counted. Strict nonzero agreement is 18, and 23 if exact ties count (shown, reproduced by two critics). Chance is about 17. Use it only as "family pattern is noise-level, not a story".
9. The Scout 2606.14153 precedent is mis-cited: it swaps encoders and has no random-table control. Drop it.

Findings I added, which the critics only half-saw:
- A random 768-d code pushed through Linear(768,256) can give arbitrary per-id outputs only for about 768 distinct ids (suggested, linear algebra; the distinct-id count is untested). So a null RAND does not rule out piece identity. Report the distinct Gemma id count on train prompts (tokenizer only, seconds). In the plan, G0 and RAND share one wrapper, so G0 minus RAND is a clean one-change step.
- G0 uses the 134,217,728-value word table (262,144 x 512, shown: eg.py:5-6), with no transformer and no forward. If G0 carries the gain, the borrowed part drops from 271M to 134M, and a pruned table is possible (suggested). That matters for rule 3.

Rules:
- Rule 1 and rule 10: the Gemma tokenizer alignment (eg.py:51-67) is hand code on the input path. This is fine for a build-time control, since nothing ships. A Gemma-tokenized input cannot ship until Ben rules that the encoder's own tokenizer counts as part of the allowed pretrained encoder (rule 2), or a learned segmenter replaces it. No such segmenter is built (U2 is spec only).
- Rule 3: the diagnostic is not a size comparison. A claim that Gemma beats the scratch reader needs a plain model of about 274M, and 8a shows B2's lead over plain shrinking from 3M to 10M.
- Rule 7: all arms inherit B2's 528-row 7-step exception (progparse.py:199). So the EGE reference is not rule-compliant for adoption either.

Gate the whole test on q39. If the 6-seed EGE mean gain is below +1.0, or EGE is ahead on fewer than 5 of 6 seeds, there is nothing worth decomposing, and the GPU hours are saved. Whether q39 is running or finished tonight cannot be checked from the files (the repo only has it staged).
chair.revised_idea:
reader-D1 (revised): a build-time ladder that decomposes EGE's gain, one change per step. It is a diagnostic: nothing it adds ships, and no deploy-time step is involved. Never run unless q39's 6-seed EGE result passes the stage-0 gate.

LADDER (every arm is B2 plus a frozen per-token table, through the same wrapper: LayerNorm(width) then zero-init Linear(width,256), added to B2's letter embedding before the window; so step 0 equals B2):
- B2: no table (references: q33 seeds 202-205; q39 seeds 206-207; same PC).
- RAND: fixed N(0,1) vectors, 512 wide, one per Gemma token id, generated once from a seed-0 generator. No Gemma stats and no fallback. The char-to-token alignment is EGE's own align() (same ids, same padding, same T). Trainable 132,352 (1,024 + 131,328). Carries piece identity and piece boundaries only. No meaning, no context.
- G0: the same wrapper, but the vectors are Gemma's own pretrained input word-table rows (512 wide; table read from the weights file, no transformer, no forward). Trainable 132,352, identical to RAND. G0 minus RAND is exactly the pretrained token content.
- EGE: Gemma's contextual final-layer states, 768 wide, trainable 3,500,881 (from q39). EGE minus G0 is context plus the 12 pretrained transformer layers' mixing, plus the 768-vs-512 width step (66,048 more trainable). That width step is a small, named confound.
- Optional, only if RAND is positive: WRAP768, a fixed random 768-d vector per letter id (108 x 768) through the EGE wrapper (198,400 trainable). Label it a reparameterisation of the letter table. It sits at B2 + letter-table duplicate and is expected to be about 0. It is a wrapper-and-capacity sanity check, not a Gemma test.
- Conditional BND (hand segmentation, in-piece offset and piece length): run only if RAND >= 2/3 of EGE, with caps sealed from train-prompt piece-length percentiles before the run. It asks whether segmentation alone carries the gain. Label it a hand-segmentation diagnostic with no adoption path. A shipped version must be learned (U2).

BUILD NOTES (code changes):
- eg.py: split the tokenizer load from the model load (load(), lines 34-49), so RAND holds no 271M weights.
- eg.py: add FrozenEG.static_states(prompts, T, mode in {rand, g0}) reusing align() and the gather at lines 90-95.
- ledger.py read() (255-267): add eg_control in {rand, g0, wrap} with width 512 for RAND and G0 (eg_proj and ln_eg sized to the width).
- Run with --save-preds and keep every checkpoint.pt, since q39 keeps none that are on hand.
- Unit tests, no training: RAND's char-to-token index equals EGE's on 1,000 train prompts; the step-0 loss of RAND equals B2's; no Gemma forward is called.
- Report the count of distinct Gemma ids on train and dev prompts (tokenizer only). If it is above about 768, then RAND cannot fit arbitrary per-id vectors (suggested), so a null RAND does not exclude identity; say that in the verdict.
- Report an anisotropy check on one batch with no training: the mean pairwise cosine and the share of per-token variance in the top 5 dimensions after LayerNorm, for RAND and for real EGE states. Gemma may have a few massive dimensions (untested; scout 2402.17762) that make EGE's input nearly collinear. Fail rule, sealed first: if RAND's spread is more than 3x EGE's on either measure, state it beside the verdict.

STAGES (all on Ben's PC, paired by seed with B2 and EGE on that box; the rented fallback needs new B2V baselines on that box and is Ben's call, since rule 6 says rent only when both local machines are full):
- Stage 0 gate (no new run): q39 6-seed EGE, addendum 15 marks: mean pooled-5 gain >= +1.0 and ahead on >= 5 of 6 seeds. Call the 6-seed mean gain E. If it is not met, stop and record "nothing to decompose".
- Stage 1: RAND and G0 on seeds 202 and 203 (4 runs, about 6 h of PC time, suggested from the 1.5 h median). Report-only reads: cipher_map, loops:0, variant, the five lookup families (order_chain, kin_chain, list_index, table_lookup, table_calc), and the Gemma-id count.
- Stage 2: extend only the arm(s) the 2-seed screen leaves open to seeds 204-207 (6 total). All claims use the sealed 6-seed rule.

PASS MARKS (to seal as a new PASS-MARKS addendum before any run; g = arm minus same-seed PC B2 on pooled-5; chain-5 >= 99.0 on every seed for validity):
- Say in the addendum: diagnostic only; EGE's own addendum-4 verdict is unchanged; this reverses addendum 4's "no shuffle control" clause for EGE only because EGE did not pass.
- Stage 1 triage (2 seeds, direction only):
  - "Identity or wrapper looks like the cause": RAND mean g >= 0.67 E and both seeds >= +0.5. Next: extend RAND to 6 seeds, then WRAP768 and BND.
  - "Not identity": RAND mean g <= 0.33 E and both seeds <= +1.0. Next: read G0.
  - Anything else: extend RAND to 6 seeds. Do not call it.
- Stage 2 and G0 verdicts (6-seed means; need >= 5 of 6 seeds ahead of B2 for any "carries" claim):
  - RAND carries it: 6-seed mean g >= 0.67 E.
  - Token content carries it: G0 mean g >= 0.67 E, and G0 minus RAND >= +1.0 on the 6-seed mean.
  - Context carries it: EGE minus G0 >= +1.0 on the 6-seed mean and G0 mean g <= 0.5 E.
  - Mixed: any other result. State the numbers and stop.
- Proved wrong: "EGE's gain needs Gemma content or context" is wrong if RAND's 6-seed mean g >= 0.67 E. "It is only piece identity or the wrapper" is wrong if RAND's 6-seed mean g <= +0.5 and E minus RAND >= +1.0 with EGE ahead of RAND on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
- Two-seed power is about 25% to find a true +1.0 difference (suggested). No 2-seed result is a verdict.

WHAT EACH OUTCOME DOES (the autonomy exit for each branch):
- RAND (identity/boundaries) carries it: stop spending on Gemma adapter repairs (LayerNorm + gate, middle layer, LP-FT). Build a from-scratch, task-trained piece or letter-group embedding with no tokenizer: U2 learned letter groups, or hashed letter n-gram embeddings (Over-Tokenized Transformer, 2501.16975, suggested). That is rule-10 clean. Note U0 (BPE input, lost -3.1/-5.4) put word pieces in place of letters; here they are added beside letters, so U0's loss does not predict this (suggested).
- G0 (pretrained token content) carries it: Gemma's tokenizer then needs Ben's ruling under rules 1, 2 and 10. The borrowed part is the 134M table, not 271M, and may be prunable (suggested). Run the rule-3 comparison against a plain model of the same total size, which is a separate, larger test.
- Context carries it (EGE >> G0): the full 271M forward is needed at deploy. Rule 3 then needs a plain model of about 274M, untested. B2's lead over plain shrank at 10M (8a first look), so expect this to be hard.
- All arms near 0 except EGE across seeds, or EGE itself fails the gate: the Gemma input line stops at 6 seeds.

Rule 7: every arm, including the q39 EGE reference, inherits B2's 528 answer-only rows (N_RES = 7), so no result in this ladder is rule-compliant for adoption until N_RES is lifted on every arm.

Dropped from the original: the Gemma stats pass and the N(0,1) fallback; the 4-run, 4-hour estimate; the rented-box +1.86 reference and the +0.30 margin; the 2606.14153 precedent; BND in stage 1; the undefined T0.

1. Gate on q39 first. The addendum 15 6-seed marks are: mean pooled-5 gain >= +1.0 and EGE ahead on >= 5 of 6 seeds. If q39 misses, the ladder is not run. Whether q39 is running, finished or still staged cannot be verified from the files. Say so in the plan and let Ben confirm. Addendum 15 makes q39 Ben's call.

Only the table values differ. Name the EGE-versus-G0 step's extra confound (768 vs 512 width, 66,048 more params). Keep WRAP768 optional and labelled a reparameterisation.

   - The post-LayerNorm anisotropy check (RAND vs real EGE states).

6. Label every claim shown, suggested or untested. Examples:
   - Shown: 132,352 and 198,400 trainable counts, 262,144 x 512 table (eg.py:5-6), 22.99% Gemma linear letter read.
   - Suggested: the 768-id capacity cap; the simulated powers.
   - Untested: any RAND or G0 result; whether the Gemma input table loads without the full model on the PC; solo PC run time.

7. Keep the small card experiments (B2) separate from the village model. Do not mix claims.

9. Ask the outside reviewers (Astra, GPT) only if RAND comes back "between" after 6 seeds. Otherwise the ladder is routine.

10. Plain-language summary for Ben, in the plan. Something like: "We keep Gemma's piece boundaries but swap its meaning for random numbers, then for Gemma's raw word vectors, then back to full Gemma. Whichever swap makes the gain vanish tells us what Gemma was giving us."

plan.title: Gemma gain ladder: random codes, then raw word-piece rows
plan.ben_line: We keep the same slot where Gemma's vector goes, but swap what fills it: first a random label for each word piece, then Gemma's own word vectors, then Gemma's full output. The step where the gain disappears shows which part of Gemma was helping. Nothing from this ships; it only tells us what to build next.
plan.question: Once the six-seed EGE gain over same-PC plain B2 (E6, from queue 39) passes its gate, how much of it is carried by (a) which Gemma word piece a letter sits in (random codes, RAND), (b) Gemma's pretrained word-piece vectors (G0 minus RAND), and (c) Gemma's context and depth (EGE minus G0)?
plan.one_change: One slot changes: the per-character vector that EGE adds to B2's letter embedding. Today it is Gemma's contextual 768-d state. The ladder replaces it with a context-free 512-d vector per Gemma word piece: random codes first (RAND), then Gemma's own input word-table rows (G0). The wrapper (LayerNorm(512), then a zero-initialised Linear(512 to 256)), the tokenizer alignment, the letter window, the training recipe, the seeds and the dev splits stay fixed in both arms. A new random vector per character (FRESH) is the size-matched noise control, run only if RAND shows a gain.
arms: B2 (reference, same PC, same flags): seeds 202-205 from queue 33 and 206-207 from queue 39. No change. Shown: queue 33 header says all runs share one device; B2 pooled-5 per seed from RESULT.json final_eval (6,040 rows) is 73.00, 74.27, 74.74, 74.02, 73.63, 74.47 (mean 74.02, SD 0.63). Seeds 202 and 203 train_s 5,446 and 5,473 s.
EGE (reference and gate): queue 39, seeds 202-207, trainable 3,500,881 (shown: ledger.py:184-187 plus arithmetic). Read only; no new run.

RAND: frozen N(0,1) 512-d vector per Gemma token id (torch.Generator seed 0). Wrapper LayerNorm(512) plus zero-init Linear(512,256) = 132,352 trainable (shown arithmetic: 1,024 + 131,328). Total trainable 3,434,833, which is 92,953 above the rule-3 band top 3,341,880 (shown arithmetic). No Gemma transformer forward.

G0: same wrapper; the vectors are the 512-d rows of Gemma's input word table. The table has 134,217,728 values, which is 262,144 x 512 (shown: eg.py:5-6 and arithmetic; the vocabulary size 262,144 is inferred). Read once from the weights file, no forward, 132,352 trainable. The safetensors tensor key is untested, and the weights are not in this container.

FRESH (conditional): a new N(0,1) 512-d vector for each character occurrence, seeded by a stable hash (hashlib, not Python's salted hash) of (prompt, character index). Same wrapper, 132,352 trainable. It carries no identity and no context. Run on seeds 202-207 only if RAND's two-seed mean is at least 0.33 x E6.

Dropped, with reasons: WRAP768 (a fixed random 108 x 768 letter table through LayerNorm and Linear(768,256) can realise any 108 x 256 letter table, so it tests reparameterisation, not Gemma; suggested, from linear algebra). BND (hand segmentation from piece offsets and lengths; a diagnostic with no shippable path). The Gemma stats pass and its N(0,1) fallback (a fixed N(0,1) table needs no Gemma forward).

PRETRAINED TOKEN CONTENT: G0 >= 0.67 x E6 and G0 minus RAND >= +1.0. CONTEXT AND DEPTH: E6 minus G0 >= +1.0 and G0 <= 0.5 x E6, labelled as confounded with the 66,048-parameter width step until a width-matched arm exists. MIXED: anything else; report the numbers and stop.

If G0 row std is near 0.003 or below, LayerNorm's epsilon (1e-5) starts to matter; state it.

plan.proved_wrong: Stop-and-wrong cases, each falsifiable from the numbers above: (a) the stage-0 gate fails, so there is nothing to decompose; (b) 'piece identity alone carries the gain' is wrong if RAND's six-seed mean is <= +0.5; (c) 'pretrained token content matters' is wrong if G0 minus RAND is <= +0.5 on the six-seed mean; (d) 'context and depth matter' is wrong if E6 minus G0 is <= +0.5 on the six-seed mean (width-confounded, so a pass here is not clean); (e) 'input noise carries it' is wrong if FRESH's six-seed mean is <= +0.5. None of these is shown yet: no RAND, G0 or FRESH run exists. A stage-1 LIVE or NOT call is never a result by itself.
plan.null_risk: Could the marks pass with no real change? Noise (suggested; my own stdlib Monte Carlo, 40,000 draws per cell, E assumed 1.5 because the PC value is unknown, per-seed paired SD 0.63 to 0.89, E6 itself noisy): with zero true gain, a two-seed LIVE call fires 1-4% of the time, a six-seed LIVE call 0.1-1.1%, and the stage-0 gate passes falsely 0.01-0.3%. Power: at a true +1.0 the six-seed LIVE call passes about 50%, so a real modest effect often lands in MIXED (a miss, not a false pass); at +1.5 it passes 87-95%. If one arm truly gains +1.0 and the other is at zero, the two-seed stop rule ends the ladder 9-11% of the time. Systematic risks: (1) RAND, G0 and FRESH add 132,352 trainable parameters (+4.0% over B2, and 92,953 above the rule-3 band top; shown arithmetic). FRESH matches RAND's size, so RAND minus FRESH and G0 minus RAND are size-matched. EGE minus G0 is not: the 768-wide wrapper adds 66,048 trainable parameters (2.0% of B2), and EGE minus G0 also includes Gemma's transformer stack and its output projection (layer count untested). A context verdict can therefore be partly a width effect. (2) Rank cap: one shared Linear(512 to 256) can give every token an arbitrary vector only if at most 512 distinct ids occur (arithmetic shown). Above that, RAND is rank-limited, so a RAND null does not exclude identity; the id count is untested. (3) If G0 or EGE rows are nearly collinear after LayerNorm, the arm is close to a constant offset; the sealed cosine check (>= 0.8) catches this (suggested threshold). (4) WRAP768 is dropped: it is a letter-table reparameterisation, not a capacity or Gemma test (suggested, from linear algebra). (5) Every arm and every reference inherits B2's 528 answer-only rows (progparse.py:8 sets N_RES = 7 and progparse.py:199 keeps only shorter programs; shown), so results are relative only, and rule 7 blocks adoption until N_RES is lifted on all arms. (6) The rented EGE screen (+1.59 and +2.12) is not a same-PC value, and seed 200 is cross-box (addendum 13), so only q39's PC E6 sets thresholds.
plan.autonomy: Build-time diagnostic. No step here runs in the deployed model, and nothing it adds ships. But every arm sends the input through two hand steps: the Gemma tokenizer alignment (eg.py:51-67, which token holds each character) and a fixed lookup keyed by that tokenizer's ids. Ben's rules 1 and 10 allow a hand step between question and answer only inside a tool the model chooses to call, so no arm here can ship as built. Successors: if identity carries the gain, the deployed model would learn its own piece or letter-group codes from the task loss (U2 or hashed letter n-grams, with no tokenizer; suggested to be rule-10 clean in principle). If content or context carries the gain, Ben must rule whether Gemma's tokenizer can be a tool the model calls (rules 1, 2 and 10) before anything is built. The random table and FRESH noise are build-time constants with fixed seeds, not runtime steps. Every threshold, mark and stop rule is a fraction of EGE's own gain, sealed before any run, and none is tuned on dev answers.

Use 768-d codes (cap 768) and make the line refutable only if the train count is <= 768; otherwise report only.

[shown in plan text] FRESH is defined two ways: 'a new N(0,1) vector for each character occurrence' and 'seeded by a stable hash of (prompt, character index)'. The second is fixed per prompt across 24,000 steps, so the thinker can memorise a per-prompt key. FRESH would then score low for reasons unrelated to noise, and the IDENTITY line (FRESH <= 0.33 x E6) would pass too easily. Drop FRESH; WRAP768 below replaces it as the content-free control.

[suggested, central] Missing capacity control. EGE adds 198,400 trainable parameters (LayerNorm(768) plus Linear(768 to 256), models/ledger.py lines 184-187). No planned arm gives the same wrapper a non-Gemma input. A fixed random 768-d code per letter (WRAP768, no Gemma forward) is trainable-identical to EGE and is the cheapest test of whether any gain comes from extra trainable input weights or random-feature effects. The plan drops it as 'reparameterisation, not Gemma'; that is the main confound and should be tested first.

[shown arithmetic] Width confound beyond the context line. RAND and G0 are planned at 512-d (132,352 trainable) and compared with E6 at 768-d (198,400). The identity and content lines therefore also change width, so the plan's 'one change' claim fails against EGE; only RAND versus G0 differ in content alone. Put every arm at 768 so only the slot content changes.

[shown, models/eg.py lines 6 and 10] The plan's width-matched G0 ('valid only if Gemma's 512-to-768 projection sits at the input') misreads the code: the 512-to-768 projection is after the transformer, so Gemma's input rows are natively 512-d. A width-matched G0 needs a fixed, non-trainable random 512-to-768 lift on the rows (G0-768).

[shown] Size accounting. G0 borrows the 134,217,728-entry Gemma word table, and rule 2 counts borrowed parts. The plan reports trainable only (3,434,833 for RAND/G0/FRESH). At 768 the whole size of G0 is 137,718,609. ledger.size() (lines 269-275) sets frozen_borrowed = N_TEXT (271,002,624) whenever eg_embed is on, so reusing that flag would misreport G0; a table kept outside parameters() would be silently uncounted. Report the whole size of every arm.

[shown arithmetic] Rule 3. The planned 512-d RAND/G0 are 92,953 above the band top (3,341,880). At 768 they match EGE (3,500,881, 159,001 above the top). All of them are B2-internal diagnostics, not rule-3 results. The plan labels this for EGE but should say the arms share it.

[suggested] Grouping versus identity. RAND and G0 give all letters of one piece the same vector, so they also encode where piece boundaries fall (the letter-groups idea in U2). A gain could come from grouping rather than identity. A boundary-only control (BOUND-768: four fixed random 768-d codes keyed by a letter's role in its piece: single, first, middle, last) needs no identity and no training-time segmentation. Make it optional in stage C; it is the link to U2.

[shown in RESULTS-EG2.md; mechanism untested] Leak as a shortcut. EGE's loops:0 in_dist is 18.09 (seed 200) and 4.49 (seed 201), against plain B2 at 1.40 / 4.34 on the rented box and 0.00 / 10.81 on the PC. Gemma's contextual states may carry answer information past the thinker. The plan reports loops:0 only. A CONTEXT line without the leak clause could credit a shortcut as reasoning.

[shown: results/CONFIRM-ANALYSIS.json arms.B2.diffs.pooled5_vs_tfsteps sd 1.33] Noise model is optimistic. The plan uses paired SD 0.63-0.89, but an architecture change against B2 gave SD 1.33 across six seeds. My stdlib Monte Carlo in this review (E6 noise included, thresholds as planned): null two-seed stage-C LIVE fires 1.3% / 4.2% / 9.0% at SD 0.63 / 0.89 / 1.33; null six-seed LIVE 0.06% / 1.2% / 6.1%; power at a true +1.5 for six-seed LIVE 94% / 87% / 77%. The plan's figures hold only up to SD 0.89. Also, when E6 is near 1.0 the 0.67 x E6 bar is near 0.7, which is within one standard error of zero for a six-seed mean.

[shown] Hours understated. The fixed plan's 'hours: 6' is stage 1 only. With stage 2 (8 runs) and FRESH (6), the ladder is 18 runs: about 27-28 h at the B2_s202-205 pace (3,559-5,583 s each), or about 66-76 h at the B2_s200-201 pace (13,160 and 15,164 s on a shared device). The board's q39 ETA of 6-7 PM ET for 8 runs cannot be checked from the repo (queue_local/39-pc-ege-confirm.txt has no timings); read the PC run log.

[shown: models/progparse.py line 8 N_RES = 7; line 199 keeps programs of at most 7 steps; progress board: 528 rows, lift to 16 next] Rule 7. Every arm, including the q39 reference, trains 528 long rows answer-only. The plan calls results 'relative only' and says rule 7 blocks adoption, but it spends about 28 h on arms that would need rerunning once N_RES is lifted. Ben should rule on N_RES before stage C.

[shown: models/eg.py lines 51-67 align()] Rules 1 and 10. RAND and G0 need the Gemma tokenizer alignment, a hand step between question and answer if shipped. The plan says no arm can ship; that is right. The successor logic should say that identity can be pursued with learned or hashed letter-group codes (no tokenizer), while content or context needs Ben's ruling on whether a tokenizer may be a tool the model calls, before any build.

[suggested] Cheaper test missed. A no-training test-time lesion on the q39 EGE checkpoints (zero the EGE vector; swap in RAND-768 or G0-768 codes) needs only dev inference and shows whether the trained model reads Gemma content at all. The plan lists it as an optional probe at step 2; it should run first, before any new training.

[shown in plan text] Label problem. The CONTEXT line is called 'context and depth', but E6 minus G0 also contains Gemma's transformer stack and its output projection, which G0 does not have. Label it 'Gemma transformer plus context' and never 'context alone'.

[shown in plan text] Seed reuse. Stage 1 uses seeds 202-203, which are also inside E6. The stage-1 call is therefore not independent of the E6 threshold. Acceptable as a direction screen, but say so in the marks.

[shown: PASS-MARKS.md addendum 18 and addendum 20] U0's sealed branch: a from-scratch word-piece side channel is the next gain test only if U0 was 'Ben right' (>= +2.0). U0 was 'letters fine' (<= +1.0). RAND is a piece side channel outside that branch; the plan should say so and give it a low prior. U0's base was plain_tf_steps at the 64-character cap (840 answer-only rows), so the U0 verdict is itself not clean.

fixed_plan.title: Gemma gain, same-width ladder: capacity control first
fixed_plan.ben_line: We first check whether the Gemma gain comes from Gemma at all, or just from giving the model extra trainable input weights. Only if it does not do we test which part of Gemma's word-piece codes carries it. Nothing from this ships; the expensive steps wait for Ben's rulings.
fixed_plan.question: Once the q39 EGE six-seed gain E6 has been read against addendum 15 (or Ben approves a diagnostic on a failed arm in writing), how much of E6 survives (a) a no-Gemma control with the same 768-wide wrapper (WRAP768), then (b) fixed random codes per Gemma piece (RAND-768), then (c) Gemma's context-free input rows lifted to 768 (G0-768)? The context part (E6 minus G0-768) is labelled 'Gemma transformer plus context' and is judged with the leak clause.
fixed_plan.one_change: Only the 768-d vector each character adds to B2's letter embedding changes. EGE uses Gemma's contextual state per character. The arms replace it with: a fixed random 768-d code per letter and no Gemma (WRAP768); a fixed random 768-d code per Gemma piece id (RAND-768); the Gemma input-table row of the piece lifted to 768 by a fixed random map with no trainable parameters (G0-768). Everything else is identical to EGE: LayerNorm(768) plus zero-initialised Linear(768 to 256), 198,400 trainable, the window, the recipe (24,000 updates, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16), seeds, dev splits, and no dev data in construction.
arms: EGE (reference, read only): queue 39 seeds 202-207 on the PC. E6 = mean over seeds of pooled-5 minus plain B2 on the same seed and device.

B2 reference on the PC: seeds 202-205 from queue 33 (train 3,559-5,583 s each, one shared device) and 206-207 from queue 39. Pooled-5 per seed 73.00, 74.27, 74.74, 74.02, 73.63, 74.47 (mean 74.02, SD 0.63), recomputed from final_eval in results/33-pc-confirm-b2.
WRAP768 (control, no Gemma, no Gemma forward): fixed random N(0,1) 768-d code per letter id (108 rows, generator seed 0). Trainable 3,500,881, borrowed 0, whole 3,500,881. Runs first.

RAND-768: fixed random N(0,1) 768-d code per Gemma piece id, over the full seeded table (262,144 ids), generated from seed 0 with no data read. Trainable 3,500,881, borrowed 0, whole 3,500,881. Train-prompt piece count is a stage-A report; if it is above 768, RAND-768 is report-only.

G0-768: Gemma input-table rows (512-d; the 134,217,728-entry table; tensor key to be checked) lifted to 768 by a fixed random orthogonal 512-to-768 map (no trainable parameters). Trainable 3,500,881, borrowed 134,217,728, whole 137,718,609 (rule 2 counts it).

BOUND-768 (optional, stage C, only if the piece count is above 768 and Ben approves): four fixed random 768-d codes keyed only by a letter's role in its piece (single, first, middle, last). Carries grouping, not identity.
Dropped: FRESH (per-prompt key artifact; replaced by WRAP768); RAND-512 and G0-512 (width confound); BND hand segmentation (replaced by BOUND-768); the Gemma statistics pass.
fixed_plan.seeds: Stage A: no training. Stage B: WRAP768 on seeds 202-203. Stage C: RAND-768 and G0-768 on seeds 202-203 (plus BOUND-768 only if triggered). Stage D (after Ben's rulings): WRAP768, RAND-768 and G0-768 on seeds 204-207 (12 runs). References: EGE 202-207 and B2 202-207 from queues 39 and 33.
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's PC RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (cuda), the same device and flags as queues 33 and 39 (pairs must share a device). WRAP768 needs no Gemma load. RAND-768 and G0-768 need the Gemma tokenizer on CPU; G0-768 needs one read of the weights file (PC disk had about 3.5 GB free, undated; check first). No rented GPUs (rule 6).
pass_marks: Gate 0 (addendum 15, all four clauses, unchanged): E6 >= +1.0 with EGE ahead of plain B2 on >= 5 of 6 seeds; no dev split down more than 2.0 on the 6-seed mean; chain-5 >= 99.0 on every seed; 6-seed loops:0 mean <= 4.33 (plain B2 3.33 + 1.0) and donor in_dist <= 5 on every seed. If any clause fails, record it. Ben decides in writing whether a diagnostic on a failed arm runs; the decision comes before any stage B run.
Validity for every arm and seed: chain-5 >= 99.0 (B2 six-seed range 99.4-99.7).

Stage A (no training): distinct Gemma piece ids on TRAIN prompts only (tokenizer offsets as in eg.py align). Dev count reported for information only. If the train count is above 768, RAND-768's identity line is report-only. Test-time lesion on the EGE checkpoints if q39 kept them for seeds 202-203: zero the EGE vector; swap in RAND-768 codes; swap in G0-768 codes. Report pooled-5 drop per seed; no gate.

Stage B, WRAP768 on seeds 202-203, mean g = WRAP768 minus B2 on the same seed. CAPACITY-LIVE if mean g >= 0.67 x E6: stop, the gain is not Gemma-specific. Continue to stage C only if mean g <= 0.33 x E6 and each seed is <= +1.0. Anything else: stop as a no-call.

Stage C, RAND-768 and G0-768 on seeds 202-203 (direction only): LIVE if mean g >= 0.67 x E6 and both seeds >= +0.5; NOT if mean g <= 0.33 x E6 and both seeds <= +1.0; BETWEEN otherwise. Stop if both arms are NOT.

Stage D, six-seed means over 202-207, only after Ben's rulings: CAPACITY: WRAP768 >= 0.67 x E6 (no Gemma content claim). IDENTITY: RAND-768 >= 0.67 x E6 and WRAP768 <= 0.33 x E6, only if the train piece count is <= 768. CONTENT: G0-768 minus RAND-768 >= +1.0, with G0-768 >= 0.67 x E6 and G0-768 loops:0 mean <= B2 mean + 1.0. CONTEXT (Gemma transformer plus context): E6 minus G0-768 >= +1.0, G0-768 <= 0.5 x E6, and EGE loops:0 mean <= B2 mean + 1.0. Lines may overlap; report each with numbers; MIXED otherwise.

Report only, never a verdict: cipher_map, variant, the five lookup families (order_chain, kin_chain, list_index, table_lookup, table_calc), loops:0 and donor in_dist per arm, the train piece count, and the post-LayerNorm mean pairwise cosine on about 2,000 characters for RAND-768 and G0-768 (>= 0.8: that arm reads 'not interpretable').
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Gate 0 failure: nothing to decompose. WRAP768 >= 0.67 x E6 on six seeds: the gain is not Gemma-specific. IDENTITY is wrong only if RAND-768 <= +0.5 on six seeds AND the train piece count is <= 768; otherwise it is untestable. CONTENT is wrong if G0-768 minus RAND-768 <= +0.5 on six seeds. CONTEXT is wrong if E6 minus G0-768 <= +0.5 on six seeds. None of these is shown yet; no RAND-768, G0-768 or WRAP768 run exists.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Computed in this review (stdlib Monte Carlo, not in the repo; E6 noise included; thresholds as above). Paired SD 0.63 / 0.89 / 1.33 (the 1.33 is the repo's own B2 minus plain_tf_steps SD, so the plan's 0.63-0.89 is optimistic). Null false LIVE at two seeds (stage C): 1.3% / 4.2% / 9.0%. Null false CAPACITY-LIVE at six seeds: 0.06% / 1.2% / 6.1%. Power at a true +1.5 for six-seed LIVE: 94% / 87% / 77%. Also, when E6 is near 1.0 the 0.67 x E6 bar is within one standard error of zero. Structural risks: the train piece count is probably above 768 (suggested), which voids the identity falsifier; G0-768 borrows 134M frozen parameters, so a G0 result is a 137.7M-model result, not a B2-size claim; a leak-driven context gain looks like a gain (loops:0 clause guards it); RAND and G0 also encode piece boundaries, so a gain may be grouping (BOUND-768 separates it, optional).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Diagnostic only; nothing here ships. WRAP768 uses only B2's existing letter alphabet. RAND-768 and G0-768 need the Gemma tokenizer alignment (eg.py align, character offsets), a hand step between question and answer that breaks rules 1 and 10 if shipped as built. If CAPACITY wins, nothing Gemma-specific is needed. If IDENTITY wins, the successor is learned or hashed letter-group codes (U2 or letter n-grams) with no tokenizer, tested in its own run. If CONTENT or CONTEXT wins, Ben must rule whether a tokenizer can be a tool the model calls (rules 1, 2, 10) before any build. The seeded tables and thresholds are build-time constants, not values tuned on dev answers.
steps: Gate (no training, about 0.5 h of reading): read q39 results (EGE_s202-207, B2_s206-207; status ok) from the PC run log, not the board's ETA. Compute E6 and E2 and apply Gate 0 exactly as addendum 15 (four clauses), recording each clause. If a clause fails, stop unless Ben approves a diagnostic in writing.

Stage A, CPU (minutes): count distinct Gemma piece ids on train prompts only, using the tokenizer offsets from eg.py align(). Record the dev count separately. Decide whether RAND-768's identity line is testable (count <= 768).

Stage A, GPU (minutes, only if q39 kept checkpoint.pt for seeds 202-203): test-time lesions on the EGE checkpoints: zero the EGE vector; replace it with RAND-768 codes; replace it with G0-768 codes. Report pooled-5 drop per seed. No gate; this shows whether the trained model reads Gemma content.

Seal PASS-MARKS addendum 21 with the marks above before any stage B run. It must cite addendum 15 and state that FRESH was dropped (per-prompt key) and that all arms are at width 768 with no dev data in construction.

Build, no training (models/eg.py and models/ledger.py): eg_control in {wrap768, rand768, g0_768}, each using the EGE wrapper at 768 unchanged. Split load() so G0 reads only the table, with a tensor-key check. RAND and WRAP tables are seeded generators. Fix size() so frozen_borrowed is 0 for WRAP and RAND and 134,217,728 for G0 (not N_TEXT). CPU unit tests: step-0 output equals B2 for each arm; trainable is 3,500,881 for each; no Gemma transformer forward is called for the three; the character-to-code index equals EGE's on 1,000 train prompts.

Stage B on the PC: WRAP768 on seeds 202 and 203 with queue 33 flags (--steps 24000 --batch 256 --lr 1e-3 --bf16 --seed N --log-every 500 --final-eval), checking chain-5 for each. Apply the stage-B rule; stop on CAPACITY-LIVE or a no-call.

Stage C on the PC, if stage B says continue: RAND-768 and G0-768 on seeds 202-203 (4 runs, about 6 h at B2 pace). Add BOUND-768 on 202-203 (2 runs) only if the piece count is above 768 and Ben approves. Apply the stage-C rule; stop if both arms are NOT.

Ben's rulings before any stage D: (a) whether a diagnostic on a failed Gate 0 runs; (b) N_RES (rule 7): lift to 16 for all arms and rerun the B2 and EGE references, or accept the 528 answer-only rows as a labelled limit; (c) whether a tokenizer may be a tool the model calls (rules 1, 2, 10).
Stage D, after the rulings: WRAP768, RAND-768 and G0-768 on seeds 204-207 (12 runs, about 18 h at B2_s202-205 pace). Apply the six-seed rules and report every line with its numbers.

If the read is MIXED, or CONTEXT rests on width or on the leak clause alone, write an outside-review prompt under /home/user/learner/reviews/ for Ben (Astra can read the repo; GPT cannot), including the rule 10 successor question.

Cost: stages A-B about 3.5 h at B2 pace; A-C about 10 h; full A-D about 28 h at B2_s202-205 pace (18 runs x about 5,500 s), or about 66-76 h at the slower B2_s200-201 pace. Stage D is not approved by this plan.

fixed_plan.confirm: Any positive line needs: (1) N_RES lifted and all references rerun (rule 7); (2) a plain model of the same size, within 3%, scored on the same marks (rule 3); for G0-768 (137.7M whole) that is a model of about 135-140M, and for EGE about 275M, not 3.3M; (3) a tokenizer ruling (rules 1, 2, 10) before any shipping claim; (4) the successor (learned letter groups or hashed n-grams) tested in its own run. final.why: Run it, in order: seal the marks and build the arms now (no GPU), do the CPU piece count, and start GPU runs only after the q39 6-seed EGE result is read. EGE (+1.59/+2.12, 2 seeds) is the only positive input result, and nothing shown in the repo says why it works. The arms need no 271M forward, so each costs about one B2-class run, and the answer picks between three paths. Piece codes learned from scratch (U2, hashed letter n-grams) are rule-10 clean. A Gemma tokenizer would need Ben's ruling. Or the Gemma input line stops. Checked in code (shown): eg.py:5-6, 10 and 85 show the 262,144 x 512 word table, the 512-to-768 projection at the output, and the wrapper LayerNorm(768) + Linear(768,256) = 198,400 trainable (ledger.py:184-187). size() sets frozen_borrowed to 271,002,624 for any eg_embed run (ledger.py:269-275), so G0 would be misreported unless that is fixed. The score stays at 6, not higher, because the opening arm is a near-null by construction, a RAND null cannot refute identity if the piece count is above 768 (suggested), 2-seed power is poor (suggested), and every arm inherits B2's 528 answer-only rows. The gain at 3M may also not survive scale (8a shows B2's lead over plain shrinking at 10M).
final.ben_line: We keep Gemma's word-piece boundaries but swap what goes in them (a plain extra letter code, then random numbers, then Gemma's raw word vectors, then full Gemma), and the step where the gain vanishes tells us what Gemma was really giving us.
plan_fixes: WRAP768 is placed as a stage-B gate, and it should not be. A fixed random 108x768 table through LayerNorm and Linear(768,256) is linearly the same as adding a second trainable letter table to B2's own letter table, so it adds no function capacity (suggested, linear algebra: 108 random vectors in 768-d are independent). It is a wrapper and optimiser-dynamics control that should read about 0. Rename it 'wrapper-only control', not 'capacity control'.

The stage-B stop rule fires on noise. A true-null WRAP768 fails 'mean g <= 0.33 E6 and each seed <= +1.0' about 40% of the time at per-seed SD 0.9, and then 'anything else: stop as a no-call' ends the ladder (suggested, normal approximation, untested). Run WRAP768, RAND-768 and G0-768 together on seeds 202-203, with 3 in parallel as q33 did, and make WRAP768 report-only. Define the action for BETWEEN: extend that arm to seeds 204-207.

G0-768 minus RAND-768 is biased toward G0 for a non-semantic reason. With more than 768 distinct ids, a rank-768 map fits low-dimensional structured rows better than full-rank random ones (suggested). Add P0, which is G0 with the table rows permuted across ids. It keeps the spectrum and marginal geometry and removes per-id meaning, and it is the cleaner content control. Make CONTENT require G0 minus P0 >= +1.0, and report G0 minus RAND only as a secondary read. P0 is the permuted-G0 follow-up the original idea named but the fixed plan dropped.

Thresholds as fractions of E6 stop meaning anything when E6 is near 1.0, because 0.33 E6 and 0.67 E6 are then within one standard error of zero. Seal a floor: if E6 < 1.5, stage-C calls are direction-only and no 'carries' line is claimed from 2 seeds. Also seal that seeds 202-203 sit inside E6, so stage C is not independent of the threshold.

The test-time lesion that swaps RAND or G0 codes into trained EGE checkpoints is uninterpretable, because the trained adapter is tuned to Gemma's final-layer contextual states and a different input distribution breaks it whatever the cause. Keep only the zero-the-vector lesion, label it reliance-only, and drop the swap lesions. Also check that q39 kept checkpoint.pt (train.py:201 writes it when --out is set) before promising any lesion.

The identity falsifier depends on an untested piece count. A RAND-768 null cannot refute identity if the train piece count is above 768, which is likely (suggested; 18,496 distinct regex words, 13,084 of them made-up syllable words). Write the sealed text so that only a RAND positive is a result in that case. A null then says only 'rank-limited random codes do not carry it'.

Gate 0 needs Ben's written ruling before sealing. The leak clause (6-seed loops:0 mean <= 4.33) will probably fail, because the screen values were 18.09 and 4.49, and the split-drop clause is noisy on 2 seeds. Decide now whether a pooled-gain-only gate (E6 >= +1.0, ahead on >= 5 of 6 seeds, chain-5 >= 99.0) is enough for a diagnostic. The 'unchanged' wording is wrong if it drops clauses. The addendum must also say it reverses addendum 4's 'no shuffle control' clause for EGE only because EGE did not pass.

Cost is understated if read as one number. Stages A-B are about 3.5 h at the 1.5 h shared-run median (from the 3,559-5,583 s train_s of B2 seeds 202-205). B2_s200/201 took 13,160 and 15,164 s on the same PC, so the range is 3.5-16 h for stage B. The decision-bearing stage C is about 6-10 h more, and the full six-seed ladder is about 28 h or more. Say this in the plan, and put it in the PC queue behind q39, with q40-q44 also waiting and no rented GPUs under rule 6.

Fix size() before any G0 run: frozen_borrowed must be 134,217,728 for G0 and 0 for WRAP768 and RAND-768, not N_TEXT. Hold the G0 table outside parameters() but count it in the whole size (137,718,609). Check the safetensors key for the word table, and the PC free disk (about 3.5 GB, undated), before building.

State the priors openly. U0 (letters-to-word-pieces, -3.1/-5.4) and W1 (+0.9/+0.1, lookup families -4.1) both argue against pure 'word identity or reach' stories. RAND here ADDS piece codes beside letters, so U0 does not predict it, but give RAND a lowish prior (untested). Cite U0's sealed 'letters fine' branch.

Rule notes to keep in the sealed text. Rule 7: every arm and the q39 reference inherit B2's 528 answer-only rows (progparse.py N_RES = 7), so results are relative only and nothing is adoptable until N_RES is lifted on all arms. Rules 1 and 10: the Gemma tokenizer alignment (eg.py:51-67) is a hand step, so no arm ships as built, and the identity branch's successor must be a learned or hashed letter-group code with no tokenizer. Rule 3: this is not a size comparison, and any claim that Gemma beats the scratch reader still needs a plain model of about 137.7M (G0) or about 274M (EGE).

Outside reviewers (Astra, GPT) are warranted only if a six-seed read comes back MIXED. Per CLAUDE.md, such a prompt must ask for shown/suggested/untested labels, keep B2 apart from the village model, ask for one change with fixed pass marks, and include a summary for Ben.

idea.title: Capacity-matched no-window control: R0 plus pointwise MLP
idea.summary: R0 (window removed) lost 6.84/6.26 pooled-5 but also lost exactly 656,896 params (two conv blocks), so neither 'the window is needed' nor Ben's 'the window is test-fitting' has a clean test, and the window size was only ever varied 2 vs 0. Add the same params back as a per-position MLP that mixes no neighbours (C0') and a one-block +-2 version (C1'). If C0' recovers, R0's loss was capacity; if it stays broken, the window supplies local binding that cipher_map needs.

chair.reasons:
PLAN, revised. No rule is broken and every critic's problem has a fix. Rule 10 passes (suggested): this is a build-time control and adds no deploy-time step. The hand word regex and place code are inherited by every arm and must be named. Rule 7 is inherited too. Every B2-derived arm, B2 included, trains the 528 long list_stats rows answer-only (progparse.py:199). Ben should rule on that, but it does not block a paired diagnostic, because no shipped design comes from it.

Value (suggested): R0 is the only evidence that the window matters. It lost 6.84 and 6.26 pooled-5 (shown: RESULTS-EG2.md, results/46-r0ege-s200 and 48-r0-s201). It also lost exactly 656,896 params, 19.9% of B2 (shown: R0 n_params 2,645,585; two ConvBlocks at 328,448 each). The R0 train loss is 0.0906 and 0.1018, against 0.0168 and 0.0238 for B2V on the same box (shown: RESULT.json files). So R0 underfits, but that reading fits both capacity and reach. A control with the params added back is the first clean split. No reader_layers=1 or PointBlock run exists anywhere (shown: grep of results and queue). It also bears on the Gemma area. The window-less Gemma arms (EGR, EGO, EGM, EGW) all lost with fewer trainable params and no capacity match. If capacity explains R0, a capacity-matched window-less Gemma arm becomes a fair test. If it does not, Gemma can only be additive, as in EGE.

Cost (shown): B2-class runs, no Gemma forward. Peak memory is about 2.9 GB allocated on a 5090. This is the cheapest decisive-looking item in the area.

Honest limits. (1) On 2 seeds the ratio f has SD about 0.10 to 0.15 (suggested). A true mid-value lands in 'between' about 80% of the time. So the screen can only choose a 6-seed run (rule 4). It cannot claim that the window is or is not needed. (2) The idea does not test whether the +-4 window is test-fitting. Ben's 'test-fitting' wording appears only in the orchestrator brief; no project file contains it. At most the screen separates +-4 from 0 once capacity is equal. (3) Expect the reach reading (suggested). The cipher prompts bind a letter to its digit across a separator (WHY-GEMMA-LOST line 56), and a per-position MLP cannot do that. But plain_tf and plain_tf_steps, which have no window, read cipher_map 44-112 of 120 on q33 (shown). So binding without a window is possible, and 'reach' here means reader-side reach only. The thinker still cross-attends every position.

Corrections to the idea (shown, from the critics' files):
- R0 ran on box C. The B2V baselines ran on boxes A and B (PASS-MARKS addendum 13). 'B2V exist there' is wrong.
- EGW is 3x wider (d=768), not 7x, and about 6.7x the params. It also set letters_in false, so it cannot be read as 'reach, not capacity'. Drop that sentence.
- The 0.0210/0.0139 comparator is PC B2. Use same-box B2V.

chair.revised_idea:
Capacity-matched no-window control (arms PW0, PW1; replaces reader-D2's C0' and C1').

QUESTION. Of R0's -6.84/-6.26 pooled-5 loss, how much is lost capacity (656,896 params) and how much is lost reader-side reach (the +-4 window)? Reader-side reach means neighbour mixing before the thinker. The thinker still cross-attends every position, and the hand place code stays in every arm.

CHANGE (one, separate arms). New PointBlock in models/reader.py, matched to ConvBlock (pre-LayerNorm, masked residual): x + Linear(h,256)(GELU(Linear(256,h)(LN x))). It mixes no neighbours. Its params are 513h + 768. Add a cfg key pw_hidden, wired at ledger.py:130-131 and 142.
- PW0 = reader_layers 0 + PointBlock h=1279. That is 656,895 params, so total 3,302,480 (B2 minus 1).
- PW1 = reader_layers 1 + PointBlock h=639. That is 328,575 params, so total 3,302,608 (B2 plus 127).
Check both counts by constructing the model before sealing. Both sit inside the band 3,147,208-3,341,880.
PW1 is conditional: run it only if PW0 stays broken. If PW0 recovers, PW1 is moot.
PW1 is NOT a clean reach test. It swaps block type and depth together with reach. A clean reach sweep needs the kernel knob. ConvBlock and CharReader already take k; only Ledger fails to pass it (ledger.py:142). That sweep is a separate follow-up idea, for example two k=3 blocks plus a PointBlock against two k=5 blocks. Do not bundle it.

PAIRING. Everything on one box, same code. The R0 and B2V numbers on file came from different boxes and cannot supply the denominator.
- PC (preferred, rule 6): run R0 s200/201 and PW0 s200/201 on the PC. Same-box B2 is q33 B2_s200/201 (pooled-5 73.00 and 74.27). Total 4 runs, 5 with PW1. The PC queue already holds about 16 to 20 staged runs (queue_local 39-44), so this waits.
- Rented box: B2V, R0 and PW0 for 2 seeds, 6 runs. Needs Ben's OK for spend. The credit figure is unreliable ($5.22 in PLAN-AND-MARKS line 198, $8.84 elsewhere); recheck it.
Add --save-preds so family-level rows can be scored.

MARKS (seal as a PASS-MARKS addendum before any run). G_seed = same-box B2 minus same-box R0 pooled-5, per seed, about 6.5. Judge every line per seed, both seeds.
- Capacity reading: PW0 >= B2 - 0.33G AND cipher_map in_dist >= 36/40.
- Reach reading: PW0 <= R0 + 0.33G AND cipher_map in_dist <= 20/40.
- Mixed cell A (pooled recovers, cipher stays <= 20/40): capacity for relation and lookup families, reach for cipher.
- Mixed cell B (cipher recovers, pooled does not): unexpected; check seed spread and train loss.
- Anything else: not shown; do not add a third seed. Go to the 6-seed run.
Gates and reports:
- Train-loss gate: report PW0 final train loss over same-box B2. Within 2x means it fits; 4x or more means it underfits like R0.
- Report cipher_map pooled over its 3 splits, and the non-cipher families.
- Report f with and without the list_stats rows (rule 7).
Proved wrong: the capacity reading is wrong if PW0 <= R0 + 0.33G with cipher <= 20/40 on both seeds. The reach reading is wrong if PW0 >= B2 - 0.33G with cipher >= 36/40 on both seeds.
PW1 (only if run): B2 minus PW1 >= 1.0 on both seeds means +-4 beat +-2 at equal params (with the block-type confound). Within 1.0 on both seeds means +-2 is enough. Neither screen result settles a window decision without 6 paired seeds on one box.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (suggested): PW0 recovers 0 to 30% of G and cipher in_dist stays <= 20/40. Roughly 40 to 50% of outcomes will be decisive.

LABELS. R0 and param arithmetic: shown. All reach and capacity readings: suggested until 6 seeds. The cipher separator format and any 'pair span' prediction: untested (the generator is not in the scoped code).
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. Naming and sealing. Use PW0 and PW1, not C0'/C1' (sealed arm names clash; rule 9 keeps claims separate). Seal the marks as a PASS-MARKS addendum before any run (rule 4).

2. One box, one code path. Run every compared arm on the same box with the same code. R0 ran on box C and B2V on boxes A and B (shown: addendum 13), so the old R0 and B2V pair cannot give the denominator. Verify that the pw_hidden=0 path reproduces B2 and R0 param counts exactly (3,302,481 and 2,645,585). On the PC, reuse q33 B2 s200/201 (73.00, 74.27) and re-run R0 on the PC. That is 4 runs. Rented: 6 runs, and spend needs Ben's OK.

3. PointBlock must carry LayerNorm. ConvBlock is pre-LN (reader.py:43-51). Without LN, an optimisation difference is confounded with the capacity reading. Params are 513h + 768. h=1279 gives 656,895 (PW0). The one-conv-block variant is h=639 at 328,575 (PW1, +127 over B2). Confirm by building the model and reading n_params.

4. Marks. Do not judge on the ratio f of 2-seed means alone (SD about 0.10 to 0.15). Use the per-seed 2x2 above: pooled-5 versus B2 - 0.33G and R0 + 0.33G, crossed with cipher_map in_dist (40 rows per seed) at >=36/40 and <=20/40. Name a reading for each of the four cells, and say that 'not shown' goes to a 6-seed run. No third seed. R0's cipher_map in_dist is 5/40 and 1/40 and B2 is 40/40 (shown: results/46, 48), so cipher can be bimodal across seeds.

5. Diagnostics. Pre-register a train-loss gate against same-box B2 (about 0.017 and 0.024 on rented, about 0.021 and 0.014 on PC). Report cipher_map separately from the non-cipher families. Of R0's lost rows, cipher_map is 107 and 115 (26% and 30%), and non-cipher frame is 167 and 124 (shown). Report f with and without list_stats (rule 7).

6. PW1 is conditional on PW0 staying broken, and it confounds depth and block type with reach. Say so in the writeup. The clean window-size test, a kernel knob at matched params, is a separate sealed idea. Ledger would pass the existing k argument of CharReader. Do not bundle it. It is the one that speaks to Ben's 'test-fitting' worry.

7. Claims allowed. State plainly that the screen cannot decide whether the window is needed or whether +-4 is test-fitting. 'Reach' means reader-side reach only. The thinker still sees all positions, and the hand place code and absolute position stay. Label Ben's 'test-fitting' objection as orchestrator-reported. A plain no-window transformer can read cipher at 44 to 77 of 120 (shown: q33 plain_tf), so a failure of PW0 does not prove binding is impossible without a window.

8. Rules to state in the plan. Rule 7: the 528 answer-only list_stats rows are inherited by every arm; Ben should rule on it, and the screen is paired so it does not block. Rule 1 and rule 10: no deploy-time step is added; the inherited word regex and place code (INVENTORY A10) must be named. Rule 6: PC first; the PC queue is long, so renting needs Ben's approval.

9. Optional cheap pre-step on the six existing B2 checkpoints (b2ckpt/B2_s200-205, a plan, not run here): a test-time reach-2 lesion that zeroes the outer conv taps. It is shift-confounded, so it only hints at the answer, and it cannot replace PW0. If cipher survives, that supports the +-2-is-enough hint. If it collapses, the result is ambiguous.

10. Link to the Gemma area. If PW0 recovers on pooled-5 (capacity reading), run a capacity-matched window-less Gemma arm next (a separate idea). If PW0 stays broken (reach reading), Gemma helps only as an addition to the window, as in EGE. The q39 6-seed EGE result (not in the files) decides the second half of that.

plan.null_risk: Yes, in two places, and both can be guarded. (1) Inert block: if the PointBlock is not wired in or its output is zeroed, PW0 equals R0 in distribution. My noise simulation (suggested; per-run SD 0.7 on pooled-5, two seeds, no train gate, no box offset; arithmetic only, no file written) gives the reach reading about 100% of the time. The step-3 wiring checks are the guard. (2) Slow learning: a per-character block that trains slowly at lr 1e-3 looks like reach (T_under and dev low). The train split cannot separate slow learning from reach, and B2's loss is still falling at step 24,000 (shown). This is untested. Otherwise the screen behaves as intended in simulation: with true recovery 0 the reach reading fires about 99% (correct), and with true recovery 1 the capacity reading fires about 97%. With a quarter of the gap it says reach 53% and not shown 47%, and never capacity. With half the gap, not shown is about 99%. At per-run SD 1.0 the figures are 92% (reach at 0), 90% (capacity at 1), 44% and 57% (quarter gap), and 96% not shown (half gap). A PW0 that recovers pooled but not cipher gives mixed A about 99% of the time (suggested). The simulation ignores the train gate and box offsets; same-box runs remove the box offset.

idea.title: Table-only EGE, then shrink ladder with same-size comparators
idea.summary: Feed each char the frozen 512-wide Gemma input-table row of its word piece instead of the final 768-wide body state, so the 24-layer body never runs (whole model 137.65M). If the gain survives, prune the table to train-prompt pieces plus UNK (about 6M whole), store rows at 64-d (about 4M), or keep only the first 2 layers (17.4M). Each rung has a cheap same-size plain comparator, the first affordable route to Ben's rule 3 for a Gemma-derived reader.
idea.change: Rung 1 (T0): CIO/models/eg.py FrozenEG.encode takes H from the input embedding rows (hidden_states[0]) gathered with align() ids and skips the body; CIO/models/ledger.py adapter LN(512)+Linear(512,256) zero-init (+132,352; trainable 3,434,833; whole 137,652,561 = 134,217,728 table + trainable). Rows are dumped once from the Gemma weights. Later rungs, each one change and each gated: R1 keep only rows of distinct pieces in the 200k train prompts plus a learned UNK row (borrowed 512R; R unmeasured, needs a tokenizer pass; R=5k gives whole 5,994,833); variant R1b adds the top-N FineWeb-Edu pieces. R2 fixed PCA-64 of the kept rows, adapter LN(64)+Linear(64,256)=16,768 (R=10k whole 3,959,249). R3 first 2 Gemma layers over the pruned table (11,365,930 for the body; whole 17,360,763 at R=5k).
idea.why: The table already carries piece identity: layer-0 linear letter read 26.25% and same-word AUC 0.9998 against 22.99% and 0.9502 at the final state, and spelling is flat over all 25 layers (22.6-26.3%). EGE's largest gains were frame (+3.60) and vocab (+2.69), the splits with unseen words (7.4% and 10.1% of word types). Whether the body's context adds to the table is untested. T0 needs no Gemma forward, so it costs about a B2 run, and a pruned table makes the whole model small enough for a same-size plain model.

This is the one new deploy-time hand step T0 adds (it needs a char-to-row index), and rungs R1-R3 all keep it. No rung removes it and the idea names no autonomous version. A no-go on align() ends the whole ladder, not just rung 1.

Step 5, PREFIX (shown): eg.py:22 prepends the hand string 'task: sentence similarity | query: ' to every prompt before tokenizing. It is not teaching data and not a tool. Layer-0 rows are context-free, so the prefix cannot change a row's values, but it can change the token boundary at the first word, because Gemma tokens carry their leading space (eg.py:10-11). The effect is untested. Ben to rule, or test with the prefix removed.

Step 6, table lookup H = table[token id] (shown): frozen and context-free, with no hand code and no learning, so it is deploy-autonomous. Its content is piece identity only: layer 0 gives linear letter read 26.25 and same-word AUC 0.9998 (eg-diag/LAYERS.json, P3_layers.0). So the T0 screen measures identity. The RAND control that would separate identity from pretrained row values is not built: eg.py has only last_hidden_state (eg.py:85), with no table or random option.

Step 7, adapter LN(512)+Linear(512,256), zero-init (shown arithmetic): 1,024 + 131,328 = 132,352; trainable 3,434,833; whole 137,652,561. It is learned and deploy-autonomous. LayerNorm should absorb any global scale on the raw embedding row (suggested). Whether hidden_states[0] is sqrt-scaled is untested here, since torch and transformers are not installed in this container.

Step 8, pruned vocabulary R1 (build step; shown + untested): the kept set is drawn from the 200k skills train prompts. Building is allowed under PLAN section 0, but the set comes from the generator's own distribution: 13,084 of 18,496 train word types are made-up syllable words (custom_io/research/data.md:46-47, shown). Unseen word types are 7.4% in frame and 10.1% in vocab (same file). Whether those test words hit UNK depends on piece coverage, which the idea says is unmeasured (untested). Rule 10 bars test-generator knowledge, and whether a build-time vocabulary from the training generator counts is Ben's ruling.

Step 9, UNK routing (shown): the deployed model sends every token id outside the kept set to a learned UNK row through a fixed id-to-row map. The idea says 'no hand rule at run time', but this map is a hand-built lookup applied at run time. It is the same kind as the 108-char vocab (INVENTORY A16), which the project counts as hand and removes in V1 (PLAN line 74). Count it as hand, or store it in the checkpoint and say so.

Consequence of a frozen kept set (suggested): no piece row can be added after ship, so a new word gets letters only. That cuts against the north star of learning new things from few examples. The autonomous alternative is the full 262,144-row table (134,217,728 params, eg.py:6), which breaks the rule-3 size band. The size and autonomy tradeoff is the real decision for Ben.

Step 10, inherited fixed reader and rounds (shown): the window is fixed at kernel 5 (reader.py docstring), and the thinker runs a fixed 8 rounds (ledger.py:306-307 uses n_loops). INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md line 83 (E6) says this is not allowed under the deployable-autonomy rule and points to H1, which is unbuilt. PLAN section 0 line 8 lists 'deciding how long to think' as the model's own. The idea does not mention the fixed round count.

Step 11, inherited in-forward executor (shown; the most serious item): ledger.py:333 calls execute() on every program step inside the forward pass, and ledger.py:333-339 writes the results to the slots. This is hand code between question and answer that the model does not choose to call (PLAN line 9, rule 1). The idea's autonomy field says 'no developer step beyond the tokenizer', which is false for the deployed T0. Any T0 result is rule-1 non-compliant unless T0 is stacked on T1. T1 is NOT SHOWN (architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md: write_copy operand 29.3 and 30.9, answer 42.1 and 42.4, against a mark of 99). Its only sealed fix, span copy (MARKS-D0-T1 Amendment 3, lines 66-69), has not been run.

Step 12, other inherited hand parts (shown): NUM answers are printed with str() (ledger.py:399); the program has at most 7 writes (progparse.py:8; ledger.py:319 skips rounds outside 1..7); the first 16 prompt numbers are used (progparse.py:8, 18); answers are capped at 8 chars (ledger.py:63). These run automatically and the model cannot change them.

Build-time choices (suggested, allowed by PLAN section 0): the rung sizes R, top-N FineWeb pieces, PCA-64, the rung order, and the gate 'move to R1 only if T0 keeps >= 2/3 of EGE's gain'. They use dev answers, which is permitted at build time but not at run time. The result files should label them build-time, so nobody reads them as deploy-time tuning.

Outside autonomy but affects rule 3 (shown arithmetic): T0 trainable 3,434,833 is 92,953 above the sealed band top of 3,341,880 (PLAN-AND-MARKS section 2). Whole 137.65M needs a same-size plain comparator for any rule-3 claim. The idea's note that the comparator is 'not needed' before rung 1 holds only for a screen.

Outside autonomy but blocking (shown in PLAN section 2 table): 528 long train rows (9-11 steps) get no program, and the idea's R7 note concedes it inherits this exception. Rule 7 is Ben's hard constraint.

Factual slip in the 'why' (shown): the idea's final-state figures (22.99% and 0.9502) are attributed to DIAG.json, which I did not open. In LAYERS.json itself, layer 24 gives linear 22.58 and same-word AUC 0.9495 on a 1,360-row eval. Compare layer 0 with layer 24 from LAYERS.json only.

Corrected autonomy list (suggested): new deploy-time steps are 3, 4, 5 and 9 (tokenizer, align, PREFIX, UNK routing). Learned or frozen-lookup steps that are fine are 6 and 7. Build-time steps are 8 and the choices in the build-time item. Inherited hand steps that block rule 10 for any B2-derived model are 2, 10, 11 and 12.
