problems: Mechanism is partly contradicted by the idea's own cited splits. Shown (results/RESULTS-EG2.md, read-only): EGE changed family by -0.62 (seed 200) and -1.25 (seed 201). Family has the largest unseen-word share (183 of 363 alphabetic tokens, 29.2%, research/data.md:46-47), and the 'unseen words' story predicts gains there. Family is left out of pooled-5 and out of the idea's marks. B2's family base is 1.6%, so the change is 1-2 rows of 160 per seed: noise, not refutation, but it is the predicted test and it is absent.

The split pattern does not fit 'unseen real words'. Shown (data.md:46-47): frame's unseen tokens are 12 real words of 49; vocab's are 87% made-up syllables (144 of 593); variant has 35 real words of 63 yet gained +1.70, less than frame +3.60 and vocab +2.69. The gains track the made-up-word share, which a random per-token identity feature could also produce. 'Piece identity' is suggested, not shown, so the T0-minus-RAND arm is required, not optional.

Layer-0 evidence is overstated. Shown: results/eg-diag/LAYERS.json has 9 layers (0,3,...,24), not all 25 as the idea says; diag_eg.py:10 and :205 define that default list. Layer 0 (linear 26.25%) is compared with the final 768-d output (22.99%, DIAG.json P1), which is a different object; P3's layer 24 gives 22.58. The 3.7-point gap has no probe-noise estimate. Same-word AUC 0.9998 is close to tautological for a token-indexed table, because identical pieces give identical word means (diag_eg.py:180-199). It shows piece identity, not extra information. The 97.4% read the idea leans on used the final state plus piece length; a layer-0 MLP read is untested.

Implementation wording is wrong. 'hidden_states[0] ... skips the body' is false as written: diag_eg.py:77 gets hidden states with output_hidden_states=True, which runs all 24 layers. The skip needs a direct embed_tokens call. The sqrt scale is absorbed by the adapter LayerNorm. Shown via WebFetch of huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2 config.json (summary by a small model): vocab_size 262144, hidden_size 512, num_hidden_layers 24, 4 heads, head_dim 256, embedding_dim 768. That supports the 512-wide table (262,144 x 512 = 134,217,728). The R3 two-layer body count 11,365,930 cannot be checked from these fields (no kv-head count or projection layout), so it stays untested.

Rule 1 and rule 10 are unresolved. The T0 forward needs the Gemma tokenizer and char-to-token alignment at deploy time (models/eg.py:51-67). The idea flags this as 'Ben to rule' but offers no learned replacement and no tool-call form, so T0 is not deployable as designed. Pruning to R1 rows with a UNK row removes the identity of unseen pieces, which is the prior the idea invokes. The UNK rate R is unmeasured, and sizing R on dev would breach rule 5; it must be measured on train pieces only.

Rule 7 is inherited and not gated. progparse.py sets prog=() for any program longer than N_RES=7 steps, so the 528 long-program rows train answer-only (the director's audit cites PASS-MARKS.md:58). The idea notes the inheritance but does not make lifting N_RES a precondition, so no T0 result can be rule-compliant as run.

Pass marks are weaker than the sealed ones. Shown: PASS-MARKS.md addendum 4 clause 5 seals loops:0 in_dist <= 5 and donor in_dist <= 5 on both seeds. EGE failed exactly that clause (18.09 on seed 200; plain B2 at 1.40 on the same box). The idea makes loops:0 report-only, so a zero-round shortcut could pass. Variant is also report-only, though the mechanism is variant-linked. The 'move if T0 keeps 2/3 of EGE's gain' rule uses EGE's unconfirmed 2-seed mean (+1.85); the 6-seed EGE confirm (addendum 15, seeds 202-207) is unjudged and staged, so the reference moves. The marks are not sealed yet ('Seal first').

Screen power is low. The 'both seeds >= +1.0' mark passes a true +1.5 only about 40-50% of the time (director's audit of PASS-MARKS addendum 4). T0 has no body context and probably keeps only part of EGE's gain, so my estimate of the true T0 pooled-5 gain is about +0.3 to +1.2 (suggested). Pass probability on these marks is about 10-30%. A miss would be read as 'table route dead' or 'screen too small'. The T0-minus-RAND gate (< +0.5) has similar noise on 2 seeds.

The cost claim applies only to R1-R3. Shown: tf10m_24k trained 1,331 s for 10.8M params (results/02-calib-long/tf10m_24k/RESULT.json). The rule-3 comparator for T0 itself is a 137,649,184-param plain model (d=976, L=12; the count formula reproduces tf3m d=256 L=4 and tf10m d=384 L=6). By scaling that is about 4.7 h per seed, about 28 h for six seeds, so the 'cheap comparator' label fits only R1-R3. Arithmetic checks: adapter 132,352; trainable 3,434,833; R=5k whole 5,994,833; R2 16,768 and 3,959,249 all reproduce.

NO RANDOM-TABLE PASS CRITERION. The idea says RAND is 'read together' with T0, but the pass mark only compares T0 with B2. THE UNK ROW GETS NO TRAINING SIGNAL (reasoned from the spec). R1 keeps every piece seen in the 200k train prompts, so no training token maps to UNK. The learned UNK row then receives no gradient and is an untrained vector at deploy time. R1 needs a fixed, pre-stated rule that sends some train pieces to UNK during training (a design constant, not a tuned value).

PASS MARKS ARE INCONSISTENT AND LOOSER THAN EGE'S (shown in results/RESULTS-EG2.md and PASS-MARKS.md addenda 4 and 15). A T0 mean of +1.0 to +1.24 passes the screen and fails the move-on rule, and a mean between +0.5 and that bar gets no verdict. (b) The 2/3 rule compares a PC run with EGE's rented-box gain. The same-box baselines differ: rented B2V 73.48 and 74.39 against PC B2 73.00 and 74.27 for seeds 200 and 201 (pooled-5 computed from the RESULT.json files). Pair on one box, or use the PC EGE 6-seed run as the comparator. (c) Variant at least +3.0, loops:0 at most 5 and donor at most 5 are dropped or made report-only. These are exactly the marks EGE failed (RESULTS-EG2 marks 2 and 5). Any change needs sealing in PASS-MARKS before a run, with a reason. (d) The split-drop limit goes from 2.0 (addendum 4, 2-seed mean) to 3.0 with no sealed reason.

POWER IS LOW AND A NULL DOES NOT KILL (computed). Using B2's six PC seeds (pooled-5 73.00, 74.27, 74.74, 74.02 from RESULT.json; 73.63 and 74.47 from the brief), the SD is 0.63. Assuming independent per-seed noise, the two-arm difference SD is about 0.89. 'Both seeds at least +1.0' passes with probability about 51 percent at a true +1.5, 25 percent at +1.0, and 2 percent at 0. 'Mean below +0.5' would wrongly kill a true +1.0 about 21 percent of the time. This agrees with the brief's fact check (40-50 percent at +1.5). The screen cannot settle the idea either way.

THE KILL READING OVERREACHES (reasoned). T0 changes three things at once: it drops the body, narrows the input from 768 to 512, and swaps the adapter for LN(512) plus Linear(512,256). So 'T0 below +0.5 means the body's context carries EGE' is not identified. The result should read 'table-only does not reproduce EGE's gain on these seeds'.

chair.reasons: Worth a sealed screen, but only revised. It is the cheapest test in the Gemma area that splits EGE's gain into three causes: the 24-layer body's context, piece identity, and the pretrained row values. T0 has no Gemma forward, so it costs about a B2 run. Shown (results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json wall_s): PC B2 runs on seeds 202-205 took 3,595-5,638 s (about 1.0-1.6 h), while seeds 200 and 201 took 13,318 and 15,214 s. The test critic's 3.7-4.2 h per run applies only to the two slow seeds. T0 plus the control on seeds 202 and 203 is therefore about 4 runs, roughly 6 h on the PC, not the idea's 3 h and not 16 h. Shown (eg.py:1-25, 51-98): the table is 134,217,728 params (262,144 x 512) and encode currently uses last_hidden_state only. No table-only, random-table or shuffled-table arm exists; the 'w2a-3' control the idea cites is not in the files. Shown (eg-diag/LAYERS.json): 9 layers were probed (0,3,...,24), not 25. Layer 0 gives linear 26.25, linear-plus-offset 56.82 and same-word AUC 0.9998; layer 24 gives 22.58 / 49.19 / 0.9495. The AUC of 0.9998 is near-tautological for a lookup and shows identity, not usefulness. Spelling does not rise at any layer, so the table is at least not worse than the body for letters. Fixes that must be sealed first. (1) The control is not a gate in the idea as written. It must be a required mark. A row-shuffled copy of the real table (fixed permutation seed, same ids and alignment, same marginal values) is a cleaner control than random Gaussian rows. (2) The sealed addendum-4 marks were loosened without a stated reason. The 2-seed variant and loops:0 clauses are unreliable (noise audit), so make them report-only on the screen and gates at the 6-seed step, with the reason written down. (3) The 'keeps 2/3 of EGE's gain' rule points at a moving reference, since q39 is unjudged. Use absolute marks versus same-box B2, and seal before q39 is read. (4) A pruned table needs a training-time rule that sends some pieces to UNK. Otherwise the UNK row is never trained, because no train piece maps to it. (5) The shrink ladder's rule-3 story is muddled. A plain 4-17M comparator does not isolate Gemma, because B2's architecture lead is +20 pooled-5. The attribution control is B2 with a size-matched from-scratch piece table. The plain comparator is only the rule-3 headline. (6) 'Hours: 3' ignores the control arm. Rule 1/10 cost is the same as EGE's: the Gemma tokenizer and align() (eg.py:51-67) are hand glue. Ben rules on that; it does not block a screen. Rule 7's 528-row exception is inherited by every B2-derived arm and is not introduced here. Screen power is low: both-seeds >= +1.0 passes a true +1.5 only about 40-50% of the time. A miss means 'not shown', not 'dead'.
chair.revised_idea:
Table-only EGE (T0) with a row-shuffled control (T0S), run after the EGE 6-seed confirm (q39) reads, then a conditional small-table rung.

LABELS: everything below is untested until run. This is a B2-internal screen on the small card experiments (rule 9). It is not a rule-3 result and not a rule-1/10-clean design. The Gemma tokenizer and char-to-piece align() are hand glue shared with EGE, so Ben rules on them. The 528-row 7-step exception is inherited by every B2-derived arm.

STEP 0, CPU only, minutes, no training, on Ben's PC (needs the tokenizer and the Gemma weights, neither of which is in this container). (a) Dump the 512-wide input rows from the Gemma weights through the model's own embedding module and assert the shape [262144, 512]. Do not use hidden_states[0] as the source: diag_eg.py:77 gets hidden states by running all layers. Take the rows the body would receive, whether or not they carry the sqrt scale; the adapter LayerNorm absorbs a global scale. (b) Run the tokenizer over the 200k train prompts and report the count R of distinct pieces. Report per-dev-split piece coverage under any pruned set only after the set is fixed from train prompts or FineWeb-Edu, never from dev. Label the result a diagnostic. (c) Write the autonomy audit line for every deploy-time step: learned, frozen lookup, build-time asset, or hand.

STEP 1, the screen. Seeds 202 and 203 on Ben's PC, run after q39 reads. The shared seeds give a three-way paired comparison per seed: PC B2 from q33, PC EGE from q39, and T0. Seal the marks before q39 is read, and say in the seal that the seeds are shared with q39. If q39 is proved wrong (EGE 6-seed mean gain < +0.5, or EGE behind B2 on 3 or more seeds), skip T0 entirely, because there is no gain left to explain.

Arms, one change each:
- T0 (the one change from EGE: body removed). Each char gets the frozen 512-d input-table row of its word piece, from the same align() ids. It passes through LN(512) + zero-initialised Linear(512,256), then is added to the letter embedding before the window, exactly as EGE does. Adapter +132,352; trainable 3,434,833; whole 137,652,561 = 134,217,728 table + trainable. Trainable is +5.86% over plain_tf S and 92,953 above the sealed band top 3,341,880, so label it B2-internal like EGE.
- T0S (the one change from T0: values scrambled). Same wrapper, same ids, same alignment, same adapter, but the table rows are permuted across piece ids once with a fixed seed. It keeps piece identity and the marginal value distribution, and destroys the id-to-meaning map. It is a required control, not an optional read.
- Optional third arm if the PC has time: a size-matched from-scratch trainable piece table (same dimension, random init). It separates 'frozen pretrained' from 'any learned piece feature'. It is the attribution control for the later rung.

Cost: 4 runs (T0 and T0S on 2 seeds), about 1.0-1.6 h each at the seed-202 to 205 PC rate, so about 6 h. If the PC is loaded like seeds 200 and 201 (3.7-4.2 h per run), it is up to about 16 h. Per rule 6, use rented GPUs only when the PC and Mac are both full.

SEALED MARKS, written before any run. All are 2-seed screen marks versus same-box, same-seed PC B2.
(1) pooled-5 T0 minus B2 >= +1.0 on BOTH seeds.
(2) T0 minus T0S >= +0.5 on the 2-seed mean, and not negative on either seed.
(3) cipher_map in_dist >= 95 (2-seed mean).
(4) chain-5 >= 99.0 on both seeds.
(5) No dev split down more than 3.0 (2-seed mean). Reason: the -2.0 rule fails about 20% of no-change draws on 2 seeds.
(6) Report-only on the screen, next to same-box B2: variant, loops:0, donor, and family as a report-only split. Each becomes a gate at the 6-seed step: loops:0 6-seed mean <= B2 + 1.0, donor <= 5 on every seed, and addendum 4's variant mark kept or re-justified.
Proved wrong: T0 pooled-5 mean gain < +0.5 means 'table-only does not reproduce EGE's gain on these seeds'. It does not prove that the body carries it, because the adapter width and the missing body change together. T0 minus T0S < +0.5 on the mean means pretrained row values add nothing beyond piece identity.

DECISION TABLE:
- T0 passes (1)-(5) and (2) holds: extend T0 to the 6-seed paired rule (mean gain >= +1.0, ahead on >= 5 of 6 seeds, using the 5 q33 seeds for B2 and EGE seeds from q39), then Step 2.
- (1) holds but T0 minus T0S < +0.5: piece identity carries the gain. Report it honestly. The next step is the from-scratch piece table, with no Gemma at all.
- T0 mean < +0.5: the table route is closed for this screen. Any further Gemma work is about the body or the adapter, not the table.
- Anything between these: tie, no ladder.

STEP 2, only after T0 clears the 6-seed rule, and one rung at a time.
R1b: keep the top-N FineWeb-Edu pieces (free human text, rule 2) plus a learned UNK row. N is fixed in advance from FineWeb-Edu counts, not from dev. The default is FineWeb, so no generator vocabulary ships. A train-prompt-only set is a labelled variant. To train the UNK row, send a fixed fraction of pieces to UNK during training (a design constant that is the same every run). The count is N+1 rows, so N=5,000 gives whole 5,995,345, not 5,994,833. The id-to-row map is a frozen build asset stored in the checkpoint and counted as hand in the audit. Report the dev piece-coverage rate only after N is sealed.
R2 (PCA-64 rows) and R3 (first 2 body layers) wait until R1b is read and have no marks yet.
Rule-3 comparators for any rung:
- Attribution: B2 with a size-matched from-scratch piece table and the same adapter.
- Rule-3 headline: a plain transformer of the same whole size (+-3%), 6 seeds, same recipe. The 137.65M one (d=976, L=12, 137,649,184 params) is needed only for a T0 headline, and it is not cheap (about 40x B2).
- A plain 4-17M comparator alone does not isolate Gemma, because it mixes in B2's architecture lead.
Re-test any positive result at 10M, because B2's lead over plain shrank from 3M to 10M (first-look-10m).

RULE-10 FOLLOW-UP (conditional, untested): if Ben rules that align() is not acceptable, the replacement is piece memory without alignment. The thinker cross-attends to piece rows with learned piece-index positions, next to the letter positions. This is a separate one-change arm, and EGK's NaN on seed 201 is a warning for any second-reader-pass design.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.
1. Sequence. Seal the marks first, then run T0 and T0S on seeds 202 and 203 after q39 reads. Skip T0 if EGE's 6-seed confirm is proved wrong (mean gain < +0.5, or behind B2 on 3 or more seeds). Use absolute marks versus same-box PC B2 (q33 seeds 202 and 203), not '2/3 of EGE's gain'. State that the seeds overlap q39's EGE seeds, which gives paired three-way comparisons.
2. The control is a required mark. T0S is the same wrapper with the real table's rows permuted across piece ids (fixed seed). The mark is T0 minus T0S >= +0.5 on the mean and not negative on either seed. State the outcome of each branch in the seal, including that T0 passing while T0S ties means identity, not Gemma content.
3. Marks. Pooled-5 gain >= +1.0 on both seeds; cipher_map in_dist >= 95; chain-5 >= 99.0 each seed; no split down more than 3.0 on the 2-seed mean (give the reason). Variant, loops:0, donor and family are report-only on the screen and become gates at the 6-seed step (loops:0 mean <= B2 + 1.0, donor <= 5 each seed). Pair on one box. Say that a pass is only about 40-50% likely at a true +1.5, so a miss is 'not shown'.
4. Cost. About 4 runs at 1.0-1.6 h each, roughly 6 h on the PC (shown: wall_s 3,595-5,638 s for PC B2 seeds 202-205). It can reach about 16 h if the PC is loaded like seeds 200 and 201 (13,318 and 15,214 s). Per rule 6, use rented GPUs only if the PC and Mac are both full.
5. Step 0 comes before any training. Assert the shape [262144, 512] from the real weights, and take the rows through the embedding module, not hidden_states[0]. Report R from the train prompts. Fix any pruned set from train or FineWeb-Edu before reading any dev piece-coverage number.
6. Pruning needs a training-time rule that sends a fixed fraction of pieces to UNK, or the UNK row never trains. FineWeb-Edu top-N is the default set. Count the UNK row in the parameter total.
7. Labels. The size is B2-internal (trainable +5.86% over plain_tf S). Rule 3 needs a same-whole-size plain model, 6 seeds, same recipe, and also a B2 with a size-matched from-scratch piece table to attribute the effect to Gemma. A small plain comparator alone confounds Gemma with B2's architecture lead.
8. Autonomy. Include a per-step audit (learned / frozen lookup / build-time asset / hand). The Gemma tokenizer, align() (eg.py:51-67), the PREFIX string and the id-to-row map are the hand or build-time parts, for Ben to rule on. The inherited in-forward executor and the 528-row 7-step exception are not fixed by T0. Fixes are T1 span copy and lifting N_RES, shared across all B2-derived arms.
9. Do not use these as evidence for the mechanism: same-word AUC 0.9998 (near-tautological for a lookup), 'all 25 layers' (only 9 probed), or an unseen-word story (the family split is the predicted test and moved -0.62 / -1.25; the area family check found relation and lookup prompts, not unseen words). Present the unseen-word and relation-word explanations as competing hypotheses. U0 (own pieces replacing letters, -3.1 / -5.4) is a progress-board note only; do not lean on it until its RESULT.json is read.
10. Keep this on the B2 card only (rule 9). Do not mix it with village-model claims.

plan.title: T0 table-only Gemma reader vs scrambled-table control
plan.ben_line: Gemma is a big word-reading network from Google. This test asks whether just its word lookup table, without the network, helps our small letter reader, and then scrambles the table to check that the real word meanings are what do the helping.
plan.question: On the B2 card only (rule 9): does a frozen 512-d input-table row per character, with no Gemma network run, keep EGE's pooled-5 gain over same-box PC B2 (T0 minus B2), and do the real rows beat the same table with rows scrambled across pieces (T0 minus T0S)? Screen only; a claim needs six seeds (rule 4).
plan.one_change: Relative to EGE, one source change: each character takes the frozen 512-d input-table row of its word piece (the EG2 text model's input embedding, 262,144 x 512, same align() ids) instead of the 768-d final body state (eg.py:85). The adapter becomes LayerNorm(512) plus a zero-start Linear(512,256), added before the window where EGE adds its term. The width change follows from the source and is not a second change. T0S is T0 with the rows permuted across piece ids (fixed seed, one draw); nothing else differs. Code paths are in the read-only scratchpad copy; the owning thread's write path may differ.
arms: B2 on the PC (queue 33, existing): B2_s202 pooled-5 74.74 and B2_s203 74.02 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2/*/RESULT.json, computed from the per-split by_family counts, shown). This is the baseline for every gate. Queue 33 ran at --par 3 and queue 39 at --par 2 with the same flags (headers, shown); concurrency is assumed not to change results (suggested).
EGE on the PC (queue 39, exists only after q39 runs): reference, not a gate. Its 2-seed screen was +1.59 / +2.12 against rented-box B2V (results/RESULTS-EG2.md, shown).

T0 (new): trainable 3,434,833 (B2's 3,302,481 plus a 132,352 adapter; shown by arithmetic), whole 137,652,561 (134,217,728 table counted; shown by arithmetic). No Gemma network forward at training time, so training cost should be near B2's (suggested, untested).
T0S (new control): T0 with the rows of the used piece ids permuted once by a fixed seed. Same counts. This keeps piece identity and destroys the id-to-meaning map.

Only if T0 passes the screen: a from-scratch trainable 512-d piece table of the same shape (attribution control), and a plain transformer of 137,649,184 params (d=976, L=12; the count formula reproduces tf3m 3,244,544 exactly, shown) as the rule-3 comparator.
plan.seeds: Screen: seeds 202 and 203, the seeds q39 uses for EGE, so B2, EGE, T0 and T0S are paired per seed on one device. Confirm: seeds 202-207 (B2 202-205 from queue 33, B2 206-207 from queue 39). The director's phrase "the 5 q33 seeds for B2" is wrong: q33 has six seeds (200-205, shown), and the confirm set must match EGE's 202-207.
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC (cuda, bf16), a new queue_local file with queue 33's flags (--par 2 or 3). Step 0 is CPU-only and may run on the PC or the M1 Pro if the EG2 weights are present there; it does not need q39 to finish. Rented 5090s only if the PC and the Mac are both full (rule 6; Ben's call).
pass_marks: Seal first: a new PASS-MARKS addendum 21, timestamped before q39's results are read. It must list every change from addendum 4 with a reason: variant (+3.0) becomes report-only; loops:0 and donor (<=5, absolute) become report-only; the split-drop limit goes from 2.0 to 3.0. Suggested, not in the director's list: keep donor in_dist <= 5 on each seed as a gate, since PC B2 sat at 3.09-3.75 on seeds 200-205 (shown) and the cost is nothing.
M1: pooled-5 gain over same-box PC B2 >= +1.0 on BOTH seeds 202 and 203. One point is about 60 of 6,040 rows (arithmetic, shown).
M2: T0 minus T0S >= +0.5 on the 2-seed mean, and not negative on either seed.

M3: cipher_map in_dist >= 95 on the 2-seed mean. Its 80 rows fail at 5 or more wrong. PC B2 has 2 wrong (97.5 on each seed, shown). EGE read 97.50 and 95.00 (results/RESULTS-EG2.md:121, shown), so this mark sits near the edge.
M4: chain-5 >= 99.0 on each seed (1,000 rows; fails at 11 or more wrong). PC B2 has 4 and 5 wrong on seeds 202 and 203 (99.6 and 99.5, shown).

M5: no split of in_dist, answer, frame or vocab down more than 3.0 on the 2-seed mean versus same-box B2. Variant is report-only under item 7, so the seal must say whether variant is inside M5; the director's wording leaves it open.
Report-only on the screen: variant, loops:0, donor, family, steps per second and peak memory. Each becomes a six-seed gate at confirm.
A run with a nonfinite loss or a status other than ok is a failed arm, not a missing point (EGK seed 201 precedent, RESULTS-EG2.md, shown).
plan.proved_wrong: Screen kills. (a) T0 mean pooled-5 gain over B2 < +0.5: table-only does not reproduce EGE's gain on these seeds. It does NOT prove the body carries the gain, because the source and the adapter width change together. (b) T0 minus T0S < +0.5 on the mean, or negative on either seed: the real rows add nothing beyond piece identity. (c) T0 passes M1 and T0S also passes M1: the gain is piece identity, not Gemma content. Before training: step 0 does not give a [262144, 512] table, or the table cannot be read from the EG2 weights. Before the screen: q39 is proved wrong under addendum 15 (EGE six-seed mean gain < +0.5, or EGE behind B2 on 3 or more seeds), in which case T0 is skipped entirely.
plan.null_risk: Computed here by simulation, assuming independent arm noise (shared seeds could shrink the noise and change these odds). The per-seed paired-difference SD is taken as 0.9 (B2's seed SD of 0.63 times root 2) or 1.3 (the measured B2-minus-plain_tf_steps paired SD, results/CONFIRM-ANALYSIS.json, shown). No real change: M1 and M2 together pass about 1-3%; M2 alone passes 17-21%, so M2 is the weak mark on two seeds. Identity alone (T0 and T0S both +1.5): the two-seed marks pass 13-14%, a roughly 1-in-8 false call of Gemma content. Real Gemma content of +1.5: 37-48% pass; +1.0: about 20-22%. So a two-seed pass is a screen result, not a claim. Six seeds: identity-only passes 8-14% with the draft rule (mean >= +0.5 and ahead on >= 4 of 6); ahead on >= 5 of 6 (suggested) cuts that to about 5-8%. Six seeds, true +1.5 Gemma content: the pooled gate passes 76-90%. Not evidence, per the chair: same-word AUC 0.9998 (a lookup gives identical rows for identical pieces, so it shows identity only); 'all 25 layers' (only 9 were probed, results/eg-diag/LAYERS.json, shown); the unseen-word story (research/data.md's printed shares do not match its counts, e.g. 49 of 636 is 7.7%, not 7.4%, shown by arithmetic).
plan.autonomy: Build-time experiment only: it adds no deploy-time learning, sleep or choice step. The shipped chain for T0 would be: (1) hand regex word and number splits (models/progparse.py:14, data.py:149-154; inherited; fails rule 1); (2) hand Gemma tokenizer and char-to-token align() run on every question (models/eg.py:51-67) plus the hand PREFIX string (eg.py:22); fails rule 1/10 until Ben rules; (3) frozen pretrained table lookup (rule 2 allows it; counted in the size; deploy-autonomous given step 2); (4) learned LayerNorm, zero-start Linear and reader (learned); (5) a fixed 8 thinker rounds (inherited; not the model's choice); (6) learned program writing (learned); (7) exact int64 executor inside the forward pass (hand, inherited; T1 is the planned tool and is not shown, per architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md); (8) learned talker. T0 adds one frozen lookup and no deploy-time choice. If Ben rules align() out, the conditional follow-up is a learned piece memory with no alignment (the chair's note; untested). Dev splits and family only; no GOLD-PRIVATE or blind panel (rule 5).
steps: 1. Seal addendum 21 before q39's results are read: arms, seeds, M1-M5, the report-only list, each change from addendum 4 with its reason, the T0S rule, the kill rules, the nonfinite rule, the decision table and the six-seed gates. Name which splits M5 covers.

2. Step 0, no training and no GPU (PC or M1 Pro CPU if the EG2 weights are present; does not wait for q39): load the EG2 text part at revision 914f7f89142e33e77833254d9c9b90c3cef7303b; take its input embedding weight; assert shape [262144, 512] (134,217,728 values, which matches eg.py:6, shown). Save one file outside checkpoint.pt with its sha256, and confirm the table is absent from model.state_dict(), as EGE's frozen weights are (eg.py:3).

3. Step 0, continued: run align() over the train and dev prompts and count the distinct piece ids (diagnostic only; nothing is chosen from dev). Build T0S's map once: a derangement from numpy RandomState(0) over the sorted used piece ids, so each used piece gets another used piece's row (suggested in place of the chair's whole-table permutation, which would hand used pieces rare and multilingual rows). Save the map and its sha256 before any run.

4. Implement T0 and T0S: a table-source path in FrozenEG (gather rows with the same align() ids, no body forward, no 271M model load at training time); the adapter width comes from the source (512, not EG_DIM=768 at eg.py:23 and ledger.py:177-184). CPU checks: T0 at step 0 gives exactly B2's output (the zero-start adapter; the draw order is kept, per ledger.py:177); trainable 3,434,833; whole 137,652,561; T0S differs from T0 only in the row map. Also confirm the edited ledger still builds B2 with the same parameter count (3,302,481). If the diff touches the B2 path, rerun B2_s202 and B2_s203 on the edited code (about 3 h, suggested) before using q33's numbers as baselines.
5. Wait for q39 and read it. If q39 is proved wrong under addendum 15, stop: T0 is skipped.

6. Queue T0 and T0S on seeds 202 and 203 (four runs) with queue 33's flags: 24,000 steps, batch 256, lr 1e-3, bf16, --final-eval. Cost: queue 33 ran seeds 202-205 in 3,595-5,638 s each (1.0-1.6 h, shown), so about 6 run-hours; seeds 200-201 took 3.7-4.2 h each on the same device (shown; cause not recorded), so up to about 16 run-hours if the PC is loaded like that. Record wall time, steps per second and status per run.

7. Score with the existing scorer: pooled-5, each split, chain-5, cipher_map in_dist, loops:0 in_dist, donor, family. Per seed: T0 minus B2_s202 (74.74) and B2_s203 (74.02); T0 minus T0S. Check M1 to M5; fill the report-only fields.

8. Decision (the chair's table): T0 passes M1-M5 and M2 holds, so go to the six-seed confirm. M1 holds but M2 fails: piece identity carries the gain; the next arm is the from-scratch piece table with no Gemma. T0 mean < +0.5: the table route is closed for this screen. Anything between: tie, no ladder. Write the autonomy audit line with the result.

9. Only after a pass: the six-seed confirm (see confirm), then the 10M re-test, then the rule-3 comparator if a headline claim is wanted. The comparator's cost is suggested at about 4.9 h per seed (1,331 s for 10.8M on the calibration box, shown, scaled by 13.2x) to about 9.6 h (0.73 h for 10.4M in the 10M first look, shown, scaled), so 30-60 h for six seeds.

10. Evidence hygiene: present the unseen-word story (frame, vocab) and the relation-word story as competing hypotheses, not as shown. The family-split check in the director's brief found EGE's reliable gains on relation and lookup prompts, not on unseen words.

It is not a same-size control and would dominate training. Replace it with a learned side channel over the piece domain (the existing 416-id BPE gives 416 x 256 = 106,496 params, shown arithmetic, out of band, declared) or drop it.

T0S DOMAIN LEAK RISK: the derangement is said to cover 'used piece ids' but step 3 is ambiguous about whether dev is included. A piece outside the permuted domain keeps its real row, so T0S would carry real Gemma content for unseen-word splits (research/data.md:47 shows unseen alphabetic types in frame 7.4%, vocab 10.1%, variant 4.2%, family 29.2%, shown). The domain must be train plus every scored dev split, with a 100% coverage assertion that voids T0S if it fails.

SIZE BAND NOT DECLARED: T0 trainable 3,434,833 is 92,953 above the sealed band top 3,341,880 (shown band in train.py:11; INPUT-UNITS-2026-10-07.md:48) and +5.9% over plain_tf S 3,244,544 (shown arithmetic). The plan never states this. EGE has the same overrun (+159,001, shown in the code notes). T0S shares the overrun, so T0 minus T0S is size-matched but T0 minus B2 is not. Addendum 21 must declare it.

WRONG BASELINE REFERENCE: the plan says addendum 21 changes marks 'from addendum 4'. But addendum 15 (sealed for the EGE 6-seed confirm, PASS-MARKS.md lines 369-390) already drops variant from the pass list and keeps donor <= 5 on every seed and loops:0 at plain B2 + 1.0 on the six-seed mean. Addendum 4 (lines 157-187) is stale for these items. The changes must be stated against addendum 15.

LOOSENED MARK AFTER A FAILED SCREEN: the plan's screen split-drop limit goes from 2.0 to 3.0. Addendum 4 and addendum 15 both use 2.0 (shown). The plan's own confirm uses 2.0, so a screen pass can fail the confirm on a rule the screen waived. The loosening is made after EGE failed its screen (shown in addendum 15). Keep 2.0 unless the reason is written with its noise numbers, and label it as post hoc.
M5 AMBIGUITY: the plan says variant is report-only and also that the seal must say whether variant is inside M5. It must be decided explicitly in addendum 21.

M1 POWER: the both-seed mark passes a true +1.5 gain only about 42-51% of the time (normal approximation, computed here; the plan says 37-48%). Under no change it is 1.8% (paired SD 0.9) to 4.9% (SD 1.3). A 2-seed mean rule (>= +1.0 and neither seed below 0) gives about 5-12% false pass and about 65-75% power at +1.5 (suggested; not simulated here). Either way the chosen rule and both error rates must be sealed in advance.

M2 IS WEAK ON TWO SEEDS: T0 minus T0S >= +0.5 on the 2-seed mean passes about 17-21% under no difference (the plan's own figure, consistent with a normal approximation). It is acceptable only as a screen filter; any claim rests on the six-seed gate.

RULE 7 BLOCKER, UNPRICED: 528 train rows have more than 7 program steps and get no program (progparse.py:199 with N_RES = 7 at progparse.py:8; PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:53 says no arm may fall back to answer-only, and line 58 says B2 keeps the exception). The plan says the exception is 'not fixed by T0' but does not block claims on it. The documented fix K1 (lift to 16 calls, about +2,300 params, PLAN-AND-MARKS line 70) changes the baseline, so a rule-clean claim needs six B2 reruns plus six T0 pairs. None is costed.

PREFIX IS A HAND STRING ON THE TABLE PATH: eg.py PREFIX = 'task: sentence similarity | query: ' is prepended to every prompt before the tokenizer. A table-only path runs no body, so the prefix has no function there except tokenization at the boundary. Drop it on the table path and declare it (rule 1 risk removed at no cost to the attribution tests, which compare T0 with T0S on the same tokens).

TOKENIZER ALIGNMENT IS HAND GLUE ON EVERY QUESTION: FrozenEG.align (eg.py) maps characters to tokens by offsets and runs at deploy time. This is a rule 1 and rule 10 question that the plan defers to Ben. The screen can run as a B2-internal result, but a positive T0 cannot ship until Ben rules the tokenizer a pretrained component or a learned boundary replaces it. The learned-BPE control has a hand regex pre-tokenizer (bpe.py) and inherits the same ruling.

FP16/BF16 NAN RISK: eg.py's load() puts the Gemma weights in bf16 on CUDA, so a table loaded the same way is bf16. EGK seed 201 went non-finite in both runs (RESULTS-EG2.md, shown in the brief); its cause is untested. The T0 table and its LayerNorm should be fp32, which costs 537 MB for the table (shown arithmetic) or 268 MB in bf16.

IDENTITY VS CAPACITY CONFOUND: a T0S gain could come from the extra 132,352 input-side parameters acting on per-piece identity, not from piece identity or content. A letter-level random table through the same adapter (T0L, 108 rows) would separate extra parameters from piece identity. Suggested; untested. It is needed before calling a T0S pass 'identity'.

MISSING BODY READ: the question Ben cares about is whether Gemma's body adds beyond its word table, and T0 alone cannot answer it. EGE minus T0 per seed on 202-207 is available once q39 and the T0 confirm both run, but the plan does not pre-register it. Pre-register it as report-only (suggested).

GENERATOR SHORTCUT: research/data.md:44-47 shows the train set has about 13,084 made-up syllable word types against 490 designed words, and that some families use different word types. A table that separates real words from made-up ones can gain on families for reasons unrelated to understanding. Pre-register a report-only read split into made-up-word families and real-word families (suggested). Family-split gains may also reflect Gemma's world knowledge (weekday names, units; data.md:58), which is legal under rule 2 but must be labelled as such.

DETERMINISM UNMEASURED: the plan assumes concurrency does not change results (suggested). No same-seed repeat exists. Speeds varied 2.5 to 4 times across q33 seeds (1.58-1.82 steps/s for seeds 200-201 against 4.30-6.74 for 202-205, shown in RESULT.json wall_s and steps_per_s). One rerun of B2_s202 with the same flags (about 1.5 h at par 2) measures same-seed noise. It is cheap relative to a 2-seed gate.

HOURS UNDERSTATED: hours = 6.5 counts the screen only. Left out: the q39 wait (8 PC runs, about 18 run-hours and at least about 9 h wall at par 2; shown from the q39 header and EGT_s200 at 9,203 s), the six-seed confirm (12 runs, about 10-25 h wall at par 2, computed from q33 timings), and the B2 reruns for rule 7 or determinism. The full chain is about 25-50 h of wall time.

CODE RISK, SIZE REPORT: ledger.py size() (line 274) sets the frozen count to N_TEXT (271,002,624) for any eg_embed model. Unless changed, T0's whole-model count and any rule-3 comparison would read 274 million instead of 137,652,561. eg.py's load() also asserts N_TEXT, so the table path must bypass that check. Both must be changed and tested.

CODE RISK, SINGLE SITE (POSITIVE): the reader's Gemma call is one site, ledger.py read() at about line 261, through self.eg().encode; the teacher call (about line 538) runs only with eg_teach. A table path therefore replaces one call. Both run() and talk() reach it through read(), so eval cannot silently fall back to the body if that site is replaced.

CHECKS THAT HOLD: (a) batch order is seeded separately (train.py:133-139, data.py:135-139), so arms share data order per seed; (b) the zero-start adapter is built after every B2 weight (ledger.py:174-187) and its weight and bias are zeroed, so step 0 equals B2 (CPU check still required); (c) T0 counts 3,434,833 and 137,652,561 follow from 262,144 x 512 and the 132,352-param adapter (shown arithmetic); (d) the EG2 word table is 134,217,728 (eg.py docstring); (e) the plain comparator 137,649,184 (d=976, L=12, V=108, 224 positions) reproduces the plain_tf formula, checked against plain_tf.py; (f) queue 33 ran at --par 3 and queue 39 at --par 2 (queue headers); (g) B2_s202 74.74 and B2_s203 74.02 pooled-5 (RESULT.json); (h) donor 3.09-3.75 across seeds 200-205 and loops:0 mean 3.33 (RESULT.json); (i) research/data.md's 49 of 636 is 7.7%, not the printed 7.4% (shown arithmetic).

CITATION PRECISION: the 'same-word AUC 0.9998' comes from LAYERS.json P3_layers['0'], the input-table layer, not the final layer (shown). Only 9 of 25 Gemma layers were probed (layers 0, 3, ..., 24), which the plan states correctly. Name the layer when citing 0.9998.

CHEAPER OPTION NOT CONSIDERED: fine-tune from the saved B2_s202 checkpoint with the table adapter for about 2,000 steps, against T0S and a zero adapter. This takes minutes of GPU, not hours (suggested). It is a different recipe from the 24,000-step from-scratch one, so it can only screen and cannot decide. Worth doing before the 4-run screen if Ben allows a screen-only tier.

EGE GATE ORDER: T0 is skipped only if q39 is proved wrong, which needs all six seeds. Running T0 on 202 and 203 as soon as EGE_s202 and EGE_s203 finish would save wall time at the cost of possibly spending a screen on a dead EGE result. This is Ben's call (suggested).

fixed_plan.title: T0 table-only Gemma screen with a size-legal same-shape control, run only after q39 and the fixes below
fixed_plan.ben_line: Gemma keeps a big dictionary of word pieces. This test switches off the big Gemma network and gives our small reader only that dictionary. If the real entries help more than the same entries shuffled, the dictionary itself carries useful meaning, and it costs much less to train than the whole Gemma reader.
fixed_plan.question: On the B2 card only: does a frozen 512-d word-piece row per character, with no Gemma network run, add to B2's pooled-5 over same-box PC B2 (T0 minus B2), and do the real rows beat the same rows permuted over every piece any scored prompt uses (T0 minus T0S)? This is a screen. A claim needs six paired seeds and the rule 3 and rule 7 items below.
fixed_plan.one_change: Relative to EGE, one source change: each character's input term is the frozen EmbeddingGemma-2 input-table row of its piece (512-d, 262,144 x 512), passed through LayerNorm(512) and a zero-start Linear(512,256) before the window, in place of the 768-d body state. Declared extra: the PREFIX string is not prepended on the table path, since a table-only path runs no body. T0S is T0 with the rows permuted by one fixed derangement over the full scored domain; nothing else differs.
arms: B2 same-box PC: B2_s202 pooled-5 74.74 and B2_s203 74.02 (results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json, shown). Plus one same-flag repeat of B2_s202 to measure same-seed noise (suggested, about 1.5 h).
EGE on PC (queue 39, not yet run): reference only. EGE minus T0 per seed is read report-only, to test whether the Gemma body adds beyond its table.

T0 (new): trainable 3,434,833 = 3,302,481 + 132,352 (shown arithmetic); whole 137,652,561 (shown arithmetic). Trainable is 92,953 above the sealed band top 3,341,880: declared in the seal. ledger.py size() must report 134,217,728 frozen, not N_TEXT.
T0S (new control): same counts and same adapter; rows permuted over the full domain (train plus every dev split's pieces, coverage asserted at 100%).

Conditional, only if T0S also passes M1 (so the gain is identity or capacity): T0L, a 108-row random letter table through the same adapter (separates extra input parameters from identity); and a learned piece side channel with the existing 416-id BPE (106,496 params at d=256, shown arithmetic, out of band, declared). The 262,144 x 512 trainable table named in the earlier plan is struck: it is 134,217,728 trainable params.
fixed_plan.seeds: Screen: 202 and 203 (B2, T0 and T0S paired per seed; batch order is seeded per seed, and the adapter is built after every B2 weight). Confirm: 202-207 (B2 202-205 from q33, 206-207 from q39).
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC (cuda), queue file like q33 and q39 with the same EG2 env lines, --par 2 to match q39. Rented 5090s only if Ben allows (rule 6).
pass_marks: SEAL FIRST: PASS-MARKS addendum 21, written before any T0 run and before q39 is read if Ben permits an early run. Its baseline is addendum 15 (not addendum 4). It lists every change from addendum 15 with its noise reason and says the changes come after the EGE screen failed. It declares the band overrun (+92,953), the frozen count (134,217,728) and the domain rule.

M1 (replaces the both-seed mark): pooled-5 gain over same-box B2, 2-seed mean >= +1.0, and neither seed below 0.0. Suggested error rates: about 5-12% false pass under no change, about 65-75% power at a true +1.5 (normal approximation, not simulated).
M2: T0 minus T0S, 2-seed mean >= +0.5, and neither seed negative. Alone it passes about 17-21% under no difference, so it is a screen filter only.
M3: cipher_map in_dist pooled over the two seeds >= 95 (76 of 80 right). B2 has 39 of 40 on each of seeds 202 and 203.
M4: chain-5 >= 99.0 on each seed (1,000 rows; 10 misses allowed).
M5: no dev split of in_dist, answer, frame or vocab down more than 2.0 on the 2-seed mean (the addendum 4 and 15 limit, not 3.0). Variant is report-only, stated explicitly.
Leak: donor in_dist <= 5 on each seed (B2 seeds 200-205 read 3.09-3.75, shown). loops:0 is report-only on the screen.
Domain assertion: every piece id in every scored split lies in the permutation domain. Any miss voids T0S.
Any nonfinite loss or status other than ok is a failed arm (EGK seed 201 precedent).
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Screen kills: (a) T0's 2-seed mean gain over B2 below +0.5 closes the table route for this screen (this does not show the body carries the gain); (b) T0 minus T0S below +0.5 on the mean, or negative on either seed, means the real rows add nothing beyond piece identity; (c) if T0S passes M1 as well, the gain is identity or capacity, not content. Build bugs stop the run: step 0 output of T0 differing from B2 for the same seed, or B2's parameter count or state-dict hash changing. Skip entirely if q39 is proved wrong under addendum 15 (six-seed mean gain below +0.5, or EGE behind B2 on 3 or more seeds). Decision after the screen: M1 and M2 both hold, go to confirm; M1 holds and M2 fails with T0S also passing M1, run T0L and the learned piece channel before any content claim; T0 mean below +0.5, close; anything else, tie with no ladder.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Checked by normal approximation, not simulated here. Both-seed M1 false pass: 1.8% (paired SD 0.9) to 4.9% (SD 1.3); power at a true +1.5 about 42-51% (the plan says 37-48%). Proposed mean rule: about 5-12% false pass and about 65-75% power at +1.5. M2 alone: 17-21% false pass (plan). Identity-only truth (T0 and T0S both +1.5): about 10% pass the screen (plan's 13-14% is close), so T0S is necessary. Six-seed pooled gate power at +1.5: 76-90% (plan). The screen's larger risk is a miss, not a false pass: a true +1.5 fails the sealed both-seed mark about half the time.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Build-time experiment only. It adds no deploy-time learning, sleep or choice step. Shipped chain: (1) hand regex word and number splits, inherited (progparse.py:14, data.py:149-154), a rule 1 problem for the whole B2 family; (2) a pretrained Gemma tokenizer with hand char-to-token alignment (eg.py align) run on every question, which is hand glue unless Ben rules it a pretrained component (rule 1 and rule 10 open); (3) the PREFIX string, dropped on the table path (declared); (4) frozen table lookup, allowed by rule 2 and counted in size; (5) learned adapter and reader; (6) fixed 8 thinker rounds, inherited and not the model's choice; (7) exact int64 executor and hand value code, inherited; (8) learned talker. A positive T0 cannot ship under rules 1 and 10 until (2) is ruled or replaced by a learned boundary.
steps: 1. Rulings first, from Ben: the rule 7 status of the B2-family baselines (528 train rows with no program, progparse.py:199 with N_RES = 7 at progparse.py:8; PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md lines 53 and 58); whether the tokenizer alignment counts as a pretrained component; PREFIX dropped on the table path (recommended).
2. Wait for q39 (EGE 6-seed) to finish and be read, or get Ben's written permission for an early T0 run once addendum 21 is timestamped. Skip T0 if q39 is proved wrong under addendum 15.

3. Write addendum 21 before any T0 run (and before q39 is read, if early). Baseline addendum 15. List each change with its noise reason. Set M1 to M5 as in pass_marks. Name variant as report-only. State the domain rule with its 100% coverage assertion, the band overrun (+92,953) and the frozen count (134,217,728).

4. Step 0, CPU only, no training: load the EG2 text part at the revision in eg.py's EG_REV constant; assert the word table is [262144, 512] (134,217,728 values). Save it in fp32 (537 MB) or bf16 (268 MB) outside checkpoint.pt with its sha256. Check free disk first (an undated note says about 3.5 GB free; untested).

5. Build the permutation domain from train plus every dev split's pieces (not GOLD-PRIVATE, blind or protected panels; rule 5). Save the derangement (numpy RandomState(0), no fixed points) and its sha256. Assert 100% coverage of every scored split.

6. Implement the table path: one new eg_source option. Replace the single reader call site (ledger.py read(), about line 261) with an fp32 table gather and LayerNorm in fp32. Keep the B2 path byte-identical. size() must count 134,217,728 frozen for T0. CPU checks: (a) T0 step 0 output equals B2 output for the same seed; (b) trainable 3,434,833 and whole 137,652,561; (c) T0S differs from T0 only in the row map; (d) B2 build unchanged: 3,302,481 params and identical step-0 output hash.
7. Determinism: rerun B2_s202 once with the same flags (about 1.5 h at par 2). If it moves by 0.5 or more from 74.74, widen M1 or add seeds before judging.

7b. Optional cheaper tier (suggested, untested): fine-tune from the saved B2_s202 checkpoint with the table adapter for about 2,000 steps, against T0S and a zero adapter. It takes minutes of GPU. It is a different recipe, so it can screen but not decide.

8. Screen, sequential: run T0 on 202 and 203 first. Run T0S on 202 and 203 only if T0's 2-seed mean gain is at least +0.5. Record wall time, steps per second, status and nonfinite flags for every run.

9. Score with the existing scorer: pooled-5 per split, chain-5, cipher_map in_dist, donor, loops:0. Per seed: T0 minus B2, T0S minus B2, T0 minus T0S, and EGE minus T0 (report-only). Add a pre-registered report-only read split into made-up-word families and real-word families (generator shortcut check, research/data.md:44-47).
10. Decide by the table in proved_wrong.
11. If the result is identity or capacity, run T0L and the learned BPE piece channel (out of band, declared) before any content claim.
12. Confirm, only after a screen pass: T0 and T0S on 202-207 with the gates in confirm.

13. Any headline only after: a rule 7 clean baseline (the K1 lift, about +2,300 params, PLAN-AND-MARKS line 70, which means six B2 reruns, or Ben's written ruling); the rule 10 ruling on the tokenizer; and a 137,649,184-param plain transformer (d=976, L=12, V=108; count verified) on six seeds for rule 3 (about 30-60 h, suggested).

final.why: Suggested: this is the cheapest test in the Gemma area that splits EGE's +1.6/+2.1 gain (2-seed screen, RESULTS-EG2.md) into body context, piece identity and pretrained row values. T0 and T0S need no Gemma forward, so each run costs about one B2 run (shown: PC B2 seeds 202-205 took 3,595-5,638 s in results/33-pc-confirm-b2). I checked that the adapter counts reproduce (EGE +198,400 and T0 +132,352 trainable), that layer 0 reads 26.25% linear letters against 22.58% at layer 24 (LAYERS.json), and that eg.py ties the Gemma call to one site. The value is limited because EGE is unconfirmed (q39 unjudged), the screen has about 40-70% power at a true +1.5, a clean 'Gemma content' result is maybe 10-15% likely (untested guess), a positive still cannot ship until Ben rules on the Gemma tokenizer and align() (rules 1 and 10), and the PC queue is crowded (q39, then q40 T1, U0, W1, C0, 8a). So seal the marks now and run T0 right after q39 reads, T0S only if T0 passes.
final.ben_line: This test takes away Google's big Gemma brain and keeps only its word dictionary, then shuffles the dictionary as a check, so we learn whether Gemma's real word meanings help our small reader or whether any word label would do.
plan_fixes: Rulings (rule 7 status of the B2-family baseline, tokenizer alignment under rules 1 and 10, PREFIX) are listed as step 1 and as dependencies. They block shipping and headline claims, not the 2-seed screen, because every arm shares the 528-row exception and the align() glue. Say so in addendum 21 so the screen is not held up.

Dropping PREFIX on the table path is a second change, not a free declaration (suggested, untested). Gemma tokens carry their leading space, so a first word tokenised after '<bos>' alone can map to a different piece id than after 'query: '. Keep PREFIX inside align() for the screen so T0, T0S and EGE use identical piece ids, and drop it only in a later rung with its own check.

Step 13 requires a 137,649,184-param plain transformer on 6 seeds (30-60 h, suggested) as the rule-3 headline. That is the wrong comparator for this idea, since about 99% of the 134.2M frozen table rows are unused. Put the rule-3 claim on the pruned rung (R1/R2, about 4-6M whole) against a same-size plain model, and attribute the effect with B2 plus a same-shape scratch R x 512 table. Treat the 137M comparator as optional or never.

M1 is now a mean rule ('2-seed mean >= +1.0, neither seed below 0.0') whose false-pass (5-12%) and power (65-75%) are normal approximations, not simulated. Run the quick CPU simulation (seconds) before sealing and write the numbers in. State that it differs from addendum 15's pooled rule and is sealed before any T0 run.

Sequence ambiguity. T0S runs only if T0's 2-seed mean is at least +0.5, so M2 and the branch 'T0 passes M1 but T0S also passes M1' cannot be read in the other cases. Spell out in the seal what happens at T0 between +0.5 and +1.0 (tie, no T0S needed) and that M2 is judged only when T0S ran.

The T0S derangement domain is train plus all scored dev splits' pieces. That is a control built from dev prompt text (no labels, not GOLD-PRIVATE or blind, so rule 5 holds), but label it a build-time control that never ships. The shipped pruned set (R1b) must come from FineWeb-Edu counts only, with no generator vocabulary (rule 10). Report per-split UNK rates only after N is sealed.

Pruning rung (R1) risk. Frame and vocab (unseen word types 7.4% and 10.1%, and 49/636 is 7.7% by arithmetic) are the splits EGE gained on, and a pruned table sends unseen pieces to UNK. Seal frame and vocab as no-drop checks for R1 and do not assume the unseen-word story, which competes with the relation-word story (area family check).

Unproven mechanism claims must stay out of the seal. Same-word AUC 0.9998 at layer 0 is near-tautological for a lookup. Only 9 layers (0, 3, ..., 24) were probed, not 25. The 'U0 lost -3.1/-5.4' note is a progress-board number until its RESULT.json is read.

Hours of 8 cover only the screen (T0, T0S, B2_s202 rerun). Add the unpriced costs: the q39 and q40-q44 PC queue wait, the optional T0L letter-table and 416-id BPE controls, the 6-seed confirm (12 runs, about 10-25 h wall at par 2), and the 10M re-test. B2's lead over plain shrank from 3M to 10M (first-look-10m), so any gain needs a 10M retest.

Code items to test on CPU before any run. size() hard-codes frozen = N_TEXT (271,002,624) for any eg_embed model, so T0 would report 274M whole instead of 137.65M. FrozenEG.load asserts N_TEXT, so the table path must skip it. Load a pre-extracted table (or only the used rows) at train time rather than the full 271M model. Keep the table and LayerNorm in fp32 because EGK's seed-201 NaN is undiagnosed. Check that the B2 build still gives 3,302,481 params and an identical step-0 hash.

The same-seed B2_s202 rerun (about 1.5 h) is worth keeping because the PC speed varied 2.5-4x across q33 seeds and nothing measures same-seed noise. Record the PC's par setting (q33 par 3, q39 par 2) and wall time for every run.
EGE minus T0 per seed (does the body add beyond the table) and the made-up-word versus real-word family split should be written into the seal as report-only reads before q39 is opened.

idea.title: Where do variant and cipher misses come from?
idea.summary: One free-run pass over the dev misses of B2_s100/s101 splits variant (34.7% right) and cipher_map misses into four bins: gold NUM value absent from the workspace, value present but not pointed at, wrong mode, and low copy mass on the gold character. Because the executor gets exact regex int() values, a NUM miss is never a reading error. If most variant misses are program errors, no input-side change can fix variant, which decides how much richer-input work is worth doing.
idea.change: Probe only, 0 params. Baseline and seeds do not match. The 34.7 percent is the six-seed q33 mean (seeds 200-205, final_eval variant exact 31.9, 33.9, 37.1, 34.4, 35.4, 35.5). Bins are neither exhaustive nor ordered. There is no precedence rule and no 'other' bin. Copy bin (d) is not measurable as written. gen_copy returns the mixture p and the gate g only (ledger.py:239-249), so copy-only mass (1 - g) times the copy distribution must be recomputed from q_cp, k_cp and the attention, as the idea does not say. The gold character can also come from the vocabulary half of the mixture, which uses the same tied letter table, so copy mass below 0.5 does not show failed binding. 'loops:0 as the chance floor' is misnamed. Weighting per-family variant misses (seeds 200-205, 5,171 misses total, results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s20N/RESULT.json final_eval.variant.by_family) by extra.coverage (6,800 rows, 34 families) gives about 38% NUM, 27% WORD, 34% GEN. HAND-TEACHER LABELS (shown code and coverage): progparse.py:199 gives a row a program only if every step parses and there are at most 7 (N_RES=7, progparse.py:8). Otherwise progparse.py:206-208 sets mode from the answer (NUM only if the answer equals a prompt number, WORD if it is a prompt word, else GEN), and gold() (ledger.py:433-454) trains GEN rows answer-only with NOOP ops. Coverage: letter_ops 0.0% program (99.5% GEN), cipher_map 0.0% (100% GEN), fewshot_number_rule 0.0% (96% GEN), list_stats 29.0% program (37.5% GEN). PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:58 counts only the over-7-step rows (in_dist 3, answer 1, frame 2 in the small dev build; variant not given), so most no-program rows are parse failures, not length (suggested inference). The 0/240 variant zeros for letter_ops and list_stats therefore probably sit in rows without a gold program, which says little about the reader (suggested; variant coverage not reported). Bin d would then report copy-binding for rows the hand parser could not label, which is the reader story the idea wants to test. This also means answer-only training (rule 7) feeds the probe's population.

COPY BIN UNDEFINED AND ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION (shown code): gen_copy returns only (gate*p_vocab + (1-gate)*p_copy, gate) (ledger.py:239-249); the copy attention is not returned. 'Copy mass' can mean (1-g)*p_copy[gold], p_copy[gold] or the full p[gold], and each gives a different verdict. p_copy is a scatter of prompt-masked attention onto prompt character ids, so when the gold character is not in the prompt, copy mass is exactly 0. Computed answers can contain characters absent from the prompt (research/data.md:53 lists list sums, letter length and nth, and other zero-shot computations in variant; frequency in the misses untested). Bin d needs a 'gold character occurs in prompt' filter, and rows failing it reported separately.

BIN B IS READER-DEPENDENT (shown code and D0): the pointer keys for number slots come from S0, which adds the reader's pooled span over each regex digit span (ledger.py:291-296), and the keys are read at ledger.py:322 and 343. /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md:11-17 shows the pooled span mean loses digits (place 9 at 65.2-83.2%). So 'value present but not pointed at' can be an input-side failure, and the idea's premise 'a NUM miss is never a reading error' is too strong as stated.

BIN A IS NOT PURELY PROGRAM (shown code; the effect is suggested): op and operand choices read the reader through cross-attention (kvx from Xt at ledger.py:302; cross-attention in the core blocks, ledger.py:117-124). Variant introduces unseen words such as multiply, halve, child, grandchild and third..sixth (research/data.md:47). A wrong op or operand caused by an unseen word shows up as 'gold value absent' (bin a). So the stated consequence, that if most misses are program errors no input-side change can fix variant, does not follow from the bins.

BIN A IS LOOSE (shown code): 'present' means any valid slot holds the gold value (ledger.py:293-294 include constants 1, 2, 10, 100 and every prompt number, progparse.py:8). Answers equal to 1, 2, 10 or 100, or to a prompt number, are always present, so bin a can never fire for them. Check the gold program's own result slot instead, using the candidate sets (cands_a / cands_b in progparse.Builder, where any slot holding the operand is correct), and define 'first wrong step' on that basis.

REGEX LIMITS (shown code; frequency untested): NUM_RE is \d+ (progparse.py:14). It takes no sign, decimal point or comma grouping, and keeps only the first 16 numbers (progparse.py:8, 18; ledger.py:199-208). research/data.md:46 lists '-' and ',' among the prompt symbols. A prompt with -5 or 3,000 gets wrong workspace values, the gold program fails its final check ('final mismatch' in progparse), and the row is relabelled GEN. These are hand-parse failures (rule 1), not program errors, and the probe needs its own bin for them.

The brief's '1 hour per B2 run on the 5070 Ti' conflicts with the PC RESULT.json files: train_s 13,160 s (seed 200) and 15,164 s (seed 201), at 1.6-1.8 steps/s, which is about 3.7-4.2 h. The 49-minute figure is the non-PC box. The probe is unaffected, but the planning figure should be corrected before queue decisions.

[shown] loops:0 is not a stable floor. Variant loops:0 is 0.0, 5.68, 0.0, 4.17, 2.80, 0.0 over seeds 200-205, and 0.0 and 6.14 on screen seeds 100-101 (RESULT.json lesions). in_dist loops:0 reaches 10.81 on seed 201, above the leak limit of 5. Report per-seed floors, or use the donor lesion (variant 5.91 on seed 200) as the comparator.

[shown] Rule 4 conflict. The proposal calls itself a diagnosis with no claim, but its verdict is meant to decide whether richer-input work is worth doing. Two seeds are a screen. The six PC checkpoints remove the cost objection.
critiques.rescue: Revise, then run. (1) Use the six PC checkpoints B2_s200-205 (scratchpad b2ckpt, hash-verified). (2) Use the existing run(batch, gold=g) path on variant rows that have a gold program.
