It would show whether variant failures are program writing (op or pointer) or the talker, how many misses the NUM, WORD and GEN bins cover, and whether op errors cluster on unseen operator words, which would be an input-side link. Checked and holding (shown): the zero-round mode and pointer query are shared across rows (ledger.py:321-322, 342-344); letter_ops and list_stats are 0/240 on variant over six seeds (RESULT.json); the per-seed variant figures for seeds 200-205 (31.9, 33.9, 37.1, 34.4, 35.4, 35.5) match; variant is a dev split (data.py:10), so rule 5 is not breached. Not checked: the dev rows themselves (they are on the PC, not in this container), so variant gold-mode shares are estimated.

chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test, but only as a rewritten probe. It costs no training and no params, runs on the PC in minutes, and breaks none of Ben's rules (offline diagnosis, dev split only, B2 only, nothing runs at deploy time, rule 10 does not apply). It also tests the premise that decides how much of the richer-input area is worth doing: whether B2's variant misses (66% missed) are reader-reachable at all.

As written it is unsound, and all three critics agree on the fixes. I re-computed the key numbers from the six q33 RESULT.json files (shown, results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200..s205).

1. The decision logic is a non sequitur (shown, code: ledger.py:302, 313, 321-323). The executor is exact, but the op and the operand pointers are chosen by a controller that cross-attends to every reader position, and the number-slot keys include a pooled reader span (D0-RESULT: place 9 is read at 65-83%). So 'value absent' (wrong op or pointer) is not input-independent. 'If most misses are program errors, no input change can fix variant' does not follow. Only hand caps (N_RES=7, N_NUM=16, digit-only regex, |x|>=1e9, inexact DIV) are input-independent, and they need their own bin.

2. The four bins cover under half the misses (shown, computed). Weighting the 5,171 six-seed variant misses by the gold-mode shares in extra.coverage gives about 38% NUM, 27% WORD and 34% GEN. About 61% of misses are in families with no gold program at all (letter_ops 240/240 missed, digits_parity 238, object_track 237, rule_apply 237, fewshot_number_rule 233, seq_next 229, table_lookup 213, list_index 190). For those the executor is not on the path, and the question is mode, WORD pointer or GEN copy. All of that is reader-dependent by construction. Only about 35% of misses sit in program families (prog >= 50%).

3. The sharpest target is not in the idea (shown, computed). Three families that research/data.md calls recombinations expected to transfer are nearly all missed on variant, with 100% gold-program NUM coverage: table_calc 239 of 240 missed (six-seed total), div_exact 225, compare_numbers 224. They form a clean program-versus-reader test, because the gold program exists and teacher forcing is available.

4. Other fixes: wrong checkpoints (the 34.7% is the six-seed q33 mean, while s100/s101 score 32.35/34.62, and the six q33 checkpoints exist, hash-checked); the copy bin is undefined (gen_copy returns only the mixture and the gate, and copy mass is 0 when the gold char is absent from the prompt); the cipher_map leg has about 16 misses over six seeds and no variant rows, so it is noise; loops:0 is a leak floor, not chance (variant 0.0-5.7); and no precedence rule, no 'other' bin and no no-verdict zone exist.

5. Prior work is partly there (shown): diag_ledger.py already splits gold versus predicted mode and per-path hits, and extra_evals has teacher-forced versus free-run op accuracy on 400 in_dist rows (op 100, program 98 on s200), so extend those rather than write new code.

Priority for the lead: cheap and informative, but it improves nothing by itself. Its value is to stop or direct richer-input work. W1 (+0.9/+0.1), U0 (-3.1/-5.4) and EGE (variant +1.7) have already probed variant directly, so this is an attribution step, not a model change.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must seal these before any run, in CIO/PASS-MARKS.md as a new addendum. Label every claim in the write-up shown, suggested or untested.

What it can show. Shown only: counts of misses by label, per seed and pooled. The program-versus-input question stays suggested, because op and pointer choices read reader states by construction (shown in code), so a 'wrong op' count cannot say whether the cause is the reader. The probe separates hand-cap limits, program writing, free-run compounding, mode and pointer, and copy. It does not prove an input-side fix would work.

Seeds and box. Six paired checkpoints (200-205), one box, reproduction check first. Two seeds (s100/s101) would be a screen only. Bin shares move per seed (variant 31.9-37.1), so judge on pooled counts with the same label on >= 5 of 6 seeds.

Pass marks to fix now (suggested starting values for Ben to adjust before the run):
- Hand-cap finding: rows labelled (0) hold >= 25% of variant misses on >= 5 of 6 seeds. Then the next step is a rule-clean change to the caps (tool calls or learned mechanisms), not an input change.
- Op-writing bottleneck: teacher-forced op accuracy on variant gold-program rows < 90% on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
- Talker bottleneck: teacher-forced pointer or mode accuracy < 90% on >= 5 of 6 seeds.
- Free-run compounding: teacher-forced program accuracy >= 90% and free-run program accuracy <= 70%.
- Input-link supported (suggested): unseen-word op error rate >= 1.5x the seen-word rate on the six-seed pool. Proved wrong: <= 1.2x.
- Copy finding: copy-only mass on the gold char < 0.5 for >= 50% of GEN misses among rows whose gold char occurs in the prompt, with the first wrong register logged.
- Any outcome between these gets 'no verdict, diagnosis only'. A verdict about input work needs a later six-seed screen.

Rules to flag in the plan.
- Rule 7: the probe must report how many misses sit in rows trained answer-only (progparse.py:199, 528 rows over 7 steps in the sealed build, plus parse-failed rows). It must not be used to justify answer-only fallbacks.
- Rule 5: variant is a dev split and may be scored, but it already steers ST1's training kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS:84). Any fix chosen from these bins must be tested on fresh held-out kinds, not on variant again.
- Rule 10: the probe is offline and adds no deploy step. If it shows the hand caps or the regex bind, the fix must be a tool the model calls by writing text or a learned part, not a new hand parser.
- Rule 9: B2 only, no village claims.
- Do not read 'loops:0' as chance. Report it per seed beside each bin.

Scale of work. About 1-2 h of coding (extend diag_ledger.py plus the gold-forced path), a few minutes of PC compute per checkpoint (no training; the earlier '1 h per B2 run' figure is wrong, since PC training runs took about 3.7-4.2 h and are not needed here). Dev rows are on the PC, not in this container, and torch is needed.

Leads for the write-up (shown, computed from the six RESULT.json files): table_calc 239/240, div_exact 225/240 and compare_numbers 224/240 variant rows missed (six-seed totals). They are the cleanest tests and should be reported first. After this probe, W1/U0/EGE (already run) plus its attribution tell the lead whether any remaining input-side work targets a real share of the variant gap.

plan.title: Variant-miss map: where B2's variant misses first go wrong
plan.ben_line: When the model misses a hard test question, we want to know which step broke: writing the steps, picking the right number, or writing the answer. This check only reads six finished models and changes none of them.
plan.question: On the six finished B2 runs (seeds 200-205), at which stage does each variant miss first go wrong (hand-parser limit, answer mode, program step, answer pointer, word pointer or written answer), and do op or pointer errors on program rows cluster on rows that use words never seen in training?
plan.one_change: Add one read-only labelling pass, a new file custom_io/variant_miss_map.py, that puts every B2 variant miss into one fixed bin, using the official talk() output path and gold-forced re-runs. No training, no edit to ledger.py or the data, 0 new parameters. Do not extend diag_ledger.py: its written-answer path calls readout() and skips the copy mixture that talk() uses (shown: diag_ledger.py paths(); ledger.py:365-366 vs talk() at 380-406). B2 is copy=True (shown: RESULT.json config), so diag_ledger's written answers would not match the official path.
arms: A. Free run on the official path (shown code): run(batch), then talk(..., return_modes=True) on the same tensors. Must reproduce the stored final_eval counts (gate M0).
B. Gold-forced run: run(batch, gold=model.gold(rows,'cpu')) on variant rows that have a gold program. Per-step op and pointer accuracy over gold-program positions only, plus whole-program accuracy.

C. Talker check on the gold-forced workspace: argmax lmode against the gold mode; argmax lans inside the gold answer slots (NUM rows); argmax lword inside the gold word set (WORD rows); first wrong written register and copy-only mass (GEN rows).
D. Input-link split (correlational): within each family, step errors on program rows whose prompt has a word type absent from the train prompts, against the rest.
E. Reference only, from RESULT.json, not re-run: noexec variant 16.3-18.5 and loops:0 variant 0.0-5.7 per seed (shown). Report beside every bin.
plan.seeds: Six paired q33 seeds, 200-205, all trained on one PC data build (the config data path is identical in each RESULT.json), so they share the same 1,320 variant rows. Seeds are model replicates, not new rows. Screen seeds 100 and 101 (another box) are not used. Checkpoints: scratchpad code/b2ckpt/B2_s20N/checkpoint.pt. sha256 checked here for s200 and s205; the other four have .sha256 files that were not re-checked. Rule 9: B2 only.
plan.machine: BensPC (5070 Ti box), CPU float32 first. Use its GPU with amp only if gate M0 fails, and only when GPU-BUSY.txt shows it free (PC-JOB.md convention). The M1 Pro can run the CPU path if the dev build is copied there. No training run.
pass_marks: M0 Reproduction gate, before any bin is reported: on each seed the variant correct count is within +-3 rows of RESULT.json (421, 448, 490, 454, 467, 469) and the in_dist count within +-5 rows of its RESULT.json value. If any seed fails: report no bins, retry once on GPU amp with evalx.evaluate's order (sorted by prompt length, batch 128); if it fails again, stop.

M1 Hand limit (suggested; threshold is judgement): labels (0a)-(0g) defined in step 4 together hold at least 25% of variant misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds. If so, the finding is that the teacher's parser and caps limit the score, and the next step is a rule-clean fix (a tool the model calls by writing text, or a learned mechanism), not an input change. Labels depend only on the row, so the same rows recur on every seed: the seed clause is one test, not six.

M2 Program writing (suggested): on variant rows with a gold program, teacher-forced op accuracy over gold-program positions only is below 90% on at least 5 of 6 seeds. (Do not use extra_evals' existing op figure: it counts all 7 positions including trailing NOOPs, ledger.py:578-582.)

M3 Talker or pointer (report both parts): on the gold-forced workspace, NUM-gold rows with argmax lans inside the gold answer slots below 90%, or argmax lmode equal to the gold mode below 90% over all rows, on at least 5 of 6 seeds.
M4 Free-run compounding: pooled over six seeds, teacher-forced whole-program accuracy at least 90% and free-run whole-program accuracy at 70% or below.

M5 Input link (suggested): within family, the teacher-forced op-or-pointer error rate on program rows with at least one word type absent from the train prompts is at least 1.5 times the rate on other rows, pooled over six seeds, with at least 30 error events in each cell. Proved wrong: at most 1.2 times, with at least 30 events in each cell. Anything else, including fewer than 30 events in a cell: no verdict.

M6 Copy (suggested; GEN misses only; cipher_map excluded): among GEN-gold misses whose gold character occurs in the prompt, at least 50% have copy-only mass below 0.5 at the first wrong written register. Report the mixture probability of the gold character beside it.

Bin precedence, fixed before the run; each miss gets exactly one bin: (0) hand-cap or parse flag; (1) predicted mode differs from gold; (2a) wrong op at the first wrong program step; (2b) wrong operand pointer at that step; (3) NUM-gold answer pointer wrong or invalid; (4) WORD-gold pointer wrong; (5) GEN first wrong register; (6) other. M2, M3 and M4 can all fire, so outcomes are not exclusive. Any result between thresholds is 'diagnosis only, no input-side verdict'.
plan.proved_wrong: The descriptive claim that most variant misses are step-writing errors (a wrong op or operand at the first wrong step) is proved wrong if on at least 5 of 6 seeds fewer than half of program-row misses have their first wrong step at (2a) or (2b). The claim that the caps explain variant (M1) is proved wrong if (0) holds under 10% of misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds. The input-link claim is proved wrong at M5's 1.2x line. The probe cannot show that an input change would or would not fix variant. The inference that 'program errors mean no input change can help' is not supported, because the op and pointer heads read the reader through cross-attention (shown: ledger.py:302, 321-324).
plan.null_risk: The probe changes no model, so a pass can only come from the labels, the reader or proxy shares, not from a fix. (a) M2 can fire from reader-driven op errors, since the op head reads the reader (ledger.py:302, 321-323). M2 is therefore not proof of a program-side bottleneck. M5 is the only reader route, and it is correlational with untested power. (b) M1 can fire because the teacher's parser cannot label a row. That is a teacher failure, which the bin exists to expose, but it is not a model failure. Repo facts: only 16 rows of the big in_dist build (6,800) exceed 7 steps (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:58), so N_RES alone is small. The share of variant misses that have steps but no program is untested, because variant rows are on the PC. (c) The coverage shares come from the big in_dist build (200 rows per family; RESULT.json extra.coverage), not from variant. The statement that 3,137 of 5,171 six-seed variant misses (60.7%) sit in zero-program families is my arithmetic on that proxy (shown: RESULT.json by_family plus coverage), not a measurement on variant rows. (d) Variant has 40 rows per family, so one row moves a family share by 2.5 points. Use pooled counts for verdicts. Binomial noise on a 38% bin share over about 870 misses per seed is about +-1.6 points if rows were independent (suggested; they are fixed, so this is optimistic). (e) in_dist is not a clean reference for every family. table_calc is 65.4% in_dist over six seeds and 0.4% on variant. Other pairs show the variant gap: div_exact 100.0 vs 6.2, compare_numbers 100.0 vs 6.7, list_stats 89.2 vs 0.0, letter_ops 95.4 vs 0.0 (all shown, RESULT.json by_family). (f) cipher_map is dropped: its copy gate value is 0.99995 (shown, RESULT.json extra.copy_gate) and it has no variant rows. Overall: an M1 or M2 pass needs no model change to occur, so treat it as a labelling finding, not a fix. M0 is a gate and should pass.
plan.autonomy: This is offline analysis of already-trained checkpoints. It adds no step, parameter, data source or prompt to the shipped model. The shipped path is the model's own free run, the same run() and talk() calls the eval already makes. Hand code already on that path (progparse.py:8-18 caps and number regex; ledger.py:199-209 spans; ledger.py:61-63 caps) is shared with the shipped model and is what the probe is meant to expose (rule 1 concern, not new). Gold programs (progparse.row_targets) label misses and force prefixes in the diagnostic only, never at deploy. Deploy consequence: if M1 fires, the response must not be a larger hand cap on the answer path (N_NUM 16, N_RES 7, NUM_RE, W_MAX 64, GEN_MAX 8). It must be a model mechanism or a tool the model calls by writing text (rules 1 and 10). Any input-side change the probe motivates is a new training run and needs its own sealed marks. Rule 5 note: variant is a dev split and may be scored, but it already steers ST1's training kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:84), so any fix chosen from these bins must be tested on fresh held-out kinds.
steps: Seal addendum 21 in custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md before the run. (Addendum 20 is the last in that file, shown.) Include marks M0-M6, the bin precedence, the denominators (variant rows and misses per seed), the no-verdict rule, and the note that variant steers ST1. Ben approves the sealed text before any run.
Write custom_io/variant_miss_map.py as a new file. Leave diag_ledger.py and ledger.py unchanged. Load each checkpoint with load_model (models/__init__.py:28-32), eval mode, no_grad, CPU float32.

Free run: o = run(batch); pred from talk(tuple(o[k] for k in R, vals, valid, lmode, lans, lword), batch, return_modes=True) (ledger.py:380-406), with evalx.evaluate's length-sorted batching (evalx.py:37-51). Score with is_hit on accepted answers (evalx.py:19-20).
Gate M0 on variant and in_dist per seed and record the counts. Do not bin anything if the gate fails.

Gold labels per variant row: progparse.program_for(r) for the parse reason (progparse.py:169-182); row_targets(r) for prog, mode, ans, word (progparse.py:188-209). Hand-cap flags: (0a) row has steps but no program (rule-7 answer-only rows; gold() trains them with NOOP ops, ledger.py:433-454); (0b) more than 7 program steps (progparse.py:8, 199); (0c) more than 16 prompt numbers (progparse.py:18); (0d) prompt matches a fixed proxy for number-format misses, -\d or \d[.,]\d; (0e) gold value 1e9 or more, or inexact DIV (ledger.py:62, 83-86); (0f) gold word only beyond W_MAX=64 (ledger.py:209, progparse.py:8); (0g) gold answer longer than 8 chars (ledger.py:63, 447-448). Rows with no steps at all are reported separately as by design, not in (0). Also report how many variant gold answers exceed 8 chars (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:59 lists none for variant, untested here).

Free-run step labels: for each step t the op, both pointers, and the executed value at slot R0+t-1 (run() returns steps, vals, valid; ledger.py:324-342). A step is correct if op equals gold op_t and the pointers are in cands_a and cands_b (COMM ops may swap, progparse.py:12). First wrong step = first t that is not correct.

Gold-forced run: run(batch, gold=model.gold(rows,'cpu')) (ledger.py:433, 278). Score op and pointer at step t from the unmasked step logits (ledger.py:324), counting only t up to the gold program length. Report whole-program accuracy (M4).
Talker check on the forced workspace: argmax lmode vs gold mode; argmax lans vs gold ans slots (NUM rows); argmax lword vs gold word set (WORD rows).

GEN rows: gold written registers are gold()['gen'] (units-first, ledger.py:447-448). First wrong register = first index where argmax of the gen_copy mixture differs from gold. Copy-only mass on the gold character = p_mix[gold] - g*p_vocab[gold], using the mixture p and gate g returned by gen_copy (ledger.py:239-249) and p_vocab = softmax(readout(R)) (ledger.py:365-366). This equals (1-g)*p_copy[gold] by the identity in gen_copy. Count only rows whose gold character occurs in the prompt; report the rest separately.

Bin each miss once using the fixed precedence in pass_marks, per seed and pooled, per family (33 variant families, 40 rows each per seed), with noexec and loops:0 per seed beside it (RESULT.json lesions).

Input link (M5): build the train-prompt word-type set on the PC from the train prompts (not from the generator; research/data.md:46-47 gives the counts for context: 63 unseen alphabetic types in variant, shown). Flag variant program rows containing such a type. Compare teacher-forced step error rates within family, with counts.

Run the six checkpoints on the PC CPU. Write results/variant-miss-map/ JSON per seed and one summary. Apply M0-M6 exactly as sealed. Label every claim shown, suggested or untested, and add one plain-language line for Ben.

shown: Data identity is asserted, not shown. config.data is the same PC work data path in all six seed RESULT.json files, but none records data_manifest_sha256 (count 0 for seeds 200-205). shown: The plan says only seeds 200 and 205 had their checkpoint hashes checked. All six now match their .sha256 files (checked here). Use all six in the seal.

shown (arithmetic on in_dist proxy): The descriptive claim is tested only on program-row misses. Using RESULT.json extra.coverage.by_family, 3,137 of 5,171 six-seed variant misses (60.7%) sit in families with 0% program coverage, and 1,794 (34.7%) in the 14 program families. shown: Bin (0) merges teacher-parser failures (progparse.program_for reasons such as 'unparsed step', 'final mismatch', 'no ops'; progparse.py:168-182) with length caps. The M1 test ('caps explain variant') cannot separate parser coverage from model-side caps. Split (0p) parser from (0c) caps.

shown: The M2 and M4 priors already exist. RESULT.json extra.op_acc (400 in_dist program rows, ledger.py:547-582) gives teacher-forced op 99.96-100.0 with NOOPs counted, and program 97.0-98.25 teacher-forced vs 97.0-98.25 free-run. There is no compounding gap on in_dist, so M4's free-run drop is a variant-only prediction and should be stated as one. M2 at 90% is unlikely to fire if op generalises as it does on in_dist.

shown + suggested: M5, the only input-link test, is confounded. The unseen real variant words include operation words (multiply, halve, third..sixth; research/data.md:46-47 gives variant 63 of 606 unseen alphabetic types, 35 of them real words). Rows with an unseen word are often rows with an unseen operation word, so M5 measures semantic novelty in the thinker more than reader failure. B2's reader reads letters at 99.85% linear (results/eg-diag/DIAG.json P1, held-out train-like text, not variant), so an unseen word is probably not an unseen letter input (suggested). Stratify: made-up tokens with no operation word against rows with neither.

shown: M5's floor of at least 30 error events pooled over six seeds counts each row up to six times, since the rows are the same on every seed. Use distinct rows and a row-level bootstrap. The number of distinct variant program rows with an unseen type is untested and may be below 30, which would make M5 no-verdict by construction. Count it in the label pass (G0).

shown: The confirm judges any change on variant, the same panel used to diagnose it. variant already steered ST1's training kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:84). Use variant as a diagnostic only and judge any change on fresh held-out kinds.

shown: Mark wording problems. M3 is an OR of two conditions, so either part can fire alone. M4 has no denominator. M1's 5-of-6-seed clause is effectively one test because labels depend only on rows (the plan says so). M2's 90% and M1's 25% are judgement thresholds. Make M3 two verdicts, M4 on has-program rows only, and M1 a row-level share with an interval.

shown: Predicted mode is ambiguous. talk() returns decoded modes that fall back to GEN when a NUM or WORD pointer is invalid (ledger.py:380-406). Bin (1) must use the decoded mode; the M3 mode check must use argmax lmode from the forced run. Specify both.

shown: gold() gives NOOP ops and slot-0 pointers to has=False rows (ledger.py:433-454). Gold-forced talker checks are meaningful only where the forced workspace equals the gold computation, so restrict them to has-program rows or state the workspace used for no-program rows. GEN targets are -100 where unused, so the first-wrong-register check must ignore them and count EOS.

suggested: First wrong step is scored against one canonical program (progparse program_for). Other valid programs, such as the inverse-op rewrite the plan mentions for L1, would count as step errors; only COMM swaps are accepted (progparse.py:12). Hand-check a sample of (2a) and (2b) bins before any verdict.

shown: Variant is not checked for more than 7 steps, more than 16 numbers, or answers over 8 characters. PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:58-59 gives in_dist, answer and frame counts only (16/11/17 rows over 7 steps on the big build). The label pass fixes this before any run.

shown: The probe's baseline already breaks rule 7. progparse.py (about line 199) gives answer-only training to the 528 train rows with more than N_RES=7 steps (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:58). Say so in the seal, since bin (0c) counts the same rows. Lifting N_RES is a rule-7 fix that also needs more loops than n_loops=8 (untested).

shown: The plan's talk() call is shorthand. Use model.state(batch) (ledger.py:359-362), which returns six items when span is False (the B2 default, ledger.py:130), then talk(..., return_modes=True). Use evalx.evaluate's batching exactly (evalx.py:37-51: length-sorted, batch 128, Dataset strict=False), since batch composition changes bf16 results.
shown: variant_miss_map.py does not exist yet (checked). diag_ledger.py exists, and its paths() uses readout() with no copy mixture (diag_ledger.py:18-25), so not extending it is right.
shown: The plan's 2.5 hours is low. The label pass takes about 1 h, the script plus M0 debugging 2-3 h, and approval and re-seal time sit outside the estimate. Use 5 hours.

suggested (cheaper, untested): The probe cannot give an input verdict, as the plan says. A minimal-pair probe on B2, with no training, would answer Ben's question more directly: the same program with the operation word swapped for a seen synonym, against an unseen word whose meaning the prompt defines. That separates word novelty from operation semantics. Hand-written test items are allowed, since rule 1 covers tests and scoring.
shown: Machine and queue. q39 (EGE 6-seed) is staged on the PC (queue_local/39) and may hold the GPU, so check GPU-BUSY.txt (PC-JOB.md convention). CPU work also slows queue jobs.

shown checks that hold: variant correct counts 421, 448, 490, 454, 467, 469 (sum 2,749 of 7,920; 5,171 misses; 830-899 per seed); in_dist counts 1231, 1245, 1221, 1238, 1219, 1233; 1,320 variant rows = 33 families x 40; noexec variant 215-244 (16.3-18.5%); loops:0 variant 0.0-5.7%; PASS-MARKS addendum 20 is the last addendum; 63 unseen variant types; 16 big-build in_dist rows over 7 steps; ST1 names kinds from variant (PLAN-AND-MARKS:84). The +/-1.6-point binomial figure is arithmetic-correct but optimistic, because the rows are fixed.

fixed_plan.title: Variant-miss map, fixed: label pass first, then a CUDA bf16 gate and row-level six-seed bins
fixed_plan.ben_line: When the model misses a hard test question, we want to know which step failed first: reading the question, writing the steps, or writing the answer. First we count what can be labelled from the test rows alone. Then we re-score the six finished models the same way the official score was made, and we change nothing in them.
fixed_plan.question: On the six finished B2 runs (seeds 200-205), where does each variant miss first go wrong (parser or cap label, decoded mode, program op, program pointer, answer pointer, word pointer, written answer, or no program by design), and do errors cluster on rows with a word the model never saw in training once operation words are separated out? Diagnosis only; no input-side verdict is drawn.
fixed_plan.one_change: One new read-only analysis file, custom_io/variant_miss_map.py, plus a label-only pass over the variant rows. No training, no edit to ledger.py, data or checkpoints, 0 new parameters.
arms: A0 Label-only pass, no model, no GPU: per variant row, the program_for reason (progparse.py:168-182), cap flags (0b-0g), gold mode, has-program flag, whether steps exist, and whether the row has an unseen word type (word-type set from the train build), and if so whether that type is an operation word. Output counts before any model run.

A1 Reproduction on the official numeric path: CUDA with torch.autocast bf16 around the eval, as train.py:132 and final_eval (train.py:65-85) do, with evalx.evaluate batching (length-sorted, batch 128, Dataset strict=False; evalx.py:37-51). CPU float32 is a sensitivity run only.

A2 Free run: model.state(batch) then talk(..., return_modes=True) (ledger.py:359-362, 380-406). First wrong program step per has-program row: op equals gold op and pointers fall in the candidate sets, with COMM swaps allowed.

A3 Gold-forced run on has-program rows only: run(batch, gold=model.gold(rows,'cpu')) (ledger.py:278, 433). Op and pointer accuracy over gold-program positions with NOOP excluded, plus whole-program accuracy.

A4 Talker on the forced workspace: argmax lmode vs gold mode (not the decoded mode); argmax lans vs gold answer slots on NUM rows; argmax lword vs gold word on WORD rows; first wrong GEN register (ignore -100 targets, count EOS) and copy-only mass from gen_copy (ledger.py:239-249).

A5 Word-novelty link, stratified: within family, has-program rows with an unseen made-up token and no operation word, against has-program rows with neither. Report distinct-row counts and a Mantel-Haenszel ratio with a row-level bootstrap.
A6 Reference only, from RESULT.json: noexec and loops:0 variant per seed, and per-family variant correct counts.
fixed_plan.seeds: Six paired q33 seeds 200-205, checkpoints under code/b2ckpt (all six sha256 checks pass here). The seeds are replicates on the same 1,320 variant rows (33 families x 40). Verdicts are row-level (bootstrap over rows), with per-seed numbers reported beside them. Record the sha256 of the PC dev and train jsonl files and the variant row-id list at run time, because RESULT.json has no data manifest hash. Seeds 100 and 101 are not used.
fixed_plan.machine: BensPC (5070 Ti). A0 runs anywhere the PC dev and train builds are. A1 runs on the GPU in CUDA bf16 first, then the CPU fp32 sensitivity run. Use the GPU only when GPU-BUSY.txt shows it free (PC-JOB.md convention). No training run.
pass_marks: G0 (before any model run, from A0): report variant program coverage, the number of distinct variant has-program rows containing an unseen word type, and the number of rows with steps but no program. If fewer than 30 distinct rows contain an unseen type, M5 is declared no-verdict in advance.

M0 reproduction on the CUDA bf16 path, per seed: variant correct within +/-3 of 421, 448, 490, 454, 467, 469, and in_dist within +/-5 of 1231, 1245, 1221, 1238, 1219, 1233. If this fails, report no bins and stop. A CPU fp32 mismatch alone is reported, not a stop.

Bin precedence, each miss in exactly one bin, fixed now: (0p) parser failure (program_for reason other than ok); (0c) cap flags (0b more than 7 steps, 0c more than 16 numbers, 0d number-format proxy, 0e value 1e9 or more or inexact DIV, 0f word beyond W_MAX 64, 0g answer over 8 chars); (1) decoded mode differs from gold; (2a) wrong op at the first wrong program step; (2b) wrong pointer at that step; (3) NUM answer pointer wrong; (4) WORD pointer wrong; (5) GEN first wrong register; (Z) no gold program and no steps, reported separately; (7) other.
M1 (suggested): (0p)+(0c) at least 25% of ALL misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds = limit found. Proved wrong: under 10% of all misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds.

M2 (suggested): teacher-forced op accuracy over gold-program positions (NOOP excluded), has-program rows only, below 90% on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Prior: in_dist teacher-forced op 99.96-100.0 with NOOPs counted (RESULT.json extra.op_acc; in_dist, not variant).

M3 (suggested; two separate verdicts, no OR): (a) NUM-gold rows with argmax lans inside the gold answer slots below 90%; (b) argmax lmode equal to gold mode below 90% over all rows. Each needs at least 5 of 6 seeds.

M4 (suggested): on has-program rows only, teacher-forced whole-program accuracy at least 90% and free-run at 70% or below, with a row-level bootstrap interval excluding the thresholds. Prior: in_dist teacher-forced and free-run both 97.0-98.25, so no gap on in_dist.

M5 (suggested; reframed): Mantel-Haenszel ratio of op-or-pointer error rate, unseen made-up token with no operation word vs neither, over has-program rows. Supported if the ratio's lower bound is above 1.5, with at least 30 distinct rows per arm. Proved wrong if the upper bound is below 1.2 with at least 30 distinct rows per arm. Otherwise no verdict.

M6 (suggested): among GEN-gold misses whose gold character is in the prompt, at least 50% have copy-only mass below 0.5 at the first wrong register, on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Report the mixture probability of the gold character beside it.
Descriptive claim, sealed: most variant misses are step-writing errors (2a plus 2b). Proved wrong if (2a)+(2b) are under 50% of ALL variant misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: The claim that caps explain variant is proved wrong if (0p)+(0c) is under 10% of all misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds. The claim that step writing dominates is proved wrong if (2a)+(2b) is under 50% of all variant misses on at least 5 of 6 seeds. The input-link claim is proved wrong if M5's ratio upper bound is below 1.2 with at least 30 distinct rows per arm. The probe cannot prove that an input change would or would not fix variant; it can only say where each miss first appears.
fixed_plan.null_risk: (a) Most variant misses may sit in zero-program families (in_dist proxy: 60.7%, shown arithmetic; variant untested). They land in bins (1), (3), (4), (5) or (6), so without bin Z the report misstates where the errors are. (b) M2 and M4 can fire from reader-driven errors, because the op and pointer heads read the reader through cross-attention (ledger.py:302, 321-324). (c) M5 is confounded by operation words (multiply, halve, third..sixth) and by a reader that already reads letters at 99.85% linear on train-like text (DIAG P1); it measures semantic novelty in the thinker more than input failure (suggested). (d) Pooling error events over six seeds treats one row as six events; verdicts use distinct rows. (e) Label coverage on variant is untested; G0 is the cheapest check. (f) Labels use one canonical program, so valid alternative programs can be scored as step errors (suggested). (g) B2 only; any fix must be tested on fresh held-out kinds not in variant, since variant already steered ST1's kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:84).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Offline analysis of existing checkpoints. It adds no step, parameter, prompt or data source to the shipped model. The shipped path is the model's own free run (run and talk). Gold programs are labels and forced prefixes in the diagnostic only, never at deploy. The hand parsers (progparse caps, number regex, word_spans) are on the shipped path and are what the probe is meant to expose (a rule 1 concern, not new). Any fix the bins motivate must be a model mechanism or a tool the model calls by writing text, and must not be a larger hand cap (rules 1, 7, 10).
steps: Ben approves a sealed addendum 21 in custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md before any run. It holds the bin definitions and precedence (0p, 0c, 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5, Z, 7), the M0 path (CUDA bf16 first), the row-level bootstrap rule, the distinct-row floors, the operation-word stratification for M5, and the descriptive claim on all misses. Addendum 20 is the last one (shown).
Write custom_io/variant_miss_map.py as a new file. Leave ledger.py, data and diag_ledger.py untouched (diag_ledger.py:18-25 skips the copy mixture).

Run A0, the label-only pass, on the PC dev and train builds (no model, no GPU). Record the dev and train sha256 and the variant row-id list. Re-seal before continuing if the counts differ from 1,320 rows in 33 families of 40.
On seed 200 only, run A1 on CUDA bf16 with evalx.evaluate batching. Apply gate M0. If it fails, stop and report; do not bin.
If M0 passes on seed 200, run seeds 201-205 on the same path. Run the CPU fp32 pass as a sensitivity check only.

Free run per seed through model.state and talk(..., return_modes=True). Take the first wrong step per has-program row, and assign each miss to one bin by the fixed precedence, with Z for rows that have no gold program and no steps.

Gold-forced run through model.gold and run(batch, gold=...) on has-program rows only. Op and pointer accuracy on gold-program positions with NOOP excluded; argmax lmode vs gold; NUM and WORD talker checks; first wrong GEN register ignoring -100 and counting EOS.

Run A5. Build the train word-type set from the train build; flag variant has-program rows with an unseen made-up token and no operation word; report distinct-row counts and the Mantel-Haenszel ratio with a row-level bootstrap.
Write results/variant-miss-map/ JSON per seed and one summary. Apply M0 to M6 exactly as sealed. Label every claim shown, suggested or untested, and add one plain-language line for Ben.

If a mark fires, the next step is a new sealed design, not an edit to this file. If M2 or M4 fire without M5, the candidate is a program-side change (for example lifting N_RES for the 528 answer-only train rows, which is also the rule-7 fix). If M1 fires, a cap change sealed under rules 1 and 7. If M3 fires, a pointer change. If M5 is supported, a reader-side change judged on fresh held-out kinds, not variant.
files_to_touch: custom_io/variant_miss_map.py (new; PC repo)
custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md (new addendum 21, sealed before any run; addendum 20 is the last one)
custom_io/results/variant-miss-map/ (new JSON per seed plus summary)
read only: custom_io/models/ledger.py (run 278; state 359-362; gen_copy 239-249; readout 365-366; talk 380-406; gold 433-454; extra_evals 547-582)
read only: custom_io/models/progparse.py (constants 8 and 12; prompt_numbers 17-18; program_for 168-182; row_targets 188-209; N_RES check near 199)
read only: custom_io/evalx.py (is_hit 19-20; evaluate 37-51; _dev_rows 136-138)
read only: custom_io/train.py (amp 132; final_eval 65-85)
read only: results/33-pc-confirm-b2/B2_s200 to B2_s205/RESULT.json (reference counts, lesions, extra)
read only: code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 to B2_s205/checkpoint.pt (all six sha256 checked)
not touched: custom_io/diag_ledger.py (paths() skips the copy mixture, lines 18-25)
fixed_plan.depends_on: PC dev and train builds in the PC work data folder, torch on the PC, and the six checkpoints. Does not wait for queue 39 (EGE 6-seed) or any other queued run. Needs Ben's approval of the sealed addendum 21 before step 4.
fixed_plan.confirm: No confirm for the probe itself. A fired bin only chooses the next sealed design; it does not change this file. If M2 or M4 fire without M5, the candidate is a program-side change, such as lifting N_RES for the 528 answer-only train rows (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:58), which also fixes rule 7; it needs a loop-budget and size check (untested). If M1 fires, a cap change sealed under rules 1 and 7. If M3 fires, a pointer change. If M5 is supported, a reader-side change judged on six seeds against B2 on fresh held-out kinds not in variant, with pooled-5 and chain-5 marks sealed beforehand.

final.why: It is nearly free in GPU time (minutes of eval on six finished checkpoints, no training, 0 params) and breaks none of Ben's rules (offline, dev split only, B2 only, six seeds, rule 10 not touched). It attacks B2's biggest gap, the 66% variant miss, which W1, U0 and EGE did not explain. The per-seed variant counts 421/448/490/454/467/469 match the six q33 RESULT.json files (shown), and the in_dist coverage proxy puts about 61% of misses in families with no gold program (suggested, untested on variant), so the "which stage broke first" map decides whether the reader, the talker/mode/copy path or the program is the place to work. The fixed plan is still over-built: the probe cannot separate reader from program, because the op and pointer heads cross-attend to the reader (shown in code), so it directs the next design and does not settle the input question. Seal a trimmed core and run it when the PC is free of q39, ahead of any new input-side training run.
final.ben_line: This check looks at the six finished models and finds which step breaks first when they miss the new-wording questions, so we know where to put effort before spending GPU time on anything new.
plan_fixes: The descriptive claim '(2a)+(2b) are at least 50% of ALL variant misses' is refuted by construction. Only about 35% of misses sit in program families and about 61% in zero-program families (in_dist proxy, suggested). Restate it over program-family misses only, or report every bin as a share of its own population (program, WORD, GEN, NUM-pointer, Z) and drop the all-misses claim.

Replace the '>= 5 of 6 seeds' clauses in M1, M2 and M3 with pooled distinct-row counts and a row-level bootstrap. The same 1,320 variant rows recur on every seed, so the seed clause is one test, not six. Report per-seed numbers beside the pooled one.

Demote M5 (unseen-word link) to descriptive. It is confounded by unseen operation words (multiply, halve, third..sixth). Distinct has-program rows with an unseen made-up token and no operation word may be under 30, so G0 has to count them first and declare it no-verdict if so. Do not let M5 drive any input-side decision.

State plainly in the seal that the map cannot say whether an input change would help. A bin result only chooses the next sealed design. If the lead wants an actual reader-versus-program separator, add one later: a hand-written minimal-pair test (the same program with a seen operation word versus an unseen one). That is untested and is a separate change.

Cut bins and marks to what the decision needs: 0p/0c, decoded-mode, op, pointer, NUM answer pointer, WORD pointer, GEN register, Z, other. Keep M0, a hand-limit mark, one program-writing mark with a free-run versus gold-forced compounding check, and one talker mark. Drop the Mantel-Haenszel machinery unless G0 shows enough rows.

Hand-check a sample (for example 30 rows) of (2a) and (2b) misses against the model's actual program. A different valid program (other than a COMM swap) is scored as a step error against the single canonical program_for output, and that would inflate the step-writing share.

M0 is a gate and has to pass first: CUDA bf16 with evalx.evaluate batching (length-sorted, batch 128), because the official scores were made under bf16 autocast. A CPU fp32 mismatch is reported, not a stop. Use the PC GPU only when GPU-BUSY.txt shows it free. q39 (EGE 6-seed) is staged on the PC and the CPU run may slow it.

Record the sha256 of the PC dev and train jsonl files and the variant row-id list, because RESULT.json has no data manifest hash. Without them 'same 1,320 rows on all six seeds' rests only on the M0 count gate.

Variant is a dev split that already steers ST1's training kinds (PLAN-AND-MARKS:84). Any fix chosen from these bins must be judged on fresh held-out kinds, not on variant again. Report the rule-7 answer-only exposure (528 train rows over 7 steps) and how many variant misses are in parser-failed or answer-only rows, so the probe does not read as a defence of the cap.

The 5-hour estimate is agent and engineering time, not GPU time. Ben has to approve addendum 21 before any run, so budget the approval wait separately. Addendum 20 is the last one in PASS-MARKS.md (checked).

idea.title: Reach-demand probes on trained B2 and W1 checkpoints
idea.summary: Four zero-training readouts decide whether a trained B2 uses anything beyond about +-2..4 letters: a gradient profile over offsets -6..+6, a one-letter occlusion map by distance from digits against a noise floor, exact match on copied words binned by length, and controller attention mass by region. A new fifth readout reads W1's learned attention by offset on the archived W1 checkpoints. Results gate every reach idea (dilation, depthwise, relative bias, kernel-3).
idea.change: Probe only. (a) Gradient norm of X[t0] w.r.t. input at t0+k, k=-6..6, on the 3 prompts in eg.py:25, normalised to k=0 (reader.py:82-96). (b) About 850 dev rows (25 per family), swap each letter, count answer changes (talk(state(...))); far = letters > 4 chars from any digit span; floor = swaps inside held-out frame openers. (c) Exact match for copy_word/WORD rows by copied-word length (<=5, 6-9, >=10), >= 60 rows per bin; plus gradient mass at >= 5 chars on GEN rows against a wrong-gold null. (d) Controller cross-attention recomputed for 8 rounds (reader columns start at 27), mass on digit / near-digit / word / far. (e) W1 GlobalAttn weights by |i-j| on cipher rows (reader.py:54-65).
idea.why: The window is +-4 by construction (two k=5 blocks), but use is unmeasured. R0's loss mixes reach with 19.9% fewer params; the kernel-3 option would free 262,144 params (B2 would drop to 3,040,337, below the 3,147,208 floor and need reinvestment). W1 gained only +0.9/+0.1 with lookup families -4.1; attention maps show whether its head learned local binding at all.

evidence.claim: Receptive field is two kernel-5 blocks (+-4); kernel size is not a Ledger knob; each block is 328,448 params.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Cipher letter and digit sit two characters apart ('h=2'); R0 cipher_map 2-12% vs B2 96-100%.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: W1: pooled +0.9 and +0.1 over B2 (mark +1.0), lookup-family pool F1 -4.1 (limit -2.0), chain-5 99.6/99.9.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: W1_s200/s201, U0, C0 and T1 checkpoint.pt archives (seeds 200/201) exist as split tar parts; results files are not in the project folder.
evidence.label: shown
evidence.source: PF/checkpoints/cio-1007/parts (listing; tar t of 42-w1-s200 shows only checkpoint.pt)

evidence.claim: Attention is not returned by any function; it is computed inline and must be recomputed from the block weights.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Outer letters are or are not decisive for NUM answers.
evidence.label: untested

test.where: PC or M1 (torch needed, not in this container). Checkpoints: B2_s100/s101 (PF/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen) and W1_s200/s201 (extract checkpoint.pt from PF/checkpoints/cio-1007/parts into a scratch folder). Occlusion needs a GPU (about 75k forwards per checkpoint).
test.pass_mark: (a) normalised gradient at |k|=3 and 4 both >= 0.10 on both B2 checkpoints: full window used; both <= 0.05: effective +-2, so screen a kernel-3 reader with the 262,144 freed params reinvested to >= 3,147,208. (b) far-decisive rate minus floor >= 5 points on both: reach beyond the window is used; <= 1 point on both: the window is enough for NUM answers. (c) within-family exact gap (<=5 minus >=10 letters) >= 10 points on both seeds and in-word gradient mass at >= 5 chars >= 0.15 and >= 2x null: window limits spelling. (d) far attention mass <= 10% in every round vs >= 25% in some round. (e) reported only. Fixed now.
test.proved_wrong: (a) both <= 0.05 proves the full +-4 window is not used. (c) gap < 3 points on both seeds and real/null ratio < 1.2 proves the window is not limiting spelling. (b) far rate >= floor + 5 on both proves the window is too narrow for NUM answers.

idea.rules_check: R1/R10: offline measurements of learned weights; no hand code on the model path. R3: no size change unless a kernel-3 follow-up (must reinvest). R4: two checkpoints, a screen. R5: dev only. R9: B2 only.
idea.closest_prior: R0 removed the window with 19.9% fewer params; no probe of within-word demand exists. Test LR and loops probes do not measure reach.
idea.autonomy: Offline; no deploy-time step. Any reach it supports must be learned in training.
idea.director_note: Check hardest: gradient normalisation and padding handling; whether input-embedding gradients (not post-embedding) are used; occlusion swap rule (letter swaps can create new tokens); row counts per length bin; W1 checkpoint extraction needs the Ledger gattn cfg.
idea.note: Check hardest: gradient normalisation and padding handling; whether input-embedding gradients (not post-embedding) are used; occlusion swap rule (letter swaps can create new tokens); row counts per length bin; W1 checkpoint extraction needs the Ledger gattn cfg.

problems: Rules 2, 7 and 8 are not touched (probe only). Rule 1 is fine because the scoring tools may be hand-written. Rule 10 is fine because the probe is offline and adds no deploy-time step. Rule 6 is fine because it runs on the PC first. Rule 9 is fine because it is B2 only. The problems below are rule 4, rule 5, rule 3, Ben's test-fitting objection, and measurement validity.

Rule 4 (shown: checkpoint sizes and directories): the probe uses two B2 checkpoints (PF custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 and B2_s101, checkpoint.pt, 13,243,510 bytes each). Six B2 seeds (200-205) are already in the scratchpad at code/b2ckpt/B2_s200..B2_s205, so the B2 readouts can meet the 6-seed rule with no training. W1 exists only as seeds 200 and 201 (queue_local/42-pc-gain-w1.txt, shown), so any W1 result is a screen only.

Structural zero (shown: reader.py:1-6 and 43-51; ledger.py:142 passes no kernel size): in B2 each X[t] depends only on inputs within +-4 by construction. Arm (a) over k=-6..6 is therefore exactly zero at |k|=5 and 6. That is a sanity check, not evidence. Arm (a) also measures only the local sensitivity of X[t0]. It cannot show whether the answer uses letters beyond +-4, because the controller cross-attends to every X position (ledger.py:117-124). The summary's claim that (a) decides 'whether a trained B2 uses anything beyond +-2..4 letters' does not follow.

Arm (a) uses only three prompts (shown: eg.py:25 PROBES holds three Gemma check prompts, one of them 'Echo: sune Give only the answer.'). Three prompts are too few for a gradient profile with a 0.10 / 0.05 mark, even on two seeds. Also unstated: how the input is taken (the summed embedding at reader.py:86-91, or the letter table), how prompt start and end are handled, and whether padding is excluded. Gradient is local sensitivity, not use. The 'proves' wording overclaims (suggested).

Arm (b) confounds window reach with word identity (suggested, from the architecture): a far letter inside an operator word such as 'left' or 'sum' can change the answer, because the thinker must combine letters more than 4 characters apart to identify the word, even with a perfect +-4 window. So a 5-point far-decisive rate does not show reach beyond the window. The 'far' rule (more than 4 characters from any digit) is also not the window's known job. problems: (a) The gradient profile is ambiguous and mostly architectural. Read literally (Jacobian of X[t0] with respect to the input at t0+k), it depends only on the conv weights, not on the task. Shown: ConvBlock uses pad k//2 and there are two blocks (reader.py:44-51; ledger.py:142), so the Jacobian is exactly zero for |k|>=5 for B2 and generically nonzero within +-4 for any weights, trained or random (suggested). Read as a task-loss gradient, it flows through the thinker's cross-attention over every reader column (ledger.py run(), kvx over Xt), so it measures non-local influence, not reach from t0. Either way 'both >= 0.10 means full window used' is a sensitivity statement, not a use statement. No null is given; the same profile at random init is the obvious control (Adebayo et al. 2018, Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps, cited from memory, not fetched here). Outer-tap paths are products of two taps (suggested), so |k|=3-4 can fall below 0.05 while the letter is still used; 'effective +-2' does not follow.

(a) uses only 3 prompts. The list at models/eg.py:25 (PROBES) holds the three EG build-check strings (shown; the idea cites eg.py:25 without the models/ folder). Three prompts cannot estimate an offset profile, and the 0.10 and 0.05 thresholds have no reference distribution. Missing definitions: which scalar is differentiated (answer log-prob, or the norm of a 256-vector Jacobian); which t0 (letters only; a space gives k=0 gradient zero, so normalising by it blows up); and how offsets past the prompt edge are handled (reader.py masks padding, so those offsets are exactly zero and bias edge letters low; untested). The input should be the summed reader input x = tok+pos+place, not embedding rows, which would merge repeated letters.

(b) 'Far' is defined by distance from digit spans, but the reader window is letter-to-letter (each letter sees its own +-4 neighbours). The decisive far letters are probably operator and relation words (gives, more, not, true, times, left) whose letters sit inside a single +-4 window of each other. So a far-decisive rate measures word recognition and thinker composition, not reach. The thinker reads every reader position (ledger.py cross-attention; redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md section 1, shown), so a perfect +-2 window would still show far-decisive effects. The verdict 'far rate >= floor + 5 proves the window is too narrow for NUM answers' is a non sequitur.

(b) Occlusion and swap are different operations. The title says one-letter occlusion; the change says 'swap each letter'. Deletion shifts positions and place codes (reader.py place index, shown). A swap can create keywords (not, and, or, true, yes, plus one-letter words) and change meaning in prop_eval, syllogism, verify_claim and group_induct (data.md section 1, shown). A fixed, keyword-safe replacement rule and a count of changed regex tokens per swap are needed.

(b) 'Decisive' is undefined when the baseline is wrong. B2 pooled-5 is about 74 over six seeds (CONFIRM-ANALYSIS.json, per the brief), so about a quarter of rows are already wrong and answer changes on them are noise. Count changes only on rows the unswapped model gets right, or report both. Unit (per swap or per row) is not stated; per-row rates are clustered, so the 5-point mark has to be judged on row-clustered error.

(b) The floor is not a null. Frame openers carry task identity (for example 'Echo:', 'Decode', 'Is ... odd or even?'), so swapping their letters measures family recognition. 'Far' has no meaning on families without digits (passage_qa, kin_chain, rule_apply, object_track and others), which conflicts with the stated NUM-answer scope.

(b) Sample and cost do not add up. 'About 850 dev rows (25 per family)': the dev files hold 40 rows per family per split (data.md section 0, shown), so the split must be named. '75k forwards per checkpoint' does not follow from the design: about 850 rows at a prompt median of 78 characters (data.md section 2, shown) with roughly 40 letters each is about 34k single-letter swaps; the other ~40k are unexplained (untested). 'Needs a GPU' is unsupported. A 3.3M-parameter forward on CPU is probably tens of minutes (suggested; torch is not installed here, so untested).

(c) The rule '>= 60 rows per length bin' cannot be met by copy_word from the stated design. With 25 rows per family, copy_word has 25 rows in the sample, so bins of 60 need pooling of several WORD families, and the >=10-letter bin may be sparse. Needs a row count before any use.

(c) Confound: a WORD key's content is the mean of the reader output X over the word's characters (ledger.py:231-237, word_content, shown). Long words average over more local features, so an exact-match drop at >=10 letters can come from pooling dilution rather than the window. That alternative has to be ruled out (for example with a same-length control, or a pooled-feature control) before (c) can say the window limits spelling. 'Gradient mass at >=5 chars against a wrong-gold null' has no defined null.

(d) The description checks out: the workspace has 27 slots (R0 = 16 numbers + 4 constants = 20, plus N_RES = 7; progparse.py:8-9 and ledger.py run(), shown), so reader columns start at 27. But 'far' is not defined, attention mass is not use (Jain and Wallace 2019, Attention is not Explanation, cited from memory), and the recomputed attention must match the inline SDPA (ledger.py:117-121, shown). Reported-only status is right.

(e) Reported-only is correct. W1 gave only +0.9 and +0.1 pooled, and lookup families F1 -4.1 (progress-board data.json, shown), so its head may be idle. The W1_s200 archive is a gzip tar part set with 42-w1-s200/W1_s200/checkpoint.pt (shown); the W1_s201 archive was not listed, so check it.

The gate would miss modest real effects while the thresholds are still arbitrary.

Decision value is limited. The probe measures use inside a model trained with the +-4 window. It cannot show whether a different window would generalise, because use is not need. Ben's question (is +-4 test-fitting?) needs a training-time test. Kernel 3 frees 262,144 parameters (shown arithmetic: 2 x 131,072), B2 drops to 3,040,337, below the 3,147,208 floor, so 106,871 to 301,543 parameters must be reinvested (the reinvestment has to be fixed in advance).
