problems: Not the cheapest decisive test: gradient (a) measures the reader's own linear Jacobian, not use. Shown (code): reader.py:43-51, 92-93 make X[t0] depend only on inputs t0-4..t0+4, so |k|=5,6 are zero by construction (a sanity check, not a finding). For B2 the normalised k=3,4 values track the learned outer conv weights, so a small value means small weights, not an unused window. The probe is also run on the 3 check prompts in eg.py:25 only.

The 0.10 / 0.05 gradient thresholds have no null. Shown (code): ledger.py:153-157 re-initialises only Linear and Embedding, so conv taps keep PyTorch default init (uniform, bound 1/sqrt(1280)). Suggested (my arithmetic, not measured): an untrained reader's outer-offset normalised gradients could land around 0.05-0.3, i.e. on the thresholds. A random-init reader is needed as the null.

Gradient on X[t0] ignores the thinker, which reads every reader position through cross-attention (ledger.py:117-124; ledger.py:302-304, kvx over all Xt). Far letters can change the answer with no reader reach, so (b)'s claim that far-decisive minus floor >= 5 'proves the window is too narrow' is a non sequitur. Its 'proved wrong' line (<= 1 point 'means the window is enough') is equally invalid.

(b) defines far by distance from digit spans, but many families have no digits (copy_word is 'Echo: sune', research/data.md:8), so distance is undefined for them. The swap rule is unspecified: a swap can create or remove a digit or space, which changes NUM_RE (progparse.py:14) and word_spans (data.py:149-154), so the hand-written spans change, not only the reader. The unit (per swap or per row) is not stated; per-swap rates are pseudo-replicated. The floor (frame openers) is not matched by distance or family. No power calculation: with about 850 rows, rate standard errors are roughly 2-3 points (suggested, my arithmetic), so a 5-point margin sits near noise.

(c) copy_word is at ceiling in distribution. Shown (results/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 and B2_s101 RESULT.json): in_dist 40/40, answer 40/40, vocab 40/40 on both seeds; failures sit in frame (32/40, 39/40) and variant (11/40, 19/40). Each split has 40 copy_word rows, so 200 per seed across all five dev splits. The rule of at least 60 rows in each of three length bins (<=5, 6-9, >=10) probably cannot be met; the copy_word word-length distribution is not in the files (untested).

(c) also has a mode confound. Shown (ledger.py talk, 380-406): in WORD mode the talker prints the prompt slice exactly, so a WORD-mode copy_word success or failure is a pointer or mode error, not spelling. The word key includes a learned word-length embedding (len_emb of word length, ledger.py word_keys), so length effects in pointer selection come from the pointer's own features. The probe must split rows by talker mode (talk(..., return_modes=True) exists) and test spelling only on GEN-mode rows. Which mode B2 picks for copy_word is untested here.

Power and logic for (c): with 60-row bins at p about 0.7, the standard error of a difference is about 8 points (suggested, my arithmetic), so a true 10-point gap has roughly 50% power per seed. The 'gap < 3 on both seeds and ratio < 1.2 proves the window is not limiting spelling' rule is underpowered and cannot prove anything.

Reach channels outside the +-4 window are not measured. Shown (reader.py:17-23, 86): the place code gives each char its index from the right end of its regex word, a word-level signal with no conv tap, and reader.py:72 adds an absolute position table of 208 rows at input. Neither is a letter path, so the gradient ignores both. No test-time lesion removes them: the ledger.py:128 LESIONS list and the lesion options in run() cover noexec, opswap, ctl27, nocopy and nowordc only. Place-code effects on B2 are untested (RESULTS-SCREEN addendum 1 covers plain transformers only).

(d) has no uniform-attention baseline and no definition of 'far'. Suggested: with about 27 workspace keys plus up to about 200 reader keys, a far region can hold most keys, so under uniform attention its mass would already exceed 10 percent. The thresholds (<= 10 percent every round vs >= 25 percent in some round) have no stated consequence and no 'between' outcome. Shown: the reader columns do start at index 27 (S0 has 20 rows, Rs has 7; progparse.py:8-10; ledger.py:118-120), so the index is right. Recomputing attention must reproduce run() exactly, which needs a check.

Cipher is not a window test. Shown (research/data.md cipher row, about line 35): 'Code: h=2' puts the letter and digit two characters apart, which fits a plus-or-minus-2 window too. Shown (results/RESULTS-EG2.md): R0 cipher_map in_dist 12.5 and 2.5 versus B2V 100, which shows only that some local reading is needed. Cipher cannot decide between plus-or-minus 2 and plus-or-minus 4.

The cheapest decisive test is missing: a test-time lesion that zeroes the conv taps at offsets +-2 in both blocks (weights 0 and 4 of each kernel-5 conv, reader.py:47). That leaves composite reach +-2, the same as kernel-3, with no training. It needs an equal-count random-weight control, because zeroing any weights disrupts the model. Suggested (not run); it can be run on existing checkpoints in minutes and would tell whether the kernel-3 retrain is worth about 6 GPU-hours.

Seed and box mismatch and the rule-4 floor. The B2 arm uses B2_s100 and B2_s101 from 29-b2-screen, whose RESULT config records data path /job/data, unlike the PC's C:\ path in 33-pc-confirm-b2 (suggested that they come from another machine). W1_s200 and W1_s201 were run on the PC against queue-33 B2 (queue_local/42-pc-gain-w1.txt header). Use B2_s200 to B2_s205 (sha-checked copies in the scratchpad b2ckpt folder, cfg copy only) as the six-seed B2 arm, and B2_s200 and B2_s201 as the W1 pair. A probe that gates a design (kernel-3 reinvestment) is not a screen to be read on two seeds.

Pass marks are not sealed. Shown: PASS-MARKS.md has no reach addendum (grep found none). 'Fixed now' in the proposal is not the project's practice of sealing an addendum before any run. The 'between' outcomes are undefined for (a), (b) and (d), and no decision table maps mixed outcomes (for example (a) yes and (b) no) to dilation, relative bias or kernel-3.

Reinvestment arithmetic is right but incomplete. Shown: kernel-3 frees 2 x (327,936 - 196,864) = 262,144; B2 drops to 3,040,337; the floor is 3,147,208 (0.97 x 3,244,544). So at least 106,871 params must be reinvested (computed). W1's 33,632 alone is not enough, and a 16-token scratch block (about 4,096) is nowhere near. The reinvestment target must be named before the run (rules 3 and 4).

Feasibility checked (read-only). Shown: `cat` of the five 42-w1-s200 parts piped into `tar -xzO 42-w1-s200/W1_s200/checkpoint.pt` gives a 13,381,376-byte torch zip whose data.pkl contains 'gattn', so the cfg-based load works with no special handling; the orchestrator's extraction worry is resolved. Hours: the proposal's 1.5 h covers only coding. Suggested: 3-5 h including a reproduction check (run the loader on untouched dev rows and match RESULT.json per family within 1 row). Compute: about 0.9 GFLOP per prompt forward by my arithmetic (reader convs about 131 MFLOP at T=100; 8 rounds x 2 blocks of controller), so about 70 TFLOP per checkpoint for 75k forwards. That is minutes on the 5070 Ti, and CPU is probably 10-30 min per checkpoint (suggested, not measured). 'Needs a GPU' is overstated. Memory is far under 16 GB.

Minor implementation points. Shown: talk takes (state, batch) (ledger.py:380), so the proposal's talk(state(...)) omits batch. Swapped prompts must be re-encoded (prompt_ids, prompt_mask and rows together) before the forward and before talk, since WORD slices read rows' prompt text. Dev only and no GOLD-PRIVATE use are fine (rule 5). Rules 1 and 10 are fine because the probe is offline, and the hand regex is analysis code only.
critiques.rescue: Revise to a lesion-first probe on existing checkpoints. (1) Use B2_s200 to B2_s205 (six seeds) and W1_s200 and W1_s201 paired with B2_s200 and B2_s201, all from the PC. Run: zero the +-2 taps in both conv blocks (composite reach +-2); zero +-2 in block 2 only; zero +-1 in both; an equal-count random-weight control; place ids reset to PLACE_NONE; optionally absolute position embedding off. Measure per-family exact match on the 850 dev rows (or full dev), with a reproduction check against RESULT.json first. Report GEN-mode and WORD-mode rows separately. (2) Keep gradients only as a diagnostic: end-to-end gradient of the gold answer log-probability with respect to the summed reader input (reader.py:91), plus a random-init null. Report it, do not gate on it. (3) Drop the window claims from (b). If kept, restrict to NUM families, measure distance from the target digit span, swap letters with letters that keep word lengths and create no digits or spaces, match the floor by family and distance, and use per-row units. (4) (c) only on GEN-mode rows, in-distribution and variant reported separately, with bins only where at least 60 rows exist, and power stated. (5) (d) with a uniform-attention baseline; (e) report only. (6) Seal as a PASS-MARKS addendum before any run, with a decision table. Suggested marks (for Ben to fix): if zeroing the +-2 taps costs at most 1.0 pooled-5 on the six-seed mean and at most 5 points on cipher and copy families, outer taps are treated as unused and a kernel-3 retrain screen runs on six seeds with a named reinvestment of at least 106,871 params; if it costs at least 3.0, keep the window and test dilation or global reach instead; in between, not shown. (7) Hours: 3-5 h of coding and checking, under 1 GPU-hour or a few CPU-hours of compute. Label every number shown, suggested or untested.
critiques.already_tried: Closest prior: R0 (reader_layers 0) removed the window and 656,896 params (19.9 percent), so it is confounded (results/46-r0ege-s200 and 48-r0-s201, RESULTS-EG2.md). No tap, place or position lesion exists: the ledger.py:128 LESIONS list has shuffle_state, zero_state, noexec and opswap, and nocopy and nowordc are added at ledger.py:163; ctl27 is a read-only test lesion in run() (ledger.py:315-316). The window was never varied beyond 2 versus 0 (director fact check). W1 (one global block, +0.9 and +0.1 pooled, progress board) is the only reach arm built. Test LR and the loops probes do not measure reach. No within-word demand probe exists in the repo.
critiques.expected_effect: As written, the probe would likely produce numbers that cannot gate the kernel-3, dilation or relative-bias decisions: (a) is architecture plus weight size, (b) and (d) measure thinker demand rather than window reach, and (c) is confounded by mode, length and split. As revised, the tap lesion and place lesion on six B2 seeds plus the W1 pair would answer within minutes whether the outer taps (+-3 to +-4 composite reach) carry answer-relevant signal. A clean 'unused' result would justify a kernel-3 retrain screen (about 6 GPU-hours on six seeds, plus the reinvestment arm). A clean 'used' result would argue against shrinking the window. Either way the decision is the cheapest one available; a 'between' result stays not shown.

chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test, but only after a rewrite: the rule-clean, cheap core is a test-time tap lesion on saved checkpoints, not the gradient/occlusion gates as written.

WHY PLAN, NOT CUT. (1) Rules (shown): it is offline on saved weights, so rules 1, 5, 6, 9 and 10 are clean (no deploy-time step, dev rows only, B2 only, PC or Mac CPU). Six paired B2 checkpoints already exist (shown: scratchpad code/b2ckpt B2_s200..B2_s205), so the B2 half can meet rule 4's six seeds with no training. W1 exists only as seeds 200/201, so any W1 result is a screen. (2) Decision value: it is the only cheap way to shrink the unknown behind Ben's 'is +-4 test-fitting' objection. No window-size sweep exists (shown: reader_layers is the only knob, reader.py:69, and R0 also removes 656,896 params, so it is a window-plus-capacity lesion). Kernel-3 frees 2 x 131,072 = 262,144 params and drops B2 to 3,040,337, below the 3,147,208 floor (shown: three critics' arithmetic; I re-derived R0 = 2,645,585 = B2 minus 2 x 328,448). A lesion that says 'outer taps unused' justifies a retrain screen; one that says 'used' stops one.

WHY THE IDEA AS WRITTEN MUST NOT RUN. (a) The gradient profile is exactly zero at |k|>=5 by construction (shown: two k=5 ConvBlocks, reader.py:43-51), measures conv weight size rather than use, has no random-init null, runs on the 3 Gemma load-check strings at eg.py:25 instead of dev rows, and its 0.10/0.05 marks have no reference distribution. (b) The far-from-digit letter swap mixes word identity and thinker composition with window reach, because the controller cross-attends to every reader position (shown: ledger.py:117-124, 302-314). Swaps can also create keywords, digits or spaces and change the hand regexes. The clause 'proves the window is too narrow' is a non sequitur. (c) Length-binned copy_word exact match is WORD-mode pointer accuracy (shown: the talker prints the prompt slice; word keys carry a length embedding), copy_word is near ceiling, and 60 rows per bin is unreachable from 40 rows per split. Word keys also mean-pool X over the word, which dilutes long words (suggested confound). (d) Attention mass has no uniform baseline and no definition of 'far'. (e) is fine as reported-only. Every 'proved wrong' clause overclaims from a two-seed null. The marks are not sealed: PASS-MARKS.md has no reach addendum (shown by grep, and I confirmed none in the tail or by search). Several outcomes have no decision. B2 seeds 100/101 are unpaired with W1 seeds 200/201. The name 'reader-D5' clashes with INVENTORY D5.

WHAT SURVIVES: the cheapest decisive probe, as critic 4 and the autonomy critic both converge on, is to zero the outer taps in the trained conv blocks, which leaves a composite reach of +-2 with no training, and to read W1's learned attention by offset as a diagnostic.
chair.revised_idea:
Rename to 'reach-lesion-L1' (not reader-D5). Probe only, no training, no model change, no deploy-time step. Run on the PC, same machine for all arms. Seal a dated addendum in PASS-MARKS.md (after addendum 20) before any run.

Models: B2_s200..B2_s205 (six paired seeds, code/b2ckpt, sha-checked) plus W1_s200/s201 (screen only, paired with B2_s200/s201). W1 extraction (shown by two critics): cat the 42-w1-s200 parts | gzip -dc | tar -x gives 42-w1-s200/W1_s200/checkpoint.pt; cfg carries gattn so load_model rebuilds it. First step: reproduce each checkpoint's RESULT.json per-family counts within about 1 row on the unmodified model. If it does not reproduce, stop.

Rows: dev rows only. Prefer a fresh enlarged dev panel from the generator's --dev-per-cell 200 option (shown: research/data.md:5, local_runner.py:84; identical train hash, old dev as prefix), separate from the scored rows. No GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected panels. Report GEN-mode and WORD-mode rows separately via talk(..., return_modes=True).

Arms (one lesion family, test time only):
L-outer: zero the offset-+-2 taps (kernel indices 0 and 4) in both conv blocks, composite reach +-2, the same as a kernel-3 reader.
L-outer2: zero the offset-+-2 taps in block 2 only (composite reach +-3).
Controls: L-inner (zero offsets +-1 in both blocks, same tap count as L-outer) and L-rand (zero a random same-count set of conv weight entries, fixed seed) to separate 'outer taps unused' from 'any weight damage hurts'.
Place-code lesion: reset place ids to PLACE_NONE at test time (the hand channel that INVENTORY A9 wants removed, untested on B2).
Reported-only diagnostics (no gate): (i) gradient of the gold-answer log-probability with respect to the summed reader input (tok+pos+place, reader.py:86-91), on dev rows, with a random-init-reader null; (ii) W1 GlobalAttn weights by |i-j| on cipher_map rows, recomputed from reader.glob q/k and checked against the module's own output; (iii) controller cross-attention mass over digit / word / other reader columns (columns start at 27), with a uniform-attention baseline stated.
Dropped: the far-from-digit occlusion gate (b), length-binned WORD copy (c) unless restricted to GEN rows with a pooled-feature dilution control and bins that actually reach 60 rows, and all 'proves' wording.

Measure: per-family and pooled-5 exact match with row-clustered error; cipher_map and the copy families (copy_word, list_index, passage_qa) reported separately.

Decision table (fixed before the run, six-seed B2 mean): L-outer costs <= 1.0 pooled-5 and <= 5 points on cipher_map and copy families, AND L-inner costs clearly more than L-outer: outer taps are unused, so a kernel-3 retrain screen is justified, with the reinvestment named first. L-outer costs >= 3.0 pooled-5: outer taps carry signal, keep the window, and test a learned reach arm next instead. In between, or L-inner no worse than L-outer: not shown, no decision. Inference limits: a small L-outer cost is suggestive for kernel-3 but is not a retrain result, because the trained net could route differently when trained at k=3, and a large cost is weak evidence about retraining. Any window claim needs a 6-seed retrain under rule 4.

Follow-up, a separate single change and not part of this probe: a kernel-3 reader that stays in the 3,147,208-3,341,880 band. Suggested arithmetic (mine, a k=3 block is 197,376 params): three k=3 blocks cost 592,128, giving B2 = 3,237,713 params with composite reach +-3. That is a depth-and-reach change, so it needs its own sealed marks and six paired seeds.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must get these right:
1. Seal first. Write a dated addendum in custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md (D0 is the precedent, addendum 16) with the decision table before any run, using 'shown / suggested / untested' labels and no 'proves' wording. Give a decision for every outcome, including the middle cells.
2. Six B2 seeds (200-205) on one machine, with the W1 pair (200/201) as a labelled screen. Do not reuse B2_s100/s101. Do a reproduction check against RESULT.json before any lesion, and record the machine. Plain-B2 loops:0 differs by machine (seed 201 reads 10.81 on the PC and 4.34 on the rented box), so never compare across machines.
3. The lesion needs equal-damage controls (L-inner, L-rand). Zeroing any weights hurts, so a bare L-outer drop proves nothing. State that inference runs only one way (small cost suggests kernel-3 is viable; large cost does not prove it is not).
4. Use dev rows only. Use the enlarged dev panel (--dev-per-cell 200) if it is available, and keep the scored panel separate. Never use GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected panels. Count answer changes only on rows the unmodified model gets right, or report both.
5. Report GEN versus WORD mode per family. Do not call WORD-mode copy a spelling test, and do not use length-binned copy_word.
6. The hand regexes (word_spans, NUM_RE) and the place code are analysis-side or an existing hand part here. Any perturbation must re-encode prompt_ids, prompt_mask and rows together and must create no digits, spaces or keywords. Do not touch the hand parts in the claim.
7. Keep gradients and attention maps as diagnostics only, with a random-init null and a uniform baseline. Do not gate on them.
8. Cost: CPU or the PC, a few hours including coding and the reproduction check (suggested). Occlusion at about 75k forwards is not needed, so the GPU claim is dropped.
9. Rename it (not reader-D5) and keep it in the small-card B2 track (rule 9). Any later kernel-3 or reach change is a separate single change with a named reinvestment and a six-paired-seed confirm (rule 4). Because B2's lead over plain shrank at 10M (8a), a window result at 3M may need retesting at larger size.
10. Priority: low-to-medium. W1 (+0.9/+0.1) and U0 (-3.1/-5.4) already weakened richer-reach ideas, so this should run only when the PC is idle between larger runs (for example after q39), not ahead of the EGE confirm or T1 span copy.

plan.title: reach-lesion-L1: cut the trained reader's outer taps
plan.ben_line: We take six trained B2 models and, with no retraining, make each letter look only two letters to each side instead of four. If the answers mostly survive, the wide view may be more than the model needs, so a narrower, cheaper reader is worth testing. If they fall apart, the outer letters are doing real work and the window stays.
plan.question: On six trained B2 checkpoints, with no retraining, does cutting the direct convolution taps that reach two letters away (reader reach +-4 becomes +-2) leave exact-match scores intact, judged against equal-size controls and marks fixed in advance?
plan.one_change: At test time only, zero the offset plus-or-minus-2 conv taps (kernel indices 0 and 4) in both reader blocks: reader.blocks.0.conv.weight[:, :, [0,4]] = 0, and the same for blocks.1. Kernel index j reads offset j-2 because ConvBlock uses padding k//2 (reader.py:43-51, shown). No training, no new parameters, no shipped-file change.
arms: intact (reproduction): the old 40-per-cell dev against RESULT.json final_eval.by_family for each seed, then the baseline on the fresh panel.

L-outer (GATE): taps 0 and 4 in both blocks, 262,144 weight entries removed (2 taps x 256 x 256 x 2 blocks, shown). Composite reach becomes +-2, the same reach as two kernel-3 blocks (suggested). The other taps keep their trained weights.
L-inner (GATE control): taps 1 and 3 in both blocks, the same 262,144 entries. Tests whether same-size damage at +-1 shows up in this model.

L-rand (reported control, not gated): three fixed-seed draws, each choosing two non-centre tap positions per block from {0,1,3,4}, same entry count; report mean and range. Entry-level random zeroing is rejected: it removes 262,144 of 655,360 conv entries (40%, shown arithmetic) in an unstructured way, which is a much larger shock than tap removal (suggested).
L-outer2 (reported): taps 0 and 4 in block 2 only (composite +-3; 131,072 entries).

Place-channel lesion (reported only): replace reader.places with a constant PLACE_NONE (15) through an instance override. This touches only the hand place code. A gate on it would be a separate single change.

W1_s200 and W1_s201 (labelled two-seed screen): an intact re-run (no W1 RESULT.json exists in the repo, shown) and L-outer. W1 has a global attention block (reader.py:54-65), so its structural test is expected to fail. Its L-outer result asks whether global attention compensates for the cut, not whether the window is needed.
Dropped to keep one change: gradient profiles, W1 attention by offset, controller attention mass, and one-letter occlusion. The critics showed these measure architecture or thinker use, not reach.
plan.seeds: Gate: B2_s200 to B2_s205, the six paired q33 PC runs (RESULT.json per seed, shown). The checkpoint.pt sha256 matches its .sha256 file for all six (verified here). Run seeds 200 and 201 first as the screen. W1_s200 and W1_s201 are a two-seed screen only. Both archives are present (five parts each, gzip tar, cfg gattn 32, shown), so the earlier note that s201 was missing is wrong. Do not use B2_s100 or B2_s101. Dev rows only; no GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected panel (rule 5).
plan.machine: BensPC RTX 5070 Ti (cuda), the machine that wrote the RESULT.json files for seeds 200 to 205 (config data path C:\Users\benja\..., shown). One machine and one code path for every arm. evalx.evaluate runs without autocast (fp32, shown), but cuDNN may use TF32 on the GPU (suggested), so do not mix CPU and GPU numbers. Never mix with rented-box numbers: per the brief, seed 201 loops:0 in_dist is 10.81 on the PC and 4.34 on the rented box. Run under the GPU-BUSY lock (as queues 33 and 42 did) after queue 39 finishes or is paused.
pass_marks: Seal first: addendum 21 in custom_io/PASS-MARKS.md after addendum 20 (line 515 of 529, shown), dated before any run, with these marks, the decision table and the panel rule. Use addendum 16 (D0) as the template. Label every claim shown, suggested or untested.

Reproduction rule (before any lesion): on the old 40-per-cell dev, every family's correct count matches RESULT.json final_eval.by_family within 1 row, and pooled-5 is within 0.05 points, for every seed. Otherwise stop.

Gate panel (fresh rows): data_big dev in_dist, answer, frame, vocab and variant, beyond the first 40 rows per family and split (prefix claimed in data.md, untested here), minus the five chain families' in_dist rows (already scored as chain-5, shown in evalx.chain_panel), deduplicated, with zero overlap with train prompts. The family split is not used. Costs are intact minus lesion in exact-match points, as six-seed means with t-intervals and per-seed values. Fresh row count is about 23,000 (suggested from data.md's enlarged counts).

PASS (the cut is cheap, so the outer taps carry little): all of G1 to G5 hold. G1: L-outer pooled-5 cost <= 1.0 (six-seed mean). G2: L-outer cost <= 2.0 on at least 5 of 6 seeds. G3: L-inner cost minus L-outer cost >= 3.0 (six-seed means). G4: L-outer cost <= 5.0 points on each of copy_word, list_index, passage_qa and cipher_map (fresh rows, six-seed means). G5: L-outer chain-5 cost on the existing 1,000 rows <= 2.0 (six-seed mean). The numbers are suggested values that the owning thread seals as written.
FAIL (the outer taps carry signal; keep the window and test a learned-reach arm next): L-outer cost >= 3.0 (six-seed mean) and >= 2.0 on at least 5 of 6 seeds.

NOT SHOWN (no decision) for every other outcome. That includes: G1 and G2 hold but G3 fails (the controls show no visible damage, so the test has no teeth); G1 holds but G4 or G5 fails (a cipher failure alone is not FAIL, because distance-2 pairs can also be bound through two +-1 taps, shown in data.md's cipher template); a six-seed mean between 1.0 and 3.0; and old-panel and fresh-panel means on opposite sides of 1.0 or 3.0.

Structural check (must pass before any lesion number is used): for a mid-prompt position t, add a random vector at offset k to the summed reader input with reader(batch, extra=E). Intact X_t changes for |k| <= 4 (conv geometry). Under L-outer, X_t is exactly unchanged for |k| >= 3 and changes for |k| <= 2. Expected to fail for W1.

Reporting, not gating: flips per family (right to wrong and wrong to right, scored on rows the intact model gets right, with both counts reported) and a McNemar test on the pooled fresh rows; GEN and WORD mode separately per family via model.state then model.talk(..., return_modes=True); L-rand mean and range; L-outer2; the place lesion; the W1 pair.
plan.proved_wrong: The idea (the outer plus-or-minus-2 taps carry little, so a narrower reader is worth a retrain) is proved wrong for the trained reader if L-outer costs at least 3.0 on the six-seed mean and at least 2.0 on five or more of six seeds (fresh panel, pooled-5). That falsifies only the cheap-cut claim. It does not prove that a retrained two- or three-block k=3 reader would fail, because removing trained taps can shock the activations and a retrain can route information differently (suggested). A PASS likewise does not prove a kernel-3 retrain would match B2.
plan.null_risk: Could the marks pass with no real change? Yes, in these honest ways. (1) A PASS means the cut costs about a point or less on six seeds. It does not mean the outer taps are unused. Assuming a per-seed SD near 1 (suggested; the intact pooled-5 SD over six seeds is 0.63, shown), a true cost of 0.5 passes G1 about 90% of the time and a true cost of 1.5 about 10% (suggested arithmetic). (2) The thinker reads every reader position through cross-attention (ledger.py run, shown), so letters two to four apart can still reach the answer through separate reads. A small cut cost therefore means the reader's joint features are not needed, which is narrower than "letters are not needed." (3) G3 is weak. The plus-or-minus-1 taps sit next to the centre and carry most of the signal, so same-size plus-or-minus-1 removal almost always hurts. G3 catches a fully tolerant model, not an unused outer tap. (4) A PASS holds only with the hand place code in place (reader.py:17-23, shown), which is itself a hand part under rule 1. (5) In the other direction there is no shock-matched control, because random tap pairs include the plus-or-minus-1 taps, so a FAIL can be partly the shock of removing trained taps (suggested). (6) Copy-family costs also move through word-content pooling (ledger.py word_content, shown), so they do not isolate spelling. The gate is a guard against a large false pass, not a precise measure of the outer taps' use.
plan.autonomy: Deploy time: nothing changes. The probe edits no shipped model and adds no step to answering. The deployed model still reads, writes its program, runs its exact executor and talks as it does now, so rule 10 holds at deploy time. Build time: the lesion, the panel and the marks are researcher measurements, which rule 10 allows because building before shipping is not a deploy step. The probe does not give the model a choice of reach. If a PASS later leads to a narrower reader, the kernel size would be a fixed build constant set by a researcher from dev results. That is not the model learning its own reach, and the output should be labelled that way. The autonomy-clean route, a learned reach (W1-style global attention or a learned mix of block sizes), is not tested here. The hand parts the probe touches (word_spans, the number regex, the place code) stay as they are in the gate. The place-channel lesion touches one of them and is reported only.

fixed_plan.ben_line: We take six trained models and, with no retraining, switch off the two outermost parts of each letter filter, then compare that with a control that changes the same parts by the same amount but keeps them in place. fixed_plan.question: On six trained B2 checkpoints (seeds 200 to 205), with no retraining, does zeroing the two outer convolution taps in each reader block cost exact-match score beyond what a same-size, reach-preserving random change costs, judged on fresh dev rows against marks sealed before any run?

final.ben_line: This check would switch off the outer letter views in six already-trained models to see if they still answer, but zeroing that much without retraining will probably break them whatever the outer letters are worth, so we should wait and design a fairer test first.
plan_fixes: G6 is probably backwards (suggested). L-noise puts random weights of the same norm into the same outer taps, so it is likely at least as damaging as zeroing them. Then L-outer minus L-noise is at most 0 and the FAIL branch can never fire. Replace the binary control with a dose-response curve: scale the outer taps by 1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25 and 0, and report the change in X_t for each. Judge the cost against how much X_t moves, and fix that rule before the run.

State the prior in the addendum. PASS (G1: cost at most 1.0 after zeroing 40% of conv entries with no retraining) is very unlikely, and FAIL is unreadable under the current G6. The expected outcome is NOT SHOWN. Either accept that the probe is only a descriptive curve, or pair it with a decision-bearing screen such as a learned-reach retrain arm. idea.title: Search-hard kind panel gated on CPU before any sleep test
idea.summary: C2's held-out kinds are mostly search-easy, so they can only show whether sleep turns search into first answers. Build a small panel of one-input kinds with 4-7 step references, keep only kinds where blind search fails at the loop's own budget but B2 can still write the program, and fix the gates before any model scores a sealed split. This is Ben's own rule for future creative tests.

Candidate kinds with reference lengths: tier-1 (4 steps) dist20, digitsum, digitprod; budget-effect controls (3 steps) tri, cube_x, mod7; deeper last2_sum (5), reverse2 (6), reverse (5), x_plus_rev (6), tri_mod10 (4), clamp with both edges shown in the examples (4-7), clamp_mod10 (5), last2_shift (7); Minecraft-flavoured ticks//20 (4), time mod 24000 (5), ceil(x/16) (7), min(x//3,5) (6), crafting kits (4x)//p (5-7); calibration controls xmod10x and sqmod10 (2 steps). Gates fixed now: (1) CPU, no model: reference exact on the whole domain in python and torch executors; pinned among panel kinds; blind first-fit RIGHT at 512 candidates <=33% and at 50k <=25% on 60 fresh questions per kind. (2) B2 probe on raw B2 s100/s101: greedy right <=5%; right-reach@512 at T 3.0 recorded; a kind is sleepable if right-reach@512 >=2% on both parents. (3) forced-reference check: teacher-forced P_ref at T 1 and T 3, and greedy agreement between sampler.sample_run, legal.sample_run_masked and the forced path. (4) false-accept share at 5 examples. Side arm (blind first): escalate on no-fit from 512 to a cap of 6,000 candidates. Score right-reach, not fit-reach, because C2's reach gates count example fits.
idea.why: On C2 DEV, blind first-fit right is 58.2% at 1k and 73.8% at 6k; on the 154 multi-step questions 31.8% and 57.8%; square, last_digit and double_add are 100, 96 and 100% by 6k, so only sq_plus and affine are search-hard. At 50k blind got 0/8 on last2_sum, 0/6 on reverse2 and on clamp-both-edges, 1/6 on last2_shift, 2/6 on clamp_mod10. Pooled over 12 kinds, escalation from 512 to 6k gained +27.5 points for blind search but tier-1 escalated first fits were right only 40% of the time (so purity matters).

problems: 1. Gate 1 contradicts the tier-1 selection (shown, code plus the idea's own numbers). blind_baseline.py:68 makes first_fit_right_within_N non-decreasing in N, because the first fit fixes the value once it appears, so the 50k value is at least the 6k value. Gate 1 caps 50k at 25%, but the idea's own 6k figures are digitsum 19/30 (63%), dist20 9/30 (30%) and digitprod 6/30 (20%). digitsum fails gate 1 for certain, dist20 probably fails, and digitprod passes only if its 50k value stays under 25%. The idea names all three as the tier-1 kinds that lucky hits could feed. Gate 1 as written therefore drops the kinds the idea wants and keeps kinds at 0-7% at 6k (tri_mod10, reverse, x_plus_rev, tetra) or kinds with no fit by 50k.

2. Gate 1 measures enumerator depth, not kind difficulty for B2 (shown, my re-run in this session, inline, not saved). blind_baseline.py:25-43 generates candidates depth by depth, so every 2-step candidate comes before any 3-step one. On a synthetic tri question the first 3-step candidate is number 487 and the first 4-step is 6,408. On 40 synthetic questions for dist20, digitsum, digitprod, reverse and tri_mod10 (my readings of the definitions), 4-step candidates were not reached by 6,000 in 37 cases. The right answers at 6k came from 2-3-step programs that agree with the examples; dist20 is right as 20 minus x when the examples and the query are below 20. So search-hard in gate 1 means the enumerator has not reached that depth yet. That says nothing about whether B2 can write the program.

3. cube_x does not match the code (shown, my re-run, inline). x cubed is two steps in this language (MUL(x,x), then MUL by x). On 12 synthetic questions with x in 3 to 29, the first fit was x cubed at candidate 71 to 77 and was right on 12 of 12, so first-fit right within 512 should be near 100%. The idea reports cube_x 0/30 at 512 and labels it 3 steps. Either its definition differs from x cubed (the idea gives no definition) or the inline run used other code. The same check puts the tri inline figures in the right range (first right fit near candidate 900 on a synthetic tri question), so the mismatch is specific to cube_x.

4. The panel is not defined and its numbers are not saved (shown). A text grep of /mnt/project-files and the creative code tree finds none of dist20, digitsum, digitprod, tri_mod10, cube_x, x_plus_rev, last2_sum, clamp_mod10, panel.py or w3d-1. The idea gives no formula, domain or reference program for any kind. Its inline panel numbers and 50k figures are labelled shown, but they are described as not saved, which breaks the project's own rule that shown means measured and cited to a file. Relabel them untested until saved. The reference step counts (4 to 7) cannot be checked. DIV is valid only when exact (programs.py:41), so floor-division kinds (digitsum, reverse, ticks//20, min(x//3,5)) need extra steps unless the domain avoids them.

5. The blind DEV figures reproduce on the first-fit metric (shown, my re-run on data/c2/dev.jsonl, 256 rows). First-fit right is 58.2% at 1k and 73.8% at 6k. Multi-step (n=154) is 31.8% and 57.8%. Per kind at 6k: affine 11.5%, sq_plus 62.7%, double_add 100%, square 100%, last_digit 96.1%. The any-right-fit metric gives 59.0% and 74.6%, so it does not explain the notes' 64.5% and 77.3% (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md lines 53-54). The source of those two numbers is untested. The 50k figure (94.9%) was not re-run because it is too slow for this session. Quote 58.2 and 73.8 only with the first-fit label.

6. Mark (3) compares different metrics (shown, code). B2 right-reach is an oracle: any right try among 512, scored with the key. Blind first-fit right uses the first fit only, chosen by the checker. Blind any-right exists (blind_baseline.py:69), but the 512 budget is not among BUDGETS (blind_baseline.py:11 has 1000, 6000, 50000), so the 512 cell needs a new run. An oracle over B2's tries against a first-fit blind arm favours B2 by construction. The +10 mark and the under-+5 proved-wrong rule are therefore decided partly by the metric choice. Use the same metric for both arms.

7. The 512-candidate budget is not matched in content (shown, code). Blind's candidates are distinct value vectors (blind_baseline.py:22 and 32-34 dedup), while B2's 512 samples come from legal.raw_samples with no dedup (legal.py:196-205). P0 found 2.1 to 4.5 distinct result-changing programs per 32 tries (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md lines 121-123), and C2 DEV had 12.6 and 15.8 distinct rule-following programs per question (results/c2dev). The B2 arm must report distinct programs per question at 512 next to the blind distinct count, or the two arms are not comparable.

8. Gate 2 scores the wrong thing for sleep (shown, code). C2's reach gates count checker-accepted tries (fewshot.py:328-365; key_luck is reported separately), and sleep records are fitting tries (c2_stuck.py has_fit, search and w_records). The idea scores right answers, which sleep cannot see. The idea's own escalation numbers say tier-1 first fits are right only 40% of the time, so sleeping on accepted tries there would mostly train wrong programs. Purity should be a gate, measured at 3 examples, which is the loop's setting (rules_real.py:128, k_ex=3). Gate 4 uses 5 examples, a setting the loop never sees.

9. Power is too low for the marks (shown arithmetic; the paired SE is suggested). Gate 2 uses 40 questions per kind per parent. A 2% per-question right-reach therefore means one question, and the chance of at least one right question per parent is 1-(1-p)^40: 33% at p=1%, 55% at 2%, 87% at 5%, and both parents are required. Gate 1 at n=60 has an SE of about 6 points at p=0.3. Its 33% cut sits on digitsum's 512 value (10/30 = 33.3%), a post-hoc risk. Mark (3) uses 120 questions per parent. If B2 and blind are roughly independent, the paired SD is about 0.48 per question, the SE about 4.4 points and the 95% half-width about 9 points (suggested, my estimate). The mark needs B2 right-reach near 34%, against a tier-1 blind pooled first-fit of about 24% (22 of 90 at 512). The evidence for B2 is far lower: P0 had 1 right in 240 question-trials at 32 tries, and that hit was op_define or unit_convert, not a numeric kind (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md lines 117-119).

10. Constants and sealed overlap (shown). B2 has constants 1, 2, 10 and 100 only (progparse.py:8). Sealed sq_plus and double_add parameters span 3 to 9 (rules_real.py:32-33), so the panel's 7 (mod7), 9 (mod9) and 3 and 6 (tetra) fall inside a sealed range. The idea concedes this for mod7, dist20, tetra and mod9. Building 7 or 6 or 20 from the constants also adds steps that the idea's step counts may not include. Mark (5) says 'at least 10 of 12 kinds' but the idea lists more than 12 names and does not say which 12.

11. Answer length is a confound the idea does not gate (shown for C2; untested for the panel). I checked data/c2/dev.jsonl: no C2 DEV answer has 4 or more digits (max 3). The panel includes 4 to 5 digit answers: cube_x (x cubed) reaches 5 digits for x of 22 or more, and the idea itself gives time mod 24000 as 5 digits. The T1 screen (architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md lines 23-26) shows copy accuracy falling to 14 to 59% at 4 digits and about 1% at 5 for a different model. B2's talker copy at 4 or more digits is untested in the files. Gate 5 uses the program-level forced bound, so a copy shortfall would be misread as a sampler mismatch. Either add a copy check by digit length or keep the first panel to answers of 3 digits or fewer.

12. Sampling and forcing details (shown, code). sampler.sample_run's first argument forces step 1 only (the 'if t == 1 and first is not None' branch), so a probability for the whole reference program needs the teacher-forced path (fastsleep.head_inputs), whose agreement with sampling is untested. legal.sample_run_masked defaults to level 4, the used-number mask retired with C1 (legal.py:47). Gate 3 should compare against level 0 (legal.raw_samples, legal.py:196), which is what C2 samples with.

13. The cost estimate is untested and probably low. The 210 tries per second in the cost line appears in no file (the 210 values in the notes are record counts). The only file estimate, MAC-JOB-8.md line 21, is 600 to 700 stuck questions times 480 tries, or 1.5 to 2.5 h per parent (untested). That implies roughly 35 to 70 tries per second. The B2 arm is 12 kinds times 40 questions times 512 samples times 2 parents, about 490k samples, so about 2 to 4 h at that rate. The blind 50k arm adds about 22 minutes if the 1.8 s per question holds (untested). The stated 1.5 h is probably low by about 2x.

14. Rule and labelling checks. I opened only dev.jsonl and the manifest (counts and hashes), not test or labelled rows, so no sealed split was read. Rule 10 (autonomy) is acknowledged as test-side and is fine. The idea cites no papers, so there were none to check. The shown and untested labels are wrong in the places noted above (items 4 and 5).

problems: GATE 1 AS WRITTEN WOULD REJECT ALL 10 PRE-REGISTERED K_NEW KINDS (shown). The 50k clause (blind first-fit right at 50k <= 25%) fails every candidate in /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/sleep7d/knew-report-2026-10-07.json (conditions.*.b.first_fit_right_within_50000): add_sq 0.984, cube 1.0, double_sq 1.0, mod_plus 0.797, mult_sub 0.859, sq_minus 1.0, sq_mod 0.984, sq_plus_x 1.0, sub_from 0.344, triple_add 0.844. The 512 clause alone would pass 6 of them (their 1k values are 0 to 0.25). First-fit right cannot fall as the budget grows (the first fitting candidate is fixed once found; blind_baseline.py summarize), so any kind that blind solves at 6k fails the 50k clause. The clause therefore selects kinds blind never solves in 50k. The roadmap says breadth-first search finds every kind B2 can write in 5 steps or fewer (/mnt/project-files/creative-roadmap/creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md, about lines 1024-1028). Expect fewer than 4 survivors, or survivors B2 cannot write. Numbers: shown. Consequence: suggested.

GATE 1 IS POST HOC, NOT PRE-REGISTERED (shown in the idea text; suggested as bias). The candidate list and thresholds (33%, 25%, +10, +5) were set after blind numbers from w3d-1 on n=30 per kind, which were never saved. 'Gates fixed now' does not make the choice pre-registered. Sixty fresh questions cannot undo a selection made on the same kinds, and nothing corrects for picking at least 4 of about 21 named families. The K_new screen, by contrast, was pre-registered by hash (candidates_hash in the knew-report) before its numbers were seen.

UNIT MISMATCH BETWEEN B2 AND BLIND (shown). B2's 512 tries are raw samples with repeats (legal.py raw_samples, about lines 196-205, 'NO dedup'). Blind's 512 candidates are distinct value vectors (blind_baseline.py search_fits drops seen vectors). C2 DEV has 12.6 and 15.8 distinct rule-following programs per question (roadmap, about line 473), so B2's 512 samples cover far fewer distinct candidates than blind's 512. Also, the shared blind code reports only 1k, 6k and 50k (BUDGETS), so every 512 figure in the idea is a new run that exists nowhere.

GATE 3 COMPARES AN ORACLE WITH A CHECKED FIRST FIT (shown numbers; suggested effect on the verdict). B2 right-reach@512 is any of 512 tries being right, chosen by the key. Blind first-fit right is the checker's first fit. Any-right is never lower than first-fit-right on the same questions. In the K_new report at 50k, mod_plus shows first-fit right 0.797 and any-right 0.938, a 14-point gap from the selection rule alone. A +10 margin can therefore come from the rule rather than the model. Compare B2's first fitting try with blind's first fit, and report any-right only as an upper bound.

NO VALUE-BLIND FLOOR FOR 'RIGHT' (shown code gap; untested size). 'Right' is equality with the key, and no gate has a value-blind floor for it. If right is scored without requiring the example fit, a random program is right by chance about 1/k of the time on a k-valued answer, so any-right at 512 saturates on small-output kinds (mod7 gives 0-6; last_digit 0-9). Even with the fit required, chance hits are not subtracted. C2 used a value-blind floor for its fit gates (fewshot.py dev_gate, GATE_FLOOR_MULT 3.0) for this reason. Use key_luck (fits AND equals key, fewshot.py score_samples) and a per-kind right floor.

GATE 2 THRESHOLD IS ONE QUESTION (shown arithmetic). 2% of 40 questions is 0.8 questions, so 'right-reach >= 2% on both parents' per kind passes on a single lucky right answer. The K_new screen used 64 questions per kind. Require counts with an interval (for example at least 4 of 40 per kind), or pool across kinds with a stated interval.

GATE 5 CANNOT FAIL WHERE IT IS NEEDED AND HAS NO DENOMINATOR (shown formula; suggested looseness). The bound 1-(1-P_ref)^512 is near zero when P_ref is small, which is exactly the hard-kind case, so the check cannot fail there. One reference path also understates the chance of writing an equivalent program, since pointers can take several valid slots (sampler.py docstring), so the bound is loose. The denominator '10 of 12 kinds' is undefined: the idea names about 21 families, and gate 1 needs only 4 survivors.

THE IDEA'S OWN NUMBERS DISAGREE (text inconsistencies shown; the numbers themselves untested). (a) 'tri 0/28/30' at 512/1k/6k puts the cliff between 512 and 1k, but the why-text says it jumps at 6k. (b) The why-text denominators (dist20 8/9, digitsum 10/19, digitprod 4/6, reverse 0/2, x_plus_rev 0/0) cannot all be n=30 per kind; they look like fit counts. (c) tetra appears in the numbers and the overlap check but not in the candidate list. (d) cube_x shows 20/30 at 1k; if cube_x is x cubed, K_new's cube (first-fit right 1.0 at 1k, median 74 examined, in the knew-report) conflicts. K_new's definitions are hash-sealed and unreadable here, so this cannot be checked. (e) Nothing is saved: no panel code or result files were found under the scratchpad creative code or /mnt/project-files.

THE PARAMETER-OVERLAP CLAIM IS PARTLY WRONG ON THE IDEA'S OWN READING (shown from rules_real.py PARAMS). Held-out ranges are affine a 3-6 and b 3-15, sq_plus b 3-9, double_add b 3-9. CONSTANTS AND LANGUAGE (constants and op sets shown; step counts untested). Constants are only 1, 2, 10, 100 (progparse.py; programs.py CONSTS). CHECKER CONFLICT FOR CLAMP (shown code). fewshot.py structure() rejects any answer pointer to a prompt number other than the query input. A clamp whose edges are read from the example outputs cannot pass the checker. Either the edges are fixed constants built from 1, 2, 10, 100, or the kind is outside the checker's language. The idea does not say which.

chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right. It must not read the sealed test, the labelled file or any GOLD-PRIVATE panel. It is a measurement: do not train or sleep on any of its rows, and do not call it an autonomy result.

1. FIXED RULES BEFORE ANY NUMBER (inherit K_new, do not tune).
- The 10 candidates and their order are as in knew-report-2026-10-07.json (candidates_hash fc30f04a9a67bdbfd2917806aaf0bc260f8b71964c2758f5a7cd62e799535050). Do not add any.
- A kind QUALIFIES if all three hold: (a) representable; (b) blind search fits at most 20% of DEV within its first 512 candidates examined; (c) N' reach@512 is 2-40% on BOTH parents (K_new ruling, 64 rows per kind).
- Pass: at least 4 kinds qualify. The ruling's stop-and-report applies if fewer than 4 qualify.
- DROP the 50k purity cap. Blind first-fit-right is non-decreasing, so the cap empties the panel. Report 50k as context only.

2. WHAT THE RESULT MEANS.
- 4 or more kinds qualify: the roadmap's S1 may proceed on those kinds, as ruled. Still a 2-parent screen, with no claim.
- Fewer than 4 qualify and the reachability bound or the sampled right-reach is at most 1 question of 64 on every 4-5 step kind: cold start is total, so model-made stepping stones (C6) are needed before any sleep test on search-hard kinds. This is the likely outcome (suggested; from N' = 0 at 32 tries on all of them, C2 multi-step 1.9-5.2%, affine 0-4%).
- Reachability bound and sampled reach disagree by more than 5 points on 10 or more kind-parent cells, or greedy teacher-forced and raw_samples differ: the sampler and forced path must be reconciled first. No creative number counts until then.
- To prove the idea wrong, any one of these suffices: P_ref bound under 0.1% and sampled right-reach 0 on both parents for all six blind-hard kinds; or B2/N' first-fit-right at 512 minus blind first-fit-right at 512 under +5 on both parents on the pooled blind-hard kinds. The second is checker-picked on both sides, with any-right never used for the margin. Add 'zero for the cold start' as the stated null.

3. STATISTICS. Report counts out of 64 per kind with Wilson intervals, and give pooled paired-bootstrap intervals over the six blind-hard kinds. Per-kind 2% bars are one question (1/64 = 1.6 points), so never gate on a single hit. Qualification uses the ruled 2-40% band, but the written readout must also say how many questions that is (2% of 64 is 1.3 questions, so effectively at least 2).

4. UNITS. State candidates examined for blind and raw draws for the model on every table, and add distinct value vectors for both. Do not claim 'matched cost' unless distinct counts are shown. For the blind arm, add CMP (op 8) to the searcher or show no reference needs it.

5. SAVE EVERYTHING. Per-question rows go to a results file in the repo before the numbers are quoted. Mark every quoted number shown only with a file citation. Treat D1's inline figures (tri, cube_x, dist20, 27.5-point escalation gain, 1.8 s per question) as untested and do not quote them. Settle blind_baseline.summarize on dev.jsonl: first-fit-right and any-right keys at 1k/6k, re-run in a torch-enabled environment (this sandbox has no torch).

6. COST. Time one parent end to end and replace the 210/s figure. Teacher-forced reachability first, as it costs minutes. Sample only the kinds that need it. Run order: reachability, then one parent timed, then both parents, then the raw-B2 column. If job 9 still occupies the Mac, run on Ben's PC CPU.

7. SIDE ARM (optional, only if cheap). Blind escalation from 512 up to 6,000 when nothing fits is report-only. Report first-fit purity at 3 examples, because wrong fits are what sleep would learn from (D1's 40% purity figure is unsaved).

8. PLAIN-LANGUAGE SUMMARY FOR BEN (high-school senior): 'We already picked 10 new rule kinds and sealed them. A simple brute-force searcher with no model solves some of them fast and some not at all inside a few hundred checks. Before spending hours having the model try, we first measure whether the model can write the right program at all, even by luck. If it cannot, the model needs to make its own easier practice problems first, and a sleep test on these kinds would just waste computer time.' Also state outright that this is a measurement on kinds we picked by hand, so it cannot count as the model choosing its own practice (rule 10).

9. KEEP SEPARATE. B2 and the C2 line only. Do not mix with the village model.

plan.title: K_new 512-try screen: cold start on six kinds
plan.ben_line: We locked 10 made-up rule puzzles ahead of time, and a plain search with no AI never gets the right answer on six of them within 512 guesses. This test asks whether the model can get those six right within 512 tries of its own; since we picked the puzzles by hand, it can only show whether the test is usable, not that the model chooses its own practice.
plan.question: At the loop's real budget of 512 tries per stuck question (32, then 480 more if none fits), does B2 fit an example-checked answer on at least 2 and at most 25 of 64 DEV questions per kind, on both parents s100 and s101, for at least 4 of the six kinds that blind search cannot solve within 512 candidates?
plan.one_change: Re-measure the ruled K_new conditions (b) and (c) at 512 tries instead of 32, on the same ten frozen candidates and the same 64 DEV rows per kind, with sampling temperature fixed at 3.0 (job 8's value, not re-picked on K_new). Everything else is a pre-run gate or a reading, not a change to the rules.
arms: A calibration (gate 0b): rebuilt N' on s100 and s101, 32 tries on the four 2-step controls (cube, double_sq, sq_mod, sq_plus_x). These are not qualifiers: each fits 98% or more of DEV questions within 1,000 candidates (shown: knew-report), so they fail condition (b) at 512 by construction.

B main: rebuilt N', 512 tries per DEV question on the six blind-hard kinds (add_sq, mod_plus, mult_sub, sub_from, triple_add, sq_minus), 64 rows each, both parents. Pass 1 = 32 tries; pass 2 = 480 more on questions with no fit (c2_stuck.search, unchanged). Temperature 3.0.
C blind search (no model, no key in the search): the same 640 DEV rows; budgets 512, 1k, 6k and 50k candidates examined; ops 1-7 for qualification; ops 1-8 (CMP) as a sensitivity column only.
D raw B2 column: the same six kinds at 512 tries on the raw s100 and s101 checkpoints (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/), reported apart from N'.
E value-blind floors per kind: fit floor and right floor from random programs drawn as fewshot.value_blind_floor draws them, with the pyfit prefilter first.

F reachability diagnostic: teacher-forced lower bound 1-(1-P_ref)^512 at T 1 and T 3 for each reference program. Reported only, never a skip gate. Greedy agreement on 20 rows per kind is a gate (gate 0c).
plan.seeds: Screen: 2 parents, s100 and s101 (rule 4: a 2-parent screen, no claim), 64 DEV rows per kind, 10 kinds. Confirm: 6 parents, s200-s205.
plan.machine: Ben's RTX 5070 Ti PC, CPU only (rule 6). The M1 Pro is busy with job 9 for about 10 h (MAC-JOB-9.md estimate, untested). Torch must be installed: blind_baseline imports custom_io.data (reader copy, data.py:4), which imports torch.
pass_marks: Gate 0 (provenance, before any number): the knew-v1 builder and candidate file are recovered, reproduce candidates_hash fc30f04a9a67bdbfd2917806aaf0bc260f8b71964c2758f5a7cd62e799535050 (shown: /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/sleep7d/knew-report-2026-10-07.json), and regenerate 64 DEV rows per kind. Stop if not. The ten kinds' list order must come from that file, since the report's conditions block is alphabetical and does not record it.

Gate 0b (calibration): rebuilt N' at T 3.0 reproduces the four controls' 32-try fit-reach inside the 95% Wilson interval of the report's values (shown): cube 1/64 and 0/64; double_sq 13/64 and 34/64; sq_mod 0/64 and 0/64; sq_plus_x 31/64 and 26/64 (s100 and s101). Stop if not.

Gate 0c (sampler agreement): on 20 rows per kind, the teacher-forced argmax path matches sampler.sample_run(greedy=True) and legal.raw_samples at level 0, step for step. A mismatch stops the run until reconciled.

Qualify, per kind and per parent, fixed now, counts out of 64: (a) representable as the report says (passed; mod_plus has 3 of 7 parameter values usable, mult_sub 40 of 52, sub_from 15 of 16); (b) blind fit within 512 candidates examined on at most 12 of 64 DEV rows, ops 1-7 as ruled (12/64 = 18.8% passes; 13/64 = 20.3% fails); (c) B2 fit-reach@512 on 2 to 25 of 64 rows on BOTH parents (2/64 = 3.1% passes; 1/64 = 1.6% fails; 25/64 = 39.1% passes; 26/64 = 40.6% fails).
Pass: at least 4 of the six kinds qualify. S1 may then run on those kinds as a 2-parent screen, with no claim. Fewer than 4 is the ruled stop-and-report (roadmap section 7d, about lines 1035-1046).

Efficiency reading (reported, not a qualifier; pooled over all six kinds on both parents): B2 first-fit-right@512 minus its value-blind right floor is at least +5 points, with the paired interval above 0. Blind first-fit-right@512 is 0 on all six kinds (derived from the report: the earliest right fit on any DEV question is at candidate 805, mult_sub), so this margin is also the margin over blind.
plan.proved_wrong: The idea is proved wrong if fewer than four of the six kinds qualify (the ruled stop). That shows these kinds are not a usable creative test at 512 tries; it does not show that B2 cannot learn these rules. If fit-reach@512 is at most 1 of 64 on every kind on both parents, the cold start is total, and no sleep test on these kinds should run until model-made stepping stones (C6) exist. The efficiency reading is proved wrong if its pooled interval's upper end is below +5 on either parent. Scale of a zero result: 0 hits over 64 questions by 512 tries bounds the per-try fit rate near 1e-4 (suggested: rule of three on 32,768 tries).
plan.null_risk: High for the count, and the outcome is open rather than predicted. Shown: fit-reach@32 is 0 of 64 on all six kinds on both parents (knew-report). Qualifying needs a per-try fit rate near 6e-5 (suggested: 1-(1-p)^512 = 2/64), and the 32-try zeros are consistent with rates up to about 1.5e-3 (suggested: rule of three on 2,048 tries per kind per parent). The marks can pass with no real change in four ways: (1) condition (b) already holds for five of six kinds (shown: fit within 1,000 candidates is 0 or 1 of 64), so only sq_minus (16 of 64 at 1,000) is open and the count rests on (c); (2) the (c) band starts at 2 of 64, which two value-blind fits could supply, so the floors must be reported beside it (suggested reading: a kind whose B2 reach sits inside the floor's interval counts as luck; this reading is not in the ruling); (3) the efficiency reading is against a zero blind baseline, so a few value-blind right answers can pass it; (4) the 64 DEV rows were already read at 32 tries after the budget was changed (disclosed in roadmap 7d), so the qualifiers are partly chosen on the rows they are scored on.
plan.autonomy: Measurement only. No training, no sleep, and no row changes the model; this is not an autonomy result. The deployed loop's steps on these kinds, and who sets each: (1) B2 writes tries with its own weights at temperature 3.0, a setting we fixed from C2 DEV work; (2) each try is checked by the example check, a hand-written tool with no answer key and no kind label (fewshot.verdict); (3) the budget is 32 tries, then 480 more where nothing fits, a hand rule (c2_stuck.search); (4) the answer is the first fitting try. The answer key is read only to score. Steps 2 and 3 are hand code, so the arm is "no outside help" for the tries but not "own choices" under roadmap section 7c. The ten kinds were picked by hand: held-out measurement only, never practice.
steps: Changes to the brief, checked against the files: (i) the P_ref bound is a lower bound and, for 4-5 step references, is probably near zero (suggested: sampler.py:85 draws op, a and b independently at each step), so it is a diagnostic only; using it as a skip gate would stop all six kinds before any sampling. (ii) Temperature is 3.0 for both parents, as job 8 ran (MAC-JOB-8.md line 3). c2b's per-parent DEV re-pick would give 4.0 for s101 (c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md lines 8 and 43), and re-picking on K_new DEV would be a fit on the scored rows. (iii) Condition (b) stays on ops 1-7, as ruled and as the report was computed (fewshot.py:232); CMP (ops 1-8, programs.py:45) is a sensitivity column, and any change it causes is reported, not re-qualified. (iv) fastsleep.head_inputs (fastsleep.py:127-157) returns states, not probabilities, so the bound needs new code. (v) fewshot.value_blind_floor counts fits only (fewshot.py:291-308), so the right floor is new code. (vi) The 210 tries per second is in no file (grep of creative-pilot, creative-roadmap and fast-sleep). (vii) The N' rebuild needs train.jsonl and data_big, which are not under /mnt/project-files.

Seal first: write the marks, the six kinds, temperature 3.0, the 512 budget, the 64 DEV rows per kind, the count bands, and the ops-1-7 rule into the results folder before any number exists. Do not open K_new TEST, the C2 test or labelled files, or any GOLD-PRIVATE or blind panel.

Gate 0 (provenance): recover the knew-v1 builder and candidate file (the roadmap names commits 07abf1eea and 91fda2267; neither exists in /home/user/learner, checked with git cat-file). Check the hash and the row counts. Check how many examples each DEV prompt has (the loop's default is k_ex=3, rules_real.py:128; the K_new rows' count is not in the report). Record the maximum answer digits per kind, since B2's copy at 4+ digits is untested.

Gate 0b (calibration): rebuild N' for s100 and s101 with the c2_keep route (warm-up, stones sleep with replay, seed 0; c2_keep.py docstring). Do not substitute fast-sleep/parents/s100/N_ss.pt unless it passes gate 0b. Run the four controls at 32 tries and check them against the report.
Gate 0c (agreement): on 20 rows per kind, compare the teacher-forced argmax path with sampler.sample_run(greedy=True) and with legal.raw_samples at level 0 (level 0 is sample_run, legal.py:49-51).

Marginalise the operand draws on NOOP steps, because sampler.py:85 and 106-108 keep sampled a and b even when the op is NOOP. Report 1-(1-P_ref)^512 as a lower bound on any-right. Suggested, not measured: single-program probabilities for 4-5 step references are likely far below 1e-6, so the bound will be near zero and will not separate anything.

Blind arm (CPU; the notes' 1.8 s per question is inline and unsaved, so untested): for the 640 DEV rows, call blind_baseline.search_fits with budget 50,000 and max_fits 64, ops 1-7 (SEARCH_OPS, fewshot.py:232). Save each question's list of (examined index, value, right flag) before summarising. Compute counts at 512, 1k, 6k and 50k; summarize() reads BUDGETS of 1k, 6k and 50k only (blind_baseline.py:11). Run ops 1-8 as a sensitivity column in a copy of the code.

Estimate: about 0.4 million tries per parent including raw; at 210 per second that is about 30 min per parent, at 35 per second about 3 h (both untested).

idea.title: Affine wall ladder: census, class ranking, per-step writability
idea.summary: Affine stays at 0-4% in every arm and nobody knows if B2 cannot write the program, cannot tell the class from the examples, or writes it but never samples it. One forward-only ladder of probes on raw and warmed parents separates the three, and each branch points to a different cheap fix. The seven-step cap is not the cause (all affine pairs are representable).
idea.change: Probe only, new read-only script under creative/. Part 0: confirm sampler greedy equals Ledger.run greedy (tests exist but were not run). Part 1 census: 32 tries per affine question (205 pool, 52 DEV) at T 1.4 and T 3.0; sort each try by its exact outputs over the 26 DOMAIN inputs into not-an-affine-function, affine wrong class, right class; swap control (same query, examples from another class where the answer differs); read count (tries that read a non-query prompt number and reproduce every unread pair). Part 2 teacher-forced class ranking: log-probability of each of the 49 usable class reference programs with the real examples minus the mean over 3 placebo example sets at the same query; positive control fresh practised add. Part 3 per-step gold-prefix agreement against all minimal programs per class (cap 20), with controls fresh add, fresh mult and one-step kinds square/last_digit. Part 4 train-fit: greedy first try on the 410 pool affine rows the PC arm trained on.
idea.why: Shown: affine first try is 0-4% in N, PC, PC' and W; PC reach@32 is 9.6% at T 1.0 with 24.1 distinct structure-valid expressions per question, so tries vary but almost none compute the right class. A class-list follower that ignored the examples would hit 1/49 = 2.0% per try, about 30 times the observed rate. Shown by count: the first two examples of every DEV and pool affine question already pin one affine class, so the failure is in B2. The three affine pairs listed as not shown representable ARE representable (5-6 steps), and every usable pair needs at most 5, so the 7-step limit cannot be the wall. Explanations (a) forgotten parts and (b) cannot build a parameter are both only suggested.

test.pass_mark: Fixed before running, 95% bootstrap over questions, both parents. WRITABLE if affine-function share >=0.30 at T 1.4; NOT WRITABLE if <0.05. IDENTIFIED if own-class share >=0.10 and swap-class share >=0.05, both lower bounds above 0.02. CLASS SIGNAL if teacher-forced top-1 >=0.10 (chance 0.020) with lower bound above 0.05 and add control top-1 >=0.50. Per-step WRITABLE if affine agreement >=0.80 at every step and piece agreement >=0.80; COMPOSITION wall if pieces >=0.80 but join-step <0.50. Train-fit <=10% means underfit, >=50% means memorised not identified. ROUTE LIVE if read-and-fits share >=0.05 (opens the relaxed-check idea).
test.proved_wrong: 'Not identified' is wrong if swap-class share has a lower bound above 0.02. 'Not writable' is wrong if affine-function share >=0.30. 'Parameter not writable' is wrong if both piece controls score >=0.80. 'Composition wall' is wrong if join-step agreement >=0.80. If the add control fails class ranking the method is void.

chair.reasons:
Verdict: worth a cheap, re-scoped CPU probe. As written it is not ready to run.

Why it is worth doing:
- Affine is the one creative wall with a clean spec (shown: 0-4% first try in every arm, creative-pilot/c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md and results/c2stones, c2keep).
- Ben's rule says new creative tests must use kinds where blind search fails, and affine is one (shown: 6 of 52 DEV questions get a fit by 6k candidates, per the fact check).
- The probe is forward-only on a 3.3M model, with no GPU, no training and no teacher (rules 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 pass).
- It separates three causes that nobody has separated: cannot write, cannot tell the class from the examples, can write but never samples it. Explanations (a) and (b) in roadmap section 7 are only suggested; the GPT reply is not in any file.
- It is a developer diagnostic, so rule 10 does not bind the probe itself (autonomy critic). It binds every fix it points to.

Haiku-critic findings I weighed (re-checked where noted):
- I confirmed by ls: N_ss.pt, warm.pt and setup.pt exist for s200-s205 under /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm/, and raw B2 s200-s205 exist under CODE/b2ckpt. So a 6-seed run is possible without any training. Rule 4 therefore forbids a 2-seed verdict.
- The census cannot do its job as written (shown by count from the result JSON): right-class affine tries are about 1 (warm4, T 1.4), 3-20 (stones parent, T 1.0) and 6 (PC) out of 1,664 samples per arm. The IDENTIFIED bar (own-class share >=0.10) is 8-170 times higher than anything seen. The teacher-forced class ranking is the only part with real power, so make it the main test.
- Raw B2 is useless for a census (shown: results/c2dev/nowarm-s100.json, distinct_rules 0.0 at T 0.5-1.4; the file has no T 2.0 or 3.0). It never writes a checker-valid program, so use it only to report that zero.
- Part 4 (train-fit on the 410 PC rows) is not forward-only. No PC or warm4 checkpoint is saved (c2_stones.py saves only the warm base). Drop it.
