chair.revised_idea:
Affine wall probe, v2: read-only, forward-only, CPU, six seeds. A diagnostic that ships nothing and counts as a 6-seed descriptive screen, with no sealed claim. Build one new script under creative/ that reads only dev.jsonl and pool.jsonl and never touches test.jsonl or labelled.jsonl.

Parents:
- warm.pt (add/mult warm-up only, no affine exposure) and N_ss.pt (stones parent), for s200-s205, from /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm/. Add s100/s101 as extra rows.
- Raw B2 only to confirm and report that it writes no checker-valid program. Never read it as the warmed parent.
- N_ss was taught hand-written affine stones (a=2), so label it 'stones parent, not a no-hand-code baseline'. warm.pt is the clean zero-affine reading.

Splits: pool 205 affine questions is the primary split. None of the parents above trained on pool affine rows, which PC did. DEV 52 is the replication split. Record in the report that affine has 49 usable classes out of 52 and that (3,15), (5,13), (6,15) are excluded only by the 600k-state search cap. Do not change any split.

Part 0, parity gate (all later parts void if it fails): for each parent, the sampler's greedy ops, pointers and answers equal Ledger.run's on all 257 affine rows (and on a fixed 200 add/mult rows). Check the B2 config's eg_embed (default False, ledger.py:131) before trusting the reader path. Use fastsleep.head_inputs (fastsleep.py:126-158) for teacher-forced per-step forcing, not Ledger.run(gold=...), which forces masked-argmax slots.

Part 1, census (descriptive counts per question, not share thresholds). Run a fixed grid T 0.5, 1.0, 1.4, 2.0, 3.0, 32 tries per question, and report all five, with no DEV-picked T as the mark. For each question report:
- structure-valid share;
- reads-x share;
- reads-a-non-query-number share;
- reads-a-non-query-number-and-reproduces-every-example share ('read-route', using a relaxed structure function that is named in the spec);
- right-class reach, meaning the try computes the true (A,B) on all 26 DOMAIN inputs;
- affine-with-slope-in-3..6 share.
Report every share next to a measured value-blind sampler rate on the same questions (fewshot.value_blind_floor machinery, which is 0.0 for every DEV affine question). Report the A/B pairs reached. State denominators (all 32 tries versus structure-valid tries). Add the swap control: same query, examples drawn from a different class whose answer at that query differs, asserted in code. Add a hand-checked read-route family count, y1 + ((y2-y1)/(x2-x1))*(x-x1), which takes 6 steps.

Part 2, the main test, teacher-forced class ranking.
- Score each of the 49 affine classes as the logsumexp, over all its minimal programs (cap 20, new enumeration code), of the teacher-forced log-probability. That log-probability includes the NOOP tail and the answer pointer. Remap the stored programs to a 3-example prompt with the query at slot 6 (rules_real.remap), since references are stored for the 5-example layout with the query at slot 10.
- Adjusted score = real-example score minus the mean over 3 placebo example sets. A placebo set keeps the same query, the same example count and similar digit length. It comes from other affine questions whose answer at this query differs from the true one. It must not be the true class.
- Top-1 over 49 classes, chance 1/49 = 0.020, plus top-5.
- Controls: fresh practised add/mult (stones.fresh_practised), whose candidate set is the 28 add classes (chance 0.036), and the swap control (the ranking should follow the example class). The control must reach top-1 >= 0.50 or the method is void. Report each parent's raw add/mult accuracy first.

Part 3, per-step screen. Run only if Part 2 shows a signal or gives 'unclear'. Define each term before running:
- piece = the sub-program that builds the parameter, such as 10 DIV 2 = 5;
- join step = the step that combines it with x;
- agreement = the gold-prefix argmax match against the minimal-program set.
Controls: fresh add, fresh mult, square, last_digit. Use s100/s101 plus any four more seeds only if it passes.

Dropped from the original: Part 4 (train-fit on the 410 PC rows), because no PC checkpoint exists. If it is wanted later, re-run PC and save its checkpoint as its own step.

Schedule: queue after job 9 finishes on the Mac, or run on the PC's CPU. Estimate 1-2 CPU hours (untested; the 126-210 tries/s figure is not a settled number).
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must fix all of the following before any run. Label each statement shown, suggested or untested.

1. Seeds and parents.
- Run warm.pt and N_ss.pt for s200-s205 (shown to exist by ls under /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm/). Add s100/s101 as extra rows.
- The Part 0 parity gate needs a pass mark: identical ops, pointers and answers on all 257 affine rows per parent. If it fails, void everything and fix the sampler first.
- Raw B2 is a sanity row only (shown: it writes no structure-valid program, so a raw census is empty).
- Every verdict is labelled 'six-seed screen, descriptive', not a claim.

2. Main test: teacher-forced class ranking, on pool (205 questions) first and DEV (52) as replication.
- Score = logsumexp over all minimal programs per class (cap 20), with the NOOP tail and answer pointer included, remapped to the 3-example prompt (query slot 6).
- Subtract the mean of 3 placebo example sets with the same query and different answers.
- Pass marks, fixed in advance:
  - CLASS SIGNAL if pool top-1 >= 0.15 with Wilson lower bound > 0.05 on at least 5 of 6 seeds, and the add control top-1 >= 0.50 (add has 28 classes, chance 0.036).
  - NO SIGNAL if top-1 upper bound < 0.06 on at least 5 of 6 seeds.
  - Anything else is 'unclear', and every band must be written out.
- Power (suggested, a critic's simulation): a true top-1 of 0.10 passes the bar about 50% of the time on pool and 43% on DEV, and a true 0.15 passes about 98% on pool. So 0.15 is the mark. A true value of about 0.10 will read 'unclear' by design.
- It is proved wrong in these cases:
  - 'No signal' is wrong if pool top-1 >= 0.15 with lower bound > 0.05.
  - The method is void if the add control fails.
  - Identification is void if the swap control does not follow the example class.

3. Census as counts, not share thresholds.
- Use a fixed temperature grid (0.5, 1.0, 1.4, 2.0, 3.0), not a DEV-picked T.
- Report per question: structure-valid share, reads-x share, right-class reach, slope-3..6 affine share, and the read-route family (read-and-fits).
- Put a measured value-blind rate next to every share (floor is 0.0 on DEV affine). A bare 'affine-function share >= 0.30' is not a valid mark: a value-blind linear sampler can reach about 0.15-0.37 (suggested), and trivial functions like x+1 and 2x count.
- The census cannot return IDENTIFIED from the saved right-class rates (shown: about 1-20 hits in 1,664 samples). State that it is expected to be near empty, which is why it is not the main test.
- The ROUTE LIVE mark (read-and-fits share >= 0.05) needs its not-live band (< 0.01) written out and a swap-control check.

4. Build the swap control and the placebo sets with assertions in code that the query answer really changes. There is no existing code for either (grep found none).

5. Branch table must be rule-10 compliant. Write down what each outcome does before running, and do not list the following as shippable fixes:
- the 49-way class head (generator labels);
- fresh generator example sets;
- hand-composed practice;
- edits to the hand checker.
Compliant follow-ups to name:
- CLASS SIGNAL but census near empty ('writes it but never samples it' — the case the original table had no branch for): model-ordered search or a learned verdict head trained on the model's own checker verdicts (C4, AUC >= 0.80). The ordered-search algorithm is a fixed design constant and the checker is hand code until B3 exists, so flag both for the lead.
- NO SIGNAL: the checker as a model-called tool whose reply carries per-example values ('fail: got 17, want 19'; fewshot.outputs_py and parse()['ys'] already hold them), and the 10M scaling question. No compliant fix exists in the files for a model that cannot identify the class at all. Say so plainly.
- Do not train any arm on pool affine classes without noting that pool, DEV and test share the same 49 classes.

6. Report the corrections:
- PC greedy affine is 0/52 (s100) and 2/52 (s101) for the job-5 c2stones PC. The 1/52 figure is the job-6 c2pilot PC arm. Name the job for every PC number.
- The 2.0% class-list chance is a computed bound that assumes the class list is known. It is not a value-blind floor.
- 'The failure is in B2' is not shown by the two-example pin.

7. Schedule and cost.
- Do not run on the Mac while job 9 runs (it takes about 10 h on CPU, estimate untested). Queue after job 9, or use the PC's CPU.
- Cost is 1-2 CPU hours (untested).
- Read only dev.jsonl and pool.jsonl. Do not open test.jsonl or labelled.jsonl, which are sealed.

8. Plain-language summary for Ben (a high-school senior): 'We ask the model, without making it guess answers, whether it can tell which affine rule (y = a*x + b) the three example pairs show. If it can, the problem is how it writes programs. If not, it is not learning rules from examples yet.'

Also tell the lead that this probe's value is as a go/no-go for the whole 'few-example rule learning' line, with a prior that 'weak or no signal' is the likeliest result (suggested). It does not depend on job 9's outcome.

plan.title: Affine class-ranking probe v2 (read-only, CPU)
plan.ben_line: We check whether, after seeing three example pairs, the model leans toward the right rule (like y = 3x + 7) over the other 48 rules more than it leans when shown fake examples. If it does not lean, it is not yet using the examples to find the rule.
plan.question: Does B2's own probability over programs prefer the affine rule that the three example pairs pin, beyond what the same programs get from placebo example sets, and does that preference follow the examples rather than their digits? Primary parent: warm.pt (add/mult warm-up only). Value: a go/no-go for the whole few-example rule line. Suggested prior: unclear or no signal is the likeliest result. Independent of job 9.
plan.one_change: One new read-only, forward-only CPU script that scores B2's own program probabilities for the 49 usable affine classes, given the real examples versus three placebo example sets, with add, swap-follow and permuted-value controls. No training, no new parameters, and no change to any split, checker, sampler or gate.
arms: warm: warm.pt, the checkpoint after the 2,048-row add/mult warm-up (4 visits, lr 3e-4, 200,000 skills replay rows; shown: fast-sleep/confirm/s20X/warm.pt, c2_stones.py:16-20 and 51-52, c2dev/s100.json warmup.replay=200000). Primary and clean: the warm split holds only add and mult (shown: MANIFEST warm kinds add 1024, mult 1024). Seeds s200-s205.

N_ss: N_ss.pt, warm.pt plus 2,048 stepping-stone rows (shown: setup.json ss records 2048). The stones include affine slope 2 with b 3-15 and affine a 3-6 with b 1-2 (shown: stones.py:9-10), which are outside the 49 usable classes. A stones parent, not a no-hand-code baseline. Seeds s200-s205; s100 and s101 N_ss.pt are extra screen rows only.

raw B2: B2_s200-s205 checkpoint.pt under scratchpad/code/b2ckpt (sha256 files present). Sanity row only. Its top-1 should sit near chance; a Wilson lower bound above 0.05 means a scorer leak, so stop.

Controls on each warm and N_ss parent: add (205 fresh add-only questions over the 28 usable add classes; top-1 and swap-follow); swap-follow on the affine placebo-1 prompt (descriptive); permuted-value (affine gate; add descriptive).

Census (descriptive, one mark only: ROUTE): 32 samples per question at fixed T 0.5, 1.0, 1.4, 2.0, 3.0 on pool and DEV. No T chosen on DEV. About 65 s per temperature per 256 questions at the shown rate of about 125 samples per second (c2dev/s100.json), so about 65 min for 12 parents.
Not arms: PC (trained on pool affine rows, so the pool is contaminated for it; shown c2_stones.py:88); W, R, H, M and the sealed test (job 9); the stones arms SS and P.
plan.seeds: Six paired seeds s200-s205 for warm and N_ss: 12 checkpoints, all present under /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm (shown by ls). s100 and s101 have N_ss.pt only and no warm.pt (shown: fast-sleep/parents/README.md and folder listing), so they are screen rows outside the six-seed marks. Raw B2 sanity rows for s200-s205 (shown: scratchpad/code/b2ckpt). Rule 4 is met only by the six-seed marks.
plan.machine: CPU only. Ben's PC CPU if it is free; otherwise the M1 Pro after job 9 (job 9 holds the Mac for about 10 h on six parents, untested: MAC-JOB-9.md lines 29). The PC GPU is busy until q39 ends (MAC-JOB-9.md line 29), so no GPU.
pass_marks: PARITY (void everything if it fails): for each parent, on real checkpoints, the sampler's greedy ops, operand pointers, answer pointer, values and valid flags match Ledger.run's exactly on all 257 affine rows (pool 205 + DEV 52) and 200 fresh add/mult rows. Must be 100 percent. test_c1.test_sampler checks only a random model, so it does not count as this gate.

ADD CONTROL (method valid; void if it fails): on at least 5 of 6 warm seeds, (a) top-1 over the 28 add classes is at least 0.50 (chance 1/28 = 0.036) on 205 fresh add-only questions, and (b) swap-follow on add (top-1 equals the swap prompt's class) is at least 0.50. Untested risk: the warm base's sampled first try on fresh add/mult is only 0.20-0.27 (shown: c2stones s100/s101 practised_check first_try 0.266/0.203), so the 0.50 bar may fail for reasons unrelated to affine. If it fails, no affine verdict may be read.

PERMUTED-VALUE CONTROL (gate for any signal): on at least 5 of 6 warm seeds, the true class's adjusted score under the real examples exceeds its adjusted score under the permuted-output examples (outputs shuffled among the example inputs, not the identity, permutations that fit any affine class dropped and counted). Paired question-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples): 95 percent lower bound of the mean difference above 0.

CLASS SIGNAL (primary, warm parent): on at least 5 of 6 seeds, pool top-1 over the 49 classes has a Wilson 95 percent lower bound above 0.05 (the smallest passing count is 17 of 205), AND gates 2 and 3 pass. Suggested power (exact binomial, n=205, independent questions, computed here): 0.71 at true top-1 0.10, 0.98 at 0.12, 0.00 at chance 0.020. Replaces the brief's 'top-1 at least 0.15 and lower bound above 0.05', which passes only 51 percent per seed and 12 percent on 5 of 6 at a true 0.15.

NO SIGNAL (primary, warm parent): on at least 5 of 6 seeds, pool top-1 has a Wilson 95 percent upper bound below 0.08, and gate 2 passes. Suggested null pass rate 0.99 at chance; 0.01 at true 0.05; 0.00 at 0.10. Replaces the brief's 'upper bound below 0.06', which passes only 55 percent under the null.

UNCLEAR: anything else. A true top-1 between about 0.05 and 0.10 mostly lands here (at true 0.10, CLASS SIGNAL 0.71 and NO SIGNAL 0.00, so UNCLEAR about 0.29). Report the per-seed table; do not re-run with changed marks.

N_ss and raw B2 use the same bands and are reported beside the warm verdict. A CLASS SIGNAL on N_ss alone is a stones effect (the stones taught affine-like programs) and cannot be claimed for the autonomous path. Raw B2 with a lower bound above 0.05 means a scorer leak, so stop.

CENSUS (descriptive; the only mark is ROUTE): per question and per fixed T, report structure-valid share, reads-x share, reads-a-non-query-number share, right-class reach (outputs equal the true (A,B) on all DOMAIN inputs), affine slope 3-6 share, and read-and-fits share (relaxed read rule, all examples reproduced). Each share sits next to a value-blind rate on the same questions (fewshot.value_blind_floor machinery; the DEV affine floor is 0.0 for all 52 questions, shown in dev_floors-s100.json). ROUTE LIVE if pool read-and-fits share has a Wilson lower bound above 0.01 on at least 5 of 6 seeds; NOT LIVE if its upper bound is below 0.01 on at least 5 of 6; else unclear. ROUTE only opens a relaxed-check idea; it is not a build.
plan.proved_wrong: NO SIGNAL is proved wrong if warm pool top-1 has a Wilson lower bound above 0.05 on at least 5 of 6 seeds with gates 1-3 passing. CLASS SIGNAL is proved wrong if the permuted-value control matches or beats the real examples (the ranking then follows digit content, not the rule), or if the add control or add swap-follow fails (method void; no affine verdict may be read). A raw-B2 lower bound above 0.05 proves a leak in the scorer. Interpretation, not a proof: a warm NO SIGNAL with the add control passing places the break at identifying the rule from examples, not at writing or sampling it.
plan.null_risk: Yes, the marks can pass with no real change, in three ways. (1) Digit-content shortcut: boosting programs whose constants or form resemble digits in the prompt would survive placebo subtraction, because the placebo prompts are digit-matched. The permuted-value gate targets this; its power is untested (suggested). (2) The add control checks method validity on add programs that the warm split trained, so a pass shows the scorer can detect a practised rule, not that affine transfers. (3) Example-driven form bias not tied to the rule survives subtraction; only the affine swap-follow share (descriptive) checks it. The brief's original marks were underpowered (see pass_marks 4 and 5; binomial numbers computed here, suggested). Independent questions are assumed; shared question difficulty across seeds makes the 5-of-6 numbers optimistic (suggested). Also untested: whether the add bar of 0.50 is reachable at all for these parents.
plan.autonomy: Developer diagnostic. Nothing here is a deploy-time step. Scoring may be hand-written under rule 1: the 49-class list and its reference programs (generator knowledge), the placebo, swap and permuted sets, the logsumexp, the cap of 20 programs, the census checker and the marks. None of these may become a runtime signal. The model-internal quantity read here (teacher-forced probability of the model's own program choices) counts as autonomous only if the model learns to produce it itself. Branch follow-ups, none built: (a) CLASS SIGNAL but census near empty (writes-but-does-not-sample): the model ranks its own candidate programs by its own likelihood, with a checker it calls by writing text (B3 tool loop, not built); the ordering constant is a fixed design choice to flag for the lead. (b) Gates pass but NO SIGNAL: no compliant fix exists in these files for a model that cannot use examples to choose the rule. Pre-training with hand-written worked traces on a new held-out family is allowed by rule 1 and is not a deploy step, but it needs a fresh sealed panel and a six-seed test. (c) Permuted-value gate fails: no build; it means the ranking is not identification.
steps: Brief corrections to carry into the readout (shown unless marked): DOMAIN is 3-29 without 10 (rules_real.py:26), not 2-29. The brief's power figures are wrong (pass_marks 4-5). The PC greedy affine figures 0/52 (s100) and 2/52 (s101) are from job 5 (c2stones, PC trained on pool), and PC is excluded. s100 and s101 have no warm.pt. The three excluded affine pairs have short programs by hand (suggested): (3,15) 4 steps (10 DIV 2 = 5; x+5; (x+5)+(x+5); +(x+5)); (5,13) 5 steps (5 = 10 DIV 2; 5x = MUL(x,5); +10; +2; +1); (6,15) 5 steps (5 = 10 DIV 2; 2x; 2x+5; 4x+10; 6x+15). fixed_plan.title: Affine class-ranking probe v3 (CPU, staged)
fixed_plan.ben_line: We check whether B2, after seeing three example pairs, puts more of its own odds on the one rule those pairs fit than on the others, and more than when the pairs are fake or scrambled. If it does not, it is not yet using the examples to pick the rule.
fixed_plan.question: Does warm B2's probability over constant-built affine programs shift toward the rule the examples pin, beyond placebo and permuted examples? This tests only the constant-built route.
fixed_plan.one_change: One new read-only CPU scorer over the 49 affine classes, with placebo, permuted and add controls. No training, no split, checker or gate change. The census becomes a later job.

fixed_plan.seeds: Stage 0: s200 warm only. Stage 1: warm s200-s205, only if Stage 0 passes.
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's PC CPU when free, otherwise the M1 Pro after job 9. No GPU.
pass_marks: Stage 0 gate (abort on fail): scorer equals a Ledger-based recompute on 50 rows (tolerance 1e-4); per-row sums equal head_loss on a batch; add control top-1 at least 0.50 over the 28 add classes; row count within the cap fixed before scoring.
Scoring: per question, rank the classes that are not placebo classes. Adjusted score = real score minus the mean of 3 digit-matched placebo scores (other class; query answer differs).

CLASS SIGNAL: on at least 5 of 6 warm seeds, the paired question-level 95 percent lower bound of (real minus permuted) is above 0, AND the top-1 Wilson lower bound is above 0.05 (17 of 205 is the first passing count).
NO SIGNAL: on at least 5 of 6 warm seeds, the top-1 Wilson upper bound is below 0.08 AND the contrast interval includes 0.
UNCLEAR otherwise. Report the per-seed table, with per-seed and 5-of-6 rates given separately. No re-run with new marks.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: CLASS SIGNAL is proved wrong if permuted matches or beats real on 4 or more seeds, or if the add control fails (method void). NO SIGNAL is proved wrong if the top-1 Wilson lower bound exceeds 0.05 on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Even a NO SIGNAL does not exclude example-reading routes; it only says constant-built programs do not shift with examples.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Digit-content artifacts can survive matched digit counts; the permuted contrast is the check, and its power is untested (suggested). Warm may be contaminated if the 200k replay has affine rows (untested until scanned). The 5-of-6 rule assumes independent seeds that share question sets, so pass rates are optimistic (suggested).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Developer diagnostic, not a deploy step. Candidate lists, placebo and permuted sets, and marks are test code (rule 1). The teacher-forced probability counts for autonomy only if a later build has the model produce it itself (B3 tool loop, not built). N_ss is a positive control with no autonomous claim (roadmap 7c).

Compute pool value-blind floors with the same machinery; report N_ss and raw B2 beside warm; write one readout labelled shown, suggested or untested.

final.why: The probe is sound and costs no GPU, but its main arm is built to come out empty. A parent that never wrote the 49 target programs will rank them near chance with or without examples, since warm-only affine luck was already 0.0006 per try (shown: c2dev). A NO SIGNAL result would therefore not separate "cannot read the rule from examples" from "was never taught it", which is the question the probe exists to answer. The informative parents, the ones sleep-trained on checked finds (the job 9 W arm), are on Ben's Mac and not available yet. In job 6, affine had only 5 and 1 records (shown: c2pilot readout), so even those may show little. The cost is also high for a diagnostic: about 10 to 14 hours of work, mostly new enumerator, scorer and tests code (suggested), against a most-likely null. Every follow-up branch breaks rule 10 or has no compliant fix. Park until job 9 finishes, then re-scope the same ranking probe onto the W and N' checkpoints with warm kept as the floor, or fold it into the 10M and 8a scaling question.

idea.title: Budget-matched failing-try placebos for the sleep gain
idea.summary: Job 9's W minus R contrast mixes the checker's choice with up to 16 times more samples, because W can draw 512 tries on stuck questions while R takes failing tries from the first 32. Add placebo arms with the same 512-try budget and the same per-kind counts so only the checker's choice differs. This tells whether lucky hits teach something that unchecked tries from the same stream do not.
idea.change: Add two arms to the job-8 pipeline (c2_stuck.py with c2b.py arm code), from the same 32 plus 480 sample stream: R512 = failing tries (structure ok, runs on every example, not fitting) from the same stuck-question stream, count-matched per kind to W's records (at most 2 distinct per question), each trained on its own output; P_rand = distinct tries drawn at random from the same stream in their natural fit/fail share. Keep P_solver (2,048 more add/mult solver rows, job 5's placebo) as a third reference. All arms: updates = |W|, 32 visits, 16 skills plus 16 warm rows per 64-row batch. Held-out C2 kinds (stuck), not practised add/mult.
idea.why: Shown: R and H records come from the first 32 pass-1 tries (failing_records on t[:n1]) while W draws from up to 512; in job 6 R sat at N (3 of 256 and 1 of 256 first tries), so W minus R equalled W minus N and carried no independent check. Shown: the job 9 pooled +15 mark could be met by square and last_digit alone (multi-step net 0 in the DEV pilot), so the label rule not the pooled mark decides a climb claim. A budget-matched placebo is the missing control; the search stream already exists so the extra cost is two sleeps and two evals per parent.

'THE SEARCH STREAM ALREADY EXISTS' IS FALSE (shown). results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json keep counts, timings and per-kind finds only. Per-try data for jobs 6-8 was never saved, and job 9's rec_*.pt files are on Ben's Mac. Every arm needs a fresh 512-try search per parent (night-1 search 1,890 s and 1,898 s in the JSON). The 'why' says the extra cost is two sleeps and two evals; the arms need four sleeps (W, R512, P_rand, P_solver) and five evals per parent.

Job 9 holds the Mac for an estimated 10 h (MAC-JOB-9.md, untested), so this run needs Ben's PC GPU (rule 6).

A +5 mark read on night 1 would fail. The idea must name the night, the search seeds (job 8 used seed + 10 x night), and whether W is re-run with job 8's seeds so it can be checked against +10.4 and +9.7.

P_RAND IS R512 IN DISGUISE IF DRAWN FROM THE STUCK STREAM (shown arithmetic). Only the stuck questions get the 480 extra tries. The 295 (s100) and 316 (s101) stuck questions that had a pass-2 fit each hold at least one fitting try among 364,800 and 367,200 pass-2 tries (c2stuck JSON). So 809 or 841 natural draws hold about 0.65 and 0.72 fitting tries in expectation or more. P_rand then equals R512 apart from about one fit, and its mark (W minus P_rand at least +5) repeats R512's mark. It is a real unchecked control only if it draws from each question's full stream, including the 32 pass-1 tries on the 264 solved questions. The idea does not say which.

R512 IS MATCHED PER KIND, WHICH IS LOOSER THAN THE CODE (shown). c2b.failing_records matches counts per question (counts.get(row id), c2b.py:51-69), and MAC-JOB-9.md says 'same questions and same count'. Per-kind matching lets R512 use different questions from W. Restricting R512 to stuck questions also drops the records W takes from the 264 pass-1 solved questions (s100 JSON), so the question sets differ. Also, night 1 of job 9 uses the first 32 pass-1 tries (c2b.py:173) while night 2 draws a fresh 32 from each arm's own model (c2b.py:217-218). Fix: run failing_records on the full 512 stream per question, passing tries rather than [t[:n1] for t in tries].

R AS CODED HAS A FILTER THE IDEA OMITS (shown). failing_records keeps only tries whose relabel is valid, meaning example outputs from 0 to 9999 (fewshot.relabel_prompt returns None otherwise; c2b.py:51-69; fewshot.py:172-185). The idea's R definition (structure ok, runs on every example, does not fit) is therefore not the arm that would run. The spec must name the filter.

THE PROVED-WRONG LINE CANNOT FIRE AT A TIE (interval shown; power arithmetic suggested). Job 8's night-2 multi-step interval is [5.19, 15.58] around +10.39 on 154 questions, so the standard error is about 2.65 points per parent. If W and R512 truly tie, the upper 95 percent end is about +4 to +5, so 'upper end below +2 on both parents' needs R512 to beat W by about 3 points. A tie lands in 'between' and cannot prove that the checker adds nothing. Under rule 4 the spec should state the minimum detectable effect at this size and what a tie means.

LIKELY OUTCOME IS A PASS THAT RESTATES JOB 8 (shown for inputs; prediction suggested). Job 6 showed that failing tries from 32 samples teach nothing: R is 1.2% and 0.4%, equal to N (c2pilot-readout line 12). If R512 is also near N', then W minus R512 is about W minus N' (about +10 on night 2), so the +5 mark passes almost by construction. P_solver (job 5's placebo, c2_stones.py:5; reach@32 4.3% and 5.1% against N 5.1% and 9.8%, roadmap line 505) is also near N on held-out kinds. The three controls will probably pass or fail together, so the screen carries about one bit. R512 minus N' with its interval and a harm mark should be reported as its own number.

DOSE RULE CONFLICTS WITH THE CODE (shown from the formula). 'Updates = |W|, 32 visits' for every arm does not hold. In c2b's sleep_on, visits per record = updates x 32 / records with replay, and short arms have their visit cap raised silently. P_solver (2,048 rows) at about 809 updates gets about 12.6 visits per row, not 32. P_rand with few records gets more than 32. The spec must choose matched updates and report visits, or matched visits and accept more updates.

RULE 10 GAPS NOT NAMED (shown). The W recipe includes 16 hand-written add/mult warm rows per 64-row batch (c2_stuck.py sleep_on, replay_extra=warm_rows; stones.py solver rows, which the model did not produce), the has_fit stuck signal, the 32/480 allocation, the per-question cap of 2, and the pool temperature (frozen at 3.0 in job 8, but picked on DEV in job 9, c2b.py train_parent setup). The rules check mentions only the checker. The result is a control on a non-autonomous recipe and cannot be a shipping claim. Rules 1-9 otherwise pass: records are the model's own tries, the solver rows are teaching data, DEV only, no sealed panel, same model, a 2-seed screen that must be labelled as a screen.

N_SS PROXY IS UNNECESSARY AND IS A DIFFERENT PARENT (shown). fast-sleep/parents/s100/setup.json records a 2,048-row warm-up and one 256-update stepping-stone sleep, with no add/mult replay step. MAC-JOB-9.md says N' includes add/mult replay 'as job 7', and job 8 used job 7's N'. The raw B2_s100 checkpoint is on the mount (custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100/checkpoint.pt), and c2b.train_parent rebuilds the warm-up and N' from a raw checkpoint when warm.pt is absent (c2b.py setup stage; c2_stones._warm). The PC run should use that path and check the rebuilt W against job 8's +10 (untested).

CLOSEST PRIOR IS MISSED (shown). The C1 spec has an R placebo 'from a separate pool, matched to W's puzzles and per-puzzle counts' (roadmap line 360). fewshot.build_arms' docstring says pool_tries = separate pool (fewshot.py:186-188), but job 6 passed the same samples (c2_pilot.py:149), so the separate-pool design was specified and never run. The multi-step set is 154 questions (affine 52, sq_plus 51, double_add 51; c2_keep.MULTI). One question is 0.65 points, so a +5 mark is about 8 questions per parent. The marks should say so.

chair.reasons: CUT. The idea's central premise is wrong, and all four critics accepted it without checking. The premise is that W (up to 512 tries) minus R (failing tries from the first 32) is confounded by budget. Only the records are trained on. Sampling more from the same model at the same settings does not change what a failing try looks like. Pass 2 uses the same model, the same T and level 0 as pass 1, with a different seed (c2_stuck.py search, lines 43-54; shown from code). So the failing, rule-following tries in 512 draws are drawn from the same distribution as those in 32 draws (suggested, by the sampling logic). The only thing 512 draws add is more distinct failing programs to choose from. That matters only if the supply of failing programs runs out. R is matched per question to W's count (c2b.failing_records, lines 51-69; shown from code), and the cap is at most 2 per question. In job 6 supply did not run out: n_R = n_W = 365 (s100) and 210 (s101), with short = {} (results/c2pilot/s100.json and s101.json, arm_build.diag; shown). At 32 tries and T 3-4, DEV tries already hold 12.6 to 15.8 distinct rule-following programs per question (results/c2dev; shown), against a need of at most 2. The one thing that differs between W and R is what the checker keeps (fits the examples or does not). That is the contrast Ben wants. It is a clean contrast, not a budget-confounded one. Second error in the idea: 'R sat at N, so W minus R carried no independent check'. A placebo that sits at baseline (R 1.2% and 0.4% first try, H 0.0%, job 6; shown in creative-pilot/c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md) is the placebo working, not a flaw. R512 would be expected to land at N' again. Then W minus R512 is about W minus N' (about +10 on night 2, job 8; shown), and the +5 mark passes by construction. The critics put the chance of a real learning difference at 10-20% and said the screen would carry about one bit (suggested). Cost is real. There is no saved per-try stream for jobs 6-8 (shown), so every arm needs a fresh search, about 1,890 s of CPU per parent per night. The design needs at least 4 sleeps and 5 evals per parent (not 'two sleeps and two evals'), and two nights if the marks are read as job 8's were. The +10 effect on multi-step exists only on night 2 (night 1 was +3.9 and +4.5; shown, c2stuck JSON). The honest cost is 4.5 to 5 h per parent, not 3 h for both. The Mac is held by job 9 for about 10 h (untested). The PC GPU would need N' rebuilt from raw B2 (N_ss is a different parent: add/mult reach@32 0.11 against 0.61 for N'; shown). The power is also poor. With about 2.6 points of standard error per parent on 154 multi-step questions, the 'upper end below +2 on both parents' falsifier almost never fires, so a tie lands in 'between' and proves nothing (suggested from the shown job 8 intervals). The design also has mismatches with the code: matching per kind instead of per question; an omitted relabel-valid filter on R and H; a dose rule (updates equal to |W| at 32 visits) that cannot hold for P_solver's 2,048 rows; and P_rand drawn from the stuck stream is mostly failing tries, so it duplicates R512 (about 97% of multi-step questions have no fit in the first 32 tries; shown, c2stuck JSON). Rules 1-9 are not broken (a control is exempt as scoring). Rule 10 is not advanced: the W recipe keeps the scripted stuck signal, the 32/480 allocation, the checker, the warm rows and the DEV-picked temperature, so a pass could not support an autonomy claim. Already covered by job 9 for free: it reports multi-step W minus N' and W minus R intervals, pooled R minus N' and H minus N' (c2b.py report()), and logs R and H short_records and short_questions per night (c2b.py lines 185-186 and 231-232). The one residual worry, that R or H cannot be filled to W's counts, is answered by those logged numbers when job 9 lands, at no extra compute. Plain-language summary for Ben: the idea worries that the 'lucky hits' arm saw more tries than the 'unlucky' arm, but extra tries from the same model do not change what an unlucky try looks like; the only difference is that the checker kept the ones that fit. That difference is the experiment. So the extra test would cost about 5 hours per seed to restate job 9.
chair.revised_idea: No new test. Read job 9's own numbers when they arrive (zero extra compute): (1) R and H short_records and short_questions per parent per night, in train.json under night1.R, night1.H and night2.R, night2.H; (2) multi-step W minus R first-try interval; (3) pooled R minus N' and H minus N' intervals. Reopen a single R512 arm only if the R or H shortfall exceeds about 10% of W's multi-step record count on at least 2 of 6 parents. In that case the revision is one arm only, a one-line change at c2b.py:173: pass the full per-question stream `tries` to failing_records instead of `[t[:n1] for t in tries]`, with per-question counts from W, the relabel-valid filter named, T 3.0 frozen, N' rebuilt from raw B2 (not N_ss), two nights, and a screen label. Drop P_rand (a duplicate of R512) and P_solver (job 5 already shows it near N).

If reopened: one change only, R512 = failing_records applied to the full per-question 512 stream with W's per-question counts; N' rebuilt from raw B2_s100 and B2_s101 through the c2b setup path and checked to reproduce job 8's multi-step gain of about +10 on night 2; pooled paired bootstrap over both parents (about 308 multi-step questions) with the power stated; marks fixed in advance as the share of W's gain that R512 keeps, plus R512 minus N' with a harm bound. State plainly that the result is a 2-seed screen on stones-built parents with a scripted checker, allocation and warm rows, and supports no autonomy claim and no 6-seed claim.

idea.title: Replay stop rules on one logged stuck search
idea.summary: Tonight every question with no fit gets 480 more tries, and about 60% of them find nothing. Re-run job 8's night-1 search once with a per-try log, then replay several stop and reallocation rules on the saved tries with no new model run. Search is 40-95% of a night's compute, so a safe stop is the biggest cost lever and is also the model's own decision of when to stop.
idea.change: New logging run (c2_trylog.py beside c2_stuck.py): re-run c2_stuck.search for s100 and s101 from N' (or N_ss.pt as proxy) at T 3.0 with the job-8 seeds (10 and 1010), logging per try: block, temperature, result_key, structure ok, examples reproduced (0-3), fit flag, query output, log-prob of the picks. Step 0 must reproduce job 8 night 1 (150 and 168 multi-step questions with a fit; 180 and 237 multi-step records) or stop. Then replay on the log (valid because raw draws are independent, legal.py:196-205): fixed 480 (control); fixed cut at equal calls; no-new-fit window (stop after 96 consecutive tries with no new accepted program, cap 480); yield-ratio stop on doubling blocks 32/64/128/256 (stop when the newest block's new-near-miss rate per try is below the previous block's, or 2 distinct fits reached); Good-Turing allocation index (singleton near-miss programs + 1) / (tries + 2) redistributing the same total; Luby prefix (control); index shuffled across questions (placebo).
idea.why: Shown: night-1 pass 2 drew 364,800 (s100) and 367,200 (s101) tries on 760 and 765 stuck questions; 465 and 449 of them got no fit; 150 and 168 multi-step questions with a fit came almost entirely from pass 2; only 30 and 69 questions reached a second distinct fit so the 2-fit cap alone saves little. Tries cost about 25.5 TFLOP a night against 0.8-1.2 TFLOP for notebook sleep and 19-39 for fine-tune sleep. Risk: blind search keeps finding candidates with no knee (+12.8 then +17.6 points per decade of budget), so an early stop could cut the climb; the replay measures how much.

test.arms: Fixed 480; fixed cut at equal calls; 96-window stop; yield-ratio stop; Good-Turing allocation; shuffled-index placebo; Luby control.
test.pass_mark: Both parents: multi-step questions with a fit >=95% of the fixed-480 count at <=75% of its pass-2 calls (<=273,600 on s100, <=275,400 on s101), and >=3 points of the 614 multi-step questions above the fixed cut at equal calls; Good-Turing index AUC at block 1 for a fit in blocks 2-4 >=0.65 and beats its shuffled placebo by >=3 points at equal calls.

Rule 7: only sampling ends, no target is cut. Rule 8: stuck questions only. Rule 10: window and block sizes are settings fixed before deployment (7c allows); the stop becomes the model's own decision only when it writes STOP after reading a check reply (B3).

problems: [shown: roadmap 7c, rules_check of this idea] Rule 10 and 7b: every stop window, block size, yield ratio and index is a hand function run by script, and the idea itself says the stop is a script rule until B3 (a tool the model calls). As a probe that is allowed. A deployed rule would break rules 1 and 10. The replay also chooses among six arms by pool/DEV outcomes, so a constant picked after the replay (96, 32/64/128/256, the index) is a runtime value tuned on dev results. 7c allows 'a setting fixed before deployment'; the constant must be fixed before the replay.

[shown: c2_stuck.py:17 N2=480; :50 draws 480 for every stuck question] The Good-Turing arm and the shuffled-index placebo cannot 'redistribute the same total' on this log. A question the index favours cannot get more than 480 logged tries, so the total can only fall. Only cut-only arms can be replayed, compared at equal total calls. Reallocating upward needs a log to a larger cap (about 1,920 per stuck question, roughly 4x pass 2).

[shown: RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md line 116] The project's own untested lever, 'stop sampling a question as soon as one try fits', is missing from the arm list. The idea calls it solved-question-only, but as coded it applies to stuck questions in pass 2: c2_stuck.py:43-54 draws all 480 whatever fits. It is the simplest cut. It also changes records (keeps 1 distinct fit, not 2; fewshot.py:157 _distinct, c2_stuck.py:57 per_cap=2), so it must be scored on the sleep as well as on finds.

[shown: results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json seconds] The cost framing is overstated. 'Search is 40-95% of a night's compute' mixes TFLOP shares; the 95% (RESEARCH sec 6) assumes memory (notebook) sleep, which job 8 does not use. Measured job-8 wall-clock: night 1 search 1,889.5 s against fine-tune sleep 932.2 s and eval 185.8 s (search 63%); night 2 search 1,179.6 s against 1,320.0 s and 188.9 s (44%). The pass mark (<=75% of pass-2 calls) saves about 14% of night-1 wall-clock and about 10% of night 2 (arithmetic from those seconds). 'Biggest cost lever' is not supported.

[untested estimate from job-8 seconds] The replay measures multi-step finds, not the first-try climb. The idea says 'the replay measures how much' the climb could be cut, but no sleep is run. A stop that keeps 95% of finds can still change the record mix and the climb. A sleep check (control and one stop arm, both nights, on two parents) costs about 44 min per arm per parent from the job-8 seconds, so about 3 h, not the 1.1 h stated.

[shown: results/c2stuck JSON counts] Noise and marks. One logged run per parent, no intervals, no second seed. The two parents already differ by 18 multi-step fits (150 vs 168). The 3-point mark on the 614 pool multi-step questions is about 18 questions, the same size. The 95%-of-150 count mark allows a loss of about 7 questions. The idea's 'screen' label is right, but the pass lines read as claims. A second logged seed per parent or a paired question bootstrap is needed before any mark is read.

[shown: MAC-JOB-8.md lines 15-16; results/c2stuck/s100.json nprime] The reproduction gate is fragile. Job 8 ran on the Mac from /Users/ben-hannan/.../Nprime.pt with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4. The mount's fast-sleep/parents/s100/N_ss.pt was built from /root/fs/B2_s100.pt (setup.json). Nothing in the files shows it is the same checkpoint, so the proxy will probably fail the gate and only the Mac N' works, which waits for job 9 (untested estimate 3 to 3.5 h per parent). The JSON records no torch version or thread count, so an exact count match is not guaranteed. Set a tolerance before running, and do not use cuda (a different RNG stream).

[shown: sampler.py:23-27 TryRec; sampler.py:35-39 _pick] The logging spec asks for more than the code keeps. TryRec holds only Try (ops, pointers, answer), mode and branch. 'Log-prob of the picks' needs _pick and sample_run to return probabilities, which is a sampler change that must not alter the RNG draws. Drop the field or name the change. 'Examples reproduced' needs fewshot.outputs_py, which exists.

[shown: grep of creative code finds no 'near-miss', 'luby' or 'good-turing'] Undefined terms. 'Near-miss' has no definition (for example 2 of 3 examples reproduced). 'New program' has two keys in this repo: result_key (programs.py:110, canonical expression) and the value vector of blind search (blind_baseline.py:15-44). The idea does not choose. Also unstated: whether pass-1 tries count toward the 96-try window. The 'Good-Turing' index (singleton+1)/(tries+2) is a smoothed rate, not Good's estimator (N1/N; suggested, Good 1953, not in files). Rename it.

(a) '+12.8 then +17.6 points per decade' is wrong: 77.3-64.5 and 94.9-77.3 are raw differences over 0.78 and 0.92 decades (1k to 6k, 6k to 50k). From the job-8 JSON, search is 63% and 62% of night-1 wall time (1,889.5 s of 3,007.5 s including sleep and eval) and 44% and 42% of night 2. A 25% cut to pass-2 draws saves about 23% of night-1 draws (0.25 x 364,800 / 397,568), roughly 10 to 14% of a night's wall time. The idea's '<=75% of pass-2 calls' is pass-2 only, not total calls.

shown (mark gaps): pass needs at least 95% of the fixed-480 count at 75% of pass-2 calls; proved wrong needs under 85% at 75% of calls. Counts from 85% to 95%, and parents that meet one clause but not the other, get no verdict. '3 points of 614' is about 18 questions and is not tied to a parent. The pass counts questions, but the climb rides on sleep records (multi-step records 180 and 237 under fixed 480). Name one endpoint (multi-step records, then W first try after one night) and close the gaps before any run.

shown (2-fit figure is multi-step only): '30 and 69 questions reached a second distinct fit' equals multi-step records minus multi-step finds (180-150 and 237-168). Across all kinds, 250 (s100) and 266 (s101) questions hold two records (809-559 and 841-575, from the job-8 JSON), mostly square and last_digit. The cap does matter there, so state the scope.

shown (risk numbers are the critic's own arithmetic on unverified figures): '+12.8 then +17.6 points per decade' is 77.3-64.5 and 94.9-77.3 from /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 2. No project file uses the phrase 'per decade'. Per decade the steps would be 16.4 and 19.1 (1k to 6k spans 0.78 decade; 6k to 50k spans 0.92). The 64.5 and 77.3 figures were not reproduced by the area fact check (58.2 and 73.8 on the same file, reported by that check, not re-run here; untested). Fix the wording and re-run blind_baseline before citing it.

shown (new-program key is defined in code): use programs.result_key (canonical expression of the answer cone, programs.py:110-114), the key W uses for its two distinct records (fewshot._distinct, fewshot.py:157-169). Blind search counts value vectors (blind_baseline.py docstring), so do not mix them. Canonical expressions count two programs that compute one function as new, so the count measures written variety, not behaviour (suggested).

untested (log-prob column needs a sampler change): sampler.sample_run returns only ops, operands, answer and mode (sampler.py:103) and draws with torch.multinomial (sampler.py:39). Logging probabilities must draw no extra random numbers, or the step-0 reproduction breaks. The cost of per-try logging is not measured.

shown (temperature is a DEV pick inherited by the replay): T 3.0 comes from the DEV rule 'best reach@32 among temperatures passing sameness' for each parent (results/c2keep/s100.json and s101.json, pool_temperature.chosen = 3.0). Under rule 10 that is a DEV-tuned value. A learned or per-question temperature is a separate step (roadmap 7c table).

shown (throughput checks out): (32,768 + 364,800) / 1,889.5 s = 210.4 draws per second and (32,768 + 367,200) / 1,897.7 s = 210.8, from results/c2stuck. The idea's rate and its 32-minute estimate hold. Job 8 ran both parents side by side (MAC-JOB-8.md section 2), so 'about 1.1 h for both' is the sequential figure.

shown (walk-through of a deployed night, step by step): (1) pass 1, 32 tries at T 3.0: the model samples, but T is DEV-picked. (2) stuck test: a hand checker on pass 1, run by the script, needs a checker tool plus the model's own stuck decision (C9, not built). (3) budget: 480 more where none fits, script-set. (4) stop rule, this idea's subject: script-set, needs B3 and a learned head. (5) records: at most 2 distinct fits chosen at random, script-set; the fixed cap is allowed, the random pick is hand code. (6) when to sleep and the nightly schedule: script-set (7c 'when to sleep'). (7) practice pool: the researcher's held-out-kind questions, not allowed. (8) parent: stones written by us (C6 replaces them).

critiques.expected_effect: If the replay passes as written, it would show that a stop rule can cut pass-2 draws by 25% (about 23% of night-1 draws, roughly 10 to 14% of a night's wall time) while keeping at least 95% of multi-step finds on both parents. Replay of prefix stops is valid: raw_samples draws independent tries with no dedup or branching (legal.py:196-205), so a stop that reads only a question's earlier tries can be replayed on the log. It would not show that the model decides when to stop; that stays a script rule until B3 exists. It is a two-parent screen (rule 4) on the researcher's pool with a stones parent, so it cannot carry an autonomy label. Its useful output is a cost estimate and the yield curve a learned stop head would need to learn from.

problems: Cost basis is wrong. The idea says tries cost about 25.5 TFLOP a night and search is 40-95% of compute. shown: /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6 row 'The night's tries: 32 per question on 1,024 pool questions' = about 25.5 TFLOP, measured on s205 for 64 questions (1.59 TFLOP) and scaled. That is pass 1 only (32,768 draws). The 95% in section 6 is the memory-sleep case. derived: 25.5 TFLOP / 32,768 draws = 0.78 GFLOP per draw. Job 8 pass 2 adds 364,800 (s100) and 367,200 (s101) draws (c2stuck/s100.json night1_search.samples), so the stuck search is about 285 TFLOP a night. Search share against fine-tune sleep (19-39) is about 88-94%, and about 99% against memory sleep. A 25% cut saves about 70 TFLOP, more than a whole fine-tune night.

The no-new-fit window rule as written probably fails by design. It stops after 96 consecutive tries with no new accepted program, counted from try 1 (suggested reading; the idea does not say the window starts at the first fit). A question with no fit yet would stop at try 96. Under a flat per-try hazard matched to job 8 (double_add 83 of 197 stuck found in pass 2; affine 10 of 203), the window keeps only about 20-25% of pass-2 finds (suggested, a rough model), far below the idea's own 85% proved-wrong floor. The window needs to start only after a first find, or be set per kind.

The Good-Turing reallocation cannot be replayed on the log and cannot keep the same total under the 480 cap. The log holds 480 pass-2 draws per stuck question (c2_stuck.py:43-54; results/c2stuck). Every stuck question is already at the cap, so moving tries to some questions above 480 needs draws that were never logged, and keeping the same total is impossible without going above 480 somewhere. The log needs more draws per question (for example 960) or the total must fall. The idea does not say which.

The pass marks do not test the cost claim and leave a gap. A rule that uses 75% of calls and keeps 85-95% of multi-step finds is neither a pass (needs at least 95%) nor proved wrong (under 85%). The 95% threshold has no stated source. Job 8's own search gate is already written and looser: at least 75 (s100) and 90 (s101) multi-step records (c2_stuck.py:19; search_check in s100/s101.json). Actual records were 180 and 237, so headroom is 2.4x and 2.6x. The marks also need per-kind retention, because the earlier climb came from square and last_digit (c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md): a rule could keep all double_add finds, lose affine ones, and still pass pooled.

Undefined terms the marks depend on. 'Near-miss' is not defined (examples reproduced 0-3 is logged, but no threshold is stated). 'New accepted program' has no key; the code's distinct key is result_key, the canonical expression of the answer cone (programs.py:110-114), and blind search uses a value vector, so counts differ. 'Fixed cut at equal calls' is not defined, and the 3-point mark depends on it.

The reproduction gate cannot be met on the mount and has no tolerance. Job 8's N' is job 7's Nprime.pt, which exists only on Ben's Mac (nprime path in c2stuck/s100.json). The mount's fast-sleep/parents/s100 and s101 N_ss.pt is job 6's parent N, not N' (fast-sleep/parents/README.md). The warm-up checkpoint for these two parents was not kept, so N' cannot be rebuilt on the mount. Using N_ss as a proxy searches from a different model, so Step 0 would fail by construction. The gate says 'reproduce or stop' with no tolerance for float differences across machines.

The replay gives one draw realization per parent, and the marks have no interval. A 3-point gap on 614 multi-step questions is about 18 questions. Rule 4 needs 6 or more paired seeds. A bootstrap over questions would give an interval on the one realization. The replay is a screen only.

The placebo is confounded by kind. Shuffling the index across all questions removes kind structure, and kind strongly sets find rates (square 56 pass-2 finds versus affine 10 in s100). An AUC above 0.65 could come from kind alone. The control should shuffle within kind.

Rule 10 is at risk. The stop rule and block sizes (96, 32/64/128/256, yield ratio) would be chosen by replay on pool outcomes, the same questions the marks are scored on. Until a learned gate or B3 exists, the stop is a harness script, and the idea itself says so. Pre-register one rule before the replay, and report the chosen rule's sleep effect on separate questions.

Mislabelled blind-search slope. The idea says '+12.8 then +17.6 points per decade'. Those are raw increments (77.3 - 64.5 and 94.9 - 77.3) across 1k to 6k (0.78 decades) and 6k to 50k (0.92 decades), so per decade they are about 16.5 and 19.1. The base figures (64.5/77.3/94.9) are unverified: a re-run gave 58.2/73.8 at 1k/6k (orchestrator fact check). The notes also label the column 'Guesses per question' while the code counts candidates examined (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 2; blind_baseline.py:10-11). The 'no knee' claim is an analogy to blind search, not a measurement of the model's tries.

The '30 and 69 questions reached a second distinct fit' figure is correct arithmetic but covers only multi-step questions (180 - 150 and 237 - 168 from the json). Pool-wide, second records are about 250 (809 - 559) and 266 (841 - 575). The 2-fit cap therefore saves more than the idea implies, mostly on square and last_digit.

Verified and consistent: 760 and 765 stuck questions; pass-2 draws 364,800 = 760 x 480 and 367,200 = 765 x 480; pass-2 finds 295 and 316; 465 and 449 with nothing (61% and 59%); 150 and 168 multi-step questions with a fit, of which pass 2 supplies 135 and 149; records 180 and 237; seeds 10 and 1010 (c2_stuck.py:153 uses seed + 10 x night; :50 uses seed + 1000); throughput (32,768 + 364,800) / 1,889.5 s = 210.4 per s and (32,768 + 367,200) / 1,897.7 s = 210.8 per s; 614 multi-step pool questions (205 + 204 + 205); 75% limits 273,600 and 275,400. Draws are independent within each raw_samples call (legal.py:196-205, one generator per call), so replaying a stop rule on the first k logged draws per question is valid as a simulation, provided the log is not extended.

Citations are real. Luby, Sinclair and Zuckerman 1993, 'Optimal speedup of Las Vegas algorithms', Information Processing Letters 47(4):173-180 (checked by web search, standard mode). Good 1953, Biometrika 40(3-4):237-264 (checked by web search). Good's estimator is n1/N; the idea's (singletons + 1)/(tries + 2) is a Laplace-style variant and should be labelled suggested. Luby's result concerns restarts of one run; for independent tries it is only a fixed-budget control, which the idea already says.

critiques.already_tried: No replay of stop rules on saved draws was found. Closest prior work: job 8 fixed-480 search (creative/c2_stuck.py; results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json, no stop rule); fast-sleep stop-on-first-fit lever (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6, untested); NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md (chaining, not stopping). critiques.expected_effect: As a cheap screen (about 1.1 h Mac CPU; job-8 timings were about 1,890 s per parent), the logged run is worth doing once, mainly to give other ideas a per-try log. As a test of the stop rules as written, expect a fail. Suggested, from a flat-hazard model: a fixed cut at 75% of calls keeps about 75% of multi-step finds (below the 85% floor), and even with front-loaded finds about 85-90%. The no-new-fit window keeps about 20-25% (proved wrong by its own floor). A rule that works could save about 20-35% of search, about 57-100 TFLOP a night (derived), more than a whole fine-tune night (19-39). The sleep climb is not measured by this screen and needs a separate training test. Records have 2.4-2.6x headroom over job 8's gate, so the chosen mark, not the stop rule, may decide the outcome. Rule 10 stays unmet until a model-decided stop exists (B3).

problems: Step 0 gate cannot be passed by a valid rerun as written. It has no tolerance on 150/168 multi-step fits and 180/237 records. Suggested: a fresh draw of the same process has an SD of about 9-10 questions on the 150-168 fits (Bernoulli approximation to the job-8 pass-2 counts in results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json), so an exact match has about a 4% chance even if the code is right. Shown: Nprime.pt is not in the snapshot (only Mac), and MAC-JOB-8.md sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, so the Mac CPU with the same torch build is the only exact check. On the PC, N_ss.pt (present at fast-sleep/parents/s100/N_ss.pt) is job 6's parent rebuilt on the cloud CPU, whose losses match the Mac only 'to 4 digits' (fast-sleep/parents/README.md). Suggested: a CUDA generator (legal.py:198, torch.Generator(device=device)) draws from a different stream than CPU. Fix: exact match on the Mac only, or a band of about plus or minus 20 questions per count on the PC.

Pass mark 1 (at least 95% of fixed-480 multi-step fits at no more than 75% of pass-2 calls) is probably unreachable under the flat-hazard picture the idea's own risk paragraph describes. Suggested arithmetic on shown job-8 counts: a constant per-draw find rate fitted to each multi-step kind's pass-2 finds keeps about 79% (s100) and 81% (s101) of finds at 75% of draws. The mark passes only if finds are strongly front-loaded, and no file shows the arrival curve. Restate it as lost finds per call saved, with a paired bootstrap interval over the 614 multi-step pool questions (the project already uses paired bootstrap intervals, c2_stuck.py:176), and print the per-kind arrival curve before any arm is judged.

Proved-wrong criterion 3 ('finds in the last 240 draws >= 40% of all finds') is a property of the log, not of any stop rule. Suggested: under the same flat hazard it holds (about 45% on s100 and 42% on s101), so it would reject every within-question stop from the log alone. It also says nothing about the across-question allocators (Good-Turing, shuffled placebo), which the test is meant to judge. Limit it to a gate on the window arms, or delete it.

The replay measures finds, not the climb, and the stated use overreaches. Nothing in the design runs a sleep. Shown: the sleep dose is set by record count (updates = 32 x records / 32, c2_stuck.py:102), so a stop rule that drops records also cuts the sleep. The job-8 climb (multi-step first try +10.4 and +9.7, results/c2stuck JSON) came from sleep on those records. Any rule that passes needs one matched-update sleep per parent before any climb claim, and the orchestrator's 'replay measures how much climb is lost' should be dropped.

Stuck-question cost sits almost entirely on low-yield kinds (shown, results/c2stuck JSON). Multi-step questions are 599 of 760 stuck on s100 and 595 of 765 on s101, and take 78-79% of pass-2 calls. Pass-2 draws per multi-step find: affine about 9,700 (s100) and 7,000 (s101); sq_plus about 2,300 and 3,600; double_add about 1,100 and 850. The marks therefore turn on affine's 10 and 14 finds and sq_plus's 42 and 27. A 96-try no-new-fit window will stop slow-find kinds first and can drop the hardest records. Require per-kind records and finds under every arm.

The 2-fit-cap claim is for multi-step only. '30 and 69 questions reached a second distinct fit' is correct for multi-step (180 minus 150; 237 minus 168). Across all kinds, records minus fitted questions gives 250 (s100: 809 minus 559) and 266 (s101: 841 minus 575) pool questions with two kept records (computed here from shown JSON counts). The sentence should state its scope, because the cap binds widely.

The allocator arm cannot be replayed as written. raw_samples gives 480 contiguous independent draws per stuck question (legal.py:196-205), so a Good-Turing allocation that 'redistributes the same total' can give some question more than 480 only if the log is larger. Specify the per-question cap; 480 is the only cap the log supports. 'Block 1' is also ambiguous with pass 1, which by definition has no fit for a stuck question.

Keys and terms are undefined. 'New accepted program', 'singleton' and 'near-miss' (examples reproduced 2 of 3?) need definitions. Shown: the repo already dedups records by result_key, the canonical expression of the answer cone (programs.py:110-114; fewshot.py:157-169). The test should use result_key for every 'new program'. Value-vector counts (blind_baseline.py) are a different unit and must not be mixed in.

Several arms share two draws with point thresholds. About seven arms (fixed 480, fixed cut, 96-window, yield-ratio, Good-Turing, Luby, shuffled placebo) are replayed on two logs, and the marks are point estimates ('at least 3 points', 'AUC at least 0.65') with no intervals. Name one primary arm before the run and report the rest as exploratory. The two-parent pass is a screen under rule 4, and the wording should say so.

Rule compliance is overstated. rules_check says 'Rule 1: the stop reads only checker outcomes inside a tool'. Shown: today the checker and the stop are hand code inside c2_stuck.search (c2_stuck.py:43-54), and roadmap 7c lists the try budget (32, then 480) and the example checker run by the loop as hand choices to be replaced. 7c allows a fixed setting only under the 'no outside help' label; the 'own choices' label needs B3. Each arm should carry both 7c labels. The 96 window, block sizes and T 3.0 (picked on the DEV grid in job 6 and frozen, c2_stuck.py:6) must be fixed before the run, not chosen after the replay.

'One logged run feeds five ideas' is partly false. Shown: the job-8 search runs at T 3.0 only (c2_stuck.py:16). Suggested: logged picks cannot be re-weighted to another temperature without the full distributions. Stuck features that need hidden state are not in the logged fields. The log supports stop rules, the census and the allocator, not temperature schedules.

Blind-search 'no knee' figures are unverified. '+12.8 then +17.6 points per decade' uses RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 2's 64.5 / 77.3 / 94.9 (shown in that file, not re-run here). The steps span 0.78 and 0.92 decades, so 'per decade' is wrong. The brief's fact check reports 58.2 / 73.8 from the code's first_fit_right metric (blind_baseline.py:62-70). Cite a re-run, or label the figure untested.

The cost sentence is wrong. 'Tries cost about 25.5 TFLOP a night' is RESEARCH section 6's figure for the 32-per-question pass only (32,768 draws, counted on s205 and scaled; shown). Job 8's night 1 draws about 398,000 per parent, roughly 12 times that. Wall-clock shares from the job-8 seconds are search 62.8% / 62.2% on night 1 and 43.9% / 42.3% on night 2 with weight sleep (shown). The '40-95%' range mixes in notebook sleep, which failed its 6-seed confirm (0.87x; shown).

Hardware and schedule. Shown: job-8 timing gives about 32 min per parent on CPU at about 210 draws per second (1,889.5 and 1,897.7 s). Mac CPU after job 9 delays the test; MAC-JOB-9.md estimates about 10 h for job 9 (untested). Suggested: the PC RTX 5070 Ti (rule 6's first choice) can run the search in float32 in about 5-15 min per parent, because the per-try Python checks (pyfit, torch verdict on survivors) become the bottleneck. B2 at 3.3M params (13.2 MB checkpoint) and a 2048-row sampler fit in 16 GB easily. Untested: GPU speed, and whether sample_run_masked runs on CUDA.

What holds (shown). Raw draws are independent per try (legal.py:196-205: one seeded generator, contiguous per-question draws), so replaying first-k prefixes is a valid stop simulation. Per-try data for jobs 6-8 was not saved (c2_stuck.py writes only aggregates, lines 90 and 162-165), so a fresh log is needed.
