chair.reasons:
PLAN, after revision. Worth about one Mac CPU hour as shared infrastructure, not as the biggest cost lever. All four critics said revise, and the problems they found are real. I re-read the job 8 files and they hold up.

What holds (shown, results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json):
- Pass 2 drew 364,800 (s100) and 367,200 (s101) tries on 760 and 765 stuck questions.
- Multi-step questions with a fit: 150 and 168. Pass 2 supplied 135 and 149 of them (pass 1 gave 15 and 19).
- Multi-step records: 180 and 237.
- Search is the biggest slice of a night, but not 40-95%. Night 1 search is 1889.5 s (s100) and 1897.7 s (s101) against about 1118 s and 1155 s of sleep plus eval, so about 63%. Night 2 is 44% and 42%. Job 8 uses weight sleep, so the 95% figure (notebook sleep) does not apply.
- A cut to 75% of pass-2 calls saves about 14% of night-1 wall time and about 10% of night 2. That is my arithmetic from those seconds, not a measured run. 'Biggest cost lever' is not supported.

What fails as written, and the fix for each:
- The Good-Turing reallocation cannot 'redistribute the same total'. Every stuck question was already drawn to the 480 cap, so the log cannot hold more tries for any question. Only arms that cut draws can be replayed.
- N_ss.pt is not N'. It is job 6's parent (no warm-row replay), rebuilt on a cloud CPU. N' (Nprime.pt) is on Ben's Mac only. The step-0 reproduction needs the Mac, or the PC run must be labelled a different parent.
- The yield-ratio and no-new-fit window rules, with constants chosen from the arms, would be tuned on the pool they are scored on (rule 10).
- The pass mark of 95% of finds at 75% of calls is probably unreachable. A flat per-try hazard keeps only about 79-81% of finds at 75% of calls (suggested, critic arithmetic). The original 'proved wrong' clause 'last 240 draws hold at least 40% of finds' is a property of the log, not of any rule.
- The bands are not closed: results between 85% and 95% get no verdict.
- 'Near-miss' and 'new program' are undefined. 'Log-prob of the picks' needs a sampler change that must not touch the random draws.
- The 'one log feeds five ideas' claim is only about three of five. Draws are at T 3.0 only, and hidden-state features are not logged.
- The '+12.8 then +17.6 per decade' blind-search risk argument rests on unreproduced figures (58.2/73.8 re-run versus 64.5/77.3 in the notes) and on raw differences, not per-decade ones. Remove it.
- The '30 and 69 reached a second distinct fit' figure is multi-step only. Across all kinds it is about 250 and 266 (809-559, 841-575).

Rules:
- Rules 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9 hold. Rule 6 holds: CPU only.
- Rule 4: this is a two-parent replay screen, not a claim.
- Rule 10: it passes only as a probe. A stop rule written in the loop script is hand code between question and answer. It becomes the model's own decision only once it comes from a learned stop head or from the model writing STOP after reading checker replies in the B3 tool loop. The useful output is a labelled per-try dataset that such a head could be trained and tested on. The probe does not make the loop autonomous.
- Overlap: this is the stop-rule slice of the planned C9 stuck signal and of the untested fast-sleep 'stop once a try fits' lever (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md line 116). Label it as such.
chair.revised_idea:
Replay stop and give-up rules on one logged stuck search of job 8's night 1. This is a CPU feasibility study for a later learned stop head (C9). It is not a deployable rule and not a climb test.

Design, with every constant fixed before the run:

1. Run and step 0.
- Re-run c2_stuck.search for s100 and s101 from N' (Nprime.pt) at T 3.0 with job 8's recorded seeds. Do this on Ben's Mac CPU with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and the same torch build, after job 9.
- Step 0 gate: the per-kind pass-1/pass-2 find counts, the 150/168 multi-step fits and the 180/237 multi-step records must match job 8 exactly. If the match is not exact, allow a band of plus or minus 20 questions per count, fixed now. Outside the band, stop.
- If the Mac is busy, run N_ss.pt (fast-sleep/parents/s100 and s101) on the PC CPU instead. It is a different parent, not N'. Label it that way, skip the reproduction gate, and use only a sanity gate on per-kind find rates.

2. Log, written outside the sampler so the random draws are unchanged.
- Per try: question id, pass (1 or 2), index within the pass, structure ok, examples reproduced (0-3, from fewshot.outputs_py), fit flag, result_key (programs.py:110), query output.
- Also store the full try (ops, operands, answer pointer), so records can be rebuilt and a sleep run without re-searching.
- Drop the log-prob field.
- Run a second fresh sampling seed per parent, as a held-out replay.

3. Definitions.
- New program = programs.result_key only.
- Near-miss = structure ok and exactly 2 of 3 examples reproduced.
- The give-up window counts pass-2 tries only. Stuck questions have no pass-1 fit by definition.
- Every arm caps each question at 480 tries and is compared at equal total calls. No arm may reallocate above 480.

4. Arms.
- Control: fixed 480.
- Fixed cut at equal calls: truncate every stuck question to the same k.
- Arm A, pre-registered: stop a question when it holds 2 distinct fits by result_key. This is the existing record cap, so the record count is unchanged by construction; only which two programs are kept changes (first two found instead of a random pick). It has no tuned constant.
- Arm B, pre-registered: arm A plus give up on a question with zero near-misses after its first 96 pass-2 tries. The 96 is three times pass 1's 32, a design constant.
- Exploratory, no pass marks:
  - a cut-only allocator that ranks stuck questions by first-96-try near-miss rate (a smoothed singleton rate, not Good-Turing) and spends 75% of the calls on the top ranks;
  - a within-kind shuffled placebo for the allocator;
  - the oracle stop at the last find (reported only, not deployable);
  - the per-kind arrival curve of finds at 96/192/288/384/480 tries.
- Drop the Luby arm, since it is a fixed cut for independent draws. Drop the doubling-block yield-ratio rule unless the arrival curve motivates it.

5. Marks, per parent. Estimate each with a paired question bootstrap over the 614 pool multi-step questions; the mark is read on the interval.
- Arm A passes if it saves at least 15% of pass-2 calls and multi-step records are at least 99% of control.
- Arm B passes if multi-step fits and multi-step records are at least 90% of control at 75% or fewer of control's pass-2 calls, and it beats the equal-call fixed cut by at least 2 points of the 614 with the interval above 0.
- Arm B is proved wrong if either parent is under 80% of control fits at 75% or fewer calls, or if it is no better than the fixed cut on both parents.
- Results between 80% and 90% get the verdict 'between': report the curve and run no sleep.
- Allocator signal (exploratory): the mean of per-kind AUCs for first-96-try near-miss rate predicting a fit in tries 97-480 must be at least 0.65 and beat the within-kind shuffle. Compute it for double_add and sq_plus only. Affine has only 10-14 pass-2 finds per parent, so no affine read is possible at this size.
- Report per-kind fits and records under every arm.

6. Follow-ups.
- If an arm passes on both parents, run one night-1 sleep from the rebuilt records on each parent, about 16 min of sleep plus 3 min of eval, with no new search.
- Only after that, run a live night 2 with the rule, and then a 6-parent confirm on s200-s205 at job 9's chosen T.

7. Wording corrections for the write-up.
- Replace '40-95% of compute' with 'search is 63% of night-1 and 44% of night-2 wall time; a 75% pass-2 cut saves about 14% and 10%'.
- Remove the 'per decade' blind-search risk line.
- State that the 2-fit-cap figures (30 and 69) are multi-step only; all-kind counts are about 250 and 266.
- Label each arm with both roadmap 7c labels: 'no outside help' is yes only if the constants were fixed before the run, and 'own choices' is no until B3 exists.
chair.plan_guidance:
What the test plan must get right. Labels in brackets.

Step 0 and the parent
- Reproduction needs Nprime.pt on Ben's Mac, with the same torch build and threads (OMP_NUM_THREADS=4) [shown: MAC-JOB-8.md; the c2stuck JSON nprime path is a /Users/ben-hannan path].
- N_ss.pt is job 6's parent, not N' [shown: fast-sleep/parents/README.md]. On the PC it is a different parent. Label it so, with no reproduction claim and only a sanity gate.
- Write the tolerance before the run: exact on the Mac, otherwise plus or minus 20 questions per count (about 2 SD under a Bernoulli approximation, suggested).
- Do not use CUDA for the reproduction. The generator stream differs [suggested].
- Compare these job 8 counts (shown, c2stuck JSON):
  - s100 per-kind pass-1/pass-2 finds: affine 2/10, double_add 7/83, last_digit 101/104, sq_plus 6/42, square 148/56.
  - s101: affine 2/14, double_add 13/108, last_digit 91/111, sq_plus 4/27, square 149/56.
  - Stuck questions 760 and 765; pass-2 draws 364,800 and 367,200; records 809 and 841.

Replay validity
- Replaying a first-k prefix is valid because draws are independent (legal.py:196-205, one seeded generator per call) [shown by two critics reading the code; not run].
- A live rerun with a stop rule would change which draws later questions get. That is why the rule is replayed on the log first.

Fixed rules
- Pre-register Arm A and Arm B with their constants (the 96 window, the 2-distinct-fit stop, near-miss = exactly 2 of 3 examples).
- Do not pick constants from the replay output. Everything else is exploratory with no pass mark.

Marks
- Close every gap: define 'between' for 80-90% retention.
- Use a paired question bootstrap over the 614 multi-step pool questions. The 3-point mark equals about 18 questions, which is also the gap between the two parents' fit counts (150 versus 168).
- Do not read bare point values.
- Report per-kind fits and records. Pooled retention can hide an affine loss, and affine's 10 and 14 finds cannot carry a mark.

Expectation
- Under a flat per-try hazard, a cut to 75% of calls keeps about 79-81% of multi-step finds [suggested, critic arithmetic on shown job 8 counts]. The retention mark may therefore be 'proved wrong', which is itself a useful, honest result: the draws are memoryless and the only gain is Arm A plus whatever near-miss information adds.

Records and sleep
- Arm A keeps the record count by construction, but the choice of which two programs are kept changes. The records come from fewshot._distinct, which shuffles all fits and takes the first 2 distinct by result_key (c2_stuck.py:57; fewshot.py:157-169) [shown].
- Any arm that changes records needs a sleep check before any climb claim, because updates equal records (c2_stuck.py:102).
- Log the full tries so the sleep check needs no re-search: about 16 min of sleep plus 3 min of eval per parent for night 1 [shown from the job 8 seconds: night-1 sleep 932 s and 970 s, eval 186 s].
- The job 8 climb at +10 came after night 2 (night 1 gave +3.9 and +4.5), so a night-1 sleep check cannot show that the climb is kept. It only shows the sleep still learns.

Cost wording
- Use wall-clock shares: search is 62.8% and 62.2% of night 1 and 43.9% and 42.3% of night 2 [shown: seconds in results/c2stuck JSON].
- Drop the '25.5 TFLOP a night' sentence. It covers pass 1 only: 32 tries on 1,024 questions, counted on s205 for 64 questions and scaled [shown: RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6]. Pass 2 is about 11 times as many draws.

Blind search
- Do not cite 64.5/77.3/94.9. A re-run gave 58.2/73.8 at 1k/6k [shown by the area fact check], and 'guesses' there means examined candidates.
- Remove the 'per decade' phrasing.

Rule 10 text for the plan
- The stop reads only checker outcomes (fit flag, examples reproduced, result_key). It reads no kind label, no answer key and no test field.
- The constants are design constants, the same every night.
- The stop is a script rule today. It becomes the model's own decision only through a learned head or the B3 tool loop.
- A later learned-head variant could be fit on the s100 log and tested on the s101 log (and across the two sampling seeds), with labels taken from the model's own later fits.

Scope limits to state
- The parent was given stepping stones we wrote (roadmap 7c). Call it a positive-control screen, not an autonomous result.
- T 3.0 is a DEV-picked value inherited from job 6/8. Job 9 re-picks T per parent, so a 6-parent confirm must use job 9's T.
- The log supports stop rules, census and cut-only allocation. It does not support temperature schedules, and hidden-state stuck features are not in it.

Schedule
- Mac time is taken by job 9 for about 10 h [untested estimate: MAC-JOB-9.md].
- The logging run is about 32 min per parent when two run side by side [shown: job 8 ran side by side at about 1,890 s each].
- Two sampling seeds per parent is about 1.1-2.2 h of wall time. The PC CPU (with N_ss) can go first if the Mac is busy.

plan.title: Stop rules replayed on one logged stuck search
plan.ben_line: When the AI is stuck, it keeps trying hundreds of times on each hard question, even when it is getting nowhere. This test asks whether it can give up sooner and still keep the answers that work. It only replays attempts the model already made, on a computer, to measure that.
plan.question: Can a fixed stop rule cut the extra search on stuck multi-step questions by about a quarter while keeping their checked fits and the sleep records they feed?
plan.one_change: Stop a stuck question's extra search early by a fixed rule (arm B): after 96 extra tries with no checked fit and no near-miss, give up. Any question also stops at its second distinct checked fit (arm A). Measured by replaying logged job-8 night-1 tries. The screen trains nothing; one sleep check runs only if the screen passes.
arms: C (control, job 8 as run): every stuck pool question gets 480 extra pass-2 tries at T 3.0 (c2_stuck.py:16, :50). Records: at most 2 distinct checked fits per question, chosen at random (w_records, c2_stuck.py:57-68). Pass 1 (32 tries per question) is identical in every arm.

A (report only, pre-registered): a stuck question stops at its second distinct checked fit, keyed by programs.result_key (programs.py:110-114). Record counts are unchanged by construction (see null_risk); only which two fits are kept can change.

B (the one change, pre-registered): A plus a give-up. After its first 96 pass-2 tries, a question with no checked fit and no near-miss stops. Near-miss = structure ok (fewshot.structure, fewshot.py:34-47) and at least 2 of the 3 examples reproduced (fewshot.outputs_py, fewshot.py:50-58). A fit counts as a near-miss. Fixed here, before the run: the brief's 'exactly 2 of 3' would give up a question that holds a fit but no 2-of-3 try, which removes the second-fit search B is meant to keep. The give-up applies only to questions with zero fits and zero near-misses.

F (comparator at equal calls): fixed cut. Every stuck question stops after k pass-2 tries, with integer k chosen so multi-step pass-2 calls equal B's on the same draw. A is not a separate matched comparator, because its multi-step saving is small (null_risk), so F is the matched test.
Records for every arm: w_records applied to the tries that arm actually drew, so every arm builds records the same way.

Exploratory, no pass mark, no claim: (a) cut-only allocator: each stuck question gets its first 96 pass-2 draws; then questions ranked by near-miss count in those 96 draws are extended toward 480 in rank order until total pass-2 calls reach 75% of C's; (b) the same allocator with the ranking shuffled within each kind (placebo); (c) oracle stop at each question's last fit (reported only, not deployable); (d) arrival curve of fits at 96, 192, 288, 384 and 480 draws, per kind. The Luby and Good-Turing arms are dropped.
plan.seeds: 2 parents (s100, s101) x 2 sampling draws = 4 cells, a screen only (rule 4). Draw 1 is job 8's own night-1 search: search seed 10, pass-2 seed 1010 (seed + 1000). It doubles as the step-0 reproduction. Draw 2 is a held-out search seed 100 (pass-2 seed 1100). Scoring uses the 614 multi-step pool questions (affine 205, double_add 204, sq_plus 205; c2_keep.MULTI). No claim comes from 4 cells; a claim needs 6 paired parents (s200-s205).
plan.machine: Ben's Mac CPU with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and the same torch build as job 8, for step 0 and both parents (Nprime.pt under ~/creative/c2keep-s100 and -s101; Mac only, MAC-JOB-8.md section 2). The PC CPU with the mount's N_ss.pt is an allowed fallback only as a labelled positive-control sanity run, because N_ss is job 6's parent, not N'. No GPU for any reproduction: the sampler's generator is device-specific (legal.py:196-205), so streams are expected to differ [suggested].
pass_marks: [Marks fixed now. Scored per cell (parent x draw). Pass 1 is shared by all arms. Labels: shown = measured in this project; derived = arithmetic on shown counts; suggested = reasoned.]

M1 fits (arm B): multi-step questions with at least one checked fit must be at least 90% of C's count (C = 150 on s100 and 168 on s101, shown in results/c2stuck JSON), measured at B's own calls, which M2 caps.

M2 calls (arm B): multi-step pass-2 calls at most 75% of C's (C = 287,520 on s100 and 285,600 on s101; derived from shown per-kind counts: 599 and 595 stuck multi-step questions x 480). All-kind calls are reported, not scored.

M3 beats the fixed cut (arm B): M1 fits minus F's fits (F matched on multi-step calls) at least +2.0 points of the 614, with the paired 95% lower bound above 0 (2,000 resamples over the 614 questions, seed 0, as c2_pilot.boot, c2_pilot.py:45-51).
M4 dose (arm B): all-kind records at least 90% of C's. Updates equal records (c2_stuck.py:102), so this is the sleep-dose check. A miss makes the cell BETWEEN, not PASS.
Cell PASS (arm B): M1 to M4 all hold. Screen PASS: all four cells pass.
BETWEEN: any cell that is neither PASS nor PROVED WRONG (for example multi-step fits at 80-90% of C at 75% calls, or an M3 interval that crosses 0). Report the curve and run no sleep.

Arm A (cost fact only): all-kind pass-2 calls saved at least 15% on both parents. No multi-step call mark for A: it cannot reach 15% on multi-step calls (derived upper bounds 5.0% on s100 and 11.5% on s101).

Exploratory (reporting only, no claim): allocator AUC for a checked fit in draws 97-480, among stuck questions with no fit in their first 96 pass-2 draws, with the near-miss count in those 96 draws as the score; per kind for double_add and sq_plus. The 0.65 bar and beating the within-kind shuffle are reported, not claimed. Affine has 10 to 14 pass-2 finds per parent, so no affine AUC.

What a screen PASS would show: a give-up rule can cut multi-step search by about a quarter on two parents and two draws without losing checked fits, and beat a fixed cut. It would not show learning, a climb, autonomy or a deployable rule.
plan.proved_wrong: Arm B, judged per parent on the job-8 draw: proved wrong if multi-step fits fall below 80% of C's at 75% or fewer multi-step calls on either parent, or if M3's point difference is 0 or below on both parents. The held-out draw must agree in sign before either verdict stands. Arm A: proved wrong as a cost lever if all-kind pass-2 calls fall below 5% on both parents. Context [suggested, from job-8 per-kind counts with a constant per-question rate fitted to each kind]: a plain cut at 75% of calls keeps 78.7% (s100) and 80.5% (s101) of multi-step pass-2 finds, so the 80% line sits close to the no-signal case. Within-kind spread would raise that figure, which is why M3 is needed.
plan.null_risk: Yes, in four ways. (1) Arm A cannot change record or fit counts. w_records keeps min(2, distinct checked fits) (fewshot._distinct, fewshot.py:157-169; c2_stuck.py:57-68), and a question stops only after two distinct fits, so A's record and fit marks pass trivially. Only its calls are informative. Its multi-step saving is bounded above at 5.0% (s100) and 11.5% (s101) [derived: 180-150 = 30 and 237-168 = 69 multi-step questions hold two records; each saves at most 478 draws]. Any all-kind pass therefore comes from square and last_digit. (2) A plain fixed cut can keep 90% or more of multi-step finds at 75% of calls if finds are front-loaded within each kind. Then M1 passes for the comparator with no near-miss signal. Only M3 catches that. (3) M2 is cheap to pass if the give-up fires broadly rather than selectively. A 25% multi-step cut needs about 188 (s100) and 186 (s101) give-ups among 464 and 446 never-found multi-step questions [derived; each give-up saves 384 draws], so M1 and M3 carry the test. (4) Scope: T 3.0 is DEV-picked. s100's own grid ties 3.0 and 4.0 at 0.254. s101's own pick was 4.0, where 3.0 gives 0.195 and 4.0 gives 0.207 (fast-sleep/parents/s100 and s101 setup.json). So a pass is specific to T 3.0 and s101 runs at a non-own T. Also: two draws per parent is a screen, the five kinds were chosen by us, and N' carries stones we wrote. A false PASS is unlikely if all four cells and the held-out draw agree. A cost-only reading of arm A could pass with no change to learning, so A is never reported as a learning result.
plan.autonomy: Not autonomous today. The probe is labelled 'no' on both 7c labels (outside help: yes, the parent's stones were written by us and the pool was chosen by us; own choices: no, B3 is not built). Step by step, with what the deployed model would need: (1) Deciding it is stuck: has_fit over pass 1 is a script over the example check (c2_stuck.py:38-40). The model needs its own stuck decision from a checker tool it calls (C9, B3). (2) Trying: sampling at T 3.0 is a DEV-picked setting (the job-6 rule). Under Ben's rule 10 it counts only when a rule the model runs picks it from its own checks, or when it is learned. (3) Checking: the Python example check runs in the loop (fewshot.verdict). It must become a tool the model calls. (4) Stopping: arms A and B are script rules. Their constants (2 fits, a 96-try window, near-miss = 2 of 3) are design constants, allowed under 7c if identical every night. The stop itself must become the model's own write-STOP decision after a check reply (B3). (5) Keeping records: the 2-fit cap keyed by result_key is a script rule. (6) Sleep dose (32 visits per record, lr 1e-3, 16 + 16 replay rows) is a fixed design setting and allowed. The nightly schedule is a script (fast-sleep thread). (7) Practice: the five held-out kinds were picked by us, which rule 10 does not allow. The deployed model must pick its own practice (C9). (8) Parent N' has stepping stones we wrote for these exact kinds (7c: positive control only). The logger, the replay and the marks are tests, outside the model (7c). Nothing here claims the model stops itself.
steps: Preflight: run creative/tests/test_c2_stuck.py and test_c2_keep.py. Record the torch version, the thread count and each parent's Nprime.pt path (job 8 used ~/creative/c2keep-s100/Nprime.pt and -s101). Mac first; the PC with N_ss is the labelled fallback.

Write creative/c2_trylog.py (new). Load the pool as c2_stuck.run does (c2_stones._with_nums(R.load_split(DATA, 'pool')), c2_stuck.py:93). Load N' with sleep.load_parent, call N.eval() (c2_stuck.py:122; the parents README notes the model is left in train mode), then call c2_stuck.search(N, pool, vocab, device, seed=S, T=3.0, n1=32, n2=480). Log each try after the fact, with no sampler change and no extra RNG draws: question id, pass, index, structure ok, examples reproduced 0-3, fit flag (c2_stuck.fits), result_key (programs.result_key on the query-valid array, as fewshot._distinct does), query output, and the full try (ops, operands, answer).
Test (creative/tests/test_c2_trylog.py, new): tries with and without the logger are identical on a 20-question slice, and the logged fit flags match c2_stuck.has_fit on the same slice.

Step 0 (S=10, both parents, Mac): reproduce job 8 night 1 exactly. Check pass-1 and pass-2 finds per kind (10 numbers per parent), stuck counts 760 and 765, pass-2 draws 364,800 and 367,200, records 809 and 841, records by kind, multi-step records 180 and 237, and multi-step fits 150 and 168. Rebuild records with w_records(pool, tries, seed=1), the call c2_stuck.run makes for night 1 (seed + night). Any mismatch: stop and report; do not tune. Draw 2 (S=100, both parents, same pool and T): the held-out draw.

Replay, pure Python on the logs (no model, no new draws). For each stuck question, cut each arm's drawn sequence by its rule. Count pass-2 calls, fits (any checked fit, pass 1 included), records via w_records on the tries drawn, and all-kind records. For F, find the integer k that matches B's multi-step calls. Then score M1 to M4 per cell with the paired bootstrap, and write per-kind fits and calls for C, A, B and F to creative/results/c2trylog/. Cost wording (replaces the brief's 40-95% line): search is 62-63% of job-8 wall time on night 1 and 42-44% on night 2 (shown seconds in results/c2stuck). A 75% pass-2 cut saves about 14% of night-1 and 9-10% of night-2 wall time [derived]. Drop the 25.5 TFLOP sentence: it covers pass 1 only (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md line 112). Do not cite 64.5/77.3/94.9 (unverified, RESEARCH lines 53-55; the area check gave 58.2/73.8).
Apply the screen rule: B passes only if all four cells pass. Write the verdict as one row per cell (M1 to M4, the M3 interval, calls and records by kind).

Only if B passes all four cells: one night-1 sleep per parent for C and for B, each built from that arm's records. Updates equal records, with the job-8 dose (32 visits per record, lr 1e-3, 16 + 16 replay rows of 32). Each run takes about 19 min (job-8 timing: sleep 932 s and 970 s, eval 186 s). Compare the multi-step first try with N' (job 8 night 1 gave +3.9 and +4.5). No new search. This shows only that sleep still learns from B's records. It is not a climb.

Only if step 8 passes: a live two-night run of B in the loop against C on the same parents. Job 8's full runs took 6,022 s and 6,003 s per parent, so budget about 1.7 h per parent. Then the confirm below.

Rules during all steps: pool and DEV only (rule 5; the sealed test is not read). T stays 3.0 for the screen, and s101's own job-6 pick was 4.0 (fast-sleep/parents/s101/setup.json), so s101 runs at a non-own T and this is reported. No new teacher or model (rule 2). No edits to sampler.py, legal.py, fewshot.py or programs.py.

fixed_plan.title: Give-up rule replay on one logged stuck search
fixed_plan.ben_line: When the AI is stuck, it keeps trying hundreds of times on one hard question. This tests whether it can stop early on hopeless questions and still keep the answers it would have found. It replays tries the model already made and trains nothing.
fixed_plan.question: Does a fixed give-up rule (after 96 extra tries, stop a stuck question that has no fitting try and no 2-of-3 try) keep at least 90% of multi-step checked fits, use 75% or fewer multi-step calls, and beat a random placebo with the same number of give-ups?
fixed_plan.one_change: Only the give-up rule. No second-fit stop in the screen. Everything else as job 8: 32 pass-1 tries, 480 extra tries for stuck questions, T 3.0, at most 2 distinct fits kept.
arms: C: job 8 as run, replayed from the log.
B: C plus the give-up rule (the one change).
P: placebo, same number of give-ups as B, applied at random to never-fitted stuck questions.
F (reported only): fixed cut at 75% of C's calls, no near-miss test.
fixed_plan.seeds: 2 parents (s100, s101), pool only, 614 multi-step questions. Decisive draw: fresh search seed 100 (pass-2 seed 1100). Seed 10 (job 8's draw) is a reproduction check only, counts within plus or minus 20. Screen only; a claim needs s200 to s205.
fixed_plan.machine: PC CPU or the Mac after job 9. Any CPU works because all arms are cut from one logged run. Start point: the Mac Nprime.pt, or a CPU rebuild that passes the count check. No GPU needed. Hours 1.2 = gate 0.15 + one draw per parent side by side 0.55 + rebuild check, tests and replay 0.5 (estimates, untested).
pass_marks: Gate (200 never-fitted multi-step questions, one draw, before the full screen): give-up fires on at least 40% of them, else stop.
M1 per cell, against that cell's own C: B keeps at least 90% of C's multi-step questions with a checked fit.
M2: B's multi-step pass-2 calls at most 75% of C's in the same draw.
M3: B minus P in multi-step checked fits at least +2.0 points of 614, paired bootstrap 95% lower bound above 0 (c2_pilot.boot, 2000 resamples, seed 0).
M5: gold-correct share of B's kept records at least C's minus 2 points; distinct result_key per question at least 0.9 x C's.
Screen PASS: M1, M2, M3 and M5 hold on both parents on the fresh draw.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: M1 fails on both parents, or M3 is 0 or below on both, or the gate fraction is under 40% (M2 cannot pass). As a cost lever: B's calls stay above 90% of C's on both parents.
fixed_plan.null_risk: High on cost: if 2-of-3 tries are common the give-up rarely fires, and no file measures that rate. Moderate on losses: with about 135 finds per parent, 2 points is about 12 questions. P matches the give-up count, so M3 tests the near-miss signal itself. Two parents, one fresh draw on the same questions.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Not autonomous. The give-up and near-miss test are script rules over the hand example checker, and the stop is not the model's own decision. T 3.0 is DEV-picked. The constants (96 draws, 2 of 3) are allowed under 7c only if fixed every night. Cost-only result; nothing here shows the model stops itself.
steps: Start point: check the Mac Nprime.pt, or a CPU rebuild by c2_keep.py from raw B2 (mount: custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100/checkpoint.pt). The rebuild must match job 8 night-1 counts within plus or minus 20.

Write c2_trylog.py: wrap c2_stuck.search with no sampler change; log per try question id, pass, index, structure ok, examples reproduced (0-3), fit flag, result_key, query output and gold-correct flag. Test: logged fit flags equal c2_stuck.has_fit on 20 questions.
Gate: 200 never-fitted multi-step pool questions, one draw (about 8 min at an untested 210 tries per second). Report give-up fraction and find loss. Stop on failure.
Full draw: both parents side by side, seed 100. Replay C, B, P and F in pure Python on the log; one row per cell.
Only if the screen passes: one sleep per parent for C and for B with the same update count; mark: multi-step first try vs N' not below C's minus 2 points. Not a climb.
Stop there. Live runs and any confirm need marks and hours written first.

fixed_plan.confirm: Not written; needs marks and hours first. Six parents (s200 to s205) with one fresh draw each is about 3 CPU-h of search. final.why: The job 8 counts in the plan check out against results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json (shown). Pass 2 drew 364,800 and 367,200 tries on 760 and 765 stuck questions. Multi-step pass-2 finds were 135 and 149 (affine+double_add+sq_plus). Night-1 search was 62.8% of night-1 wall time and 43.9% of night-2 wall time. The fixed plan (a give-up rule, a random placebo, no second-fit stop) is a sound CPU screen, but the ceiling is low. Marks M1 and M2 are scored on multi-step calls only, so a 25% multi-step cut saves about 11% of night-1 wall time and about 8% of night-2 (derived, not run). Under a flat per-try hazard the cut keeps only about 79-81% of finds (suggested), against the 90% mark. The give-up is a script rule, not the model's own decision, so rule 10 is met only as a probe, and it becomes real only with a learned stop head or the B3 tool loop (neither built). Its value also depends on job 9: the Mac is busy with it for about 10 h (untested estimate), and if the sealed test shows no multi-step climb, a cost lever for that loop is moot. Park it until job 9 is read. It is cheap CPU (0 GPU hours), so it can run soon after, after the placebo and gate fixes below. Keep the per-try log, since a learned stop head or stuck signal (C9) would need it as training data.
final.ben_line: This test replays tries the AI already made, to see whether it could give up sooner on hopeless hard questions, but it would save only about a tenth of a night's work and the give-up rule would still be our code, not the AI's own choice, so it waits until the big job 9 test is finished.
plan_fixes: Placebo P is ill-defined as written. 'Random never-fitted stuck questions' is picked by hindsight, so P would lose zero finds by construction and M3 could not be read. Draw P at random from the set eligible at 96 pass-2 tries (stuck, no fit yet), with the same number of give-ups as B. Report a kind-blind and a within-kind shuffle, because near-miss may only proxy kind.

The gate's denominator is outcome-defined ('never-fitted'). Define the give-up fraction over stuck questions known at runtime (no fit in pass 1 plus the first 96 pass-2 tries). Add a gate mark on find loss, since the plan says 'report find loss' but sets no threshold, for example at least 85% of finds kept in the 200-question sample.

The gate needs a pass-1 run over the pool first to know which questions are stuck, and per-question data was never saved. Add that cost, about 2 min for 614 questions x 32 tries at the untested 210 tries/s.

Hours are inconsistent. 1.2 h covers one draw per parent, but the plan also runs a seed-10 reproduction draw. Budget about 1.8 h for two draws per parent plus a rebuild check (estimates, untested), and say the Mac wait for job 9 is not counted.

State that M2 is on multi-step calls only. Report the all-kind wall-time saving (about 11% of night 1 and 8% of night 2, derived) so nobody quotes 25% as a night-level saving. Drop any '40-95% of compute' or 'biggest cost lever' wording.

M1 (at least 90% of fits kept at 75% of calls) probably sits above the flat-hazard null of 79-81% (suggested). Say in advance that 'proved wrong on M1 on both parents' is an expected and useful outcome, and that M3 and the per-kind arrival curve are the informative reads.

Say that no constant (96, 2 of 3) may change after the first per-try log is read. Draw 2 is the decisive draw, but it uses the same 614 questions and the same parent, so it is not a new-question test.

The sleep check is underpowered: 1 DEV multi-step question is 0.65 points of 154, so a 'not below C minus 2' mark is about 3 questions. Use a paired interval vs C, keep the update count equal for B and C, and write down the visits-per-record difference. Call it a sanity check, not a climb.

N' (Nprime.pt) is Mac-only. A PC CPU rebuild from raw B2 s100 (custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100/checkpoint.pt) is a different torch stream. Label any PC run as approximate, and use the plus or minus 20 band as a sanity gate only.

Label the arms under roadmap 7c: 'no outside help' only if the constants are fixed before the run, and 'own choices' is no until B3 or a learned stop head exists. The parent carries stepping stones we wrote and T 3.0 is DEV-picked (s101's own pick was 4.0), so call the result a positive-control cost screen. The log supports stop rules and cut-only allocation, not temperature schedules or hidden-state stuck features.

idea.title: Let the example check accept leave-out reads of example numbers
idea.summary: The current checker rejects any try that points at a prompt number other than the query input, yet B2's pointers can address all 16 prompt slots and the whole affine family has short in-context programs (affine 6 steps) that read the examples. Test first, with free probes, whether a relaxed check that lets a try read example pairs it leaves out of the fit would accept right affine programs; only then run a sleep screen.
idea.change: Stage 1 (no training, DEV only): (a) blind search extended with prompt-number operands at 6,000 candidates, scored against the key; (b) draw 512 plain tries per DEV question from N_ss.pt (s100, s101) at T 3.0 and score each under the strict verdict and the relaxed verdict; relaxed = fewshot.structure drops the rule at lines 43-44, a try may read example slots provided at least one example pair stays unread, and verdict accepts iff every unread pair is reproduced with only the query slot rebound (leave-out avoids the trivial fit of a pair that was read). Count relaxed-only accepted tries, their key agreement, and affine DEV questions with a relaxed-only fit. Stage 2 (only if stage 1 passes): 2-seed screen of sleep under strict versus relaxed check, with value_blind_floor (fewshot.py:291-308) recomputed over the relaxed read set. It changes the C2 spec, so any claim needs a fresh seal (C2-R); the job 9 test is never used.
idea.why: Shown: fewshot.py:43-44 rejects such reads, so training can never reward them; the GPT prompt's claim that x + (y1 - x1) also passes the check is wrong as coded, and its input range 2-29 is wrong (3-29 except 10). Shown by inline check: read programs give the right answer on 52/52 affine DEV rows and on all other kinds. Affine reach@512 with the strict check is only 12/205 and 16/205 on the pool. Relaxing can only add accepted programs, so the probe measures their precision directly. Strict precision is 100% at T 0.5-1.4 but 93.9-95.3% for the stone parent at T 3.0.

test.where: CPU or M1 Pro. Stage 1: DEV 256 questions, N_ss.pt s100/s101 (/mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/parents), 512 tries each (about 0.5 h at 210 tries per second); blind-with-reads on CPU. Stage 2 if triggered: PC, s100/s101, about 4 h.
test.arms: Strict versus relaxed (leave-out) verdicts on the same samples; blind search with prompt-number operands; stage 2: strict versus relaxed sleep, nothing else different.
test.pass_mark: Stage 1, both parents: relaxed-only accepted tries right >=85%; >=3 of 52 DEV affine questions get a relaxed-only fit; read programs >=5% of affine samples. Stage 2, both seeds: affine DEV greedy first try +8 points (4 of 52) over strict, reach@32 +15, skills harm <=2, relaxed value-blind floor under 0.5% reach@32 per kind; claim needs six parents on a fresh sealed C2-R split.
test.proved_wrong: Stage 1: relaxed-only right <75% on either parent, or no affine question gets a relaxed-only fit on either parent. Stage 2: affine gain <=+2 on either seed, or read share under 1% (the checker is not the blocker).

idea.rules_check: Rule 1: the check is a hand-written tool; deploy needs the model to call it by writing text (B3, roadmap D3). Rule 2: no teacher. Rule 3: 0 params. Rule 4: probe, then screen, marks fixed here. Rule 5: DEV and pool only; job 9 test untouched. Rule 7: whole programs. Rule 8: affine is the stuck kind. Rule 10: until the check is a tool call, a pass is a result about the checker, not about the deployed model.
idea.closest_prior: Roadmap D3 (checker as a tool) changes who runs the check, not what it accepts. Fast-sleep gpt two-constant prompt assumes reads pass. No run has tested reads.
idea.autonomy: The reads are pointer choices B2 already makes. The check must become a tool the model calls; the keep rule (at most 2 distinct fits) is hand-set.
idea.director_note: Critics should check: leave-out semantics (a program that reads x1 and y1 trivially fits example 1, so only the unread pairs are a real test); that the relaxed floor is recomputed; that a pass is not read against strict-check numbers; the new-seal requirement; and that the ladder (affine wall) shows reads are actually written (ROUTE LIVE) before stage 2 is spent.

problems: 1. It reverses a deliberate, restated spec, so it is a new task rather than a checker tweak. Shown: fewshot.py:5-6 says a pointer at any other prompt number 'has no role and is rejected'; fewshot.py:43-44 enforces it; creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:454-456 (C2a) says 'built this way in PR #44'; fast-sleep/gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md:24 says the model 'may never read the example numbers'. The idea gives a C2-R seal but does not say it changes what C2 measures: the value-blind floor, the 3x-floor cold-start gate (fewshot.py:311, 319-325), and 'rules built from constants'. It needs Ben's ruling before any seal.

2. The causal premise is weak. Shown: direct supervision on strict-correct affine programs does not teach affine: PC' affine 2%/4% first try, 'still rising, so feasibility may be understated' (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:606-607); PC affine 0%/4% (line 568). So the checker is not shown to be the blocker; writing the affine program is. Shown: the constant-form affine reference is 3-5 steps (data/c2/MANIFEST.json ref_steps, per brief). Untested: the idea's 6-step read form, which comes from an unsaved check. Reads may not remove the multi-step problem. The read-share count is the right first measurement, but the idea should say the read route may fail for the same reason.

3. The affine leave-out check tests one point. Suggested, from the arithmetic of the affine form: fitting both A and B needs two example pairs read, which leaves one pair to check. A random affine program can pass one point by chance. By contrast sq_plus and double_add need one pair read (two checks). A pooled 'relaxed-only right >= 85%' can be met by the other kinds and hide affine. Precision must be reported per kind, with affine separate.

4. No chance control. The design measures accepted tries against the key, but has no placebo. The C2 spec already has a corrupt-the-keys leak test (c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md table, 'leak test (corrupt every key) pass'). The analogue here is corrupting the unread example outputs. Stage 1's mark ('>= 3 of 52 affine questions get a relaxed-only fit') counts accepted tries, not right ones.

5. Pass-mark defects. (a) 'affine DEV greedy first try +8 points (4 of 52)': 4 of 52 is 7.7 points, so the mark is internally inconsistent. On 52 paired questions a 4-question gap is about 1.5 standard errors (suggested, arithmetic), too noisy for a 2-seed screen. (b) 'relaxed value-blind floor under 0.5% reach@32 per kind': shown, the strict floor is 0.16% mean per try and 4.8% reach@32 pooled (results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json, floor and floor_reach32). The idea says relaxing only adds accepted programs, so the relaxed floor should be at least as high. The mark looks unreachable as written. (c) No verdict is given for stage-1 precision between 75% and 85%, for 1-2 affine questions, for read share between 1% and 5%, or for stage-2 affine gain between +2 and +8. Rule 4 needs every outcome decided in advance.

6. Precision claims are misstated, and the spec's own mechanism mark is never reported. The idea says 'strict precision is 100% at T 0.5-1.4'. That holds only for the warm-only parent N. The stone parent SS at T 1.4 is 63% (s100) and 75% (s101) (shown, computed from results/c2stones luck and key_luck). At T 3.0 SS is 95.3% and 93.9% (shown; the idea's numbers are right). The C2 mechanism mark requires at least 99% key agreement on accepted tries (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:462; fewshot.py:106-117 mechanism_report). No results or roadmap file reports it, and the operating point already fails it. The idea's 85% bar for relaxed tries is looser than the spec's own mark, and the idea should say so.

7. The stage-2 parent named 'PC' is contaminated and not autonomous. Shown: PC is built from pool rows' hidden rule parameters (rules_real.py:203 uses r['params']; c2_stones.py:88 PC = stones.solver_records(pool, copies=2); c2_stones.py:6 'report only'). Using it as the stage-2 parent imports generator knowledge, which Ben's 10-07 autonomy rule excludes. Stage 2 must start from the stone parent (N_ss.pt, the SS arm).

8. Rule 10 is not met in stage 2. Stage 2 runs a hand-written verdict inside sleep. The roadmap's statement that 'choosing training data and scoring may stay hand-written under Ben's rule' (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md lines 897-899) predates the 10-07 autonomy rule and conflicts with it. The stage-2 result can therefore only be a screen. The idea says so, but it should not carry any deploy label.

9. The leave-out rule is ambiguous. 'At least one example pair stays unread' does not define a pair as read when a program reads x_k but not y_k. In that case the check on pair k rebinds a slot the program itself reads. Define a pair as unread only when both its slots are unread, and check only those pairs.

10. Stage 1(a) is underspecified and unmatched. The blind search with prompt-number operands has no stated fit rule (full fit or leave-out) and no strict comparator from the same run. The notes' 64.5/77.3 blind figures are unverified (per the area fact check; reported 58.2/73.8 at 1k/6k on the same file). Compare within one run and report candidates examined, not guesses. The operand space grows from about 5 to 27 slots, so budgets must be matched on candidates examined.

11. Unsaved checks are labelled 'shown'. 'Read programs give the DEV key on 52/52 affine rows and all other kinds' and 'step-level in-context programs give the key on all 256 rows' come from an inline check that was not saved, and the idea's own evidence list says so. They are existence proofs with hand-built programs, not B2 results. They should be labelled untested.

12. Timing and resources. The 210 tries per second figure is supported (shown: results/c2stuck/s100.json night1_search 1,889.5 s for 397,568 samples), so the 0.5 h estimate holds. But the Mac is running job 9 (creative-pilot/MAC-JOB-9.md; roadmap file time 10-07 18:49), so the probe should wait until job 9 finishes or use the 5070 Ti.

Checks that hold as stated: fewshot.py:43-44 rejects example reads, so the GPT prompt's claim that x + (y1 - x1) passes is wrong (shown; gpt-c2-no-climb-2026-10-07.md:33). The GPT prompt's input range 2-29 is wrong: rules_real.py:26 gives 3-29 except 10 (shown). B2 has 27 slots including all 16 prompt numbers (progparse.py:1-10, shown). The affine pool finds are 12/205 and 16/205 (c2stuck s100 and s101, pass1+pass2 affine, shown). Relaxing can only add accepted programs (by code reading, suggested). N_ss.pt exists for s100 and s101 (shown, ls).
critiques.rescue: Make it rule-safe and new in this order. (0) Free step first, no checker change: from DEV 512-try samples per question at T 3.0, histogram the existing rejection reasons (fewshot.py:34-47). Count the share of tries rejected only because they point at a non-query prompt number. Stop if it is under 1%. (1) Define a pair as read if either slot is read, and check only fully unread pairs. Report relaxed-only right fits (key agreement) per kind, with affine reported separately. (2) Add a placebo: corrupt the unread example outputs on the same tries, and require the real relaxed-only right rate to beat the placebo by a fixed margin. (3) Fix the marks before running: keep the precision bar at the spec's 99% mechanism mark, or state the amendment and its reason. Express the affine gain as a count with an interval, not '+8 (4 of 52)'. Drop the 0.5% floor, or give the relaxed floor's sampling rule and a number the 4.8% strict floor allows. Fill every verdict gap (stage-1 precision 75-85%, 1-2 affine questions, read share 1-5%; stage-2 affine gain +2 to +8). (4) Ben rules first: whether C2 may read example numbers changes the spec in fewshot.py:5-6 and the affine prompt, so get a ruling before any C2-R seal, and seal with a recorded hash. (5) Stage 2 parent is the stone parent (N_ss.pt, SS arm), never PC. Label stage 2 a screen with a hand checker, not a deploy result, until the checker is a tool the model calls (D3). (6) Run the probe after job 9, or on the 5070 Ti. (7) Later, not in this probe: a supervised read-form affine arm built from hand-written teaching data (allowed under rule 1), compared with PC' affine 2-4%. If it stays near that, reads are not the fix."
critiques.already_tried: None found for the idea itself. No relaxed or leave-out checker exists in the creative code outside archive/ and tests/. No read-the-example-numbers run appears in the roadmap, creative-pilot, papers or fast-sleep notes. Closest prior: the strict checker by design (fewshot.py:5-6, 43-44; creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:454-456, PR #44). critiques.expected_effect: Stage 1 steps 0-2 would show whether B2's own tries write example reads at all, and whether any relaxed-only affine fits are right rather than lucky. It costs about 0.5 h of CPU after job 9, and the rate (about 210 tries per second) is supported by the job-8 timing. It cannot show a deployed gain: stage 2 is a screen under a hand checker and changes the C2 spec. Suggested: even if reads appear, affine is likely still limited by writing the longer multi-step program, as PC' (2-4%) suggests, so expect a small or null climb on affine.

problems: Parent conflicts with roadmap 7c (shown: creative-roadmap lines 946 and 954-956). Stages 1 and 2 both run from N_ss.pt, whose stepping stones were written by us in code for the five held-out kinds (stones.py; roadmap 7c row N'). 7c says no later test may use such stones except as a positive control. Stage 2 is a sleep screen on that parent, so it is out of bounds as written. Stage 1 is also a later test on it. The rules_check cites rule 10 only and does not address 7c.

Precision claim is misstated (shown: results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json, arms N, SS, P; precision = key_luck / luck). The idea says strict precision is 100% at T 0.5-1.4. That holds only for the warm-only N arm (100% on both seeds) and the P arm. The stone parent (SS, the one this idea uses) is 57-63% on s100 and 67-75% on s101 at T 0.5-1.4. It reaches 95.3% (s100) and 93.9% (s101) only at T 3.0. So the strict check is not a precise judge of the stone parent at low temperatures, which matters for any sleep on its tries.

A stone-free parent exists only for seeds 200-205 (shown: fast-sleep/confirm/s200..s205/warm.pt present). fast-sleep/parents/README.md says the warm-only checkpoint for s100 and s101 was not kept. Warm-only N reaches reach@32 of 5.1% (s100) and 9.8% (s101) at T 3.0, against the 10% gate (shown: c2stones N arm). Stages 1 and 2 could run on seeds 200-201 with DEV only, leaving job 9's sealed test untouched. Stage 2 cold start would then depend on the relaxed check itself, which is a real test.

Temperature is a DEV pick (shown: c2b.py:143-144 picks T on DEV; c2_stuck.py:16 default 3.0; roadmap 7c row 'Sampling temperature picked on a DEV grid', line 966). Rule 10 excludes a runtime value tuned on DEV. Autonomous route (suggested, in the spirit of 7c's rule that a setting re-picked per kind is allowed when it uses the example check alone): sample several temperatures per question and keep the one whose tries fit the examples. No key and no DEV grid are needed.

The relaxed verdict is hand code that the deployed model cannot call yet (shown: roadmap D3 lines 895-921 waits for B3's tool loop and T1's call grammar; fewshot.verdict returns a reason string, not per-example values, fewshot.py:84-103). Autonomous route: the relaxed check as a tool the model calls by writing text, with its own fidelity mark (D3 mark 1: 10,000 fuzzed tries at 100%) and a reply that names the failed example. The idea's test list has no fidelity mark for the new verdict.

The practice pool is made for the held-out kinds (shown: data/c2/MANIFEST.json pool of 1,024 questions with kind labels; c2b.py draws the W and R records from it). Rule 10 says a hand-picked practice set does not count. 7c says a no-outside-help arm uses nothing made for the specific new kinds. Stage 2 fails this. Stage 1, a probe of tries, can keep it. Autonomous route: C9 (the model chooses its own practice by learning progress), which is not built.

The keep rule is syntactic, so relaxed reads break it (shown: programs.py:110-114 result_key is the canonical expression of the answer cone; fewshot._distinct uses it, fewshot.py:157-169). Under relaxed reads, y1 + a(xq - x1) and y2 + a(xq - x2) compute the same function but are different expressions. The cap of 2 and the sameness gate would then count syntax, not behaviour. The cap of 2 is a fixed design constant and allowed if untuned. Fix: key distinctness on query output or on values over the examples.

Warm add/mult replay during sleep needs a ruling (shown: c2b.py:91 passes warm_rows as replay_extra in every sleep arm; 16 of 64 rows per batch per the code notes; the rows come from our breadth-first solver, fewshot.py:235-271; roadmap 7c row 'Warm-up programs from our breadth-first solver', line 969). Pre-deployment warm-up counts as building the model (7c). A fixed hand-made set replayed every night is not clearly allowed under rule 10. Stage 2 is defined as 'nothing else different', so it inherits this.

The stuck schedule and stuck signal are hand code (shown: c2_stuck.py:38-54, has_fit on pass 1 then 480 more tries; roadmap 7c row 'Try budget', line 965). Under D5 the signal becomes relaxed fits, which changes which questions count as stuck. Autonomous route: a learned stuck signal (C9), not built. Until then the schedule is a fixed script, which 7c itself labels 'own choices: no'.

Leave-out is under-specified and the marks leave gaps (suggested, reasoned from fewshot.py:84-103). (a) 'A pair is read' is undefined when only x_i or only y_i appears. (b) With three examples, a program that reads two pairs is checked on one pair only, so its check is structurally weaker than the strict check. (c) Stage 1 passes at relaxed-only right >= 85%, while the strict baseline on the stone parent at T 3.0 is 94-95%. The 75-85% band has no outcome. Stage 2's affine band (+2 to +8 points) also has no outcome. One affine question is 1.9 points on 52, so the 2-seed screen needs paired intervals as job 9 uses.

Unsaved claims are labelled shown. 'Affine 6 steps' and 'DEV key on 52/52 affine rows and all 256 rows' come from an inline check that is not saved in any file. They should be labelled untested. A 6-step read program does exist by hand (suggested, not run): y1 + DIV(SUB(y2, y1), SUB(x2, x1)) times SUB(xq, x1). That is within the 7-step cap (progparse.py:8). A grep of creative-roadmap, creative-pilot and fast-sleep found no saved trace of one.

Verified shown: strict affine reach@512 on the pool, night 1 from the stone parent N': 12/205 for s100 (pass1 2 + pass2 10) and 16/205 for s101 (2 + 14) (results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json, night1_search.questions_with_find_by_kind). The read block is fewshot.py:43-44. The 'relaxed-only' effects the idea predicts are not tested by any saved run.

The ROUTE LIVE check and the affine wall ladder named in the brief are not in any file. A grep of /mnt/project-files for 'ROUTE LIVE', 'affine wall', 'affine ladder' and 'C2-R' returned nothing. Stage 1's 'read programs >= 5% of affine samples' is the only route check, so it must pass before any stage 2 is spent.

Cost: 0.5 h at 210 tries per second is not in any saved file. Saved timings on this CPU give 164-184 tries per second (results/c2stones/s100.json: 8,192 samples in 44.6-50.0 s). At 184/s, the 262,144 tries (2 parents x 256 x 512) take about 24-27 minutes before the blind-with-reads arm. That arm has no rate in the files.

The blind-with-reads arm (stage 1a) has no pass mark. Rule 10 lists search among methods the model must run itself, so a blind search over prompt-number operands is at most a hand tool. Keep it as a control only; it cannot count as the model's own search.

Roadmap line 127 lists 'no example slot' as a B2 limit (shown). progparse.py slots 0-15 are the prompt numbers (shown), so the slot exists but no role for it is trained. The idea should say which it means. Whether B2 ever points at example pairs is untested.

Rule 4: stage 2 is a 2-seed screen whose pass mark has no paired interval (job 9 uses paired intervals). That is acceptable only if it is reported as a screen. The claim needs six parents and a fresh C2-R seal, which the idea already states.

problems: [shown, code] The no-reads rule is real: fewshot.py:43-44 rejects any answer-cone leaf that is a prompt slot other than the query. But the idea's causal claim that this rule is what walls affine is NOT shown. The C2 manifest (creative/data/c2/MANIFEST.json, _spec.not_shown_representable) lists only 3 affine pairs, and the area fact check reports that constant-only blind search finds 6 of 52 DEV affine questions at 6,000 candidates (that figure is in no saved file I could find; untested here). So the strict wall looks like a sampling wall: B2 rarely writes the constant-built programs that exist. Relaxing the checker adds a longer, pointer-heavy family (the idea itself says 6 steps; the C2 reference affine programs are 3-5 steps per the brief's fact list) that is at least as hard to sample. Nothing in the idea predicts the read share.

[shown] Parent mix-up. The affine counts 12/205 and 16/205 (night-1 pass1 plus pass2 in results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json) come from N', whose recorded source is c2keep-s100/Nprime.pt. Stage 1 probes N_ss.pt from fast-sleep/parents/s100 and s101, a different saved parent (inferred to be the stones-sleep arm; results/c2stones/*.json records raw B2_s100.pt as its ckpt). The 95.3% and 93.9% precision figures come from the stones SS arm. Three parents are mixed under one set of numbers. Stage 1 should name one parent and report that parent's own counts.

[shown] Omitted night-2 result that cuts against the premise. On the pool, strict affine finds rose after one night of sleep on 17 and 23 strict affine records: pass1 plus pass2 went from 12 to 15 (s100) and from 16 to 24 (s101) out of 205 (results/c2stuck night2_search). So the strict check is not a fixed ceiling, and sleep on strict records already moves affine on the pool. DEV affine did not move (reach@32 0.0 and 1.9% at night 1 and night 2 in c2stuck by_kind). Pool (18/205) and DEV (1/52) disagree for the same night-1 model at roughly p 0.05 per seed by a rough binomial check. The 52 DEV affine questions may be unrepresentative, so a stage 1 on 52 questions is weak; the pool should be reported too.

[untested, mislabelled] The 'shown by inline check' claims (read programs give the right answer on 52/52 affine DEV rows and all other kinds; affine 6 steps) rest on a check by w1c-1 whose output is not saved (the idea's own source line says so). Under the project's label rule these are untested. Even if true, they show that such programs exist when someone writes them, not that B2 writes one.

[shown, code] Leave-out statistics are underspecified. With k=3 examples (rules_real.py:128), a try that reads one example pair leaves 2 checks, and one that reads two pairs leaves 1. Precision will fall for the tries that read the most, which are exactly the tries the probe is meant to accept. 'Unread' is undefined when only x_k or only y_k is read. Fix: require at least two unread pairs, and report precision by the number of unread pairs.

[shown] The precision base is thin. Stones SS arm at T 3.0 (results/c2stones s100.json, s101.json; luck and key_luck times 8,192): about 121 of 127 (s100) and 93 of 99 (s101) accepted tries right, so six wrong tries per seed. The 100% at T 0.5 to 1.4 for the warm-only arm rests on 5 to 21 accepted tries per temperature. The 85% relaxed bar has no minimum count. With a few dozen relaxed-only accepted tries per parent, the interval on precision is roughly 10 to 15 points wide either side.

[suggested] No null control. Shuffle each question's example outputs (keep the query) and count relaxed accepts; on shuffled data every accept is false by construction, which gives the chance floor the value-blind floor is meant to supply. fewshot.py:291-308 has no read path, so that floor does not cover reads. Without a null control, a precision pass cannot separate reads that generalise from reads that fit by luck.

[shown, idea text] Stage 1 arm (a), blind search with prompt-number operands at 6,000 candidates scored against the key, has no pass mark, so it cannot fail. That breaks Rule 4 (marks fixed before running). A wider operand space at the same budget will dilute the search, so the fair comparison is constant-only blind at 6,000 on the same DEV questions.

[shown, idea text] Stage 1 gates are loose and partly undefined. 'Read programs at least 5% of affine samples' does not say whether 'read' means any prompt-slot pointer or relaxed-accepted. 'At least 3 of 52' has low power: at a true relaxed rate of 5%, P(at least 3) is about 0.5, and at 8% about 0.8 (binomial, my arithmetic); requiring both parents to pass lowers this further. The gate sets no effect size.

[shown, idea text] Stage 2 is underpowered and ambiguous. '+8 points (4 of 52)' on one kind is roughly 3 to 4 points of paired standard error per seed by my estimate from a few discordant pairs, so a two-seed screen cannot separate +8 from the +2 proved-wrong bar. 'Reach@32 +15' is not said to be affine-only or pooled. Affine is 52 of 256 DEV questions and 52 of 154 multi-step questions, so +20 on affine adds about +4 pooled and +7 on multi-step on DEV. That cannot meet job 9's pooled +15 mark on its own.

[shown, idea text] Rule 10 gaps the idea does not name: the sampling temperature T 3.0 is picked on DEV (best_temperature in results/c2stones and c2dev), the 512-try budget is hand-set, and the verdict is a hand tool. The idea names only the checker and the keep rule. The relaxed verdict must not be wired into job 9's strict arms (creative-pilot/MAC-JOB-9.md is running on the strict check now); the idea says the sealed test is untouched but not that the training verdict is.

[shown] Cost estimate is roughly right but its rate is not from a file. The stones SS arm's T 3.0 pass of 8,192 samples took 44.6 s (about 184 tries per second, results/c2stones/s100.json seconds), so 262,144 tries take about 25 minutes plus verdicts. The 210 tries per second figure in the idea appears in no file.
critiques.rescue: (a) Before building the relaxed verdict, run one fresh 32-try DEV sample from N_ss.pt and from N' (about 0.1 h at the logged rate). Histogram the structure reasons (fewshot.py:34-47) and count tries that point at example numbers, split by how many pairs they read. If the read share is near zero, stop; this is cheaper than the full stage 1 and answers the premise first. (b) Use the strongest mechanism argument, which the idea omits: in the 200k skills rows B2 trained on, a later step reads a fresh prompt number 94% of the time (creative/results/legal-probe/REPORT.md:30), and roadmap line 51 says the rules that need a number read off the examples did not move. That is a better case than pointer capacity. (c) Pre-register before running: at least two unread pairs per accepted read try; at least 30 relaxed-only accepted tries per parent before any precision mark is read; a shuffled-example null control whose accepts must be 0 right by construction; a blind-arm mark (relaxed blind at 6,000 must beat constant-only blind at 6,000 on the same DEV affine questions, or it is reported as a ceiling). (d) Run stage 1 on the pool (205 affine questions) as well as DEV, and name the parent in every number. (e) Sequence it after the cheap affine census (constant-only versus read programs by step count), so the relaxed check is built only if reads are both sampled and cheaper than constants.
critiques.already_tried: None found for reads or a leave-out verdict: no saved C2 file tests reads, and the idea itself marks 'whether any relaxed-only fit appears' as untested. Closest prior: fewshot.py:43-44 (the strict no-reads rule, a design choice in roadmap section 7 C2a, roadmap lines 455-456); roadmap line 51 (number-reading rules did not move); results/c2stuck s100.json and s101.json (affine pool counts, nights 1 and 2); results/c2stones s100.json and s101.json (precision at T 3.0 and warm-only at T 0.5 to 1.4); results/legal-probe/REPORT.md:30 (skills rows read prompt numbers 94% of the time). The idea cites no papers, so none were checked.
critiques.expected_effect: Honest estimate (suggested, reasoned, untested): P(stage 1 passes on both parents) about 0.35, since B2's read prior makes a non-zero read share likely but length, pointer choice and the precision bar cut against it; P(stage 2 affine +8 on both seeds | stage 1 pass) about 0.3; P(six-parent sealed confirm | stage 2) about 0.5. Overall about 5%. If it holds, affine first-try rises perhaps +5 to +15 on DEV, which is about +1 to +3 pooled-5 and +2 to +5 on the 154 multi-step questions, inside one-split noise (pooled SD 1.6 to 2.1).
