Checked correct as coded: fewshot.py:43-44 rejects non-query prompt pointers; the relaxed verdict accepts a superset of the strict verdict (strict-accepted tries have every pair unread), so 'relaxing can only add accepted programs' holds; progparse.py:8-10 slot layout (16 prompt, 4 constants, 7 results) holds; DOMAIN is 3-29 except 10 (rules_real.py:26), so the GPT prompt's '2-29' is wrong and x + (y1 - x1) fails structure().

problems: [shown, code] Stage 2 names PC as the parent, but PC is the reference-solver positive control built from pool (kind, params) solver programs with no example check (c2_stones.py:6 and :88 solver_records(pool, copies=2); stones.py:97-100). Neither the strict nor the relaxed verdict touches PC records, so the strict-versus-relaxed sleep contrast is null by construction. Stage 2 must sleep on the checked W arm (tries that pass the check) of N_ss.

[shown, results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json, key_luck/luck per arm] The claim 'Strict precision is 100% at T 0.5-1.4' holds only for the warm base N. For the stone parent SS, key agreement of accepted tries is 0.57-0.63 (s100) and 0.67-0.75 (s101) at T 0.5-1.4, and 0.953 / 0.939 at T 3.0. N is 1.0 at T 0.5-1.4 and 1.0 / 0.939 at T 3.0.

[shown, creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md, C2a 'Pass (mechanism)' about line 462] The project's own checker mark is key agreement of at least 99% on accepted tries. The design's relaxed-only bar of 85% is not that mark, and the strict checker on the stone parent is already below 99% at T 3.0 (94-95%). The design must hold relaxed to 99% or state and justify a replacement mark before running.

[shown, arithmetic and design text] Pass and fail bands are incomplete or internally inconsistent: (a) no minimum count of relaxed-only accepted tries is required, so 2 or 3 accepts can read as 100% (suggested); (b) relaxed precision between 75% and 85%, and 1 or 2 affine questions with a relaxed-only fit, fall into no verdict; (c) the stage 2 example '+8 points (4 of 52)' is 7.7 points, so it fails its own threshold; 5 of 52 (9.6 points) would be needed; (d) 'reach@32 +15' does not name its question set; (e) stage 2 gains have no paired interval, although the job 9 marks use one (c2b.py:385-393 per the code note, not re-read here).

[shown, fewshot.py:34-47] structure() returns only the first failing reason, and no per-try read flag is logged in any saved result. 'Read programs at least 5% of affine samples' therefore has no baseline; the probe must log read flags on tries before a pass can be read.

[shown, fewshot.py:291-308 and blind_baseline.py docstring] No null or no-model comparator is in any pass mark. Blind-with-reads (stage 1a) is reported but not gated, and the value-blind floor is defined only over x and constants, so no random-read floor exists. The brief's fact-check pass reports about 11.5% of DEV affine questions right at 6,000 blind candidates without reads (untested here, not re-run); the pool N' figure is 12/205 and 16/205 at 512 tries (c2stuck JSON). Reads count only if relaxed-only fits beat search with reads at matched examined candidates.

[shown, rules_real.py:136-137 for distinct x; algebra] The in-context affine program (s1=y2-y1, s2=x2-x1, s3=s1/s2, s4=x-x1, s5=s3*s4, s6=s5+y1; 6 steps) reads pairs 1 and 2. Under 'at least one pair stays unread' it is checked on one equation only. It is exact on every affine question by algebra, so the '52/52' claim is shown by algebra; the inline run it cites is not saved and should not be labelled shown. A single-pair check also gives weak chance control for wrong read-programs. Suggested: require at least two checked pairs, or leave-one-out fitting, and measure the chance acceptance rate with a random-read floor.

[shown, fewshot.py:243-247; rules_real.py:80-95 and 198-207; stones.py:34] Every warm, stone and PC solver record comes from find_reference, whose search base is the query slot and the constants only. N_ss has therefore never been trained on an example-slot read. The 200k skills data does read prompt numbers (creative-pilot/rules-breaks-diagnosis-2026-10-06.md, 'Shown: not the skills prior'). A low read share in N_ss may come from C2 training, not from the checker. Add read counts for the raw B2 checkpoint (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100/checkpoint.pt, present, 13.2 MB) as a comparator. The behavioural effect is untested.

[shown, c2stuck JSON seconds; c2stones seconds] No cheap first gate exists. Read share and reject reason on 52 affine DEV questions at 32 tries each (1,664 tries, roughly 10 s) from N_ss and from raw B2 would decide whether the 512-try stage is worth running. The 210 tries per second figure is supported by c2stuck night-1 search (about 400,000 tries in about 1,890 s). Stone-arm scoring runs at 160-185 per second.

[shown, seconds fields; suggested for GPU] Cost: stage 1 is about 262,000 tries (256 DEV x 512 x 2 parents) plus two verdicts, roughly 25-30 min on checker-bound CPU, so the 0.5 h estimate holds. The RTX 5070 Ti speeds only the B2 forward pass; the Python verdict (fewshot.py:84-103, both executors per try) is the bottleneck. Stage 2 is larger than stated: c2stuck shows about 6,000 s total per parent per arm on CPU (about 1,900 s search and 930-1,320 s sleep per night). Two arms and two seeds is about 6-7 h CPU, not 'about 4 h' for PC, which is also the wrong arm. A 3.3M model and its sleeps fit in 16 GB by a wide margin; the GPU saves only the sleep share (suggested: about 1 to 3 min per night).

[shown, rules_real.py:127-167 and dev.jsonl/pool.jsonl read here; test and labelled not opened] The 'held-out' kinds share formulas with the pool. make_questions draws (kind, params) from one grid for every split, and 'avoid' blocks only identical (kind, params, examples, query) tuples. In DEV, 32 of 33 affine (a,b) pairs also occur in pool; every DEV square, last_digit, sq_plus and double_add parameter occurs in pool (square and last_digit each have one formula). So any DEV gain from sleeping on pool records is partly same-formula memory, and the stage 2 DEV affine mark cannot separate reading examples from memorising formulas. A C2-R split built the same way inherits this. The sealed test's overlap is inferred from code, not checked. The fast-sleep note's 'every question has a different a and b' (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md line 15) is contradicted by the DEV file.

[shown, parents/README.md and c2stones SS arm] The stone parent N_ss matches the SS arm, and the README says N_ss is job 6's parent N after stepping-stone sleep. The 12/205 and 16/205 counts come from the Mac N' checkpoint (c2stuck N_prime source path); N_ss is a cloud rebuild whose losses match to 4 digits. Treat them as the same parent at that precision. Also rename the label 'creative-D5': it collides with roadmap D5 'Climb a ladder of checkers' (creative-roadmap line 197) and with roadmap '(D5)' used for C2b.

[shown, stones.py:3 and dev/pool counts] Rule 10: the relaxed verdict is hand code inside the sleep loop, so even a stage 2 pass is a result about the checker, not about the deployed model. The design says this; it stays a probe until the check is a tool the model calls (roadmap D3).
critiques.rescue: Revised sequence. Gate 0 (CPU, about 1 minute): 32 tries on each of the 52 affine DEV questions from N_ss and from raw B2 (29-b2-screen). Log whether each try points at a prompt slot other than the query, and the first reject reason. Stop if read share is under 1% on both checkpoints. Gate 1 (only if reads appear, CPU, about 30 min): the 512-try run, with the relaxed verdict requiring at least two checked pairs (or leave-one-out fitting). Fix before running: relaxed-only precision at least 99% per kind with n reported, a minimum n of relaxed-only accepts (for example 20), explicit stop and revise bands, a blind-with-reads comparator at matched examined candidates, and a random-read floor as the null. Stage 2 only if Gate 1 passes: sleep on the W arm of N_ss (not PC) with strict and relaxed verdicts on the same tries. Affine DEV mark fixed at 5 of 52 with a paired interval. Label any DEV gain as same-formula evidence until a C2-R split with unseen (a,b) pairs is sealed. Any claim needs six parents on that split.
critiques.already_tried: No relaxed verdict or leave-out check appears in the results folders, so none has been run. Closest prior evidence: the strict verdict (fewshot.py:84-103); stone-parent SS per-kind rates at T 3.0 (results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json, affine luck 0.0 and 0.0006, reach@32 0.0 and 0.019); pool affine finds 12/205 and 16/205 (results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json, pass1 plus pass2 counts); and the rejection reasons in diagnose.json, which cover the older puzzle task and not C2. Roadmap D3 (checker as a tool) changes who runs the check, not what it accepts.
critiques.expected_effect: Run as a gated probe, Gate 0 would most likely show a low read share on N_ss, because its C2 training (warm-up, stones and PC records) never contains an example-slot read. That would end the idea for this parent in minutes. A read share on raw B2 well above N_ss would point to training suppression, a cheaper and different fix (suggested). If reads do appear, relaxed-only precision decides the claim against the 99% mark, and DEV affine gains are read as same-formula evidence until an unseen-(a,b) split is sealed. The expected cost is about 1 minute for Gate 0, about 30 minutes CPU for Gate 1, and roughly 6-7 hours CPU for a two-seed, two-arm stage 2. Labels: shown items cite the file or line in the problem text; the 210 tries per second rate is shown from c2stuck seconds; the 11.5% blind affine figure is reported by the brief and was not re-run.

chair.reasons:
Worth a small gated CPU probe (under 1 hour), not a sealed test yet. It asks whether the example check itself throws away what B2 would write, and no other idea in this area asks that.

WHY IT IS WORTH ONE PROBE
- Shown (fewshot.py:34-47, read this session): structure() rejects any answer-cone leaf that is a prompt slot other than the query slot. The docstring (lines 1-8) says this is by design.
- Shown (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md C2a, PR #44; fast-sleep/gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md:24): the no-reads rule was a deliberate spec choice. Relaxing it is a spec change that needs Ben's ruling before any seal.
- Shown (gpt-c2-no-climb-2026-10-07.md:33): the GPT prompt says x + (y1 - x1) also passes the check. As coded it does not. Its question 3 (lines 126-128) asks whether parameter-building is a language problem, and this idea tests that directly.
- Shown (roadmap about lines 568 and 606-607): affine is 0-4% in every arm, including direct supervision on strict programs (PC 0%/4%, PC' 2%/4%). No run has ever let a try read the examples.
- Suggested: constants-only programs make the thinker infer A and B in its head and re-encode them as constant sums. Reads let B2's exact calculator do that arithmetic, which is the design point of B2. Reads also work for parameters outside the 3-30 range that constants reach, which fits the north star of learning a new rule from few examples.
- Shown (legal-probe REPORT.md:30): in the 200k skills rows a later step reads a fresh prompt number 94% of the time. Suggested: the pointer heads default to prompt numbers, so reads may appear in tries even though no C2 training row contains one.
- Shown (architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:83): fewshot_number_rule has no program in the skills data, so B2 has never been taught to write an example-reading program.

WHY IT IS ONLY A PROBE
- Untested: whether B2's tries contain any relaxed-only fit. Suggested (mechanism critic, about 5% overall): the 6-step in-context affine program needs a precise pointer sequence, and all C2 teaching rows (warm-up, stones, PC) are constants-form with zero example-slot reads (shown: find_reference searches over x and constants only, fewshot.py:235-271). Expect a low read share on the stone parent.
- Shown: PC' (2-4%) says writing a long affine program is hard even with direct supervision. Relaxing the check may not remove that. Suggested: the sampling route is likely to find few relaxed-only fits, and the real test may be a read-form teaching-data arm (see plan_guidance).
- Rule 10 (shown by code): the relaxed check is hand code, same as the strict check today. It is a result about the checker, not the deployed model, until it becomes a tool the model calls (roadmap D3, needs B3). Temperature, the 32/480 schedule and the cap of 2 records stay hand-set.
- Roadmap 7c: N_ss was built with our hand-written stepping stones, so it may serve only as a positive control, not as an autonomous parent. A probe that measures the checker is fine on it if labelled so.

WHAT THE CRITICS GOT RIGHT, AND WHAT I CHANGED
1. Stage 2 must not use PC (shown: pool-parameter solver records, c2_stones.py:6 and :88, no example check, so strict versus relaxed would be null by construction). It must sleep on checked W-arm tries.
2. The precision claim was misstated (shown, results/c2stones s100.json and s101.json, key_luck/luck). 100% at T 0.5-1.4 holds only for the warm-only arm. The stone parent SS is 57-63% (s100) and 67-75% (s101) there, and 95.3%/93.9% at T 3.0.
3. The 85% bar is looser than the spec's own mechanism mark (99%, roadmap about line 462, fewshot.py:106-117). The strict check on SS at T 3.0 is already below 99%. The revised mark uses 95% and states the amendment.
4. Marks had gaps. '+8 (4 of 52)' is 7.7 points. 'Relaxed value-blind floor under 0.5% reach@32 per kind' cannot be right because the strict floor is 4.8% reach@32 pooled (c2stones). Several outcome bands had no verdict. All are fixed in the revised idea.
5. 'Unread pair' was undefined. Fixed: a pair is read if either of its slots is in the answer cone.
6. The keep rule (distinct canonical expressions, programs.py:110-114) counts syntax. y1 + a(xq - x1) and y2 + a(xq - x2) are different expressions for the same function, so stage 2 needs distinctness by behaviour.
7. The three inline claims (read programs fit 52/52 affine DEV rows, affine 6 steps) were not saved. The 6-step program is shown by algebra only (exact whenever x2 differs from x1, which rules_real.py:136-137 guarantees), not by a saved run. Label them suggested.
8. The parent mix is confused: the 12/205 and 16/205 pool counts come from N' (Mac checkpoint), N_ss is a cloud rebuild that matches to 4 digits (parents/README.md). Name the parent in every number.
9. DEV shares formulas with the pool (32 of 33 affine (a,b) pairs also appear in the pool; test critic read dev.jsonl and pool.jsonl). A stage-2 DEV gain is therefore partly same-formula memory and cannot show reading. The stage-2 test must use a split with (a,b) pairs disjoint from the pool.
10. The label 'creative-D5' collides with roadmap D5 (checker ladder). Rename to creative-reads.
11. The Mac is running job 9 (about 10 h). Run on Ben's PC (CPU-bound Python verdict; GPU helps only the forward pass).

COST (shown from c2stuck and c2stones seconds): 164-210 tries per second. Affine-only 52 x 512 = 26.6k tries is about 2-3 minutes per parent. All 256 DEV questions x 512 is about 11-13 minutes per parent. Stage 1 totals about 30-45 minutes of CPU plus about 30 lines of new code.

RULE CHECK: rules 1, 2, 3, 5 (DEV only; the C2 test is never opened), 7, 8 (affine is a stuck kind) and 9 (card experiment only) pass. Rule 4 passes once the revised marks are fixed before running. Rule 10 is a stated limit: the result concerns the checker only.
chair.revised_idea:
creative-reads: let the C2 example check accept programs that read example numbers, judged on example pairs the program did not read. Do the model-free census first, then a small sampling probe. Both use DEV only.

DEFINITIONS (fixed before running)
- A pair i is READ if x_i or y_i appears among the leaves of the answer cone. A pair is UNREAD only if neither slot is read.
- Relaxed verdict: the try must still read the query input, run only ops 1-8, run on every row, and be valid in both executors. It must have at least one UNREAD pair. It is accepted iff every UNREAD pair is reproduced when only the query slot is rebound to that pair's x.
- With no reads, relaxed equals strict, so strict-accepted tries are a subset of relaxed-accepted tries on the same samples (shown by code reading). 'Relaxed-only' means accepted by relaxed but rejected by strict.
- Always report precision by number of checked pairs: 1 versus 2 or more. Reads of two pairs leave one checked pair (k=3, rules_real.py:128), so the two-point affine program is checked on one equation only.
- Label as suggested, not shown: 'read programs give the key on 52/52 affine DEV rows'. It is shown by algebra only, not by a saved run.

STAGE 0 (model-free census, minutes of CPU, no checkpoint)
(a) Random-read floor: draw 20,000 random programs per DEV question over x, the example slots and the four constants, lengths 1-4 (same sampler as value_blind_floor, fewshot.py:291-308, widened by the example slots). Judge each with the relaxed verdict and record the per-try wrong-accept rate by kind. Fixed rule: if the relaxed per-try wrong-accept rate on any kind is more than 3x the strict floor's per-try rate on that kind (or above 0.5% per try where the strict floor is 0), the one-pair leave-out check is too lenient. Then require two or more checked pairs and rerun this stage once.
(b) Hand-built existence check: enumerate read-form programs for the five kinds and confirm they are accepted and right on all 256 DEV rows. Include the hybrid form for affine (A from constants, B = y1 - A*x1, reads one pair and leaves two checked). Label the result 'existence, not B2'. Save the per-question output.
(c) Blind search with read operands at 1,000 and 6,000 candidates examined, same run as constant-only blind (re-run blind_baseline.score_rows with both operand sets; do not quote 64.5/77.3). Report only: it is a control, not a mark. The notes' 64.5/77.3/94.9 do not match the fact-check rerun (58.2/73.8 at 1k/6k; 31.8/57.8 on the 154 multi-step questions; affine 11.5% at 6k).

STAGE 1 (sampling probe, CPU on Ben's PC, DEV only, nothing trained)
- Parents: N_ss s100 and s101 (fast-sleep/parents), labelled 'positive control: our hand stones, roadmap 7c'. Comparator: raw B2 s100 and s101 (custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen), to see whether C2 training suppresses reads. Name the parent in every number.
- Sampling: 512 plain tries per DEV question at T 3.0 (gated) and at T 1.4 (reported), through the same sampler C2b uses (legal.raw_samples, level 0). Run the 52 affine questions first (about 3 minutes), then all 256.
- Log per try: the set of read pairs, the first strict reject reason, the strict verdict, the relaxed verdict, and the answer against the key.
- Report per parent, T and kind: relaxed-only accepted count n_rel, key agreement, count of questions with a relaxed-only right fit, strict-right question count on the same samples, and the same figures for the pool affine questions (205) as a second panel, since DEV affine is only 52 questions.
- Also report for the first reject reason: the share rejected only because of a non-query prompt pointer.

STAGE 1 VERDICTS (mutually exclusive, applied in this order, both N_ss parents, T 3.0)
1. PROVED WRONG for the sampling route if any of: n_rel under 10 on either parent; relaxed-only precision under 85% on either parent; zero affine questions with a relaxed-only right fit on both parents.
2. PASS if all of: n_rel at least 30 on each parent; relaxed-only precision at least 95% overall and at least 90% on affine with n of at least 20 affine relaxed-only accepted tries; at least 3 of 52 DEV affine questions with a relaxed-only right fit on both parents, on top of the strict-right count from the same samples; the Stage 0(a) floor rule not tripped.
3. BETWEEN (anything else): rerun once with the two-checked-pairs requirement as the single change. No stage 2 from a between result.
4. The 95% mark amends the spec's 99% mechanism mark. Reason: the strict check on SS at T 3.0 is itself 93.9-95.3% (shown). State the amendment in the readout.

STAGE 2 (only after Ben rules that C2 may read example numbers, and Stage 1 passes)
- Seal C2-R first: a new split with (a,b) pairs disjoint from the pool and warm sets, and with a hash. Never touch the job 9 test. Do not compare against strict-check numbers on the old split.
- Arms: sleep on W-arm tries (checked, at most 2 behaviourally distinct programs per question) under strict versus relaxed check. Identical sampling budget (32 plus 480 where none fits), identical dose, nothing else different. Behaviour-based distinctness (query output plus values on the examples), not canonical expression.
- Parent: warm-only if one can be rebuilt for s100/s101 (the checkpoint was not kept, parents/README.md), else N_ss as a labelled positive control. Never PC.
- Cold-start gate recomputed with the relaxed floor (3x its own floor, 10% reach@32).
- Marks, 2 seeds, paired bootstrap interval: affine greedy first try, relaxed minus strict, at least 5 of 52 (+9.6 points) on both seeds with the pooled interval above 0; skills harm at most 2; add/mult practised check no more than 2 below. Proved wrong: gain of 2 questions or fewer on either seed, or reads in under 1% of greedy affine first tries (the check is not the blocker).
- A claim needs six parents on C2-R. It is a screen with a hand checker until the check is a tool the model calls (D3).
chair.plan_guidance:
Order of work, cheapest first, each gate able to stop the idea.

1. Run Stage 0 and the 52 affine questions of Stage 1 first. Together they take under 10 minutes of CPU and decide whether the rest is worth running.
2. Write the readout to answer one question per number: does B2 write example reads at all (raw B2 versus N_ss, shown only if measured), are relaxed-only fits right, and does the relaxed check keep a random-program wrong-accept floor close to the strict one. Do not cite any strict-check pass mark (the 99% mechanism mark, the 4.8% floor) against relaxed numbers.
3. If Stage 1 returns PROVED WRONG because reads are never sampled, the sampling route is closed but the language question is not. The next single change is a read-form teaching-data control: a copy of the stepping-stone parent trained on hand-written read-form affine programs (hybrid form first, since it keeps two checked pairs), compared with PC and PC' on the same DEV split. Mark fixed in advance: affine first try at least 15% (8 of 52) on both seeds against the 0-4% strict result. Proved wrong: 6% (3 of 52) or less on either seed. This is allowed teaching data (rule 1) but report-only, because it uses pool parameters (roadmap 7c). If it passes, only then open the question of a relaxed check plus read-form stones in sleep. If it stays near 2-4%, the wall is not the check or the language. Mark this as untested.
4. Needs Ben's ruling before Stage 2 or any seal: may C2 accept programs that read example numbers? It changes what C2 measures (rules built from constants, the 3x-floor gate, the cold-start gate) and reverses the PR #44 spec.
5. Note for the lead's ranking: expected chance of a sealed claim is low (about 5%, mechanism critic; suggested). Expected cost is about an hour of CPU. The value is in the information: it separates 'the check forbids the natural program' from 'B2 cannot write long parameter programs', and it answers the open question 3 in gpt-c2-no-climb. Even if it works, the effect on affine is likely small on DEV (about +1 to +3 pooled-5, +2 to +5 on the 154 multi-step questions; suggested) and cannot meet job 9's +15 pooled mark alone.
6. Rule 10 handling: label every result 'about the checker, not the deployed model'. Stuck signal, temperature and 32/480 schedule stay hand code. No deploy claim until the relaxed check is a tool B3 calls by writing text, with its own fidelity mark (D3, 10,000 fuzzed tries at 100%).
7. Do not touch job 9: the Mac is busy (about 10 h) and job 9's strict arms and sealed test must stay on the strict check. Run on Ben's PC.

plan.title: Creative reads: leave-out example check (DEV probe, then screen)
plan.ben_line: Right now the checker that grades the model's guesses throws out any guess that uses an example answer, even when the guess is right. This test asks whether we can let guesses use some example answers and check them only on the examples they did not use, and it counts as progress only if the kept answers are mostly right and not lucky.
plan.question: On the stepping-stone parent (N_ss, seeds s100 and s101), using DEV questions only: does a checker that accepts tries which read example pairs, and checks each try only on the pairs it did not read, keep right affine answers at a high rate (not lucky), while the random-program floor stays low?
plan.one_change: Add one new verdict, the leave-out verdict. A pair is READ if x_i or y_i is a leaf of the answer cone, and UNREAD only if neither is. A try may read pairs, provided every UNREAD pair is reproduced when only the query input slot is rebound to that pair's x (read slots keep their prompt values). With no reads it equals the strict verdict. Nothing else changes: same parents, same DEV questions, same 512 samples per question, same temperature (3.0 gated, 1.4 reported), and the strict verdict is computed on the same samples as the control. The strict verdict and job 9's code are untouched.
arms: Stage 0a, no model: strict and leave-out verdicts on the same 20,000 random programs per DEV question, reported by kind and by number of checked pairs (the random-program floor).

Stage 0b, existence only, not B2: hand-built read programs for sq_plus, double_add and affine (full read form, and a hybrid with A taken from constants and B = y1 - A*x1) through the leave-out verdict on all 256 DEV rows.

Stage 0c, optional, report only: blind search with example-pair operands against constant-only blind at 1k and 6k candidates. Needs a read-aware dedup, because blind_baseline.py dedups by value vector only (shown in its docstring).
Stage 1 control: strict verdict on the same N_ss samples at T 3.0 (gated) and T 1.4 (reported). At T 1.4 strict SS precision is only 63% and 75% (shown: results/c2stones), so T 1.4 is report only.
Stage 1 test: leave-out verdict on the same samples, per parent and temperature.
Stage 1 report only: raw B2 s100 and s101 at T 3.0, 128 tries per DEV question, to see whether training suppresses reads; pool affine (205 questions) as a second panel, not gated.
Replication precheck: 32 plain samples per DEV question from N_ss at T 3.0, strict verdict only, against the c2stones SS arm.
plan.seeds: Two parents, s100 and s101 (N_ss from /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/parents), DEV only: 256 questions, 52 of them affine. This is a 2-seed screen under rule 4 and makes no claim by itself. A six-parent confirm on a sealed C2-R split comes later, only after the Stage 2 screen passes.
plan.machine: Ben's PC: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB for the B2 forward pass. The verdicts are CPU Python plus torch and are the bottleneck. Not the Mac, which job 9 holds for about 10 hours. No rented GPU.
pass_marks: Replication precheck (both parents): strict luck at T 3.0 within +-20% of the c2stones SS arm (about 0.0155 for s100 and 0.0121 for s101, shown in results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json). If not, stop and report: the rebuilt parent or the sampler differs, so Stage 1 is not about the same model.

Stage 0a floor gate (fixed): the one-check leave-out accept rate is at most 0.5% per try on every kind. If tripped, the two-check rule applies to every later stage (the BETWEEN branch, declared now). The census of 2-plus-check rates is reported, not gated.
Stage 1 early stop (52 DEV affine questions, 512 tries each, T 3.0): if fewer than 1% of tries contain an example-slot pointer on both parents, stop and record PROVED WRONG (no reads sampled).

PROVED WRONG (sampling route), per parent at T 3.0: fewer than 10 leave-out accepted tries (n_rel); or leave-out key agreement below 85%; or no affine DEV question with a new leave-out right try on both parents.

PASS, all of, per parent at T 3.0: n_rel at least 30; leave-out key agreement at least 95% overall and at least 90% on affine with at least 20 affine leave-out accepted tries; at least 3 DEV affine questions with a new leave-out right try, meaning some leave-out try is right and no strict-accepted try on the same samples is right; the Stage 0a gate and the replication precheck both passed. Wilson intervals reported; distinct programs reported next to tries.
BETWEEN (any other result): one rerun with two checked pairs required, as the only change, declared now. Both results are reported. No Stage 2 from a BETWEEN.

Stage 2 screen (only after Ben's ruling and a PASS), 2 seeds: affine greedy first try, leave-out minus strict, at least +9.6 points (5 of 52) on each seed, with the paired interval above 0 pooled; skills harm at most 2 points; practised add/mult check at most 2 points below strict; record counts matched across arms.

Confirm (six parents, sealed C2-R, see confirm): pooled affine gain of at least +9.6 points with a paired interval above 0; positive on at least 5 of 6 parents; reads in at least 5% of greedy affine first tries.
plan.proved_wrong: Sampling route (Stage 1, per parent at T 3.0): fewer than 10 leave-out accepted tries; or leave-out key agreement below 85%; or no affine DEV question with a new leave-out right try on both parents; or fewer than 1% of tries with an example-slot pointer on both parents in the 52-question run (no reads sampled, which closes the sampling route at about 5 minutes of CPU). Stage 2 screen: an affine gain of 2 questions or fewer on either seed, or reads in under 1% of greedy affine first tries (then the checker is not the blocker). Confirm: pooled affine gain at most +2 points, reads under 1%, or leave-out key agreement under 95% on C2-R. A PROVED WRONG sampling result does not close the language question (see step 11).
plan.null_risk: Can the marks pass with no real change? Not with an unchanged checker: the strict verdict rejects every example read (fewshot.py:43-44, shown), so n_rel is zero and PASS fails. Remaining risks, in order of weight: (1) The 95% key-agreement bar lowers the spec's 99% mechanism mark (roadmap line 462). It is set where strict SS already sits at T 3.0 (93.9-95.3%, shown), so a PASS is a weaker claim than the spec. The readout must print the 99% figure too. (2) n_rel counts repeats, and 32 or more samples per question can repeat one program, so report distinct programs and questions. (3) A leave-out right try can compute the same function as a strict-right program (a*x+b written with reads or with constants). That is a re-expression, not a new rule. The 'new on this question' test does not catch it, so count distinct behaviour on 8 fixed probe inputs as well. (4) DEV affine has 52 rows but 33 distinct formulas, and 51 of 52 rows use a formula that appears in the pool (shown). This does not affect the probe, which trains nothing, but it inflates any Stage 2 DEV gain. (5) Stage 2: a looser check gives W more records and so more updates. Match record counts, or the gain may just be dose. (6) I changed the Stage 0a comparator. The chair's 3x-strict rule would trip for one-check programs by construction, because they are checked on fewer pairs (suggested, not measured), so I used the absolute 0.5% line. The owning thread must accept this before sealing. Likelihood (suggested, not measured): a PASS is unlikely. The likeliest result is no reads on N_ss, because its C2 training rows come from a search that starts from the query and constants (fewshot.py:235-250, shown). Raw B2 may read more, since 94% of later steps in its skills rows read a fresh prompt number (creative/results/legal-probe/REPORT.md line 30, shown).
plan.autonomy: No. This is a probe of the checker and is not autonomous. Hand code in the probe: the verdict (Python plus torch), the sampler driver, the pair-selection rule, and the T 3.0 setting, which was picked on DEV by example-check reach (c2_dev.py line 48; no answer key), so it is a DEV setting. Parent N_ss has hand-written stepping stones (stones.py lines 9-10 include affine with a=2), which roadmap 7c allows only as a positive control. Deploy path, untested here: the leave-out verdict becomes a tool the model calls by writing text, 'check <program>', and gets one line per checked pair ('pass' or 'fail: got X, want Y') with no key. The model writes its own program, decides whether to read example pairs, reads the reply, and picks its own temperature per question from example-check reach, as roadmap 7c allows. The tool must pass D3's fidelity mark (10,000 fuzzed tries at 100%) before any claim. Until B3's tool loop exists, a PASS says only that the checker can accept read programs, not that the model learns to write them.
steps: Seal before any run (no compute): write this plan's definitions, marks, the Stage 0a comparator change (absolute 0.5% line for one-check programs) and the BETWEEN rerun into the owning thread with a file hash. Ben or the thread must accept the 0.5% change. If they will not, stop here.

Build the leave-out verdict in a new file (read_verdict.py) that reuses fewshot's parser and executors and leaves structure() and verdict() unchanged, since the strict arms and job 9 use them. Rules: the try reads the query input, uses ops 1-8, gives valid outputs on the query and every example row, has at least one UNREAD pair, and reproduces each UNREAD pair with only the query slot rebound. Test (tests/test_read_verdict.py): on 10,000 fuzzed read-free programs, the leave-out and strict verdicts agree 100%. If not, stop and fix.

Stage 0b (minutes): hand-built read programs for sq_plus, double_add and affine (full read form, and the hybrid with A from constants) through the leave-out verdict on all 256 DEV rows. Expect acceptance and the key answer on every row (algebra; label as existence, not B2). A miss is a bug: fix it and do not report it as a result.

Stage 0a (CPU): time 100,000 random programs first. Then run 20,000 per DEV question (5.12 million, both verdicts) if that fits in about 1.5 hours; otherwise use 4,000 per question, the count the existing strict floor used (results/c2dev/dev_floors-s100.json, n=4000, shown). Gate: one-check leave-out accept rate at most 0.5% per try on every kind. If tripped, the two-check rule applies to all later stages. Report the census by checked-pair count and kind.

Replication precheck (about 1 minute per parent): 32 plain samples per DEV question from N_ss at T 3.0, strict verdict only, against the c2stones SS arm (luck about 0.0155 and 0.0121). A mismatch beyond +-20% means stop and report that the parent or sampler differs.

Stage 1, affine first (about 5 minutes): 512 plain tries per DEV affine question per parent at T 3.0, both verdicts on the same samples, using legal.raw_samples at level 0 as C2b does. Log per try: read pairs, first strict reject reason, both verdicts, key agreement. Apply the early stop (under 1% pointer share on both parents means PROVED WRONG, no reads sampled).

Stage 1, full (about 1 to 1.5 hours): 512 plain tries per DEV question per parent at T 3.0 (gated) and T 1.4 (reported); raw B2 at 128 tries per question at T 3.0 (report only); pool affine (205) as a second panel (not gated). Report per parent and kind: n_rel, distinct leave-out programs, key agreement with Wilson intervals, split by checked-pair count (1 versus 2 or more), new-right affine questions, and the strict control on the same samples. Do not open test.jsonl or labelled.jsonl.

Apply the Stage 1 verdicts in this order: PROVED WRONG, then PASS, then BETWEEN. A BETWEEN gets one rerun with two checked pairs required (single change, declared now). Report both runs. Neither the 1-pair nor the 2-pair run alone can PASS if the other is BETWEEN.

Readout, one number per question: raw B2 read share against N_ss; leave-out precision by checked-pair count; the floor census; the replication result. Label every result 'about the checker, not the deployed model'. Print the 99% figure next to the 95% bar and state the amendment.

If PASS and Ben rules that C2 may read example numbers: Stage 2 screen on s100 and s101. Sleep on W-arm tries under the strict and leave-out checks, same budget, same dose, matched record counts, distinctness by behaviour on 8 fixed probe inputs drawn from DOMAIN before any run, parent N_ss (or a warm-only rebuild), never PC. Screen only.

If PROVED WRONG because no reads were sampled: the sampling route is closed, not the language question. The next single change is a hand-written read-form teaching control (report only, rule 1 allows hand teaching data), with its own sealed marks (the chair's step 3). That is a separate test, not part of this plan.
Confirm only after a Stage 2 PASS (see confirm).

idea.title: Stuck-signal features scored within kind on the same log
idea.summary: Three cheap signals could tell the model from its own pass-1 tries which stuck question is worth more tries: how many examples its best near-miss reproduces, whether failures are right-region or wrong-region, and its own confidence from one greedy run. Score each within kind, because kind alone already predicts pass-2 finds with AUC 0.83-0.90.
idea.change: On the stop-rule log: features from pass 1 only, labels from pass 2 only. best_reproduced = max over structure-ok tries of examples reproduced (0-3); region_share = right-region misses (reads x, runs on every example, misses) over right plus wrong-region rejects (no answer cone, reads a prompt number, never reads x), with the reason histogram reported first; greedy_logp = summed log-probability of one greedy program at T 1 plus step-1 entropy (read-only copy of sampler.sample_run returning pick log-probs); also behaviour count and plurality agreement as reported-only. Signs fixed before running: best_reproduced positive, region_share positive, greedy_logp negative. Score within kind on stuck pool questions.
idea.why: Shown: pass-2 find rates differ by kind (night 1 double_add 42/57%, sq_plus 21/13%, affine 5/7%, square and last_digit about 100%), and a kind-only predictor reaches AUC 0.83-0.90 on stuck questions, so a pooled AUC measures kind. Suggested: a wrong constant shifts every example by the same error, so best_reproduced may be flat on affine and sq_plus; the probe is built to show that. Untested: the reason histogram for B2 on these kinds. Positives are scarce: sq_plus 27-42 and affine 10-14 per parent on the pool.

problems: shown (recomputed from per-kind counts in results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json, questions_with_find_by_kind; stuck = pool minus pass-1 finds): the pooled multi-step tercile mark (top minus bottom >= 15 points) is met by kind alone. Ranking stuck multi-step questions by each kind's pass-2 rate gives gaps of 37.0 (s100 night 1), 53.3 (s100 night 2), 48.1 (s101 night 1) and 39.3 (s101 night 2) points, averaged over random tie-breaks. The mark cannot tell a feature from kind, which is the leak the idea itself warns about. Fix: compute terciles within kind, or drop the mark.

shown (recomputed): the kind-only AUCs in the idea reproduce exactly: 0.879 and 0.860 (s100 nights 1-2), 0.897 and 0.832 (s101 nights 1-2). Within-kind AUC is kind-proof because kind is constant inside a kind, so that part of the design is sound and is the only mark that tests a feature.

shown (idea text): the primary score is never named. Three features and three signs are given, but there is no combination rule, and the AUC mark says 'within-kind AUC >= 0.65' for no stated score. Picking the best of three features after seeing results is a forking-path risk under rule 4. Fix: pre-register one score (a fixed rank sum, or a single feature) before any run, and report the others as reported-only.

shown (c2_stuck.py:43-54 gives every stuck question the same 480 tries): the marks test whether a feature predicts a pass-2 find, not whether re-allocating tries changes first try, records or the sleep gain. There is no allocation arm and no budget-matched placebo, and the expected effect on the C2 result is not stated. Fix: add a kind-blind, threshold-free allocation rule and compare it with a random placebo at equal total tries, with first-try and multi-step records as the marks.

The idea's 'no extra sampling beyond one greedy decode' is wrong, because the features need 32 pass-1 tries and the labels need 480 pass-2 tries per stuck question. greedy_logp also needs new code: sampler.sample_run (sampler.py:81-84) returns logits only at stop_at 1 and returns no log-probabilities.

Affine, the kind the features most need to help, is excluded because positives are scarce, and last_digit and square are saturated (pass-2 finds about 97-100%), so they carry no variance. suggested (Hanley-McNeil approximation worked by hand, not run): with 27-42 positives per kind, the standard error of AUC near 0.65 is about 0.05-0.06. A 1,000-resample lower bound above 0.5 therefore needs an observed AUC near 0.60 or more. Achievable but noisy; report it as a screen.

shown (fewshot.py:34-47 structure reasons; fewshot.py:84-103 verdict reasons): the verdict reasons are 'no answer cone', 'op not allowed', 'points at a prompt number that is not the query input', 'never reads the input x', 'does not run on every example', 'does not reproduce every example', and 'executors disagree' or crash (unresolved). The idea's right-region bucket (does not reproduce every example) and wrong-region bucket (the three structural reasons) leave 'does not run on every example', 'op not allowed' and 'unresolved' unassigned. The region_share denominator and the 'reason histogram reported first' need every reason placed, and 'examples reproduced' needs a rule for None outputs (outputs_py, fewshot.py:50-58).

shown (c2_stuck.py:22-35 pyfit and fewshot.verdict): a try that reproduces all three examples and passes structure is a fit, so on a stuck question best_reproduced is 0-2. The value 3 arises only in edge cases (all examples reproduced but the query run fails, or the torch check disagrees). The idea's '0-3' range is misstated.

suggested, untested: best_reproduced is probably flat on sq_plus and affine, because a wrong constant shifts every output alike (the idea concedes this). The idea does not say which feature carries the sq_plus mark. The files do not measure B2's structure-ok rate on C2 tries; if that rate is low, best_reproduced is 0 for most questions and has no ranking power.

shown (roadmap lines 898-900: the checker 'must become a tool when the model settles its own answer by testing tries'): region_share needs the hand checker's reason strings. Under rule 1, that hand code can enter the loop only as a tool the model calls by writing text, and the tool loop (B3) is not built. greedy_logp is the model's own forward pass and is deployable now. The stuck decision stays hand code (c2_stuck.py:38-54), so D6 adds a feature to a hand loop rather than replacing it. The idea's rules_check ('counts come from a checker tool') describes a tool that does not exist.

rule 10 (idea silent): no deployed decision is stated. The idea does not say how a score becomes an action (rank, threshold, share of the 480-try budget) or who gets how many tries. A threshold tuned on DEV fails rule 10. Kind labels in the scoring are allowed as a scoring choice under rule 1, so the fix is a pre-registered, kind-blind, threshold-free rule.

rule 4: the 2-parent run is a screen. A pass licenses a 6-parent run, not a claim, and the pass wording should say so. The features were chosen after reading the same job 8 counts (the kind-only AUC and find-rate evidence), so those counts cannot serve as confirmation. The marks must be written down before the run.

suggested, untested (greedy_logp): the pre-registered negative sign has no stated reason, and a sign chosen without a reason can hide a real effect. The interquartile-range mark (>= 0.5 nats) only checks that the feature varies, not that it predicts, so it can pass on noise. The feature is greedy at T 1 while the search runs at T 3.0, so it measures something different from search success.

shown (overlap): C9 is the planned home of this signal (roadmap line 965: a learned 'I can't do this yet' signal from failed checks; line 1008: C9 later lets the model pick). D6 is a candidate feature set for C9 and should say so. The 7d loop-3 'unsure' measure (roadmap line 998: pass rate on 8 own samples between 1/8 and 7/8) is a different planned signal. The H1 stop uses a fixed 0.5 confidence readout (architecture/redesign-ideas-2026-10-07.md:137), and the no-hardcoding notes record post-hoc confidence readouts matching learned gates (papers/no-hardcoding-papers.md:282-283, abstract note). gpt-creative-sleep-loops-2026-10-07.md:61 asks 'Is there a better measure at this size?', which D6 can answer. A wrong constant shifts every example, so a structure-ok try matches 0 examples. On pooled multi-step stuck questions, the kind-only top third minus bottom third of pass-2 find is 36.9 and 53.2 points (s100 nights 1 and 2) and 48.1 and 39.2 (s101), against a 15-point mark. The within-kind AUC mark is underpowered (computed here with the Hanley-McNeil SE, normal approximation). The label does not match the decision (suggested). 'Any fit in 480 tries' saturates for kinds with a useful per-try rate. From the find rates (shown: double_add 42 to 56 percent, affine 5 to 7 percent) the implied per-try rates are about 0.001 for double_add and about 0.0001 for affine. A stop rule decides whether to spend more tries, so the label should be the find rate in tries 241 to 480 among questions with no find in tries 1 to 240, or a per-try hit curve from logged tries.

greedy_logp has three problems. (a) Its sign is stated as negative with no mechanism; confidence would predict a positive sign, so either the sign is a slip or it is an unstated sameness hypothesis. (b) It is computed at T 1, while every try runs at T 3.0 (c2_stuck.py:16; frozen T 3.0 in the JSON), so it measures a different distribution from the one that makes the tries. (c) It is a sum over steps, so it falls with program length, and length varies within kind (shown: manifest _spec.ref_steps gives sq_plus 3 steps for 121 pool questions and 4 for 84; double_add 3 for 183 and 2 for 21; affine 3, 4 and 5 for 32, 140 and 33). The IQR mark (at least 0.5 nats over sums of up to 7 steps) is nearly certain to pass and says nothing about signal.

sample_run returns step indices and vals, not log-probabilities (sampler.py:35-39, 85, 103), so greedy_logp needs new code. The idea calls it a read-only copy. It must match Ledger.run; sampler.py:4-6 says only the greedy mode is tested against run().

region_share is underspecified. 'op not allowed' cannot fire, because cone() returns None on a NOOP (programs.py:65-82). The idea's numerator and denominator leave out 'does not run' and 'executors disagree', and the value when the denominator is zero is not given. Also, on stuck questions best_reproduced can only be 0 to 2 (a 3 needs an executor disagreement), not 0 to 3.

The marks do not measure the payoff the probe is for. The idea reads a within-kind AUC, not the allocation gain a stop rule would buy. The job-8 multi-step interval half-width is about 5 points (SE about 2.5 to 2.7; results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json). A few-point allocation gain (suggested) would sit below the roughly 7-point limit for 80 percent power on one parent. An offline allocation test on per-try logs is needed.

Autonomy (rule 10). Features 1 and 2 are computed by Python outside the model from 32 tries per question, and the stop decision would be a threshold. The idea's own note concedes that only greedy_logp is the model's own, and it is the weakest of the three. A threshold tuned on DEV breaks rule 10. Within-kind scoring must stay evaluation-only; any per-kind normalisation in deployment would also break rule 10.

Premises that do hold (shown). Night-1 pass-2 find rates by kind (double_add 42.1 and 56.5 percent, sq_plus 21.1 and 13.4, affine 4.9 and 6.9, square and last_digit about 100) match results/c2stuck. critiques.expected_effect: As written, the probe has a low chance of a clean pass on both parents, roughly 10 to 20 percent (suggested). The main reasons are that best_reproduced is flat on double_add and sq_plus, and the AUC marks are underpowered. A pass would be a two-parent screen under rule 4, not a claim. If a within-kind signal does exist (true AUC about 0.7), the best case is a stop rule that reallocates the fixed 480-try budget. The gain on multi-step first try is plausibly a few points (suggested), below what one parent can detect (about 7 points). The value is real but small. A per-try offline allocation test in the same logged run would show it at no extra sampling cost (suggested).

problems: Pass-mark tercile clause is passed by kind alone (shown: my arithmetic on results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json per-kind counts). Ranking the 599 (s100) and 595 (s101) stuck multi-step questions by kind find rate (double_add above sq_plus above affine) gives a top-minus-bottom tercile find gap of 39.7 points (s100 night 1) and 53.5 points (s101), above the 15-point mark, with no feature at all. The clause is also pooled across kinds, which contradicts the idea's own within-kind rule. Drop it or restate it within kind.

The pass mark does not say which feature must pass, or whether the clauses are all required; only the first clause has an AND. The greedy_logp interquartile clause (at least 0.5 nats) is a spread check, not a prediction check (suggested: summed log-probs of 3-7 step programs will almost always spread more than 0.5 nats), so it is nearly guaranteed to pass. The 1,000-resample lower bound above 0.5 is mostly implied by AUC at least 0.65 at these sizes (suggested). The band between 0.55 and 0.65 has no outcome, and the bootstrap percentile is not named.

The within-kind AUC clause is safe against chance but weak on power (suggested; Hanley-McNeil SE from shown counts). The null SE on sq_plus is 0.050 (s100: 42 positives, 157 negatives) and 0.060 (s101: 27, 174), so AUC 0.65 is z = 3.0 and 2.5 under no signal, and the false-pass risk is small. Power is poor: a true AUC of 0.60 clears 0.65 on sq_plus in about 16-21% of parents, and a true AUC of 0.70 in about 80-85%. The probe reliably detects only AUC of about 0.67 or more on sq_plus.

Cost is understated by about 2.5 times. The 0.2-0.3 h figure assumes a stop-rule log with per-try data. No such log exists in the snapshot: 'stop-rule' appears only in the roadmap at lines 356 and 382, where it means C1's G2 stopping mark. c2_stuck.py saves only aggregates (c2_stuck.py:88-90, 150-163) and discards the search tries (lines 43-54). The labels need the pass-2 search. On the Mac, s100 night 1 took 1,889.5 s for 397,568 tries (32,768 pass 1 plus 364,800 pass 2), about 210 tries per second (shown, results/c2stuck/s100.json 'seconds'). A full-pool logged run is therefore about 0.53 h per parent, about 1 h for two. Restricted to double_add and sq_plus (396 stuck questions, about 190k tries) it is about 16 min per parent. Six seeds cost about 1.6 h restricted or 3.2 h full on the Mac.

The test ignores where the tries go. Affine and sq_plus take 53% of pass-2 tries (192,960 of 364,800 on s100 night 1; 193,920 of 367,200 on s101) but produce 17.6% and 13.0% of pass-2 finds (52 of 295; 41 of 316). A stop rule that saves tries would mostly act on these two kinds. The probe drops affine (10 and 14 positives, too few for AUC) and measures sq_plus with only 27-42 positives. The economics a stop rule needs are not measured.

AUC on binary find labels is a ranking proxy, not the allocation test. The labels saturate: square and last_digit stuck questions reach 97-100% pass-2 find (shown, results/c2stuck JSON), so they carry no information there. The decisive test is whether feature-ranked allocation finds more fitting questions than uniform or random allocation at matched total tries. Save all 480 per-try outcomes per stuck question once and simulate budgets by resampling tries, so no new sampling is needed. Use the fit count out of 480 as a continuous label.

No placebo for question difficulty. Parameters sit in the prompt (rules_real.py:31-33, shown: sq_plus and double_add b in 3-9; affine a in 3-6 by b in 3-15). Find rates may depend on these values (whether the target fits in 7 steps), so a within-kind AUC may track b or query size rather than the model's near-miss signal. Add within-kind prompt-only placebos (b, a, query digit count, prompt length) and a random score, and require each feature to beat the best placebo by a fixed margin (suggested: 0.05 AUC).

Region definitions leave gaps. structure() also rejects 'op not allowed' (NOOP in the answer cone; fewshot.py:21 and :41, shown), which the wrong-region list omits. verdict() reasons 'does not run on every example', 'executors disagree' and 'crash' (fewshot.py:84-103) fall in neither region, so the region_share denominator is undefined for them. best_reproduced is stated as 0-3, but on stuck questions a 3 needs a try that reproduces every example yet fails another check, so in practice the range is 0-2 (c2_stuck.py:22-40).

Flat-feature risk (suggested, consistent with fewshot.py:50-58 and the verdict code): with a wrong constant every example is off by the same error, so best_reproduced is probably 0 for most affine and sq_plus tries. The 'at least 90% at 0' kill clause can then fire from flatness alone even when region_share works. Name the kill rule per feature and state how ties are scored in the AUC.

Log-probability definition. 'Greedy program at T 1' is contradictory: greedy is argmax (sampler.py _pick, greedy or temperature at most 0). sample_run returns sampled picks and no log-probs (sampler.py sample_run return dict), so summed log-probs need a new loop, not a read-only copy of existing output. Step-1 entropy is available through the stop_at=1 branch. The sign 'greedy_logp negative' has no stated reason and no AUC direction; write the direction for every feature before running.

Pooled use is untested. The deployed stop rule must be kind-free and pooled across kinds, because the model cannot read a kind label (Ben's rule 10). A within-kind AUC does not show that one cross-kind threshold ranks questions well, since per-kind find rates range from about 2% to 100% (shown). The probe also does not test a brand-new kind, where the stuck signal matters most (roadmap wall: 0-4% on brand-new kinds). Both are untested.

Rules 1 and 4. Passing on 'both parents' is a two-seed screen and must be labelled that way. The six-seed version is possible from project files: N_ss.pt exists for s100 and s101 (fast-sleep/parents) and s200 to s205 (fast-sleep/confirm), shown by ls. Its identity with job 8's Nprime.pt is untested; Nprime.pt sits on the Mac at /Users/ben-hannan/creative/c2keep-s100/Nprime.pt (shown, JSON 'nprime' field). The features come from the checker as hand code, which is fine for a probe, but any deployed use needs the checker as a tool (B3), as the idea says.

Job 9 cannot supply the features. c2b.py:51-61 skips questions with no W record, so the R arm holds no tries for stuck questions. rec_W1.pt (c2b.py:175-177) holds per-question fit counts, which give pass-2 labels for stuck questions once job 9's night 1 finishes on the Mac, but no per-try outcomes. The features therefore need a fresh pass 1. Job 9 status is not in the files (untested).

Hours and hardware. The 1-hour-per-24,000-update figure is for training and does not apply; the probe is inference only. Torch is not installed here (brief), so no run was possible. A 3.3M checkpoint of about 13 MB (brief, shown by ls) fits easily in 16 GB (suggested). The Mac CPU rate is shown at about 210 tries per second. The RTX 5070 Ti rate for this Python-loop sampler is untested; expect a speedup well below 10 times (suggested).

Checked and holds: the pass-2 find rates by kind (double_add 42.1 and 56.5%, sq_plus 21.1 and 13.4%, affine 4.9 and 6.9%, square and last_digit about 100%) and the kind-only AUCs (0.879 and 0.897 night 1; 0.860 and 0.832 night 2) match the JSON per-kind counts (shown, my arithmetic). chair.reasons:
PLAN, but only as a cheap add-on to the one logged stuck-search run, with the marks rewritten. It is not worth its own run and should not rank high by itself.

WHY NOT CUT. (1) Rule 10 names "deciding it is stuck" and "when to stop" as things the model must do itself. Today the stuck signal is has_fit on pass 1 only and the 32/480 schedule is fixed (shown: creative/c2_stuck.py lines 38-54). No file tests any feature of the model's own tries as a stuck or stop signal (shown: the critics found none, and I read c2_stuck.py). (2) If it shares the planned logged run, the extra cost is one greedy decode per stuck question. (3) A clean negative would still help: it would say the C9 signal has to be learned from thinker state, not from summary features.

WHY NOT AS WRITTEN. All four critics agree, and I rechecked the key points.
- The pooled tercile mark is passed by kind alone. Three critics recomputed 37 to 53 points from the saved per-kind counts, against a mark of 15 (shown by them, not re-derived by me). Only the within-kind AUC tests a feature. The kind-only AUCs 0.879, 0.860, 0.897 and 0.832 reproduce exactly (shown by three critics).
- The "stop-rule log" does not exist. results/c2stuck/s100.json and s101.json hold per-kind counts only. A fresh logged run is needed. It costs about 0.5 h per parent, not 0.3 h (shown: JSON "seconds" night1_search 1,889.5 s on s100 and 1,897.7 s on s101, which I read, for 32,768 pass-1 plus 364,800 pass-2 tries, about 210 tries per second). N' is on Ben's Mac only (shown: the JSON nprime path).
- best_reproduced is probably flat on double_add and sq_plus, the two kinds the mark needs (suggested). A wrong constant shifts every example by the same error, and one critic's toy enumeration (not B2 tries) found no candidate matching two examples. On a stuck question its range is 0-2, not 0-3 (shown: a try that matches all three examples is a fit by definition, c2_stuck.py:22-35 and fewshot.py:84-103). The idea's own kill clause (90% or more at 0) will probably fire from flatness alone.
- greedy_logp has no stated reason for its sign. "Greedy at T 1" is a contradiction, since greedy is argmax. The tries run at T 3.0. A summed log-probability scales with program length, which is set by kind (shown: manifest ref_steps, sq_plus 3 or 4 steps, affine 3 to 5). The 0.5-nat spread mark tests spread, not signal. sample_run returns no log-probabilities, so this is new code (shown: sampler.py).
- region_share leaves "does not run on every example" and "executors disagree" unassigned, and has no value when the denominator is 0. "op not allowed" is unreachable because cone() returns None on a NOOP (critic read, suggested).
- No mark names a primary feature. Three features across two kinds, two parents and no multiplicity rule is a forking-path risk under rule 4. The two parents share one pool, so they are not independent replication. Power is low: with 27 to 42 sq_plus positives the AUC standard error is about 0.05 to 0.06, so the probe reliably sees only a true AUC of about 0.67 or more (suggested, Hanley-McNeil by hand).
- Nothing measures the payoff. Affine plus sq_plus take 53% of pass-2 tries and give 13 to 18% of pass-2 finds (shown by the test critic from the JSON counts). The real question is whether a stop or allocation rule saves tries or finds more at equal tries. An AUC does not answer that.

RULE 10 VERDICT. greedy_logp and step-1 entropy are the model's own forward pass and are deployable now. region_share and the near-miss score need the checker's per-example reply, so they are usable only when the checker is a tool the model calls (B3, marks sealed, not built; shown in the roadmap section 7b). Until then, label any result "hand-checker probe, not autonomous". Within-kind scoring is evaluation only. Deployment cannot use a kind label, and the job-8 kind-blindness test must stay passing. Ranking stuck questions across a night's pool is fine, because the pool is the model's own saved questions. An in-the-moment stop rule needs a learned probability with a fixed design constant, never a DEV-tuned threshold.

FIT WITH BEN'S OTHER RULES. Rules 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9 are fine: 0 params, pool only, B2 family only, stuck questions only. Rule 4: two parents is a screen, so a pass licenses a 6-parent run (s200-s205) and not a claim.
chair.revised_idea:
Rename it (roadmap D6 is already the notebook gate), for example "stuck-signal features on the logged run". Make it an add-on to the single fresh logged stuck-search run, not its own job. Run it on the Mac after job 9 finishes, and do not touch job 9's arms or sealed test.

LOG, per stuck pool question (N' from s100 and s101, night 1 only, pass 1 = 32 tries at T 3.0, pass 2 = 480 tries only where no pass-1 try fits):
- per try: structure reason, the outputs_py list, fit flag, and for pass 2 the index of each fitting try;
- one greedy program decoded with per-step log-probabilities, plus step-1 entropy, at T 3.0 (the temperature the tries use). This is a new read-only function, and it must first be shown to reproduce Ledger.run's greedy answer (same check as tests/test_c1.py:215-234).

FEATURES (pass 1 and greedy decode only; labels from pass 2 only):
1. region_share. Every checker reason gets a bucket. Right-region = structure ok, runs on every example, misses. Wrong-region = no cone, reads a prompt number, never reads x. "Does not run" and "executors disagree" are reported but kept out of the ratio. A question with an empty denominator gets the median rank, and the share of such questions is reported. The reason histogram is reported before anything is scored.
2. near-miss shape score, which replaces best_reproduced as the primary checker feature. It is the share of structure-ok runs whose residual (output minus the example y) is the same nonzero constant on every example. A wrong additive constant gives exactly that. Report best_reproduced (range 0-2) and the share of questions where it is 0.
3. greedy_logp, as a per-step mean log-probability at T 3.0, with step count as a covariate. Pre-register the sign positive, with the written reason "a confident greedy program means the model has a candidate near the answer". Record that the opposite sign counts as "reverses: report, do not pass".

Reported only: behaviour count, plurality agreement, step-1 entropy.

SCORE within kind (double_add and sq_plus; affine and the saturated kinds reported only). Add three within-kind placebos: random score, prompt-only (b or a, query digits, prompt length), and a label-shuffle placebo that must give AUC near 0.5.

DECISIVE OFFLINE TEST, no new sampling. From the logged per-try hits, compare at the same total tries: feature-ranked allocation, uniform 480 and a random-rank placebo. Measure (a) stuck multi-step questions that get a fitting try, and (b) tries saved while keeping at least 95% of finds. The rule is kind-blind and threshold-free, a fixed design constant that is the same every night. Within-kind normalising is never used in allocation.

AUTONOMY LABELS: greedy_logp and step-1 entropy are the model's own forward pass. The other two are "hand-checker probe" until the checker is a tool the model calls (B3). The deployed route is a small learned head trained on the model's own pass-1 features and the checker verdicts. That head is the C9 slot, not built.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right.

1. Fresh log, shared. The probe needs per-try rows that no saved file holds (shown: c2_stuck.py saves aggregates only; results/c2stuck JSON has per-kind counts only). Budget about 0.53 h of CPU search per parent on the Mac (shown: 1,889 s and 1,898 s). Restricting to double_add plus sq_plus cuts it to roughly 16 min per parent (suggested), but the allocation test is fairer on the whole stuck pool, so log the whole pool. Start only after job 9 releases the Mac, and do not change job 9. Before running, confirm that the checkpoint used (fast-sleep/parents/s100 and s101 N_ss.pt, plus the setup) is the same N' that job 8 used (untested). The JSON nprime path is /Users/ben-hannan/creative/c2keep-s100/Nprime.pt, on the Mac only.

2. Marks to fix in writing before the run (nothing here is measured yet; the numbers below are proposals for the planner to confirm).
- Primary: for the single pre-registered primary feature, within-kind AUC at least 0.65 on double_add AND sq_plus, on both parents, with a percentile bootstrap lower bound above 0.5. It must also beat the best of the three placebos by at least 0.05 AUC (the margin is a suggestion).
- Decisive: at equal total tries, feature-ranked allocation beats uniform 480 on questions found. A proposed bar is at least 15 more finds per parent out of about 600 stuck multi-step questions (job 8 found 180 and 237, so roughly 8% relative; shown for the counts, suggested for the bar), with a paired-bootstrap lower bound above 0 on both parents. The alternative is at least 30% fewer tries at 95% or more of the finds. The planner fixes one of the two.
- Dead: within-kind AUC at most 0.55 on both kinds on both parents. Also dead is any feature with no variance, meaning 90% or more of questions at the same value, or one reject reason covering over 95%. Flat is reported per feature. A flat best_reproduced kills only that feature.
- Between marks: AUC 0.55 to 0.65 is neither a pass nor a kill; report it and do not extend.
- Drop the pooled tercile mark (kind alone meets it, 37-53 points) and the 0.5-nat spread mark.

3. Label. Primary label is any fit in the 480 pass-2 tries, for power. Report as secondary a marginal label (a fit in pass-2 tries 241 to 480 given none in tries 1 to 240). Use night 1 only, because night 2 starts from a different model and gives only 3 and 6 affine positives. Positives are sq_plus 27 to 42 and affine 10 to 14 per parent (shown). The probe sees only a true AUC of about 0.67 or more (suggested), so call it a screen.

4. Not independent replication. Two parents share one 1,024-question pool. If the primary mark passes, run s200-s205 (rule 4) before any claim. Include a brand-new-kind check, because the stuck signal matters most there (B2 scores 0-4%, shown), and the within-kind design does not cover it.

5. Hand code vs autonomy. Label every result "hand-checker probe" for the checker-derived features. State that the in-the-moment stop rule will need a learned probability with a fixed design constant. Ranking across the night's own stuck pool is fine. Tell Ben this probe feeds the C9 slot and the stop-rule ideas in the same logged run. Merge the confidence-type readouts (C9, the H1 stop, the 7d unsure measure) into one definition.

6. Rank for Opus. The standalone value is low to medium. The value is mainly in being free on the logged run and in telling C9 whether summary features carry any signal. Do not spend Mac time on it alone. Expect a modest chance of a clean pass (critic estimate 10-20% as written, suggested) and a gain of a few points at most, below what one parent can detect (about 7 points on multi-step first try). The use is cost and rule-10 planning, not a capability gain.

plan.title: Stuck-signal features on the logged run
plan.ben_line: When the model is stuck, can it look at its own guesses and tell which hard problems are worth more guesses? We check this on a saved log. The test uses only the example checks, never the answer key, and asks whether using that sense finds more right answers than picking at random.
plan.question: On B2's stuck pool questions for seeds s100 and s101 (night 1, from job 8's N'), does the model's own greedy-program confidence, pre-registered as the mean log-probability at temperature 3.0 with sign positive, rank questions within kind (double_add, sq_plus) by their chance of a fitting try among 480 more tries better than prompt-visible and random-weights placebos? And does ranking by it find more multi-step questions than random ranking at the same number of tries?
plan.one_change: Add per-try logging and one greedy log-probability decode to job 8's night-1 search, using the same seeds and the same search (no training, no weight change, no change to sampling). Then score three pre-registered features within kind and run one matched-tries allocation test offline on the saved pass-2 tries.
arms: A. Logged night-1 search on N' (job 8 seeds: pass 1 seed 10, pass 2 seed 1010; T 3.0; 32 tries per pool question, then 480 more where no pass-1 try fits). Saves every try: structure reason, example outputs (python), fit flag, pass number and index. Job 8 JSON (shown) gives 760 stuck questions for s100 and 765 for s101.

B. PRIMARY, pre-registered, sign positive: greedy_logp = (sum of log p(op), log p(a), log p(b) over the non-NOOP steps of the greedy program, plus log p(answer pointer)) divided by (3k+1), where k is the number of non-NOOP steps. Probabilities use softmax(logits/3.0). The greedy argmax itself does not depend on T (sampler._pick, greedy branch). Step count k is a covariate. Reason written before the run: a confident greedy program means the model has a candidate near the answer. Rival sign (peaked model, less variety at T 3, fewer finds) is recorded: a reversal is reported, not passed.

C. Secondary, hand-checker probes, reported only (cannot pass without the checker as a tool): region_share = right-region misses / (right-region misses + wrong-region rejects), with the full reason histogram printed first; near-miss shape score = share of right-region misses whose three residuals (output minus example y) are one identical nonzero constant; best_reproduced (0 to 2 in practice).
D. Reported only: behaviour count, plurality agreement, step-1 entropy at T 3.0, and sensitivity variants of greedy_logp (sum only; 22-decision mean).

E. Placebos: random score (seeded); prompt-visible features (query digit count, prompt character length, log mean magnitude of example outputs); random-weights B2 (config S, seed 0, same greedy decode); label shuffle (must give AUC 0.45 to 0.55). Oracle placebo from the row's params field (reported only: params is hidden from the prompt).

F. Allocation, offline on the same logged tries, one fixed split (no sweep): F = rank all stuck questions by greedy_logp (kind-blind, pooled); top half gets its 480 pass-2 tries, bottom half its first 96 (288 tries on average, 60% of uniform, 40% saved). R = same split with random ranking, averaged over 1,000 rankings. U = uniform 480. K = kind-oracle ranking using labels (reported only).
plan.seeds: Screen: 2 paired parents, s100 and s101, night 1 only (rule 4: a screen). Confirm: s200 to s205 (6 paired parents) with job 9's Nprime.pt per parent, only after job 9's sealed test is scored (roadmap line 888 confirm rule, adopted here). Both screen parents and all six confirm parents share one 1,024-question pool (shown, data/c2/MANIFEST.json), so the bootstrap resamples questions and the claim covers this pool only. Question-level generalization needs a fresh pool, which is not in the files.
plan.machine: Ben's M1 Pro Mac, CPU, torch, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 with two parents side by side, as in job 8 (MAC-JOB-8.md, shown). It starts only after job 9 releases the Mac. No GPU.
pass_marks: Gate 0 (pipeline; a failure stops the run and is not a result): pass-1 per-kind find counts equal job 8 exactly. s100: affine 2, double_add 7, last_digit 101, sq_plus 6, square 148. s101: 2, 13, 91, 4, 149. Pass-2 totals equal job 8: s100 stuck 760 with pass-2 finds 10/83/104/42/56; s101 stuck 765 with 14/108/111/27/56 (shown, results/c2stuck JSON). Greedy decode equals sampler.sample_run(greedy=True) on every stuck pool row (program, answer pointer, values). Label-shuffle AUC between 0.45 and 0.55 in every cell.

P1 primary: greedy_logp within-kind AUC at least 0.65 on double_add AND on sq_plus, on both parents (four cells). Question-level stratified percentile bootstrap (1,000 resamples): lower bound above 0.5 in every cell.

P2 placebo margin (margin suggested): in each of the four cells, the primary AUC exceeds the best placebo by at least 0.05, where a placebo's strength is |AUC - 0.5| + 0.5, so reverse-direction placebos count. Placebos: random, prompt-visible, random-weights control.

P3 covariate (suggested): AUC stratified by (kind, step count k), using strata with at least 5 positives and 5 negatives; at least 0.60 in each cell. A cell whose usable strata cover under 70% of its positives fails P3.

P4 decisive, offline (bar suggested): F minus R on multi-step stuck questions with a fit in the logged tries is at least +10 finds on each parent, with a paired question-bootstrap lower bound above 0 on both parents. A crude simulation (suggested, in memory, not a measurement) gives a mean F minus R of about +8 to +11 at AUC 0.6, +16 to +22 at AUC 0.7, and +23 to +32 at AUC 0.8, with sd about 4 per replicate.

Reported, not gated: F versus U finds and tries (40% saved by design); the 95%-of-finds ratio (the same simulation keeps only 89 to 92% of uniform finds even at AUC 0.8, so it is not used as a mark); K; the reason histogram; secondary features. Sign is fixed positive; a reversal with AUC at least 0.65 is reported as 'reverses, do not pass'.
Between the marks: AUC 0.55 to 0.65 in any cell is neither pass nor kill. Report it and do not extend the screen.
plan.proved_wrong: Primary AUC at most 0.55 in all four cells on both parents: dead. Or a reversed sign with AUC at least 0.65 in any cell: reported as reversed, not passed. Or the random-weights control within 0.05 of the primary in at least 3 of 4 cells: the feature is a difficulty proxy, dead. Or F minus R at most 0 on either parent: allocation dead for this feature. Or fewer than 20 distinct greedy_logp values in a cell: that cell reports no variance and does not pass. A failed Gate 0 stops the run without judging the idea.
plan.null_risk: Chance alone is negligible. Under no signal (Hanley-McNeil normal approximation, suggested), a cell reaches AUC 0.65 with probability about 0.0002 for double_add and about 0.006 for sq_plus on s101. The real risk is confounding, so the marks could pass with no stuck signal if greedy_logp tracks program length (only partly covered by P3), parameter size (the b in 3 to 9 sits in the hidden params field, so only the oracle report sees it), or kind. The in-sample kind-only AUC on night-1 stuck questions is 0.879 (s100) and 0.897 (s101) (shown from results/c2stuck JSON; recomputed here). The random-weights control and the oracle report are the checks, and the decisive mark must beat R, not K. Power is limited: with four cells, a true AUC of 0.65 passes about 6% of the time, 0.70 about 56%, and 0.75 about 94% (suggested). So 'no pass' at 0.65 does not prove absence. Both screen parents share one question set, so their agreement is not independent replication.
plan.autonomy: greedy_logp is the model's own forward pass, so it is autonomous: no outside step, no weight change. Region_share, the shape score, best_reproduced and the reason histogram use the hand example checker (fewshot.py) and are hand-checker probes until the checker is a tool the model calls (B3). The stuck gate (has_fit, c2_stuck.py:38-40), the 32/480 schedule, the 50/50 split with 96 tries, and T 3.0 are hand code or hand-chosen. T 3.0 was chosen on DEV in job 6 (fast-sleep/parents/s100/setup.json: 3.0 and 4.0 tie at reach@32 0.254), so under rule 10 it counts as a DEV-tuned runtime value unless re-fixed as a design constant. The deployed route would be: rank by greedy_logp, a fixed top-half split (design constant), the checker as a tool (B3) for the stuck gate, and a learned allocation head trained on the model's own pass-1 features and checker verdicts (roadmap C9 slot, not built). The probe changes no weights and is labelled as a probe.
