fixed_plan.title: Within-kind stuck-signal probe, T=1 feature, fixed gates
fixed_plan.ben_line: When the model is stuck, does its own confidence in its best guess tell which hard questions are worth more tries? We test this on saved questions using only the example check, and compare against random and look-alike controls. The answer key is used only to score.
fixed_plan.question: Within each kind (double_add and sq_plus; affine reported), does greedy log-probability at T=1 rank stuck pool questions above chance and above controls for having an example-fitting try among 480 more? Does allocating tries within kind by that rank find more multi-step questions than random allocation at the same budget?
fixed_plan.one_change: Logging plus one greedy log-probability decode added to job 8 night-1 search. Same seeds and sampling; no training, no weight change; features and allocation are offline.
arms: A. Job 8 night-1 search on N' (pass 1 seed 10, 32 tries; pass 2 seed 1010, 480 tries on stuck questions; T 3.0 as job 8). Save every try: structure reason, example outputs, fit flag, pass and index.
B. Primary, sign positive: greedy_logp at T=1 = mean log-probability over the non-NOOP op, a and b decisions plus the answer pointer (3k+1 terms). Covariates k and b-bin.
C. Reported: same at T=3.0; sum-only variant.
D. Placebos: seeded random; prompt-visible (query digit count, prompt length, log mean example-output magnitude); random-weights model with the checkpoint's own config; label shuffle.

E. Allocation within kind: each batch of 32 same-kind stuck questions; top 16 by B get 480 tries, bottom 16 get 96. R = same batches with random order, averaged over 1000 batchings. Report U minus R headroom and q first.
F. Reported only: kind-oracle K, params oracle, key agreement on logged fits, reason histogram.
fixed_plan.seeds: Kill screen: DEV (256 questions), parents s100 and s101, same design. Screen: pool, parents s100 and s101 (one pool). Confirm only if the screen passes: s200 to s205 plus a fresh unsealed question set with its own hash.
fixed_plan.machine: M1 Pro Mac, CPU, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, two parents side by side (needed for exact Gate 0). PC GPU only as a labelled non-exact rerun.
pass_marks: Gate 0 (a stop, not a result): pass-1 finds s100 affine/double_add/last_digit/sq_plus/square 2/7/101/6/148 and s101 2/13/91/4/149; pass-2 stuck 760 and 765, finds 295 and 316 (shown, results/c2stuck). Greedy decode equals sampler.sample_run(greedy=True) on every stuck row. Shuffle AUC within mean plus or minus 1.96 SD in the four primary cells (a miss means check the code, not a stop).
P1: within-kind AUC of B at least 0.65 on double_add and on sq_plus, both parents (four cells); question-bootstrap lower bound above 0.5 in each.
P2: in each cell B beats the best placebo by at least 0.05 in strength terms (|AUC - 0.5| + 0.5).
P3: AUC at least 0.60 within each (kind, k) and (kind, b-bin) stratum, with usable strata covering at least 70 percent of positives.
P4: E minus R on multi-step finds at least +10 on each parent, paired question-bootstrap lower bound above 0; counted only if U minus R is at least 10, else reported uninformative.
P5: key agreement on logged fits at least 0.99 (roadmap line 462); otherwise the claim is about fits only.
Sign fixed positive; AUC 0.65 or more with reversed sign is reported as reversed, not passed. AUC 0.55 to 0.65 is neither pass nor kill.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Primary AUC at most 0.55 in all four cells on both parents; or E minus R at most 0 on either parent with headroom at least 10; or the random-weights control within 0.05 of primary in 3 or more cells; or within-(kind, b-bin) AUC at most 0.55 (the feature tracks the parameter).
fixed_plan.null_risk: Shown: under no signal, AUC 0.65 has p about 0.0002 (double_add s101) and 0.006 (sq_plus s101). Real risks: confounds (length, b; kind is removed from P4 by design) and low power (about 6 percent pass at true 0.65, suggested). A no-signal pass would need the placebo and b checks to fail together.
fixed_plan.autonomy: greedy_logp is the model's own forward pass: no outside step, no weight change. The example check (has_fit), the 32/480 schedule, the batch-32 rule and the 96-try cut are hand code or design constants until the checker is a tool (B3). T=1 avoids a DEV-picked value. The batch size must be fixed before the run.

With 135 and 149 multi-step pass-2 finds, +10 needs q at most about 0.85. Compute q from the log first and mark P4 uninformative if the headroom is under 10. idea.title: Audit how often a fitting try is wrong, then filter
idea.summary: Sleep keeps tries that reproduce all three examples and trains on each try's own output. On a blind search over B2's op set, 70.6% of square fits and 76.3% of last_digit fits give a wrong query answer, and W keeps random fits, not the shortest. Count how often B2's own accepted tries are wrong on stored records, then test two key-free filters: drop questions whose fits disagree, or keep the shortest fit.
idea.change: Step 0 (no training): load setup.pt for s200-s205 (torch needed), replay each W record's program on its query and on 20 fresh x, and count records whose output differs from the true rule (key used for scoring only), per kind; count two-record questions with different answers; then re-sample 32 tries on 64 pool questions per kind (about 1.6 TFLOP each) to count disagreement among ALL fitting tries, not just the 2 kept. Step 1 (only if it passes): in fewshot.build_arms (L186) variant A keeps a question's records only when all its distinct fitting tries agree on the query answer; variant B keeps only the shortest accepted try. Param cost 0.
idea.why: The generator makes the examples pin the answer only over the 103-instance rule table (1,024 of 1,024 pool rows), not over all programs, so a program can fit and still be wrong (MAX(x*x,100) fits '28->784; 11->121; 25->625' and gives 100 at x=3). Leave-one-out gives no extra protection for a fixed program. Wrong W records are one candidate cause of the crowding seen when same-kind records are added (square 84 to 61 in MC), and every fine-tune and notebook arm reads W. The shortest breadth-first fit was wrong on 0 of 231 fit rows, so a shortest-fit tie-break is cheap to try.

evidence.claim: Blind breadth-first fits (ops 1-7, budget 6,000, first 60 pool rows per kind): 144 of 204 square fits (70.6%) and 193 of 253 last_digit fits (76.3%) give a wrong query answer; fits disagree on the query in 53% of square and 93% of last_digit rows; the first (shortest) fit was wrong on 0 of 231 fit rows.
evidence.label: shown
evidence.source: Fact check verify-spurious-fit (own run) on creative/creative/data/c2/pool.jsonl with creative/creative/blind_baseline.py L15-46

evidence.claim: W picks accepted tries by random shuffle (per_cap 2) and each record's answer is the program's own output, so a wrong fit is trained as a wrong answer.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: The examples pin the answer over the 103-instance rule table on all 1,024 pool rows, not over all programs.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: For a fixed program a leave-one-out fold is the same test as the all-example check, so it adds no protection.
evidence.label: suggested

evidence.claim: The blind-BFS proxy is not B2's sampler; B2's own accepted tries may be mostly right (W square is 83-95% right on DEV). The wrong share of B2's accepted tries is unmeasured.
evidence.label: untested

evidence.claim: The w1a-3 numbers (7-template library answers 1,015 of 1,024; 421 leave-one-out accepts) appear in no file and could not be verified; they are not relied on.
evidence.label: shown

test.where: PC (torch) or cloud CPU: setup.pt for s200-s205 plus a 64-question-per-kind resample on N_ss; pool and fresh generated x only; DEV for the screen scoring; test and labelled not opened
test.arms: Probe: counts only (wrong-by-key share, disagreement share, per kind). Screen if the probe passes (s100 and s101): W as built vs W-agree vs W-shortest at equal updates.
test.pass_mark: Probe passes (go to screen) if at least 5% of W records are wrong by key or at least 5% of two-record questions disagree. Screen: held-out pooled first try at least +3 over W as built on both parents, no kind down more than 2, chain-5 harm at most 2.
test.proved_wrong: Under 1% of W records wrong by key and under 2% of questions disagree: B2's accepted tries are reliable, the blind-BFS proxy misled, and the filter is dropped.

idea.rules_check: Rule 5: the key is used only to score the audit; the filters use only the model's own answers. Rule 4: probe, then 2-seed screen with marks fixed; claims need 6 seeds. Rule 6: about 3 TFLOP. Rule 7: nothing truncated, questions are dropped and counted. Rule 9: C2 only. Rule 10: variant A is a count of the model's own answers; variant B needs the model to prefer its own shortest try (a night script until then, flagged).
idea.closest_prior: fast-sleep-papers C1/C4 (verify before trust, test-time) and angle-1 card 4 (distinct-solution cap); RESEARCH section 8 step 2 (top-4 checked at test time). Differs: measured first, and used as a training-record filter at night.
idea.autonomy: The model counts its own fitting tries' answers and step counts using the example-check tool it already calls; no key or developer input at run time.
idea.director_note: Check hardest: (1) setup.pt holds only kept records and a cache, so the per-record replay and the all-fits disagreement count may need the resample; (2) 'wrong by key' must compare the program's own output on the prompt's query, not the stated answer; (3) the BFS proxy may badly overstate B2's problem, so a null is plausible and cheap; (4) variant A drops hard multi-fit questions, so report W counts by kind.

problems: PREMISE ALREADY MEASURED, AND NOT AT 70% (shown). The stepping-stone arm SS in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/creative/creative/results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json gives accepted DEV tries (luck x 8192) and key-correct ones (key_luck x 8192). SS is the job-6 parent N (/mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/parents/README.md; suggested that it is the same recipe). At T=3.0, the night temperature (confirm/s200/setup.json, parents/s100/setup.json), 12 of 226 accepted tries are wrong by key (5.3 percent; my Wilson 95 percent interval about 3-9, understated because tries cluster by question). At T=2.0 it is 28 of 146 (19 percent). Across all six temperatures it is 22-28 percent. The idea labels this 'untested'. Its 70-76 percent figure is for all blind fits, not for B2's sampler.

THE FIRST OR SHORTEST FIT IS ALREADY RIGHT ON DEV (shown). /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md ('What we already know') reports that the shortest chain of stored programs is right on 100 percent of DEV, and blind first-fit is right on 64.5, 77.3 and 94.9 percent at 1k, 6k and 50k guesses (also RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 2). The 0-of-231 shortest-fit result is consistent with this. The 70 percent wrong figure describes all blind fits, so it does not describe what variant B would keep.

THE PROBE'S PASS BAR SITS ON THE MEASURED POINT ESTIMATE (shown numbers, suggested reading). The pass rule is '5 percent of W wrong OR 5 percent of two-record questions disagree'. Night-temperature wrong share is about 5 percent, so the first prong is a coin flip. The second prong is unmeasured: no file counts two-record disagreement. The 1-5 percent gap is left undecided. A decision-relevant bar (for example 10 percent, fixed before the run) is needed.

CEILING ON THE KINDS THE FILTER TOUCHES (shown per-kind numbers, suggested arithmetic). W is almost all square and last_digit (/mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md L28), and each of those kinds has one usable rule (MANIFEST per the brief). In the compliant 71.3 recipe these score x squared 98.7 and x mod 10 93.1 (/mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md L28). A perfect filter on those two kinds adds at most (1.3 + 6.9) / 5 = 1.6 pooled points, below the screen's +3 bar. The idea does not name its recipe. For a W-only fine-tune (job 6, 37.5 DEV) the per-kind numbers are not in the files, so this ceiling holds only for the 71.3 recipe (untested for other recipes).

COST IS LARGER THAN THE GAIN (counts shown, logic suggested). Variant A drops whole questions with disagreeing fits, so it discards the right record along with the wrong one. For a table-pinned answer (creative/creative/rules_real.py L51-62, L144-146), two right fits always agree. Any disagreement therefore implies at least one wrong record. Two-record questions: 97 of 323 on s200 (420 W records, confirm/s200/setup.json) and 98 of 267 on s100 (365 records, parents/s100/setup.json). With per_cap=2 (fewshot.py L186), the worst-case loss is 194 of 420 records (46 percent) on s200 and 196 of 365 (54 percent) on s100. Variant A also drops single-record questions when a non-kept distinct fit disagrees.

DOSE CONFOUND (suggested). The screen compares W-filtered and W as built 'at equal updates'. Fewer records means more visits per record, since updates = visits x |W| / 32 (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6; fastsleep.py L117 per the brief). Match visits per record, or report both.

WRONG RECIPE (shown, /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md L38-46). The 71.3 recipe trains on W plus chain records and replays each record's program on 3 fresh input sets (3 new prompts per record, batch 1024, 80 visits). Replay gave the largest share (-16 without it, L46). Each replayed prompt is 'right by construction' (L41-42). A filter on W alone leaves replayed copies of wrong programs and the chain records untouched. The creative/rl/ code is not in this snapshot (checked), so the replay filter cannot be read here.

OVERLAP WITH PLANNED WORK, AND A NEAR-TEST ALREADY RUN (shown). research report L67 (hypothesis 2: one canonical shortest program per rule); /mnt/project-files/papers/research-loop-c2/angle-1-self-training.md L98 (card 4: at most 4 distinct fits, each the shortest after dead-step removal; untested); angle-2-augmentation-constants.md L102 (step 0: count pool questions each program fits, a key-free spurious check; untested); RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md L139 (top 4, use the first that fits; test-time). NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS: MC minus MB = 0.0 pooled, where MB is blind first-fit and MC is shortest chain (right on 100 percent of DEV). Record counts differ (MB found 409-551, MC 701-843), so this is not a clean correctness test. It still does not show wrong records costing score. The square crowding (84 to 61 in MC) is a notebook effect (retired path, RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md L84), not shown to come from wrong records.

RULE 10 (Ben's 2:45 PM autonomy rule, shown in the brief). Variants A and B are night-time gates coded by hand, and the model does not choose them. Rule 10 lists 'gates' as something the deployed model must do itself. The research report (L57-58) accepts sleep-time filters only as tools the sleep calls. Variant B's own text says 'a night script until then, flagged'. This needs Ben's ruling before any screen.

SCREEN DESIGN (shown numbers). (a) 'Held-out pooled first try' names no split. DEV is the tuning split. The 512-question holdout has a cap of 12 calls (1 used per segment, RESEARCH-LOOP report L60 and L97), so do not spend holdout calls on a screen. (b) +3 on 2 seeds is about 1.5 standard errors (sigma 1.94 on DEV and 1.84 on holdout, report L84), a weak bar, and rule 4 still needs 6 seeds before any claim. (c) build_arms also builds R and H with counts matched to W (fewshot.py L197-212), so changing it changes the placebos. The idea must say whether R and H match filtered or unfiltered W.

COST TEXT IS INCONSISTENT (shown, suggested arithmetic). rules_check says about 3 TFLOP, but step 0 is about 1.6 TF per 64 questions per kind (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6 gives 1.59 TF per 64 mixed questions at 32 tries each). Five kinds is about 8 TF per parent, about 48 TF for six parents. Still cheap, but the number should be fixed. The all-fits disagreement check also needs re-sampling, since setup.pt keeps only kept records (fewshot.py L193-197).

NUMBERS WITHOUT A SOURCE (shown absence). 'W square is 83-95 percent right on DEV' has no file: a grep of /mnt/project-files for '83-95' and '83 to 95' returned nothing. The 70.6, 76.3, 0-of-231 and 1,015/1,024 figures come from a fact-check run that appears in no file. I did not re-run them. Label them as unverified.

NOT ALREADY BUILT (shown code check). c2_stuck.py L22-24 mentions an 'agreement test', but it means torch-vs-python executor agreement, not answer agreement. No answer-agreement or shortest-fit filter exists in the local creative or fastsleep code (grep for agree, shortest, spurious, majority, consensus). So the idea is new as a W filter, but it is not new as a planned card (see the overlap item).
critiques.rescue: Step 0 becomes zero compute and decisive. (1) Replay the stored W records (setup.pt cache, via fewshot._recover) on each record's query for s100, s101 and, if the files allow, s200-s205 at T=3.0. Report wrong-by-key share and two-record disagreement share, with counts and interval. This needs no resample. (2) Fix the decision bar before running: stop if the wrong share is under 10 percent and the two-record disagreement share implies under 10 percent of records lost. The 1.6-point ceiling on the 71.3 per-kind profile already argues against building it. (3) Only if step 1 passes: run the screen on the recipe that matters (W plus chain plus replay, the research loop's compliant sleep), applying the same filter to replayed and chain inputs, with visits per record matched and DEV named as the split. problems: [shown] Misread figure. The idea says 'W square is 83-95% right on DEV'. The 83-95 range is the trained models' DEV square first-try score (M notebook square 83.6 in /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md L78-83; W-ft square 0.90-0.98 in /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm/s20x/confirm.json). No file gives the share of W records that are right. The proxy premise is therefore not contradicted by a measured share, and the 5% probe bar is not calibrated by it.

[shown] The causal claim is contradicted by the file it relies on. The idea says wrong W records may cause the square crowding (84 to 61 in MC). NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md L21-23 reports that the shortest two-note chain's answer is right on 100% of DEV questions for all five kinds and all eight parents. MB (W plus first blind fit, which the idea's own proxy says is 0 of 231 wrong) gives square 73.8. Crowding therefore happens with records the files call correct, so wrong-record crowding does not explain those arms. Caveat: the 100% is on DEV questions, not pool questions. RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md L122 repeats the 'should stop the crowding' claim and needs the same correction.

[shown] The only wrong-record-like gap in the files is last_digit, not square. In confirm.json, the reference-program arm PC (same questions and record counts as W) gets last_digit 1.0 on all six parents. W-ft (the chosen B arm) gets 0.80-0.94 (mean about 0.85). At matched learning rate, the pooled-5 difference PC minus W is 5.1, 3.1, 5.1, 4.3, 2.0, 4.3 (mean 4.0), of which last_digit is about 2.9. Square contributes about 0.5, sq_plus and double_add under 1 each, affine 0. The whole measured headroom is about 4 pooled points, and PC is a different program set (form may matter as well as wrongness), so the gap is not proof of wrong records.

[shown] The +3 screen bar is at or above the measured ceiling. The idea requires +3 pooled over W on both parents. On s204 the PC-minus-W gap is 2.0, so even a perfect conversion of W to reference programs would fail +3 there. Passing on the other parents would need about 75% of the mean gap closed on each parent. Honest estimate: best variant about +0.5 to +1.5 pooled (suggested), with variant A possibly negative.

[suggested] Variant A (keep a question only if all distinct fitting tries agree) is not a neutral filter. The blind proxy says 93% of last_digit questions have disagreeing fits. My own 8-question spot check (first 8 pool rows per kind, budget 6,000, inline run, no files written) found 7 of 8 last_digit questions and 3 of 8 square questions with disagreeing fits, 20 of 28 last_digit fits and 17 of 25 square fits wrong on the query, and 0 of 8 first fits wrong. If B2's tries behave similarly, variant A removes most last_digit records, the kind that carries the only measured gap, and could fail the 'no kind down more than 2' mark. The direction of the proxy reproduces, but the sample is small and the proxy is not B2's sampler.

[shown] Agreement cannot catch systematic wrong fits. The idea's example MAX(x*x,100) fits 28->784, 11->121, 25->625 and gives 100 at x=3 (true 9); I checked that arithmetic. The clip constants only matter for query x in 3-9, so tries sharing the same clip agree and survive variant A. Catching them needs fresh inputs, as in AlphaCode/CodeT-style behaviour clustering (confirmed in secondary summaries of arXiv 2207.10397; CodeT also notes that clusters of trivial wrong programs can grow large). Choosing fresh inputs from the generator's 2-29 domain would be knowledge of the test generator, which rule 10 bars unless the choice is a generic constant that Ben rules on.

[shown] Autonomy claim is false as written. The idea says the model uses 'the example-check tool it already calls'. B2 has no example checker in its forward pass; the only executor is the per-step calculator (ledger.py). The fit check is fewshot.verdict, run by the sleep script inside fastsleep.setup via fewshot.build_arms. Variant A and variant B are therefore hand data-selection steps in the night pipeline, under Ben's 2:45 PM rule 10 (checking tries must be the model's own or a tool it calls). The existing W builder already has this status. The idea should say so and ask for a ruling, not claim a tool the model calls.

[shown] The probe pass mark is too loose to discriminate. 'At least 5% of W records wrong by key' sits far below the shown 15-point last_digit gap, so it will almost surely pass whether or not the filter helps. The proved-wrong line (under 1%) leaves 1-5% undefined. A better first step is an oracle ceiling (diagnostic only, not a method): one fine-tune per parent on W minus records wrong by key, compared with W. Pass: ceiling gain of at least +2 on both parents. If the ceiling fails, any key-free filter is proved wrong. Cost is one fine-tune per parent (about 30-40 TF), far below the night.

[shown] Power is low. DEV has 256 rows, so one run's first-try SE is about 3 points (binomial at p near 0.4). angle-1-self-training.md card 4 uses the same 1 SE of about 3 points. Requiring +3 on both parents gives a pass chance of roughly 10-40% even if the true effect is +2 to +4 (suggested arithmetic). A run that fails the screen will likely be read as 'not shown', not as a clear result.

[shown] Budget line is wrong. 64 questions x 32 tries x 0.78 GFLOP is about 1.6 TF per kind (the idea's own figure). Five kinds is about 8 TF per parent, about 48 TF over six parents, not 'about 3 TFLOP'. The time estimate is still small, but the budget should be corrected before anyone runs it.

[shown] Scope of the proxy. blind_baseline.py searches ops 1-7 (ADD to MAX), not B2's full op set (NOOP and CMP are excluded). The idea's own evidence covers square and last_digit only. affine, sq_plus and double_add, the kinds the fast-sleep work is about, have no proxy evidence. W is almost all square and last_digit (gpt-fast-sleep-two-constant-rules-2026-10-07.md L31), so the filter would touch little of the held-out kinds.

[shown] Counts inside the proposal are not from B2. The idea's own evidence line says 'B2's own accepted tries may be mostly right' and marks the wrong share as untested. A trained W model's DEV square of 90-98% and last_digit of 80-94% make heavy wrongness in W less likely, but this is an inference (suggested), not a measure. The step 0 probe (replay W programs on the query and on fresh x) is feasible: W programs read only x, constants and results (structure() bans example slots), so fresh-x replay is well defined. That is the best part of the idea and should lead.

[shown] The '1,024 of 1,024 pool rows' example guarantee is a generator construction (rules_real.py generation loop rejects rows where the table gives more than one prediction), not a measured result. It means the examples pin the answer over the 103-instance table only, as the idea says. The table is not the set of all programs.

[suggested] Rule 7 is not broken by dropping whole questions, but variant A drops exactly the questions where the model is least sure, which skews the training mix toward easy questions. This should be counted and reported by kind. Rule 5 is fine: the key is used only for scoring and diagnostics. Rule 4 is fine for a screen, with the claim needing 6 seeds.

problems: 1. The proposed test is not the cheapest decisive one. shown: the probe's pass mark (5% of W records wrong by key, or 5% of two-record questions disagreeing) uses only records already stored in setup.pt, so the 32-try resample of 64 questions per kind does not feed the decision. Replaying stored W records needs no model FLOPs. Its cost line is also inconsistent: step 0 says about 1.6 TFLOP each, rules_check says about 3 TFLOP. RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md L112 gives 1.59 TFLOP per 64 questions per parent, so 5 kinds is about 8 TFLOP per parent and about 48 for six parents.

2. The probe pass mark passes with no real effect. shown from setup.json counts (records minus questions = two-record questions): s200 97, s201 62, s202 26, s203 69, s204 32, s205 36. A 5% bar is 5 questions on s200 and 2 on s202, so one or two disagreeing pairs pass it. The 1% to 5% zone has no decision attached.

3. No oracle control, so the screen cannot show the ceiling of any filter. shown: the W-only fine-tune row (gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md section 4: square 100, last_digit 82) and the notebook arm M (NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md L80-83: square 83.6, last_digit 73.0) bound what removing wrong fits could add. If the whole gap were wrong fits: about +3.6 pooled for the fine-tune arm (last_digit only) and about +8.7 for M (square and last_digit), using equal-weight five kinds. The +3 screen bar is about 83% of the fine-tune ceiling. Suggested: add a labelled oracle arm (W minus key-wrong records, diagnostic only, never shipped) and a size-matched random-drop placebo before any variant.

4. Noise. shown: placebo_gain in /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/confirm/REPORT.json runs from -3.13 to +0.78 over six parents (mean -1.04, SD about 1.35, derived). So +3 over W is roughly 1.5 SD of an arm difference, which is not an obvious chance pass on pooled DEV. The per-kind rule 'no kind down more than 2' is loose: one DEV row in a 51-row kind is 1.96 points (dev.jsonl has 256 rows).

5. Confound on updates. shown: fastsleep.py m_ft sets updates u = visits x n_w // per (per = 32 with replay), and mv rises to fit. A smaller W-agree arm gets fewer updates and more visits per record unless n_w is fixed by hand. 'At equal updates' is therefore an unstated design choice. Without a size-matched random-drop placebo, any W-agree gain could come from fewer or easier records rather than cleaner ones.

6. Variant A cannot remove unanimously wrong questions. It acts only where distinct fits disagree (the idea's own blind-search figures: 53% of square and 93% of last_digit rows). Questions where every fit gives the same wrong answer survive, so the probe must split wrong records into disagreeing and unanimous questions or the reachable share is unknown. Variant B is also mis-specified: shown, fewshot.py _distinct (L157-169, called at L193) draws 2 random accepted tries before any choice, so 'shortest of the kept two' is not the shortest fit. Shortest would have to be taken over all 32 tries.

7. The screen needs a resample that is neither costed nor stored. shown: fastsleep.py setup saves only kept records (W, R, H, PC) and their cache, not the 32 tries per question that build_arms needs. Each parent's variant screen therefore needs the whole pool resampled, about 25.5 TFLOP per parent (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md L112, scaled). The sampling temperature T is also DEV-tuned per parent (setup.json: 2.0 to 4.0). Rule 10 does not count a DEV-tuned runtime value, so any wrong share must be reported at that T.

8. The autonomy premise is false. The idea says the model 'already calls' an example-check tool. shown: the fit check is fewshot.py verdict() (L84-103), run by the build script. A grep of ledger.py for example, verdict and fit returned no lines. B2 writes a program and answers; it does not check its tries against examples. So variants A and B are researcher-side hand code inside the night, which fails rule 1 and the 2:45 PM key rule (rule 10). As a diagnostic it is acceptable. As a method it needs a model-written check call or a learned selector, and that has to be settled before the screen, or a pass cannot be deployed.

9. Two supporting numbers are misattributed. 'W square is 83-95% right on DEV' has no source I could find. The nearby figures are DEV scores of trained arms (M square 83.6; W-only fine-tune square 100), and neither measures the share of W records that are right. The W-only fine-tune reaching square 100 is evidence against the square-harm story for that arm.

10. The crowding link is not established. shown: MB (NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md L38-40, first blind breadth-first fit, only for questions with no W record) drops square from 83.6 to 73.8. The idea reads this as wrong records crowding out right ones. But MB covers only questions B2 failed, a different population from the 60-row audit sample, so the drop neither shows nor rules out wrong records. It should not be cited as evidence.

11. Relevance to the goal is small. shown: W is mostly square and last_digit (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md L553-557: 257 and 149 square, 87 and 39 last_digit; gpt-fast-sleep-two-constant-rules-2026-10-07.md L31). A filter over W cannot touch affine, which sits at 0-4% and is the main gap to 70%.

12. Hours and memory. The orchestrator's '1 hour per 24,000 updates' is the 5090 figure (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md, C1 cost bullet about L432: 49 min on a 5090). On BensPC (RTX 5070 Ti), q33's B2 took 3.66 h for 24,000 updates (whole-model-roadmap/8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md L235, shown). Each fine-tune arm here is about 210 updates (16 visits x 420 / 32 at s200), so each sleep should take minutes on the PC (suggested, not timed at batch 64). Estimates (suggested): probe about 0 GPU and minutes of CPU; oracle plus placebo on 2 parents about 0.2 h; screen with the resample about 0.5 h; 6-parent confirm about 1 to 2 h. Memory: B2 checkpoints are 13.2 MB (shown, N_ss.pt 13,235,380 bytes), so 16 GB is ample.

13. The claim split and sleep method are unspecified. shown: C2 work so far is on DEV, the tuning split (RESULTS-2026-10-06.md L5). A 2-parent DEV screen is tuning evidence, not a claim; rule 4 needs 6 paired seeds and an untuned split. The idea also does not say which sleep is used (fine-tune or notebook M), and the ceilings differ (+3.6 vs +8.7).

14. Proved-wrong is set only for the probe, and it is weak: under 2% of questions is 0.5 to 2 questions per parent. The screen has no result that would prove the filter wrong, so a null would be ambiguous.

15. Minor, shown: W records have no kind field (fewshot.py L153 pops it), so join by 'source' to pool.jsonl. Replay needs only the stored prompt and cache, with no model FLOPs. The 20 fresh-x check needs the rule parameters, which records do not store; the query check alone matches the score.
critiques.rescue:
Restructure into three gated steps. Thresholds are suggested and must be fixed by the orchestrator before running. Before any new run, find the raw files behind the 10:01 PM board entry (sleep on own checked finds +35/+27 vs the reference-program ideal +40/+42, equal counts). If they exist, the oracle gap may already be measured, and the W-vs-PC difference (which also includes program form) is the first thing to read.

(A) Zero model FLOPs, on the six existing setup.pt files (torch needed to load). Replay every stored W record on its query, with the answer key used for scoring only. Report wrong share by kind (join via 'source'), and split wrong records into questions whose two records disagree and questions with one record or unanimous fits. Go on only if at least 10% of W square or last_digit records are wrong on at least 4 of 6 parents. Otherwise stop: the filter family's ceiling is then small.

Resample all 32 tries per question (about 25.5 TFLOP per parent) and store them. Compare variants with the oracle at fixed updates on 6 new seeds, with a named claim split that is not DEV. Report wrong records split into disagreeing and unanimous questions. Pass marks fixed before running.

critiques.expected_effect: The idea claims that removing wrong fits from W (variant A: drop questions whose fits disagree; variant B: keep the shortest) gains at least +3 pooled DEV over W on both parents. My estimate, from shown per-kind tables: the ceiling of any perfect filter is about +3.6 pooled for the fine-tune arm (last_digit 82 to 100, nothing else moves) and about +8.7 for the notebook arm M (square 83.6 to 100 and last_digit 73 to 100), and only if the whole gap is wrong fits. Partial filters reach only a subset of the wrong records (the disagreeing ones, or those whose shortest fit is wrong), so a realistic gain is about +0.5 to +2 pooled (suggested, untested), which the +3 bar would usually miss even if the mechanism is real. Affine, the main gap, is unchanged in every case. If the wrong share of W square and last_digit records is under about 3% on most parents (untested; the probe would show it with no GPU), there is nothing to gain and the idea should be dropped.

chair.reasons:
CUT as a method. Keep only a zero-FLOP count, folded into the existing spurious-fit audit, not ranked as its own idea. I re-read the key files myself.

1. The premise is measured and much smaller than the idea says (shown). The 70.6% and 76.3% wrong shares come from blind breadth-first search on pool rows, in a fact-check run that is saved in no file. They are not B2's sampler. B2's own accepted tries are in creative/creative/results/c2stones/s100.json and s101.json (arm SS, 8,192 tries per temperature; luck = fits all examples, key_luck = fits and is right by key). At the night temperature T=3.0, s100 has about 127 accepted and 121 key-right, and s101 has about 99 and 93. That is 12 wrong of 226, or 5.3%. At T=2.0 it is 28 wrong of 146, or 19%. SS is the job-6 parent N (suggested). These are per-try counts on DEV, not per-W-record counts, so the record-level share could differ. There is no per-kind split (untested).

2. The ceiling is tiny on the recipe that now matters (shown). The compliant research loop reaches 71.3 +/- 2.5 on the holdout over 6 parents (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md). Per kind: a*x+b 15.5, x^2 98.7, x^2+k 76.6, x mod 10 93.1, 2(x+k) 72.5. W is almost all x^2 and x mod 10 (gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md). Those two kinds are only 1.3 and 6.9 points below 100. A perfect W filter would add at most about 1.6 pooled points (suggested arithmetic), below the idea's own +3 screen bar. The remaining gaps (affine, x^2+k, 2(x+k)) are filled by chain-search records. Those records were 100% right against the pool key (shown, same file), so a W filter cannot reach them. At the older job-6 budget, training on the answer key's own programs gave 45.7 against 42.3 for W+chain, a small oracle gap on 2 parents, and per kind only last_digit clearly moved.

3. The causal story is unsupported. The square crowding (84 to 61 in MC) is not shown to come from wrong records. MB used the blind first fit, which the idea itself says was wrong on 0 of 231, and MB still dropped square to 73.8, so the crowding appears with records the files call correct. The MC-minus-MB result is 0.0 pooled (NIGHT-CHAIN-MARKS.md). The best that can be said is that wrong records are a candidate cause (untested).

4. Rule 10 is not met (shown). B2 calls no tool. The fit check is fewshot.verdict, run by the sleep script, so the claim that the model counts its tries using a check tool it already calls is false. Variants A and B are fixed night keep-rules, labelled 'own choices: no' in the roadmap 7c table. The research loop report accepts sleep-time checks only as tools the sleep calls, and the parent N_ss is built from hand-written stepping stones. Nothing here lets the deployed model choose the filter.

5. The pass marks are weak. The probe bar (5% of W records wrong, or 5% of two-record questions disagree) sits on the measured 5.3% estimate. The 1% to 5% zone has no decision attached. The screen bar is above the ceiling in point 2. Variant A can also delete correct records, since two right fits always agree on a table-pinned answer. Its worst case is 46% of W on s200 and 54% on s100 (suggested arithmetic from the setup.json counts), and it falls hardest on last_digit, where the blind proxy says 93% of questions have disagreeing fits. Variant B as written is wrong, because _distinct draws 2 random fits before any choice. The cost line is also inconsistent: about 1.6 TF per kind means about 8 TF per parent, not about 3 TF.

6. The idea overlaps work that is already planned: research hypothesis 2 (one canonical shortest program per rule), angle-1 card 4 (distinct-solution cap), the angle-2 step-0 support count, and RESEARCH section 8 step 2. It points at none of the gaps that remain: affine, brand-new rule kinds, the 2,400 TF cost, and held-out rules.

7. What is worth keeping is the zero-FLOP replay of stored records. If the loop's own records are available, it takes minutes on CPU and no GPU. It reports the wrong-by-key share by kind, split into disagreeing and unanimous questions. Because of the 1.6-point bound in point 2, its result should not decide a build. It belongs in the existing spurious-fit audit as a side count.
chair.revised_idea: Do not build the W filter (variants A and B), and do not spend GPU time on a screen or an oracle fine-tune. Salvage: a zero-FLOP side count inside the existing spurious-fit audit. On the records the compliant research loop actually trains on (arms S, C, Y), or setup.pt for s200-s205 if those are the only ones available, replay each W record on its query. Use the answer key for scoring only. Report per kind how many records are wrong by key, split into disagreeing and unanimous questions. Label it 'research diagnostic, not deployable'. Fix the decision bar before running: if under 10% of W records are wrong and the pooled bound stays under about 2 points, drop the filter family for good.
chair.plan_guidance:
Only if the Opus lead overrides the cut. The plan must do the following.
(1) Replace the OR rule with a count-first design. Step 0 is a zero-FLOP replay of the stored records of the compliant recipe, not just job-6 W. It reports the wrong-by-key share by kind and by seed, with counts, and splits wrong records into disagreeing and unanimous questions. Go to step 1 only if at least 10% of x^2 or x mod 10 records are wrong on at least 4 of 6 parents. State the bar in advance.
(2) Run an oracle diagnostic on 2 parents (s200, s201) before any key-free filter: W minus key-wrong records, W as built, and W minus the same number of random questions. Fix updates and visits per record to the W arm. Name the sleep recipe (the 71.3 recipe with replay) and the split (DEV, tuning, 2 seeds is a screen only). Pass only if the oracle beats the random-drop control by at least +2 pooled on both parents; otherwise any key-free filter is proved wrong. Per-kind change is reported with a 1-row noise note (51 rows per kind, one row is about 2 points).
(3) Test variant B (shortest accepted try, taken over all 32 tries, not over the 2 randomly drawn ones) before variant A. B drops no questions. Report the count of W records and questions removed, by kind. Do not run variant A on last_digit unless the dropped share is counted first.
(4) Apply the same filter to replayed and chain inputs, because replay copies of a wrong program would otherwise stay.
(5) Re-sample the 32 tries (about 25.5 TF per parent) only after step 2 passes.
(6) Say whether R and H placebos match filtered or unfiltered W.
(7) State rule 10 honestly: this is a fixed night script, labelled 'own choices: no', until the model calls a checker tool. Do not claim the model already calls one.
(8) Rule 4: the 2-seed screen is not a claim; confirm on 6 seeds. Do not spend the holdout calls (1 of 12 used per segment) on a screen.
(9) Keep the card experiments (B2, C2) separate from the village model.
Plain-language summary for Ben: some of the model's lucky guesses fit the three examples but are the wrong rule. We measured that at about 5% on the temperature the night uses. Cleaning them out can add at most about 1.6 points. The real gap is the a*x+b rules, so this is not worth GPU time.

idea.title: Do B2's own tries ever read the example numbers?
idea.summary: fewshot.structure() throws away every try that points at an example slot, although the sampler is unmasked, so nobody has counted how often B2 writes such programs. Count fitting tries that read example slots on affine, sq_plus and double_add, and read the pointer mass when the 6-step two-point program is forced as gold. A supply makes a rule-10-clean bootstrap possible; no supply means example-reading must be taught by hand (next idea).
idea.change: Probe only, no training, no repo change. (a) Sample 32 tries on 64 pool questions each of affine, sq_plus and double_add from N_ss (s200, s201) at the parent's pool temperature, level 0; score with the structure ban lifted for the probe (the query must still be read); count fitting tries that read at least one example slot (0-5) and their wrong-on-query share (key for scoring only). Also compare pool affine reach@32 with example-slot pointers blocked (new mask level in legal.py) vs unblocked. (b) Force the 6-step two-point program (SUB 3,1; SUB 2,0; DIV; SUB 6,0; MUL; ADD 1,.) as gold via Ledger.run(gold=...) on 256 DEV affine and 256 square rows; read per-step gold-op probability and pointer mass on slots 0-5.
idea.why: The ban is one scorer check (fewshot.py L43-44) feeding verdict, W, R and H; the sampler and model are unmasked, so example-reading tries are sampled and silently discarded. A constant-free 6-step program fits all 257 affine pool and DEV rows inside the 7-step cap and uses the same slot ids on every question, so if B2 already writes it, sleep on its own such tries is the rule-10-clean route to affine, and a stored copy would also transfer. If B2 writes none, the 0-4% affine is not a filter artefact.

problems: Step 1, question source (blocker for any follow-on): the probe samples the generator's pool (fastsleep.py L46 and L68; pool.jsonl holds 205 rows per held-out kind; shown). Rule 10 allows sleep only on the model's own day questions, so a follow-on built on pool questions is generator-supplied practice. The autonomous version is the day's own stuck questions, as in creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md section 7d (about L978; shown). Open point (suggested): RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md L3 says the compliant night still learns from 'the night's practice pool', and only replay is restricted to day questions (L31-35; shown).

Step 2, regime mismatch: the probe makes 32 tries on every question. Section 7d's day is one greedy try, and tries happen only where the example check fails (shown). Supply should be counted on greedy-failing questions, or the number does not describe the deployed night (suggested).

Step 3, temperature (blocker for the follow-on, not the probe): the parent's pool temperature is chosen on DEV (fastsleep.py L61-65 via c2_dev.dev_report; shown). Rule 10 says a DEV-tuned temperature does not count. The compliant precedent is segment 2 of the research loop, which picked T = 3.0 on s200 from the model's own tries on a 256 x 8 probe (report L31-35; shown). The probe should fix T in advance and report a curve without selecting from it.

Step 4, parent contaminates the supply count: N_ss is built by a stepping-stone sleep on hand-written program families for the held-out kinds (fastsleep.py L56-59; stones.py L1-10; shown). The report says warm-up and stepping stones are researcher-designed and not counted (about L60; shown). An example-reading count on N_ss may therefore reflect the stones. Raw B2 is present for the probe: scratchpad/code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 and B2_s201, each with checkpoint.pt and a sha256 file (shown by ls).

Step 5, the keep test is an orchestrator step: fewshot.verdict() (L84-103) checks the structure ban, runs two executors (outputs_py and outputs_torch) and compares with the example outputs. build_arms (L186-193) applies it to every try in the night loop (shown). Under rule 10 the model must do this itself or call a tool it chooses to call. The autonomous version is one text call to an exact example-checker that returns the fit flag and the query answer, which section 7c already lists as a change (table about L960-968; shown).

Step 6, where the executor lives: B2's exact executor runs inside the forward pass (ledger.py L76 defines execute; it is called at L333 inside run, defined at L278; shown). Rule 1 allows hand calculation only inside a tool the model calls by writing text. So the probe's supply is measured under a design the rules do not allow, and it may not carry over to the tool form. The tool form has a known copy failure: operand copy is 14% and answer copy 59% at 4 digits, and about 1% at 5 (T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md, 'Where S3 breaks'; shown). Keeping the whole program in one call limits copies to the answer, which for the affine ranges in the brief is 3 digits or fewer (suggested, from the brief's bounds).

Step 7, the keep rule is seeded and random: build_arms keeps up to two distinct fitting tries per question by rng.shuffle with a seed (fewshot.py L157-169 and L186-193; shown). A seeded choice is not the model's own decision. An autonomous version is a fixed rule the model can compute, such as the shortest fitting program. The area fact check reports 0 of 231 wrong for shortest breadth-first fits, but 70.6% of random accepted square fits and 76.3% of last_digit fits wrong on the query (brief fact check; not re-run here). The tie-break on B2's own sampled tries is untested (suggested).

Step 8, replay is generator data: sleep.py takes half of every batch from the 200k skills TRAIN file (sleep.py L20, L85-86; load_replay at L43-48; fastsleep.py L44; shown). Rule 10 allows only what the model saw in its own day, plus fixed constants. Segment 2 of the research loop replaces this with day-question replay (report L31-35; shown), and the report says dropping replay costs 16 points (L46; shown). A follow-on that reuses sleep.py needs that swap before it can count as rule-10 clean.

Step 9, the forced 6-step program (probe b) is hand-written teaching of the held-out kind's own solution. As a diagnostic of pointer capacity it is fine. As the 'next idea' it would be pre-ship teaching, which rule 10 does not bind, but it removes affine from the held-out set, the same issue the stones already raise (N_ss). Any claim that uses it must say so.

Probe (b) has the wrong sample size: it asks for 256 DEV affine rows and 256 DEV square rows. dev.jsonl holds 52 affine rows and 51 square rows (kind counts from dev.jsonl; shown). The counts need correcting and the rows named.

Deploy-scale supply is unknown. The pass mark of at least 3 of 64 is about 4.7% of questions, roughly one example-reading question per 20 (suggested arithmetic). No file I searched gives how many stuck questions a day holds (fast-sleep, creative-roadmap, progress-board and whole-model-roadmap folders; shown by search). Without that count, the sleep signal per night could be close to zero.

Dependency, not a deploy step: lifting the ban (fewshot.py L43-44, shown) is scorer ruling C2-R, still open. It changes W, R, H and every score, so the probe's supply must be reported under the new rule and compared with blind search at equal guesses (blind_baseline.py reads only x and constants; from the brief).

Rule 4 and rule 5: pool and DEV only is compliant with rule 5, and this check did not open test or labelled (I read only file names and kind counts from those folders). But two seeds (s200 and s201) is a screen. A 'supply exists' claim needs six seeds and marks fixed beforehand.

(5) Report per kind with the marks at six seeds and a rate per 20 stuck questions. (6) Report probe (b) as a capacity diagnostic on the real 52 affine and 51 square DEV rows. Before any run, write the follow-on's rule-10 preconditions: day questions only; the example checker as a tool the model calls with one whole-program text call; a fixed keep rule (shortest fit) with no seeded choice; day-question replay in place of the skills file; no DEV-chosen temperature. problems: [shown] Wrong parent. The probe is specified on N_ss, which is raw B2 warmed on 2,048 add/mult reference programs and then stone-slept on 2,048 more (c2_stones.py docstring L1-6; fastsleep.py L53-59). Reference programs read only the query slot and constants (fewshot.find_reference and blind_baseline use x and constants only), so both sleeps train query-slot pointers. N_ss example-slot pointer mass may differ from B2's, probably lower [suggested, untested]. The premise concerns raw B2; raw B2 s200 and s201 are in scratchpad b2ckpt (sha256 files present) and should be the primary arm.

[shown] The operating point is tuned for fit supply. T=3.0 was chosen as the DEV reach@32 maximiser of N_ss (fastsleep.py L61-66; setup.json pool_temperature: s200 reach@32 0.09 at T=1.0 vs 0.32 at T=3.0; s201 0.12 vs 0.32). A fit count at T=3 mixes the model's prior with a flattened sampler, so it cannot be read as the prior. Needs a T=1.0 arm and a value-blind floor at the same sampler and T; the idea concedes the floor is untested.

[shown] Impossible row counts. The forced-gold arm asks for '256 DEV affine and 256 square rows'. DEV has 52 affine and 51 square rows (MANIFEST.json dev.kinds; dev.jsonl counts re-checked). The arm can use at most 52 and 51.

[shown] Pass mark (b) is ambiguous and partly unsatisfiable. The gold program's step 3 (DIV) reads result slots 20 and 21, so no example-slot argmax can be the gold pointer there. 'Steps 1-3' must be restated per step and per pointer. '70% of the 6 step-rows' is unclear (per step or per row). Mechanics that do work: steps stores raw logits before the gold mask (ledger.py L324), so pointer mass can be read from it; the forced step takes the argmax within the gold mask (L329-330), so each gold mask must be a single slot.

[shown arithmetic] The probe cannot resolve the rates that matter. With 64 questions per kind, a true per-question rate of 4.7% (the 3-of-64 bar) passes 58% of the time per kind, 34% for both kinds, and about 12% if both kinds on both parents must pass. The 'bootstrapping is dead' verdict (0 of 64 on both kinds) fires about 7.5% of the time at a true 2%. Two seeds cannot support 'proved wrong'; rule 4 needs six.

[suggested arithmetic] The bar is not tied to what sleep needs. 3 of 64 per kind over 205 pool affine questions gives about 10-20 affine records per parent (up to two distinct tries per question, fewshot.py L186). The W sets are 420 records for s200 and 344 for s201 (setup.json n_W), mostly square and last_digit. A pass at the bar would barely move affine, so the marks should be set in records.

[shown] The counted score is unchanged by any supply. verdict() rejects structure failures before any fit check (fewshot.py L34-44, L84-100). chair.reasons:
PLAN, with the design rewritten. The probe is cheap and breaks no rule. It has a payoff no other fast-sleep idea has.

WHY IT IS WORTH A SEALED TEST
- It gates the only route that could reach unseen (a,b) pairs (suggested). The compliant loop's 71.3% (affine 15.5) is "same rules, new questions" (shown: fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, caveats). The report lists a held-out-rules split as a next step. Programs that build a and b from the constants 1, 2, 10, 100 are rule-specific (shown: gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md, 48 distinct programs over 202 affine chain records). A program that reads the examples is one program for every affine rule. The two-point reading fits the key on 52 of 52 DEV and 205 of 205 pool affine rows (shown: three critics re-ran it; reading fits do not prove B2 can emit it).
- Cost is tiny (shown basis: about 0.78 GFLOP per try, RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6). A 2-seed, 64-question screen is about 10 TF, minutes on cloud CPU (suggested arithmetic). No training and no repo edit are needed.
- Nothing like it has run. No saved file counts example-slot reads or reject reasons (shown: grep by three critics). I found no "C2-R" ruling anywhere in /mnt/project-files (shown: my grep). The ban sits only in the provisional C2 spec (creative-roadmap section 7, about L455), in fewshot.py L43-44 and in the GPT prompt as a "hard rule". It is a design rule, not one of Ben's ten. The probe is the evidence for Ben's ruling.
- Raw B2 seeds 200-205 are present at the scratchpad code/b2ckpt (shown: ls). Six raw-B2 seeds are possible. The test critic's claim that only s100 and s101 exist is wrong for the scratchpad.
- Rules: 1, 2, 5, 6 and 9 pass (pool and DEV only, no hand code inside the model). Rule 10 is not touched by a measurement. Rule 4 needs the six-seed stage.

WHAT THE CRITICS GOT RIGHT (verified or corroborated by two or more), AND THE FIXES
1. Row counts. DEV has 52 affine and 51 square rows, not 256 each (shown: I counted dev.jsonl; pool is 205/205/205/205/204). Use the real counts.
2. Mark (b) as written is unsound.
   - Step 3 of the gold program reads result slots, so "example-slot argmax at steps 1-3" cannot hold there.
   - With about 11 valid slots at step 1, 6 of them example slots, chance is about 55% (suggested arithmetic), so a 50% bar is at chance.
   - With gold set, Ledger.run returns the argmax inside the gold mask (shown: ledger.py L325-331), so the returned pointer equals the forced slot. Raw logits are stored before the mask in `steps` (shown: ledger.py L324). Read those.
   - The square control has no defined gold for steps 2-6.
3. Parent. N_ss was warmed and stone-slept on programs that read only the query and constants (shown: fastsleep.py L53-59; fewshot.py L244-246; stones.py). Its example-slot pointers may be suppressed (suggested). Raw B2 is the primary arm, N_ss only secondary.
4. Temperature. T=3.0 was picked on DEV answers (shown: setup.json; fastsleep.py L61-66). That is a DEV-tuned value under rule 10 and it distorts the prior. Fix T in advance at 1.0, and report 2.0 and 3.0 as a curve with no selection.
5. Count definition. The ban looks at leaves(t, t.ans), the answer cone only (shown: fewshot.py L39-44). Count reads in the cone, report dead-step reads separately.
6. The idea says "no repo change", but it needs a lifted structure() check and a new mask level. Do both as monkeypatches in a scratch script.
7. The blocked-vs-unblocked arm has no pass mark. Blocking renormalises the sampler, and the affine floor is 0-4%, so it cannot show a drop. Drop it.
8. The pass and kill bands are undefined, and double_add has no mark. Fix below.
9. A 2-seed null cannot support "proved wrong". Rule 4 needs six seeds before any claim. Use a two-stage run.
10. Fits are weaker evidence for reading programs. A two-point program fits two of the three examples by construction (suggested). So wrong-on-query by the key is a required output, and a placebo is needed.
11. The id collides with the roadmap section 7c row "D2" (temperature on a DEV grid; reported by the autonomy critic, not re-checked by me). Rename.

WHAT I DISCOUNT
- The rules critic's "likely positive, so uninformative" is a prediction. Prompt-number reading is 94% of later steps in the skills rows (shown: rules-breaks-diagnosis, via critic). That does not say whether B2 reads example numbers to fit a rule. The placebo and wrong-on-query share answer exactly that.
- The autonomy critic's demand to count only greedy-failing questions is kept as a secondary table, not the mark. The probe measures the prior, not the deployed night.
- Both the "records audit" and the "value-blind floor with example slots" matter little. Random 1-4-step programs fit 0 of about 300k draws on DEV affine (suggested: one critic's inline check, not saved). A shuffled-output placebo on the same tries is cheaper and more relevant.

AUTONOMY (rule 10)
- The probe is a diagnostic. The follow-on's sleep would match the compliant research-loop night (own night, own temperature, fit check as a sleep-side tool, replay on the day's inputs), which that report treats as the allowed tool form (shown: report caveats).
- It is rule-10 clean only if: the pool is replaced by the day's own stuck questions; T is not DEV-tuned; the keep rule is fixed (shortest fit) and not a seeded shuffle; and replay uses the day's own inputs.
- The forced six-step gold is a hand-written trace. It must stay out of any training run on a held-out kind.
chair.revised_idea:
Rename to fastsleep-EX1 ("Does B2 already write programs that read the example numbers?"). Measurement only: no training, no repo edit, no scored claim. Run as a scratch script that monkeypatches fewshot.structure (drop ONLY the "points at a prompt number that is not the query input" check; keep "answer cone exists", "reads x", and the ops filter) and adds a mask level outside the repo. Pool and DEV only. Test, labelled and the C2b sealed test are never opened.

STAGE 0, seconds: step-1 read. Use sampler.sample_run(stop_at=1) (sampler.py L82-83) on raw B2 s200-s205 and 64 affine and 64 square pool questions. Report the softmax mass on example slots 0-5, on the query slot, and on constants, against uniform (about 6/11 on example slots at step 1). Report only; no gate.

STAGE 1, SCREEN (about 10 TF): raw B2 s200 and s201 (primary) and N_ss s200 and s201 (secondary, labelled as confounded by warm-up and stones). Kinds: affine, sq_plus, double_add, plus square as a control. 64 pool questions per kind, 32 tries each, level 0. Temperature fixed in advance: T=1.0 is the primary; T=2.0 and 3.0 are reported as a curve, selecting nothing.
Per kind, per seed, per T report:
 (i) number of questions with at least one try that fits all three examples under the lifted ban AND reads at least one example slot in the answer cone (leaves(t, t.ans) containing a slot 0-5, never the query slot);
 (ii) the share of those fitting tries that are wrong on the query, judged by the key (key used for scoring only);
 (iii) the placebo: the same tries scored against example outputs shuffled across questions of the same kind;
 (iv) distinct example-reading programs (one two-point shape or many);
 (v) dead-step reads (example slot read outside the cone), reported separately;
 (vi) the same counts restricted to questions where the greedy try fails the example check, as a secondary table.
Also report, for context, the existing ban-compliant fitting supply on the same tries (what W sees today).

STAGE 2, CLAIM (only if Stage 1 passes or lands in the middle band): raw B2 s200-s205 (six seeds, rule 4), T=1.0 on all pool questions of affine, sq_plus and double_add (about 92 TF, suggested arithmetic), T=2.0 and 3.0 on 64 each. Optional N_ss arm.

PROBE (b), forced gold, DEV (52 affine rows, 51 sq_plus rows): teacher-force the six-step two-point program (SUB y2 y1; SUB x2 x1; DIV; SUB q x1; MUL; ADD y1 .) on the 52 affine rows. For sq_plus force the analogue (SUB y1 (x1*x1); MUL x x; ADD), which has 3 steps and reads y1 and x1. Read the RAW logits stored in steps (ledger.py L324), never the returned gold-masked argmax. Per step and per operand report: probability of the gold op; probability of the gold slot; rank of the gold slot; and mass on slots 0-5. Also report, per row, the sequence log-likelihood of the reading program against the ban-compliant reference program (rules_real.reference), which says which one the model prefers.

PASS MARKS (suggested values; write them in a dated file and seal BEFORE Stage 1 runs):
 SUPPLY PASS (Stage 2, raw B2, T=1.0): on at least 4 of 6 seeds, at least 5% of pool questions (at least 10 of 205) of affine AND of sq_plus have at least one fitting example-reading try; at most 30% of those fitting tries are wrong on the query (pooled per kind); the shuffled-output placebo gives at most one fifth of the real count.
 FORCED-GOLD PASS: at steps 1, 2 and 4 (the steps whose operands are example or query slots), mean gold-slot probability is at least 3x uniform and the gold op is argmax on at least 70% of affine rows at steps 1 and 2.
 KILL: at most 1 of 64 on both affine and sq_plus on both screen seeds at all three T, on raw B2 and N_ss. This says only "supply is below about 5%", not "zero".
 MIDDLE band (1-2 of 64, one kind passing, or a placebo that does not separate): report, run Stage 2 only on the kind that passed, and draw no follow-on.
 Inconclusive on N_ss alone does not count as a kill of raw B2.

OUTPUT FOR BEN'S RULING: how many affine, sq_plus and double_add W records would exist under the lifted ban. This feeds the C2-R scorer ruling, which does not exist yet; write it before any scored claim.

DO NOT claim a learning gain from this probe. Any later score under a lifted ban must be reported under a new scorer and against an example-aware blind search at equal guesses (blind_baseline.py reads only x and constants, and a search that reads examples solves affine at once). The job-9 sealed test stays under the old rule, so a later claim needs a fresh sealed split.

FOLLOW-ON (separate idea, NOT in this test): sleep on the model's own example-reading fits only if the supply mark passes, one change at a time, with six seeds. Its marks are written before it runs. Its rule-10 preconditions are listed above.
chair.plan_guidance:
A planner turning this into a sealed test must get these right.

1. SEAL BEFORE RUNNING. Write the marks into a dated file under fast-sleep/ (as D6's marks were sealed in the creative-roadmap) before Stage 1. Fix T=1.0 as the primary; no temperature is chosen from results.

2. Parents and seeds. Primary is raw B2 from code/b2ckpt B2_s200..B2_s205 (sha256 files are present). N_ss from confirm/s20x/N_ss.pt is a secondary, labelled confounded arm. Run Stage 1 on s200 and s201 only, then Stage 2 on all six. A 2-seed result is a screen; only the 6-seed stage may be called a result (rule 4).

3. Patch outside the repo. Do not edit fewshot.py or legal.py. In a scratch script, monkeypatch structure() to drop only the example-pointer rejection (L43-44), keeping "cone exists", "reads x" and the op filter. Define "example read" as an example slot (0..q_slot-1) appearing in leaves(t, t.ans). Report dead-step reads separately. Keep level 0, so the sampler matches every C2 call site. No new mask level is needed once the blocked arm is dropped.

4. Placebo and wrong-on-query. Score the same sampled tries against example outputs shuffled within kind, and report the fits. A two-point program fits two of three examples by construction, so "fits all three" is weaker evidence here than for compliant programs (suggested). Report wrong-on-query by the key (scoring only) and the number of distinct programs.

5. Forced gold. Teacher-force and read the raw `steps` logits (ledger.py L324). Do not read the returned prog pointers, which come from the gold mask (L325-331) and are circular. Each gold mask must be a single slot, so the argmax is unambiguous. Slot indices with three examples: x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3 are slots 0-5 and the query is slot 6. The six-step gold is SUB 3,1; SUB 2,0; DIV; SUB 6,0; MUL; ADD 1,<result>. Steps 1, 2 and 4 read example or query slots; steps 3, 5 and 6 read result slots, so steps 3, 5 and 6 are scored on op only. Use the real DEV counts (52 affine, 51 sq_plus). Drop the square control with undefined later steps; if a control is kept, give it its own one-step gold and score only step 1.

6. Chance floors. State them in the sealed file. About 6/11 of the pointer mass is on example slots at step 1 with uniform logits. The gold op is 1/9 uniform. A specific gold slot is about 1/11 at step 1.

7. Stage 0 first. The step-1 read costs seconds. If affine example-slot mass is not above square's, still run Stage 1 (it is cheap) and report both.

8. Venue and cost. The PC is busy until about midnight ET and the Mac until job 9's test is scored, so cloud CPU is fine for Stage 1 (about 10 TF, minutes; shown CPU rate about 0.05 TF/s). Stage 2 on six seeds is about 92 TF plus the curve (suggested arithmetic), so run it on the PC GPU or Mac after job 9. Time one forward before launching.

9. Label every output shown / suggested / untested. Keep the C2 card experiment separate from the village model (rule 9).

10. Ask Ben for the scorer ruling (name it, since "C2-R" appears in no project file) only after Stage 1 or 2 reports. Give Ben the W-record counts under the lifted ban. If the ruling is no, drop the whole route; the probe still stands as a diagnostic.

11. Merge the six or seven other ideas that open with this same count into this one probe, with the hand-taught reading idea as the gated follow-on.

12. Plain-language summary for Ben (high-school senior): "We ask whether B2, on its own, ever writes a program that peeks at the example numbers (like finding the slope from two examples) instead of building the rule out of 1, 2, 10 and 100. If it does, the model can learn one general line-fitting trick instead of 49 separate rules. If it never does, we would have to teach it by hand. This is only a measurement; it changes no scores."

13. Do not use 10,000 TF or "5 hours" as the sizing basis; use the per-try cost above (shown: no file converts the 5-hour goal to TF).

plan.title: EX1: does raw B2 already write programs that read the example numbers?
plan.ben_line: We check whether the model, before any practice, ever writes a small program that uses the example numbers (like finding the slope from two examples) instead of building the rule only from 1, 2, 10 and 100. If it does, a general line-finding trick might be teachable; if it never does, that trick would have to be taught by hand. This is only a measurement, and it changes no scores.
plan.question: On raw B2 with no training, how often does a sampled try read an example number, fit all three examples, and fit them for real (not by chance), on the held-out kinds affine, sq_plus and double_add, with square as a control? (A supply question only. It is not a learning question.)
plan.one_change: One measurement-only change, in a scratch script outside the repo: drop only the 'points at a prompt number that is not the query input' check (creative/creative/fewshot.py L43-44; the same two lines are in fastsleep/creative/fewshot.py, checked) so that tries reading example slots are counted. The cone check, the reads-x check, the op filter, the two executors, the level-0 sampler and T=1.0 all stay as they are. No training, no weights, no repo edit, no scored claim.
arms: Stage 0 (report only, no gate): raw B2 s200-s205; 64 pool questions each of affine, sq_plus and square (seeded draw); one partial forward to step 1 with sampler.sample_run(stop_at=1) (sampler.py L82-84). Report softmax mass on example slots 0-5, the query slot 6 and constants 16-19. Uniform values at step 1 are 6/11, 1/11 and 4/11 (shown from sampler.py L59-60: 7 prompt numbers plus 4 constants are valid), but only for rows with three examples, so check each row's shape first (fewshot.parse). Cost about 0.2 TF (suggested).

Stage 1 (2-seed screen): raw B2 s200 and s201 (primary). Kinds affine, sq_plus, double_add and square (control), 64 pool questions per kind, drawn by a fixed seed before running. Sample with legal.raw_samples(model, rows, vocab, device, n=32, temperature=T, level=0, seed), which is the call fastsleep.py setup() makes for its pool (shown). That gives 32 independent samples with no dedup and no branching. Do not use sampler.sample_tries: its top-8 first-step branching and dedup change the try distribution (shown, sampler.py L137-176). T=1.0 is primary; T=2.0 and T=3.0 are reported as a curve with nothing selected. N_ss s200/s201 is a labelled secondary arm, confounded by warm-up and stepping stones (fastsleep.py setup(), shown).

Stage 2 (six-seed supply claim): raw B2 s200-s205 at T=1.0 on all pool questions of affine (205), sq_plus (205) and double_add (204), 32 tries each. T=2.0 and T=3.0 on 64 per kind. Square is not run here. N_ss is optional and labelled.

Per-try readouts (scoring only, same tries, no extra sampling): (i) questions with at least one fitting try that has an example slot 0-5 in leaves(t, t.ans); (ii) share of those fitting tries that are wrong on the query, judged by the pool 'answer' field (scoring only); (iii) placebo: the same tries re-scored after each example output y_i is replaced by the output of another same-kind question at the same position (seeded), counting fits; (iv) distinct example-reading programs; (v) dead-step example reads (an example slot read outside the answer cone; the original structure() never checks these, so report them separately); (vi) the (i) counts restricted to questions whose greedy try fails the example check (sampler.greedy_tries, level 0). Also report the ban-compliant fit count on the same tries, which is what W sees today. A try whose two executors disagree counts as no hit (fewshot.py L92-94).

Forced-gold probe (DEV, all six seeds, cheap): teacher-force the 6-step affine reading on the 52 DEV affine rows and the 4-step sq_plus reading on the 51 DEV sq_plus rows, plus a one-step square control (MUL 6,6). Read the raw step logits (ledger.py L323-324), not the returned pointers. The returned pointers are argmax over the gold mask, so they are circular (ledger.py L325-331). Decoy control: the same-role other example slot.
plan.seeds: Stage 0: s200-s205 (cheap). Stage 1: s200 and s201 only (a 2-seed screen, rule 4). Stage 2: s200-s205 (six seeds; the only level that may be reported as a result, and only as a supply claim). Pool draws are fixed by seed in the sealed file before any run. Forced gold: s200-s205.
plan.machine: Cloud CPU for all stages. Ben's PC and Mac are busy (chair's note). Stage 0 plus the Stage 1 primary arm is about 13 TF (minutes). The full Stage 1 with the T curve and N_ss is about 51 TF. Stage 2 with the T curve is about 150 TF (91.5 TF at T=1.0 plus 57 TF for the T=2.0/3.0 curve), which is roughly 35-50 min at the CPU rate of 0.05-0.07 TF/s implied by the brief's 9-14 h per 2,400 TF (suggested). A GPU would be faster but is not needed. Time one 32-try batch of 64 rows before launching.
pass_marks: SEAL FIRST: write /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/EX1-MARKS-2026-10-07.md with these marks, T=1.0 as primary, the seeds, the pool draw seeds and the chance floors, before any Stage 1 run (rule 4). D6's marks were sealed the same way (creative-roadmap section 7b).

Chance floors (shown arithmetic): step 1 example-slot mass 6/11 = 54.5%; a specific gold slot at step 1 is 1/11; gold op is 1/9. Uniform for a given-slot operand at step 4 is 1/14 and at step 6 is 1/16 (valid slots = 7 prompt numbers + 4 constants + written results).
Stage 0: report only. No gate.

Stage 1 can only STOP the route, never pass it. Stop if, at T=1.0, T=2.0 and T=3.0, on both seeds, affine AND sq_plus each have at most 1 of 64 real questions. Treating the 12 cells as independent (suggested; they share questions, so this is approximate), this fires mostly when the true supply is about 1% or less (about 18% at 1%, about 60% at 0.5%) and essentially never at 2% or 5%. Otherwise go to Stage 2. The stop is read on raw B2 only; N_ss is reported but cannot stop or pass the route.

Stage 2 SUPPLY PASS (affine AND sq_plus both required; raw B2; T=1.0; six seeds). Per-seed rate r = share of pool questions with at least one fitting example-reading try. Pass for a kind if: the mean of r over six seeds is at least 4%; AND the one-sided 95% lower bound, mean - 2.015 x s/sqrt(6) with s the sample SD over the six seeds, is at least 2%; AND the placebo mean is at most 1/5 of the real mean; AND the wrong-on-query share (pooled per kind, key-scored) is at most 30%. double_add is reported, not gating. This replaces the chair's rule of at least 10 of 205 on at least 4 of 6 seeds, which has only about 12% power at a true 5% supply (suggested binomial arithmetic).

Stage 2 KILL: for affine AND sq_plus, the six-seed mean of r is at most 1% (about 2 of 205 questions) at T=1.0. This says supply is about 1% or less. It does NOT rule out 2-4%, and it does not show zero. Do not describe it as 'below 5%'.
MIDDLE BAND (every other outcome, including a pass on one kind only, or a placebo that does not separate): report all counts; run the T curve only on a kind that passed; draw no follow-on.

FORCED-GOLD PASS (six seeds, DEV, affine). At each given-slot operand of the 6-step reading (7 operands: steps 1 and 2 have two each, step 4 has two, step 6 has one (slot 1); steps 3 and 5 read result slots only, so op only), the mean gold-slot probability is at least 3x the uniform value for that step. The gold op is argmax on at least 70% of rows at steps 1 and 2. The gold slot beats its same-role decoy example slot on at least 70% of rows at step 1. Square control: mean query-slot mass at step 1 is above 1/11, or the readout is broken.

FORCED-GOLD FAIL: mean gold-slot probability below 2x uniform at steps 1 and 2 on six seeds. B2 then cannot point at example slots even when told, so example reading is dead for raw B2 whatever the supply.
A follow-on is planned only if SUPPLY PASS and FORCED-GOLD PASS both hold. Its own marks are written then, not now.

Output for Ben (a table, not a mark): per kind, per parent and per T, the number of pool questions with a ban-compliant fit (today's W) and with an example-reading fit (new under the lifted scorer), plus the union. This is the input to the scorer ruling. Scale check (shown): a 4% pass is about 8 affine questions per 205, against 420 W records for s200 (setup.json n_W, shown).
plan.proved_wrong: Stage 2 KILL (six-seed mean at most 1% on both affine and sq_plus at T=1.0) together with FORCED-GOLD FAIL. Then B2 neither writes nor points at example slots, so example reading would have to be taught by hand and the EX1 route is dead for raw B2. A Stage 1 stop is shown to be wrong if Stage 2 finds a six-seed mean of 2% or more on both kinds, which the screen cannot see.
plan.null_risk: Moderate (suggested). A supply pass could come with no real learning. (a) B2 may read prompt numbers in a simple expression (for example y1 - x1 + q for affine with slope 1) that fits the examples without a learned rule. The placebo removes chance fits but not this. (b) The 30% wrong-on-query bar is loose. (c) Forced gold at 3x uniform can pass on a positional preference for example slots; the same-role decoy is the only guard against that. (d) The held-out kinds may appear in the 200k skills TRAIN rows (the brief says the real C2 rows come from the fewshot_number_rule and rule_apply families). Not checked here, so a supply may reflect training; the precondition check in the steps is required. (e) For a two-point reading, the first two examples fit by algebra (shown: the reading gives y1 at x1 and y2 at x2), so only the third example is a real check. (f) Even a pass at 4% gives about 8 affine records per 205-question pool, too few to move affine alone. A pass proves supply, not learning. Also, the lifted scorer changes W and every score, so no current score is comparable to any new one.
plan.autonomy: Measurement only, so no deployed step is claimed. It is compliant as a diagnostic: T=1.0 is fixed in advance, not the DEV-chosen T=3.0 that fastsleep.py setup() picks by reach@32 on DEV (shown: setup.json T=3.0, pool_temperature curve). The pool is a researcher practice set used only as a stimulus. The scoring, the executors and the placebo are hand-written tests, which rule 1 allows. Nothing here ships. Any follow-on would need, written before it runs: (1) sleep only on the model's own day questions and tries, not the pool; (2) its own sampling at a fixed T; (3) a keep rule the model computes, such as the shortest fit, not the seeded rng.shuffle in fewshot.py _distinct (fastsleep copy L160, shown); (4) the example check run by the model itself, either as a tool it chooses to call by writing text (needs the scorer ruling) or as a fixed sleep rule on examples it saw; (5) day-question replay instead of the 200k skills file (sleep.py load_replay, shown). The forced readings are hand-written solutions. They measure pointer capacity and stay out of all training.

Stage 0: for the 64 affine, sq_plus and square pool rows, run sampler.sample_run(model, make_batch(rows, vocab, device), stop_at=1). Softmax lop, la and lb over the valid mask (sampler.py L59-60). For each try compute: the lifted verdict; the example-read flag over leaves(t, t.ans) intersected with slots 0-5; the dead-step flag; executor agreement; key correctness; the placebo re-score; and the original ban-compliant verdict on the same try (the W baseline). Aggregate readouts (i) to (vi).

Stage 2 on s200-s205 at T=1.0 on all pool rows of affine, sq_plus and double_add (32 tries each), and the T=2.0 and 3.0 curve on 64 per kind. Compute the six per-seed rates, the placebo ratio and the wrong-on-query shares, then apply the SUPPLY PASS, KILL and MIDDLE rules exactly as written.

Forced gold on DEV, all six seeds: build gold tensors in the shape Ledger.gold returns (reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py L433-455): op [B,7] and a, b [B,7,27] booleans with one True per written operand. Affine: (SUB 3,1), (SUB 2,0), (DIV 20,21), (SUB 6,0), (MUL 22,23), (ADD 1,24). Check: slot 20 is step 1's result (R0=20). sq_plus: (MUL 0,0), (SUB 1,20), (MUL 6,6), (ADD 22,21). Square control: (MUL 6,6). Call Ledger.run(batch, gold=g) (ledger.py L278) and read the raw logits in steps[t] (ledger.py L323-324). Softmax over valid slots. Score only the given-slot operands (7 for affine, 5 for sq_plus) and the op at each written step.

Report. Shown items need file citations (counts, rates, placebo, forced-gold numbers). Suggested items are the binomial power notes and time estimates. Untested items are the contamination check and any control not run. Include the W-count table for Ben's ruling and the plain-language line.

Keep this C2 card experiment separate from the village model (rule 9). Ask Ben for the scorer ruling only after this report, under a name he can find (for example 'scorer ruling on example-slot reads'; 'C2-R' appears in no project file). If the ruling is no, drop the route and keep the probe as a diagnostic. Any later score under a lifted scorer must be compared with example-aware blind search at equal guesses, because blind_baseline.py reads only x and constants (brief).
