fixed_plan.ben_line: We first check whether the model can point at the example numbers when we tell it which ones to use. Only if it can, we count how often it writes such a program on its own at the same heat the nightly practice uses. This only measures; nothing is trained or changed.
fixed_plan.question: On raw B2, untrained: can it point at the example numbers when told to, and at T=3.0 how often does a sampled try read an example number, fit all three examples and match the key on held-out affine and sq_plus (square as control)?
fixed_plan.one_change: Measurement only: in a scratch script, lift the one prompt-number check (creative/creative/fewshot.py L43-44) and change nothing else. No weights, no repo edit, no scored claim.
arms: Gate 1 (DEV, six seeds, under 1 TF): teacher-forced 6-step affine and 4-step sq_plus readings plus a 1-step square control through ledger.run(gold=...), read from raw steps logits (ledger.py L324), with a same-role decoy at every given-slot operand.

Main (pool, six seeds, T=3.0 fixed, 32 tries, level 0 via legal.raw_samples with a fixed seed): affine and sq_plus 205 questions each, square 64 as control. Count r_right, fitting-but-wrong, placebo (scrambled y_i), ban-compliant W count on the same tries, dead-step example reads, and the random-program floor.
Reported only, never pass or kill: raw B2 at T=1.0 and N at T=3.0 on s200 and s201, 64 questions per kind.

fixed_plan.machine: Cloud CPU sandbox. About 85 TF: gate under 1; main about 61 (6 seeds x 410 questions x 32 tries x 0.78 GFLOP); square control about 9.5; reported arms about 12.8. About 20-30 min at 0.05-0.07 TF/s (suggested). Time one 32-try batch first.
pass_marks: Seal first: write the marks file (EX1-MARKS-2026-10-07.md, not written by this agent) with seed integers, decoy rule, op-id map, T=3.0 primary and the precondition result, before any run.

Precondition HARD STOP: the skills TRAIN file, found and grepped for affine, square, sq_plus, last_digit and double_add in family or rule fields, shows no held-out kind in training. Any hit stops the probe.

GATE 1 PASS: at every given-slot operand (affine 7, sq_plus 5) mean gold-slot probability is at least 3x its uniform value, the gold slot beats its same-role decoy on at least 70% of rows, and the gold op is argmax on at least 70% of written steps. Any failure: stop and report pointer capacity absent.

SUPPLY PASS (affine AND sq_plus, six seeds, T=3.0): per-seed r_right has mean at least 4%, AND the one-sided 95% lower bound (mean minus 2.015 x SD/sqrt(6)) is at least 2%, AND the placebo mean is at most 1/5 of the real mean, AND the real mean is at least 2x the random-program floor measured under the same lifted verdict on the same questions.
KILL: mean r_right at most 1% on both kinds at T=3.0. MIDDLE: any other outcome; report all counts, no follow-on, no T curve.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Gate 1 failure (pointer capacity absent when told), or KILL at T=3.0 on both kinds: example reading is not a supply for raw B2 at the night's heat. A supply pass that fails the random floor would mean the fits are chance, not learning.
fixed_plan.null_risk: High (suggested, with the shown prior above). A pass at 4% for affine alone would be a large share of all correct tries. Piecewise CMP, MIN or MAX programs can fit examples and miss the query. Positional preference can mimic pointing; the per-operand decoy guards it. Without the floor, a placebo ratio can pass on chance fits.
fixed_plan.autonomy: Measurement only; nothing is shipped. The forced readings are hand-written targets for a diagnostic and stay out of all training (rule 1 allows hand-written tests). The pool is a researcher stimulus, not day questions; any follow-on must use only the model's own questions and tries (rule 10).
steps: Write the marks file before any run.
Find the skills TRAIN file and grep its family and rule fields for the five kind names; stop on any held-out hit.
Build the scratch probe with the one-check lift. Sanity: a planted two-point affine reading passes; never-reads-x and no-answer-cone tries still reject; executors agree.
Time one 32-try batch of 64 rows on cloud CPU and record TF/s.
Run Gate 1 on DEV, six seeds, with per-operand decoys; stop on failure.
Run the main at T=3.0 on six seeds with the counts listed above.
Run the reported arms (raw B2 at T=1.0, N at T=3.0) on s200 and s201.
Apply SUPPLY PASS, KILL and MIDDLE as written. Label each number shown, suggested or untested, and give Ben the W-count table for the scorer ruling.

final.why: It costs minutes of cloud CPU (about 60-85 TF at the shown 0.78 GFLOP per try), trains nothing, edits no repo file and opens no protected panel, so rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 9 hold. It is the only fast-sleep idea aimed at the real gap, because the compliant loop's 71.3% is "same rules, new questions" over 65 rules the night had already seen (shown: fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md caveats). One reading program would cover every affine rule, whereas the constant-building programs do not. The expected result is a null (suggested: B2's pointer prior has not been trained on example reading, and a 6-step exact chain is very unlikely by chance, so I put a pass at about 15%), and a null still leaves the hand-teaching route open, so the information is worth a cheap run but not a high rank. A pass would not raise any score by itself. It still needs Ben's scorer ruling, a fresh sealed split and an example-aware blind baseline.
final.ben_line: We check, at almost no cost, whether the model ever writes a program on its own that peeks at the example numbers (like finding a line from two points); I expect it does not, and if so that trick would have to be taught by hand.
plan_fixes: Gate-1 decoy is wrong for affine. Any two of the three example points give the correct line, so SUB y3 y1 or SUB y3 y2 are equally right alternatives to SUB y2 y1. A 'same-role other example slot' decoy would therefore fail a correct model about half the time. Score mass on the whole set of equivalent correct slots, and use a wrong-role slot as the decoy (an x slot where a y slot is needed, or the query slot). The single-slot gold also understates a model that prefers a different valid pair.

Gate 1 is a 12-way conjunction (7 affine and 5 sq_plus operands, each at least 3x uniform and at least 70% against the decoy, plus op argmax) that stops the whole probe. Its fail message 'pointer capacity absent' over-claims, since a teacher-forced probability shows preference, not capacity. Make it informational. At most gate on steps 1-2 only. It should not block the sampling run, which is only about 20-30 min of CPU.

T=3.0 as the fixed primary for raw B2 is wrong. It was chosen on DEV answers for the stone-slept parent N (setup.json), not for raw B2. At T=3 a weak prior flattens toward uniform, where about 6/11 of step-1 mass sits on example slots, so a 'pass' there can be mostly a random-floor effect. Either use the loop's own rule (pick T from the fraction of day questions with a fitting try on a 256 x 8 probe, no answers) under the lifted verdict, or report T in {1, 2, 3} with no selection. In both cases measure the random-program floor at the same T and require at least 2x that floor.

Make N_ss s200-s205 co-primary. confirm/s20x/N_ss.pt exists for all six seeds, and the sleeping parent in the follow-on and in the compliant loop is N_ss, not raw B2. The plan lets only raw B2 pass or kill. A raw-B2 pass with a null on N_ss would not enable a bootstrap, because N_ss was stone-slept on programs that read only x and constants. Decide on N_ss and use raw B2 to explain the result.

The 4% mean and 2% lower-bound pass marks are not tied to what a follow-on needs. Execution replay re-runs one program on fresh inputs and was shown to give +21.9, so a single correct reading shape (same slot pattern on every affine question) found on a few seeds could be enough to seed a sleep (suggested). Make the primary readout 'distinct correct example-reading shapes, and on how many questions and seeds'. Fix the minimum seed in the follow-on's own sealed marks, not by a rate guess. Keep the rate as a secondary readout.

Add a difficulty ladder as a control. Use the practised kinds add (2-step reading: SUB y1 x1; ADD q .) and mult (DIV y1 x1; MUL q .) on warm rows, then sq_plus (4 steps), then affine (6 steps). Warm rows are not protected. A null on affine alone cannot tell 'B2 never reads examples' from 'a 6-step exact chain is too long to hit by sampling'. The ladder shows where supply drops to zero and whether the 2-step case is ever hit.

The precondition hard stop is unrunnable as written (no skills TRAIN file in any readable folder) and partly answered already. rules_real.py L5-8 shows affine and pair_diff are held out of the skills split by hash and that square, sq_plus, last_digit and double_add are not in the skills generator (shown). Cite that, and grep the skills file only if it turns up. Note that fewshot_number_rule add, mult and pair_sum are in B2's training with answers only (no worked steps, the family where B2 trails by 9 points), so there is probably no trained example-reading program (suggested; confirm in the generator). Include this in the null-risk text.

Fits are weak evidence for reading. A two-point program fits examples 1 and 2 by algebra, so only example 3 is a real check. Piecewise CMP, MIN or MAX lookups can fit three examples and miss the query. Keep the key-scored wrong-on-query share and the shuffled-output placebo. Also report a count of distinct programs, so repeated copies of one fit are not counted as supply.

Seal the missing details before Stage 1: pool-draw seed integers, the corrected decoy and equivalence rule, the op-id map, and the exact patch (lift only fewshot.py L43-44; keep cone, reads-x and op filter). Rename the idea, because 'D2' collides with the roadmap 7c row. Do not call the scorer ruling 'C2-R' (it appears in no project file). Time one 32-try batch on the actual machine first, since this sandbox has no torch.

Do not claim the follow-on on a pass. It needs Ben's ruling, a fresh sealed split (the job-9 sealed test is under the old rule), an example-aware blind baseline at equal guesses, and rule-10 conditions (the day's own questions, a T the model picks itself, a shortest-fit keep rule, replay on the day's inputs). The forced six-step gold stays out of all training on a held-out kind.

chair.revised_idea:
Measure B2's speed and counted FLOPs on the M1 Pro (MPS and CPU) at the shape the 71.3% loop night actually uses. Report seconds first and TF/s second. Drop the PC/CUDA arm.

PRECONDITIONS (ask Ben):
(a) Job 9 is finished or stopped, and the Mac is idle (log a process list at start and end).
(b) Ben allows one MPS probe, overriding MAC-JOB.md L31.
(c) Ben says which reading of "5 hours" binds. Reading 1 is wall-clock for the 2,400 TF night (needs at least 0.133 TF/s). Reading 2 is the 10,000 TF cap in 5 h (needs 0.556 TF/s). The loop only showed the FLOP cap (2,400 TF is under 10,000 TF), not wall-clock on this device.

PROTOCOL (all fixed before running):
- Model: B2 checkpoint (s100 or a q33 B2 seed). Check sha256 as MAC-JOB.md section 1 does.
- Rows: pool.jsonl and skills-TRAIN rows only. Never test.jsonl, labelled, GOLD-PRIVATE or any protected panel.
- Dtype: fp32 on all Mac arms. Write the dtype and device per op into the output JSON. If bf16 is wanted, run it as a separate labelled arm.
- Arms, one process unless stated: (1) CPU, 1 process, all threads. (2) CPU, 2 processes x 4 threads (the job-8 setup, to reproduce 0.16 and label the sharing effect). (3) MPS.
- MPS runs first with PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=0. Any run that needs a CPU fallback is invalid and is reported as "goal device blocked until code changes". Do not size ideas against MPS in that case.
- Numeric gate: on one fixed batch, MPS loss and logits must match the CPU run within a tolerance written down now (for example relative 1e-3 in fp32). No MPS rate counts without it.
- Workloads:
  (i) Fine-tune updates at batch 64 (job-8 shape) and at batch 1,024 (loop-night shape: half W/chain/replay rows, half skills replay). Discard 5 warm-up updates, then time at least 20 updates (about 10 at batch 1,024 if it is too slow). Repeat 3 times. Call the device synchronise before each clock read. Record peak memory. Use gradient accumulation if batch 1,024 does not fit, without changing rows or updates.
  (ii) One sampling pass of at least 256 questions x 32 tries on the same sampler code the Mac job used (host syncs included, so it is overhead-honest). If time allows, 1,024 x 32.
- FLOPs: count once with FlopCounterMode (reuse count_flops, fastsleep.py L103-107) on CPU, around the job's own sleep and sampler functions. Convert every device with those counts. State the 0.78 vs 0.97 GFLOP-per-try basis and the SDPA gap (about 3%).
- Report model-only time and job-level time separately. Output one JSON with device, dtype, threads, processes, batch, warm-up, repeats, seconds, counted TF, TF/s, peak memory, fallback ops.
- No new CUDA run. Convert the existing PC and 5090 rates (and the loop's own 5090 trial logs, if they hold wall-clock plus counted TF; their existence is untested) to TF/s from one FLOP count, for context only.

PASS MARKS (report only; computed at batch 1,024 for the loop-recipe night):
- night_hours = 2,400 TF / (measured TF/s) / 3600, with the sampling-pass time added.
- at most 4 h: fits with margin.
- 4 to 5 h: fits but tight (equivalent to 0.133 to 0.167 TF/s).
- over 5 h: does not fit. Name the needed FLOP cut as night_hours / 5. Below 0.07 TF/s (about 9.5 h) the cut is about 2x or more.
- MPS is adopted for the goal only if it passes the numeric gate with no fallback and is at least 1.5x the CPU single-process rate at batch 1,024. Otherwise plan on CPU or rented GPUs, and Ben chooses under rule 6.
- Under Reading 2, 10,000 TF in 5 h needs 0.556 TF/s. Judge it with the same table.

PROVED WRONG: the job-8 estimate is wrong if the same-harness arm (2) CPU two-process batch-64 rate for search plus sleep differs from 0.163 TF/s by more than 30% (outside 0.114-0.212), or if tries and sleep disagree by more than 25% under one FLOP basis.

NEXT STEP NAMED NOW: if the night does not fit on MPS or CPU, the next one change is the loop's own hypothesis 4 (smallest visits/replay that keeps 70%), tested at 6 paired seeds. It is not a bigger machine.

Claim limit: this measures speed only, not learning. Rule 9: card experiments only.
chair.plan_guidance:

1. Time the shape the 71.3% loop night used: fine-tune at batch 1,024 with 40-80 visits per record, about 700 updates (suggested; about 4,500 records x 80 visits / 512 record rows). Do not time batch 64 only. Add a sampling pass of at least 256 questions x 32 tries on the real sampler code (host-sync bound).
2. Separate the Mac arms: CPU single process, CPU two processes x 4 threads (reproduces the job-8 0.16 TF/s per-process figure), and MPS. Fix dtype (fp32), threads, warm-up discard (5 updates), at least 20 timed updates, 3 repeats, and a device synchronise before each clock read.
3. MPS needs Ben's ruling (MAC-JOB.md L31 says do not use) and a no-CPU-fallback run (PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=0). It also needs a numeric match to CPU within a tolerance fixed in advance. Check the int64 executor (ledger.py L76-86).

5. Fix pass marks for every outcome, with no gap: at most 4 h, 4-5 h, over 5 h (name the required cut), under 0.07 TF/s (about 2x cut or more). Add the MPS adoption bar (at least 1.5x CPU, numerics match, no fallback). Judge Reading 1 (2,400 TF in 5 h, 0.133 TF/s) and Reading 2 (10,000 TF in 5 h, 0.556 TF/s) separately. Ben must say which binds.
6. The Mac must be idle (job 9 is still running or waiting on Ben as of the last board update). Record a process check at start and end. Use pool.jsonl and skills-TRAIN rows only (rule 5).
7. Skip the PC/CUDA run. Convert existing 5090 and PC rates (box.json, FIRST-LOOK, loop trial logs if they exist) with one FLOP count, for context only.
8. Drop the unsourced "55-80 GF/s hand count of job 6" and the 4.5 TF peak (or measure peak with a GEMM benchmark on the same device). State the spread of Mac values honestly: 0.16 measured per process under sharing, 1.5 assumed in the whole-model roadmap, about 0.56 implied by the loop's 1/8 assumption.

plan.title: Mac speed test for the loop-shaped night
plan.ben_line: We time how long one night of the new sleep would take on Ben's Mac, and check whether the Mac's graphics chip runs the model correctly. The model does not change, and this does not show that the model learns anything.
plan.question: On Ben's M1 Pro, how many hours does one night shaped like the 71.3% loop take (about 2,400 counted TF: 32 tries per pool question, then a sleep at batch 1,024 with 80 visits per record, about 700 updates) on CPU and on MPS? Count FLOPs once with FlopCounterMode and convert to night hours, with seconds as the primary metric. No change to the model, data, loss or learning rule.

pass_marks: Fixed now. Night hours H = [sleep counted TF / R_sleep + tries counted TF / R_tries + measured non-FLOP seconds (chain search, replay build)] / 3600, for the whole counted night. The loop reports 2,250-2,450 TF per sleep (centre 2,400; /mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md L13). Known stages are about 2,090 TF of sleep (about 700 updates x 1,024 rows x 2.9 GF = 2.97 TF per update) plus about 25 TF of tries (suggested arithmetic). The one-time warm-up and stepping stones (about 100 TF per parent, uncounted, report L59) sit outside the night and only enter a six-parent total.

Reading 1 (2,400 TF in 5 h, needs R of at least 0.133 TF/s): H <= 4.0 fits with margin. 4.0 < H <= 5.0 fits, tight. 5.0 < H <= 9.5 does not fit; the FLOP cut needed is H/5 (1.0 to 1.9x). H > 9.5 (about R < 0.07 TF/s) needs a cut of 2x or more.

Reading 2 (the 10,000 TF cap in 5 h, needs R of at least 0.556 TF/s): H2 = 10,000 / R_all / 3600. Fits iff H2 <= 5; otherwise the cut needed is H2/5 (about 3.4x at the 0.163 CPU rate, suggested arithmetic).

MPS is adopted for the goal only if all four hold. (i) No fallback error with PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=0. (ii) Numeric gate: logits max relative difference <= 1e-3 on 64 probe rows, executor outputs identical (int64 exact), one-update loss relative difference <= 1e-3 from the same seed. (iii) FlopCounterMode totals on MPS and CPU agree within 10% for one batch-1,024 update. (iv) R_MPS >= 1.5 x R_CPU-1-process at batch 1,024. If (i) or (ii) fails: goal device blocked for B2 until code changes. If (iii) fails: MPS rate reported but not comparable. If (iv) fails: plan on CPU, and Ben chooses under rule 6.
Repeat rule, fixed now: three timed windows per shape; if they differ by more than 10%, add up to two more. Report every window.

plan.null_risk: Partly yes. (1) The bands sit on the estimate: job 8 implies about 4.1 h (stage rate 0.163) to 4.6 h (whole-job rate 0.144) for 2,400 TF, so a 10% timing error can flip "fits, tight" and "fits with margin" (suggested). (3) MPS can look 1.5x faster by doing less arithmetic (a different attention path or skipped ops); count parity (pass mark iii) guards this. idea.title: Hold out constants and pairs to separate memorising from reading
idea.summary: No split holds out constant values, and the loop's 71.3% is 'same rules, new questions', so it cannot tell learning a rule from memorising the 65 usable programs. Sleep with some sq_plus and double_add constants (and later some affine pairs) removed, then score the removed ones. Run on PC' first, which is cheap and has signal.
idea.change: Fix before running: hold out b in {8,9} for sq_plus and double_add, with a second interior arm b in {5,6} to separate interpolation from extrapolation. Sleep on PC' reference records with the other b values (about 57 TFLOP per arm per seed), updates fixed at the full count. Score seen b (DEV 33 rows per kind) and unseen b (DEV 18 per kind plus the 115 pool rows with those b, never trained). Stage 2, only if affine seen-pair first try is at least 8%: hold out 12 of 48 pool affine pairs under a rule that keeps every a and every b present in the other pairs, and score fresh questions on them. Param cost 0.
idea.why: Splits are keyed by (kind, params, examples, query), so every DEV constant is in the pool; a model with 7 per-constant programs would score the same as one that reads b. If the sq_plus 53-61% of PC' comes from reading b, unseen b should score near seen b; if from per-constant memory it should fall toward zero. The same logic applies to the 48 affine pairs, 32 of the 33 DEV pairs being in the pool.

problems: CONFOUND (shown from code and counts, arithmetic suggested): the 'unseen' constants are already practised as parts. The warm-up has add rows for every B in 3..30 (rules_real.py L31; warm.jsonl: add B=8 has 37 rows, B=9 has 33) and mult rows for A in 3..9. Job 7 replays all 2,048 warm rows in every sleep, PC' included (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md L570-571; creative-pilot/MAC-JOB-7.md L5). sleep.py L75-110 draws 16 warm rows per update; over about 614 updates each warm row gets about 4.8 visits, so the add-8 and add-9 rows are replayed about 5 times each per sleep. The 'b in {8,9} held out' arms still train the add parts that sq_plus and double_add are built from. A pass can therefore come from composing practised parts, not from reading b. The affine stage 2 has the same problem, since every a and b part is practised.

THE 7/5 ARITHMETIC IS WRONG (shown from code and counts). With updates fixed at the full count (about 614), the sampler is balanced over records (sleep.py L51-63), so every record in the edge arm gets 614/499 = 1.23 times the visits, affine included. Removing b 8 and 9 removes 115 records (sq_plus 55, double_add 60), not 2/7 of those kinds. The affine share of each batch also rises from 33% to 41%, so the arm changes the kind mix too. The job-7 rule sets updates = visits x records / 32 (creative/creative/c2b.py L187 and L231), so fixing updates is a second change in dose (rule 4). The dose does not bias the within-arm seen-vs-unseen contrast, because unseen rows are never trained, so the stated confound is misdescribed.

INTERIOR ARM CONFOUNDED BY PROGRAM LENGTH (shown: data/c2/MANIFEST.json _spec.ref_steps). sq_plus b=3,4,8,9 need 3 reference steps and b=5,6,7 need 4. double_add b=5 needs 2 and b=3,4,6,7,8,9 need 3. The interior held-out {5,6} therefore differ in length from the seen values. The edge holdout {8,9} is length-matched for sq_plus and double_add, so it is the cleaner arm. The idea does not say this.

COMPARATOR AMBIGUOUS AND PARTLY TRAINED. The pass mark says 'on the pool holdout rows', but pool rows with seen b are in the training set of the edge arm (it trains b 3..7). Only DEV seen-b rows (33 per kind, never trained) are a valid seen comparator. 'Agreeing in direction on the DEV unseen rows' has no measure. The band between 0.3x and 0.6x has no verdict, because the idea gives only a pass at 0.6x and a proved-wrong at 0.3x. chair.reasons: Worth a sealed test, but only after a rewrite. Why: (1) The question matters. The loop's 71.3% is "same rules, new questions" (shown: fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, Caveats: "the 65 rules ... are all seen in practice"). So it cannot tell reading a rule from picking one of about 65 memorised programs, and Ben's north star is learning new rules from few examples. (2) It is cheap. A PC' sleep is a 3.3M-param fine-tune of about 500-600 updates. The proposal's 57 TF per arm is unsourced; a rough 0.19 TF per update (from the 19-39 TF / 103-210 update fine-tune costs, suggested) gives about 95-115 TF. Two seeds is about 200 TF, so six seeds is also affordable (untested on the PC; time one sleep first). (3) No rule is broken. It is a measurement: rule 5 holds if only DEV and pool rows are used, rule 9 holds, rule 1 holds. Not cut because every critic problem has a fix. But as written the test cannot be read, and I verified the key counts myself. (a) Shown (my count from data/c2 dev.jsonl and pool.jsonl): DEV sq_plus b=8 is 5 rows and b=9 is 13, so 18 unseen; double_add b=8 is 8 and b=9 is 10, so 18. Pool holds 55 sq_plus and 60 double_add rows with b in {8,9}. b=9 alone is 13 of 18 DEV rows per kind and 31 of 55 and 33 of 60 pool rows. So an edge holdout is dominated by one constant and the "always write the b=9 program" floor is 56-64% on unseen rows against 0% on seen rows, which passes the stated ratio mark with no reading. (b) The pass mark also passes a model that learned nothing (0 >= 0.6 x 0). (c) The unseen constants are not unseen as parts: warm add rows cover B=3..30, including 8 and 9 (about 37 and 33 rows; critics counted warm.jsonl), and all 2,048 warm rows are replayed in every PC' sleep. So a pass would show composition of practised parts into a new kind-constant pair, not reading an unseen value. (d) The scorer bans programs that point at example slots (fewshot.py L43-44), so "reading b" really means decoding b into a constant-building program with no example-slot read. (e) The seen comparator is undefined on the pool, because pool rows with trained b are in the sleep set. (f) Program lengths differ between held-out and trained sets (MANIFEST ref_steps: sq_plus b=3,4,8,9 take 3 steps and b=5,6,7 take 4; double_add b=5 takes 2 and the rest 3). The edge arm is easier and the interior {5,6} arm is harder, so the sign of the gap flips by arm. (g) The 7/5 dose arithmetic is wrong. Holding updates at about 614 with 499 records left gives every record about 1.23x the visits, affine included, and the c2b rule is updates = visits x records / 32. (h) PC' trains on reference programs from the rule function, so it is a positive control (roadmap 7c: outside help yes, own choices no). It says nothing about the loop's own tries, chain records and replay, which is the 71.3% claim. The autonomy field in the idea is wrong on this. (i) The research loop already lists this as its next hypothesis 3 (report L68) and the GPT prompt asks it (gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md Q3). (j) Stage 2 (affine) cannot run: its gate is seen >= 8% and PC' affine is 2% and 4%. The loop's affine is 15.5%, so stage 2 only makes sense inside the loop arm. Expected value: a screen, not a verdict. Do not stack a rule-4 claim on two seeds.
chair.revised_idea:
Constant-holdout split (rename from "D5": D5 is already "Climb a ladder of checkers" and a C2b try-budget label). A measurement of whether sleep on programs for sq_plus and double_add produces a controller that handles a constant value it was never slept on, separating (i) picking one of the per-constant programs it was trained on from (ii) composing a practised constant-builder into a new kind-constant pair. Claim wording after the fix: "generalises across held-out constant values for sq_plus and double_add, with the constant's parts practised in warm-up". It does not claim "reads b" and does not claim unseen-piece generalisation.

STAGE 1 (positive control, cheap, run first). Parent: N' built as in creative/creative/c2b.py L118-131 (warm-up, hand-made stones, 2,048 warm add/mult rows replayed), labelled "outside help: yes (our stones and reference programs), own choices: no" per roadmap 7c. Change: PC' sleep records (reference programs, c2_keep.py) for sq_plus and double_add with b in {4,7} removed from the sleep set. Warm-up, stones and replay stay untouched (tier A, composition holdout). Reason for {4,7}: interior (no extrapolation confound), and step-matched on the manifest ref_steps (sq_plus unseen mean 3.5 vs seen 3.4; double_add unseen 3.0 vs seen 2.8). Verify the step mix from the records PC' really trains on before sealing; the manifest counts may not be minimal. The full-b PC' arm is reused only if the code and dose are identical (re-run it once to check it reproduces sq_plus 53/61). Dose: the c2b rule (lr 1e-3, 32 visits per record, updates = visits x records / 32), so visits per record match across arms; no "same updates" variant.
Rows scored (never trained in the holdout arm): unseen = pool rows with b in {4,7} (sq_plus 34+31=65, double_add 33+41=74; per b pooled over both kinds: b=4 67 rows, b=7 72 rows) plus DEV unseen (sq_plus 8+7=15, double_add 10+5=15) reported separately. Seen comparator = DEV rows with b in {3,5,6,8,9} (36 per kind, 72 pooled), same arm. Pooled over sq_plus and double_add, and per kind.
Statistic: per held-out b, pooled over both kinds, first try right (verdict accept); report the worst of the two b values, not the macro mean (with two held-out values a fixed-answer strategy scores 50% macro; the worst-b rule gives it 0).
Marks to seal in a file before running (proposed numbers, for the lead to fix): Gate: seen (DEV, pooled) first try >= 25% on the parent, else the arm is "unmeasured" (kills the 0 >= 0 pass). Parts kept (job 7 marks): fresh add/mult reach >= 50% and skills harm <= 2 vs N', else the arm is invalid. Pass (both seeds): worst-b unseen pooled >= 0.6 x seen pooled, and DEV unseen pooled >= 0.4 x seen (direction check with a number). Proved wrong (both seeds): worst-b unseen <= 0.3 x seen. Anything else, including mixed seeds: "between the marks, no claim, run six seeds". Six paired seeds before any claim (rule 4); two seeds (s100 s101, which already have PC' runs, or two of s200-s205 with rebuilt N') is a screen. Primary scoring is pool-unseen, DEV secondary (DEV was used to pick the PC' dose, roadmap L578).
STAGE 1b (only if stage 1 is "pass" or "unclear", a separate single change): remove 4 and 7 from the warm add rows and from replay too, and rebuild the parent for that arm. That tests piece-level holdout. Do not run it in the same step as tier A.
STAGE 2 (the arm that bears on the 71.3%): the same split values and marks, but inside the compliant loop recipe (own night, chain search, replay on the day's own inputs, batch-1024 fine-tune, 80 visits), with b in {4,7} removed from the practice pool, replay and chain library. This is the loop thread's own hypothesis 3, so hand it to the fast-sleep thread rather than building a second copy. Cost about 2,400 TF per sleep (shown: report), so two seeds is about 4,800 TF; run it only if stage 1 is not "proved wrong" (if PC' with teacher programs cannot cross to an unseen constant, the loop arm is unlikely to, suggested). The creative/rl loop code is not in the scratchpad checkout I was given, so the lead should ask the fast-sleep thread for it.
AFFINE: dropped from stage 1 (PC' affine 2% and 4% fails any seen >= 8% gate). If kept, it lives in stage 2 only, gated on the loop arm's own seen-pair first try >= 8% (the loop scores affine 15.5%), holding out 12 of the 48 pool pairs with every a and every b still present elsewhere. Note a and b parts are all practised in warm-up, so it is again a composition test. Pair (4,7) is in DEV once and in the pool zero times (64 of 65 rules are practised, not all 65), one row, no power.
Device: not named in the idea. Rule 6 says Ben's PC (on q39 then q40/T1) and Mac (job 9 until about 4 PM ET, then the sealed-test ask) first; cloud CPU or rented GPU only with Ben's OK. Time one PC' sleep first (untested); the "2.5 h" is setup, not GPU time.
chair.plan_guidance:
What the test plan must get right:

1. Say what it measures. The scorer bans example-slot reads (fewshot.py L43-44, shown), so "reading b" is not the mechanism. The only live alternatives are per-(kind, constant) program memory and composition of practised parts (warm add rows cover B=3..30 and are replayed, shown). Label the claim composition-across-constants, tier A. A piece-level holdout (stage 1b) is a separate, later change.

2. One change at a time, marks sealed in a file first (suggest fast-sleep/CH1-PASS-MARKS.md). Include a gate (seen >= 25%), a parts-kept check (fresh add/mult reach >= 50%, skills harm <= 2 vs N'), and an explicit "between the marks" verdict. Define seen and unseen rows by name. Seen = DEV rows with b in {3,5,6,8,9}, which are untrained. Unseen = pool rows with b in {4,7}, which are removed from sleep, plus DEV b in {4,7} reported separately. Use worst-held-out-b so a fixed-constant guesser scores 0, and report per-b numbers.

3. Dose: use the c2b rule (updates = visits x records / 32, 32 visits, lr 1e-3) in every arm. Drop the "fixed updates, 7/5 visits" claim, because it is wrong (about 1.23x for every record) and the confound runs toward a false "memorising" verdict.

4. Match program length. Edge {8,9} is length-matched but is mostly b=9 (13 of 18 DEV unseen per kind) and mixes in extrapolation. Interior {5,6} is longer (4 vs 3.2 steps). {4,7} is length-matched and interior. Re-measure the step mix from the actual PC' records, because the manifest counts may not be minimal.

5. Power: DEV unseen is only 30 rows for {4,7} (15 per kind), so the pool holdout (139 rows) carries it. Per-b SE is about 6 points per seed at p near 0.4 (suggested). The ratio is only readable at the extremes (<= 0.3 or >= 0.8). Two seeds is a screen only; because a PC' sleep is cheap, plan the six-seed run in advance and trigger it on "pass", "proved wrong" or "between" alike (a claim needs six).

6. Label honestly: PC' uses reference programs from the rule function (key-informed teaching data). Under roadmap 7c that is "outside help: yes, own choices: no", a positive control. It cannot speak to the 71.3% loop. Fix the idea's autonomy field. Do not call stage 1 evidence about the deployed sleep. The loop-regime arm (stage 2) is what bears on the 71.3% and on rule 10, and the loop's sleep-time search is itself reported as hand code that "the sleep calls", which Ben must rule on separately (text-called tool or not).

7. Avoid duplication. Cite RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md L68 (hypothesis 3) and gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md Q3 as prior. Coordinate with the fast-sleep thread so one split definition is shared; do not let two threads run different holdouts.

8. Fix the stated numbers before anyone budgets: 57 TF per arm has no source (about 95-115 TF per arm at 32 visits, suggested); 64 of 65 rules are in practice, not all 65 (affine pair (4,7) is DEV-only); DEV counts and pool counts above are shown. Name the device and queue slot (rule 6) and time one sleep first. Do not open test.jsonl or labelled.jsonl (rule 5), and do not generate fresh questions that would need their keys to deduplicate.

9. Drop stage 2 affine from the PC' step (it cannot pass its own 8% gate). It can live in the loop arm, gated on the loop's own affine seen-pair score.

10. Plain-language summary for Ben, to put in the final write-up: "Right now the test questions use the same 65 rules the model slept on, so a high score could just mean it memorised 65 answers. We hide two of the seven numbers for two kinds of rule during sleep, then see if the model still gets those rules right. The numbers are still taught during early practice, so a pass means it can combine pieces it knows, not that it invented a new number. A fail means it learned a lookup list."

11. Ranking note for the lead: this is a cheap, low-risk measurement that decides how to read the headline 70% claim. Its main value is stage 2, so rank it by whether the fast-sleep thread will run the loop arm. If that thread already plans hypothesis 3 with a held-out split, fold this idea into that and do not run a separate stage 1 unless the 2,400 TF gate is wanted.

plan.ben_line: Right now the test questions use the same rules the model practised on, so a high score could just mean it memorised answers. We hide two of the numbers from its sleep for two kinds of rule, then check whether it still gets those rules right on new questions. Those numbers were still taught in early practice, so a pass means it can combine pieces it already knows, and a fail means it only learned a list of answers.
plan.question: When sleep teaches sq_plus and double_add rules with constants 4 and 7 left out (those constants are still in early practice), does the model get new questions with 4 or 7 right at least 60% as often as questions with constants it was taught?

BETWEEN (anything else, including seeds that disagree): no claim; go to the six-seed confirm under the same sealed marks.
plan.proved_wrong: On both seeds, the worst held-out constant's pool score is at most 0.3 times the seen score (about 12-15% if seen is 40-51%, with the gate and parts-kept marks met), or unseen is within 10 points of N' on both seeds. Read as: in this build, neither the sleep on these two kinds nor the untouched warm-up practice carried to a constant the model never slept on. That is the composition route the claim names, so the claim fails for these two kinds. Two-seed odds (suggested, normal approximation, not simulated): a true ratio of 0.3 gives a both-seed proved-wrong call about one time in four.
plan.null_risk: Yes, the marks can pass with no real effect from sleep. The thinker may already build 4 and 7 from practised parts: warm add rows B=4 (44) and B=7 (38), mult A=4 (138) and A=7 (158) (shown: warm.jsonl counts), and the affine stone (a=2, b=4), which is usable at 2 steps (shown: results/c2stones/s100.json info.usable). The stone (2,7) was dropped at 4 steps, so 7 has less practice. If the parts already carry, unseen can match seen with or without the PC' rows. The anti-null only excludes a model that scores zero on unseen; it does not exclude composition from warm-up. Stage 1b is the check for that. Two more risks: (a) the holdout arm has 23% fewer updates and a different kind mix (affine 205 of 475 = 43%, against 33% of 614). Seen and unseen can move together; the within-split ratio absorbs a uniform shift, not a selective one. (b) Per-seed standard error on the ratio is about 0.15 (suggested, from about 70-row cells at p near 0.3-0.45; not simulated), so two-seed calls are reliable only at the extremes and BETWEEN is the most likely outcome. Probability that the marks pass with no real change: untested.
plan.autonomy: Measurement only. No step in this plan is a deployed method, so the deployed model does none of the stage-1 steps itself. The held-out values come from the generator's parameter list; that is measurement design, and the sleep never reads it. For stage 2 (not run here) the model would write its own tries, keep the ones that fit, and sleep on its own records. But the loop's chain search and example check are hand code the sleep calls, not a tool the model chooses to call by writing text. Ben must rule on that before any stage-2 result can count as autonomous.

idea.title: Stop the weight sleep from the model's own held-out check
idea.summary: The sleep is about 85-90% of the loop's roughly 2,400 TF, and its dose (32 or 80 visits, lr 1e-3) was picked by us on DEV with answer keys. Run the sleep in chunks and let the model stop when its own fit rate on questions it did not sleep on stops rising, with rollback. DEV rose 64.6 to 72.7 between 40 and 80 visits, so the test must show the rule does not stop too early.
idea.change: sleep.py: run the night as chunks of 2 visits (8 at the loop's scale) at a constant learning rate after 20 warm-up updates, so a stopped run equals a shorter run (the current cosine decays to the run's own total updates). Withhold 20-25% of the pool questions from training in both arms. After each chunk measure greedy fit rate on the withheld questions (the executor's example check, no key) and fit count on 256 stored old questions; stop when the paired gain over the last chunk is below one paired SE or an old question stops fitting, keep the previous chunk's weights. Cheap variant first: N' parents at the job-8 dose (32 visits, about 932 s per arm on the Mac), then the loop's 80-visit recipe. Param cost 0.
idea.why: Fine-tune and loop FLOPs scale with visits, so a self-chosen stop is the one lever on the dominant cost that also removes a DEV-key choice. The risk is noise: one chunk's true gain (about 1.6 points per 8 visits) is near one paired SE on 256 questions (about 1.5-2 points), so the rule may fire at random around 40 visits. At lr 3e-4 gain saturates between 16 and 32 visits but at lr 1e-3 it does not (0.129 at 16, 0.164 at 32 on s100).

problems: Mislabelled split (shown). The 72.7 in the cited table (fast-sleep/gpt-c2-affine-after-big-sleep-2026-10-07.md section 4, the '80 visits' row) is labelled holdout, 2 seeds. Only the 64.6 at 40 visits is DEV, so 'DEV 64.6 to 72.7' mixes splits. The compliant DEV figure at 80 visits is 71.2 (4 parents; fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md reference table).

The two pass marks conflict (suggested arithmetic on the idea's own numbers). S sleep FLOPs at most 0.6 x F means stopping by about 48 of 80 visits. A straight line from DEV 64.6 at 40 visits to about 71 at 80 gives about 66 at 48 visits, while DEV at least F minus 2 needs about 68 visits (about 0.85 x F). The idea says lr 1e-3 does not saturate, so both marks cannot pass together. The screen can fail on its own arithmetic.

The cheap variant's chunk is far below its own noise (shown numbers, suggested inference). In creative/creative/results/c2keep/s100.json the lr 1e-3 dose grid goes from pooled first try 12.9% at 16 visits to 16.4% at 32. That is about 0.44 points per 2-visit chunk, roughly a quarter of the idea's one paired SE (1.5-2). If chunk noise is about one SE, the 1-SE stop fires at its first allowed check (4 chunks, 8 visits) about three times in four. The same file gives DEV 7.8% and skills_harm_points 4.3 at 8 visits, so the cheap screen would mostly measure noise and fail its DEV and harm marks whatever the idea's merit.

The paired SE is asserted, not computed (untested). A paired SE depends on how many questions change status between consecutive chunks. The idea gives no measure of that and no file measures it, so the 1-SE stop and the chunk size cannot be set yet. A similar small-sample threshold already caused harm: a 0.99 quantile from 24 rows (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 7, 'Gate maths').

Fit is not the same as right (suggested; partly untested). The stop watches greedy fit on withheld questions, while DEV counts fit AND right. A grep of fast-sleep/ and creative-roadmap/ finds no measured fit-but-wrong rate for B2's greedy tries. The area fact check (not re-verified here) reports that 70.6% of accepted random square fits and 76.3% of last_digit fits give a wrong query answer, so a fit-rate stop can keep rising while the right rate does not. The test needs a per-chunk log of withheld fit and DEV right, showing that they move together.

Harm is invisible to the stop, and it is worst at the early stops (shown). In the same c2keep file, skills_harm_points at lr 1e-3 is 2.1, 4.3, 2.2 and 0.9 at 4, 8, 16 and 32 visits. The canary is fit-only (the idea concedes it may not see skills harm) and keeps keyed harm as a report. PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md L95 (D8) requires the model to check its own harm on held practice, so this does not meet D8.

'256 stored old questions' is undefined (shown code). sleep.load_replay returns the 200k skills rows (fastsleep/creative/sleep.py L43-48), the same rows the sleep trains on. A fit check on those needs the answer key, which the idea says it does not use. If instead the rows are the C2-format warm rows, they cannot see skills harm. Replay rows are also in-sample, so they are not a held-out canary.

Key rule and rule 10 (ruling needed). The stop logic (1-SE test, rollback, cap, chunking, the 20-25% split) is hand-written code that decides when to stop. The key rule names 'gates' and 'when to sleep or stop' as things the deployed model must do itself. Allowed hand code is an outside tool the model calls by writing text, and fixed constants are allowed only if they are the same every night and not tuned on DEV. A fixed statistic that decides the stop fits neither clearly, and the idea's own text says a learned stop would replace it. Ben must rule on this before any run.

The constants are not clean, so 'removes a DEV-key choice' is overstated (shown). The 80-visit cap is research-loop trial 6, chosen on dev seeds (RESEARCH-LOOP report, findings item 3). lr 1e-3 came from the dose rule in c2keep/s100.json dose_choice, which the idea itself says used DEV keys. The idea moves only the length choice to the model. The 71.3 'compliant' recipe keeps these same choices, so its label is not clean under rule 10 either. The keyed 2.0 guard also still runs in deployment, which the key rule does not allow.

One-change breach (suggested). The test bundles three changes: constant lr in place of cosine (needed for the prefix trick, but a change to the compliant recipe), 20-25% withholding of pool questions in both arms (removes a fifth of W and chain records; affine records are already scarce, 202 records over 48 programs in the GPT file section 4), and the self-stop. F and S both carry the first two, so no arm compares with the compliant 71.3 recipe. Missing: F0 (cosine, full pool), F1 (constant lr, full pool), then F2 (withholding), then S.
Mixed outcomes are undefined. The pass needs both seeds to pass and the proved-wrong needs both to fail. One seed of each is neither, and rule 4 requires the decision to be fixed before the run.

Vague terms (suggested). 'Chunk of 2 visits' does not say updates, records or batch size (job 8's sleep uses batch 64, the compliant run 1,024). 'Paired gain over the last chunk' does not say which questions. 'An old question stops fitting' does not say one miss or a rate. Unset: the rollback when the first chunk fails, the cap (80 or 32), whether withheld questions also leave the chain search, and whether check FLOPs count against 0.6 x F.

Check FLOPs are not counted (suggested). Each chunk checks about 500 questions (withheld plus old). At the 0.78-0.97 GFLOP per try or row figures in the area file and the code notes, that is about 0.4-0.5 TF per check. Over 16 checks in the cheap screen that is 6-8 TF, about 15-40% of a 19-39 TF fine-tune.

The '290 TF of tries' cite does not match its source. The idea cites fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6, but section 6 gives about 25.5 TF for the 32-try night and 290 does not appear in that file. It may include a 480-try pass, but no file says so. If tries are 25.5 TF, weight sleep is about 98% of the night, not 85-90%. The direction holds; the number is unsourced.

Scheduling (shown, progress-board/data.json). The board has the Mac training job 9 until about 4 PM ET and the PC on q39, then q40 (T1) until about 11 PM. The cheap screen cannot start as written without waiting. This is a timing issue, not a rule breach.

Label clash. The roadmap uses D6 for the learned notebook gate (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md L853, section 7b) and for honesty rules (L199). The id 'fastsleep-D6' should be renamed so claims do not mix.
critiques.rescue: Make the first step a measurement, not a stop. (1) Run a logging-only sleep on the full pool at constant lr after 20 warm-up updates, with C2-format old rows, that writes per chunk: withheld greedy fit rate, the old-row fit count, and DEV right (reported, never used by the stop). Fix the mark in advance: the withheld-fit gain tracks the DEV-right gain on 6 parents. (2) Measure the paired SE from consecutive-chunk discordance on the same parent, then set the chunk size so a true per-chunk gain is at least one SE. (3) Replace the two conflicting marks with one: DEV at the stop within 2 of the full run, and sleep FLOPs including checks at most 0.8 of the full run. Add a mixed-outcome rule. (4) Test constant lr against cosine on the full pool as a one-change test, then withholding as a second test, then the stop. (5) Get Ben's ruling on whether a fixed hand-written stop counts under the key rule. If not, the stop must be the learned gate (roadmap section 7b) or a tool the model calls by writing text. (6) Define chunk units, the old-row canary and the cap, and label any DEV-chosen value (80 visits, lr 1e-3) as a disclosed constant. Until the model has its own harm check (D8), the idea cannot be called autonomous.
critiques.already_tried: Not run as a self-chosen stop. Closest prior: fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, 'Next hypotheses' item 4 (smallest visits that keeps 70%, offline and DEV-tuned; not run). The planned home is D8: creative-roadmap/creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md L970 and no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md L95. Both set the goal but have no marks. The visits curve at lr 3e-4 and 1e-3 (16 vs 32 visits) is already measured in creative/creative/results/c2keep/s100.json, and that is the pilot the stop must beat. No file measures whether withheld fit rate tracks DEV right. The idea is not a duplicate; its nearest relatives are H4 and D8.
critiques.expected_effect: If the stop works as the idea says, the S arm stops at a fixed fraction of the full run on both seeds, with DEV within 2 of the full run. That would cut the weight-sleep share of the roughly 2,400 TF loop (suggested: about 0.5-0.6 x if the stop lands near 40-48 of 80 visits). Clear on the text: rule 1 (stop code runs outside the forward pass), rule 2 (no teacher), rule 3 (0 params), rule 5 (DEV only scores; the pool is practice) and rule 7 (no targets cut). As written, the most likely outcome (suggested) is a noise-driven stop near 8-16 visits, with harm above 2 and DEV below F minus 4. That would say little about the idea itself.

problems: AUTONOMY (rule 10; roadmap 7c 'Own choices: no'): the stop is hand code in the sleep driver (chunking, paired-SE test, rollback, withheld split). The model never decides to stop and never calls a stop tool, so the idea's claim that 'chunking, held-out split, greedy tries, example check, rollback and stop are the model's own steps' is not met as written (shown: the change field and the 7c table). An autonomous form is not specified: the model writes CONTINUE or STOP after reading a fit-count tool's output, or a learned stop head is trained on a signal it can check without keys (suggested).

EARLY STOP UNDER THE IDEA'S OWN NUMBERS (suggested arithmetic on shown grid): the test uses 2-visit chunks, but the noise argument uses 8-visit gains (1.6 per 8 visits). The cosine grid on the job-7 parent (c2keep/s100.json dose_grid, lr 1e-3, pooled first try at 4/8/16/32 visits = 5.1/7.8/12.9/16.4) gives about 1.3 points per 2 visits early and about 0.4 late. The paired SE is sqrt(d/256), which is 1.1 to 2.0 points for d = 3-10% of questions changing fit between chunks. Under a normal approximation the chance that the observed gain falls below one SE is about 0.4-0.6 per early chunk and 0.7-0.8 per late chunk. The earliest allowed stop (4 chunks = 8 visits) is therefore likely, and a stop by 8-20 visits is more likely than the 'around 40' the idea predicts. The screen's own 'DEV at stop below F minus 4' proved-wrong mark would then probably trigger, so the screen as specified would most likely fail.

UNDEFINED CANARY: 'stop when ... an old question stops fitting' read literally stops the sleep on the first lost fit among 256 old questions. Some flip is likely in any 2-visit chunk. The idea needs a fixed threshold and its justification.

BUNDLED CHANGES (rule 4, one change at a time): constant lr replaces the cosine, 20-25% of the pool is withheld from training, and the chunked stop, fit canary and rollback all change together. The F arm is not the compliant recipe (cosine, all pool questions, 80 visits, 71.3 holdout), and every mark is relative to F. A loss from constant lr or withholding would pass unseen, and the screen cannot attribute a pass or fail to any one part. F must first be checked against the 71.3 recipe.

DEV-TUNED VALUES LEFT IN AND NOT FLAGGED (rule 10; roadmap 7c lists sleep learning rate and 'when to sleep' as choices the model must make itself): lr 1e-3 and the 32-visit cap come from the c2keep/s100.json dose_choice rule, which is DEV greedy first try and multi-step first try, with keyed harm <= 2 (shown). The pool temperature T on N' is 'best DEV reach@32' (c2keep/s100.json pool_temperature.rule, shown). The c2pilot dose_choice picked 16 visits, so the dose has already moved between runs on DEV keys (shown). The rules_check flags only chunk size, 1-SE, split and cap as constants.

KEYED HARM GUARD STAYS AT DEPLOY (rule 10): the nightly off-switch (fastsleep.py:566-580) turns memory off when chain-5 harm on DEV keyed rows exceeds 2.0 (fastsleep.py:88-95, shown). The idea keeps it 'until the guard idea replaces it', so deployment still needs answer keys, and no autonomous skills-harm check is proposed. The fit-only canary may not see skills harm (the idea's own orchestrator note). The keyed harm is non-monotone in visits (lr 1e-3: 2.1, 4.3, 2.2, 0.9 at 4/8/16/32, c2keep/s100.json dose_grid, shown). The worst point, 4.3 at 8 visits, sits at the earliest stop the idea allows.

SCORER RULING NEEDED FOR THE FIT CHECK: verdict() (fewshot.py:84-101) requires structure() (fewshot.py:34-48), which rejects any program that reads a prompt number other than the query. That is a test format rule, which rule 10 excludes as test-generator knowledge, and it needs Ben's C2-R ruling. If the stop's fit check uses only example reproduction, banned example-reading programs count as fits (the area fact check found 6-7 step example-reading programs fitting all 257 affine rows, which the idea does not address). Balance (shown): in the c2keep arms the greedy fit count equals first-try right for every kind (N' 0.0039/0.0039, PC' 0.1641/0.1641, W' night 1 0.3164/0.3164, c2keep/s100.json), so the verdict-based fit is a good DEV proxy for greedy tries.

PARENT AND POOL BREAK ROADMAP 7c: the cheap test runs on N' parents whose stepping stones were written by us (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md section 7c: 'No later test uses stepping stones... made by us'; RESEARCH-LOOP report L59 says the same for the 71.3 parents). The pool is 1,024 unanswered questions of the five held-out kinds (fast-sleep gpt-c2-affine file, section 1), so the practice set is hand-picked by kind, which rule 10 excludes. The idea's autonomy section mentions neither.

NUMBERS TO FIX: (a) 'DEV rose 64.6 to 72.7' mixes splits. The 72.7 cell is labelled holdout in gpt-c2-affine section 4, and RESEARCH-LOOP report L35 gives 70.7 as the segment-1 DEV figure, so the DEV step is about 6 points over 40 visits (about 1.2 per 8 visits, not 1.6; suggested). (b) '290 TF of tries (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6)': that section gives about 25.5 TF for a 32-try night (line 112, shown). 290 does not appear there, so the 85-90% weight-sleep share is the idea's own subtraction (suggested). (c) The dose-grid figures do match c2keep/s100.json dose_grid (shown), but that grid is on N' with 614 records and cosine decay, so constant-lr chunks would not reproduce it.

COST UNDERSTATED: the 1.2 h estimate leaves out per-chunk DEV scoring and the per-chunk greedy checks on 205-256 withheld and 256 old questions. One full evaluation in c2stuck took 186 s (c2stuck/s100.json seconds.night1_eval, shown), so 16 chunk evaluations per seed could add a large share of the budget (suggested, not costed). The S arm's sleep FLOPs should count these checks against the 0.6 x F bar.

chair.reasons: CUT as a standalone 2.5 h screen. All four critics said revise (scores 3-5) and their main points hold; I re-read the key numbers. (1) The pass marks cannot all pass. Shown (creative/creative/results/c2keep/s100.json and s101.json, lr 1e-3, 2-seed mean pooled first try): DEV 7.8 / 8.8 / 14.7 / 19.0 and keyed harm 2.7 / 3.0 / 2.2 / 1.4 at 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 visits. Sleep FLOPs <= 0.6 F needs a stop near 19 visits or earlier; DEV >= F-2 needs about 24+ (suggested, interpolated); harm <= 2 needs about 19+. The window is empty. At loop scale, fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md (shown) says 80 visits beat 40 by +7.0 on fresh seeds and the model is still under-trained at 40; the 40-visit row (64.6) is under the 70% goal. Early stopping suits an overfitting curve, and this curve is still rising, so the likely results are a noise-driven early stop that fails F-4, or running to the cap, which saves nothing (both are the idea's own proved-wrong results). (2) The 1-SE rule is noise-dominated at 2-visit chunks (suggested): a chunk gains about 0.4-1.5 DEV points against a paired SE of 1.5-2 on 256 questions, and s101 dips between 4 and 8 visits. The paired SE was never measured (no per-row predictions are saved). (3) Harm is non-monotone and a fit-only stop cannot see it (shown): the worst harm sits at the earliest allowed stops. The old-question canary is undefined; skills replay rows are the sleep's own training rows, not held out. (4) Three changes are bundled (constant lr instead of cosine, withholding 20-25 percent of W, the stop), against rule 4, and no arm equals the compliant 71.3 recipe. A constant-lr prefix is also un-annealed, so it should look worse than the cosine grid. (5) Autonomy gain is overstated: lr 1e-3 and the 80/32 cap were chosen on DEV keys and stay, the keyed chain-5 guard stays, and the fit definition needs Ben's C2-R ruling on the structure() example-read ban. (6) Cited facts to fix: 72.7 is a holdout figure (gpt-c2-affine file section 4), not DEV; the 290 TF of tries is a residual, not measured (RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 6 gives 25.5 TF per 32-try night); the id D6 collides with the roadmap learned-gate D6. Rules 2, 3, 5 and 7 are not violated, and greedy fit equals greedy right on DEV in the c2keep arms (shown), which is the idea's one real strength. Near-duplicate of H4 (smallest visits that keeps 70%) and roadmap D8.

idea.title: CPU probe: does B2 read the examples in its fewshot prompts?
idea.summary: Run the saved B2 models on hand-built fewshot prompts and change one thing at a time: swap the example outputs for another rule's, swap the pair order, put the query first, drop to one example, split by minus sign, count how often the thinker writes any step, and feed it a hand-solved program. No training is needed. It says whether B2's 34.6 vs 60.8 in-distribution gap is a reading, position, sign, missing-program or digit-writing failure, and it routes most of the other fewshot ideas.
idea.change: No model change. One new test script (hand-written scoring, allowed) run on CPU on B2_s100 and B2_s101 (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/, 13,243,510 bytes each, verified present), with plain_tf and plain_tf_steps seeds 100 and 101 (checkpoints/20-screen-s100-w1 and 22-screen-s101-w1, verified present) as comparators. Rows: 400 per stratum per seed, hand-built in the sk200k format '12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?' (research/data.md section 1) and in the own72 wrapper 'Examples: a -> b; ... Now q -> ?'; rules mult y=A*x (A 2-9), add y=x+B (B about -30..30), pair_sum; 2 or 3 pairs; prompts under 208 characters. Readouts from the same forward passes: (a) donor swap: keep x1, x2, q, replace the example outputs with another rule's, count answer follows donor / keeps original / copies an example output / unchanged; (b) pair-order swap (invariance share); (c) query moved to the front (accuracy drop); (d) accuracy at 1, 2, 3 pairs (4-7 reported apart, since training holds 2 or 3 pairs); (e) accuracy split by minus sign in the prompt; (f) share of rounds where the op head writes NOOP, the step-1 op chosen, and a hand-solved program teacher-forced through Ledger.run(gold=...) using the tensor layout of Ledger.gold(); (g) digit-error type among wrong answers (wrong length, wrong units digit, wrong tens digit); (h) add rows with B built in 1, 2 or 3 steps from {1,2,10,100} at k=2, inside the trained B range, as a build-cost ladder; (i) loops:0 lesion on the same rows as a control.
idea.why: The brief's open question is whether the fewshot failure is in reading the examples or in writing the rule. Shown: fewshot in-distribution is 34.6 for B2 against 60.8 for plain_tf_steps and 62.9 for plain_tf, and plain_tf_steps gets no steps either, so the gap exists without steps on either side. Shown: the family has 0.0% program coverage and 96% of its gold answers are GEN mode, and rows with no program are trained toward NOOP at weight 0.1 with the gold NOOP teacher-forced. No file saves per-row outputs, so none of these causes has been measured. The fact check refuted the 'plain_tf_steps memorised digit shapes' story (a shape predicts the answer only 2.6% of the time), so the cause is inside B2.

evidence.claim: fewshot_number_rule per split over seeds 200-205, B2 / plain_tf_steps / plain_tf: in_dist 34.6 / 60.8 / 62.9; answer 28.3 / 41.7 / 40.4; frame 25.0 / 47.1 / 47.1; variant 2.9 / 0.8 / 0.4; pooled-5 22.7 / 37.6 / 37.7. Paired B2 minus plain_tf_steps in_dist is -26.25 (CI -31.9 to -20.6, negative on 6 of 6 seeds). plain_tf_steps minus plain_tf is -2.1 (steps add nothing on this family).
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: Gold program coverage 0.0% and gold GEN mode 96.0% for fewshot (a label of the target, not a measurement of what B2 emits). Copy share on its GEN registers is 0.02-0.05.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: In training, rows with no program use the gold op NOOP, which is teacher-forced in run(), so the executor writes nothing; the op loss on those rows has weight w_noop = 0.1.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: A predictor that outputs the most common answer for each masked digit shape scores 2.6% on 9,324 held-out pool rows, so digit-shape memory cannot explain a lead of 26 points.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: No saved file has per-row B2 outputs; RESULT.json keeps family totals only. The bench note suggests saving per-row outputs before the next design.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: The analysis sandbox has no torch; the skills generator and dev rows are not on disk (data.py DEFAULT_DATA absent). So this probe must run on the PC or M1 with hand-built rows, and its rows are diagnostics, not the sealed dev.
evidence.label: shown

evidence.claim: With a one-example prompt and a mult-plus-add prior, about 8.1% of questions are ambiguous and with two examples 0%, so an ideal reader can reach about 100% at two examples.
evidence.label: suggested
evidence.source: a scout's unsaved simulation of 20,000 questions (w3b-1)

evidence.claim: A 40-row cell has a standard error of about 7.5 points near 50%; the paired in_dist difference has SD 5.4 so a 2-seed mean below about 10 points cannot be judged on 40-row cells. Use 400-row strata.
evidence.label: shown

test.where: PC or M1 Pro CPU (torch must be installed; it is not in the analysis sandbox). Checkpoints B2_s100, B2_s101, tf_s100, tf_s101, tfsteps_s100, tfsteps_s101 from /mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/.
test.arms: B2 seeds 100 and 101, each with plain_tf and plain_tf_steps of the same seed as comparators; strata: original, donor-swapped, pair-swapped, query-first, k=1/2/3, positive-B vs negative-B (minus sign), build-cost levels 1-3; loops:0 control.
test.pass_mark: Fixed now, read on both seeds. Validity gate: B2 accuracy on the unmodified hand-built rows is within 10 points of 34.6, else nothing is judged. READS EXAMPLES: donor-follow share is at least 0.6 times original accuracy and copy-an-example share is at most 5%. IGNORES: follow at most 0.2 times original accuracy and unchanged at least 60%. ORDER-BOUND: invariance share at most 0.70; ORDER-FREE: at least 0.90 and accuracy change within 3 points. POSITION-BOUND: query-first drop of 15 points or more; free: 5 or less. SIGN: minus-sign rows 20 or more points below positive rows. NO PROGRAM AT TEST: NOOP share at least 90%. OUTPUT PATH OK: teacher-forced hand program exact on at least 90%; broken below 50%. DIGIT-LEVEL: at least 50% of wrong answers have the right length and units digit. Routing: READS plus NOOP-high plus OUTPUT-OK goes to the traces idea; IGNORES goes to the example-structure augmentations; SIGN goes to signed numbers; ORDER or POSITION-BOUND goes to the layout arm; DIGIT-LEVEL with traces failing goes to the causal digit readout.
test.proved_wrong: This is a decision tool, not a claim. It is misleading if the validity gate fails, or if the traces idea later passes while this probe says IGNORES (then the donor test missed a reading path and should be redesigned). Between the READS and IGNORES lines is 'partial': rerun on 6 seeds before routing.

idea.rules_check: Rule 1: hand-written rows and scoring are tests (allowed); B2's regex number reader is an existing debt the probe inherits and does not claim to fix. Rule 2: no teacher. Rule 3: no change. Rule 4: a 2-seed probe with marks fixed before running; no claim. Rule 5: fresh hand-built rows, no GOLD-PRIVATE or blind panel. Rule 6: CPU. Rule 7: nothing truncated (prompts under 208 chars, answers under 8). Rule 9: B2 and its plain comparators only.
idea.closest_prior: BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114 asks for per-row outputs on a different model; evalx.donor_eval swaps the thinker state, not the prompt's examples; D0 probes digit reading only. No result file puts example-following, ordering, sign and program-writing on the same fewshot rows.
idea.autonomy: Nothing is added to the deployed model; this measures whether the deployed model's own pointers use the examples in its prompt. The test rows and scorer are outside tools, which rules 1 and 10 allow for tests.
idea.director_note: Cheapest decisive item in the area. Critics should check hardest: (1) the validity gate, since the own72 wrapper differs from the sk200k format and a wrapper mismatch could cause a fake drop; (2) that donor pairs are pinned and have a different answer; (3) the assumed rule families (mult 2-9, add about +-30) match the real generator, which is not on disk; (4) the scout claim in w1e-4 that no plain_tf checkpoint exists is wrong (they exist, verified), so plain comparators are available; (5) w1j-5's build-cost levels for mult have no level-3 value inside A 2-9, so use add only.
