problems: OUTPUT PATH mark cannot pass on the mix the idea describes. The own72 fewshot rows (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/built/own72.tgz, skills.jsonl, 46,618 fewshot rows, streamed and counted here) include 5,543 rows with a negative example output ('-> -'), all in add rows (36.9% of add rows; 11.9% of all fewshot rows). Prompt numbers are read with NUM_RE = \d+ (progparse.py NUM_RE definition; ledger.py:206), so the minus sign never reaches the workspace the hand program runs on. A hand program that uses the obvious route is therefore exact on at most about 88.1% of an unrestricted mix, below the >=90% mark. The idea's own '88.1% traceable' figure equals the non-negative share. (shown: counts; the ceiling is an inference)

The SIGN stratum is predictable from code, and the defect is already known and already planned for repair. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/../ is not needed: the shown files are /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/INVENTORY-2026-10-07.md:70 (B2's number regex drops minus signs), /mnt/project-files/architecture/MARKS-D0-T1-2026-10-07.md:40 (the thinker's number values come from the hand regex NUM_RE), /mnt/project-files/creative-roadmap/creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:263 (C2 avoids prompt numbers equal to constants for this reason) and /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:419 (planned 2c1: replace NUM_RE with a learned digit reader). The sign split therefore confirms a known defect and does not diagnose reading. (shown)

Sign is unlikely to be the main cause of the in-distribution gap. Using the own72 negative share (11.9%), and only if the sk200k share matches (untested), the sign defect can cost at most about 11.9 points, against the 26.25-point in_dist gap between B2 and plain_tf_steps (B2 83/240 vs plain_tf_steps 146/240 over seeds 200-205, from results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json files). This caps the sign stratum's role in the routing. The cap assumes B2 cannot use the minus character from reader output; cross-attention could let it, which is untested. (shown for the counts; the cap is conditional)

READS is confounded by the hand parser. Prompt numbers, including the example outputs and the query, enter the thinker through a hand-written regex (ledger.py:200-212, :206), so a READS verdict means the thinker's pointers use hand-parsed values, not that B2 learned to read examples. The idea's rules_check calls this existing debt and says the probe does not fix it, but the verdict wording ('reads the examples') would over-claim. The regex breaks rule 1 (hand logic between question and answer, outside a tool called by writing text) and rule 10 inside the model under test. (shown)

The validity gate is loosely defined. Its target, 34.6, is the 6-seed in_dist mean for seeds 200-205 (83/240, from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/results/33-pc-confirm-b2/*/RESULT.json). The probe runs on seeds 100 and 101, where the screen RESULT.json files (results/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 and B2_s101) show B2 in_dist fewshot 15/40 (37.5) and 12/40 (30.0). The hand-built mix is not required to match the own72 variant mix (add 32.2%, mult 34.9%, pair_sum 32.8%; k = 2 or 3; mult A 2-9; add B -30..30). A pass or fail within plus-or-minus 10 points therefore does not show that the hand rows match the family, and a fail leaves nothing judged. (shown for the numbers; the gate design is a suggestion)

k = 1 is outside training. The own72 fewshot rows have only 2 or 3 example pairs (k=2: 6,037 add, 6,553 mult, 6,216 pair_sum; k=3: 8,981 add, 9,735 mult, 9,096 pair_sum). The idea reports k=1 without a mark, so a k=1 drop would show distribution shift, not a reading failure. sk200k is not on disk, so its k range is untested. (shown for own72)

'The generator is not on disk' is only half right. own72 skills.jsonl contains the fewshot generator's output: three variants (add 15,018 with A = 1; mult 16,288 with A in 2-9; pair_sum 15,312 with 'infer pair rule'), add B spanning -30..30 (59 values), and example outputs that can be negative (add only). The idea's rule set (mult 2-9, add -30..30, pair_sum) matches own72. Affine (A and B both nonzero) is absent here, which fits data.md section 3 listing 'fewshot affine' in the variant split. Whether sk200k, B2's real training data, has the same rule set is untested. (shown for own72)

Two wrappers, one gate. The idea mixes the bare sk200k format ('12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?', data.md section 1) with the own72 'Examples: ... Now q -> ?' wrapper, whose openers ('Try this problem.', 'Think it through.', 'Read carefully.') are not shown to be in B2's training set. own72 is also not shown to be B2's pool (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md). Each wrapper needs its own gate and verdict. (shown for the formats; untested for B2's training)

Ledger.gold() fails silently on fewshot rows. The steps text 'rule x*A+B' and 'infer pair rule' match no progparse pattern, so to_program raises 'unparsed step', program_for returns None, and row_targets returns prog=() (progparse.py to_program/_targets). gold() then gives an answer-only NOOP target with no error (ledger.py:436-449). A hand program passed through gold() would be replaced by NOOP without notice. The cache key is r['id'] (progparse.py:185-192), so hand rows need unique ids. The probe should build the op/a/b tensors directly and assert that each program is non-empty. (shown)

Routing has gaps and some strata route nothing. READS needs donor-follow >= 0.6 x original plus copy <= 5%; IGNORES needs follow <= 0.2 x original plus unchanged >= 60%; the band between is 'partial' and needs 6 seeds. The six B2 checkpoints exist in the scratchpad b2ckpt folder (B2_s200 to B2_s205), so a 6-seed B2 rerun is possible, but the plain comparators exist only for seeds 100 and 101 (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/20-screen-s100-w1 and 22-screen-s101-w1). Query-first, pair-order, digit-error and build-cost have no pass mark that routes to anything. (shown for the marks; the gap is a design issue)

The build-cost ladder (h) is mis-specified for fewshot. The rule constant B is never written in a fewshot prompt; it is implied by the outputs (own72 add rows), so SUB(y1, x1) gives B. A ladder over constants built from {1, 2, 10, 100} tests a program-writing route, not example reading. (suggested)

Protected-panel caution. own72 has not been cleared against GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind hashes (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/DATA-POOL-PLAN-2026-10-06.md lines 23, 128, 164). The idea takes only the wrapper format from it, which is allowed. Copying any own72 row into a probe would break rule 5. (shown)

Overlap and history. /mnt/project-files/bench/BENCH-RECIPE.md:114 says the pointer-program version flat-lined at 77/160 on fewshot, cipher_map, group_induct and seq_cycle across five designs (bench model, not B2) and suggests saving per-row outputs first. This probe does that, which is a point in its favour. The director's recommended first step is this same battery. The w1*/w3* idea IDs named in the brief appear in no project file I searched, so overlap with them cannot be checked. (shown)
critiques.rescue: Keep the probe (cheap, CPU, about 0.5 h, and it is the right first diagnostic), with these changes made before any run: (1) Score the output-path mark only on rows with no negative example output (about 88.1% of the own72 mix), and report negative-output rows as a separate regex-bound stratum with no mark. (2) Make the sign stratum a code check (ledger.py:206), not a routing input, and say in every verdict that example values come from the hand regex, so READS means the thinker's pointers use hand-parsed values. (3) Replace the gate: use each seed's own in_dist (37.5 on s100, 30.0 on s101), print plain_tf_steps on the same hand rows (both checkpoints exist for s100 and s101), and generate rows with the own72 mix (add, mult and pair_sum about one third each; k = 2 or 3; mult A 2-9; add B -30..30). Report the gate before any routing. (4) Remove k=1 from the marks and report it as descriptive. (5) Use one wrapper (the bare sk200k format) for all marks; run the own72 'Examples:' wrapper as a separate descriptive frame check. (6) Build the teacher-forced tensors directly, assert each hand program is non-empty, and use unique row ids. (7) Write a prediction table before running (donor-follow share, NOOP share, output-path exactness on non-negative rows, and the 11.9-point sign cap), close the routing gaps by naming the partial band and running the six B2 seeds (200-205) for any partial result, and drop marks that route nothing. (8) Label the result against planned item 2c1 (/mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:419): a READS result on the regex-fed model is not evidence that a learned reader works.
critiques.already_tried: No B2 prompt-example probe found in the project files. Closest prior, each with its limit: evalx.py donor_eval swaps the thinker state, not the prompt examples (scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/evalx.py, donor_eval); /mnt/project-files/bench/BENCH-RECIPE.md:114 (bench pointer programs flat-lined on fewshot across five designs; bench model, not B2); /mnt/project-files/model-audit/probe_prefix_cpu.py:41-44 (hand-written fewshot prompts with the same mult, add and pair rule types, but it measures front-vector norms and attention in the frozen-LM sandwich, not B2 answers); /mnt/project-files/creative-roadmap/creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md:388 (a donor-prompt lesion planned for C2, not B2; keep the claims apart under rule 9).
critiques.expected_effect: If run with the fixes above, a CPU-only result (about 0.5 h on the PC or M1, no training) that splits the in-distribution fewshot gap (34.6 vs 60.8) into example reading, order and position, sign (a known regex defect, capped at about 11.9 points if the sk200k share matches own72), program writing and digit writing, on rows that the hand regex can read. The result would mainly tell whether the thinker follows example outputs; it would not by itself move pooled-5 or new-kind scores. Without the fixes, the output-path mark fails by construction, the gate may leave the verdict unjudged, and the READS verdict over-claims because the examples reach the model through a hand regex.

problems: Autonomy (shown): the probe has no deployed footprint, so it does not break rule 10 by itself. Its steps are researcher steps: donor, pair-order, query-first, k-count, sign and build-ladder prompts are counterfactuals a deployed model never sees; the forced hand-solved program is a gold intervention in the forward pass (ledger.py run(), gold branch near lines 325-331); op-head and pointer readouts come from hooks; marks, validity gate and routing are research-side. Only the executor check and a self-check have deployable versions.

The deploy-usable signal the probe never measures: whether the model's own written program reproduces every example pair in its prompt, with no answer key. The creative roadmap already uses this check (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md lines 46 and 521, card experiment C2). A leave-one-out check (predict each example from the others, compare with the printed example) is also answer-free and allowed by rule 10. Suggested: measure how often a fits-all-pairs program is right on the query.

Rule 1 blocks B2's in-forward executor as the deployed check: execute() runs inside the forward pass, not as a text tool (PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md item 1, line 9). The outside calculator route T1 is not shown: copy of a result is 85-98 percent for 1-3 digit operands and 14 percent at 4 digits (architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md lines 21-26).

The NOOP condition in the READS route cannot fail for the reason it tests. Rows with no program get gold NOOP teacher-forced at weight 0.1 (ledger.py line 501). fewshot coverage is 0.0 percent prog and GEN 96.0 over n=200 (29-b2-screen B2_s100 RESULT.json, extra.coverage.by_family). NOOP-high is what training taught; the 96 percent is a label count from progparse coverage (progparse.py line 212), not an output measurement. Shown.

The SIGN stratum is defined two ways: the strata list says positive-B versus negative-B, while step (e) says minus sign in the prompt (probe text). A negative B shows a minus sign only when a printed number is negative. Also prompt_numbers reads only digit runs (progparse.py lines 14 and 17-18), so the program path drops signs before any run. A SIGN drop is expected from code and cannot separate reading from parsing.

Undefined inputs: pair_sum is named in the rule list but defined in no file on disk. The own72 wrapper shows pair sums such as (32, 3) -> 35 and the form Examples: 24 -> 33; 20 -> 29; 21 -> 30. Now 29 -> ? (data-pool/built/own72.tgz, read to stdout), so the probe mixes two formats without saying which arm uses which. The A 2-9 and B about -30..30 ranges and the 2-or-3-pair training counts are not on disk (research/data.md line 36 shows one 2-pair example). Untested.

Validity anchor and seeds: the gate compares hand rows with 34.6, the six-seed confirm mean on real rows (83 of 240, shown). The two probed seeds score 15/40 and 12/40 on real rows (29-b2-screen RESULT.json). On those seeds B2 minus plain_tf_steps is -15 on both (15 vs 21, 12 vs 18 of 40), against -26.2 over six seeds, so a two-seed read is too noisy for the marks. Rule 4 requires six seeds, and B2 seeds 200-205 are present (scratchpad/code/b2ckpt, 13,243,510 bytes each, shown). Comparators exist only for seeds 100 and 101, so comparator contrasts stay two-seed.

The READS branch routes to a known ceiling: BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114 records a pointer-program version flat-lining at 77 of 160 on fewshot_number_rule and three other families across five designs (another model, shown). PLAN-AND-MARKS item 2 (line 10) says a deployed model gets no hand-made traces for a new kind, so traces help only the trained add and mult kinds; new-kind claims wait on L1 or ST1, which sit behind T1.

Downstream traces route (from the area director's summary; the traces idea text is not on disk): the traces leave about 11.9 percent of rows (minus-sign rows) answer-only, which rule 7 forbids. These are the same rows the SIGN stratum tests, so measure that set directly rather than routing around it.

Position and order confounds: query-first is outside the trained layout (query last, data.md line 36), so a 15-point drop routed to POSITION-BOUND could be format novelty, with no matched control. The ORDER marks leave the band from 0.70 to 0.90 undecided. The k=1 stratum has no ambiguity control (suggested: about 8 percent of one-pair questions are ambiguous, from an unsaved scout simulation).

The donor mark differs from the project's. research/data.md line 70 requires accuracy down 20 or more points and at least half of swapped outputs equal the donor answer. The probe's READS mark (follow share at least 0.6 times original accuracy) is a new threshold with no reason. evalx.donor_eval (evalx.py lines 93-102) swaps the thinker state, not the prompt examples, so the prompt-level swap is new code.

Forced program and slot map: the OUTPUT PATH gate needs a hand-built gold tensor over 27 workspace slots (progparse.py lines 8-10). A slot-map error would fail the gate for the wrong reason. The executor's DIV is exact-only, so a two-step fewshot program is feasible. The forced program is a diagnostic and must never be reported as the model's capability.
critiques.rescue: Keep the CPU run but change four things first. (1) Run B2 readouts on six seeds (scratchpad/code/b2ckpt, seeds 200 to 205) and label comparator contrasts as two-seed. Anchor the validity gate on the same run's real dev fewshot rows if they can be found; otherwise use the six-seed confirm mean with its interval. (2) Add answer-free self-checks on the model's own prompts: fits-all-pairs (its written program reproduces every example pair) and leave-one-out agreement. Report P(query right given fits all pairs) and P(query right given fits none). This is the one deploy-time signal rule 10 allows, and it must run through an outside text tool (T1) before it counts as deployable, because B2's in-forward executor breaks rule 1. (3) Keep donor, order and query-first as researcher controls only, using the project's donor mark (data.md line 70), a format-matched query-first control, and no undecided ORDER band. (4) Define pair_sum and the B range from the generator's own files before use; split SIGN by sign in the prompt, separately from B's sign; drop NOOP-high as a route condition; state the prompt format per arm. A READS route to traces counts only for trained add and mult, not new kinds. The score of 6 assumes these edits; as written it is closer to 4.

problems: [shown] A third of the fewshot family is answerable without reading any example. own72 fewshot rows (/mnt/project-files/data-pool/built/own72.tgz, skills.jsonl, 46,618 rows): pair_sum is 32.8% of rows (15,312) and its answer equals the sum of the query pair in 15,312 of 15,312; mult is 34.9% (A 2-9); add is 32.2% (B -30..30, 58 distinct values, top share 1.9%). own72 has 159 distinct answers and answer-appears-in-prompt share 0.047, matching data.md line 36 (D159, V.05), so it is probably the same family [suggested: the in-distribution mix is inferred from this match, not read from dev rows].

[shown arithmetic] A no-reading predictor that sums pair rows exactly scores about 37.2% (32.8 + 34.9/8). B2's in-distribution fewshot is 34.58 (six seeds, range 22.5-40.0), at or just under that ceiling; plain_tf_steps at 60.83 is above it. The pooled number cannot separate 'reads nothing' from 'misses some pair rows but reads add/mult rows'. If B2 gets all pair rows right, it reads about 3% of add/mult rows; if it gets 70% of pair rows right, about 17%. Per-variant accuracy (pair, mult, add) must come first.

[shown arithmetic] The pooled donor marks are biased low. If pair rows are answered correctly and do not change under donor swap, donor-follow D = 0.672r and original accuracy O = 0.328 + 0.672r, where r is the add/mult read rate. READS (D >= 0.6 O) then needs r >= 0.73. A tfsteps-like reader (r about 0.42) gives D/O = 0.46 and lands in 'partial', not READS. The donor test is also undefined for pair rows, because the family has one pair rule (a+b) and no in-family donor rule.

[shown] The validity gate cannot detect a no-reading model. 'Within 10 points of 34.6' accepts 24.6 to 44.6, and a no-reading model sits near 37. The screen seeds' B2 in-distribution fewshot values are 37.5 and 30.0 (results/29-b2-screen RESULT.json), so 34.6 is the wrong reference for seeds 100/101. Use the paired B2-minus-tfsteps gap on the same rows, plus per-variant accuracy, as the gate.

[shown] The sign stratum (e) is confounded with rule type. Every minus sign in an own72 fewshot prompt is in an add row (36.9% of add rows); pair and mult rows contain none. 'Minus vs positive' therefore compares add rows with pair and mult rows, so the 20-point mark can pass or fail for rule reasons. The fair comparison is add rows with and without a minus. The idea also merges 'negative B' (16.4% of rows) with 'minus in prompt' (11.9%), which are different strata. The sign loss is real in the exact path: ledger.py spans() (lines 206-208) reads NUM_RE values unsigned. Fewshot answers are GEN (neural), so this stratum may not exercise the executor at all.

[shown] The position stratum (c) is confounded with slot identity. ledger.py line 296 adds a per-slot ordinal embedding to every number slot, so moving the query to the front changes every number's ordinal. A 15-point drop may reflect slot dependence rather than failure to read; routing POSITION-BOUND to a layout arm would misroute.

[shown] Order invariance (b) is inflated by pair rows. A pair answer does not depend on example order, so the ORDER-FREE mark (>= 0.90) is met by a model that reads nothing. Report invariance on add and mult rows only.

[shown] Format mismatch. All 46,618 own72 fewshot rows use spaced arrows and an 'Examples:' label. data.md line 36 gives the in-distribution form as tight ('12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?', no label). ORDER-BOUND ROUTE IS NOT CONDITIONED ON CORRECTNESS (suggested, from the definition). Invariance (answer unchanged after a pair swap) is low for any answerer whose output is noisy, so a near-chance model with invariance at or below 0.70 gets routed to ORDER-BOUND. Compute invariance only on rows where the original answer is correct, and compare with a chance baseline.

DONOR OUTCOME BUCKETS ARE NOT EXCLUSIVE OR EXHAUSTIVE (suggested). 'Keeps original' and 'unchanged' look like the same outcome. 'Copies an example output' can coincide with 'follows donor'. There is no 'other' bucket. Define one ordered assignment (donor answer, then original answer, then example-output copy, else other) and report the other bucket.

RELATIVE THRESHOLDS LOSE MEANING AT LOW ACCURACY (suggested). READS needs donor-follow of at least 0.6 times original accuracy, and IGNORES needs at most 0.2 times. At 15% original accuracy, READS passes with a follow rate of about 9% (about 36 of 400 rows), which is not separated from noise without a chance baseline. Use absolute follow shares measured against a chance rate for a fixed-output control.

POSITION READOUT IS CONFOUNDED BY FORMAT NOVELTY (suggested). Every shown example puts the query last: 'Now q -> ?' in research/data.md line 36 and in the own72 fewshot rows. A query-first layout is never trained, so a drop of 15 points or more is expected from any format-brittle model and does not show position-bound reading. Add a control that keeps the query last, for example the same examples with a neutral re-wording.

SIGN ROUTE MIXES TWO FAILURE PATHS (shown in code, interpretation suggested). progparse.py:14 defines NUM_RE as \d+, and ledger.py:206-208 uses the same regex to build the number slots and the executor values, so a minus sign never reaches the value path. The reader is character-level and the controller cross-attends to all reader positions, so it can still see '-'. The SIGN cell therefore mixes a value-slot loss with a reader misreading. The route 'SIGN -> signed numbers' needs a control that separates the two.

READOUTS WITHOUT MARKS OR ROUTES (shown in the proposal text). Readouts (d) k=1/2/3, (h) the build-cost ladder, (i) the loops:0 control, and the plain comparators have no pass mark and feed no route. 'ORDER or POSITION-BOUND -> layout arm' does not follow: order-bound reading is not a layout fault, and the orchestrator's own check caps the layout share of the variant miss at 28%.

The proposal's 'closest prior' says no file covers these rows, which is wrong for lesions. Use them as baselines. Prompt-level example swaps, pair order, query-first and sign on fewshot rows are still new.

ROUTE TO TRACES CONFLICTS WITH THE BENCH WARNING (shown). BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114, 'Warning for B2's next step', says the pointer-program version of this idea flat-lined at 77/160 on fewshot across five designs. chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed test, but only in a cut-down, staged form. Cost is low: CPU only, no training, about 0.5 h of compute; the real cost is writing the scripts, about 3-6 h (critic estimate, untested). It breaks no rule: the hand-built rows and the scorer are tests (rules 1 and 5 allow them), B2 is unchanged, no teacher is used, and nothing is added to the deployed model, so rule 10 is not touched. It is the right first step for the area because no file says why B2 trails on fewshot_number_rule (in_dist 34.6 vs 60.8 for plain_tf_steps; shown: CIO/results/33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json, negative on 6 of 6 seeds).

Two things I checked in the files change the design.

1. A model that reads nothing could score almost exactly what B2 scores. The own72 fewshot rows are about one third pair_sum (15,312 of 46,618, from a critic's count that I did not re-run), and a pair_sum answer is the sum of the query pair, so it needs no example reading (suggested). If B2 gets every pair row right and add/mult at chance, it scores about 33 + 2 = 35, against its 34.6. plain_tf_steps at 60.8 would then read add/mult at about 42%. This is untested. It makes accuracy by variant (pair, mult, add) the decisive first readout. It also means the idea's pooled donor mark is biased low: a reader as good as plain_tf_steps would score about 0.46 of original accuracy, which is below the 0.6 READS line. As written, the idea cannot pass its own READS mark.

2. Existing lesions already answer part of the question (shown: results/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 and B2_s101 RESULT.json, fewshot in_dist cells of 40 rows).
   - loops:0 is 0/40 on both seeds, and loops:1 is 1 and 2 of 40.
   - noexec is unchanged: 15/40 and 12/40, equal to intact.
   - The thinker-state donor lesion gives exact 0.0 and donor_match 22.5 and 20.0.
   So fewshot answers come from the thinker's rounds and are written by the neural GEN path. The executor is not used on this family. The forced hand-solved program (readout f) and the build-cost ladder (readout h) therefore test a path the model does not use on fewshot, so they come out of the first pass. The loops:0 control (readout i) is already measured.

Other points the critics raised that hold and are folded into the plan below:
- 34.6 is the wrong gate reference for seeds 100 and 101. Their real cells are 15/40 and 12/40, with a standard error of about 7.5 points on a 40-row cell.
- Six B2 checkpoints (seeds 200-205) are available in the scratchpad with sha256 files. Rule 4 therefore says B2-only readouts should run on six seeds. The plain comparators exist only for seeds 100 and 101, so they stay a 2-seed screen.
- Sign: ledger.py reads numbers with NUM_RE = \d+, so a minus sign never reaches the workspace. That is a known defect, and planned item 2c1 replaces the regex with a learned digit reader. The sign stratum confirms a known defect and should not route anything. It is capped at about 11.9 points of in_dist if the sk200k mix matches own72, which is untested.
- In own72, every prompt with a minus sign is an add row. A sign comparison must therefore be add rows with and without a minus, matched by magnitude.
- Moving the query to the front is confounded by format novelty and by the per-slot ordinal embedding (ledger.py line 296). Report it as slot-order dependence with a query-last reworded control, not as proof of a position fault.
- BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114 is headed 'Warning for B2's next step'. It is addressed to B2, but its evidence is from the bench planner (pointer programs flat at 77/160 on four families across five designs). The idea's 'different model' wording is wrong. Any later route to traces has to cite it.
- This probe measures example-reading inside a family B2 was trained on. It says nothing directly about brand-new kinds (0-4%). Fewshot is 160 of 6,040 pooled-5 rows, so perfect fewshot would add only about +2.05 pooled-5. The value is as a routing tool for Ben's learn-from-examples goal, not as a score mover.
chair.revised_idea:
Same idea, run in stages so the cheap decisive readout comes first. No model change. It is a CPU forward-only probe with hand-written rows and scorer. Label every verdict "example values reach the thinker through B2's hand regex NUM_RE (ledger.py:206), so READS means the thinker's pointers use hand-parsed values, not that B2 learned to read." A READS result on this model is not evidence that a learned reader works (planned item 2c1).

SEEDS AND COMPARATORS
- B2-only readouts run on six seeds, 200-205, from the scratchpad copies (branch claude/b2-confirm-checkpoints f41d0f7d5, sha256 checked).
- B2 seeds 100 and 101 plus plain_tf and plain_tf_steps seeds 100 and 101 (checkpoints/20-screen-s100-w1 and 22-screen-s101-w1) are a labelled 2-seed screen. The comparators only answer 'does a plain transformer follow the donor?'.

ROWS
- One format for all marks: the tight sk200k format '12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?' (data.md line 36).
- The own72 'Examples: a -> b; ... Now q -> ?' wrapper is a separate descriptive frame check with no marks.
- Equal thirds of mult (A 2-9), add (B -30..30) and pair_sum, with 2 or 3 pairs. This is the own72 mix. Whether sk200k, B2's real training data, has the same mix is untested, so the first step on the PC is to read the real in_dist fewshot dev rows and compare their mix.
- 400 rows per stratum per seed, prompts under 208 characters, unique row ids.
- Reject rows where a mult-or-add rival rule that also fits the examples gives a different query answer. At 2-3 pairs this should remove nearly all ambiguity (a scout's unsaved simulation says about 0% at 2 pairs; untested).
- One pair count of 1 is reported descriptively only, because training holds 2 or 3 pairs.

STAGE 0, VALIDITY GATE
- Pooled accuracy on the hand-built equal-thirds rows must be within 10 points of the same checkpoint's real in_dist fewshot accuracy. For seeds 200-205 that is 83/240 = 34.6 pooled, with a standard error of about 3. For seeds 100 and 101 the real cells are 15/40 and 12/40, so report only.
- Also score the real dev fewshot rows on the PC in the same run.
- Report the gate before anything else. If it fails, nothing is routed.

STAGE 1, THE DECISIVE READOUT
- Accuracy by variant: pair rows (the no-reading prior stratum), mult rows, add rows.
- Prompt-level donor swap on add and mult rows only. Keep x1, x2 and the query. Replace the example outputs with those of a different constant of the same variant, with the donor answer pinned different from the original answer. Drop rows where the donor answer equals an example output or a prompt number.
- Bucket each output once, in order: donor answer, original answer, copies an example output, other.
- Chance correction: d_corr = donor-follow share on the swapped prompts minus the share of the unswapped prompts whose output equals the donor-answer string.
- Descriptive: share of rounds where the op head writes NOOP in a free run, with no teacher forcing. This is what training taught (gold NOOP at w_noop 0.1), so it can only surprise by being low.

STAGE 2, ONLY IF add/mult accuracy r is 20% or more
- Pair-order swap, scored on rows whose original answer is correct. The invariance baseline must be computed on add and mult only, because pair_sum is order-free.
- Query-first with a query-last reworded control (position or slot-order dependence, not 'reading').
- Add rows with vs without a minus sign, matched by magnitude.
- Digit-error type among wrong answers: right length, right units digit. Compare with chance (about 10% for a units digit) and with plain_tf.

STAGE 3, OPTIONAL, NOT BLOCKING
A forced hand-solved program through Ledger.run(gold=...), only if a later traces test needs it. Rules for it:
- Build the op, operand and mode tensors directly, assert each program is non-empty (Ledger.gold() silently turns unparsed fewshot steps into NOOP), and use unique ids.
- Run on non-negative-output rows only, and force and report the NUM vs GEN mode.
- Report minus-sign rows separately with no mark.

DROPPED
- Readout (h) the build-cost ladder.
- Readout (i) the loops:0 control (already 0/40).
- The k=1 mark.

PREDICTION TABLE, WRITTEN BEFORE RUNNING
- Pair accuracy 80% or more.
- Add/mult accuracy 15% or less.
- Donor-follow d_corr under 5 points.
- NOOP share 90% or more.
- Hand-built equal-thirds mix 28-40%.
chair.plan_guidance:
The test plan must get these right (labels: shown / suggested / untested).

1. State the no-reading ceiling first. Pair_sum is about one third of own72 fewshot rows and needs no example reading (suggested; from a critic's count). The ceiling is about 33-37%, against B2's 34.6 (shown) and plain_tf_steps' 60.8 (shown). Report accuracy per variant (pair, mult, add) before anything else. Pooled marks are biased low and cannot tell 'reads nothing' from 'reads some add/mult rows'.

2. The unit of reading is the add/mult rows. All donor, order, position and sign marks apply to add and mult rows only. Pair rows are the prior stratum, reported separately. No donor test exists for pair_sum, because the family has a single pair rule.

3. Fix these marks before running. Read them on six B2 seeds (200-205), with at least 5 of 6 seeds required.
- Gate: hand-built equal-thirds accuracy within 10 points of the same checkpoint's real in_dist fewshot accuracy (34.6 pooled over seeds 200-205). The gate is reported first. A failed gate means no routing.
- READS: add/mult accuracy r is 40% or more (the level plain_tf_steps needs if it gets pair rows right) AND chance-corrected donor-follow d_corr is at least 0.6 r.
- IGNORES: r is 15% or less AND d_corr is 5 points or less.
- PARTIAL: anything else. Do not route. Go to the Stage 2 split by number size, pair count and sign.
- PAIR-LOW: pair accuracy under 60%. Part of the gap is then not about add/mult reading, and that is reported as its own finding.
- Use absolute thresholds on d_corr, not a ratio to original accuracy alone, because the ratio is meaningless at low accuracy.

4. Define one ordered outcome bucket for the donor test: donor answer, then original answer, then copies an example output, then other. Pin the donor constant to differ from the original and the donor answer to differ from the original answer and from every example output and prompt number.

5. Order invariance counts only rows whose original answer is correct. It is computed on add and mult, never pooled with pair rows.

6. Position is reported as slot-order dependence, with a query-last reworded control. Do not map it to a layout fault. The orchestrator's own check caps the layout share of the variant miss at 28% (suggested).

7. Sign is descriptive. It is a known regex defect (ledger.py:206 and planned 2c1), capped at about 11.9 in_dist points if sk200k matches own72 (untested), so it routes nothing. Compare add rows with and without a minus, matched by magnitude.

8. Routing, with no unmapped outcome and no route that contradicts a shown fact:
- IGNORES with pair OK: the in_dist gap is a reading failure on add/mult. Pick ONE sealed change from the reading-teaching set (worked traces written as text tool calls so they carry over to the T1 design; episode-shuffled training from the existing rows; the C2 read-the-example-pairs change). The probe does not choose among them. Any traces route must cite BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114 and must leave the minus-sign rows (about 11.9%) answer-only, which rule 7 forbids, so that gap has to be closed first.
- READS: the gap is not example reading. Run Stage 2 digit-error and sign splits, then look at the digit-writing path.
- PARTIAL: Stage 2 only.
- PAIR-LOW: separate look at the pair rows first.
- Gate fails: no routing, fix the generator.

9. Keep the claims honest.
- Say in every verdict that example values enter through the hand regex.
- Seeds 100 and 101 comparators are a 2-seed screen. They can only show that plain transformers follow or ignore the donor, not support a B2-vs-plain claim.
- The probe measures a trained family, not brand-new kinds (0-4%).
- Keep the B2 claims separate from the sandwich and village models (rule 9).

10. Rule 5: build rows by hand from the generator rules. Copy no own72 row, because own72 has not been cleared against GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind hashes (a critic read DATA-POOL-PLAN; I did not re-check). Use the own72 wrapper only as a descriptive frame, not as the gate.

11. Report the existing lesion cells as baselines (shown: 29-b2-screen B2_s100 and B2_s101 RESULT.json): loops:0 0/40, noexec equal to intact (15/40 and 12/40), thinker-state donor exact 0.0. State what the new prompt-level swap adds beyond them: it swaps the examples, not the thinker state (evalx.donor_eval, shown).

12. Budget honestly: about 0.5 h of CPU compute plus roughly 3-6 h of scripting (critic estimate, untested). A deployable answer-free fit-check (does the model's own written program reproduce every example pair?) is a separate idea. B2 writes no program on fewshot, so it cannot be part of this probe, and the lead should rank it separately.

plan.title: B2 few-shot: does it use the example outputs? (CPU donor-swap probe)
plan.ben_line: We want to know whether the model looks at the example answers when it is shown a few examples and asked for the rule, or ignores them and guesses. We test this by changing only the example answers to another rule's answers, then checking whether the model's answer changes the way that rule says it should.
plan.question: Does B2 (3,302,481 params) use the example outputs in its own few-shot prompts, or does it answer from the query alone? Measured by a CPU donor-swap probe on hand-built add and mult prompts. No training and no model change.
plan.one_change: No model change. One manipulation: in each hand-built add or mult prompt, the example outputs are replaced by the outputs of a donor constant, while the example inputs, the query and the format stay the same. Every other readout (accuracy, pair order, query first, sign, NOOP share) measures unchanged or existing prompts.
arms: B2, seeds 200-205 (primary, six paired seeds): unmodified and donor-swapped hand rows. Scratch copies at scratchpad/code/b2ckpt/B2_s200 to B2_s205 (checkpoint.pt 13,243,510 bytes; sha256 files present, shown by listing).
B2, seeds 100-101 (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/B2_s100 and B2_s101): cross-check of the screen run. Descriptive, two seeds.

plain_tf, seeds 100-101 (20-screen-s100-w1/tf_s100 and 22-screen-s101-w1/tf_s101): positive control for donor sensitivity (gate V4). Descriptive. Confirm-seed plain checkpoints are not on disk (shown: only RESULT.json in results/33-pc-confirm-b2).

plain_tf_steps, seeds 100-101 (tfsteps_s100 and tfsteps_s101 in the same checkpoint folders): comparator for gate V3 only. Descriptive. Sizes: B2 3,302,481; plain_tf 3,244,544 (-1.7%); plain_tf_steps 3,260,928 (-1.2%); shown in RESULT.json n_params.
plan.seeds: Primary: B2 seeds 200-205, six paired seeds. A verdict counts only if it holds on at least 5 of 6 seeds and on the pooled six. Controls and comparators: seeds 100-101 only, labelled as a screen and descriptive. One fixed hand-row set, generated and hashed before any run, is scored by every arm.
plan.machine: Ben's M1 Pro (CPU) or the RTX 5070 Ti PC's CPU, after torch is installed there. Forward passes only: no GPU, no rented GPU, no training. Torch is not installed in this sandbox, so nothing here was run. Numbers below were read from files or counted from the own72 archive (counts only).
pass_marks: GATE V1, mix and format (before any readout): hand-built shares of pair, add and mult each within 5 points of the real in_dist fewshot dev rows read on the PC in step 1; identical separators and wrapper in every hand row. Fail: rebuild, no readout.

GATE V2, accuracy (same run): pooled over seeds 200-205, B2 accuracy on unmodified hand rows within 10 points of its real in_dist fewshot accuracy measured on the same machine in the same run. The saved confirm RESULT.json gives 83 of 240 = 34.6 (shown); re-measure it on the PC. Fail: no routing.

GATE V3, sign (screen seeds): on the hand rows, B2 minus plain_tf_steps fewshot accuracy is negative on seeds 100 and 101, as on the real rows (shown: B2 15 vs tfsteps 21 of 40 on seed 100, and 12 vs 18 of 40 on seed 101; each -15 points). Fail: rebuild.

GATE V4, sensitivity (positive control): plain_tf on the same hand rows, seeds 100-101, shows donor-follow d_corr of 20 points or more on add and mult. Its real in_dist fewshot is 62.9 pooled (shown), so it must read some rows (suggested arithmetic). Fail: the donor test is blind on these rows; make no B2 verdict.

Definitions on the marked stratum (add and mult rows with no minus sign in the prompt; pair rows reported separately): r = add-plus-mult accuracy on unmodified rows, in percent. d_corr = share of donor-swapped answers equal to the donor answer, minus the share of unswapped answers equal to the donor answer, in points. p = pair accuracy, in percent.

Stage 1 verdicts: READS if d_corr >= 20 and d_corr >= 0.6 x r. IGNORES if d_corr <= 5 and r <= 15. PRIOR if d_corr <= 5 and r > 15. PARTIAL otherwise (tag WRONG-FOLLOW when r <= 15 and d_corr > 5). A verdict counts only if it holds on at least 5 of 6 seeds.
Flag PAIR-LOW if p < 60. It is reported as its own finding, not as a reading result.

Predictions written before running: p >= 80; r <= 15; d_corr < 5; free-run NOOP share >= 90 (descriptive); verdict IGNORES. Arithmetic (own72 mix, shown from counts): 34.6 = 0.328 p + 0.672 r, so p = 0.9 implies r of about 7.5. If step 1 finds no pair rows in the real mix, the arithmetic changes: 34.6 would mean r near 35 with no pair prior, and the predicted verdict becomes READS or PARTIAL. Write whichever applies before the run. If a run that passes V1 and V2 gives r of 25 or more at p of 0.9 or more, the hand rows do not match the real mix: treat as a gate failure.

Stage 2, only if r >= 20: order invariance on correct add and mult rows (0.90 or more = order-free; 0.70 or less = order-bound; between = undecided, reported). Query-first accuracy drop more than 10 points beyond a query-last reworded control = position-bound (slot-order dependence, not a layout fault). Sign gap of 20 points or more between minus and matched no-minus add rows = sign-bound (descriptive only). Digit-level if at least 50 percent of wrong marked answers have the right length and units digit (chance for the units digit about 10 percent, suggested).

Routing: IGNORES leads to one reading-teaching change, sealed in its own plan (this probe does not choose it). READS leads to the Stage 2 digit and sign checks, then the digit-writing path. PRIOR leads to a query-only lesion (remove the examples; unchanged answers mean the answers come from the query). WRONG-FOLLOW leads to the digit-level path. PARTIAL runs the six-seed Stage 2 before any route. PAIR-LOW leads to a look at the pair rows first.
plan.proved_wrong: The IGNORES route is wrong if d_corr exceeds 5 points on at least 5 of 6 seeds, because then B2's answers do move with the example outputs. The READS route is wrong if d_corr is below 20 points, or below 0.6 times r, on at least 5 of 6 seeds. The probe itself is wrong, and makes no B2 verdict, if V4 fails: plain_tf does not move with its donor, so the test cannot see reading on these rows. The pair-share explanation of the 34.6 is wrong if r reaches 25 or more at p of 0.9 or more on rows that pass V1 and V2. Scope: a passing IGNORES result would say B2 does not use example outputs in this format and this mix. It would not show that B2 cannot learn a rule from examples in any format.
plan.null_risk: Medium, highest for IGNORES. Three ways to get IGNORES with no real change in B2. (1) Format: a hand row can break a reading that the real rows allow. Gate V2 cannot catch this, because B2's real score (34.6) already sits near the no-reading ceiling of about 37 under the own72 mix (shown from counts; the 1-in-8 guess on mult is suggested), so a broken format and a non-reader look alike on accuracy. V1 (mix and format) and V4 (a positive control that does read these rows) are the guards. (2) Mix: the marked stratum drops minus-sign rows (shown: 36.9 percent of own72 add prompts contain a minus), so the verdict covers only the non-negative subset. (3) Sample: 800 marked add and mult rows per seed gives a standard error under 2 points at any level (computed), so row noise is small and the real risk is seed-to-seed variation, which is why the rule is 5 of 6 seeds. READS is hard to fake, because it needs answers that change to the donor's constant. The collision baseline removes chance hits on the donor string.
plan.autonomy: Nothing is added to the deployed model. This probe is a research-side measurement: the hand rows, donor swaps, gates, marks and routing are researcher steps, which rules 1 and 10 allow only as tests. The question it asks is about the deployed forward pass: does the model use the examples in its own prompt, with no researcher step at deploy time. The marks are fixed research values, not runtime thresholds, so the tuned-threshold clause of rule 10 does not apply. Two caveats, not fixed here. (a) B2's deployed path still runs hand code between question and answer: the regex number reader (progparse.py:14, prompt_numbers at 17-18; ledger.py:198-212 and 286-300, where the number slot is the value code plus pooled reader features). That breaks rule 1 as the brief defines it, so a READS or IGNORES verdict describes this hand-parsed path, not a learned reader (planned item 2c1). (b) Any later reading-teaching change must add no deploy-time step; training before shipping is allowed. The answer-free fits-all-pairs check is a separate idea. B2 writes no program on fewshot, so this probe cannot test it.
steps: PC or M1, before any model run (torch installed there): read the real in_dist fewshot dev rows (dev only; not labelled, test or blind). Count pair, add and mult shares, the separator and wrapper, k (2 or 3), the share with a minus sign, and the longest prompt. Re-measure the real in_dist fewshot count per seed for B2 seeds 200-205 on this machine. The confirm RESULT.json reads 15, 16, 15, 16, 9, 12 of 40 (shown); the same seed can leak differently by machine (per the brief), so re-measure rather than reuse.

Write a hand-written row builder from the rules in the sk200k format (data.md line 36: '12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?', answer 40, mult) and the own72 rule ranges (mult A 2-9; add B -30 to 30 with the marked stratum at 1-30; pair sums only if step 1 finds pair rows). Use k = 2 or 3 in equal shares, prompts under 208 characters, answers of at most 8 characters, unique ids. Copy no own72 or dev row (rule 5). Use pair rows in whatever format step 1 finds; if none exist in the real mix, drop them and say so.

Generate ONE fixed row set with a fixed generator seed: about 400 add and 400 mult marked rows, about 200 minus-sign add rows (a separate descriptive stratum), and pair rows only if step 1 finds them. Build the donor pairs (donor constant different from the original; donor answer different from the original answer, from every prompt number and from every example output; donor example outputs not equal to any other prompt number; drop failing rows at build time and report the count). Build the Stage 2 variants (first two examples swapped; query first; query last reworded as the control). Hash the row file and write the prediction table to disk before any model is run. Do not edit the row set after seeing results.

Gates, same machine and same run: score the unmodified hand rows and the real dev fewshot rows for B2 seeds 200-205; score the unmodified rows for plain_tf_steps and plain_tf on seeds 100-101. Check V1 (mix and format), V2 (pooled accuracy within 10 points), V3 (B2 minus tfsteps negative on seeds 100 and 101), then V4 (plain_tf donor d_corr at least 20 on add and mult). If V1, V2 or V3 fails, stop and rebuild. If V4 fails, make no B2 verdict.

Stage 1 readouts on B2 seeds 200-205: score unmodified and donor-swapped rows through evalx.evaluate with return_preds=True (evalx.py:37, which returns per-row predictions by id). Bucket each swapped answer once, in order: equals donor answer; equals original answer; equals one of the swapped example outputs; other. Compute r, p, d_corr (with the collision share from unswapped answers), and the free-run NOOP share from the op head through Ledger.run (descriptive). Save every per-row output as JSON; the bench recipe (BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114) asks for per-row outputs before any program-route design.

Apply the Stage 1 verdict rules to the per-seed and pooled numbers. A verdict counts only if it holds on at least 5 of 6 seeds. Record the verdict next to the prediction written in step 3. Flag PAIR-LOW separately.

Stage 2 only if r >= 20 (any verdict): order invariance on correct add and mult rows; query-first against the query-last reworded control; sign split matched by magnitude (descriptive); digit-error type among wrong marked answers. Apply the Stage 2 marks in pass_marks. Only the marked stratum enters any mark.

Report. Label every claim shown, suggested or untested, with the file or count it comes from. In every verdict, state that example values reach the thinker in two ways: the hand-parsed number value (progparse NUM_RE, ledger.py:206 and the value code at 289-293) and pooled reader features in the same workspace slot (ledger.py:289-293). So READS or IGNORES describes this path, not a learned reader. Keep B2 claims separate from the sandwich and village models (rule 9).

Optional, not blocking: a forced hand-solved program through Ledger.run(gold=...) only if a later traces test needs it. Build the op and operand tensors directly, assert each program is non-empty (a critic's code read says an unparsed step turns into NOOP inside gold() without an error; untested here), run only non-negative rows, and report minus-sign rows separately with no mark.

Scope of changes: no edit to models/, train.py or data.py. Only one new probe file and one new output folder, written in the owning thread's writable checkout (the scratchpad copy is read-only). Checkpoints are read-only.

fixed_plan.ben_line: We check whether the model reads the example answers it is shown, by swapping only those answers in real practice questions and seeing whether its answer changes. Nothing is trained, and the result tells us what to test next, not that the model is finished.
fixed_plan.question: Does B2 use the example outputs in its in_dist fewshot prompts, on the regex-parsed path that exists today?
fixed_plan.one_change: One manipulation: replace the example output digits of real in_dist fewshot dev prompts with a donor constant's outputs (non-negative, not a prompt number). Inputs, query, wrapper and number positions stay the same.
arms: B2 seeds 200-205 on the PC: unmodified vs donor-substituted real rows (primary).
plain_tf (text reader) on the same rows: seeds 200-205 if the PC holds them, else 100-101 (positive control, GATE 4).
B2 seeds 100-101 cross-check, and a k = 1, 2, 3 example-count curve (descriptive, confounded by slot shift).
fixed_plan.seeds: Primary six paired seeds 200-205. A verdict needs 5 of 6 seeds and the pooled six. Seeds 100-101 are descriptive.
fixed_plan.machine: Ben's PC or M1, CPU forward passes after torch is installed. No GPU, no training, no rented GPU. Check PC checkpoint sha256 against the scratch sha files first.
pass_marks: GATE 1 format, before any readout: per row, substituted and unmodified prompts differ only in example output digits; donor outputs non-negative and not a prompt number. Count and drop failures. Fail: rebuild.
GATE 2 counts: unmodified B2 fewshot in_dist correct per seed within 2 rows of 15,16,15,16,9,12 of 40 (shown). Fail: machine or checkpoint differs; stop.
GATE 3 sign, screen seeds 100-101: B2 minus tfsteps negative on both (shown: 15 vs 21 and 12 vs 18 of 40). Fail: rebuild.
GATE 4 sensitivity: plain_tf donor-follow d_corr >= 20 on add and mult in the same rows. Fail: no B2 verdict.

Verdicts as in the plan: READS if d_corr >= 20 and >= 0.6 r; IGNORES if d_corr <= 5 and r <= 15; PRIOR if d_corr <= 5 and r > 15; else PARTIAL or WRONG-FOLLOW. Stage 2 only if r >= 20 for any verdict. PARTIAL and WRONG-FOLLOW with r < 20 rerun on 200-per-cell rows.
No prediction is written until step 1 reports the real fewshot mix. own72 is not used for the mix.
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: IGNORES is wrong if d_corr > 5 on at least 5 of 6 seeds. READS is wrong if d_corr < 20 on at least 5 of 6 seeds. No verdict if GATE 2 or GATE 4 fails. Any verdict describes the regex-parsed number path, not a learned reader or a shippable design.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Medium. Real-row substitution removes most format risk. Remaining: the no-minus stratum may cover only part of real rows; 40-row cells are noisy (about 7 points per seed) unless the 200-per-cell rebuild is used; a changed digit may move the NUM pointer to another slot (collision check needed).
fixed_plan.autonomy: Research-side measurement. The deployed model is unchanged and no deploy-time step is added. Verdict routing is a research step. Rule 1 is already broken on this path by the hand regex (progparse.py:17-18), so no verdict here approves it. A later change must remove the regex (roadmap 2c1) or be labelled a test.
steps: Step 1, PC: install torch and check the six checkpoints' sha256. Re-score the real in_dist fewshot rows for seeds 200-205 (GATE 2). Report the real mix: add, mult, any pair class defined from the rows, sign share, k, separators. Do not read own72 for the mix.
Step 2: build substituted rows from the real rows (200-per-cell rebuild if available). Save the row file, its SHA-256 and the prediction table before any readout.

Step 3: score unmodified and substituted rows with evalx.evaluate(return_preds=True). Bucket each swapped answer as donor, original, swapped example output, or other. Compute r, p, d_corr with the collision share. Score plain_tf on the same rows for GATE 4.
Step 4: apply GATES 1-4 and the verdict rules. Run Stage 2 only if r >= 20.
Step 5: descriptive k = 1, 2, 3 curve on seeds 200-205, labelled confounded.
Step 6: report with shown, suggested and untested labels, the scope line, and a plain-language summary for Ben. Keep B2 claims separate from the sandwich and village models.

final.why: Run the fixed (real-row) version. It uses no GPU hours and no training, only CPU forward passes plus about 3-6 h of scripting (critic estimate, untested). It breaks none of Ben's rules: the rows and scorer are tests, B2 is unchanged, and no deploy-time step is added. It is the cheapest way to split the fewshot gap (B2 34.6 vs plain_tf_steps 60.8 in_dist, negative on 6 of 6 seeds; shown, CONFIRM RESULT.json) into 'ignores the examples' versus 'reads them but fails elsewhere'. Existing lesions already point to the answer path (shown, 29-b2-screen RESULT.json fewshot in_dist, 40 rows): loops:0 is 0/40 on both seeds, noexec equals intact (15/40 and 12/40), nowordc equals intact, and the thinker-state donor gives exact 0.0. The new prompt-level example swap adds what those cannot, namely whether the examples' values move the answer. The score stops at 6 because the likely outcome is IGNORES (a prediction; untested). Fewshot is only 160 of 6,040 pooled-5 rows, about +2 points at most. The probe covers a trained family, not the 0-4% brand-new kinds, and it tests the 8-round B2 with its hand regex number reader, while T1 and the 8a rung are moving the design. The harness can be reused on later checkpoints as the examples-needed ruler, which is its main lasting value.
final.ben_line: We will change only the example answers in practice questions the model already knows, then see whether its answer changes to match; if it does not, the model is ignoring the examples and we know what to fix first.
plan_fixes: Sample size is the biggest hole. Real in_dist fewshot dev is 40 rows, and the same 40 rows are scored by every seed, so the six seeds replicate training luck, not row sampling. After dropping pair rows and minus-sign rows, perhaps 15-20 add/mult rows remain (untested), and one row is about 5-7 points. The IGNORES line (d_corr <= 5) then means 'at most one row'. Require at least 200 marked add/mult rows (use the 200-per-cell rebuild in local_runner.py if the generator is on the PC; otherwise hand-build rows and validate their format against the real 40 rows). Make no verdict below that count, and say that '5 of 6 seeds' only covers training seeds.

Add a rival-rule filter on both unmodified and swapped prompts. Drop any row where another add/mult rule that also fits the (swapped) examples gives a different query answer, so the donor answer is the only consistent reading. The fixed plan only pins the donor answer away from the original and the examples. Also require donor example outputs to be non-negative and under 8 chars, since the digit regex drops minus signs (progparse.py:14, 17-18).

Pair class is undefined in data.md and data.py. Step 1 must define pair_sum (and any other fewshot variant, e.g. affine, which is variant-split only) by fitting rules to the real rows, and report the real mix before any threshold is read. The 'about one third pair' ceiling came from own72, which is not B2's training pool and is not cleared against protected-panel hashes, so do not use own72 for the mix or the prediction table.

Gate 3 (B2 minus tfsteps negative on seeds 100 and 101) just re-reads already-shown cells (15 vs 21 and 12 vs 18 of 40) and adds nothing; drop it. Gate 2 should also record fp32-CPU versus the original bf16/GPU differences, and state the pass rule (within 2 rows) up front so a small drift does not look like a gate failure.

Gate 4's plain_tf positive control exists only for seeds 100-101 (confirm-seed plain checkpoints are not on disk). Use the same-seed real cells (plain_tf 26/40 and 27/40, shown) as the reference, with the same row-count floor. State the fallback: if plain_tf's d_corr is under 20, say the instrument is blind and drop the B2 verdict. Do not make a B2-versus-plain claim from 2 seeds.

Pre-commit the routing before running. IGNORES currently routes to 'one reading-teaching change' that is not named, so the probe decides nothing. Name the one candidate and its precondition now. Any traces route must cite BENCH-RECIPE.md line 114 (pointer programs flat across five designs on fewshot_number_rule) and the minus-sign rows (about 11.9 percent if sk200k matches own72; untested), which rule 7 forbids leaving answer-only. READS or PARTIAL routes need the same one-line pre-commitment.

Stage rules still conflict. 'Stage 2 only if r >= 20' versus 'PARTIAL and WRONG-FOLLOW with r < 20 rerun on 200-per-cell rows'. WRONG-FOLLOW is defined with r <= 15 but routes to a Stage 2 digit-level check. Pick one rule: Stage 2 runs when r >= 20, otherwise only the larger-sample rerun.

Query-first and the k = 1, 2, 3 curve are confounded by the per-slot ordinal embedding (ledger.py line 296) and by training only 2 or 3 pairs. Report them as descriptive slot-order and example-count dependence, with a query-last reworded control, and never as a layout fault or a few-shot result.

Write the harness model-agnostic (anything evalx.evaluate can score) and label it as the examples-needed ruler, so it can be rerun on the 8a 3M rung (12 rounds, 106 slots), T1 and B3 checkpoints. The current verdict covers only the 8-round 16-number B2 and its hand regex number reader (progparse NUM_RE, ledger.py:206). Put the line 'example values reach the thinker through hand-parsed numbers, so READS is not evidence of a learned reader' in every verdict.

Check for collisions in the substituted rows. A changed digit can shift the NUM pointer to another workspace slot (a pointer collision), so log the answer mode (NUM, WORD or GEN) per row alongside the donor bucket. Save every per-row output as JSON, since no run has saved per-row B2 predictions so far. Run a sha256 check on the PC copies of the checkpoints before scoring.

idea.title: Probe T1's copy break with letter replies instead of digits
idea.summary: T1 (calculator outside the model) ran on two rented 5090s and was NOT SHOWN: pooled-5 and chain-5 passed, but exact copy of a calculator result into the next call or the answer drops from 96-98% at 1-3 digits to 59%, 1% and 0% at 4, 5 and 6-9 digits. Every tool idea waits on this. Reuse the write-copy harness on the two saved T1 checkpoints with random letter strings of 1-8 letters, which separates 'digit place rows never trained' from 'copy attention is length-bound' in minutes on CPU.
idea.change: No weight change. In tool.py swap the write_copy oracle (tool.py lines 449-482, rand_digits at 452-453) for a letter oracle: lowercase, 1-8 letters, balanced across lengths, fixed per row and round; keep the digit oracle on the same checkpoints as a paired control. Report answer copy at every length 1-8 and operand copy by length 1-10 (the cell path) as a separate line. Use every dev row whose intact answer is a call result, not a 3,000-prompt subsample, so each length has n >= 300. Checkpoints: /mnt/project-files/checkpoints/cio-1007/40b-t1-s200/T1_s200/checkpoint.pt (13,139,957 bytes, verified present) and the seed 201 copy; T1 code at commit 2b1cbd4d7.
idea.why: Shown: S3 write_copy exact copy by digit length (seed 200): operand 86/93/85/14/1/0% and answer 96/98/98/59/1/0% at 1/2/3/4/5/6-9 digits, and training results are 1-3 digits in 99.6% of operands. The thread's reading (place rows 4+ almost never trained) is suggested and untested. Letters travel through the same copy path in the model, but words of any length are heavily trained in the reader, so if letters copy at 4-8 the break lives in the digit place rows and word-valued tool replies can be built now; if they fail, the break is length and span copy must cover words too.

problems: [shown] The n >= 300 per length mark cannot be met on the data the probe names. write_copy reads only dev/in_dist.jsonl (tool.py line 345), which has 1,360 rows (research/data.md section 0). The idea says it avoids a 3,000-prompt subsample, but subsample(prows, 3000) already returns every program row (tool.py line 454; evalx.subsample returns the full list when k >= len). The answer copy trial takes at most one result per row and draws its length uniformly, so with 8 lengths there are at most 1,360 / 8 = 170 answer trials per length before the intact-answer and path filters. The idea never says how to add trials (replication or an enlarged dev).

[shown] The pass mark is vacuous when n is small. The idea says a cell with fewer than 300 rows is 'reported, not judged'. A run where every answer cell is under 300 has no judged cell, so it has no pass and no fail. The mark needs a fixed floor or a fixed number of independent prompts per cell, set before the run.

[shown] The pass mark tests the answer path only (answer copy >= 99%). The S3 break is on both operand and answer (T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md lines 13, 25-26), and the sealed R1 mark requires both at each length (MARKS-D0-T1-2026-10-07.md Amendment 3, line 77). The answer path is also partly predicted by existing B2 evidence: GEN spells letters from the prompt (cipher_map 97 pooled, /mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/INPUT-UNITS-2026-10-07.md line 40; PASS-MARKS.md addendum 6 says the talker spells with its letter table). A pass on the answer path alone would not show that the operand writer can copy letters.

[shown] Letters are out of distribution for the writer, so the length reading is confounded. Writer gold operands are str() of integer workspace values (tool.py row_gold, lines 233-250; cell_ids 251-253; gold 255-273), and operands are 1-3 digits in 99.6% of training (T1-SCREEN line 29). The writer has never been trained on a letter operand at any place. A letter failure at 1-3 letters is domain shift, not length. The proved-wrong rule (any 4-8 letter cell below 90% means length-bound, so span copy must cover words) and the pass rule (word-valued replies can be built now) both ignore the 1-3 letter cells, so they cannot separate the two readings.

[shown] The stated mechanism is wrong in part. The idea says digit place rows 4+ are almost never trained. The place table is shared by reader and writer (reader.py lines 17-23; tool.py cells() lines 110-113 uses reader.place.weight[:CELLS]), and words of 5+ letters train those rows (research/data.md line 47). D0 reads digits at places 1-9 from the reader output at 99.997-100% on all six seeds (/mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/D0-RESULT-2026-10-07.md). What is untrained is the writer's query-to-key match at places 3+, for every character type (train numbers go to 9994; operands are 1-3 digits). The probe tests that match, and the idea should say so.

[shown] Overlap with the sealed plan. MARKS-D0-T1-2026-10-07.md Amendment 3 (lines 66-84) seals span copy and already names a read-only diagnostic (fine-tune on 4-9 digit rows, line 82) to separate place-rows-untrained from length-bound. The letter probe is a different diagnostic, not a duplicate. But 'word-valued tool replies can be built now' is a plan change that Amendment 3 has not sealed, and line 84 says diagnostics decide nothing about the fix. The probe must be recorded as read-only and must not change R1-R4.

[shown] Selection bias is not handled. write_copy keeps a row only if its call path is unchanged (path_changed skip inside the write_copy loop, tool.py about lines 452-462). Letter replies may change the path more often, and the surviving rows are then the easier ones. The probe must report path_changed by length and by operand and answer.

[shown] Under-specified and inconsistent. (a) Operand copy is 'by length 1-10' but the oracle draws 1-8 letters. (b) 'Every dev row whose intact answer is a call result' must mean in_dist only (the code's row set) or a changed row set; the idea does not say which, and changing the row set is a second change. (c) 'Swap the oracle in lines 449-482' is not a standalone edit: the block uses extra_evals locals (run_rows, prows, rows, is_hit, pc, out; tool.py lines 338-345 and 414-457), so the probe needs its own script or a flag, and the digit control needs both oracles on the same rows. (d) rand_digits is defined at tool.py line 60; lines 452-453 are the oracle that calls it.

[untested] The 'minutes on CPU' estimate is not measured here: torch is not installed in this sandbox, and the write_copy block needs two forward passes over every in_dist program row plus the extra_evals closure. Measure the run time on BensPC before the run.

[suggested] Rule 4: the probe is 2-seed, so 'word-valued tool replies can be built now' must be labelled a screen, not a result. Rule 5: in_dist dev only is allowed. If the dev is enlarged with the rebuild in research/data.md line 5, nothing in the notes shows that rebuild was checked against the protected-hash list (PROTECTED-HASH-JOB.md concerns a different pool). Check before use.

VERDICT: cut as a standalone idea. It is cheap (CPU, no training), but no outcome changes what Ben does next, its marks as written cannot be met, and it is not a new-kinds idea.

1. It cannot change the next step (shown). MARKS-D0-T1 Amendment 3 seals span copy as the one T1 fix and says the 4-9 digit diagnostic "decides nothing about this fix". The re-screen R1-R4 runs either way. The most likely probe result (suggested, untested) is that letters fail at 4+ like digits, which only confirms what is already sealed. The informative branch (letters pass at 4-8 while digits fail) is unlikely, because the register queries for places 4+ were never trained to pick a tape entry.

2. The mechanism story is partly wrong (shown in code). Letters and digits share one place table: tool.py cells() and the registers both use reader.place.weight, and reader.py place_ids applies to any word token. So a letter pass cannot show that "digit place rows" are the break. What is untrained is digit-by-place use of the writer's match at places 4+ (operands are 1-3 digits in 99.6% of training). The 4-digit cell (operand 14%) is also not explained by 'rows 4+', since a 4-digit number uses places 0-3.

3. The letter arm is confounded (shown in code, effects suggested). The answer path is ledger.gen_copy, a pointer-generator that mixes a vocab readout with copy attention. At 1-3 digits the answer may be spelled from register state rather than copied from the tape, so write_copy does not isolate the copy path. Letter results on the tape are out of distribution (T1 tape results are digits). calc() in tool.py accepts integer strings only, so a letter operand is an invalid call and the operand line says nothing about place rows. talk() also routes mode 1 to a prompt-word copy that cannot see tape entries, and the oracle block drops path_changed rows silently (tool.py about 460). Letters may change the path more often, which biases the surviving cells.

4. The marks cannot be met as written (shown, counts suggested). write_copy reads in_dist only, and the 3,000 cap never binds (2,793 program rows on the big dev). About 1,500-2,100 eligible answers over 8 lengths gives about 170-260 per length, not 300. Because 'fewer than n is reported, not judged', the probe can end with no verdict. A flat 99% line is above the digit control at 1-3 digits (answer 96-98, operand 85-93), and by a binomial calculation from the critics a true 99.5% copier passes all 16 cells only 2-26% of the time. The pass line judges answers only, while R1 needs operand and answer.

5. It collides with sealed rules (shown). Amendment 4 (6:10 PM ET) already changes the write_copy scorer: unambiguous operands only, n >= 200 per cell, a disclosure check first, and a re-score of the current T1 checkpoints once with the new scorer. A letter probe on the old scorer gives numbers that cannot be compared with R1. 'Word-valued tool replies can be built now' is a plan change with no sealed mark, and two checkpoints are a screen under rule 4. There is also no word-valued tool in any plan.

6. It does nothing for new kinds (shown). No variant or fewshot number moves. It is T1-line infrastructure, so it should not take a new-kinds ranking slot.

7. Rules check: rule 10 is fine (pre-ship eval, no deploy step). Rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 are fine. The problems are evidence design and decision value, not a rule break.

The only cheap, useful piece is a free rider on a run Amendment 4 already requires (see revised_idea).

idea.title: Fine-tune on k single pairs, with a shuffled-label control
idea.summary: Instead of putting examples in the prompt, fine-tune a copy of the model for a fixed small recipe on k single input-output pairs of one new kind, then test on fresh inputs. Shuffling the outputs across the same k inputs must fail, which shows the curve comes from the rule and not from label statistics. Single-pair items carry one number each, so B2 can reach k = 8, 16 and 32, which the in-prompt route cannot.
idea.change: Items are single prompts 'x->?' with answer y, one kind per run, on the ruler's new number kinds. Recipe fixed once for every kind and arm: whole-model AdamW, 100 steps, batch 16 drawn with replacement from the k pairs, lr 1e-4 (chosen once on seed 100 from 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4 using the practised kinds add and mult, which are outside the battery), fp32 on CPU. k in {1,2,4,8,16,32}. Arms: TRUE (real pairs), SHUF (the k outputs permuted across the k inputs; the test key stays the true rule), NONE (checkpoint unchanged). Test on 100 fresh x per kind, one greedy decode. Skills harm: pooled-5 dev after each fine-tune (PC). An autonomous arm is a separate run: the model holds out one of its own k pairs, fine-tunes, and stops when the held-out pair is right.
idea.why: Test-time training on the examples is the closest published route to learning a rule from a few pairs (Akyurek et al.), and fewshot.labelled_sets (k in 0, 8, 32, 128) was written for the plain nets but never run. Shown: forgetting is real, since fresh add/mult reach@32 fell from 0.61 to 0.109 after one sleep, so skills harm must be measured. Single-pair items also test whether B2's no-program rows (NOOP at weight 0.1) can learn a rule from answers alone.

problems: [shown, code] Answer-only single pairs give the op head no path to a computed value. A row with no program has gold op NOOP at every step (ledger.py:436-444, op starts as zeros). The executor returns ok=False for NOOP (ledger.py:83), so result slots stay invalid (ledger.py:294, 337). The answer pointer only covers prompt numbers and constants, because progparse._targets sets ans only when a program exists or the answer is a prompt number (progparse.py:206); otherwise mode=GEN (progparse.py:208). The answer-pointer loss is masked to mode 0 (ledger.py:478). Op and pointer losses are NOOP-only for has=False rows (ledger.py:501, 507, 513). So the TRUE arm's only learnable path is the GEN character head (ledger.py:486-492), which is a direct-answer net on 8 pairs. The brief reports plain_tf at 0.6-2.5% on held-out families. The idea's stated test ('can no-program rows learn a rule from answers alone') cannot pass under this loss.

[shown, code] The NOOP term is active harm, not neutral. The op head is trained toward NOOP at weight 0.1 on these rows (ledger.py:501, 507). At test time ops are argmax (ledger.py:326), so the fine-tune can suppress the computing path. Skills harm and new-kind scores would then reflect this suppression, not rule learning.

[suggested] No positive or negative control. There is no run of the same recipe on practised kinds with programs, where B2 already has programs for add and mult, to show the recipe can work at all. Without it a fail cannot be told from a broken recipe. A pass cannot be told from copy either: last_digit (x mod 10) can be read from the last character via place codes (reader.py:17-23 per code notes) and the copy path (ledger.py:239-249). So a TRUE-minus-SHUF gap on last_digit need not involve the thinker.

[shown] Pass and proved-wrong marks leave a gap and pool across kinds. Pass needs TRUE-minus-SHUF >= 20 and TRUE >= 50% at k <= 8. Proved wrong needs TRUE-minus-SHUF < 5 at k=8 on both seeds, or TRUE < 50% at k=16 on both seeds. A result such as a gap of 12 at k=8 is decided by neither. Pooling over kinds lets square and last_digit, which C2 already climbs with search (c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md line 40), carry the pass while sq_plus, double_add and affine stay near 0 (same line). Use per-kind marks.

That is a runtime value tuned on dev-style answers, and seed 100 is also one of the two screen seeds (rule 4). The plan lists 'learning rate during sleep' as a researcher choice that must become the model's own (/mnt/project-files/no-hardcoding/PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md section 2a). Steps 100 and batch 16 are fixed constants, which rule 10 allows if they are the same every night.

STEP NEEDS A RESEARCHER (shown in the idea): the k examples are packed into single 'x->?' items by the researcher's generator. That is a test format rule, which rule 10 excludes. The deployed model must find example pairs in its prompt in whatever form they arrive. The idea has no pair detector and does not say whether the reader can do this (untested).

NO TRIGGER (shown in the idea): one run per kind, started by the researcher. Nothing says when the model decides a kind is new or that it is stuck (rules 0 and 8). An autonomous trigger could use the model's own failed tries or a fit check against its examples. The compliant fast-sleep sleep already chooses its own temperature from its own tries (/mnt/project-files/fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, segment 2, T = 3.0 on s200). That report treats hand-written search as an outside tool the sleep calls, which is the rule's allowed form. The AdamW loop and the batch sampler are not discussed in any file I read, so the idea should say whether they count as learning machinery or as hand code.

DIFFERENT RECIPE FOR THE AUTONOMOUS ARM (the idea concedes it needs its own run): TRUE and SHUF stop at a fixed 100 steps, while the autonomous arm stops when one held-out pair is right. A single exact-match check is noisy, and a constant or copy guess can pass it. Leave-one-out over all k pairs is the stronger self-check (suggested). At k = 1 or 2 there is nothing left to hold out.

HARM CHECK NEEDS DEV ANSWERS (shown in the idea): skills harm is pooled-5 dev after each fine-tune, run on the PC. The deployed model has no dev answers, and the idea gives no autonomous harm check. The compliant fast-sleep result has the same gap: its guard is a researcher's chain-5 set with gold answers (RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, findings, guards held). Possible self-checks, both untested: replay of the model's own earlier answers (this detects change, not correctness), and exact calculator checks on arithmetic skills, which rule 1 allows as an outside tool.

NO REPLAY (shown in the idea and the fast-sleep report): the recipe fine-tunes only on the k pairs (batch 16 drawn with replacement) and keeps no old skills in the mix. The compliant fast-sleep result found replay carries most of its gain: dropping it cost -16.0 on the first parent (RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md, failures, trial 4). Fast-sleep's replay can create new practice items because each record's verified program can be run on fresh inputs. A single unknown rule has no such generator, so the deploy-time source of more practice items is undefined. Self-training is the only candidate and is untested.

MECHANISM: NO EXECUTOR ROUTE FOR THESE ROWS (shown from code, effect untested): gold() in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-learner/25dd80f7-54e0-50c0-b0e0-f697e28becce/scratchpad/code/reader/custom_io/models/ledger.py (about lines 433-454) gives a single-pair row has=False and op NOOP. The loss weights that op term by w_noop = 0.1 (default at ledger.py:130; weight line about 501). The pointer term is masked to op > 0, so it is zero for these rows. The answer is mode 2 (GEN, written from continuous registers) unless y is a prompt number (mode 0) or a prompt word (mode 1) (progparse.py _targets). So the fine-tune cannot train the op choice from these rows, and any rule must be learned through the continuous answer path, which is a plain direct-answer route. The idea's untested question about no-program rows is answered in part by this reading. Suggested fix: train on search-verified programs (tries kept only when they reproduce all k pairs), which is what C2 and the compliant fast sleep do.

Choosing the copy is a kind decision the model has to make, and the idea does not show how. Stored copies also multiply the shipped size. Rule 3 counts params, so the total should be stated.
