critiques.expected_effect: Checked and holding: the in-prompt route caps at 8 pairs, because progparse.py line 8 sets N_NUM = 16 and each pair uses 2 numbers, so the claim that k = 16 and 32 are out of reach in-prompt is right. If run as written (CPU, 2 seeds), it would give a first k-curve for learning from k single pairs, which the project lacks. Given the loss routing in item 7, I expect fresh-x accuracy on TRUE to stay low at k = 8, so the +20 mark would fail (suggested). Memorising 8 pairs does not raise fresh-x accuracy, so a passing TRUE would need a real rule. SHUF is a fair control for answer-range learning because the output values are the same, but it does not catch memorisation. Any result stays a measurement, not a deploy method, because the lr, trigger, harm check and stop rule are still researcher steps.

problems: MECHANISM (shown, ledger.py gold() ~lines 433-454 and loss w_row ~line 501): single-pair answer-only rows have has=False, so the op target is NOOP at w_noop=0.1 and pointers default to slot 0. The op is chosen by a discrete gold index or argmax, and the executor output is an int64 with no gradient, so the answer loss never tells the thinker to pick MUL or ADD. The TRUE arm therefore cannot teach the calculator route. It measures whether the talker writes the answer digits directly (row_targets mode 2, progparse.py ~195-215). The proposal's own question, whether NOOP rows can learn a rule from answers alone, is answered by the code: not for the op choice. The NOOP target also pushes the model toward not computing.

PREDICTION (suggested): with no program signal, the TRUE arm should reach high accuracy only on copy-type rules such as x mod 10 (last digit copied from the prompt). x^2, 2(x+k), x^2+k and a*x+b should stay near 0 at k=8. Pooled TRUE >= 50% at k<=8 is very unlikely, so the pass mark is almost certainly unreachable as designed.

MARKS HAVE A GAP: pooled TRUE at 50% for k=16 or less but below 50% at k=8 is neither a pass nor a proved-wrong. The pass rule also says 'at k<=8' while the difference mark says 'at k=8'. The pooled set of kinds is never named, and the 'ruler's new number kinds' are not defined in the proposal.

SHUF CONTROL DEFECT: at k=1 a permutation of one output is the identity, so SHUF equals TRUE by construction. A random permutation also has fixed points that keep correct pairs, so it needs a derangement. SHUF is not chance. It is a matched label-statistics control, and for small-range outputs (mod 10 has 10 values) its exact-match rate is not zero. The 'SHUF is chance' question (critic check 1) has answer: no, it is not chance.

OVERREACH IN THE 'WHY': the proposal says 'Shown: forgetting is real'. The cited file (creative-pilot/c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md line 44) shows fresh add/mult reach@32 fell from 0.61/0.57 to 0.109/0.113 for seed 100/101, but also says pooled-5 skills harm is small, attributes the loss to the add/mult question format of this checker, and marks the cause untested. Relabel as 'shown drop, cause untested'.

IN-PROMPT COMPARATOR NOT BUILT: fewshot.labelled_sets (creative/creative/fewshot.py:370-376) only builds nested sets; creative/creative/README.md:35 says it builds the data only; there is no training code and no 'labelled' folder in creative/creative/results. The claim that B2 cannot read k=8 in the prompt does hold: progparse.py:8 and prompt_numbers [:N_NUM] cap operands at 16 numbers, and 8 pairs plus a query is 17. But plain nets have no such cap, and the cheap first k-curve (in-prompt, plain_tf, no training) is skipped.

D6 uses different marks (TRUE minus SHUF >= +20; pooled >= 50%) without saying why. Either use the roadmap ruler or justify the change.

The 100 steps and batch 16 are researcher constants. The autonomous arm (hold out one own pair, stop when right) needs k>=2 and is untested. CITATION CHECK (Akyurek et al., arXiv 2411.07279; verified this session through search snippets, not the full PDF): their test-time training builds leave-one-out tasks, adds rule-based augmentations (rotation, flip, scale), and trains per-task LoRA on a large pretrained LM. D6's TRUE arm has neither augmentation nor leave-one-out. The 6x figure was against fine-tuned baselines in v2 and against a 1B model in v1, so the baseline changed between versions. The 12 h on one A100 figure (fast-sleep-papers.md line 43) was not verified here (untested). The citation supports the route in general, not this arm's design.

UNUSED COMPARATORS: the fast-sleep research loop reached 71.3% holdout on C2 with search and replay (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07.md line 6, about 2,400 TF per sleep). Blind search solves 77% of C2 DEV at 6,000 guesses (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 2 as relayed). A fine-tune on search records lifted x^2+k to 20-27% on 2 parents (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md section 5). D6 should be compared with these at matched compute, not with the 0-4% floor.

KIND LIST MISMATCH: fewshot.py HELD_OUT is (affine, square, add_double) and PRACTISED is (add, sub, mul). The C2 pilot uses sq_plus and double_add. The proposal's battery kinds are not named in any file it cites.

ONE KIND PER RUN, FIXED STEPS: each kind gets its own weight copy, so the arm measures per-task adapters, not accumulated learning, and no multi-kind forgetting is measured. At fixed 100 steps and batch 16, exposures per pair are about 1600/k, so the k-curve mixes data amount with repetition unless this is stated.

critiques.expected_effect: Suggested, not measured. On B2 the TRUE arm at k=8 should give pooled TRUE minus SHUF of about +2 to +12, driven mostly by copy-type rules such as x mod 10. Pooled TRUE at or above 50% at k<=8 has under 10% chance. Four of five kinds should stay near 0 at k=8 and k=16. If the curve appears, it mainly shows copy-type rules, not rule learning from examples. The arm would be a useful direct-answer ruler on B2, but it cannot yet count as a route to learning new kinds (rule 10 gap and no program signal). The 2-seed screen should be read as a screen.

problems: BLOCKING (shown by code reading). Single-pair rows cannot teach an operation. A row with no program gets prog=() and has=False (progparse.py _targets; ledger.py gold, line 451), so its op target is NOOP at weight w_noop=0.1 (ledger.py:501, 507). In training the executor runs on the gold op (ledger.py:328), and the pointer loss is masked to op>0 (ledger.py:513). The answer's only gradient path is the talker. For single-pair items the answer is not a prompt number, so the mode is GEN (progparse _targets ans/mode lines). The TRUE arm is therefore a neural fit of x->y digits from k pairs, not calculator use. The proposal's 'why' sentence (NOOP rows learning a rule from answers alone) is answered by the code: they cannot learn an op under the current losses. Prediction (suggested, not measured): TRUE minus SHUF will be large only for copy-like kinds (last digit, reversal) and near zero for arithmetic kinds (square, add-constant, affine), so the pooled mark mostly measures copy.

MARKS CONFLICT AND ARE UNDEFINED. 'Pooled TRUE reaches 50% at k<=8' (pass) and 'pooled TRUE below 50% at k=16' (proved wrong) can both hold on the same data, so the verdict is undefined. TRUE minus SHUF between +5 and +20 is neither pass nor fail. 'Reaches' does not say at which k. Skills harm is in the pass mark but not in the proved-wrong clause. The kind set is not defined in any file I searched: grep for 'ruler' across /mnt/project-files finds only the in-context and whole-model rulers in the roadmaps (creative-roadmap-2026-10-06.md; whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-05-night.md:157), and no list of new number kinds. The 430-run total (72 runs per kind across 2 models x 2 seeds x 6 k x 3 arms) implies about 6 kinds. Pooling over kinds lets copy-like kinds carry the pass, so require per-kind marks and list the kinds.

NOT THE ROADMAP'S RULER. whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-05-night.md:157 (and the 10-06 file, row 6) fixes the in-context ruler (8 examples at least 25 points above 0 examples; shuffled-answer examples within 5 points of 0) and asks for examples-to-learn: the k at which a same-size plain net matches. D6 runs plain_tf_steps but has no plain-match criterion and no check that SHUF sits within 5 of the k=0 floor. Adopt those marks or state that D6 measures something different.

FLOORS AND CHANCE. SHUF is a fair control for label statistics, but its accuracy floor depends on the kind. For last digit (10 possible outputs) a constant guess scores about 10 percent (suggested arithmetic). For large-range kinds the floor is about 0. Report each kind's best-constant floor, computed by hand-scoring (rule 1 allows this). NONE (k=0) is measured but appears in no mark. B2 was trained in bf16, and the screen runs fp32, so NONE must be re-measured in fp32 rather than copied from RESULT.json.

K-CURVE CONFOUND. A fixed 100 steps at batch 16 gives 1,600 pair presentations, which is 1,600/k per pair: 1,600 passes over each pair at k=1, 50 at k=32 (shown from the stated recipe). A curve over k mixes the number of examples with the number of passes. Either report presentations per pair, or add a second arm with fixed passes per pair. Change one at a time (rule 4).

TEST INPUTS. 'Fresh x' does not say whether the 100 test inputs are disjoint from the k training inputs, or how 32 distinct inputs are drawn from a small range. fewshot.labelled_sets (fewshot.py:370-376) says its pool is disjoint from the test questions, and D6 should state the same. Without disjointness, TRUE gains at k=16 and 32 can come from looking up trained inputs.

FORGETTING EVIDENCE IS OVERREAD. The 0.61 to 0.109 figures are shown (creative-pilot/c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md:44). They compare the warmed parent (job 5) with N after the stepping-stone sleep. The same line says pooled-5 skills harm is small and attributes the add/mult drop to the checker's question format, with cause untested. So 'forgetting is real' is not shown. The same add/mult probe is the proposal's learning-rate selection signal, and the readout shows it is unstable under sleep.

LEARNING-RATE SELECTION (rules 4 and 10). The lr is chosen from 3e-5, 1e-4 and 3e-4 on seed 100, which is also a pass seed, so the screen is not clean. The selection metric is not stated. The probe is add/mult, which the readout shows is unstable. Use a third seed (for example 102), a stated metric and a stated selection rule. State that lr, 100 steps and batch 16 are fixed design constants that do not change per kind (rule 10), and why the chosen values are fixed.

CLOSEST PRIOR IS MISDESCRIBED. papers/fast-sleep-papers.md:43 says Akyurek et al. use leave-one-out records, augmentations and a per-task LoRA on pretrained 1B to 8B language models. D6 has none of augmentation, leave-one-out or LoRA. It is whole-model AdamW on a from-scratch 3.3M model. A fail therefore does not refute that method, and a pass without augmentation would be surprising and should be reported as such. The augmented version is a separate change under rule 4.

OPERAND-CAP CLAIM IS OVERSTATED. 'Which the in-prompt route cannot' holds only for the executor route. progparse.py limits operand reads to the first 16 numbers (N_NUM=16), which is 8 pairs. The talker still reads the whole prompt (shown). Reword the claim.

TARGET LENGTH. Restricting targets to 3 digits or fewer does not break rule 7, since nothing is truncated. But T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md (checked) shows copy at 85-98 percent for 1-3 digits, 14-59 percent at 4 digits and about 1 percent at 5. The screen would hide that failure. Report pass or fail by answer length.

AUTONOMY GAP (rule 10). The researcher picks the kind, the lr, the steps, the batch and k for every run. The autonomous arm stops on one held-out pair, which is a 0-or-1 signal and too noisy to stop on. Use leave-one-out over all k pairs, scored, before any deploy claim. The proposal says this itself, so keep it as a blocker for deploy language.

COST ESTIMATE. The 1.5 h CPU figure is untimed (untested). The fine-tunes are tiny: 1,600 presentations is about 0.03 percent of B2's 24,000 x 256 training rows. The real time is 430 harm evaluations on 6,040 dev rows each (about 2.6 million row evaluations), which the estimate leaves out. The 3.3M-parameter model fits in 16 GB with a wide margin (suggested, from the parameter count). Cheapest decisive step: a 3-to-6-run pilot (one kind, k=8, TRUE, SHUF, NONE, seeds 100 and 102) plus the op-emission check below, before the grid.

(3) Equalise presentations per pair, or add a fixed-passes arm. (4) Pick lr on a third seed with a stated metric, and state the constants as fixed. (5) Run the pilot first, then the grid. chair.reasons:
CUT D6 as written. The k-curve question it asks is worth keeping, but it should be rerun inside the fast-sleep line (see revised_idea), not as D6.

1. Mechanism (shown; I read models/ledger.py gold() lines 433-454 and loss() lines 497-535, and the rules, autonomy, mechanism and test critics agree). A single-pair answer-only row has no program, so has=False and the op target is NOOP at w_noop 0.1. The pointer loss is multiplied by (op>0), which is 0 for these rows. The answer-pointer loss is masked to mode 0, and a computed y is not a prompt number, so the row is mode 2 (GEN). The only informative gradients are the mode term and the GEN character loss. The fine-tune therefore turns B2 into a direct-answer net fitted to k pairs, and it pushes the op head toward NOOP. It cannot test the project's real claim (the thinker writes a program and the calculator runs it). The idea's side question, whether no-program rows can learn a rule from answers alone, is answered by the loss: not for the op choice.

2. Predicted outcome (suggested, untested). TRUE minus SHUF is large only for copy-like kinds such as x mod 10, which the place codes and the copy path can read. It stays near 0 for x^2, x^2+k, 2(x+k) and a*x+b. Pooled TRUE at or above 50% at k<=8 is very unlikely. Shown context: the same-size plain nets score 0.6-2.5% on held-out families (33-pc-confirm-b2 RESULT.json files), and C2 affine is 0-4% under every method tried (creative-pilot/c2pilot-readout-2026-10-07.md; fast-sleep/RESEARCH-2026-10-07.md). A fail would come from the loss, not from evidence about learning rules, so it would not answer Ben's new-kinds question. A pass would mostly mean copy kinds.

3. Marks are broken (shown). 'TRUE reaches 50% at k<=8' (pass) and 'TRUE below 50% at k=16' (proved wrong) can both hold, and a gap of +5 to +20 is neither. The pass clause says k<=8 where the difference mark says k=8. The pooled kind set is never named, so copy-like kinds can carry a pooled pass. The marks differ from the roadmap in-context ruler (whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-06.md line 431; whole-model-roadmap-2026-10-05-night.md line 157: 8 examples at least 25 points above 0 examples, shuffled answers within 5 of 0), and two mark sets invite picking the one that passes (rule 4). SHUF is not chance: at k=1 it equals TRUE, and at k=2 a random permutation is the identity half the time. For x mod 10 (10 outputs) a best-constant guess alone scores about 10%. SHUF needs a forced derangement and a per-kind best-constant floor.

4. Rule 10 and rule 4 gaps (shown from the idea text; the critics found no lr-sweep record). The lr is picked on dev-style add/mult answers on seed 100, which is also a screen seed. That is a runtime value tuned on dev answers. The trigger, the 'x->?' packing of examples, the kind choice and the harm check on dev answers are all researcher steps. The autonomous arm stops on one held-out pair, which cannot separate rules (at x=3, x^2 and 3x both give 9). The recipe keeps no replay, and the compliant fast sleep lost 16.0 points on its first parent without replay (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07-report.md). The 'at most 3 digits' filter is chosen from the test side and hides the shown T1 copy failure at 4+ digits (architecture/T1-SCREEN-RESULT-2026-10-07.md). The TRUE and SHUF arms alone are research measurements, not deploy evidence.

5. Overstated evidence (shown). 'Forgetting is real' rests on add/mult reach@32 falling from 0.61 to 0.109. The source line says pooled-5 skills harm was small and puts the drop in the checker's add/mult question format, cause untested. Also, 100 steps at batch 16 means 1,600/k passes per pair, so the k-curve mixes the number of examples with repeats.

6. The rescue is a different experiment. Every critic's fix (candidate programs kept only if they reproduce all k pairs, then replay on fresh inputs) is the compliant fast-sleep loop that already reaches 71.3 +/- 2.5% on C2 holdout (fast-sleep/RESEARCH-LOOP-2026-10-07.md, shown). After the fix, SHUF is a built-in control because no program fits shuffled labels. What remains new is only the k-sweep, and it belongs to the fast-sleep thread. In-prompt reading is capped at 7 pairs because progparse.py N_NUM=16 (shown), but that cap only matters for the search route, not for D6's single-pair weight fit.

7. Cost is not the reason to cut. CPU is cheap, but the 1.5 h figure is untimed, and 430 harm evaluations of 6,040 rows each are left out. The skills dev rows are not on disk and torch is not installed in this sandbox. No fact check is needed: the verdict rests on code I read.
chair.revised_idea:
Drop D6 (single-pair whole-model fine-tune with TRUE/SHUF/NONE). If the lead wants Ben's examples-to-learn k-curve, run it as a one-parameter sweep of the already-compliant fast-sleep loop (creative/rl/), owned by the fast-sleep thread, as its own sealed one-change test.

Change: vary only the number of example pairs per question, k in {1, 2, 3, 5, 7}, on the C2 held-out kinds. B2's in-prompt reader caps at 16 numbers (progparse.py N_NUM), so 7 pairs plus the query is the maximum; the roadmap ruler's 'k=8' cannot be run in the prompt route and must be declared as 7 before running. Everything else is the compliant sleep unchanged: its own night, its own temperature from its own tries, chain search, replay of program-checked records on the day's own inputs, and the same batch-1024, 80-visit fine-tune. These are design constants that are identical for every kind and k, so there is no per-kind lr tuning.

Arms: TRUE; SHUF (labels forced into a derangement, with a count of coincident outputs); NONE (parent unchanged); a blind-search floor at the same guess budget with no weights; a no-replay arm. SHUF should find no fitting program, so it checks the checker and is not a learning control. Per-kind marks on x^2, x mod 10, x^2+k, 2(x+k) and a*x+b, with a per-kind best-constant floor.

Test items come from a fresh generator tag (the seed-7031 convention), disjoint from the example inputs. Never use the labelled or test split. Report results by answer length. Report skills harm from pooled-5 plus chain-5.

Marks are fixed before running and use the existing ruler: the 7-example result at least 25 points above the 0-example result, and shuffled answers within 5 points of 0, plus a gain over the blind-search floor (the size of that gain is to be fixed by the fast-sleep thread). Screen on 2 parents, then 6 paired parents before any claim.

Rule 10: the model decides by itself that it is stuck and when to stop, using leave-one-out over its own k pairs, not one held-out pair. The harm check uses the model's own replayed answers plus exact calculator checks on arithmetic skills. Predictions (suggested, untested): k=1 is ambiguous, so the sleep learns a wrong program; the gain is concentrated at k=2-3; x^2 and x mod 10 climb; and a*x+b stays near 0 as in every earlier method.
chair.plan_guidance:
Only relevant if the lead keeps any form of this idea (the cut stands for D6 as written). Keep it separate from the village model (rule 9): small-card B2/C2 claims only. The test must get these right:

- Route. Use search-verified programs (tries kept only if they reproduce all k pairs) plus replay so the op head gets real targets. Answer-only single-pair rows give no op or pointer gradient and push the op head toward NOOP (shown, ledger.py gold() and loss()). If an answer-only arm is wanted at all, label it a 'direct-answer floor' and add a zero-training check first: confirm on hand-written single-pair prompts that the emitted op is NOOP and the mode is GEN, scored with evalx.evaluate (rule 1 allows hand-written tests).
- One change. Vary only k. Hold the recipe fixed across kinds, k and arms, and report passes per pair if the number of steps is held fixed (100 steps at batch 16 is 1,600/k passes per pair).
- Controls. Include a blind-search floor and a no-replay arm. Use a forced-derangement SHUF with a coincidence count and a per-kind best-constant floor. Re-measure NONE in fp32 (B2 was trained in bf16). Do not read the k=1 SHUF as a control because it equals TRUE.
- Marks. Use the roadmap ruler (8 examples at least 25 points above 0; shuffled within 5 of 0), declare k=7 where B2 cannot take 8, and make the marks per kind rather than pooled. Close the gap between pass and proved-wrong with one verdict rule. Name the kinds. fewshot.py HELD_OUT (affine, square, add_double) differs from the C2 DEV kinds, so state which set is used.
- Data hygiene. Use a fresh generator tag (seed-7031 convention), test inputs disjoint from the example inputs, and never the sealed labelled or test split or any GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected panel (rule 5). Keep all answer lengths (rule 7) and report by digit count. Choose any build-time constant on seeds 102-103 or on training rows only, not on a screen seed and not on dev answers.
- Rule 10. State plainly that lr, visits and batch are fixed design constants. Any deploy claim needs the model's own leave-one-out stop and the model's own harm check. Say how a query finds its fine-tuned copy, or use one sleep that keeps a single model, and count any stored copies in size (rule 3).
- Evidence labels. Relabel the 0.61 to 0.109 add/mult drop as 'checker-format drop, cause untested' (pooled-5 skills harm was small). Treat Akyurek et al. 2411.07279 as suggested only: it uses leave-one-out tasks, augmentation and per-task LoRA on 1B-8B pretrained models, and none of those is in this recipe.
- Infrastructure (blocked here). The skills dev rows are not on disk and torch is not installed here, so the harm check and all fine-tunes run on Ben's PC or M1. Time one fine-tune before promising an hour count.

idea.title: Re-score saved checkpoints per row: row noise, precision, soft score
idea.summary: One eval-only pass over the saved B2 checkpoints writes per-row correctness, answer probability, margin and zero-round answer. From it, CPU analyses split row-sampling noise from seed noise, test fp32 vs stored bf16 eval precision, and test whether a soft answer score has a smaller seed SD than exact match. Zero GPU hours.
idea.change: New eval-only script (e.g. CIO/rescore.py). Load each checkpoint (B2_s200-205 are in scratchpad code/b2ckpt/B2_s20x/checkpoint.pt; B2_s100/101 in PF/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen; T1_s200/201 in PF/checkpoints/cio-1007). Run evalx.evaluate with return_preds on the five pooled dev splits in fp32 CPU, and (optional) bf16 CPU. Save per row: correct, P(gold) = P(mode) x P(pointer/chars) from lmode/lans/lword/gen_copy and Ledger.gold targets, min margin, loops:0 prediction. Analyses: (a) row disagreement q between seeds and row SE = sqrt(q/N) for pooled-5; combined SE of a six-seed gap = sqrt((sd/sqrt6)^2 + rowSE^2); replace pooled McNemar by per-seed McNemar. (b) fp32 CPU vs stored bf16 CUDA numbers for seeds 100/101 (pooled-5, loops:0 in_dist). (c) soft pooled-5 = 100 x mean P(gold), partial-credit (1 - normalised edit distance) and teacher-forced answer NLL (plain arms: text after last '#'); within-arm SD over six B2 seeds and, if plain checkpoints exist, paired SD. Dev jsonl must be copied from the PC (not in this snapshot). Param cost 0.
idea.why: Seed SD alone understates the error of small margins. Shown: chain-5 row disagreement between B2 seeds is 4.5 rows of 1000 (row SE 0.21) but 62-65 rows vs plain_tf_steps (row SE 0.80), and row correctness is correlated across seeds (ICC 0.48 B2, 0.72 plain_tf_steps), so pooling seeds does not shrink the row term. Suggested bound: row noise for B2 minus plain_tf is 0.52-1.06 points and for B2 minus plain_tf_steps 0.33-0.98, about the size of the 6-seed training SE (0.38 and 0.55), and the sealed CIs use training noise only. Pooled-5 binomial SE is 0.56 against a seed SD of 0.63, so seed noise on a fixed row set is mostly training noise (the two cannot be separated without per-row data). Continuous companions can quiet threshold metrics (arXiv 2304.15004, suggested).

test.where: M1 Pro CPU or PC CPU, eval only, after copying dev jsonl from the PC. Start on B2_s100/s101 (mount) then B2 s200-205.
test.arms: B2 seeds 100,101,200-205 (+ plain_tf_steps and plain_tf where checkpoints exist); fp32 CPU intact and loops:0; optional bf16 CPU
test.pass_mark: (a) no-change row SE on pooled-5 (B2 vs its own other seeds) <=0.3 points; (b) fp32 minus stored bf16 within 0.5 on pooled-5 and 1.0 on loops:0 in_dist on both screen seeds; (c) soft pooled-5 within-arm SD across six B2 seeds <=0.40 (hard 0.63), same sign as hard on every seed, mean within 3 points. Fixed now.
test.proved_wrong: Row SE >0.5 on pooled-5: no six-seed +-1.0 parity claim is possible whatever the seed count, so a larger dev panel is the fix; soft within-arm SD >=0.60: drop the soft score; fp32 minus stored >2.0 on loops:0: every leak verdict must be re-scored on one device.

problems: RULES (shown, code and brief): nothing breaks rules 1-3 or 6-10 as written (dev splits, CPU, developer scoring, no training, no size change). Rule 4 is at risk: the new soft metric, the per-seed McNemar swap (analyze.py:198-209 already reports per_seed_p) and a row term in the six-seed CI all change how sealed marks read. Used to re-judge verdicts after seeing numbers, they are post-hoc mark changes. They must be sealed in a PASS-MARKS addendum before any scoring and reported as informational only.

OVERLAP, chain-5 (shown, reproduced): per-row chain-5 hits already sit in results/33-pc-confirm-b2/*/RESULT.json (chain5.intact.hits, 1000 ids) for B2 and tfsteps seeds 200-205. Recomputed: B2 pairwise disagreements 1-8 (mean 4.53); B2 vs tfsteps same seed 62-65; ICC1 0.475 (B2) and 0.72 (tfsteps). These need zero compute. B2 is at ceiling on chain-5 (99.4-99.7), so they say little about pooled-5 noise.

OVERLAP, pooled-5 and T1 (shown): PLAN-AND-MARKS-2026-10-07.md:50 already plans per-row dev predictions for all six splits in every rung. Queues 40-43 pass --save-preds (queue_local/40, 41, 42, 43); queue 33, the B2 confirm, does not. The new content is therefore only the retrospective B2 and plain 200-205 re-scoring. T1's PREDS.json comes from queue 40 anyway. The fact check already recommended the same eval-only --save-preds re-run. The director lists ideas 2, 4, 5, 6 and 18 as CPU work on saved checkpoints; their texts are not visible to me, so check for duplication before running (untested).

PASS MARK (a) TESTS THE WRONG PAIR (shown in the idea plus computed): it measures B2-vs-own-seeds disagreement, where the true gap is about 0. Every claim is B2 minus plain. The idea's own suggested row bounds for B2 minus plain_tf (0.52-1.06) are above its own proved-wrong line (row SE >0.5), so the proved-wrong clause would fire on the real claim. The mark and its stop line contradict each other.

THE ROW BOUNDS HAVE NO MEASURED BASIS (computed, suggested interpretation): no file holds pooled-5 per-row predictions, so the 0.52-1.06 and 0.33-0.98 ranges are not measured. Their lower ends equal the minimum row-sampling SE implied by the measured pooled gaps: sqrt(d(1-d)/6040). With the six-seed means 74.02 (B2), 53.69 (plain_tf), 67.13 (plain_tf_steps) from RESULT.json, d = 0.2033 gives 0.52 and d = 0.0689 gives 0.33. The 0.52 floor alone exceeds the six-seed training SE of the paired difference (0.94/sqrt6 = 0.38), so the row term is not 'about the size' of training noise as the idea says. Combined SE is at least about 0.65 against 0.38 for B2 minus plain_tf. This assumes independent rows, so it is a lower bound. Sealed CIs use training noise only.

chair.reasons:
Worth a sealed, zero-GPU test, but only in a narrower form than written. All four critics said revise, and the chair agrees; none found a rule break.

Rules. Dev splits only, CPU only, no training, no size change, B2 only. Nothing here is a deploy-time method, so rule 10 is met as long as gold-based outputs never feed a sleep step or gate (suggested, from the idea text). The one live risk is rule 4: any new statistic that re-reads a sealed verdict is a post-hoc mark change. It must be sealed in an addendum before running and stay informational (shown, PASS-MARKS conventions as cited by the critics).

Why it is worth doing.
- Sealed 6-seed CIs use training noise only. Shown: B2 is at 74.02 pooled-5 with a row-sampling floor of sqrt(d(1-d)/6040) = 0.52 for the B2 vs plain_tf gap (d = 0.2033) and 0.33 for B2 vs plain_tf_steps (d = 0.0689), against a 6-seed training SE of 0.38 and 0.54 (computed by the rules critic from the confirm RESULT.json means). This is a lower bound if rows are independent. It may matter for the +-1.0 parity bands (T1, EGE, W1), where the 6-seed CI half-width is already about 1.05 x SD.
- Only the pooled-5 cross-arm number is missing. Shown, reproduced by three critics: chain-5 hits exist for B2 and tfsteps 200-205. B2 seeds disagree on 1-8 of 1000 rows (mean 4.5). B2 vs tfsteps at the same seed disagrees on 62-65 rows. ICC is 0.475 (B2) and 0.72 (tfsteps). Chain-5 is at ceiling, so it says little about pooled-5.
- The data needed is smaller than the idea assumed. Shown: C0_s200/s201 PREDS.json (plain_tf_steps, cap 107) exist in /mnt/project-files/whole-model-roadmap/first-look-10m-results/. The test critic computed that 1650 of 6040 C0 predictions differ between seeds (27.3%), which bounds C0's within-arm row SE at 0.67 or less. Queues 40-43 pass --save-preds (shown, queue_local/40-43), so T1, U0, W1 and C0 get per-row predictions for free. The only retrospective work is re-scoring B2 s200 and s201 (two checkpoints, one intact pass each). That gives B2-vs-C0 and B2-vs-T1 pooled-5 row terms on 2 paired seeds. This is a screen, not a claim (rule 4).

What must change. Mark (a) as written measures B2 against its own seeds, where the true gap is about 0, so it passes trivially and says nothing about B2 minus plain. Its proved-wrong line (row SE above 0.5) also contradicts the idea's own suggested bound of 0.52-1.06 for B2 minus plain_tf. The formula sqrt(q/N) omits the mean gap: for a paired gap the row variance is (q - d^2)/N. Rows are grouped by family (evalx.py docstring, shown), so a family-cluster bootstrap is needed. The soft score is the weakest part:
- P(gold) as written is not the decoder's probability. Shown: run() teacher-forces the gold program, talk() falls back to GEN when a NUM pointer is invalid or a WORD pointer is out of range, and is_hit accepts any string in row['accepted'].
- Gold answers are truncated at 8 characters, which rule 7 forbids reintroducing.
- Mark (c) can pass by chance about 15% of the time with no real change (P(chi2_5 <= 2.02), computed by the test critic). It also rewards a score compressed near ceiling.
- A valid check needs plain-arm 200-205 per-row probabilities, and those checkpoints are absent (PLAN-AND-MARKS line 107, shown).
Demote the soft score to an optional developer diagnostic. Do not let it enter any mark.

Best new piece, from the autonomy critic. Record the model's own decoded answer and the probability of its actual decode path, using no gold, and measure how well that separates right from wrong rows (AUROC). That is the first measured candidate for a no-gold 'stuck' or stop signal (rule 8, H1). It stays deployable only if a gate threshold is a fixed design constant or comes from the model's own tries, never tuned on these dev rows. Untested; no confiden/calibrat analysis exists in the project (critic grep, partial).

Data blockers. Shown by two critics: no dev jsonl and no sk200k or data_big dev files are in the snapshot. Ben must copy work/data/dev and work/data_big/dev from the PC and hash-check them against FULL-BUILD-MANIFEST-200k-seed1.json. The 18 confirm tf and tfsteps checkpoints are PC-only. Possible overlap with the director's ideas 2, 4, 5, 6 and 18 (CPU work on saved checkpoints) was not checkable here; the Opus lead should merge duplicates.
chair.revised_idea:
method-D2 revised: a developer-only, eval-only CPU re-score of saved checkpoints. It reports cross-arm row noise on pooled-5 and checks CPU against the stored GPU scores. Optionally it measures a no-gold answer confidence. No training, 0 GPU hours, B2 card experiments only (rule 9). The soft or partial-credit score is dropped from the main test and is never a mark.

Stage 0 (free, now, description only). From the existing RESULT.json chain5.intact.hits files, report B2-vs-B2 and B2-vs-tfsteps row disagreement, ICC, and per-seed McNemar p. Label it chain-5 only. Do not change PASS-1's pooled McNemar.

Stage 1 (needs the dev jsonl from the PC). Seal a PASS-MARKS addendum first. Then write rescore.py, which loads the checkpoint on CPU fp32, runs evalx.evaluate(return_preds=True) on the five pooled dev splits with the free-running state, and also runs loops:0 on in_dist.

Gate 0 (pass or stop, on all six B2 checkpoints s200-205, with s100/s101 as extras):
- The scorer's argmax must reproduce talk()'s own output with zero mismatches.
- Chain-5 hits must match the stored hits.
- Per-split correct counts must match final_eval.
- fp32 CPU minus stored bf16-autocast CUDA must be within 0.5 on pooled-5 and 1.0 on loops:0 in_dist on every seed.
- Reword the precision check: the weights are fp32 (train.py:201), and the stored numbers are bf16-autocast CUDA.

Analysis A (descriptive, no gate), on the claim-relevant pairs only: B2 s200/s201 against C0 s200/s201 (existing PREDS.json) and, once judged, T1 s200/s201 (queue 40 PREDS.json).
- Report q (the fraction of rows where correctness differs).
- Report the paired row variance (q - d^2)/N.
- Report a family-cluster bootstrap SE.
- Print them beside the floors 0.52 (B2 vs plain_tf) and 0.33 (B2 vs plain_tf_steps) and the 6-seed training SE.
- Keep B2-vs-own-seeds as a secondary sanity row.
- Decision rule, fixed now: if the combined SE of the six-seed gap (training SE and row SE, added in quadrature) exceeds 0.5 on any sealed +-1.0 parity gap, state that the band is underpowered. This triggers a separately sealed proposal for a larger or second dev panel regenerated from the same generator with a new seed. It never triggers a loosening of a mark, and nothing changes a past verdict without Ben's explicit approval.
- The row term matters only if the claim is about new rows. If the dev panel is defined as the benchmark itself, the sealed CIs stand. Ben must say which reading he wants before the numbers are read.

Analysis B (optional, rule-8 and H1 relevant, no gold in the column): per row, store the decoded answer and the probability of the decoder's actual path. That is P(mode argmax), times P(pointer or word) for NUM or WORD, or times the product over the 9 registers plus EOS for GEN, including the GEN fallbacks in talk(). Pass mark fixed now: AUROC against exact-match correctness is 0.75 or higher on all six B2 seeds, on pooled-5 and on the variant split reported separately. Proved wrong: AUROC below 0.65 on any seed. Use no threshold from these rows; a deployed gate needs a fixed design constant or a value from the model's own tries.

Developer diagnostics only, never in a mark, never a training or sleep signal: P(gold) summed over row['accepted'] and all decode paths, with no 8-character gold truncation; partial credit; teacher-forced NLL. Report the fraction of rows with P(gold) in 0.05-0.95 first. If it is small, stop, because the soft score is just exact match.

Exclusions: no per-seed McNemar swap and no soft score in any mark. T1, U0, W1 and C0 rows enter only after their own verdicts are sealed. T1 needs separate code (models/tool.py), so use queue 40's PREDS.json and do not build P(answer) for T1.
chair.plan_guidance:
Test plan. This is a measurement test, not a model change, so the pass marks check the scorer and the writeup (rule 4: one change, marks sealed first). Stage 0 needs no compute. Stage 1 needs Ben to copy the dev jsonl from the PC, hash-checked.

What the plan must get right.
1. Seal first. Write a PASS-MARKS addendum before any run. It lists every statistic, threshold and decision rule below. It states that nothing here changes an existing verdict, and that any change to a sealed CI, McNemar or mark needs Ben's explicit approval after the 202-205 confirm. Put the plain-language summary for Ben (a high-school senior) in the addendum: 'our error bars only count training luck; this test counts how much the fixed set of test questions adds'.
2. Data. Name the exact dev paths (work/data/dev and work/data_big/dev from the PC), hash them against FULL-BUILD-MANIFEST-200k-seed1.json, and state they are not GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved, blind or protected (rule 5). Save no hits from protected panels.
3. Compute. Use the M1 Pro, or cap threads on the PC so the queue 33/40 jobs are not slowed (suggested). First time a 300-row run per checkpoint (untested); the 1-2 h estimate is a guess. Run B2 s200 and s201 first (two checkpoints, one intact pass each) before the other four.
4. Gate 0, fixed now (an equivalence gate, not a claim):
 - Scorer argmax equals talk() output with zero mismatches.
 - Stored chain-5 hits and per-split counts reproduced.
 - fp32 CPU minus stored bf16-autocast CUDA is within 0.5 on pooled-5 and within 1.0 on loops:0 in_dist on all six confirm seeds (s100/s101 as extras).
 - Proved wrong: the difference exceeds 2.0 on loops:0, so every leak verdict must be re-scored on one device. If Gate 0 fails, stop and do not run analyses A or B.
5. Analysis A, informational (screen on 2 paired seeds, rule 4), using formula (q - d^2)/N, a family-cluster bootstrap, and the floors 0.52 and 0.33. Decision rule fixed now: a combined six-seed SE above 0.5 on a sealed +-1.0 gap means 'underpowered', which triggers a separately sealed larger-panel proposal and never a loosening. The old mark (a) (B2-vs-own-seeds row SE at most 0.3) and its row SE above 0.5 proved-wrong line are dropped. Replace them with the cross-arm decision rule above. State the which-claim-is-it question (fixed benchmark vs new rows) for Ben before reading the numbers.
6. Analysis B, optional, one at a time after A: AUROC of the no-gold path probability, pass at 0.75 or higher on all six seeds, proved wrong at below 0.65 on any seed. The 0.75 and 0.65 are suggested and untested. Do not choose any deploy threshold from these dev rows. If it passes, the next step is a separate sealed gate design (fixed constant, or the model's own tries), not a mark.
7. Soft and gold-based scores: diagnostics only. Define P(gold) over row['accepted'] and all decode paths from the free-running state with gold=None. Do not use the 8-character truncation (rule 7). Report paired SNR for B2 minus plain only when plain per-row probabilities exist for 6 seeds, and they currently do not. Drop mark (c) (within-arm SD at most 0.40), because it passes about 15% of the time by chance and rewards compression.
8. Exclusions and checks. Keep T1/U0/W1/C0 out until their verdicts are sealed. Check that the idea does not duplicate the director's ideas 2, 4, 5, 6 and 18 before building. Expect the result to be a better error bar and, possibly, a signal candidate for 'stuck' detection. It will not by itself move any model score, so rank it as cheap measurement infrastructure, not as a gain.

plan.title: Per-row CPU re-score of saved checkpoints
plan.ben_line: Right now our error bars only count how lucky each training run was. This test checks how much the fixed list of test questions adds to the wobble, so we can tell whether a small gap between two models is real, and it changes no model and no score.
plan.question: Does the fixed dev panel add question-level noise large enough to change a sealed verdict on the B2 vs plain gaps or the T1 vs B2 parity gap, and does a CPU re-score of the saved checkpoints reproduce the stored GPU numbers well enough to measure that? No training, no GPU.
plan.one_change: Add one eval-only CPU re-scorer (new rescore.py: fp32 on CPU, evalx.evaluate with return_preds on the five pooled dev splits, plus loops:0 and the chain-5 panel) that stores per-row results for the saved checkpoints, and report the row-sampling term beside the training-seed SE. Nothing else changes: no model, data, seed or sealed mark.

plan.machine: M1 Pro CPU (preferred), or the PC's CPU with OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 so the GPU queues are not slowed. No GPU and no rented box. CPU run time is untested: time a 300-row run per checkpoint before the full run.
pass_marks: Gate 0a (equivalence; tolerances suggested, untested): on each of B2 seeds 200-205, the CPU re-score's correct and n per split are within 1.0 point of the stored final_eval values, and pooled-5 is within 0.5 point. Stored values are shown in RESULT.json final_eval; for B2_s200 the pooled-5 sum is 4409 of 6040 = 73.00 (shown, computed).

Gate 0b (suggested, untested): loops:0 in_dist within 1.0 point of the stored lesion value on each seed (stored: s200 0.00, s201 10.81, shown). Chain-5: at most 5 of 1000 rows disagree with chain5.intact.hits on each seed (shown: the hits are a dict of 1000 row ids with 0/1 values).

Gate 0c (new-path check, used only for Analysis B): the no-gold path's decoded answer matches talk()'s output on 100% of rows on the same CPU run, zero mismatches. This check is circular for Analysis A, because evaluate(return_preds) is talk() itself (evalx.py lines 37-66, shown).

Analysis A decision rule (fixed now; formula suggested): SE_train = paired SD / sqrt(6), using the sealed SDs of 0.94 for B2 minus plain_tf and 1.33 for B2 minus plain_tf_steps (shown in the brief's CONFIRM-ANALYSIS). SE_row = 100 x sqrt((q - d^2)/N) per pair, where q is the fraction of rows whose correctness differs, d the mean gap and N = 6040. Compute SE_row once per pair and do not divide it by sqrt(6), because all seeds share the same dev rows. Combined SE = sqrt(SE_train^2 + SE_row^2). A parity gap is called underpowered if the 95% half-width of the combined SE exceeds 1.0 (combined SE above 0.51). For the re-sealed T1 parity mark (1a: six-seed mean of T1 minus B2 at least -1.0; 1b: lower 95% bound at least -2.0; shown in PASS-MARKS addendum 17 amendment), this only triggers a separately sealed larger-panel proposal and never loosens a mark. The rule also fires from training noise alone when the paired SD exceeds about 1.25 (computed, shown).

Analysis A floors (a consistency check, not a finding; suggested formula on shown means): under independent rows, SE_row cannot be below 0.52 points for B2 minus plain_tf (d = 0.2034) or below 0.33 points for B2 minus plain_tf_steps (d = 0.0689). A measured value below its floor means the code or the data is wrong.

Analysis B (optional, its own sealed step after A; thresholds suggested, untested): the AUROC of the no-gold decoded-path probability against is_hit on pooled-5 must be at least 0.75 on all six B2 seeds. The variant split is reported separately and is not part of the mark.
plan.proved_wrong: Gate 0: any miss on 0a or 0b stops Analysis A and B. A loops:0 gap above 2.0 on any seed means every leak verdict must be re-scored on one device, which is a re-score and not a mark change. Analysis A: the idea has no decision value if the row term leaves every sealed verdict unchanged, and that is already the expectation for PASS-1 and PASS-2. Shown (computed from the sealed SDs and means, using the suggested variance formula): even at q = 1.0, the most discordance possible, the lower 95% bound stays near 17.8 for B2 minus plain_tf (bar +2.0) and near 4.2 for B2 minus plain_tf_steps (bar +1.0). So the idea's value rests on parity marks and future small gaps. For the T1 parity gap the row term changes the decision only if q exceeds about 0.07 at a paired SD of 0.94 (computed, untested because T1 PREDS are absent). Analysis B: an AUROC below 0.65 on any seed means the answer probability is not a usable no-gold stuck signal.
plan.null_risk: Gate 0 is an equivalence check, so passing with no change is its purpose. Its real risk is circularity, which is why 0c uses a separate new path. The 1.0-point leak tolerance is untested against fp32-vs-bf16 eval differences. The cross-box leak gaps (s201: 10.81 on the PC vs 4.34 on a 5090; s200: 0.00 vs 1.40; shown) come from separate training runs with different final train losses (0.0139 vs 0.0238 on s201, shown), so they do not measure eval precision. CPU fp32 reproduced the plain_tf_steps screen scores exactly (96.3 and 96.5, shown in D0b-RESULT line 4), which makes a pass likely for the plain arm but says nothing about B2 (untested). Analysis A: the rule can fire from the panel alone, with no model change, so the report must name which term drives it. A same-checkpoint pair gives zero and is not a test. Analysis B: a no-signal AUROC sits near 0.5 with a null SE near 0.01 on about 6040 rows (shown, computed), so 0.75 cannot pass by chance. The real risk is saturation: final train losses of 0.014 to 0.024 (shown) may tie many answer probabilities near 1.0, so the report must give the tie fraction.
plan.autonomy: Everything here is developer measurement: gold-scored dev rows, run offline on CPU. Nothing in Stage 0, Gate 0 or Analysis A runs inside the deployed model, and no gold-based number may become a training, sleep or gate signal. Analysis B is the only piece with a deploy candidate: the model can compute the probability of its own decoded answer from its own forward pass with no gold. A deployed stuck-gate would need a fixed design constant or a threshold the model sets from its own tries, and no threshold may be chosen from these dev rows.

fixed_plan.one_change: Write one eval-only rescore.py that saves per-row results for B2_s200 only, plus a zero-compute bound table in a PASS-MARKS addendum. Nothing else changes: no model, data, seed or sealed mark.

Split Gate 0 into two checks. (1) Code correctness: the scorer's argmax reproduces talk()'s own output with zero mismatches, and the same CPU path run twice or in fp32 vs CPU-bf16 sets a measured noise floor. (2) Device parity: CPU fp32 vs stored CUDA bf16-autocast. Weights are fp32 (train.py:201) and the stored numbers are bf16-autocast CUDA, so a miss on (2) is a finding that leak verdicts need one device. It is not a code bug. Seal that distinction now.

Fix the chain-5 tolerance before the run. The planned 5-row tolerance equals B2's own mean seed-to-seed disagreement (4.5 rows, shown), so it can't tell a bug from precision noise. Use the larger of the measured floor on the same checkpoint and a sealed constant.

idea.title: Measure aggregate B2 updates/s at 1, 2, 3 jobs per card
idea.summary: Per-run speed on the PC moves 4x with outside load, and nobody has measured the sum over jobs that run together. Run 1, 2 and 3 B2 jobs in back-to-back 1,000-update windows with a repeat check, log card-level utilization and memory, and run a two-job test on one rented 5090. The result sets the par value, which decides how many seeds fit per day.
idea.change: No model change. (a) Three one-line queue files for local_runner: B2 seeds 998 and 999 (unused), --steps 1000 --log-every 100, no --final-eval, par 1, 2, 3, then par 1 again as drift check. Steady window = updates 200-1000 from train events. (b) A background nvidia-smi sampler every 5 s (utilization, memory.used, memory.total, compute-apps) and UTC START/END lines written into the run folders. (c) On one rented 5090 (8a command): B2 alone, B2+B2, B2+PT+LLM, 600 steps each. Check nvidia-smi memory.total first (tft_s301 reported 16,824 MiB reserved on a '16 GB' card). Param cost 0.
idea.why: Shown: queue 33 ran 18 jobs at par 3 and its aggregate was never measured; B2 rates were step-like (e.g. B2_s201 about 2.2 steps/s, then 1.1 from update 3,000, then 5.6-7.1) and B2_s205 jumped from about 5 to 8.5 when others finished. The cleanest data: three identical plain runs held 20.8 steps/s each (62.4 aggregate) and two B2 jobs on a cloud box held 8.2-8.7 each, so our own jobs share a card well when nothing else is on it; the swings probably come from outside load (untested). Windows has no CUDA MPS (suggested), so extra jobs add throughput only where one job leaves the GPU idle, which idea 1 measures. A 3M B2 reserves 4.7-4.9 GB, so 3 jobs need about 14.4 GB of a 16 GB card.

critiques.rescue: Revise, then run only as a clean PC window. (1) Hold the PC queue first: create the STOP file (local_runner.py line 24), wait for running jobs to end, check that GPU-BUSY.txt has no other owner's lines, and check that the card has no other memory in use. Log every 5 s: nvidia-smi memory, utilisation and compute-app PIDs, plus Windows host CPU. Mark any block where a non-custom_io process is on the card as invalid, not as drift. The jobs of an arm start together from one launch script (not the runner's 60 s gap), each runs for a fixed wall time (about 10 minutes), and updates are counted only in the window where all of that arm's jobs run. critiques.already_tried: Closest prior work, all shown: queue 33 (par 3, 18 runs, all status ok; per-500-step elapsed in each stdout.events.txt). 03-noise (three identical plain 3.24M runs at 20.71-20.72 steps/s, no solo). 02-calib-long/tf3m_24k (28.50 steps/s, same config, 3-way shared per CALIBRATION.md line 41). 29-b2-screen (two 8-loop B2 jobs on a rented 5090 at par 2: 8.24 and 8.17 steps/s, no matched solo). 8a box.json (arms run one at a time on a rented 5090; B2 there has 12 loops). queue_local/32 has no results folder. No concurrency measurement and no per-phase timer exists in custom_io; a grep for synchronize finds only train.py:191 and hf_baseline.py:179. Nothing in the files tests host CPU against GPU time for B2.
critiques.expected_effect: If run as written on the PC: one ratio per par level with no replicate, an undefined 1.15-1.3 zone, a par-3 verdict that cannot be wrong, a 5090 baseline of 7.1 from a 12-loop model, and a card that is probably not quiet (the queue and a blocker tenant are on it). The likely outcome is inconclusive for par 3, a false pass for par 2 in several percent of comparisons, and no answer to whether the step is host-bound. The revised plan answers the host-versus-GPU question first at near-zero GPU cost, then gives a noise-checked par answer on a dedicated card. Wall-time estimates for the 1,000-step windows, from observed rates of 1.1-8.5 steps/s: about 2-15 min each, plus 60 s launch gaps.

chair.reasons:
DECISION: plan, but not as written. The question (what do 1, 2 and 3 B2 jobs per card sum to?) is unmeasured and sets seeds per day, so a cut is wrong. The proposed test is badly designed and partly aimed at the wrong shape, so the plan must be rebuilt around free log analysis first.

RULES: No rule is touched. It changes no model or data and makes no score claim (rules 1-3, 5, 7, 8 not triggered). Rule 10 does not apply (dev-side throughput only); the sealed note should say throughput numbers size dev queues only and feed no deploy-time setting. Rule 4: marks must be sealed in PASS-MARKS.md before the first run, and they can only be a throughput screen, not a model claim. Rule 6 is the weak point: the rented-5090 arm is not clearly covered by Ben's 3:00 PM Vast approval (for important runs), and it buys almost nothing (see 5).

DEFECTS (shown unless marked):
1. Confounded. The PC is not quiet. progress-board/data.json (5:58 PM ET) shows q39 running, q40 to about 11 PM-midnight, C0 about 10 PM, T4 speed from about 9:30 PM; the blocker thread shares the card (PC-JOB.md). A fixed order W1, W2, W3, W1-repeat confounds arm with time, and PC rates move in regimes of 15 minutes to 3 hours, so one end-point repeat cannot see a dip inside W2 or W3. The 15 percent drift band is uncalibrated (critic computed ~83 percent of 1,000-step window pairs in q33 fall within +-15 percent, so it would reject about 1 in 6 valid windows).
2. Launch gap. The runner starts jobs 60 s apart, so at 1,000 updates (2-15 min per job) a trio overlaps for little time. Per-job windows summed mix solo and co-running time. Each arm needs one common window with all its jobs running.
3. Wrong baseline. The 7.1 and 11.4 steps/s marks come from the 8a 12-loop B2 (8a-results/8a-3M-s401-box/box.json: n_loops 12, 7.09/7.14/6.41 steps/s), not the 8-loop q33 B2. The same 8a spec (I2) shows a 200-update B2 probe at 0.092 s/update (10.9/s) against 7.1/s over the full run, a 1.5x gap, while plain probes match their full runs within about 3 percent. So short B2 windows over-predict B2 rate. Marks must be ratios between arms run the same way; delete the absolute numbers.
4. Memory and shape (new, from my read of box.json): the 8a-shaped B2 has peak allocated 6,462.6 MiB and reserved 6,986 MiB, against 4.7-4.9 GB reserved (and 2.9-3.1 GB allocated) for the 8-loop q33 B2. Three 8a-shaped jobs (about 21 GB) cannot fit a 16 GB card, so par 3 is set by memory, not throughput, for that shape. The board also says the 7-step cap is being lifted to 16 'next', so the shape the next PC confirms will run is not frozen; a measurement on the 8-loop shape may be stale before it is used. The 4.70-4.89 GB figures also come from Test LR and rented B2V runs, not plain B2 on the PC (q33 RESULT.json files have no memory fields).
5. The 5090 arm is not worth it. 8a boxes are one seed per box already, so par does not change wall time across seeds. Box dph is 0.48; a box wall of 5,058 s holds B2 3,423 s plus PT 589 s plus LLM about 800 s, so running arms together saves at most about 1,400 s, about 0.17 dollars a box (computed). At 10M the B2 step is 0.327 s (GPU-bound, 21 GB unsplit) and 30M is memory-bound, so concurrency cannot help there. A 5090 ratio also cannot set the PC's par.
6. Evidence slips: the three plain runs in 03-noise were 20.71-20.72 steps/s each (sum 62.1, not 62.4); 'EG arms did not slow with partners' has no solo EG run; 29-b2-screen is 8.24 and 8.17 steps/s on rented 5090s (no 8.7 anywhere) with no matched solo; 'aggregate never measured' is slightly overstated (q33 B2_s202-204 each ran about 4.4 steps/s, but overlap is not shown).
7. Mechanics: local_runner skips any run name that already has a RESULT.json, so a same-name repeat is skipped; W3 needs three distinct names and a third seed; and the 'third job starts within 2 min' validity test would fail whenever the 6000 MiB gate holds the third job back, which is itself the par-3 result.
8. Overlap: a per-phase profile (director idea 1; T4 speed thread) decides whether the step is host-bound or GPU-bound. That determines whether extra jobs can add anything (suggested: the 16 blocking host-to-device copies and per-row Python in the step make host cost likely; untested). The par test should share one PC window with the profile instead of stalling the queue twice.

WHY NOT CUT: a free first look exists. I rebuilt the q33 schedule (par 3, 60 s gap, queue order, wall_s; start times approximate to a few minutes; files hold no timestamps) and took median B2 block rates from the 500-step elapsed fields (computed by the chair, rough, confounded with the plain partners and the blocker thread): 8.5 steps/s with two jobs on the card (one B2 plus one plain, B2_s205), 5.6 steps/s each when two B2 jobs ran together, 5.5 each with three jobs on the card. Read as suggested only: a second B2 job looks worth about 1.3x in aggregate, and a third job shows no visible cost to the first two, but arms are mixed so this is not a result. It shows the log route can give a first answer at zero GPU cost, and that a controlled test only has to settle par 2 vs par 3 and the shape-specific numbers.

EXPECTED VALUE: moderate and bounded. par is already 3 by default and memory-gated, so a wrong par costs little unless the card thrashes (no sign of that). The real gain is a defensible seeds-per-day figure and a cheap per-process log that settles every later speed question. That justifies a near-free plan, not a 2-3 hour PC stall in a queue that is full until morning.
chair.revised_idea:
Measure aggregate B2 updates/s per jobs-per-card on the PC, in three stages, cheapest first, with no change to model or training numerics.

STAGE 0 (no GPU, now): rebuild the q33 and later q39/q40 concurrency from RESULT wall_s, runner order and the 500-step elapsed fields; tabulate block rates by number of own jobs running and by arm. Report as a screen (suggested), with the reconstruction error stated. Do not claim an aggregate from mixed arms.

STAGE 1 (logging patch, zero training effect): local_runner and train.py write UTC START/END and a UTC time on every 500-step train event into each run folder; a 5 s sampler logs nvidia-smi GPU utilisation, memory.used/total, clocks, power, per-process compute-apps (pid and memory) and host CPU percent, plus the count of own running jobs; each RESULT.json records peak_mem_mib and peak_reserved_mib (train.py already writes them; q33 lacks them) and the cfg (n_loops, caps). Mark any window with a non-custom_io process on the card as invalid, not as drift. Then every real queue (q39, q40, U0, W1, C0) builds the dataset for free. Check nvidia-smi memory.total once (tft_s301 reported 16,824 MiB reserved on a '16 GB' card).

STAGE 2 (controlled pilot; only if Stage 0/1 leave par 2 vs par 3 unclear, and only in one planned PC gap shared with the per-phase profile, after the STOP file lets running jobs finish and GPU-BUSY shows no other owner): use the exact shape the next PC confirm will run (so after the 7-to-16 cap lift is frozen), read peak_reserved from a 200-step solo run first, and run par 3 only if 3 x peak_reserved + 1.5 GB fits the free memory. Blocks of 1, 2 and (if it fits) 3 identical-shape jobs, each block launched together from one script (not the 60 s gap), distinct run names, seeds 998, 999 and one more unused seed, 1,500 updates with --log-every 100, steady window = the span where all jobs of that arm run. Run 4-6 blocks, each arm once per block in random order; judge by paired within-block ratios R2 = sum rate(2 jobs)/rate(1 job) and R3 = sum rate(3)/sum rate(2). If the third job cannot start for memory, report that as the par-3 result.

DROPPED: the rented 5090 arm (at most about 0.17 dollars a box of saving, and not clearly covered by the Vast approval); the absolute marks 7.1 and 11.4; seeds-only W1/W2/W3 single windows.

Marks (ratios, sealed before block 1): par 2 supported if median R2 >= 1.3 and every block >= 1.15; killed if median R2 < 1.1; 1.1-1.3 inconclusive, keep the current par. Par 3 supported if median R3 >= 1.2 and every block >= 1.05; killed if median R3 < 1.05. Calibrate the block-to-block spread on the Stage 1 data before sealing, and widen nothing afterwards. Throughput numbers size dev queues only and feed no deploy-time setting.
chair.plan_guidance:
The plan must get these right:
1. Order of work: Stage 0 (log reconstruction, no GPU) and Stage 1 (logging patch) first; Stage 2 only if they leave par 2 vs par 3 unclear, and then in one window shared with the per-phase profile (idea 1 / T4). Do not stop the PC queue for this alone.
2. Config: use the shape the next PC confirms will actually run. The q33 8-loop B2 is 2.9-3.1 GB allocated and 4.7-4.9 GB reserved; the 8a 12-loop B2 is 6,462.6 MiB allocated and 6,986 MiB reserved (box.json). Read peak_reserved from a short solo run and let that, not a guess, decide whether par 3 can start. If it cannot start, that is the par-3 answer.
3. Design: interleaved, randomised blocks (every arm once per block), one launch script per arm so all jobs start together, identical config and distinct run names (local_runner skips names with an existing RESULT.json), and a common steady window for the sum. Judge by within-block ratios R2 and R3, never by absolute steps/s; delete the 7.1 and 11.4 marks (the 7.1 is a 12-loop figure). Never extrapolate window rates to a 24k run: B2's 200-update probe ran 1.5x faster than its full run on the same 5090 type (8A-SPEC I2 vs box.json), so only ratios are used.
4. Validity: a block counts only if the per-process log shows nothing but this queue's processes on the card (blocker thread, other queues, creative jobs excluded), host CPU is logged, and the same-arm spread across blocks is reported. Calibrate the ratio spread from the Stage 1 data before sealing the marks. Record which co-tenants were seen.
5. Marks: seal in PASS-MARKS.md as a dated addendum before block 1, ratios only: par 2 supported if median R2 >= 1.3 and min >= 1.15, proved wrong (par 2 adds nothing) if median R2 < 1.1; par 3 supported if median R3 >= 1.2 and min >= 1.05, proved wrong if median R3 < 1.05; the in-between band keeps current par. This is a throughput screen with no score claim; say so.
6. Say that the test is only valid for the shape and the co-tenants on the card at the time; re-check par on the first real queue using the new per-process logs.
7. Keep it separate from the village model and from any model claim; add the one-line rule-10 note (throughput numbers size dev queues only).
8. Plain-language summary for Ben (high-school senior): 'We never measured how much work the card does when it trains 1, 2 or 3 models at once. First we read the logs we already have, then we add a small logger so every future run teaches us, and only if that is unclear do we run a short, shuffled test when the card is free.'

plan.title: Par test: jobs per card for B2 on the 5070 Ti
plan.ben_line: We have never measured how much total training the graphics card gets done when it runs one, two or three models at the same time. First we read the logs we already have, then we add a small logger so every later run teaches us, and only if that is still unclear do we run a short, shuffled test while the card is free.
plan.question: On Ben's RTX 5070 Ti, does running two or three identical B2 training jobs at once add enough total updates per second (over one job alone) to change how many jobs the PC queue should run together (its --par value)?
plan.one_change: Only the number of identical B2 jobs sharing the card (1, 2 or 3) is varied, and only in Stage 2. Stage 0 reads logs. Stage 1 adds logging that changes no model, data, optimizer or loss code. This is a throughput question only: no score claim and no training claim.
arms: A: one B2 job in the queue 33 shape (--model ledger --cfg '{"copy":true}' --bf16 --batch 256 --lr 1e-3, 8 loops), with --steps 1500 --log-every 100 and no --final-eval.
B: two identical B2 jobs started together from one launch script, same flags as A.
C: three identical B2 jobs started together, same flags. Run only if the memory check passes (see steps); otherwise recorded as 'par 3 not available on this card' and no R3 is judged.
plan.seeds: Throughput only, so seeds set no score. Use throwaway seeds 997, 998 and 999. A grep of the custom_io, custom-io and roadmap folders finds no use of seeds 996 to 999 (shown, this review). Each job needs a unique run name (for example B2_t{block}{arm}{j}), because local_runner skips any name whose RESULT.json already exists (shown, local_runner.py line 243). Final eval is off, so no dev, GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind panel is scored (rule 5).
plan.machine: Stage 0: CPU only, reading the snapshot and, if Ben copies it, the PC's runner log. Stage 1: logging patch to local_runner.py and train.py, plus one 300-step check on the PC. Stage 2: BensPC RTX 5070 Ti only (rule 6; the rented-5090 arm is dropped). Facts, shown: the card is shared by design with the ultracode blocker thread, whose PC jobs are listed in progress-board blockers and PC-JOB.md. Queue 39 (EGE) runs on the PC now with ETA about 6 to 7 PM ET (progress-board data.json, updated 5:58 PM ET), and queues 40 to 44 are queued behind it. Memory, shown: reserved 4,824 MiB for a B2 with per-round passes (results/37-pc-loop-readout/LR_s200/RESULT.json) and 4,696 MiB on a rented 5090 (results/40-egw-s200/B2V_s200/RESULT.json). Plain B2 on the PC has no measured peak, because the queue 33 RESULT.json files carry no peak fields (all None). The 8a 12-loop B2 reserves 6,986 MiB (peak_reserved_mib in the 8a-3M-s401, s402 and s405 B2 RESULT.json; box.json holds only the 6,462.6 MiB allocated figure). Three jobs at 4,824 MiB plus 1,536 MiB is 16,008 MiB (computed), which is about the whole of a 16 GB card. Whether a CUDA context per process fits outside torch's reserved count is untested.
pass_marks: Sealed as PASS-MARKS.md addendum 21 (addendum 20 is the last one, shown) before any block runs, pilot included. Ratios only, no absolute steps/s.
Par 2 supported: median R2 >= 1.30 and every counted valid block R2 >= 1.15, where R2 = (sum of the 2 jobs' updates/s) / (the 1 job's updates/s) in the same block.
Par 2 proved wrong: median R2 < 1.10.
Par 3 supported: median R3 >= 1.20 and every counted valid block R3 >= 1.05, where R3 = (sum of the 3 jobs' updates/s) / (sum of the 2 jobs' updates/s).
Par 3 proved wrong: median R3 < 1.05.
Anything between (R2 median 1.10 to 1.30, or R3 median 1.05 to 1.20): inconclusive, keep the current par.

A block counts only if it passes the validity rule in the steps. Invalid blocks are reported with the cause and never dropped quietly. A decision needs 6 counted valid blocks; with fewer, the result is a screen and must say so.
plan.proved_wrong: Par 2 adds nothing on this card: median R2 < 1.10 over at least 6 valid blocks. Par 3 adds nothing: median R3 < 1.05 over at least 6 valid blocks. Then par 1 stays, and any speed gain has to come from per-update cost (the host-side rewrite and CUDA-graph ideas in the area list). One or two pilot blocks prove nothing on their own.
plan.null_risk: Noise alone almost never passes a no-change design. With no real change (R2 = R3 = 1.0) and an assumed block-to-block SD of 0.10 to 0.15 (not measured), the chance that the median R2 of 6 blocks reaches 1.30 is far below 0.1 percent (computed, normal approximation). The real false-pass paths are: (a) a co-tenant running during only one arm, which the validity rule and random arm order address; and (b) host-CPU overlap, where one job cannot use the CPU fully and two jobs fill it, giving R2 above 1 with no GPU gain. Path (b) is a real throughput gain for the sum, not GPU efficiency. The host-CPU log says which one occurred. The larger risk is power, not false passes: a true R2 of 1.3 passes every condition only about 25 to 45 percent of the time at SD 0.10 to 0.15 (computed, assumed SD). The spread is not measured anywhere in the snapshot. Three identical plain 3.2M jobs started together ended within 0.4 s and ran at 20.71 to 20.72 steps/s (results/03-noise, shown). The same config at another time ran at 28.50 steps/s (results/02-calib-long/tf3m_24k, shown; CALIBRATION.md notes the different timing), so between-window spread can be large. The 1.15 and 1.05 per-block floors are therefore uncalibrated. Stage 1 data cannot calibrate them, because no queue has a solo arm. The pilot measures the spread; if the spread is too large, the verdict is inconclusive. The marks are not edited afterwards.
plan.autonomy: No deploy-time step. The test sets how many dev training jobs share the PC card, and the deployed model changes in no way. Nothing in the deployed model's learning, sleep, search, gates or tool choice depends on it. Throughput numbers size dev queues only and feed no deploy-time setting (one-line rule-10 note, to be copied into the addendum). The village model is not involved (rule 9).
steps: Stage 0, CPU only, now: from results/33-pc-confirm-b2/*/RESULT.json (wall_s, train_s, steps_per_s) and stdout.events.txt (elapsed every 500 steps, measured from the training-loop clock at train.py line 157, so startup is excluded), tabulate each job's rate by window and by how many of its own jobs were running. Starts can only be inferred from queue order (60 s launch gap; a launch only when free memory is at least 6000 MiB, local_runner.py lines 256-270), so the error is several minutes (suggested). Mixed-arm windows give no aggregate, so report it as a screen. The one clean same-shape sum is the 03-noise triple (plain 3.2M, 62.1 steps/s total, shown).

Stage 0 data request, no GPU: Ben copies C:\Users\benja\custom-io\work\q33.log, and q39's log when it ends, into the snapshot. The runner writes START and END lines with UTC there (local_runner.py lines 49, 254 and 270, shown). The run folders carry no UTC times (shown: rc.txt, cmd.txt, stdout.txt, stdout.events.txt and RESULT.json only). GPU-BUSY.txt keeps only the current lines, so its history is lost (local_runner.py lines 161-185).

Stage 1, logging only: (a) local_runner.py writes out/times.txt at each START and END (UTC, pid, free MiB, running count), and once per queue writes the GPU name and memory.total from nvidia-smi. (b) A 5-second sampler CSV per queue with nvidia-smi utilisation, memory.used, memory.total, power, clocks and compute-apps pid and used memory, plus host CPU percent (Windows counter; untested, psutil not confirmed installed). Per-process memory may read N/A under the Windows driver (suggested, untested); if so, match the compute-app pids to the GPU-BUSY pid list instead. (c) train.py: add a utc field to the train event at line 178. Keep log-every 500 for main runs and add no synchronize call (the only explicit one is line 191).

Stage 1 check: one 300-step B2 run on the PC with log-every 100, before and after the patch, same seed. The logged losses should match. ledger.py line 248 uses scatter_add_, which is nondeterministic on CUDA (suggested), so if the losses differ, first run a same-code twin pair (untested) and call the patch equivalent only inside the twin band.

Stage 1 timing: local_runner.py run() copies the code when a queue starts (lines 233-236, shown), so queues already running keep their frozen code. q39 keeps its code. q40 gets the patch only if it starts after the patch lands. The first logged queue is the first one started after the patch.

Stage 2 gate, run only if Stage 0 and 1 leave par 2 vs par 3 unclear and Ben agrees to one gap: (a) no local_runner process is alive on the PC, because a live queue would launch jobs into free memory and join the arms; (b) the STOP file in the work folder is set and running jobs have finished (STOP stops new launches only, local_runner.py line 24); (c) GPU-BUSY.txt shows no other owner; (d) the blocker thread agrees to pause its PC jobs (PC-JOB.md says the queue never stops them, so this is an agreement, not a switch); (e) nvidia-smi memory.total is read once (tft_s301 showed 16,824 MiB reserved on a card called 16 GB; cause unclear).

Stage 2 memory check: read peak_reserved_mib from one 200-step solo run of the same shape first (train.py lines 204-205 write it on CUDA). Start arm C only if 3 x peak_reserved + 1,536 MiB is at most memory.total. If it fails, record 'par 3 not available on this card' and skip arm C. That is a result, not an error.

Stage 2 shape: arms A, B and C use the queue 33 B2 config (8 loops, copy on, the confirm flags), with --steps 1500, --log-every 100 and no --final-eval. Build the commands with local_runner.command() so the flags match exactly. Do not use the 8a 12-loop config, whose 7.09 steps/s is a 12-loop figure (8a box.json, shown). The 'cap lift' in the brief is roadmap item 2d, a learned stop with chains up to 16 steps, which is planned and not frozen (roadmap 2d row, shown). If it is adopted before Stage 2, redo the shape first.

Pilot, then blocks: run 2 pilot blocks, not counted, to measure the block-to-block spread. Seal the marks before the pilot and do not change them after it; the pilot decides only whether the verdict is inconclusive. The chair's 'calibrate before sealing' cannot be done from Stage 0 and 1 data, because no queue has a solo arm (shown). Then 6 counted blocks. In each block A, B and C run once, in an arm order drawn from a seed written to the addendum before the pilot. Between arms the card must hold none of our jobs. Within an arm, all jobs start from one launch script within 10 s. At the 1.6 to 8.5 updates/s seen on queue 33, 1,500 updates take about 3 to 16 minutes per job (computed), so a block is about 15 to 25 minutes and the whole Stage 2 is about 2.7 hours.

Rates: the steady window runs from step 300 to the step where the first job of the arm ends. Each job's rate is its steps in the window divided by its elapsed time over the same window, from the 100-step train events. The arm sum is the sum over its jobs. Judge only R2 and R3 per block, using medians and minima over valid blocks. Identical jobs started together ended within 0.4 s in the 03-noise triple (shown), so the windows should overlap almost fully.

Validity, decided by analyze_par.py before any ratio is read: (a) every job's status is ok, with no out-of-memory error; (b) during the window, the compute processes on the card are only this arm's pids (per-process log, or the pid list if memory reads N/A); (c) host CPU and GPU utilisation are logged for the arm; (d) a co-tenant seen means the block is invalid and is rerun later. Record every co-tenant seen, including the blocker thread's runs.

Analysis and seal: analyze_par.py is read-only and writes a verdict file into the results folder and a result line under addendum 21. A par change means only the --par value in the next queue header, plus one line in PC-JOB.md. Par is changed only after the marks are judged.

Plain-language line for the report: 'We measured how much total work the card does when it trains 1, 2 or 3 models at once. This is a speed question only, not a score claim.' Keep the village model out of it (rule 9).

[shown] Stage 1(a) duplicates output the runner already writes: say() prints UTC (lines 49-50), START lines carry pid, free MiB, need and running count (line 270), END lines carry minutes (line 254). Keep the q33 and q39 logs; no runner edit is needed for this.

fixed_plan.title: Headroom check, then a bounded par test (B2 on the 5070 Ti)
fixed_plan.ben_line: We have never measured whether the graphics card finishes more training when it runs two models at once. First we log how busy the card already is, which costs no card time, and run one short solo test to see whether there is any room. Only if there is room do we run the bounded test, with its pass rule fixed before we start.
fixed_plan.question: On Ben's 5070 Ti, is one B2 job already using most of the GPU, and if not, does a second identical B2 job raise total updates per second by at least 10 percent?
fixed_plan.one_change: Only the number of identical B2 jobs sharing the card (1 or 2), and only in Stage C. Stages A and B change no model, data, optimizer, loss or eval code.
arms: A (no card time): read the existing 33 confirm RESULT.json and stdout events; in the next normal queue, log 5-second nvidia-smi utilization and host CPU, plus the runner's existing UTC START and END lines.

B (about 3 min card time): one solo B2 run of 300 steps with CUDA-event timers around to_device, forward, backward and opt.step, plus the 5-second sample, from a new probe script. Go to C only if GPU time is under about 60 percent of the step (a suggested cut, sealed before B runs).

C (only if B shows room): 6 blocks. Each block runs 1 job, then 2 identical jobs, 800 steps each, from a direct launcher that starts both within 10 s and checks free memory before each start. Arm order is random per block, with the seed written into the addendum before the first block.
fixed_plan.seeds: Throughput only. Use seeds 997 and 998 (not used in queue_local or PASS-MARKS). Final eval off. No dev, GOLD-PRIVATE, reserved or blind panel is scored (rule 5).
fixed_plan.machine: BensPC 5070 Ti only (rule 6, PC first); no rented boxes. Stage C only after the blocker thread agrees to a pause window, with no co-tenant job during a block.
pass_marks: Sealed as PASS-MARKS.md addendum 21 before any Stage C block (addendum 20 is the last one).
R2 = (aggregate updates/s of the 2 jobs) / (updates/s of the 1 job), per block, both over the steady window (steps 300 to 800, from train events every 100 steps).
Par 2 helps: the one-sided 95% lower bound of mean R2 over 6 valid blocks (mean minus 2.015 times SD divided by root 6) is above 1.10.
Otherwise keep par 3 (the status quo).
fixed_plan.proved_wrong: Par 2 does not help if the one-sided 95% upper bound of mean R2 over 6 valid blocks is below 1.05. Otherwise the result is inconclusive. In both cases par 3 stays, so the default is safe. Power at true 1.3 is 41 to 99 percent at SD 0.10-0.30 (simulated), so a no-help result is rarely reached when a real gain is small.
fixed_plan.null_risk: Under no gain (R2 = 1.0) the 'helps' bound clears 1.10 with 0.0 to 0.9 percent probability at SD 0.10-0.30 (simulated, 20k draws). The main path to a false pass is host-CPU overlap, which is a real throughput gain for the queue, not a false pass. A co-tenant during only the 2-job arm is handled by the validity rule (block invalid, rerun).
fixed_plan.autonomy: No deploy-time step. The test sizes dev queues only, and nothing in the deployed model's learning, sleep, search, gates or tool choice depends on it (rule 10 holds). Village model not involved (rule 9).

Run the 300-step solo probe with phase timers (B). Use it only as a go or no-go for C.
If go: write the addendum 21 marks and the arm-order seed, then run 6 blocks of 800 steps with a direct launcher, not the queue.
Judge with the one-sided bound. Change par only if it clears 1.10 and no blocker-thread run was in the window; otherwise keep par 3.

idea.title: Leak mark probe: what loops:0 hits really are
idea.summary: The zero-round leak mark (<=5% on every seed) fails on 3 of 8 B2 seeds and on T1 seed 200 (9.41). With zero rounds the controller state does not depend on the row, so hits are probably a fixed string or a positional pick matching a few families. A CPU probe splits hits by what the zero-round path can reach and compares them to train-only constants, so the mark can be restated as an excess over a chance floor.
idea.change: Eval-only script (CIO/leak_classes.py, new). On saved checkpoints run talk(state(batch, loops=0), batch) row by row on dev in_dist (1,360) and the big in_dist (6,800 if available, rule 5 check first), intact and loops:0. Classes from progparse.row_targets: C (computed: mode 0 with every gold answer slot >= R0), A (prompt number or constant), B (prompt word, mode 1), D (GEN, mode 2). Per family report: share of the most frequent zero-round string, the best constant answer from train (scored on dev), and excess = zero-round hits - constant. Chance floors for A/B/D from train statistics and reachable-candidate counts. Param cost 0.
idea.why: Shown: at loops=0 result slots are invalid and the pointers mask them with -1e9, so NUM answers can only be prompt numbers or the four constants; the noexec lesion shows the computed-class floor is 0.24-0.82% over 8 seeds (2,085 computed rows). Shown: B2 seed 201 hits are copy_word 35/40, prop_eval 30/40, i.e. copy and label families, not reasoning. Seed 201 moved from 10.81 (PC) to 4.34 (5090) on the same code and seed, so a single-seed line at 5 sits inside seed/box noise. Suggested: the 'word-pointer' explanation in the brief is only partly right (prop_eval is a true/false label family reached through the copy path).
